# Introduction

A Shinobi doesn't engage their enemy unless there's no other way. In service of their goals, they will use any tool or advantage they can find. When combat is unavoidable, however, they strike quickly and with absolute precision. This was our philosophy when creating this guide: teach how to use Sekiro's tools to avoid combat, and impart the knowledge needed to be absolutely deadly once your blade is drawn.

We have a long history of making books for FromSoftware's games. Each one has presented a unique challenge and surprised us in different ways. The thing that surprised us most about Sekiro, though, wasn't the complex, multiphase bosses or its multitude of systems for increasing the difficulty, brilliant as they are. It was the fact that, months after first playing it, with thousands of combined hours spent controlling the Wolf, we just wanted more. Mastering the combat is a thrill that hasn't come close to wearing off. The bosses aren't just spectacles—they are living, breathing opponents that demand respect and we hope we've given them that, and given you a fighting chance in the process.

# About the Data

The data in this guide is accurate according to Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice's second update (1.02). While it's possible that FromSoftware may make further tweaks to balance, this being an offline, single-player game, we're confident that the vast majority of the data and information we provide will remain accurate, but as much as we'd like to, we can't make any guarantees.

Chapter 1

# Shinobi School

All great shinobi have to start somewhere, usually learning their craft under the wing of an experienced master. This chapter will provide your initial guidance and take you from absolute novice to a studied practitioner of the shinobi arts.

![](images/560bad6e8c310dfe2aafb3ae2bf31d6f559f97a7b0d0949494e52b4925a2d5e0.jpg)

# Your First Steps

Before delving into the game proper, we'll go over the basic mechanical elements of how to save and load, as well as explain the HUD and menus.

# #

By pressing Menu / Options, you can pause the game. This doesn't work when you're in the middle of an action, being hit, or during a cutscene. Upon pausing you'll see four options in the menu:

# > Equipment

From here you can change your equipment. Three Prosthetic Tools, five Quick Items, one Combat Art and one Ninjutsu can be equipped at any one time. Don't feel as though you have to fill up all three Prosthetic slots just because you can. If only two are most efficient to handle a particular situation or enemy, then having only those equipped will allow you to more quickly flip between them.

# > Inventory

This tab displays all the items that you've picked up and currently hold. These are divided into four sections:

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Inventory Tabs</td></tr><tr><td>Quick Items</td><td>These are mostly limited use items (aside from the Homeward Idol). The Healing Gourd and multi-colored Gours that remedy Status Abnormalities can be replenished by resting at any Sculptor&#x27;s Idol.</td></tr><tr><td>Key Items</td><td>Items that are integral to the story, along with important lore related materials.</td></tr><tr><td>Upgrade Materials</td><td>Items needed by the Sculptor in order to Upgrade your Prosthetic Tools.</td></tr><tr><td>Prosthetic Arm Tools</td><td>Tools and Tool upgrades that you have unlocked.</td></tr></table>

# Saving and Loading

You cannot save manually in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice; the game is continually auto-saving whenever something happens. This means that every action you take will bear consequences, so you can't, for example, carelessly use certain limited-use items in the knowledge that you'd get them back by reloading the game.

Fortunately, if you're in a particularly perilous situation and need to rethink your strategy, or simply need to take a break, you can pause the game. Pausing is not possible while performing actions, when you're recovering from being hit, or during cutscenes. From the pause menu you can navigate over to Options and select "Quit Game" at any time.

Quitting in the middle of a boss battle will, upon re-loading your save file, return you to the nearest Sculptor's Idol that you travelled

# >Skills

Skills are learnt by spending Skill Points at any Sculptor's Idol after gaining the relevant Esoteric Text. There are four types of Skills:

increase your stats.</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>Ninjutsu
Techniques</td><td>Powerful abilities accessed only after a
Backstab Deathblow.</td></tr></table>

# > Options

This tab presents you with various options to configure the game to your liking. If you have a personal preference for your controller configurations, or want to change sound, brightness or camera settings, this is the place to do it.

to or rested at. Upon resuming the fight, the boss will have recovered all their Vitality, and any items that you consumed during the battle will still be gone. This means that boss battles are a commitment of your time and energy, so make sure you're ready before engaging in them. Similarly, if you quit while fighting a regular enemy, all their Vitality will be recovered once you reload your save, and you will recommence at the exact position where you quit.

As a final note, be sure to always quit properly from the menu instead of turning the console off or closing the application. Since the game is constantly auto-saving, you otherwise run the risk of corrupting your save file. Although this is rare, it will mean that the time you put in will be gone, so it's best to be careful.

# HUD

You can adjust HUD settings within the menus, under Sound and Display. The default is set to Auto Hide Partial, which always shows critical information that is essential to your survival, but hides less essential information, such as how many Skill Points or how much Sen you have, until it is relevant. If you want a more immersive experience at the expense of slightly less situational awareness,

Auto Hide All will also remove critical combat information, except for when you're in a battle. Always Show will have all information displayed at all times, which many players will find undesirable, as it results in a cluttered screen. Always Hide will permanently remove the HUD, but since there's so much to keep track of, this isn't recommended unless you already know the game very well.

1 Player Vitality Gauge: Once this is depleted you will die. It can be increased with Prayer Beads.  
② Resurrection Node: Displays the number of times you can Resurrect after being killed.  
3 Player Posture Gauge: Once this is masted out you will be Posture-broken, leaving you vulnerable. This gauge can also be increased with Prayer Beads; though the size of the gauge will not appear different, it will be slower to fill.  
4 Perilous Attack: When this symbol is on screen, the next enemy attack will be unguarded. Immediate action needs to be taken in order to avoid it.  
5 Sen: The amount of Sen in your possession.  
Quick Item: The currently selected Quick Item is displayed here. Press Left and Right on the directional pad to scroll between them, and Up to use it.

![](images/34fd78372ce8af5dd3c2b69ff835cbf89298fed5a08de87a989c9b17cd6eac8f.jpg)

7 Prosthetic Tool: You can switch between Prosthetic Tools by pressing  $\mathbf{v} / \mathbf{A}$ . You can then use it by pressing RT/R2. If you don't have enough Spirit Emblems to use the Prosthetic then this will be highlighted in red.

8 Ninjutsu: Displayed when you have Ninjutsu equipped. Highlighted in red if you don't have enough Spirit Emblems to use it, and also when sitting at an Idol. Ninjutsu can only be performed after a Backstab Deathblow.

9 Deathblow Marker: Displays the number of Deathblows you need to land on an enemy in order to kill them.  
10 Enemy Vitality Gauge: Once this is depleted a regular enemy will die and also become open to a Deathblow. Enemies with multiple Vitality Gauges will not die if you simply deplete their Vitality Gauge, instead they will be Posture-broken and you will need to Deathblow them in order to take away one of their Deathblow Markers.  
11 Enemy Posture Gauge: Once this is maxed the enemy will be Posture-broken leaving them open to a Deathblow.  
Skill Points: Shows the number of Skill Points that you hold and your progress towards the next one.  
Deathblow Target: Once you have depleted an enemy's Vitality or Posture, a red target will appear on their body, signifying that they are vulnerable to a Deathblow.

![](images/e935cc98c14f21745dae946bddc2f010962f02321294b5feb1e7250b456ca4a4.jpg)

Lock-Out: After resurrecting, your other Resurrection Nodes will be locked out until you regain resurrection potential from any source.

16 Combat Art: Displayed when you have a Combat Art equipped. Combat Arts can be performed by holding guard and then pressing attack but not vice versa.

$\langle \widehat{\mathbb{C}}\rangle$  Status Abnormality Gauge: Once this fills up you will be inflicted with either Burn, Poison, Terror, Shock or Enfeeblement.

Spirit Emblems: Displays the number of Spirit Emblems currently at your disposal.

# Traversal

Ashina is a vast and jagged land that will take a long time to traverse. Thankfully, there are many options available to expediate your travel, as well as to enter areas that cannot be accessed merely by foot.

![](images/362c51a44382f8ac6cdc841b29e7f1e14869dd2b4f8318f40eb816c1336f19ba.jpg)

# Sculptor's Idol

The fastest way to travel long distances that you've already traversed is by communing at any Sculptor's Idol and selecting the Travel option. This will allow you to instantly travel to any previously-visited Idol. This option is available right from the start of the game and does not require you to satisfy any pre-conditions to unlock.

Aside from travel, Sculptor's Idols have many other uses, such as allowing you to rest to recover Vitality and restock items, learn new skills, and purchase Spirit Emblems. We will cover these functions later on in this section.

![](images/12e52984e131966512de378c36ea5e87547f48e68877965c823cf06975174bb6.jpg)

# Homeward Idol

The Homeward Idol is given to you by Lord Kuro when you rescue him during the adventure's prologue. By selecting it, either from the Quick Item menu or from your Inventory, you can warp to either the Dilapidated Temple Idol or the Last Communed Idol. The Homeward Idol does not spend any resources and can be used as often as you want. Be sure, however, that you are somewhere safe and secure before utilizing it; during its lengthy starting animation you can easily be interrupted by an enemy attack while warping. It is not intended to be used as an escape tool during the middle of a battle.

# Grappling (L1/L2)

Once you've been fitted with the Prosthetic Arm early on in your adventure, you can latch onto Grapple Points by pressing  $\boxed{1}$  /L2. You can grapple while in mid-air during a jump or while falling, and can also chain multiple grapples together. While chaining grapples, you may need to sometimes adjust your camera mid-grapple.

Grappling is a key movement technique that gives a strong sense of momentum and flow to the game. Aside from allowing you to traverse across gaps that you would not otherwise be able to, it's an invaluable tool both in combat and stealth, which we'll explore in more detail later.

The shape and color of Grapple Points will change according to how you can interact with them, as shown in the chart here.

![](images/c899bb66ddca8ad789b4e61ee65202da510daa14a01711ed465eb02a52a4f100.jpg)  
There's always an Idol very close to a boss fight. You'll never have to fight your way through lots of opponents if you lose to one of them.

![](images/0bec3220aea52053184a930f200a6894b5119383ebf7fd59043861b6f9e42c87.jpg)  
Preparation is key. Use the Homeward Idol to return to the Dilapidated Temple and upgrade your Tools before tackling a difficult battle.

![](images/70bae2eabc6aba7c38a1fbf68f40792e72073e4e6e1e4933d84f5b2c1158924d.jpg)  
You can jump and then grapple in mid-air.

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Grapple Points</td></tr><tr><td>Mountable</td><td>A green, circular Grapple Point designates one that can be stood on afterwards.</td></tr><tr><td>Unmountable</td><td>A triangle designates an unmountable Grapple Point that cannot be stood on. This generates momentum in the direction you were travelling. Certain larger enemies can be grappled onto in order to quickly close the distance and land a powerful Grappling Hook Attack once you have unlocked the requisite skill in the Prosthetic Arts skill tree. As you come into range the grey circle will fill out, and eventually turn green when you can grapple onto it.</td></tr><tr><td>Incorrect Angle</td><td>If a cross is drawn through the Grapple Point, then there is an obstacle in the way preventing you from grappling, so you need to move into a better position.</td></tr></table>

# Sprinting (B/©)

By holding down  $\widehat{\mathbf{B}} /\widehat{\mathbf{C}}$  while moving in any direction, you'll first perform a step dodge and then automatically shift to a sprint, greatly increasing your movement speed on the ground. There is no way to go from running to sprinting directly; the step dodge is built in. From a sprint you can perform a unique attack, which we'll cover in the Attacks section (P.19).

![](images/00556c627e8133aafa4387d83dcb4362625649c5abe9d8350ebc692fb7f07e91.jpg)

Sprinting makes you extremely mobile. Use it to charge into battle, to outmaneuver your opponents, or to make a swift retreat.

# Jumping  $(\mathbf{A} / \otimes)$

By pressing  $\mathbf{A} / \otimes$ , you can perform a jump. Outside of navigating between platforms and rooftops, jumping is an indispensable tool during combat situations to close distance, evade attacks and create distance from enemies. By sprinting before jumping you can greatly increase the distance of your jump. This is called a sprint jump. As mentioned previously, you can also grapple while jumping and attack with your katana. The jumping attack is covered in the Attacks section on P.19.

![](images/430d2ac8d99e12d10876d7cda323c8978b0b1cc136267c48e478e72c9b51ca00.jpg)

By jumping at a wall, and then pressing  $\mathbf{x} / \mathbf{0}$  again, you can jump off it. Aside from gaining extra height and allowing you to gain access to rooftops and ledges that would otherwise be inaccessible, this can be very useful as an escape tool when surrounded by enemies. In very specific parts of the game, you can perform a Consecutive Wall Jump by continually jumping off of two parallel walls to reach a higher location.

![](images/e001fc08d4a736ebc9dc27accd1ea8fd0dd5bb0634907f9e60a3ffeac1a3e11d.jpg)

You'll need to wall jump in order to leave the area where you begin the game.

# Ledge Hang (x/while jumping near a ledge)

By holding  $\mathbf{x} / \odot$  while in mid-air near a ledge, you can grab on and hang from it. When standing close to a ledge or a beam, you can also press  $\mathbf{x} / \odot$  to directly drop down and grab onto it. You don't need to be directly facing the ledge in order to grab it from mid-air, so on the narrow, multi-tiered roofs of Ashina Castle, for example, you can be facing away from a roof and still perform a jumping grab.

While Ledge Hanging, you can shimmy to the left and right by moving in that direction. If you are beneath an unsuspecting enemy, you can then perform a Ledge Hang Deathblow. This will be explained in more detail later (P.21).

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Ledge Hanging Actions</td></tr><tr><td>B/◎</td><td>Drop Down</td></tr><tr><td>X/◎</td><td>Climb Up</td></tr><tr><td>A/⊗</td><td>Hop Climb</td></tr><tr><td>Hold direction away from ledge + A/⊗</td><td>Somersault Away</td></tr></table>

# Falling

Most areas you'll traverse feature plenty of verticality, so dropping down from elevated terrain is something you'll frequently be doing. Any fall shorter than 20 meters won't cause you to take damage, but bigger drops should be considered hazardous. When at the edge of a platform or elevated location, taking another step forward will only cause you to fall if the drop is shorter than 20 meters. If the drop is tall enough to result in damage, an invisible barrier will prevent you from falling unless you jump or sprint. Using ground-based attacks also prevents you from dropping off ledges, so there's

no need to worry about accidentally falling into a pit when attacking near the edge. Most enemy attacks (and even dying) won't push you off a ledge, but watch out for attacks that feature knockback since they'll send you plummeting down below. If you don't have enough Vitality to survive a fall, you won't be able to resurrect even if Resurrection Nodes are available. The table included in this section displays the consequences of a fall bigger than 20 meters.

Falling into water from above 20 meters will result in half the damage taken compared to landing on a solid surface from the same height. So, for example, after a 30 meter drop you'll incur  $15\%$  damage, not  $30\%$ . This means that dropping into bodies of water from a great height is still dangerous but far less likely to kill you.

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Fall Damage</td></tr><tr><td>Height</td><td>20-39 meters</td></tr><tr><td>Damage</td><td>20% - 39% depending on height</td></tr><tr><td>Reaction</td><td>Three second unrecoverable stun.Falls from this height cannot kill you, so even if you have a sliver of Vitality left before falling, you&#x27;ll survive the fall.</td></tr><tr><td>Height</td><td>40 meters+</td></tr><tr><td>Damage</td><td>40% fixed</td></tr><tr><td>Reaction</td><td>Over 40% Vitality: Restart on the last ledge you stood on.Under 40% Vitality: True death, meaning you cannot resurrect-be careful.</td></tr></table>

# Swimming (R1/R2 to dive)

After entering deep water you'll be able to swim on the surface. While treading water you can jump, attack, dash, guard, deflect and use the Grappling Hook. However, you won't be able to use most items (aside from Goursds and the Homeward Idol) or Prosthetic Tools while in water, nor can you perform advanced actions such as a Mikiri Counter. Do note that jumping while treading water is not very effective, as you'll gain hardly any height. After you've gained the Mibu Breathing Technique, you'll be able to dive underwater and swim freely:

RT/B2  
![](images/d5e85350cfd22ef7225f5521e3933b8c436e8b02f3d7d9881eb0595e1f33878b.jpg)  
Dives down while treading water. When underwater, this also allows you to swim further down.

U/L2  
![](images/ad4c6e39644b1c1d9a1eb1717b9e9a31b5db3430210ee2db0561c9b6d48dcfae.jpg)  
Swims towards the surface while underwater.

A/  
![](images/7a265e845111912b1ab4c1742913a94c404438c86a91b29a4b752c4187045211.jpg)  
Dashes towards the surface. If done near the surface you'll jump out of the water, allowing you to grapple to locations you otherwise can't reach.

B/O  
![](images/a7030d518d09e8517d9f7ee24cfb385494ca9768efe46f0ebac2c2cb9b33976d.jpg)  
Allows you to dash horizontally underwater. This is useful for moving more quickly, or to evade attacks and close distance while engaging in underwater combat.

B/O (Hold Left Stick)  
![](images/2d3961ba9d2c22b930078313a034251911fd960c837cf227e54df47988a6e8c1.jpg)  
Hold the left stick in the direction you want to go for this horizontal dash to have significant range. The attack at the end of a dash is the best way to get rid of Carp and hunt down Treasure Carps.

R3 RB/R1 LB/L1  
![](images/10119666336aac484728e22de68960f5f9eaf51db683c69f3913f4919a75e415.jpg)  
You can also lock on, attack, dashing attack and guard while underwater. Combat while swimming is overall quite limited, however there are some challenging enemies underwater that demand skillful dashing to evade their attacks.

![](images/e357b0161f9c5ca39ef206182c670b161b93ad3095959d1f285093cf0d068bb8.jpg)

# Shinobi Shortcuts

At specific points in the game, you can enter Shinobi Shortcuts to either reach hidden areas or travel across vast stretches of Ashina in an instant. Some are easily identifiable by the rough outline of a human figure, however others are more well-hidden by a scroll on the wall. In order to use a Shinobi Shortcut you either need to hug the wall they are placed onto, or press  $\mathbf{x} / \mathbb{O}$  when directly over/underneath a floorboard shortcut.

# The Mysteries of Ashina

As a game set in the Sengoku period of Japan, elements of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice are rooted in history. However, this is still a fictional universe with many fantastical ideas at the root of the story and setting. Here we'll explain both the ordinary and supernatural aspects of the game's systems.

# Kuro Remnants

While traversing Ashina, you will occasionally see red beams of light coming from the ground. Get close to these and you'll see an apparition of Lord Kuro appear. Interact with the Kuro Remnants to gain a deeper understanding of the story and the central characters' motivations. If you do not interact with Kuro Remnants, they will remain in place up until story events later in the game change the early Ashina areas. Those that you will interact with will eventually disappear as the game progresses.

![](images/282c2cb85b33142e4887128e8cdefe2f9ff25838a4f2d6483e861024f3279364.jpg)

# Spirit Emblems

Spirit Emblems are the resource that govern how often you can use your Prosthetic Tools as well as certain Combat Arts (P.27). You start out being able to carry a maximum of 15, which can be increased through the acquisition of the following Skills: A Shinobi's Karma: Body and Mind, A Sculptor's Karma: Blood and Scars, and A Beast's Karma. Once you've learned all of these Skills, you'll be able to carry a maximum of 20.

Prosthetic Tools are some of the most powerful options at your disposal during combat. Learning effective management of Spirit Emblems is therefore very important. After you've acquired your first Tool or Skill that requires Spirit Emblems, you will occasionally find them while traversing Ashina. Enemies will also sometimes drop them when they die. If you're carrying your maximum amount, additional Spirit Emblems will automatically be sent to your storage box, and as mentioned, if you rest at an Idol you can replenish your stock.

Spirit Emblems can also be bought from any Sculptor's Idol by using the "Purchase Spirit Emblems" option. The starting price is ten Sen per Emblem, but completing certain events within the game will raise this price. However, don't worry too much about this, since the amount of Sen you gain from enemies in later areas will scale accordingly. As a final note, dying does not result in the loss of any currently held Spirit Emblems.

# Cost Increases

SPOILER The change to Noon will increase the price from 10 to 20 Sen per Emblem. Evening increases it further to 30 Sen. Finally, the arrival of Night will bring up the price to 50 Sen.

![](images/c392a79fd99e0ab6633ba7ce34e3481ab37b4118d8523507afc47d9dc80d8f24.jpg)  
These memories provide insight into past events concerning your young master.

![](images/a9719181c1b9d9cf6aefa64e01368af3b1e1f162b196fd2d5170b3301e708ff3.jpg)  
Your stocks of Spirit Emblems are likely to grow as the game progresses.

# Buddha Storage

There is a limit to the number of items that you can carry at any one time. Exactly how many depends on the item in question—check the entries for Consumable Items in the Shinobi Toolkit chapter, starting on P.116 to see each item's carrying limit. Any surplus that you pick up will be sent to your storage box. You can replenish your stocks from this box by resting at a Sculptor's Idol, and your stocks will also be refilled after a true death.

# $\succ$  Ceremonial Tanto

![](images/1c0572bea243c3121848b04c1b99d09c9032790b33572447814be4b893e57984.jpg)

After defeating the Shichimen Warrior in the Abandoned Dungeon, you'll acquire the Ceremonial Tanto. This allows you to sacrifice half of your Vitality for 5 extra Spirit Emblems. These are separate from your regular stock—they allow you to go above the normal

limit, and will automatically be used first. If you have  $50\%$  or under of your Vitality, then the Tanto cannot be used. It has a maximum of three uses before you need to replenish it at a Sculptor's Idol.

# Night Eyes

An innate ability, Night Eye allows the Wolf to see clearly even in the darkest of places. Both a distinct chime and the unnatural glow of Wolf's eyes let you know it's active once you step foot in a dark area.

The Tanto is a very useful tool, and you shouldn't forget about it. Generating some extra Emblems before a battle in which you're certain to use your Prosthetic Tools can be a great help, especially since you can heal after using it.

![](images/0ef58c861ad18a41b0f88ec073d212d20954f5cd6027a013295b90e83404769d.jpg)

Once you have some highly upgraded Prosthetic Tools the Tanto is invaluable.

# Death

# >Resurrection

Thanks to the Divine Heir's blood that flows through Sekiro's veins, you have the power of resurrection at your fingertips. Upon death, press RB/ R to resurrect with half of your Vitality bar recovered. Pressing LB/L instead will result in a true death, as will waiting too long until the screen fades to black.

# Revenge

You can use death to your advantage. After you're killed, most normal enemies will think you are dead and naturally turn away. At this point you can resurrect, sneak up behind them and exact your bloody revenge. This is especially effective since Backstab Deathblows give access to devastating Ninjutsu techniques (P.27), allowing you take out entire groups of enemies in one fell swoop. Just take care not to wait too long, otherwise the screen will turn black and you will face true death. Also note that bosses and sub-bosses cannot be deceived into a Backstab Deathblow in this way, as they are immediately alerted when you resurrect near them.

The number of times you can resurrect is denoted by Resurrection Nodes, which are the pink orbs above your Vitality gauge. The first node, displaying a flower, can be recharged by resting at a Sculptor's Idol. The second node, displaying a leaf, needs to first be filled up by killing enemies. Exactly how much gets filled depends on the enemy that you kill. A regular enemy has a  $30\%$  chance to fill  $2 - 7\%$ , but strong enemies and sub-bosses are guaranteed to fill up  $12\%$  and  $67\%$  respectively.

These nodes will only appear after the first time you die, at which point the screen will fade to black, and you will hear Lord Kuro's voice instructing you to arise. That means if you never die, it is entirely possible to go through the entire game without any Resurrection Nodes above your Vitality Gauge. This stands as a lofty challenge to any skilled Shinobi who dares tackle it. After resurrecting there is a lock-out period before a subsequent node can be used. The lock-out is removed as soon as you regain resurrection potential from any source. This includes Deathblowing bosses and

![](images/5543adc6f64e387da8d66a01164f4ff265a0abcc23f8dc8caf805183d400f45d.jpg)

After dying you can choose to either truly die or to resurrect on the spot.

![](images/6f0ad81c1a36fa2ed13acf2e7454e73a6d85adc9066073ab81d30fe9e9a2835c.jpg)

A black ink stroke through your Resurrection Nodes means they are locked-out. Performing a Deathblow on sub-bosses and bosses always recovers a bit of Resurrective Power and removes the lock-out.

mid-bosses, drops from normal enemies, and consuming a Dragons Blood Droplet. A Bundled Jizo Statue will instantly remove the lock-out for secondary leaf nodes as well as restoring one fully. Do be careful though, as it cannot remove the lock-out from your first death when you lose the flower node. Use these items wisely, as they are quite rare, especially during your first playthrough.

# A Third Node

SPOILER After receiving the Sahara Droplet by defeating Lady Butterfly, then defeating Genichiro in Ashina Castle, you can give Lord Kuro the Sahara Droplet when you find him in the library. He'll use it to bestow a third Resurrection Node upon you, that operates the same as the second one. The Sahara Droplet can also be given to the Divine Child of Rejuvenation in Senpou Temple for the same effect.

# >Unseen Aid

![](images/77ba916d45ca0fdc126b03888ebbf364a5658cfa4cd749ea51679292adc03c37.jpg)

If you run out of Resurrection Nodes, or press [LB/L] after dying, you'll face true death. Afterwards, you'll awaken at the last communed Idol with half of your Sen gone, and half of the Skill EXP removed for the Skill Point you are currently on the way to attaining points you have already earned will remain.

There is a chance, however, that you'll be blessed by the favor of Buddha, through Unseen Aid. At its maximum, this is a  $30\%$  chance to avoid losing any Sen or Skill EXP upon true death. Resurrection extracts a heavy toll on your surroundings, particularly those who are known to you. With every true death there's also a chance that Dragonrot will overflow and contaminate NPCs. This is signified by the addition of a Rot Essence to your Key Items inventory.

# > Dragonrot

The first victim of Dragonrot will always be the Sculptor. Every other NPC has a different probability of being contaminated: NPCs cannot die as a result of Dragonrot, but the more Dragonrot Essence in your Inventory, the lower the chance of receiving Unseen Aid, and it will also halt progress on the NPC's questline. With one

Rot Essence it is halved, and with every subsequent Rot Essence it goes down by a further  $2\%$ . The minimum Unseen Aid can go down to is  $1\%$ , which requires all 17 susceptible NPCs to be both alive and contaminated. It cannot be increased beyond  $30\%$ . It is entirely possible to both contaminate an NPC with Dragonrot and also receive Unseen Aid with the same true death.

# > Dragon's Blood Droplets

![](images/f0fdf08aa19ecf85970c6c834b679a40e5c496dd276e772d4df6f5049ad99a35.jpg)

Once an NPCs is suffering from Dragonrot, you can talk to Emma about it and she'll send you to collect a blood sample from someone afflicted with it, so she can try to find a cure. Once a second NPC contracts the illness, you'll be able to bring her the sample and you a Recovery Charm the next time you talk to her. In your possession, you can use Dragon's Blood Droplets or's Idol to instantly heal everyone afflicted with Dragon's Blood Droplets are rare items, so use them wisely.

![](images/f1383378c96ecff5420dccf8076bceacae048165667f858c9d100043a1de2eb3.jpg)  
A single death can lead to multiple characters being afflicted with Dragonrot.

After a case of Dragonrot has occurred, the number of times you would have to die again for another case to occur will vary depending on whether or not you cured the previous person. If you didn't, then you would need to die a further 10 times before someone else becomes afflicted, but if you did, it would only take six deaths. Once someone has become inflicted with Dragonrot and cured, they will be immune to contracting it again until you defeat any boss (other than Gyoubu Oniwa or Lady Butterfly).

![](images/6c8640a72953712a84a812394c3e8355474a5f439ef990240a87c12cf72970c3.jpg)

# Sen

Sen was the currency used in Japan during the Sengoku period in which this game is set. It can be looted from enemies and is an invaluable resource that allows you to purchase items from peddlers as well as upgrade your Prosthetic Tools at the Sculptor.

Since there's a real risk of losing your Sen every time you die, it is advisable to purchase coin purses whenever you see merchants sell them. The mark up price is negligible, and these effectively operate as a bank, since they will not be lost upon death. Particularly before facing a tough challenge such as a boss, it's highly recommended that you either spend as much Sen as you can on items, Tool upgrades and Spirit Emblems, or convert them into coin purses.

# Acquiring Loot

When an enemy has been defeated they will usually drop an item as well as some Sen. You don't need to manually go over and pick up all the loot scattered on the battlefield—by holding  $\times / \square$  you can activate a vacuum effect to collect them from afar for convenience.

$\mathbf{x} / \odot$  doesn't need to be held down for the entire duration of the loot getting sucked in. Once you've held it down enough to trigger the vacuum effect, you can let go and it will still come towards you. Neither the sound that the vacuum effect makes, nor the loot flying in can be detected by enemies, so you can use it safely while sneaking around.

![](images/26e8bb690896bf913b213f99ee054b21682e0108ce35d0fb0ad6df40692f50a2.jpg)  
Items that weren't dropped by defeated enemies will need to be sought out and manually picked up.

![](images/cff1a7e224515e37a9cc2e8aabb928cfb59d66f060d80d6ef77fa8e066a72a09.jpg)  
If someone becomes afflicted with Dragonrot, you'll need to find a Dragon's Blood Droplet at a peddler to cure them.

![](images/17e9d379be607edbb7eef1d6dd33ca629125ce19341e2043f86a9e5f3637696a.jpg)  
Always look for merchants selling Coin Purses so you can keep your Sen safe.

You'll find that some enemies have unique item drops, and these will occur only the first time you kill them. For sub-bosses, this is often a valuable Prayer Bead, but these items will not drop a second time on New Game+; instead, these enemies will drop something different. For more on this, see the Progression and Analysis chapter, starting on P.498.

# >Offering Box

If you ever miss any key items during the course of your adventure, and access to them is blocked, for example if an NPC offering a key item dies, then they will appear in the Offering Box. Check it occasionally, especially if you feel you have missed something.

![](images/8883716cb4b227e8cd835fdacff9052825617aada9e9d6ef0e4ce9a503e186e9.jpg)  
Once the vacuum effect has been activated, you will see a gust of wind appear around Sekiro accompanied by a sound effect

# Stealth

Being a Shinobi, fighting enemies straight on is not always advisable, especially if there's a group of them. Use the shadows and stealth to your advantage to whittle down enemy numbers before directly engaging those that remain.

# Alert Indicator

Alert Indicators  

<table><tr><td>NO ICON</td><td>Unaware</td><td>°Calm</td><td>Caution</td><td>Alert</td></tr></table>

If you're trying to be stealthy, then what your enemies can see and hear is your primary concern. Luckily, an enemy's current ability to detect you is codified into an on-screen alertness indicator that is simple to understand. When you see a triangle above an enemy's head, that means they're aware of your presence to some degree. When the enemy is calm, the triangle is either empty or not present at all. If they hear or see something suspicious, the triangle will fill yellow. When it's fully yellow the enemy will enter caution status, signified by a sound played on a shamisen, and they'll move to check the disturbance. Finally, as you are closer to getting spotted the triangle will fill red. When spotted, a tribal roar and some battle

# Sentries

Sentries are weak enemies who act as lookouts. They have better vision than other enemies and will use a gong to alert others if they spot you. When using stealth to approach an area, watch out for Sentries and prioritize sneaking up on them.

# Verticality

Staying directly above the enemy's head makes it harder for them to spot you. Enemies see within a cone of vision, so the higher you are above them, the less likely you are to be seen. Use the verticality of the areas as well as your wide array of mobility options to their full advantage.

![](images/fa67c9d7e802693d1e59cb72efe21f5a0b881d3562b397ed935e0e0ab4bfb975.jpg)

music will signify the enemy going into full alert. A single enemy going into alert status does not mean that all nearby enemies will immediately go into alert. However, if you engage them, the commotion of swords clashing and gunfire will quickly attract their attention and you may soon find yourself overwhelmed. Sentries are an exception to this—once alert, they'll bang on a gong and all nearby enemies will go into a caution state and begin walking in the sentry's direction. The Sentry will keep the enemies in caution state, making it difficult to sneak up on them.

When the enemy is under alert, be very careful about engaging a group, especially if there are Archers or Riflemen supporting them, as they will continually be able to interrupt your attacks. It's often better to use your mobility, especially with the Grappling Hook, to escape their line of sight. Once enemies lose sight of you, they'll go from alert back down to caution and then eventually become calm again and return to their normal positions. You can then reposition yourself behind the enemies and continue picking off targets with Backstab Deathblows.

![](images/ce8f4f088d4d8dee0ffcbfe5d9d67672949268f02f7400dd1522d740400d3de0.jpg)

When not directly looking at an enemy, the triangles will circle around you as a sort of threat radar to give you a better sense of your surroundings.

# Tall Grass

In many areas throughout the game you'll come across patches of tall grass or flowers that, when crouched in, will obscure you from enemy vision. By moving through these you can navigate the battlefield to either sneak past enemies, or move to advantageous positions form which to launch an assault. Even if you're already in combat, using items or tools such as Fistful of Ash or Shinobi Firecrackers to blind your opponent will allow you to break line of sight, and then hide in some tall grass to reset the engagement if you were in trouble. Note that fire-based attacks can burn the tall grass and leave you exposed, so be careful.

# Crouching

Crouching reduces your visibility and audibility; the edges of the screen will go black to represent this. You may find it surprising just how close to an enemy you can get while crouching, even in broad daylight, as long as they are calm. Crouching while in tall grass will reduce your visibility even further. The enemy will need to be right in front of you in order to spot you. This makes it very easy to creep behind them and perform a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/872c515daeca9a55e7befcfc72affe24a00a19ba901ebc04f8ad05d9dae5813f.jpg)  
The edges of the screen go dark when you're crouching to show that you are very hard to spot.

# Wall Hugging

Wall hugging operates similarly to crouching in that it drastically reduces your visibility. You can also perform a unique Deathblow from a Wall Hug when an unsuspecting enemy tries to turn the corner.

# Luring

You can lure in enemies by throwing Ceramic Shards at them in order to get their attention. This will put them in caution status, and they will move in the direction in which the shard was thrown. You can then quickly reposition yourself and creep behind them to land a Stealth Deathblow. Do be careful, as the sound that a Ceramic Shard makes will often attract an entire group of nearby enemies, so you often need to be quite some distance away from before throwing one.

Later in the game you'll get the Finger Whistle, which allows you to separate a single enemy from a group by locking onto them before using the Whistle. All the applications of the Finger Whistle are covered in more detail in the Shinobi Toolkit chapter (P.114).

# Eavesdropping

You can eavesdrop on unsuspecting Ashina Soldiers by locking onto them and then pressing down on the directional pad. This will often give you valuable intel to help you beat tough upcoming enemies, as well as providing information for Vendors, such as Peddler Ayanama. You can also eavesdrop on certain important friendly NPCs, such as Lord Kuro and Isshin. Some of these eavesdrops are tied to unlocking endings. Please see the Sensitive Information chapter on P.580 for more detail.

![](images/f03478d8a0c371e4c969abf082574d2393b3257600f6dfc674478c2d4572d7bd.jpg)

# Combat

Combat in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice is quite unlike any other game. There are many intricacies and systems at play here, often with subtly interlocking mechanics, which won't be initially apparent. Understanding and eventual mastery of these mechanics will be crucial if you hope to see this journey through to its end.

# Hanbei the Undying

On the path to the right of the Dilapidated Temple, you'll find a lone immortal samurai by the name of Hanbei the Undying, who will challenge you to a simple duel. Upon defeating him, and then accepting his offer, he will act as a tutor to the fundamentals of combat. At first there are only three tutorials available; Attacks, Deflect and Step Dodge. Once you complete these, Fundamentals Free Combat becomes available. Upon completing this, more advanced tutorials become available, covering Consecutive Deflections, Vitality and Posture, Countering Thrust Attacks, and finally Countering Sweep Attacks. Once you have completed these, Applied Free Combat becomes available. After gaining the Mikiri Counter and Vault Over skills from the Shinobi Arts skill tree, Hanbei will also cover the usage of them.

Hanbei also offers you a safe space on which to test strategies, Tools and Combat Arts. He is an extremely important resource and we strongly recommend spending the time to go through his lessons

# Lock On

Situational awareness on the battlefield is key. Before anything else, you will need to be able to comfortably track and target surrounding enemies. While there is an Auto-target function that allows you to track nearby enemies that you are currently attacking even with no manual lock (this can be toggled on and off in the Options menu, though we highly recommend you keep it on), being able to track an enemy from a distance is crucial. A manual lock on will allow you to strafe around the enemy from any range, thereby making all your actions in relation to them far more accurate.

A manual lock can be activated by pressing in the right analogue stick. You can release the lock and go back to free movement by pressing it in again. When the former target dies, the lock on will then pass onto the next closest target (this can also be toggled in the Options menu), however a quicker way to change target is by flicking the right analogue stick in the direction of the enemy you want to target.

Knowing when to lock on to an enemy and when to move freely is very important. A general rule of thumb is that when you're focused on taking down a single enemy, you should lock on to them so that you can target and position yourself around them more accurately. In nearly all one-on-one encounters, locking on to the enemy should be the first thing you do. It's also essential to aim at your target when using ranged attacks, such as the Loaded Shuriken and Ceramic Shards. However, when dealing with a large group of enemies and using attacks focused on crowd control, you should avoid locking on, so that the direction of your attack isn't influenced by the movement of a single enemy.

and practice the art of combat. For more information on Hanbei, please see P.566.

Locking on is essential when targeting fast-moving enemies with Shuriken.

![](images/eb6f8bd07ae57663a4d54ddd6b1b61ed59c3a299c75cbb92593920fcf08215f8.jpg)  
When using a Combat Art to hit multiple enemies, it's sometimes better not to lock on.

Kusabimaru is your katana, given to you by Lord Kuro in the Prologue of the game. This is your primary method of attack, and mastering it is absolutely essential to your success. Pressing (RB) / (R) will perform various types of katana attack depending on the state you're in.

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Basic Attack Variations</td></tr><tr><td>Basic Attack</td><td>Pressing RB/R1 will lead to a basic attack while standing, walking or running in any direction.</td></tr><tr><td>Sprint Attack</td><td>Attack while sprinting; hold B/◎ then press RB/R1.</td></tr><tr><td>Step Dodge Attack</td><td>Attack after a step dodge; tap B/◎ then press RB/R1.</td></tr><tr><td>Jump Attack</td><td>Attack while jumping; press A/⊗ then press RB/R1.</td></tr><tr><td>Thrust Attack</td><td>Hold down RB/R1 and then release.</td></tr><tr><td>Counter-Slash/Guard-pressuringSlash</td><td>Deflect with LB/L1 or strike an enemy&#x27;s guard then quickly press RB/R1.</td></tr><tr><td>Prosthetic Follow-Up</td><td>Use a Prosthetic Tool with RT/R2 then press RB/R1 (specific Skills required).</td></tr></table>

# > Basic Attack (RB/R1)

Pressing  $\mathbb{R}\mathbb{B} / \mathbb{R}\mathbb{I}$  will lead to a fast, basic strike with Kusabimaru. Continue pressing  $\mathbb{R}\mathbb{B} / \mathbb{R}\mathbb{I}$  to trigger further strikes, up to a five-hit combo, before restarting from the beginning again. It's rare that you will ever need to use all five hits, other than when an enemy is stuck in a lengthy stun animation. If an enemy guards one of your attacks, you will instead perform a guard-pressuring slash.

Generally an attack in this game is a commitment; you cannot cancel during an attack into evasive or defensive maneuvers such as a step dodge or jump. This means you should pick your moments to attack very carefully, especially given how damaging enemy attacks can be. There are two notable exceptions to this:

Guard Cancelling: By pressing guard in the initial stages of your basic attack, you can cancel the first two hits of the katana combo into a guard. This has to be early on in the animation; once you are actually attacking it can no longer be cancelled. This also allows you to cancel into a deflect, allowing you to play much more aggressively.

Deathblows: Deathblows are completely invulnerable, and as soon as the red Deathblow target is active on screen, you can cancel any attack into it by pressing RB/R1. Deathblows are covered in much more detail later.

While you can perform these actions in between the strikes of the basic five hit combo, you will need to wait for each strike to fully recover first. This means you should pick your moments to attack very carefully, especially given how damaging enemy attacks can be.

Even normal enemies are incredibly aggressive and tend to attack in groups, so repeatedly striking a single foe will leave your back wide open to attack. Tougher enemies will never allow you to slash away continually with no repercussions; they will either plough through your ongoing attacks with an armored attack, deflect and then counter-attack or simply evade and punish. Instead, keep your offense tight and compact. Try to develop the habit of placing

# Camera

Another integral part of maintaining situational awareness is through moving the camera. The camera can be controlled via the right analogue stick. Under the Options menu you can change the direction of both the X and Y-axis, as well as the camera speed. If there is no Lock On target within range, pressing in the right analogue stick will instead reset the camera to behind you.

If your back is against a wall, the camera will move above your head, obstructing your view of enemies directly in front of you, as well as their incoming attacks. This can be a very dangerous situation, so it's best to stay away from walls when in combat, so that you can see the enemy clearly at all times. If you do find yourself with your back against the wall, repositioning yourself with a jump or wall jump, well-timed step dodge, or dedicated Prosthetic Tool such as Mist Raven should be an absolute priority.

thought and intentionality behind every single action that you take; never just press the attack button out of panic or confusion, as this is a sure-fire road to failure. Keep your mind primed and ready to react to incoming danger. We will go into more detail on when to attack and when to hold back in the Swordplay section on P.27.

![](images/64622b697084a7a010c997c02b72beb06261ed893f793dc94c48cebede756ee3.jpg)  
Against weak enemies, basic attacks quickly lead to a Deathblow opportunity.

# > Sprint Attack (RB/R) while sprinting)

Attacking while sprinting will make you swing your katana with a much wider radius than your basic attack, making it effective against groups of enemies. Despite the sprinting attack being slower than your basic attack, it deals the same damage.

# > Step Dodge Attack (RB/R1 after dodging)

After a step dodge you can press the attack button to perform a dodging counter-attack. This is essentially identical to the wide horizontal slash that you can perform during a sprint. It's the ideal move with which to punish the enemy after you've evaded their attack with a step dodge.

# > Jump Attack (RB/R1 while jumping)

The jumping attack is very weak, dealing only  $25\%$  of the damage of your basic attack, but it's very quick, so it can be good to interrupt an enemy's attack while jumping towards them from a distance. It's also guaranteed to connect in certain situations such as after jump kick is used to counter a sweep attack. This is covered in more detail in the Perilous Attack section (P.28).

# > Thrust Attack (hold RB/R1)

By holding down  $\underline{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{R}\mathbb{I}$  you can perform a thrust attack. While a thrust takes considerably longer to execute, it has some key advantages. It is  $50\%$  more powerful than your basic attack, boasts longer range and cannot be guarded. This makes it effective against certain defensive enemies and a strong tool to punish an enemy's missed attack.

Of the basic five hit combo, only the first two strikes can be charged into a thrust. From the third to the fifth you can only perform the basic attack until the string resets. While charging you can release RB/At any time, resulting in a basic attack. You need to fully charge it all the way to perform a thrust.

A thrust can be performed directly from a sprint. You can also transition from a sprint or step dodge attack directly into a thrust early on in the animation by first tapping  $\underline{\mathbb{R}} / \mathbb{R}$  and then holding it down. This can be useful to quickly change your attack on the fly if you notice that the enemy is more vulnerable than you initially thought.

Aside from its slow speed, the other major weakness of the thrust attack is its susceptibility to being deflected, which will leave you in a disadvantageous situation. We will explore deflection in much more detail later in this section.

![](images/c3878156949e90fb9579c8f4171c08b1ad47e2dfc7e42745bc538fbfc6f7b984.jpg)  
Thrusts are slow to charge, but use them while an enemy is recovering...

![](images/5072408318d1ac8c8ff310b5de0fd8dbdff1edda05cfb40d1705d715c9c113a9.jpg)  
...And they'll inflict  $50\%$  more damage than your basic attack.

# > Counter-Slash (RB/R1 quickly after deflecting)

After deflecting an enemy's attack you can immediately follow-up with a counter-slash. This deals  $50\%$  more Posture damage than a basic attack, and is a powerful tool with which to pressure the enemy. Be sure to read the Posture section of this chapter if you want to understand the full significance of this (P.22). Counter-slashes are a powerful technique, so practice getting into the rhythm of pressing the attack button immediately after deflecting an attack or striking an enemy's guard to put your opponent on the back foot or take advantage of openings.

As with any other tool, though, there is a proper time and place to time to use counter-slashes. Just because you can counter-slash right after a deflect, doesn't mean you always should. Certain attacks won't put the enemy into a reeling stun when they are deflected; they will simply keep on going. In instances like this, performing a counter-slash will only get you hurt. You should also avoid using them against armored attacks, as they will simply power through the counter-slash. The effectiveness of counter-slashes preceded by a deflect are directly enhanced by the Descending Carp Skill in the Ashina Arts skill tree.

It's generally safe to perform a single guard-pressuring slash whenever one of your strikes has been guarded, but be careful not to carelessly push your offense, as attempting a counter-slash after being deflected will leave you highly vulnerable—at this point you should stop your offense immediately, and go on the defensive with either a guard, deflect, step dodge or Mist Raven. Always be sure to carefully monitor how the enemy is reacting to every single one of your strikes, and adapt your actions accordingly.

# >Prosthetic Follow-up

Unlocking the Chasing Slice, Fang and Blade, Projected Force, and Living Force Skills found in the Shinobi and Prosthetic Arts skill trees, will allow you to follow the use of a Prosthetic Tool with a slash from your katana. These moves have a wide variety of uses and applications, and are covered in detail in the Prosthetic Tools section, starting on P.80.

![](images/e02b142cf39299ab639ebf19c066a920e5c7f63566cdb403813102b6d257474d.jpg)  
Chasing Slice lets you quickly close the gap with a powerful sword slash after throwing a Shuriken.

By tapping 5/while moving the left analogue stick in any direction, you will perform a step dodge. This will allow you to avoid attacks that cover a linear area. Though there is a period of invulnerability right at the start of the dodge, it is quite small, which means you need to dodge precisely. For example, if the enemy is using a wide horizontal attack, you need to look carefully at their animation and see from which side of their body they are striking, then dodge toward that side just before the attack would hit you.

Step dodging is particularly useful against vertical attacks, since you can dodge many of them in either direction. Enemies who use a lot of linear, downward strikes, such as the Samurai Fencer, are

![](images/cfc9206222573c351472c691ee1190a1d56f698d5ae3e4c18644c2606d244880.jpg)  
Some enemies are far more easily dodged than others.

# Deathblows

A Deathblow allows you to instantly remove a Deathblow Marker, or kill an enemy that has no Deathblow Markers, with a single, lethal strike. The vast majority of your kills will come as a result of a Deathblow. They are the ultimate reward for either successfully sneaking up on an enemy or overcoming them in close range combat—either by depleting their Vitality or Posture gauge. We'll explore the interplay between Vitality and Posture in the next section.

When an enemy is susceptible to a Deathblow, you'll see a red target on their body. Pressing the attack button when you see this will instantly cancel any attack you are performing and initiate the Deathblow.

# Deathblow Markers

Tougher enemies will generally have more than one Vitality gauge. The number of red markers above the enemy's Vitality indicates the number of Deathblows required to kill them.

While performing a Deathblow you are completely invulnerable, so if you see the red target, be sure to take your chance and dispatch the enemy then and there, even if you are surrounded. Taking advantage of this invulnerability is key to whittling down large groups of enemies down to more manageable numbers. How long a Deathblow target is active depends on how you've broken the enemy's Posture. After a Deflect it is active for less than a second, but if the enemy is Posture-broken by an attack, it will last for over three seconds.

very susceptible to being step dodged for this reason. Once you successfully dodge through an enemy attack, you'll often find yourself at their back, particularly if their attack had a lot of forward momentum. This will very often allow you to land a step dodge attack. Also, as mentioned previously, by holding  $\Theta / \Theta$  you can transition from a step dodge into a sprint.

# Step Dodge Cancel

After step dodging you are left in a vulnerable recovery state. There is, however, a brief window in which you can still guard, despite not being able to perform any other action. This means that guarding immediately after a step dodge can save you from taking damage in certain situations. Be sure not to hold  $\underline{\mathbb{B}} /\underline{\mathbb{L}}$  during the step dodge animation; instead press it at the end, otherwise the guard cancel will not work.

You can also use this cancelling technique to chain multiple step dodges one after another, much more quickly than if you were just pressing  $\mathbb{B} / \mathbb{O}$ . Learning the timing and rhythm of when to guard cancel at the end of a step dodge is crucial here. This same principle can also be applied to many Combat Arts and Prosthetic Tools to shorten the recovery, making them safer to use and allowing you to avoid taking what would be otherwise guaranteed damage. With certain techniques, such as Praying Strikes, it is an absolutely vital part of using the move properly. Please see the Prosthetics and Skills sections for more information on how guard canceling can benefit certain moves.

![](images/4b95be998934dc2d37fcd5c3b93b443ff9a10c3d059055db94348d35a6b38ee1.jpg)  
You are completely invulnerable during a Deathblow.

![](images/ee0e5aa01ae95769bc3e2ab116a5c536b951754bcaabcde5ce6f9d9dad30b72f.jpg)  
Deathblow Markers are displayed as circles above the enemy's Vitality gauge.

# > Finisher Deathblows

Against bosses, after you deplete their last Deathblow Marker you'll see another opportunity for a Deathblow shortly after. This is a Finisher Deathblow, and as the name implies, they will allow you to vanquish the boss for good with a unique, cinematic Deathblow. These are very easy to perform, and the timing is in no way strict—they simply provide a satisfying, cinematic end to an arduous battle. Just be ready for them, and make sure not to put your controller down and rest on your laurels immediately after depleting the last Deathblow Marker. If you wait too long, you will be forced to resume fighting the boss.

# > Stealth Deathsblows

When an enemy is not alert to your presence, sneaking up behind them and pressing attack will perform a Stealth Deathblow. This will instantly kill regular enemies, and if you manage to sneak up on a strong enemy or sub-boss, you'll remove one of their Deathblow markers; some sub-bosses will be immediately alerted to your presence if you try to sneak up to them, however.

There are four varieties of Stealth Deathblow:

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Stealth Deathblow</td></tr><tr><td>Backstab Deathblow</td><td>Sneak up behind an enemy. Allows you to perform powerful Ninjutsu techniques after.</td></tr><tr><td>Ledge Hang Deathblow</td><td>Shimmy underneath an enemy while hanging from a ledge.</td></tr><tr><td>Wall Hug Deathblow</td><td>Hug a wall and deathblow an enemy when they come passing by. This cannot be performed on larger enemies such as Taro Troopers.</td></tr><tr><td>Plunging Deathblow</td><td>Jump from a height onto an unsuspecting enemy. This can be quite tricky to land, so be sure to Lock-On to an enemy before jumping down onto them.</td></tr></table>

Of all these Stealth Deathblows, Plunging Deathblows are by far the loudest and will often alert many nearby enemies.

# Vitality and Posture

One of the most initially challenging, but ultimately rewarding, aspects of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice is understanding the interplay between Vitality and Posture. Let's first start with Vitality as it's easier to understand, operating very similar to a health bar in other games.

# > Vitality

Vitality damage is inflicted by landing attacks. If an attack is guarded then it will deal no Vitality damage, however, attacks with special properties such as Piercing, Fire or Spirit will be able to penetrate an enemy's guard to varying degrees, and Thrust attacks cannot be guarded at all. Status Abnormalities, such as Poison or Burn inflict ongoing Vitality damage. Most enemies cannot recover their Vitality once it has been depleted. You, however, have

![](images/195c8347f7797da9cb1facb06740649e9b8014d97b5f7dfd441d7009d46ede97.jpg)  
Luring enemies is often required for Wall Hug Deathblows to work.

![](images/45793dda17a6450576192bfdb647c1c65be71c9f288b3184122b03f1a4db3d48.jpg)  
Plunging Deathblows can also be performed by jumping on top of enemies with short statures, such as Centipedes and Sentries.

![](images/27450e6cdbeca7cc37c469c475fb21506f5280c9ca61eb4aa995c3b2edd70736.jpg)  
The Ledge Hang Deathblow requires you to learn an enemy's patrol route.

a variety of consumable items at your disposal to recover Vitality, the most prominent of which is the Healing Gourd. We'll go into more detail on healing later (P.24). It is rare to defeat most enemies simply by chipping away at their Vitality, and the coming entries in this section will explain why that is.

# >Posture

Posture damage, in comparison to Vitality damage, is inflicted regardless of whether attacks are guarded or not. In most games, if you see that an enemy is guarding your attack then you should generally stop, but here, attacking an enemy's guard is still very much in your favor. The more an enemy guards your attacks, the more Posture damage will be inflicted.

# Posture Break

When a Posture gauge is close to being broken it will flash orange, and once it's maxed out the enemy will stagger. This is called a Posture break, and leaves them vulnerable to Deathblows. Breaking an enemy's Posture is generally much easier and more practical than simply depleting their Vitality. This is why the vast majority of your kills will be the result of a Posture break.

Something that may come as a surprise is that Posture actually recovers fastest while guarding. Think of it as steeling your defense, or bracing yourself. This the opposite of how stamina replenishment works in many other games. We will cover guarding in more detail soon.

Bosses only regain Posture when they aren't actively attacking. Essentially, their Posture recovery is halted whenever they perform an action that isn't purely movement related. For the player, however, Posture recovery is also paused during movement options such as step dodging, sprinting and jumping.

# Posture Regeneration

Some powerful opponents also have a specific move that covers their body in a blue aura. They generally only perform this after their Posture has taken significant damage. This blue aura, if uninterrupted, will recover a great deal of Posture. It is vital that you interrupt this with either a quick basic attack if you are at close range, or a Shuriken from afar.

# > The Link between Vitality and Posture

Vitality and Posture are inextricably linked. In most cases, especially against tougher enemies like bosses, you won't be targeting just their Vitality or their Posture, but a combination of the two. The reason for this is that by reducing an enemy's Vitality, you also reduce the rate at which they recover Posture:

<table><tr><td>Vitality Gauge</td><td>Posture Recovery Rate</td></tr><tr><td>100% - 80%</td><td>Fast (black)</td></tr><tr><td>79% - 60%</td><td>Medium (yellow)</td></tr><tr><td>59% - 40%</td><td>Slow (orange)</td></tr><tr><td>39% - 0%</td><td>Very Slow (red)</td></tr></table>

This means that against tougher enemies, battles will broadly take a two-stage process; in the first you will deploy tactics designed around reducing their Vitality. Once this has been reduced to roughly 79 to  $60\%$ , you can then start more aggressively targeting their Posture, aiming to break their Posture and land the deciding Deathblow. In the Opposing Forces chapter (P.344), you'll find that this is a common recurring tactic.

![](images/873facb9f32d11aa26475471ff20dc6a24195105093465d32e2424fa62c09454.jpg)

# Healing

Since Vitality directly determines the rate of Posture recovery, keeping your own Vitality gauge as high as possible has extra importance in Sekiro. Healing is crucial, but you'll also need to take care when trying to heal; many healing items, such as the Healing Gourd or Pellets, take a long time to use and leave you completely vulnerable while doing so. Trying to heal at the wrong time is at best wasteful, and at worst fatal. This means that finding or creating the right opportunity to heal should always be kept in mind during combat. Use jumps or grapples to move to a safe distance before healing, and make sure you're not in the sights of any riflemen or archers.

Against most bosses or sub-bosses, a barrier will prevent you from escaping to heal, and even against the few that don't have such a barrier, straying too far from them will result in their Vitality gauges being completely replenished. Against certain bosses no distance is safe, as some have very fast and long-reaching attacks, or can fill the screen with large area-of-effect attacks. Here it's recommended to first blind them momentarily with Firecrackers or a Fistful of Ash before healing. Once you have used the Healing Gourd, a follow-up swig is much faster than normal. This is
