# The Bell Demon

The Bell Demon is a Demon Spirit sealed within the Iron Bell of Senpou Temple. Ringing the bell will place the Bell Demon in your inventory, where it will cause enemies' properties to be adjusted: their stats and drops will be those of the following time of day, ahead of where you are in the game. So if you're currently at Noon, enemies will have the same stats from Evening, and

![](images/df2f2830935ae36393cf5c7b22c8bea3f071816052144b4b1944ce45d12b258f.jpg)  
Taking on the sinister burden will noticeably make things more difficult.

once you get to Night, the stat increase continues beyond normal levels, making even that time period more difficult. Along with the increased hardships, however, there are some benefits to having the Bell Demon on you, because it will increase the item drop rates of all enemies. The difficulty increases from the Bell Demon also stack on top of those from both Hard Mode and New Game+, so if you're looking for the ultimate challenge, you'll need to combine all three.

You can choose to discard the Bell Demon at any time by simply using it in your inventory, and then if you want to acquire it again, simply return to the temple and ring the bell once more. You can only have one Bell Demon on you at a time, however. The flexibility of the item allows you to tailor the difficulty of the game to your desires, allowing you to make it harder at any time you like. It's also quite an effective strategy to acquire the Bell Demon when you're trying to gather upgrade materials or items so that you have the benefits of the increased drop rates, and then once you have everything you need, release the demon and continue at the normal difficulty. The Bell Demon does not carry over to New Game+, so if you finish the game with one in your possession, you'll need to reacquire it again on the subsequent playthrough.

# Shinobi Skills Overview

During the course of your journey, you will find or be given Esoteric Texts that will unlock the associated skill tree under Acquire Skills in the Sculptor's Idol menu. By spending your Skill Points at any Sculptor's Idol, powerful new techniques can be unlocked from these skill trees to assist you against the challenges that await.

# Skill Trees

There are five different skill trees to unlock in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. Here we'll describe what makes them unique and how to access them.

# Shinobi Arts

Hone your skills as a Shinobi

P.48

![](images/7f0400da46e876cfbbd737ddd4b04fb3d64e9a61401d889744563cbaab25c52a.jpg)

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  After gaining one Skill Point, talk to the Sculptor back at the Dilapidated Temple. He will sense that your skills are returning, and give you the Shinobi Esoteric Text, which unlocks the Shinobi Arts skill tree.

# Prosthetic Arts

Expand the utility of your Prosthetic Arm

P.55

![](images/64ebceba2b64dfa3a4c1791375a925f6a24fa4b37fa1b4c642679c82f1cbad08.jpg)

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  After you've found three Prosthetic Tools and the Sculptor has loaded them into your arm, leaving the "Fit New Prosthetic Tool" menu will trigger a conversation that results in being given the Esoteric Prosthetic Text key item, unlocking the Prosthetic Arts skill tree.

# Ashina Arts

Sharpen your skills with the Katana

P.61

![](images/8290f750303c95f4690b553e2cbeff05a778026c7cf77d398ac6ceae1ac2859d.jpg)

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  After defeating Gyoubu Oniwa, make your way into the watchtower on the opposite side of the area to the Ashina Castle Gate Idol. Inside you'll find Tenu and he'll ask you to help him kill some "rats" that have found their way into the castle area. The "rats" in question are Assassins, and you can find them in a large raised area just past the aforementioned Idol; dispatch at least one of them and return to Tenu to be rewarded with the Ashina Esoteric Text that bestows knowledge of this Skill school.

# Independent Skills

Some Skills are acquired outside of the fives kill trees, and these fall into one of two types: Hidden Arts and Master Arts. Hidden Arts are learned automatically as you progress through the game or defeat certain enemies. Some Hidden Arts must also be purchased.

# SPOILER

Master Arts are rewards for finishing the game. This means that learning about them will result in spoilers for those who haven't yet reached the game's conclusion. Avoid reading the information about them here and in their section later in this chapter unless you really don't mind story-related spoilers.

![](images/93b79b2ba6fd3858d24c7912b82f69e003382204f213dc576de6ad0e0ffab158.jpg)

# Temple Arts

Bestow secret martial arts techniques

P.65

![](images/0b5410546878af29ce14dcd2aeccfa6d85eea8535b62502a532c1f1193b333d2.jpg)

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  The Senpou Esoteric Text is the only skill tree that isn't given to you by an NPC; it needs to be found. You can find the Text in a small shrine not far from the Main Hall idol in Senpou Temple (see P.242 for the exact location).

# Mushin Arts

Upgrade specific Combat Arts into powerful new forms

P.74

![](images/0357662047b4969fc87179a38a3031bdd84083de568e0613ced86c1c8a3fc55e.jpg)

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  After obtaining the Ashina Esoteric Text, and defeating Genichiro Ashina, the mysterious Tenu will appear next to the Great Serpent Shrine Idol in Ashina Castle. Upon mastering the final Combat Art of any skill tree, he will then give you the Mushin Esoteric Text containing the Mushin Arts.

# SPOILER

You can also receive the Mushin Esoteric Text from Isshin during the Interior Ministry raid, or from Emma during the Central Forces raid if you missed the meeting with Tenu.

Hidden Arts Skills that are hidden throughout the P.69 land of Ashina

Acquisition  $\nVdash$  Varies depending on the Hidden Art.

Master Arts Devastating Combat Arts that can only P.76 be used by a Master

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  SPOILER Defeat Isshin Ashina and Isshin, the Sword Saint at the end of the game.

# Skill Types

All Skills, regardless of which skill tree they fit into or how you acquire them, are categorized according to three types, each of which is described here.

![](images/814bf75f6c5bd30bf3e385b37d5b7a9916316207f4bfcdfa70ac29f274dd81c6.jpg)

# Combat Arts

Offensive Techniques

Highlighted in red in menus. These are powerful offensive techniques that you can perform either by pressing guard and attack at the same time, or by holding guard first and then pressing attack. You can only have one Combat Art equipped at a time. The most powerful ones will cost Spirit Emblems, particularly the upgraded versions that can be learnt in the Mushin Arts skill tree.

![](images/f38ea4e7727e912b48f6441a2e372feb81359141b21141ce81884af5b5b32151.jpg)

# Shinobi Martial Arts

Core Skills

Highlighted in blue in menus. Shinobi Martial Arts are only available within the Shinobi Arts and Prosthetic Arts skill trees, as well as one which you buy from a vendor. They can be considered "core" fundamental abilities which allow you to use your existing Combat Arts and Prosthetic Tools in new ways, as well as a range of other far-reaching techniques to assist you both in combat and stealth. You should generally prioritize learning Shinobi Martial Arts as quickly as you can, as they can fundamentally alter the way you approach the game.

![](images/1a10f227ca8975d0ae9fc82eaf6546bd389219b54dece25b5fa1736698c605e3.jpg)

# Latent Skills

Passive Abilities

Highlighted in yellow in menus. These are Latent Skills that require no input from the player, instead working passively in the background. Examples include the ability to swim and breathe underwater, Vitality and Posture recovery from landing Deathblows, enhanced efficiency on healing items or an increase in the number of Spirit Emblems that you can carry.

# Ninjutsu Techniques

Finally, there are Ninjutsu Techniques. These are not Skills—they have their own slot so that you can equip them independently from Combat Arts, and as with Combat Arts only one can be equipped at a time. Ninjutsu are powerful abilities that can be only used after landing a Backstab Deathblow on an unsuspecting enemy's back. Ninjutsu techniques can also be used after Vaulting Over a Posture broken enemy or using Divine Abduction on weaker enemies.

![](images/dd5e2e5cc480a578a377d98d30b9a13d09ac37ed35d1baaca1df54771041bb5f.jpg)

# Ninjutsu

Ability performed after a

Backstab Deathblow

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  Unlocked automatically after defeating certain bosses.

![](images/8c9fb5faa6cd8d5f6fe20aa4c83800316dcddcdd12970e11e99385d1afa138e7.jpg)

![](images/ecc3b60476d9ce97167a5be2137c761f8223136adcc62e43551e75ddca1dc536.jpg)

![](images/f5b576929a7ed2093648623827b4f680498b820bb245465a695446925f411e6f.jpg)

# WhirlwindSlash Combat Art

A slashing Combat Art that whirls through its surroundings. This sharp slash can easily tear through multiple enemies and deal damage through their guard. When surrounded, use this attack to slice open a path.

Activation L1/LB +R1/RB

Properties  $\triangleright$  Piercing

Whirlwind Slash will likely be the first Combat Art that you unlock. It's a strong technique, that is useful all the way from the beginning to the end of the game, especially since it costs no Spirit Emblems to use.

This is a two-hit Combat Art, with the first hit having decent range, being relatively fast and often forcing enemies to guard, which gives a chance for the slower second hit to safely connect. However, if you miss the first strike, the second strike leaves you very vulnerable. This can be made much safer, though, by guard-cancelling; simply press guard at the very end of the animation, drastically reducing it's recovery. If you're holding guard beforehand this won't work. Due to its wide horizontal range, Whirlwind Slash is good at controlling a group of enemies directly in front of you, but avoid using it if you are surrounded by enemies, since the full animation is very long and there's a strong chance you'll be interrupted from behind. Due to its lengthy animation, you also need to be careful about using it against armored attacks.

While its Posture damage isn't great, Whirlwind Slash is effective at chipping away at the enemy's Vitality, especially since it carries the Piercing damage attribute. This means it will deal  $50\%$  Vitality damage even if the opponent guards, so adopting a hit-and-run strategy

![](images/168fcf74470682a1e0e6aaf1c868d5b299f38cb643d9f56c1ac14b1dec91a991.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>1st Hit</td><td>D</td><td>E</td></tr><tr><td>2nd Hit</td><td>C</td><td>D</td></tr></table>

can be effective, especially if canceling the attack properly. Certain enemies, such as the Shinobi Hunter, can actually deflect the second hit of Whirlwind Slash if they guard the first. While you're technically at a disadvantage in those situations, when you understand how those enemies can potentially react afterwards, it can actually work in your favor.

![](images/c486a2253d3e0a0553f7a1f4983baa3b9991866e69cc7845940f783df8f19a74.jpg)

A Combat Art devised by the Great Shinobi. This is the secret technique of the Shinobi Combat style. Unleash a long-range, powerful thrust, then use the impaled opponent as a platform to vault into the skies. Be as an owl on the hunt, and return to the skies after stabbing your prey. Spirit Emblems are consumed when leaping.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/LB  $^+$  R1/RB (hold to charge and extend range)

Properties  $\triangleright$  Thrust, Piercing

Shadowrush is a thrust attack with extremely long range. Once it connects you'll automatically leap into a rising attack; this is the part that consumes Spirit Emblems. Once in the air you can usually land two aerial strikes on the enemy, though the second one might be guarded. If you miss the attack it will not consume any Spirit Emblems, and you'll simply stop after the thrust. Being a thrust attack, it cannot be guarded, and deals good Vitality as well as decent Posture damage. Shadowrush's long range and thrust damage attribute make it an incredible tool for whittling down an enemy's Vitality, and any Posture damage should be considered a bonus. It can also be charged, increasing both the damage and range, with the usual rules for charging attacks being applicable; you cannot charge it in the air, and while you can cancel the charge at any time, only a full charge grants the range and damage increase.

Though this Combat Art may appear overpowered, it does have a few significant weaknesses. First of all, it costs Spirit Emblems, and at two Emblems per use is reasonably expensive, preventing you from using it over and over again. Secondly, the starting animation is very slow, leaving you vulnerable for a long time before Shadowrush comes out. This is mitigated somewhat by the long range, and when combined with the Mid-air Combat Arts Skill you can stay evasive and mobile while it starts, endowing it with much more flexibility. Finally, while Shadowrush tracks a moving target to a degree, against highly mobile enemies it can occasionally miss completely, leaving you wide open.

The thrust attack itself loses cleanly to armored attacks, but the leaping attack that follows the thrust is actually quite good at breaking armor. Since Shadowrush is so slow to activate, though, this is very hard to time, and more often than not, breaking armor with the leaping attack is simply the result of luck. You should generally avoid using it against enemies that have super armor or a lot of armored attacks, since they'll just punish you during the long recovery period. It's also not ideal for huddled group encounters, where you don't have much space to move around, due to the length of the starting animation and lack of horizontal range.

![](images/9b326bf1f364f3c376aabae802fee7a7ec7c5c6cf55d9fcd065e853b7ef01a17.jpg)

![](images/4c4b02d10449bbfaa1d3c2c5f8564339243b1cb4af2d2f79d937a96469e15f43.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Normal</td><td>C</td><td>D</td></tr><tr><td>Charged</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr><tr><td>Leaping Follow-up</td><td>D</td><td>B</td></tr></table>

If you try to use Shadowrush without the necessary number of Spirit Emblems in your inventory, then you will not activate the rising attack even after hitting the enemy. This is actually extremely dangerous, as the enemy will often recover from being hit before you recover from the initial thrust, leaving you wide open to being punished. Do not use Shadowrush, or its upgraded version Shadowfall, unless you have at least two Spirit Emblems at hand.

To summarize, Shadowrush is most effective in one-on-one engagements against medium-sized enemies to primarily whittle down their Vitality while dealing some Posture damage in the process. Mid-air Combat Arts will allow you to confine most of the move's lengthy starting animation to your jump, so that it starts when you land. This technique makes it very deadly for punishing enemy attacks that you evade with a jump, especially if you have Shadowfall unlocked.

![](images/65316554869664db62238208292cc1f953ae88eb986161f44a76aa7026964794.jpg)

![](images/bccdded595ab78034f8d4f836a6da7bed91ba1c98e191d8c5a776ac96b29f760.jpg)

A Shinobi Martial Art that counters enemy thrust attacks, dealing a large amount of damage to Posture. It is nearly impossible to perceive the speed of a thrust, but not for the sharp eyes of a Shinobi. Use this to stomp on an enemy's weapon, opening them up for a counter-attack. Mikiri requires impeccable timing. A mistake may mean death, but the same can be said for your enemy.

Mikiri Counter allows you to nullify thrust attacks and retaliate against them by step dodging forwards into them. During a successful counter, Sekiro forcibly pushes the enemy's weapon into the ground with his foot, dealing extreme Posture damage in the process. Mikiri Counter is by far the preferred and most optimal way to deal with thrust attacks. It cannot be overstated just how important and fundamental of a Skill this is; the sooner you get it and the sooner you become familiar with it, the better. We highly recommend for this to be the first or second Skill that you unlock; it's no coincidence that a whole section of the tutorial is entirely devoted to the Mikiri Counter.

Step dodging towards the enemy in order to counter their move seems counter-intuitive at first, and indeed if you judge the move incorrectly, you will take considerable damage. Don't let this discourage you, though, as the window for a Mikiri Counter is quite lenient, much more so than a deflect. The entirety of the forwards step dodge animation will automatically cancel into the Mikiri Counter. Unlike a deflect, using a Mikiri Counter on a thrust attack in the middle of an enemy combo will always end the combo. Once you become comfortable with using the Mikiri Counter, you will come to anticipate and even look forward to an enemy trying

![](images/18f9e7f7ada1881dbe3af34b8fcc5e16190f48ee8027e5a67f08ac3313977a51.jpg)

to thrust attack you, as it becomes your optimal path to dealing Posture damage. A countered enemy is also often vulnerable for a period of time, which will allow you to land extra hits for even more Posture and Vitality damage. As with a regular attack, the Posture damage that Mikiri Counter inflicts will increase as you increase your Attack Power. Once you unlock Shinobi Eyes later on in the Shinobi Arts skill tree, the Posture damage from a Mikiri Counter increases by  $25\%$ .

![](images/e8b658825968346a86052a91ff23d0804e2ba77f7fd740e9f78a9d13599d3b23.jpg)

![](images/afc858a5e0742d3ea1876caa07f9eb3f950a27a255630bf0ca61c629092d6e82.jpg)

# Run and Slide

# Shinobi Martial Art

A Shinobi Martial Art used for stealth. Slide into a crouched position while sprinting. Sprint through an area and slide into cover or otherwise out of view. This maneuver easily deceives an enemy's eyes.

Activation  $\triangleright$  Press Crouch during a Sprint

![](images/75567ee70765035a640b37e8b4cb0b535185f4b526b28bcbaca18d2bac709cba.jpg)

![](images/6cbf976a1ca12f9d5f09f0598013444c8a3f11521b3e5ee78631386794d9f458.jpg)

Run and Slide allows you to smoothly transition from a sprint into a crouch with a slide. Although not an essential Skill by any means, it will allow you to hide under tall grass more quickly, subtly improving your sneaking capabilities. The main reason to unlock Run and Slide, though, is that it serves as a prerequisite to a very powerful Latent Skill and Combat Art further on in the Shinobi Arts skill tree, and at the cost of only one Skill Point can be unlocked very quickly.

A Shinobi Martial Art that allows one to leap over and behind a Posture-broken enemy. This Martial Arts technique allows the use of backstab Deathblows in the middle of battle, even without using stealth. It's only expected that Shinobi have some special tricks for up-close fighting as well.

Activation  $\triangleright$  Press Jump next to a Posture-broken enemy

Besides looking stylish, Vault Over is extremely useful as it lets you instantly move behind the enemy and into position to perform a Backstab Deathblow. This only works once you've broken their Posture, but it lets you get behind a Posture-broken enemy even in the midst of battle without sneaking up on them first, as you would normally have to do in order to satisfy the conditions of a Ninjutsu Technique. To perform Vault Over, press the jump button immedi

![](images/b6876631acda5ce9ccde61c481fcb4b0074074a186eb72293b5f9256a26e697f.jpg)

![](images/e8f4ab3beee1c15bdd36e417acc5a00f10eca45abb0b48ac1c413f7f6993358e.jpg)

ately after breaking an enemy's Posture. Take care not to hammer away at the attack button when engaging the enemy, as this will make you go straight into a standard, frontal Deathblow.

Vault Over opens up a variety of tactical options and can be used to turn the tides of battle in an instant. Aim to break a weaker enemy's Posture during group encounters and use Bestowal to buff yourself before taking on the rest of the group, or turn a powerful foe into an ally by vaulting over and using Puppeteer. A group of weaker enemies can also all instantly be made vulnerable with Bloodsmoke, allowing you to easily pick them off. Do note that Vault Over won't work against bosses and certain larger enemy types, as it will instead trigger an animation that causes you to land in front of them—potentially wasting a Deathblow opportunity.

If you don't yet have Ninjutsu Techniques unlocked, Vault Over can be used to gain a positional advantage after Posture-breaking an enemy. If, for example, you notice that you're surrounded by enemies, you can quickly leap to the other side. This is a very fringe use though, so you can safely hold off spending Skill Points to purchase Vault Over until you've unlocked Ninjutsu.

![](images/9e9bcee9be0086111ac33e990522400fcc6755f794ac4269137ed674831adacb.jpg)

# Mid-air Deflection Shinobi Martial Art

A Shinobi Martial Art that allows one to guard against or deflect enemy attacks in mid-air. Guns and other projectile weapons deal additional damage to airborne targets, and this technique can serve to prevent that damage. A shinobi is not shot down so easily.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1 / L8 during a Jump

The Mid-Air Deflection Skill grants you the ability to guard or deflect in the air, including during a grapple. Despite the Skill being called Mid-Air Deflection, though, the much more practical and useful Skill on offer here is the ability to guard while in the air. This is especially useful while closing the gap against long range enemies such as riflemen and archers. Guarding while jumping to evade an enemy attack is also a useful defensive tactic, especially against attacks that cover a large area, since it effectively works as a layer of protective insurance in case you don't successfully clear the attack with a jump.

It also unlocks the path to the very useful Mid-air Combat Arts Skill on the Shinobi Arts skill tree.

![](images/892bd1995ad43a292ab253a7bcf2ff0e655f4a0e0f6c4bc2fdc192f3b85adde0.jpg)

![](images/258e76524a4a8cca7aacfe61749338d6c2a2e5176542136fcfd4ee4c9ab877d1.jpg)

A Shinobi Martial Art that enables the use of Combat Arts while mid-air. Reduce distance with a jump or avoid a sweep attack, then deliver a Combat Art attack. The perfect martial arts skill for Shinobi battles where feet will rarely touch the ground.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/LB  $+$  R1/R8 during a Jump

This grants the ability to perform Combat Arts while in the air, allowing you to stay mobile with a jump while simultaneously unleashing a Combat Art. This can be used both offensively and defensively. By jumping towards the enemy, you can greatly increase the range of the Combat Art, allowing you to initiate offense and strike at openings from a distance. By jumping away or to the side you can attack the enemy while simultaneously evading their attack.

![](images/60db02aa2a5a5c3a4c453ece3e54f13ed5f369983430e8d4ca751951f285e7c7.jpg)

![](images/a37118140af0861d67f35ecb05fbfe3e3afa48c6ebb2826d832973716408e3f2.jpg)

An important point to note about this Skill is that you cannot start the Combat Art the moment your feet leave the ground. There needs to be a minimum jump duration before you can initiate it. If you try to press guard and attack immediately after jumping, you will simply perform a regular attack. Wait just a little moment before inputting the Combat Art. Especially with slower Combat Arts, you want the move to come out as quickly as possible, and with some practice you'll be able to execute them as soon as your feet come back to the ground.

How effective Mid-Air Combat Arts is depends on the Combat Art in question. While it adds extra flexibility and utility to all of them, it most benefits those that take a long time to execute, namely: Ichimonji, Shadowrush, Ashina Cross and Mortal Draw, as well as all of their upgraded versions. The main issue with all of these moves is that you are left immobile and vulnerable for a long time while starting the move. With a jump you can deftly evade an attack while starting these formidable moves, or suddenly leap in from mid to close range to unleash your attack. Do note, though, that while many Combat Arts can be charged to increase their potency, they cannot be charged during a jump.

![](images/cbf979fd1daa4a99f85a4386fec6c70d8f4b7b853d0497d0b87b4e111ee15362.jpg)

# Suppress Presence Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that reduces an enemy's ability to perceive those who are in stealth. This is another shinobi technique. Removing one's presence is what defines a shinobi.

![](images/9e6cd876eb9b19dd80c7492e38770ce139910575a6769f6bb5d2f5169e777632.jpg)

![](images/1b66d906312e0cbd30ac9f0b3d68ecfa1a15030176b2d1072f5dd9a2de044a20.jpg)

"Presence" in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice is essentially visibility. Suppress Presence greatly reduces an enemy's ability to see you while you are wall hugging or crouching, however it will make no difference to your visibility while standing. It also increases the amount of time it takes for alert indicators to fill even once an enemy has spotted you. In open ground this means you can be crouching several meters closer to an enemy before they see you, and then it'll take even longer for them to become suspicious. With it, you'll be able to sneak your way past enemies that would have otherwise spotted you and become alerted. Suppress Presence is a great help while picking off enemies from the shadows.

A Latent Skill that suppresses movement noise inhibiting an enemy's ability to hear. This is another shinobi technique. Moving in silence is what defines a shinobi.

Unlike Suppress Presence, which affects your visibility while crouching or wall hugging, Suppress Sound reduces the sound of your footsteps no matter which action you're performing. Without Suppress Sound, when you run towards an enemy their Alert Indicator will go yellow. However, with Suppress Sound, you can literally run or sprint in circles directly behind them, and they will be none the wiser. Just about the only action you can take to make them suspicious (outside of attacking of course) is jumping right next to them. Most importantly, it also significantly reduces the sound of Deathblows.

Despite all this, this Skill is not quite as useful as Suppress Presence. Whereas Suppress Presence makes a tangible difference to your ability to stay undetected, moving while crouching is completely silent regardless of whether you have Suppress Sound or not, and running or sprinting to enemies to Backstab Deathblow them will

![](images/2b314b4aaffd931ae4bde2a09c69cefc29dbbcc66c9e37c7410d88488f609ac0.jpg)

![](images/bd2c0ad5e2c1919a11a8380e0418106d2358116d88c472ae4d2cd815d15c99c6.jpg)

not immediately put them into Alert; you still have ample time even after you see the Deathblow target. Deathblows themselves making less noise is the most useful perk Suppress Sound offers, since it can help you stay undetected while killing multiple enemies near to one another. However the enemy will still be alerted if you perform a Deathblow right next to them.

Overall Suppress Sound won't substantively help you stay undetected all that much. Considering this is actually more expensive in terms of Skill Points than Suppress Presence, and also a dead end on the Shinobi Arts skill tree, it can safely be left until later in favor of other, more important, Skills.

![](images/0e682a540a516be523fa9122cd2895347159e4868e7d80b8ab49a833eb3d11d7.jpg)

![](images/02806e0c283569ac1bcec5fcb216473aa08020619c7bddc1fc265f0c31241992.jpg)

# Shinobi Eyes Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the damage inflicted to Posture upon executing a successful Mikiri counter. A Shinobi's eyes do not follow the blade without anticipating its movements. Remaining composed even when fearful of its sharp edge is the key to victory.

![](images/a92f736eb8d04fa1a2f6054f26bc681788f87404414c3a25b6b6348a1764f3b9.jpg)

![](images/ed2566be0924c43b0696a2f5ca99f47f1138838f08e9b883e8786e7538616e33.jpg)

Shinobi Eyes increases the Posture damage inflicted by a Mikiri Counter by  $25\%$ . Since Mikiri Counter is such an important Skill, this simple damage buff will prove incredibly helpful and should be high on your priority list to unlock. As the game progresses you'll encounter an increasing amount of enemies that use thrust attacks, making this even more useful.

# A Shinobi's Karma: Body Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the maximum number of Spirit Emblems that can be held. Spirit Emblems are manifestations of regret. Those regretful of their vile actions are haunted by many Spirit Emblems. Shinobi who have killed many must bear the physical toll of those sins.

![](images/d92748ad728cf28030a746a192f6d72b47f43704b56dafc47b8d01031b16bbc0.jpg)

![](images/4972fc8bf74e3ec7ca313e302a167a1c243769c6eead9f6fedf85c0f87f63175.jpg)

# A Shinobi's Karma: Mind Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the maximum number of Spirit Emblems that can be held. Spirit Emblems are manifestations of regret. Those regretful of their vile actions are haunted by many Spirit Emblems. Shinobi who have killed many must go through life carrying the burden of their sins in their hearts.

![](images/650dc047dbad73ef4ad7bbcdc4eb9fea1b20d2e6c3d861f6acf729edead1943b.jpg)

![](images/7f0077926c64ffc1670d910248bdd122f8cb0b4ce88098f3625a26cdd9e8b4fc.jpg)

A Shinobi's Karma increases the maximum amount of Spirit Emblems you can hold by one. More Spirit Emblems means more opportunities to use your Prosthetic Arm Tools, Ninjutsu and certain Combat Arts. A Shinobi's Karma: Body should be one of your priorities after unlocking Mikiri Counter, as it leads to the incredibly useful Breath of Life: Light Skill. A Shinobi's Karma: Mind is quite expensive in terms of Skills Points and is a dead end on the skill tree, so can be left until later.

![](images/e2ba5f787dc5dd9f593551e5cf3a195afdbdde29a5510c8fa60db444fc6f5299.jpg)

# Breath of Life: Light Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that recovers Vitality upon performing a successful Deathblow. Deathblows provide shinobi with an opportunity to breathe. A shinobi can calm the body and mind through measured breathing, even while killing. Doing so allows one to continue killing unabated.

Breath of Life: Light is an incredibly useful Latent Skill. This will make a Deathblow restore  $10\%$  of your Vitality and, outside of resting at an Idol, is the only way to heal yourself without using an item. Particularly when facing a large group of enemies, this will dramatically increase your survivability. Against bosses, Breath of Life will heal your Vitality after you take out one of the Deathblow Markers above their Vitality gauge.

Breath of Life is particularly useful when used in conjunction with the Loaded Axe. Being a slow but armored attack, there is a high likelihood of taking damage while using the Axe, however it will instantly Posture-break many weaker enemies, allowing you to immediately regain some of the Vitality you just lost. Coupled

![](images/436d0f64ffcb344b031fa6e1756a57f7f163ecea3a838e460f720568af2ed6a4.jpg)

with being invulnerable during a Deathblow animation, if you find yourself surrounded, this in an excellent way of whittling down the enemy ranks to more manageable numbers.

While an expensive Skill to acquire at five Skill Points, if you're having trouble staying alive then we highly recommend grinding a bit in order to afford this Skill as soon as possible. It also gets much more effective once you defeat O'Rin of the Water in Mibu Village, which unlocks Breath of Life: Shadow and will stack another  $10\%$  of Vitality recovery with every Deathblow, totaling to  $20\%$ .

# Prosthetic Arts

![](images/2a8a9c53d8ec670b89817aafdc9b880ae8206484eb28fe40ed639af4d8f03807.jpg)

The Prosthetic Arts skill tree is divided into two branches. The top branch is focused around expanding and enhancing the utility of your Prosthetic Tools. The bottom branch could easily be considered an extension of Shinobi Arts. These Skills include a tricky new Combat Art, as well as upgrades to the efficiency of your Healing Gourd. Similar to Shinobi Arts some of the Skills that can be learnt here can be considered core, fundamental techniques that should be unlocked as soon as possible so that you can familiarize yourself with them.

![](images/aa04e2a61347d3d73de37e66cea0f395f7a429946731ec18b385f20d3e669d8c.jpg)

# NightjarSlash Combat Art

A Combat Art that is a spinning leap attack. It can quickly close with or create distance from foes. This is a technique of the Nightjar Clan, the Shinobi who serve Ashina. The Nightjar use the weight of their massive shuriken to add force to the blow. The Shinobi Prosthetic is made of heavy steel and can be used in a similar capacity.

Activation  $\triangleright$  While locked on,  $[\underline{L} ] / [\underline{B} ] + [\underline{R} ] / [\underline{R} ]$

![](images/fd74f1a115b704cfbdc6ef2c2eb8ce9fe31684c91ffe81429e6b07ecb873c655.jpg)

![](images/fcc7e798cec5238d68c1ae3ceeb31f92991e7c22a41e08cc0eeed5c5d6106e13.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Nightjar Slash</td><td>C</td><td>C</td></tr></table>

A Combat Art that is a spinning leap attack. It can quickly close with or create distance from foes. This technique allows one to decide which direction to rotate in when performing NightjarSlash. Swoop in, strike, fly away. That brand of fighting gave the Nightjar Clan their name.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/LB+R1/RB

The NightjarSlash allows you to briefly roll towards the enemy before jumping at them with a vertical slash that deals almost the same damage as your basic attack and leads into your basic 5-hit combo. Nightjar has excellent range, and is useful to punish enemies who leave their guard open from a distance; at close range it leaves you highly vulnerable, though.

![](images/0c4ee5b9a403b6b00986b579d3fc2aed239669fb7cf02b6caa26ebea70c9740b.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Nightjar Slash Reversal</td><td>C</td><td>C</td></tr></table>

When used in conjunction with Mid-air Combat Arts, you can immediately go into the vertical slash without needing to roll first. Since your standard aerial attacks are very weak, this allows you to effectively perform an attack with the strength of your basic grounded attack in the air. Since your aerial attack deals  $25\%$  as much damage as a grounded attack, this difference is quite significant. Jumping and then immediately performing the Mid-air Combat Art also has slightly more range than using the grounded version of NightjarSlash, but also takes longer to activate.

At first it would seem the Mid-air version of NightjarSlash also makes it a superior alternative to using your Jump Kick to punish enemies that try to Sweep you, as it deals both more Vitality and Posture damage. However, the enemy is stunned for a shorter duration after an aerial NightjarSlash compared to the Jump Kick, generally allowing for less guaranteed follow-up attacks and thus less overall damage. When used on the ground, the leaping attack that follows the roll will also evade Sweeps, however this is very situational.

NightjarSlashReversalisamirrorimageoftheNightjarSlash.By locking onto the enemy, and then holding away from them on the left analogue stick while initiating the move,you will do a quick slash followed by a backward roll. The initial slash has similar properties as your basic attack, except instead of a downwards strike it is an upwardslash.The roll that follows it is excellent for quickly getting out of the way of danger (although it has no invincibility),and

when used in conjunction with a regular NightjarSlash to punish missed moves and close distance, you can adopt a very evasive and effective hit-and-run strategy.

Overall, NightjarSlash and NightjarSlash Reversal have limited uses against bosses, especially against those with ironclad defenses that rarely leave their guard open. However, in group encounters it turns you into a very slippery, hard-to-catch target; constantly weaving in and out of enemy ranges while you chip away at their Vitality. If you enjoy anacrobatic and highly mobile playstyle, the NightjarSlash will suit you well. Finally, given that it costs no Spirit Emblems, you are free to use it without impacting the more powerful tools in your arsenal.

![](images/ec1d3b07b8d677c1ecbfde8b28691b81fc200066f5f8ac79f986b84b0a948742.jpg)

![](images/219f79a1113e6c0c3be3cd6c146312cfa456737d3fd8d7e66d5c341bcdd4c425.jpg)

# Grappling Hook Attack Shinobi Martial Art

A Shinobi Martial Art that allows one to leverage the momentum of the grappling hook to perform a sword attack. The Shinobi Prosthetic is the perfect tool for cutting away excess movements by combining momentum and attack into one.

Activation  $\triangleright$  R1 / R8 during a Grapple

The Grappling Hook Attack enables you to perform an attack during a grapple. This is a unique aerial move which sees you spin around in mid-air and perform two slashes in quick succession; propelled by the momentum of the Grappling Hook, these strikes deal decent damage, comparable to two basic strikes, but much faster. The Grappling Hook Attack is limited to this one unique spinning attack. It does not allow you to use mid-air Prosthetic Tools, Combat Arts or the Jump Kick.

![](images/778955f1546dfcf8b293771a30e4885a5d7c2b2bc86ea7b9e4843c2b2edff86b.jpg)

![](images/558ea3c9e53dc8c951622829f3a11070f77452492e1ad663afe4ca4b06e8e2ed.jpg)

The Grappling Hook Attack is by its very nature quite a specialized Skill, but against certain enemies which you can grapple onto, this allows you to both close distance very quickly while dealing a lot of damage in the process. Against Gyoubu Oniwa or the Chained Ogre this is one of the most useful skills you can have.

In some areas the Grappling Hook Attack also allows you to quickly dispatch enemies that are positioned next to Grapple Points. Be sure to lock-on to the enemy before attacking them, as otherwise you're likely to miss. Another point to consider is the trajectory of your swing. After using the Grappling Hook you have no influence on what direction you travel in mid-air, so be sure to swing towards the enemy.

Although the Grappling Hook Attack is not the most flexible Skill, when it is needed it is immensely useful, and some of these situations come quite early on in the game. Since it only costs one Skill Point and is the starting point for the incredibly useful lower branch of the Prosthetic Arts skill tree, we recommend you unlock this as soon as you can.

A Shinobi Martial Art that allows one to perform a forward-dashing sword slice after using certain Prosthetic Tools. A long range Prosthetic Tool attack combined with a Chasing Slice allows one to close distance on enemies instantly. Applicable Prosthetic Tools: Loaded Shuriken, Shinobi Firecracker, Loaded Spear

Activation  $\triangleright$  R1/R8 after using an applicable Prosthetic Tool

Chasing Slice allows you to follow up the Loaded Shuriken, Shinobi Firecracker or Loaded Spear with a lunging slash that boasts both good range and wide horizontal reach, particularly to the right side of the attack. This Skill is extremely useful, since it lets you

![](images/fae158214ccd85618a0a11b052b8908a162b9f479ff27d547ae23d11e564dce3.jpg)

![](images/faba5ed1fbdf3f58a4d5bdde875b576bee996458480b38b4ccb50eec1c28b92e.jpg)

instantly close the gap, making it a great tool to put pressure on your opponent and prevent them from recovering Posture or using ranged attacks. It's also good for finishing a weak enemy in a group quickly from a distance, since it can immediately be canceled into a Deathblow if you Posture-break them with it.

Due to Chasing Slice's wide horizontal range it can also hit multiple enemies at once, so you can use it as part of a hit-and-run strategy to deal damage to a group of enemies before backing away again. It's important to note how enemies react to your Tool before committing to Chasing Slice, however. For example if an enemy guards a Shuriken, they will likely deflect the incoming Chasing Slice, potentially leaving you in a dangerous position.

Due to how much it enhances some of your most useful tools, we recommend unlocking this as soon as you can. Please see the Shinobi Toolkit chapter (P.80) for more detailed advice on how to use Chasing Slice in conjunction with each individual Tool.

![](images/e51aa204ad1f4aa916813bc494979b284492f1011fa06f58fe8b35b2a3eb3b20.jpg)

# Mid-air Prosthetic Tool

Shinobi Martial Art

A Shinobi Martial Art that enables the use of Prosthetic Tools while in mid-air. The Shinobi Prosthetic is heavy as it is made from iron machinery. Despite that, it can be used in the air thanks to the techniques of its creator Dogen, and the training of its owner. It's a good thing that Prosthetic Tools can be used when one's feet aren't on the ground.

Activation  $\triangleright$  R2/RT during a Jump

Mid-air Prosthetic Tool allows you to use Prosthetic Tools during a jump. This means you can stay mobile and evasive even when attacking with a Tool. While this Skill benefits all the Prosthetic Tools to some degree, similar to Mid-air Combat Arts, this is most useful when used in conjunction with Tools that have short range or are slow to start. Not only does jumping add a great deal of range and flexibility to your Tools, but the aerial versions are faster to start than their grounded counterparts. This particularly benefits slow Tools such as the Flame Vent. Sabimaru even gains a unique double-hitting aerial attack, which is very cost effective for poisoning enemies. Another excellent mid-air use for Tools is after Jump-Kick Countering a sweep. As with Mid-air Combat Arts, you cannot charge an attack while jumping. Please see the Shinobi Toolkit chapter (P.80) for more specialized information on how each Prosthetic Tool can be used in mid-air.

![](images/de3340a46dd9b2aea0e3e19390e6ced227e1cce75ba1f20c7aa58dba942d2a80.jpg)

![](images/c476d18196e1a52d8c6d09ac2d592959808d8fae7ba1142f64a09b154388012f.jpg)

After using certain Prosthetic Tools, this Shinobi Martial Art allows one to attack with the Tool and sword simultaneously, or it provides a follow-up attack for the Tool. This move allows one to kill his enemies with the fang and the blade together. Applicable Prosthetic Tools: Loaded Axe, Loaded Spear, Mist Raven

Activation > R1/R8 after using an applicable Prosthetic Tool

Properties  $\triangleright$  Guard Crush

Fang and Blade can be used after the Loaded Axe, the second hit of the Loaded Spear, and Mist Raven. The range, strength and form of this move vary wildly depending on which Tool it is used in conjunction with. With the Axe it allows you to follow up your initial strike with a powerful armored attack using both your Katana and the Axe. This inflicts heavy Posture damage as well as some Vitality damage even when guarded, effectively making the Axe twice as efficient in terms of Spirit Emblem cost. With the Spear it allows you to follow up the second hooking attack with a slash. This serves as a good way to fish out an enemy from a group and then initiate the offense when they're isolated.

Perhaps the most useful application is in conjunction with the Mist Raven; it allows you to follow up a vanish with either a devastating downwards strike from the air or horizontal slash from the ground that boasts huge range. Overall, Fang and Blade greatly enhances all these Tools, so should be learnt as soon as possible if you intend

![](images/bd4877ae04aa8cb7eb35a97fef5d4ce127e649f1c8cde1ee5a8c243c6b5cbb6e.jpg)

to use them regularly. Check the Shinobi Toolkit chapter for advice on how to use Fang and Blade in conjunction with each Tool.

![](images/8c8e92ed84352b67205228df5376bb5bb9afb3d75fc74f5a2f63354a4a3e2a64.jpg)

![](images/d488bd7888ffdedcc769d36310ec313d4a212ea532c6f836a7fc28b54238f13a.jpg)

# Projected Force Shinobi Martial Art

A Shinobi Martial Art that, after using certain Prosthetic Tools, allows one to draw the power of that Tool into the sword and release it in a forward direction. Each color of the fang brings a different sort of colorful death. Applicable Prosthetic Tools: Loaded Umbrella, Finger Whistle

Activation  $\triangleright$  R1/R8 after using an applicable Prosthetic Tool

Properties  $\triangleright$  Guard Crush

Projected Force grants a hefty close-range attack with the Loaded Umbrella, as well as a new ranged ability for the Finger Whistle. While guarding with the Loaded Umbrella, press RB/RI to leap into a combination attack with the Umbrella and Katana. This attack has armor, allowing it to absorb light attacks, and deals good Vitality and Posture damage. Projected Force will power up as the Umbrella absorbs projectile attacks. There are three levels to this, represented by more and more steam coming off the Umbrella, each increasing the range and damage of the attack. If used with the Phoenix's Lilac or Suzaku's Lotus Umbrellas, the attack will take on the elemental properties that they have.

With the Finger Whistle, press RB/R1 after blowing the Whistle; this will make you project the sound wave with your katana, drawing enemies to wherever it lands. This is an incredibly useful tool for relocating multiple foes. If you have unlocked Mountain Echo, you can project a delayed sound-wave that goes off after five seconds, giving you even more options to manipulate the enemy. Please see the Shinobi Toolkit chapter for more detail on how to use Projected Force with the Loaded Umbrella and Finger Whistle.

![](images/1015b7d2a3ee2fc7aca84f42aad3d5c0fd057d058b55a32bcd38a26cf2777b87.jpg)

![](images/234cd68893752c6b2ec785e066f6702855917c8774b968535c178d28443b5f95.jpg)

The secret technique of the Prosthetic Combat Style. Allows one to perform a follow-up attack with certain Tools that imbues the sword with the Tool's effect. The Sculptor retired the Shinobi Prosthetic after developing this technique. He'd gone too far, killed too many. The flames of hatred had begun to manifest... Applicable Prosthetic Tools: Flame Vent, DivineAbduction Activation  $\rightarrow$  R1/RB after using an applicable Prosthetic Tool

Living Force is the final upgrade in the Prosthetic Arts skill tree, and as you would imagine is an incredibly powerful Skill. It can be used in conjunction with the Flame Vent and Divine Abduction; by pressing  $\overline{\mathbb{R}}\overline{\mathbb{B}} /\overline{\mathbb{R}}\overline{\mathbb{I}}$  after Fire Breath or Gathering Vortex, you will first perform a powerful, long-range slash attack which simultaneously infuses your blade with their essence, resulting in powerful buffs to your attack power.

![](images/746971bd45b7cf8dae346457c641dce48adaf8c3bd3f3c9025dfddf609e2ad5f.jpg)

![](images/269b70464609f581bc90c806004c6957a6b126978088f75b95ded7fc54e340d5.jpg)

The Flame Vent will infuse your katana with Fire, increasing its damage and also inflicting Burn on enemies. If you have the Lazulite Sacred Flame this will be an ethereal purple flame that deals Spirit instead of Fire damage, and inflicts heavy Vitality damage even on guarding enemies. This is especially useful against Apparitions such as Headless or Shichimen Warriors.

With Divine Abduction you can envelop your blade in divine winds after charging. Striking the enemy with your Katana will turn them around, allowing you to land a Backstab Deathblow even if they were fully alert to your presence just a moment before. Even enemies that you can't Deathblow will often be left vulnerable and confused for some time, allowing you to land several attacks, though this tends not to work on bosses. With Golden Vortex this also allows you to steal from enemies, effectively doubling the amount of loot and Sen you can obtain.

The buffers to your katana last for seven seconds each, and as with other Prosthetic Follow-up attacks, you cannot use Living Force while jumping. Please check the Shinobi Toolkit chapter for more specific information on how to use Living Force with the Flame Vent and Divine Abduction.

![](images/d2abcc3d11274938f166f244e76c3e98b5af7d5f97d202fec612df443028fdd7.jpg)

# Emma's Medicine: Potency

Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the healing effects of recovery items. Emma taught this technique to the Sculptor long ago. Memorizing the flavor will enhance its effects. However, knowing this technique doesn't make the medicine taste any better.

![](images/ec62ba2d8580c2831a62ea0ec10420c3cae462eb05f390db88a10bd8081be193.jpg)

Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the healing effects of recovery items. Emma taught this technique to the Sculptor long ago. Savoring and memorizing the aroma will enhance its effects. Be warned that the medicine still smells just as bad.

![](images/96b8e334bed84905e2d91c3172550b12881c23e2e088324ecf076fa5851e19bf.jpg)

# A Sculptor's Karma: Blood Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the maximum number of Spirit Emblems that can be held. Spirit Emblems are manifestations of regret. Those regretful of their vile actions are haunted by many Spirit Emblems. The Shinobi Prosthetic is a device mired in sin. Blood spattered upon it turns to a permanent rust, proof of the user's burden.

![](images/27659a407ac0da8aab74eacab49fdcfd28fcf9ff3664789f1834f576a89d473b.jpg)

# A Sculptor's Karma: Scars Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the maximum number of Spirit Emblems that can be held. Spirit Emblems are manifestations of regret. Those regretful of their vile actions are haunted by many Spirit Emblems. The Shinobi Prosthetic is a device mired in sin. Its many small cuts and scars are proof of the countless deaths it's caused.

![](images/128539d41972ff8fd4fc545d4313f9264926bbca351f11301d9a5c54f44aa814.jpg)

A Sculptor's Karma is essentially the same as A Shinobi's Karma, and later on A Beast's Karma. Each of these Skills allows you to hold one more Spirit Emblem. Unlike A Shinobi's Karma: Body,

both A Sculptor's Karma Skills are dead-ends on the Prosthetic Arts skill tree, so can safely be left until later while you unlock more essential Skills.

# Ichimonji Combat Art

A Combat Art that delivers a heavy, one-hit overhead sword strike. Deals high posture damage and also recovers one's own posture with a strong forward step. The move is nothing more than a savage overhead strike, but the single-minded mastery of this technique is the heart of the Ashina style's strength. Once mastered, it can likely be improved.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/LB  $^+$  R1/RB (hold to charge)

Properties Posture Recovery, Guard Crush

![](images/2819420d93a609ee3da30d059103aa2556036df291192464ff8e2adb99110ccc.jpg)

![](images/f143bec4a663ea0cabee36161801e8f074eab1d8622ace10269354e05109e625.jpg)

![](images/97872212f82b76282980f761e471f04bf4c37bb1050180fe7e48e57f6748b92c.jpg)

# Ichimonji: Double

# Combat Art

A Combat Art that adds a follow-up attack to Ichimonji, yet another overhead sword strike. Deals high posture damage and also recovers one's own posture with a strong forward step. The follow-up attack is especially useful for preventing enemy counterattacks. Ashina's Ichimonji is perfected with this follow-up strike.

Activation  $\rightarrow$  /RB after a normal or charged Ichimonji

Properties Posture Recovery, Guard Crush

![](images/c3b153336ca9446505a8988c34e34ec4ab884ec4a7dd478a2fe98528b9a4c467.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Ichimonji Follow-up Strike</td><td>C</td><td>A</td></tr></table>

Ichimonji is a devastating overhead strike with deceptive range due to the distance covered by the large step forward during the start of the attack. If you manage to hit an enemy who has left their guard open, this will also deal considerable Vitality damage, but otherwise deals none on a guarding opponent. Ichimonji can be charged for an extra  $25\%$  Vitality and Posture damage, and roughly  $30\%$  additional super armor damage, but this will not extend the range of the attack. You can release the charge at any time, but only a full charge will be endowed with the additional benefits.

Ichimonji is slow, has little to no use when you're surrounded, and has substantial recovery, meaning that if you miss you'll almost certainly get hit. Having said all that, we cannot over-emphasize just how useful this Skill is. Its utility is highly specialized, but when it comes to inflicting Posture damage, Ichimonji is simply second to none. Comparatively, other high Posture damage dealing attacks, such as the Loaded Axe, either cost Spirit Emblems, lack range, or are slower.

Using Ichimonji takes some finesse and a bit of courage. Due to its slow speed you can't just walk up to the enemy and land it. By far the best time to use it is while an enemy is either stunned or in recovery. If you use a sprint or step dodge to evade an enemy attack, you'll often have enough time to land an uncontested Ichimonji. Similarly, stunning an enemy by breaking their super armor or using a jump-kick counter on a sweep will grant you an opening. Tools such as the Shinobi Firecracker, or an item like a Fistful of Ash can also be used to temporarily incapacitate enemies, allowing you to create opportunities to safely use Ichimonji that don't rely on the enemy attacking first.

![](images/bc6a04dbc1485dae1f908b14ba3c91cf5d3da79294c6b85f2991fe34327912d7.jpg)

Ichimonji will also successfully interrupt many armored attacks, but it doesn't break through all of them so you can't use it carelessly, and will need to know your opponents. It also greatly benefits from being able to jump while starting up the attack, and is a natural fit with Mid-air Combat Arts. This allows you to both extend the range of an Ichimonji with a jump, and to evade attacks while it begins, and then punish the enemy upon landing. See the section on Mid-air Combat Arts on P.52 for more detail.

Once you've learnt Ascending and Descending Carp from the Ashina Arts skill tree, you can then learn Ichimonji: Double. This allows you to quickly follow up your first strike with a second one that deals roughly the same Vitality and Posture damage as an uncharged first strike. The follow-up strike does, however, have considerably slower recovery than the first, so if you're facing an enemy that is likely to retaliate quickly after guarding it, you may want to reconsider using it. That being said, if an enemy guards the first strike, and you think they're going to counter-attack, the follow-up strike can be used to interrupt any attempt they make, and offset the recovery that the first strike has.

On the subject of recovery, the form used with Ichimonji has been so finely honed by the Ashina clan over the years that both strikes have the additional benefit of recovering your Posture during the initial step, whether or not the attack actually hits an enemy. So not only does this Combat Art have significant offensive capabilities, but it will also aid in your defense. The Posture recovered is quite significant, so even if you've been on the defensive for a while, rather than disengaging from the enemy to recover when you see an opening, you can instead use Ichimonji to recover Posture at the same time as initiating your offense.

As mentioned, Ichimonji excels at inflicting Posture damage, so using other Combat Arts at the start of tough encounters that focus on depleting Vitality, then switching mid-battle to Ichimonji once their Posture recovery has been impeded, can be an effective tactic. Ichimonji is also a good tool to use after the enemy has been afflicted with Burn. The stun gives you ample time to set it up, and the enemy is also crippled in that they can't recover Posture while burnt, making this a good opportunity to finish them off. Overall, this is a highly specialized Combat Art, and therein lies its strength. Ichimonji is unmatched when it comes to delivering Posture damage, and since it doesn't cost any Spirit Emblems, you'll find many opportunities to use this devastating technique in battle.

![](images/646c521793b41a774802abe8217ef506ab4a4a77d2bcffca7639d289b51fea8d.jpg)

# Ashina Cross Combat Art

Combat Art unleashing a high speed attack from a sheathed stance. Hold the stance to intercept at will. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. A secret technique of the Ashina style, devoted to the mastery of a swift kill. Draw a cruciform cut in the blink of an eye; so fast it could sever the arm of Shura, or so boasts Isshin Ashina.

Activation  $\triangleright$  Hold L1/LB  $^+$  R1/RB to enter sheathed stance. Release L1/LB to cancel, or release R1/RB to initiate the attack Properties  $\triangleright$  Piercing, Guard Crush

![](images/e3fdef5d33a08edb0c667d676cb718d845d292468dda1523661c08c7e951c89a.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>1st Hit</td><td>D</td><td>E</td></tr><tr><td>2nd Hit</td><td>B</td><td>D</td></tr></table>

Ashina Cross will see you sheathe your blade and adopt a waiting Iaido stance. You can hold Ashina Cross for as long as you want by holding down  $\boxed{R1 / R8}$  , and also move around freely, but only at walking speed. Releasing  $\boxed{R1 / R8}$  (or simply just pressing it without holding) will result in a dash forward into a double strike that deals Piercing damage. The Iaido stance can be cancelled by releasing  $\boxed{L1 / L8}$  , which is useful if you need to guard, but it can also be cancelled into a jump or dodge without releasing guard first.

Ashina Cross may not have quite the range that some other Combat Arts have, but it covers ground significantly faster, and being able to hold the attack makes it an incredibly powerful defensive countermeasure. Simply create some distance from the enemy, and wait for them to come near you. As soon as they enter the maximum range of Ashina Cross, unleash your attack; many enemies will struggle to even approach you. This tactic won't work against enemies with projectiles, or those that clearly have a reach advantage, though. Thanks to its long range, however, jumping away from the enemy while starting Ashina Cross with Mid-air combat Arts to strike just as you land can be an effective strategy.

If both hits of the attack connect, the combined Vitality damage is amongst the highest of all Combat Arts; once you're familiar enough with an enemy's attacks that you can comfortably judge the range and make them miss, this becomes one of the most powerful punishment options available to you. Ashina Cross is quite good at breaking armored attacks, particularly the 2nd hit, but since it does not go through all attacks, it's another case where your enemy knowledge will be key to its use.

Similar to many other Combat Arts, if you want to force an opening to use Ashina Cross, then you should make use of Shinobi Firecrackers or a Fistful of Ash. Against most tougher enemies you'll want to focus on dealing Vitality damage first to soften them up and slow the rate of their Posture recovery; Ashina Cross is designed for just such a function. The biggest caveat to Ashina Cross is that it costs two Spirit Emblems for each use, so you'll need

to manage your resources more carefully. If you've run out of Spirit Emblems, the Vitality damage dealt by Ashina Cross drops dramatically by  $80\%$ , and the 2nd slash also loses its armor-breaking qualities. Generally though, you'll be whittling down a boss's Vitality at the beginning, not end of the battle, which is when your Spirit Emblems typically run out. Overall, Ashina Cross is one of the best Combat Arts in the game for depleting an enemy's Vitality.

![](images/6452a73a1cd7a2f6785820c7f5cb6469e546326158616961233b248e3e2cefeb.jpg)

# Ascending Carp Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the damage inflicted to Posture upon performing a successful Deflection. The Ashina Style is deeply rooted in the flow of the Fountainhead waters. They believe the act of successfully deflecting a blade is akin to a carp ascending a waterfall.

![](images/e00e0b5c718e36915395e56276b89134d4ac44af1f88d2abc616214545e579c6.jpg)

![](images/054d8fe06d0e06290d3800689246c75a1d1b3cf055d439aeb25675ca6d5d365a.jpg)

Ascending Carp will make successful deflects deal  $25\%$  more Posture damage. Considering that deflects are one of your primary ways of dealing Posture damage, and Deathblows stemming from Posture-breaks are the main way of dispatching most enemies, Ascending Carp is an incredibly useful Skill that will make many of your encounters considerably easier. This also opens up several routes on the Ashina Arts skill tree, including the immensely powerful Ichimonji: Double.

# Descending Carp

Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that, for a few seconds after Deflection, increases damage to enemy posture from all sources. The Ashina Style is deeply rooted in the flow of the Fountainhead waters. They believe the act of successfully deflecting a blade is akin to a carp descending a waterfall.

![](images/80c0e6844508ab4f88f1f0d7714fc5c7bac43e3d5099c46232459984bd8322ce.jpg)

![](images/cdeda1428eac1a4f098e1ba50a45862a69c6986349f6dfb69f801aee6fd370b3.jpg)

Descending Carp will make the counter-slash after a successful deflect inflict  $25\%$  more Posture damage. Clearly this is not as useful as Ascending Carp, since not all deflects can lead to a guaranteed counter-slash, such as in the case of Consecutive Attacks. This is reflected in how Descending Carp only costs one Skill Point whereas Ascending Carp costs two. However, both these Latent Skills need to be unlocked in order to gain access to the devastating Ichimonji: Double and Ashina Cross Combat Arts. The Combat Arts are arguably two of the most powerful in the game, and can be seen as a complimentary pair - in how Ichimonji excels at inflicting Posture damage, while Ashina Cross focuses on dealing Vitality damage.

![](images/3316deba75d3677fb0ed2f57543c2d11093cdebbbc5b169aa557bf54abeca9ee.jpg)

# Flowing Water Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that reduces the amount of damage to Posture when attacked by an enemy with a sword. Much like the flowing waters known by the Ashina Clan, strength should not be met with more force but instead redirected like the flowing of water.

Flowing Water reduces all incoming Posture damage while deflecting or guarding by  $20\%$ . While earlier on consequences for being Posture-broken are not so severe, several late game bosses will absolutely decimate you. Flowing Water is thus an essential Skill to acquire as your journey through Ashina progresses. It also stands as a prerequisite to unlocking the powerful Ashina Cross technique.

# Breath of Nature: Light

Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that recovers Posture upon executing a successful Deathblow. The Ashina Style incorporates measures for fighting when grossly outnumbered. After a kill, one must maintain a state of continued alertness, while exhaling deeply from within in order to steady the mind and body.

Breath of Nature: Light restores a third of your overall Posture after performing a Deathblow, so the value you get from this skill will heavily depend on your playstyle. If you play more stealthily, or use hit-and-run tactics where you dip into and out of combat, then the natural Posture recovery speed you have will likely be sufficient. If, however, you like to dive headfirst into combat with large enemy

![](images/205e23f1ff5cee098232ce6b1d9e014861b1093f12af76070de0238e20b3c440.jpg)

groups, then this skill can be all but essential. When facing multiple enemies there's a high likelihood that you'll need to either guard or deflect incoming attacks, and with this skill you can simply recover that Posture when using a Deathblow, allowing you to stay in combat for longer.

# Praying Strikes - Exorcism

Combat Art

A Combat Art that adds a finishing attack to Praying Strikes. Unleash a furor of attacks while thwarting enemy movement, then pursue a reeling foe with a final upper-body check. Senpou monks once used this technique as a means of purging themselves of worldly desires. Other foul passions, however... Activation Hold  $\boxed{L1 / L8} + \boxed{R1} / \boxed{R8}$  after Praying Strikes Properties Blunt, Guard Crush (Independent)

![](images/f33a9bd682616632904a4f9d93b9858b2173c0844ce44dd0cb6333985645efd4.jpg)

![](images/4194aee20d72922e9d9e2a84b33dcdb10b7e34d073f734aefee970938189f462.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>After Praying Strikes</td><td>D</td><td>C</td></tr><tr><td>Independent</td><td>D</td><td>B</td></tr></table>

Praying Strikes are a very fast pair of consecutive blows, consisting of an elbow strike to a palm strike. They deal very minor Vitality damage, but their Posture damage is quite respectable, though both strikes even when put together deal less Posture damage than a

single swipe from your basic katana. The main strength of the Praying Strikes lies in their speed. They are significantly faster and have more range than even your basic attack, making them the fastest move in your arsenal that does not cost any Spirit Emblems. Its speed allows for constant offensive pressure against many enemies, and because, unlike normal attacks, it maintains its high speed when used from a sprint or a dodge, it can even be used to punish many missed enemy attacks that you would be otherwise unable to. It can also interrupt many enemy attacks that your normal attack is too slow to accomplish, so you should always be on the lookout for small windows in enemy combos where it might sneak in.

The speed continues to be evident after deflecting some enemy attacks. Occasionally, when you deflect some heavy strikes and go for a counter-slash afterwards, you'll get a slower version than normal, that can often be interrupted if the enemy tries to attack again quickly. Praying Strikes is so much faster than the slow counter-slash that it will often interrupt that enemy attack. It can also be used to construct makeshift combos by stringing together one or two normal attacks, and then quickly transitioning into Praying Strikes without giving the enemy a chance to do anything. Against weaker enemies it can let you start a chain that will continue until their Posture is broken.

With all of these strengths, there has to come some weaknesses, and Praying Strikes' biggest ones are that the elbow strike inflicts hardly any super armor damage, and is ineffective against armored attacks. The palm strike fares slightly better in those departments, but it is not until you unlock the upgrade version of the Skill and have access to Exorcism that you'll be dealing respectable amounts.

Exorcism brings with it a lot of other utility that helps to compensate in areas where the basic Praying Strikes can sometimes be found lacking, not least of which is the significant amount of Posture damage it does, at  $50\%$  more than a normal attack. When you acquire the Exorcism upgrade, it also subtly changes some of the properties on Praying Strikes. When you just have Praying Strikes, enemies can deflect the palm strike if they guard the initial elbow strike, but once you acquire Exorcism, that's no longer the case. Enemies that use armored attacks after guarding can still use that to absorb the elbow strike and hit you, but if you're facing enemies that don't have that ability, then Praying Strikes becomes essentially safe to use.

You can use Exorcism either at the end of the normal Praying Strikes combo, or independently by holding the buttons down rather than tapping them. When used at the end of the combo it can still be deflected by a lot of enemies, but because you have such a large window within which to perform the attack, you can pause after the first two hits to see how the enemy is reacting, and then decide whether or not to continue. This is especially useful when facing enemies with armored attacks that could potentially hit you between the palm strike and Exorcism.

When used independently of Praying Strikes, Exorcism can be very good for punishing enemies after making one of their attacks miss, thanks to its combination of good range and Posture damage. The independent version of Exorcism is much more effective at hitting enemies out of armored attacks than the version at the end of the combo. It also guard crushes and cannot be deflected.

Overall, Praying Strikes are another specialized Combat Art. They lack any crowd control functionality and are quite weak in terms of damage output, but excel in interrupting opponents with their

speed. Some finesse is required to make the most of them, and you'll need to keep a keen eye on the enemy to see how they react to the palm strike. When used properly, however, Praying Strikes are very effective at overwhelming enemies and quickly racking up Posture damage.

![](images/15c30a930013712c8cc6e60a5e79678d950b85a0b78dd79c41ca3c43f96a0d86.jpg)

![](images/cb851f18891481b94ed7cefec9a7ecedd578b8b4c17c906dc2c5f70cf5bae4ae.jpg)

A technique refined by the recluses of Senpou. According to their practices, mastery of the Leaping Kick proves one has attained true enlightenment. First, kick. Only then can training begin.

# High Monk Combat Art

A Combat Art adding sword slashes and additional kicks to the Senpou Leaping Kick. The Secret Technique of the Senpou Style. Attaining enlightenment causes one to be the embodiment of Buddha. The mind is freed, allowing for flowing flurries of attack. The technique has no form, and the attacks differ from person to person. For Wolf, it's only natural that he'd rely on his master's gift when performing the technique.

Activation  $\triangleright$  After Senpou Leaping Kicks: (R1/RB, R1/RB)

Properties  $\triangleright$  Blunt, Guard Crush (final hit)

Although it can be hard to see, the first hit of Senpou Leaping Kicks is actually during the initial jump animation, and since that jump also has a considerable amount of invulnerability, it's very effective for hitting enemies out of the air, inflicting critical Posture damage to them. After that initial hit, you'll automatically follow up with a downwards kick that counts as an armored attack, so it's very good for interrupting enemy attacks on the ground.

The properties of both parts combine when used against sweep attacks. The invulnerability will help you avoid the attack if your timing of the jump is slightly off, and then the downward kick will counter the sweep and inflict massive Posture damage. So large is the amount of Posture damage that you can inflict when using this attack against a sweep, that it dwarfs the amount inflicted by a normal jump-kick counter, and a mid-air Ichimonji: Double follow-up. If you have Mid-air combat Arts, initiating this attack in the air will immediately perform the downwards kick. This means you can manually jump the sweep and still reap the benefits of the downward kick if you're having trouble timing the built-in jump at the start of the grounded version.

After the downwards kick you have quite a large activation window within which you can continue the combo with a double roundhouse kick. That generous window allows you to read the situation and check enemy reactions before you commit to using the round

![](images/3b610964200d8b85cbe4164d16fac7128a1e8873c6b17536c6e55b947e6368a9.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Sword Slash (1st &amp; 2nd Hit)</td><td>E</td><td>E</td></tr><tr><td>Final Kick</td><td>E</td><td>D</td></tr></table>

house kicks; if the enemy is likely to use an armored attack that will absorb the kicks and hit you, press nothing, but if you're sure you'll interrupt any retaliation attempt, continue with the kicks.

If you don't follow-up with the roundhouse kicks, you'll automatically perform a backwards roll after the downwards kick. The roll cannot be canceled and has no invulnerability, but because it moves backwards, it can sometimes still avoid enemy attacks. While the roundhouse kicks can be deflected if you continue with them, that option is sometimes better than having the enemy hit you during the backwards roll. Which option you choose will usually come down to the individual enemy that you're facing.

When you unlock the High Monk skill, you'll gain the ability to further extend the combo after the roundhouse kicks with a double sword slash, followed by one final powerful kick. You can delay this part of the combo as well, allowing you to again check for enemy reactions after the roundhouse kicks before committing to High Monk. The sword slashes have very little recovery and cannot be deflected, making them a safe place to stop the combo if you don't want to commit to the last blow. The final kick is like the downwards kick in that it's slow to start, but it's extremely effective at hitting enemies out of armored attacks, and when it connects, it will briefly stun them. While the final kick guard crushes, it can be deflected, so prepare to guard cancel if you see deflection sparks.

![](images/0946fc682c70ee9de2055e281aa80453a53b8b77df26ab6ece974ad9b98073dd.jpg)

# Devotion Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that increases the amount of time a Spiritfall candy's effects last. The deeply devoted enjoy the gods' extended blessings.

![](images/07c8c998ae8fd3e4651eef8e753991a9e5330f90aca12e26e5a79fdafdfe62a3.jpg)

Devotion boosts the duration of status buffing Sugars and Spiritfalls by  $50\%$ . This means Sugars go up from 30 seconds to 45 seconds (Gachiin's Sugar, which helps you in stealth, goes from 60 to 90 seconds), while Spiritfalls go up from 15 seconds to 22 seconds. This extension is particularly useful when used in conjunction with Sugars; 45 seconds is a long time in battle, and this Skill is of great use in tougher boss battles.

# Hidden Arts

Hidden Arts contain the Skills that do not fall under a skill tree, and thus do not cost Skill Points to acquire. Hidden Arts cover the entire gamut of Skill types, and can be acquired either by defeating certain enemies, advancing the story, or by purchasing the relevant Text from a vendor.

Combat Art that unleashes repeated attacks, overwhelming enemies with flowing, dance-like movements. While an Ashina Combat Art, it was taught by an outsider, and as such is considered heretical. The master of this technique crossed the Floating Passage and descended to Ashina. Her name was Tomoe. Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/L8 + R1/RB, R1/RB, R1/RB Properties  $\triangleright$  Piercing, Guard Crush

Acquisition Purchase the Floating Passage Text from Pot Noble Harunaga in Hirata Estate for 5 Treasure Carp Scales P.173

![](images/15a84ea6f65b9876e25802bd7e335edaa20f8d829c26cd1b8e691bceed49ce3e.jpg)

![](images/afe5f9abaf56423ef57cd0aae2b087133196425d3c51f97722def2e11d2b01ab.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>(1st-4th Hit)</td><td>E</td><td>E</td></tr><tr><td>(5th Hit)</td><td>D</td><td>D</td></tr></table>

Floating Passage is a quick, multi-hitting combo, consisting of five slashes. The initial input will lead to a two-hit slash, the next input leads to another two-hit slash, and the third input will activate the final hit. Like other multi-part combat Arts, each input can be delayed for a short time, allowing you to check the enemy's reaction and decide whether to continue the combo, or cancel it into a defensive option. This is especially important against enemies with armored attacks, because after each of pair of slashes there's a large enough gap for them to initiate an attack, and if you continue the combo, they'll easily hit you out of it.

The final hit of Floating Passage, however, is considerably better that the previous slashes at hitting enemies out of armored attacks, but it is prone to being deflected by many enemies. Be sure to guard or dodge-cancel the final hit to put yourself in a less disadvantaged situation if you're unsure of how the enemy will react,

Against enemies that cannot deflect, or ones that you're hitting in the back, the rapid hits of Floating Passage can allow you apply near constant pressure and Posture damage. As a very handy added bonus, every hit of Floating Passage also pierces through enemy guard. The low base damage of the combo means you won't be inflicting a large amount of Vitality damage to a guarding enemy with every combo, but it will add up and aid the Posture damage you're inflicting.

You're also quite mobile during the slashes and the entire combo covers a considerable amount of ground, making it excellent for staying up close and personal with enemies, or rapidly switching between multiple targets.
