The seeping mist extends the range of the blade. A technique using the blade that cannot be drawn is a feat only the oathbound of the Divine Heir could achieve.

Activation  $\nrightarrow$  L1/LB  $^+$  R1/RB, R1/RB

Properties  $\triangleright$  Spirit, Guard Crush

# Acquisition

SPOILER Obtain the Mortal Blade from the Divine Child of Rejuvenation after defeating the Folding Screen Monkeys  $\triangleright$  P.453

Once you have obtained the Mortal Blade, the Mortal Draw Combat Art will be unlocked alongside it. On initial activation you'll perform a single slow, but powerful and far-reaching horizontal slash that costs three Spirit Emblems. Pressing attack again will lead to a second, vertical slash, for three more Spirit Emblems. Both hits deal the exact same damage, but the first hit excels at dealing with groups of enemies because of the horizontal radius it covers, and the second hit is better against single, stronger opponents. Many enemies will respond to being hit by the first attack by guarding the second, making it not always worth the cost.

Mortal Draw has massive horizontal and vertical range, which is good for both crowd control and striking from a safe distance. It deals Vitality and Posture damage even on a guarding opponent, and impressive Vitality and Posture damage overall. Each slash also guard crushes, so enemies aren't able to counter-attack easily. It isn't the best at any of these things, but it's ability to do all of them makes it a jack of all trades; if you just want to put one Combat Art on and not switch between them, Mortal Blade is a good option.

The way that Mortal Draw distributes damage is quite unique, and the first thing to understand is that there are two ranges associated with the Mortal Draw: an inner and an outer. The outer slash boasts tremendous range, but deals less damage than the inner slash. If the enemy is guarding, the sweet spot has reduced damage, but it still does more damage than the outer slash would do when

<table><tr><td></td><td>Inner &quot;Sweet Spot&quot;Slash</td><td>OuterSlash</td></tr><tr><td>Guarding Enemy</td><td>56% damage</td><td>28% damage</td></tr><tr><td>Open Enemy</td><td>100% damage</td><td>38% damage</td></tr></table>

![](images/127e6f27f3fce28f1f5f01769b393c336cc2d1e5b9c2adfe0661c0aaa5cedfbb.jpg)

![](images/b845be3524fc0dc46faf2a81e244ee2945c53cdce885ef977b175d91837f61a9.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>(1st &amp; 2nd Hit)</td><td>B</td><td>A</td></tr></table>

hitting an open enemy. When the outer slash is guarded, the damage an enemy takes is reduced considerably.

The drawback to Mortal Blade is the expensive Spirit Emblem requirement, meaning you can't use your Prosthetic Tools as much. If you don't have the required Spirit Emblems you can still perform Mortal Draw, but the outer slash will no longer be there, which means it has vastly reduced range, and the inner slash also deals less damage. Being a jack of all trades results in it being the master of none; many other more specialized skills are better at doing something Mortal Blade can do, such as Vitality damage through guard, or high Posture damage. Very rarely does Mortal Draw offer an optimal solution. It does have the benefit of being free to acquire once you first gain the Mortal Blade, meaning no matter what your current skill point build is, it's always available to fill a gap in your options.

# Anti-air Deathblow Shinobi Martial Art

A Shinobi Martial Art designed to stop cold any enemies that leap high in the air. Allows one to exploit an enemy's vulnerability in the air by jumping toward them and performing a sudden Deathblow. The perfect skill for Shinobi looking to turn the tables on airborne enemies.

Activation  $\triangleright$  R1/RB near an enemy high in the air

![](images/ad380b37e72044b6676703703a3a43974aa000a9223f85e0589d67101e2edc91.jpg)

# Acquisition

Purchase the Anti-air Deathblow Text from Blackhat Badger in Ashina Castle for 1200 Sen P.565

Anti-air Deathblow allows you to instantly perform a Deathblow without needing to break an enemy's Posture first, providing you manage to jump toward them while they're airborne. This Skill is very situational, only working on certain enemies, but by anticipating and taking advantage of Anti-air Deathblow opportunities against those enemies, you can end a battle immediately.

Do note that in almost any situation where you can perform an Anti-air Deathblow you can also throw a Shuriken from a safe distance for a critical hit leading to heavy Posture damage; this is considerably less risky than attempting an Anti-air Deathblow. If you're feeling confident in your skills, however, then an Anti-air Deathblow is both more rewarding than a Shuriken, and also doesn't consume any resources. Landing an Anti-air Deathblow is generally not as simple as just jumping towards an airborne enemy.

![](images/ce791fc0479aceb200285134d0237b16f2ccbbb938199d6ebefa246e221ea5a2.jpg)

Sometimes special pre-conditions need to be satisfied, for example with Shichimen Warrior you need to have infused your katana with Spirit energy either through Divine Confetti or Living Force. Not all aerial attacks are vulnerable to Anti-air Deathblows. Please check the Opposing Forces section for more information on when and where to perform the Anti-air Deathblow.

![](images/b3884fc042382de8730dcf035db4d0dbb8bad1ccbd4fd37aaa91a5330224c5cc.jpg)

Technique. This Latent Skill allows one to dive under water, as well as breathe underwater indefinitely. Developed by the founder of Mibu Village. "Those who seek to join the procession must master the Mibu Breathing Technique. Without it, the Divine Dragon cannot be met."

Activation  $\triangleright$  R2/RT after entering deep water

# Breath of Life: Shadow Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that recovers Vitality upon performing a successful Deathblow. Deathblows provide shinobi with an opportunity to breathe. Experiencing battles with powerful opponents further deepens this moment of respite.

Breath of Life is easily one of the most useful Latent Skills that you can acquire, granting you far more survivability than normal, especially in

# Breath of Nature: Shadow Latent Skill

A Latent Skill that recovers Posture upon performing a successful Deathblow. A Shinobi must be prepared for battles in which he is outnumbered. After killing an enemy, one must exhale, expelling both regret and reaffirming one's core to regain Posture. Experiencing battles with stronger opponents further deepens this moment of exhalation.

![](images/02da4e24235a8ce079f88d17abe543ae7372586b95bf7548b845237d0b7ff2de.jpg)

SPOILER Defeat the Armored Warrior in Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo P.232

Breath of Nature: Shadow recovers a third of your Posture upon landing a Deathblow. This stacks with Breath of Nature: Life to recover two-thirds of your Posture with every Deathblow. By the time you unlock Breath of Nature: Shadow, you should be well into the second half of your journey through Ashina. At this point enemies, particularly sub-bosses, tend to ruthlessly pick you apart if they break your Posture, so it's very important not to allow yourself to be Posture-broken.

# Mushin Arts

![](images/cdd8ab6f74677516b590dbd982041208fef7f066d5a68d2ec0d68118f6cd4601.jpg)

The Mushin Arts gives access to powerful new forms of existing Combat Arts. There are only three Combat Arts available in this skill tree, and each one requires that you have mastered two previous skill trees. These enhanced Combat Arts endow them with devastating new extensions and properties.

![](images/1ac33ed421e481cc7c1290732f5ac1e23a51486a56bc5576a6dad5e8642a3df9.jpg)

# Shadowfall Combat Art

An evolution of Shadowrush, this is a Secret Technique of the Ashina Mushin Compound Style. Shadowfall is a descending, spinning slash follow-up attack that can be performed after leaping off an enemy with Shadowrush. Pierce, fly, and then dive back down. Freely flying through the skies is what it means to be an owl. Jumping off the enemy consumes Spirit Emblems.

Activation  $\rightarrow$  R1/R8 after hitting an enemy with Shadowrush and leaping into the air

Properties  $\triangleright$  Piercing, Guard Crush

Shadowfall adds an incredibly wide and powerful, double-hitting aerial slash after Shadowrush (P.49). All other properties of the move remain the same, and you only need to press the attack button once after Shadowrush in order to get both of the Shadowfall slashes. Normally after hitting an enemy Shadowrush you can connect with two aerial hits before landing, although the second one may be guarded. The same logic applies here, except now the Shadowfall aerial slashes deal much more Vitality and Posture damage. Because it can pierce through an enemy's guard, even if your timing is off and you do the follow-up late, you'll still get some damage out of it.

These aerial slashes also boast incredible horizontal range, which means that alongside dealing more damage, Shadowfall also becomes quite effective at crowd control, giving it multi-purpose functionality. Shadowfall takes an already effective Combat Art and makes it even better, and is almost unquestionably the best Skill available in the Mushin Arts skill tree.

![](images/461d70be041387a2301505ab873716a02d42d8d4ee30e999dc6d1c855aa62b44.jpg)

![](images/39e9b7dc80e243f5402d03564a770f583478f0bf3e9c46e9f43ded72fa020c4f.jpg)

As with Shadowrush, do not use Shadowfall unless you have at least two Spirit Emblems at the ready. Otherwise you won't perform the rising attack to aerial slashes, leaving you wide open even if you hit the enemy, due to how slowly the thrust attack recovers.

# Spiral Cloud Passage Combat Art

Spiral Cloud Passage is a Combat Art developed to unleash shockwaves. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Its namesake comes from a large eddy of distant cloud forming near the headwaters; the Fountainhead Spiral. Tomoe would watch her young master as he gazed longingly at the coiling clouds. The sight meant everything to her.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/LB+R1/RB,R1/RB,R1/RB,R1/RB,R1/RB

Properties  $\triangleright$  Piercing, Guard Crush (final hit)

Spiral Cloud Passage is an enhanced version of Floating Passage, and increases the number of slashes from five to nine, as well as unleashing shockwaves around each strike. The shockwaves count as additional hits alongside every slash, both of which deal piercing damage. The shockwaves's boast significant range, but the range on the slashes does not extend beyond the tip of your sword. Nearly all the damage of this Combat Art is done by the slashes and not the shockwaves, so while it's possible to hit enemies from further away, doing so will very rarely be worth the Spirit Emblem cost. That being said, if you're focusing on one enemy within a group, any damage dealt to the surrounding enemies is a welcome bonus.

The increased number of strikes means that the full string deals more Posture damage, while the Piercing damage means that Spiral Cloud Passage will weaken both an enemy's Vitality and Posture. This may sound great, but in practice Spiral Cloud Passage has some severe shortcomings. As with the base version, enemies that have armored attacks can still hit you between the slashes, so you should use caution against those foes. Spiral Cloud Passage is very resource hungry, especially compared to Floating Passage, which costs no Spirit Emblems. The first four inputs are double slashes, and the last one is a single, diagonal strike, resulting in nine hits with five inputs in total. Each input expends one Spirit Emblem, which means that with all the Spirit Emblem upgrades unlocked, you can only use the full Spiral Cloud Passage combo a maximum of four times.

![](images/85e3b268fea5c87c694c7002b33fc7accf6873571e9e6d02af4a0f0daaeb2863.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>1st-8th Hit</td><td>E</td><td>E</td></tr><tr><td>9th Hit</td><td>D</td><td>D</td></tr></table>

If you try to use any strike in Spiral Cloud Passage when you have no Spirit Emblems, then the shockwaves around the slashes will disappear. This slightly reduces their range and damage by about  $5\%$ . It isn't much of a downgrade, though, and considering Spiral Cloud Passage is now essentially freed up from using any Spirit Emblems, it neatly overrides a major limiting factor. The main drawback to using it without Spirit Emblems is that without the shockwaves, the final hit loses its guard crush properties.

![](images/7252fbf0e2392c130186b4314cf576c30d19ad79e6df0cc029ad7d46bd87db52.jpg)

![](images/feb4b0b0cd768308ee6aba3c7f0d8237562ef8f883efa4a7e1e5762a334c3729.jpg)

# Empowered Mortal Draw Combat Art

A secret Combat Art using the Mortal Blade. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. By focusing one's mind before unsheathing the Mortal Blade, one can draw additional power from it, resulting in an even more devastating, longer-ranged slash attack. A technique using the blade that cannot be drawn is a feat only the oathbound of the Divine Heir could achieve.

Activation  $\triangleright$  Hold L1/L8 + R1/R8, hold R1/R8

Properties  $\triangleright$  Spirit, Guard Crush

Empowered Mortal Draw allows you to charge up the Mortal Blade for a more powerful attack, increasing the range, and doubling the formidable damage of Mortal Draw (P.70). As with all charging attacks this can be unleashed at anytime, but needs to be charged all the way in order for the damage and range to be increased.

![](images/0a501355437c70dc42a334a70c0edf15e0d87b8b656a815d485a6741c56e0167.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>1st &amp; 2nd Hit</td><td>A</td><td>S</td></tr></table>

The fully charged Empowered Mortal Draw deals extreme Vitality and Posture damage; double that of a regular uncharged Mortal Draw. The slower speed of the charged attack is counter-balanced by the sharp increase in range. Empowered Mortal Draw still

![](images/c2d8d989618bb5f8bd0bfe224ad33d202e6156721382d5143300e27df663ce2c.jpg)

retains two ranges, an outer and an inner, still costs three Spirit Emblems and still keeps its damage distribution. If you are skilled enough to successfully land a fully charged Empowered Mortal Draw at close range then you can absolutely decimate most enemies, and take a good chunk off of the Vitality and Posture bar of even the toughest bosses. If landing the sweet spot on a regular Mortal Draw was a challenge, though, then landing it on a fully charged Empowered Mortal Draw verges on impractical. More often than not you will simply get hit, especially given that you cannot charge it while jumping with Mid-air Combat Arts. A good set-up for a fully charged Empowered Mortal Draw is to throw a Fistful of Ash at the enemy first. This should stun them long enough to land this devastating blow. Shinobi Firecrackers can also serve a similar function.

If you try to use Empowered Mortal Draw without the required number of Spirit Emblems, then the attack will be missing the outer slash, and the inner slash will do slightly reduced damage.

# Master Arts

Master Arts are your ultimate reward for completing Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. Depending on the path you chose, you will fight a different version of the sword master Isshin. Isshin Ashina awaits you at the end of the destructive Shura Path, where as the resurrected Isshin, the Sword Saint is your final foe should you stray from the iron code and forge your own path. Defeating Isshin Ashina and Isshin, the Sword Saint will reward you with One Mind and Dragon Flash respectively; some of the most powerful Combat Arts in the game.

![](images/65e4d81b94fa7813438614c7d2559edb7a96aa5abb649e64a729963a30143b70.jpg)

# One Mind Combat Art

A Combat Art that unleashes a storm of attacks from the   
sheathed stance; so fast the blade is nigh invisible. One must   
focus their soul on the release of the blade, nothing else. Through   
that focus, the strikes achieve a god-like speed. Only one as   
honed as the aging Isshin Ashina could perform this technique.   
Activation  $\nrightarrow$  Hold  $[\underline{1} /\underline{1} +\underline{R} 1 / \underline{R} ]$  Release L to cancel.   
Press R after the vortex for a follow-up attack.   
Properties  $\nrightarrow$  Piercing, Guard Crush (Follow-up Strike)

Acquisition SPOILER Defeat Isshin Ashina P.485

One Mind operates like an upgraded version of Ashina Cross. Once you unleash One Mind you will launch into a single vertical strike, which is good at breaking through armored moves but is unfortunately very narrow. This is followed automatically by a vortex of multi-sword slashes. You can then finish this off by pressing  $\underline{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{B} / \mathbb{R}\mathbb{I}$  one more time for a massive horizontal slash.

Though the Posture damage is quite lacking, when they all connect it inflicts considerable Vitality damage, and an incredible feature of One Mind is that the initial strike and vortex cannot be guarded. Also, the vortex will come out even if you are hit just after the initial slash, so it might interrupt the enemy and save you from taking damage. The hits on the vortex deal very low armor damage, so this

![](images/e63f8ae41e893e10d3c66a2be02827bdc578a07bce81c681ce5ec36d12f12427.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Initial Strike</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr><tr><td>Vortex (1st-4th Hit)</td><td>E</td><td>E</td></tr><tr><td>Follow-up Strike</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr></table>

attack should not be used against heavy enemies, and some very agile enemies can slip out between the initial strike and the vortex. Once you see the vortex connect and the enemy is reeling, you should follow up with the final slash for guaranteed damage

Unlike the initial strike and the vortex, the follow-up strike can and almost always will be guarded, but since it's a piercing attack, you'll still get  $50\%$  of the damage. One Mind can be effective against single and multiple opponents due to the size of the vortex and the final horizontal slash. At four Spirit Emblems per use, this is a very expensive Combat Art—by the time you will unlock it you should

have a wide selection of powerful Prosthetic Tools at your disposal, which are also in contention for your Spirit Emblems. Though One Mind is a powerful technique, you will need to carefully consider how much you tap into its power.

If you try to use One Mind without four Spirit Emblems in your inventory, then you will merely perform the initial strike—it won't be followed by the vortex. You are still left in a lengthy recovery animation as if the vortex had come out, however, meaning most enemies can hit you even if you hit them with the strike.

![](images/c144f65847d00de888ef2081194ddfa2aaeff0b4b9e4a28efd4d77b8bc89a46d.jpg)

![](images/db4ebfc6d4d5dc6b372e5119aa97f8d178f23c675e57adc436e494be5b7160c1.jpg)

# Dragon Flash Combat Art

Combat Art that performs a high-speed cut from a sheathed stance. Charge to send out shockwaves. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. In his younger years, Isshin was a devil with the sword, spending his days in pursuit of life-or-death combat. He often ruminated on how a cut should be made, but his blade always moved first.

Activation  $\triangleright$  L1/LB + R1/RB Quick Draw. Hold L1/LB +

R1/RB: Dragon Flash

Properties  $\triangleright$  Piercing

Acquisition

SPOILER Defeat Isshin, the Sword Saint P.492

If One Mind is best used in the mid-range, then Dragon Flash specializes at long-range crowd control. Again, it takes quite a while for it begin, and although you sheathe your katana, this is not the same Iaido stance as One Mind or Ashina Cross; you can't hold, cancel or walk around with it. It is simply a standard starting animation where you coincidentally sheathe your katana for a moment to charge the attack.

Once unleashed, you will perform a single close-range slash. This attack can be guarded, but since it's a Piercing attack, you'll still deal  $50\%$  of the damage. However, the range of Dragon Flash far exceeds that of the mere visible range of your katana. It cuts through the very air in front of you, and this invisible shockwave will extend indefinitely, essentially making Dragon Flash a projectile. Just like the initial strike and vortex of One Mind, the shockwave cannot be guarded and even passes through multiple enemies, dealing just under half the damage of a close-range Dragon Flash.

The shockwave effectively makes Dragon Flash the most damaging projectile in your arsenal. While it lacks the speed and flexibility of a Shuriken, it makes up for it in raw power. Since the shockwave cannot be guarded, Dragon Flash is a potent tool for chipping away at a tough enemy's Vitality from a safe distance, and since it passes through multiple enemies it's also strong against groups of enemies. Dragon Flash's power can be pushed even further if you charge it. This increases the damage output of the slash and shockwave slightly, as well as releasing a secondary vertical shockwave.

Overall, Dragon Flash excels at long-range damage across a wide area, as well as whittling down a tough enemy's Vitality from safety. However if the enemy is very fast and aggressive, or has a projectile attack, then you'll likely be interrupted due to Dragon Flash's slow starting speed. As with One Mind, arguably the biggest drawback to Dragon Flash is how resource hungry it is. If you attempt Dragon Flash without at least three Spirit Emblems in stock, then

![](images/07a8707db645ae13496331f3cb13119d2bbee99a241560650f1896d2cec8eb6d.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td></tr><tr><td>Quick Draw Slash</td><td>C</td><td>D</td></tr><tr><td>Quick Draw Shockwave</td><td>D</td><td>D</td></tr><tr><td>Charged Slash</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr><tr><td>Diagonal Shockwave</td><td>C</td><td>D</td></tr><tr><td>Vertical Shockwave</td><td>D</td><td>E</td></tr></table>

you will only perform the initial close-range slash. It will not be followed up by either the invisible or grounded shockwaves, even if you charge it, taking away the biggest strength of the attack.

![](images/eff45d5c356f6f143c357faf92346e907818d86f85cabc76e3c985351109382b.jpg)

![](images/8a9d54725dc1034ab90e800cd64dbe21356b88bd2d153b87817e736bede33089.jpg)

# Ninjutsu Techniques

Ninjutsu are powerful techniques that can totally shift the tides of battle, but you can only use them after performing a Backstab Deathblow. This rewards you for successfully sneaking up on an unsuspecting enemy, however there are several tools and techniques, such as Vault Over (P.51) and Divine Abduction (P.112), which can allow you to land Backstab Deathblows even on enemies that are in full Alert, thus opening the path to devastating Ninjutsu.

![](images/e93e8fd2c98923b62b812382cdb71547b4c53737e999e7d78acd6169c6cc5a4f.jpg)

# Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu

Ninjutsu technique that turns the spraying blood of a victim to smoke. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Activated after a Backstab Deathblow. The smokescreen allows one to retake the element of surprise. Life or death struggle defines a shinobi, for whom a kill is a source of strength.

Activation Perform a Backstab Deathblow, then press R1/RB again

Acquisition

SPOILER Defeat Genichiro Ashina in Ashina Castle P.442

![](images/b383ccc2f57d6f0d42ae450606c9218eccbc772462d935aed026914d5908851c.jpg)

![](images/1d7f152cb94a5cf0f8fbcdd540c052f65e948e069ab554408dc63972b8049d42.jpg)

Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu weaponizes the enemy's blood into a plume of red smoke that will daze and disorientate nearby enemies. Weaker enemies are made instantly vulnerable, allowing you to pick them off with Backstab Deathblows. Sub-bosses and tougher enemies will be stunned by the smoke, allowing you to land some hits, but you cannot perform a Deathblow on them.

Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu is therefore best used against groups of weaker enemies that are clustered together. For this purpose, it's one of the best crowd-control techniques in the game. An interesting quirk of Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu is that it causes Geckos to instead produce a green cloud of poisonous smoke and Albino Geckos to producing a cloud of white smoke that heals you.

![](images/451bcbe741ad475b39b510dd74a6ff31caa9d0d053e412247d967354cf3777b6.jpg)

# Puppeteer Ninjutsu

Ninjutsu technique that manipulates the victim like a puppet.

Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Activated after a Backstab

Deathblow. This technique temporarily forces one who should have fled this realm to remain. A puppet moves on behalf of its master, but its strings are destined to snap.

Activation Perform a Backstab Deathblow, then press R1/R8 again

Acquisition

SPOILER Defeat the Folding Screen Monkeys in Senpou Temple, Mt.

Kongo P.453

![](images/c8d216711be658073c08a7ea73515d978203a144cee88bc9edf1ea417d77a089.jpg)

# Unique Uses

Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Temple Grounds

Details Puppeteer the Assassin so that he operates the nearby kite device.

Sunken Valley Passage Bodhisattva Valley

Details Using it on the ape in the cave just past the Toxic Memorial Mob to distract the Great Serpent, allowing you to sneak past

![](images/ac3757418ebd0f119466c32f439c676a82dde47b8f767e69ea1a363ed051c833.jpg)

Puppeteer Ninjutsu allows you to turn enemies into puppets who will fight by your side for a short period of time. During that time they cannot be killed, and will keep fighting until the time runs

out, at which point they will automatically die. The fact that they cannot be killed for the duration of the skill means that any enemy you puppet can become a force on the battlefield, regardless of how traditionally weak they are. Puppets will automatically alert and engage any enemies that come within their range, with means they can be excellent distractions, allowing you to sneak past the otherwise preoccupied enemies.

Ideal candidates for becoming a puppet are fast, aggressive enemies that will attack often and inflict a lot of damage, or enemies with wide sweeping attacks that will hit multiple opponents and cause large distractions; avoid using enemies that are traditionally defensive or passive in nature. Other than the amount of Spirit Emblems you have, there is technically no limit to the amount of puppets you can have active at any one time, but in practical terms you'll rarely be able to have more than two or three before the initial ones start dying.

The enemies that your puppets kill will also give you all the Skill EXP that you would have gained had you killed them yourself. Do watch out though, as your puppet's attacks can still accidentally hurt you, so be careful when fighting next to one of them. One of the best applications for this skill is to use it on a strong enemy that's near a sub-boss, giving you a powerful ally that can help give you an advantage in the battle.

![](images/848093b82b25d893d1e7987d6746a6dc87afd64097ec07bf0aef5ccdea3cf2a1.jpg)

# Bestowal Ninjutsu

Ninjutsu technique that wreathes a blade in the victim's blood, extending its reach. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Activated after a Backstab Deathblow. The Wolf discovered this technique upon beheading a foe with the Mortal Blade, forming a cursed sword from spilled blood. Though it bears likeness to the Mortal Blade, it cannot kill the undying.

Activation  $\nrightarrow$  Perform a Backstab Deathblow, then press [R1/R8] again

# Acquisition

SPOILER Use the Mortal Blade on the Guardian Ape after defeating it in the Guardian Ape's Burrow P451

The Bestowal Ninjutsu will wreathe the blood of your enemy around your katana for thirty seconds. This blood acts as a second, separate source of damage that surrounds your basic attacks, essentially creating a blood-blade, which boasts incredible range—especially the thrust attack, which fires a stream of blood almost like a projectile.

The blood-blade deals half the Vitality and Posture damage of your attacks, and this damage cannot be guarded against. When the attacks from your katana and the blood-blade coalesce, their damage output will stack, allowing you to deal  $50\%$  more damage at close range. This allows you to quickly overwhelm and Posture-break even some of the most difficult strong enemies in the game. While the blood-blade is extremely powerful, enemies can still deflect it, or use armored attacks to hit you out of your attacks, meaning you still can't use it recklessly.

![](images/4b5bdc817d8c7af7ed2287efdef122302a21a20eefc29c79d8af115c4bff3b97.jpg)

![](images/e2b7cbc7375d3730fb9c548bb12d55e4e3adafa640cde1945abfb1ca48e9f64c.jpg)

Similar to the Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu, using Bestowal Ninjutsu on a Gecko will envelop your katana in the blood of the beast, allowing your blood-blade to take on additional properties. With a normal Gecko your blade will become coated in poison, with each attack you do also inflicting poison build-up. Track down a rare Albino Gecko, however, and you'll be able to gain the ability to heal yourself with every strike.

# 忍县

Chapter 2

# The Shinobi Toolkit

Mastery of the sword is essential, but a true shinobi will use absolutely anything at their disposal before drawing their blade in battle. The many tools and items that the Wolf draws upon are catalogued and explained on the pages that follow.

![](images/6c31e7f3f6cd9474bfdd9a290e8d996476bbf2d2fc230ffd24f3a7db4e9604b8.jpg)

# Shinobi Prosthetic Tools

While travelling through Ashina you will find ten items that can be converted into Tools for your Prosthetic Arm. To attach these items, after you've exhausted all the initial dialogue with the Sculptor, talk to him again and select the Fit New Prosthetic Tool option.

Prosthetic tools have a wide variety of applications and require Spirit Emblems to use. Once these tools have been mastered, they can give you an immense advantage in both combat and stealth situations. It is no exaggeration to say that your survival hinges upon mastery of the Prosthetic Arm.

# Restructuring Prosthetic Tools

All Prosthetic Tools can be upgraded. First though, you will need the Mechanical Barrel item, which you gain early on in your adventure after defeating Gyoubu (P.170). Return to the Sculptor who will fit the Mechanical Barrel to your arm.

From here, you can then talk to the Sculptor and pick the Upgrade Prosthetic Tool to bring up the Prosthetic Tool Upgrades tree.

Within the Prosthetic Tool Upgrades tree there are six levels of upgrades, each which will be unlocked as you gain more tools. The lines stemming from each Tool show what subsequent Tools it unlocks, so for example the Spinning Shuriken will unlock the Loaded Spear Thrust Type and Spring-load Axe. Once a Tool has been unlocked, you then have the option to upgrade if you have the required resource materials and Sen to pay the Sculptor. On the right side of the upgrade tree you can see information for each tool. Pressing  $\mathbf{Y} / \mathbf{A}$  will toggle between between a brief summary of what the tool does, how to use it, as well as the required materials. These upgrade materials can be found dotted around Ashina and will be dropped by certain enemies.

# Farming Resource Materials

The big table to the right shows the best spots to find enemies to farm resource materials from, as well as which Peddler sells each. In general, don't focus too much on trying to unlock as many tools as quickly as possible. The best farming spots aren't available until quite late in the game, and if you're picking up items as you progress, you will naturally have enough in your inventory to upgrade at a steady rate. When you do decide to farm materials though, the Virtuous Deed and Most Virtuous Deed Latent Skills in the Temple Arts skill-tree as well the Mibu Possession and Pilgrimage Balloons will increase the drop rate of rare items. Golden Vortex also allows you to double the amount of items and Sen that enemies drop. It will be impossible for you to unlock all the tool upgrades in a single playthrough, mainly because there are only six Lapis Lazuli available, and you will need ten in order to upgrade to all the Lazulite Tools.

# > Upgrade Items

Certain tool upgrades also need an additional Key Item in addition to the required Sen, upgrade materials and Tools. The table to the right shows the relevant information.

As the time of day changes (P.42), rare item drop rates increase. Certain enemies only drop certain items at specific times of day. Also only specific sub-categories of enemies may drop the resource materials that you need. This information is next to the enemy in question on the table. If a time of day is shown in the table here, it means from that time of day onwards, unless there's an arrow specifically showing a range.

# Loaded Shuriken

# Prosthetic Tool

A Shuriken Wheel Prosthetic Tool, fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Pull a shuriken loaded into the wheel and launch it at a target in a single, flowing motion. The swiftly thrown shuriken damages enemy Vitality and Posture, particularly against those with a tendency to take to the air.

![](images/05ea4b527620c53bbc8ac977dee6a5e8dd883309af381d493c86fcb6414d9ead.jpg)

# Overview

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Shuriken Throw</td><td>D</td><td>E</td><td>1</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4">Acquisition Pick up the Shuriken Wheel next to the dead Nightjar Ninja near to the “Outskirts Wall - Castle Gate Path” Idol in Ashina Outskirts (P.159).</td></tr></table>

Due to its multi-purpose nature the Loaded Shuriken is an indispensable part of your toolkit. We recommend always keeping it equipped in one of your Prosthetic slots, except in very specialized situations which we'll cover later. Loaded Shuriken are incredibly fast and, as you would expect from a projectile, have huge range. Aimlessly throwing Shuriken at enemies won't do much good, though. Many enemies can guard Shuriken, which is generally a waste of Spirit Emblems. They don't deal a lot of Vitality or Posture damage either, except against specific attacks. However, when used skillfully at the right moments, it has a plethora of uses against a wide variety of enemies. At only one Spirit Emblem per use, this is also a very cost-effective tool, and its utility only expands as you learn new Skills and upgrade the Shuriken.

Shuriken are extremely effective against fragile enemies such as Hounds or Old Maids, who can be quickly dispatched with a single throw. Remember to manually switch targets after each kill as it's faster than allowing the auto-lock to do it for you. Slightly sturdier, but still defensively weak enemies, such as the Matchlock-wielding Ashina Soldiers, can have their Posture reduced quickly with a few Shuriken, allowing you to weaken them from a distance. They are also very effective against airborne enemies; a single well-placed Shuriken will send them crashing to the ground. This sometimes results in a Critical Hit signified by a very satisfying "ching" noise to signify you've timed the Shuriken correctly. This anti-air hit deals considerable Posture damage and can even result in an instant Posture-break against certain enemies.

Shuriken can also be used to interrupt moves from a distance if you don't have time to dash in and attack. A good example of this is the blue aura that Samurai Generals and Samurai Fencers will sometimes use when they have accrued enough Posture damage. Not all attacks can be interrupted, though, especially those with armor. Finally, against enemies who cannot, or seldom, guard ranged attacks, the Shuriken is a good way to safely deal Vitality and Posture damage. Even against guarding enemies, the Shuriken can be used to maintain pressure from a distance before their Posture gauge begins to recover.

![](images/84908228525d251db71a3a26dd19a5f63339b8d82bec6be5aaf5407f6904a306.jpg)  
Landing a Shuriken on an airborne opponent is often considered a Critical Hit, resulting in massive Posture damage.

![](images/49ee12aee5ae51d7bed9288fde60db86e297e4505263d6616f70f31d209db4de.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

Usually when throwing a Shuriken, you are unable to move and are briefly vulnerable. By unlocking the Mid-Air Prosthetics Skill in the Prosthetic Arts skill tree, you can throw a Shuriken in the air while jumping in any direction. A mobile target is much harder to hit than a stationary one, so throwing a Shuriken while jumping is less risky and allows you to reposition yourself even while maintaining pressure on the enemy.

Mid-air Shuriken can be used to deal a bit of damage when jumping laterally or backwards to avoid long-reaching attacks. Although jumping directly towards an enemy while throwing a Shuriken may seem like a good idea, this can often put you in a bad position as there's a good chance your opponent will have recovered before you land.

![](images/4b4eb8ea30652a61fb4ced0048bbed2023fa75d45d568261e7d5813ce2af7c59.jpg)  
After evading an attack with a jump, throw a Shuriken at the vulnerable enemy.

The Chasing Slice, as the name implies, allows you to follow up a Shuriken with a dashing attack. Against enemies who are forced into a guarding state by the Shuriken, this is an excellent way to quickly take the initiative from range. Weaker enemies can be quickly Posture-broken with a single Shuriken into a Chasing Slice followed by a few attacks. Be careful against stronger enemies though, since if they guard the Shuriken they will often Deflect the Chasing Slice, leaving you in a bad position.

Chasing Slice is also useful for maintaining pressure. Mobile enemies such as the Nightjar Ninja will try to escape or jump away once they've taken a certain amount of Posture damage. The Chasing Slice also turns Shuriken into a very effective way of punishing enemies who leave their guard open. If you see an enemy miss an attack from a distance, then the Shuriken-Chasing Slice combo will serve as a speedy and dependable punisher.

Be careful when using this combo against armored attacks, however, as neither the Shuriken nor Chasing Slice can interrupt them.

![](images/e6aa11934b6753dd42b9c2b98e0c77539d90dbe46c4d50ac24055b63da5cd2ad.jpg)

Chasing Slice can be used to initiate the offense and quickly overwhelm weaker enemies. This strategy won't work against stronger enemies who guard the Shuriken though, as they will Deflect the incoming Chasing Slice. Against them, the Shuriken-Chasing Slice combo should only be used as a punisher.

# Spinning Shuriken Tool Upgrade

An enhanced Shuriken that can be empowered with rotational energy. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Damage an enemy's Vitality and Posture, and does huge damage to jumping enemies. Taking a moment to further bend the spring and build rotational energy will cause the blade to rotate after landing, damaging the enemy multiple times on hit. Similar to a spinning top, but with blades.

![](images/a907951a16044038b2eedd035cc13bdf229d0c928f1368481d3aa4b76df514ef.jpg)

Spinning Shuriken allows you to charge up the Shuriken, making it hit three times without raising the cost in Spirit Emblems. The triple Shuriken is only released after a full charge; anything less will result in a single Shuriken. This is the same with all the Prosthetic tools; they need to be fully charged if you want the upgraded attack. Charging takes time which leaves you vulnerable for longer, so you'll need to exercise more caution on when to to throw a charged Shuriken as opposed to an uncharged one.

Aside from the extra Vitality and Posture damage that it deals, the biggest benefit to a charged Shuriken is how it puts enemies into a protracted reeling stun if it connects. If you manage to land a charged Shuriken on an enemy who has their guard down, typically after they have missed a move, they'll be vulnerable for a long time. This will allow you to set up powerful attacks, such as an Ichimonji,

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Spinning Shur. Throw (1st attack)</td><td>E</td><td>F</td><td>1</td></tr><tr><td>Spinning Shur. Throw (2nd attack)</td><td>E</td><td>F</td><td>-</td></tr><tr><td>Spinning Shur. Throw (3rd attack)</td><td>E</td><td>E</td><td>-</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4">Additional Properties ▶ Can charge the Shuriken to hit three times.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4">Req. Materials ▶ 200 Sen, Scrap Iron x3</td></tr></table>

which deals major Posture damage even if it's guarded. Do take note that this reeling stun generally won't work on heavier enemies. Overall, Spinning Shuriken improves the Shuriken's efficacy as a ranged attack tool and punisher; just be sure to account for the extra charge time when using it.

![](images/fc4959ade451db0bfdd5feb08f6287ea0d0044a774cc98c512b1188b9ed1d0db.jpg)  
Spinning Shuriken places enemies into a reeling stun if it connects...

![](images/8e1ce293fe27a21e8ada11b7c9b871f42dfc1b615dbad1ed91d2e4bd9b15f492.jpg)  
...allowing you to set-up powerful Combat Arts such as Ichimonji if you're close enough.

# Gouging Top Tool Upgrade

An enhanced shuriken that pierces enemies with its sharp blades. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. These piercing blades retain momentum after landing, and will damage an enemy's Vitality and Posture, even if guarded. Taking a moment to further bend the spring and build rotational energy will cause the blade to rotate after landing, damaging the enemy multiple times on hit.

![](images/d30f48a26485410cd15d641988f96b1d0ce79cceecba31f2232ebae2a563ddb7.jpg)

Gouging Top adds the Piercing damage attribute to Shuriken, which means they inflict Vitality damage even against guarding enemies. They don't deal any more Posture damage though. Think of it as a latent buff to the Spinning Shuriken. It does everything that regular Shuriken can do, but better, thanks to the extra Vitality damage it inflicts when guarded.

![](images/27afff4f96a2da6990ae3eb2eb7050c71635cafdc2e79931f5db30f090337f96.jpg)  
The Gouging Top can rip through multiple enemies at a time.

When charged, this is a decent way to whittle down an enemy's Vitality and Posture from a safe distance. It's still not recommended to just aimlessly throw Shuriken though, as this isn't a very efficient use of your Spirit Emblems. Another useful feature of the Gouging Top is that they will cut clean through flesh when they hit. This means that if there is a line of enemies ahead of you, then a Gouging Top will cut through and hurt them all, with no reduction in damage on the way. Even if an enemy guards a Shuriken, the one behind them may still get damaged by it.

# Phantom Kunai Tool Upgrade

Lady Butterfly's kunai, fitted into the shuriken wheel. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Creates a special sound when thrown, which causes phantom butterflies to follow the path of the kunai. The phantom butterflies chase after enemies and inflict damage even when guarded.

![](images/fa8fe1d6b6584303939aaea4f99bde3388174d69984ea9a3b59043d8a29ac8de.jpg)

Phantom Kunai releases Phantom Butterflies that home in on enemies. These appear alongside the regular Shuriken, now shaped as a Kunai.A standard Kunai toss releases three Phantom Butterflies, a charged Swarming Dance Kunai releases seven. The Kunai do not deal Piercing damage like the Gouging Top, nor do they cut through flesh. A charged Kunai toss also won't result in the same reeling stun that charged Spinning Shuriken do.

The Phantom Butterflies go directly towards a target if you're locked onto it, otherwise they'll home in on the closest enemy along their flightpath. Locking onto a target greatly increases the range that the butterflies can travel, though, so we recommend locking on before throwing the Kunai. The Kunai has the same travel speed as a Shuriken, but the butterflies travel much slower. This speed differential can be used to your advantage when combined with Chasing Slice, since the Phantom Butterflies will trail behind you and cover the recovery on your attack. The Kunai therefore boosts the Shuriken's utility as an offense initiator.

Since these Butterflies have the Spirit attribute, they will inflict Vitality damage to guarding enemies and are very effective against Illusions. Swarming Dance Kunai can also deal very impressive damage for a projectile, but only if all seven Butterflies connect.

Often though, the outer Butterflies tend to miss unless your distance from the enemy is just right in the mid-range. Landing all the Butterflies against more mobile foes is also quite inconsistent. If there's an obstacle blocking the way such as a pillar or some raised ground, the Butterflies will be stopped by them. However, against slower, bigger enemies faced on even terrain, running away and throwing charged Phantom Kunai is a safe, effective way of whittling down their Vitality.

# Sen Throw Tool Upgrade

A Prosthetic Tool that shoots loaded coin bundles. Costs sen and Spirit Emblems to use. While it lacks a shuriken's range, it inflicts far more damage, as the coins hit multiple times. The amount of coins thrown increases depending on how much money one possesses. Being rich makes the blast incredibly strong, but an empty purse will shoot nothing but dust.

![](images/f3670612e2d71a05a52804dafadd37753643a039746312e644d8a5a93b39acb5.jpg)

As the name suggests, Sen Throw will hurl Sen instead of Shuriken. You will throw more coins depending on how much money is in your inventory. Of all the Shuriken types, these have the potential to deal the most Vitality and Posture damage. A single charged Sen Throw when you have  $1000+$  Sen can severely damage the Posture of even the strongest of enemies at close range. The coins also have a wide spread, which makes them a surprisingly effective crowd-control tool, especially when combined with Chasing Slice. However, there are a few caveats, the most obvious being that they cost money. At 10 Sen for Sen Throw and 15 Sen for Raining Money, hurling Sen around is not sustainable in the long term. Secondly,

![](images/8aa770dcf8af2313057ed4b90b42e2f761b05c6ca95308419a34cd893caf47c0.jpg)  
The wide spread of the coins makes Sen Throw and particularly Raining Money good at dealing with groups of enemies.

if the opponent guards the Sen, they deal no Vitality damage and minimal Posture damage, so you may just be wasting your money and Spirit Emblems. They also lack the range of traditional Shuriken and the coins spread out the further they travel. This means that you want to be as close to enemies as possible when using this tool. Because of the added risk (and since the coins can be guarded) this tool is best used when an enemy is recovering after they miss an attack. On New Game+, it becomes more practical, since enemies drop more Sen and you'll have already purchased many Key Items and Tool Upgrades.

# Lazulite Shuriken Tool Upgrade

Shuriken blessed with the favor of the Fountainhead Lapis Lazuli. Its piercing edge heavily damages Vitality, and damages Vitality and Posture even if guarded. These blades do not slow down, even after striking an enemy. The lazulite blue trail of light it emits in flight is reminiscent of a shooting star.

![](images/0bdf74fc15892c19fdf58d04abb765845d2fff41b126e6edbb238043dfea5f0a.jpg)

Lazulite Shuriken are another latent buff that stack along with the Gouging Top, dealing both Piercing and Spirit damage. Both attributes damage an enemy's Vitality even when they guard. This means that the Lazulite Shuriken inflict even more Vitality damage against guarding enemies than the Gouging Top. This makes it an excellent tool to whittle down an enemy's Vitality from a safe distance. Compared to the Butterflies surrounding the Phantom Kunai, the Spirit damage of the Lazulite Shuriken is all concentrated within the Shuriken itself. Although the Phantom Kunai has the potential to deal more damage than the Lazulite Shuriken, this is only if all the Butterflies connect, and as mentioned previously they tend to miss unless you're at the perfect range. The Lazulite Shuriken consumes less Spirit Emblems and is more reliable than the Phantom Kunai, especially against highly mobile enemies or on uneven terrain. Whether to use the Kunai or Lazulite Shuriken therefore depends on the situation. If you're looking to initiate of

# Loaded Axe Prosthetic Tool

![](images/a49bef5313ba1f7959364814bd81b408580da8d0a08611f26d05e74fd7983512.jpg)

A Prosthetic Tool loaded with a heavy Shinobi Axe. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. The strength of the Loaded Axe lies in its heft. One strike can easily turn a wooden shield into splinters or shred an enemy's posture.

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Strike</td><td>B</td><td>S</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td>Mid-air Strike</td><td>D</td><td>D</td><td>2</td></tr></table>

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  Take the Shinobi Axe of the Monkey from the shrine about to be looted near the "Estate Path" idol in Hirata Estate (P.177).

# Overview

The Loaded Axe is a real powerhouse of a weapon. It deals tons of Posture damage, and is an armored attack, meaning that it cannot be stopped by most other moves. Although the reward for landing a blow with the Axe is great, it also carries a weighty risk. The Axe is slow, recovers slowly, and you still take  $100\%$  damage during the armored phase. Without knockback to move you out of the way of subsequent enemy attacks, using it at the wrong time could outright kill you. The Axe's armor is far from infallible though; you can still be interrupted by heavier, more powerful attacks. However, if you start the Axe early enough it can interrupt them.

Since the Loaded Axed takes a while to strike, it will often result in a trade with the enemy's attack. Since enemies deal so much damage, a trade is usually not to your benefit, meaning its uses are far more specialized than the multi-purpose Shuriken. However, when the Axe is needed, it is absolutely indispensable. The Axe is the only tool that will allow you to directly damage enemies with wooden shields. After reducing their shield to splinters with a single blow, weaker enemies are left in a Posture-broken state.

Since the Axe deals so much Posture damage, it can Posturebreak certain enemies like Ashina Soliders and Bandits in one strike. When you find yourself surrounded, this can be a good way to quickly reduce the ranks of nearby enemies. Remember that if you Posture-break an enemy, the recovery on your attack is

canceled. This is especially useful with the Axe's lengthy recovery. You may take some damage while attacking, but if you've acquired the two "Breath of Life" Latent Skills, then this damage will be mitigated. You can further reduce the damage of incoming enemy attacks with an Ungo's Sugar or Spiritfall, which temporarily raises your defense. Ungo and the Axe make a powerful combination.

Aside from leaving you immobile for so long upon use, the other issue with the Axe is its relatively short range. Using the Axe while sprinting though will help alleviate this quite a bit, since you will transfer the momentum from the run into the swing of the Axe. This allows you to pull off some exciting berserker runs at the enemy to quickly dispose of them. Use this against archers and rifle-men, since they'll constantly interrupt you with their projectiles. Run at them with the Axe to make short work of them.

The Axe is also a good way to rack up Posture damage against bosses, but only when you pick your moments carefully, for example after performing a successful Mikiri Counter. This is by no means a rule of thumb though, so watch out. Also, when you see a tough enemy's Posture gauge is flashing red, and you need just a bit more damage to Posture-break them, then this can be a good time to sprint at them with the Axe. Just make sure you have enough Vitality to withstand the incoming attack. Finally the Axe is also capable of guard crushing enemies, which is especially useful in conjunction with the Fang and Blade follow-up..

![](images/eca21c3ce51f73789c36367b4324e9e3fb6c81b655b7b6aceefc9ffdf7c95163.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

The Axe's biggest shortcomings are its relatively short range, along with its lengthy windup that leaves you wide open to enemy attacks. The Mid-air Prosthetics Skill goes a long way to alleviating both these problems, while retaining its ability to armor through attacks. The extra mobility comes at the price of damage however. The mid-air strike only deals  $60\%$  of the Vitality damage of a standard grounded Axe strike, and  $44\%$  the Posture damage. Relative to most other mid-air attacks this is still very damaging, though.

Using the Axe while in mid-air not only makes it quicker, it also greatly extends its range and flexibility by extension of the jump. By jumping towards an enemy and unleashing the Axe, you cover a great distance. Backwards and lateral jumps also help add some evasive qualities to the Axe. If you successfully dodge an attack with a jump, and then unleash the Axe while the enemy is recovering, you can deal some respectable Vitality and Posture damage.

![](images/e67122f3d78f75fb0418eb4e29e1bfa0af37a48d306498e94535b87e06a118f8.jpg)  
Jump towards an enemy and unleash the Axe to greatly increase the range of its attack.

After unlocking Fang and Blade in the Prosthetic Arts skill tree, you can follow up an Axe attack with a huge double slice, where you leap forward with both the Axe and katana. The follow-up attack deals roughly  $55\%$  of the Posture damage to the preceding Axe strike and also boasts armor, essentially giving you a large increase in Posture damage, at no additional Spirit Emblem cost. This can also be done after a mid-air Axe attack.

Since the initial Axe strike will crush the guard of most enemies (even stronger bosses), this prevents them from retaliating and makes it safe to follow up with the Fang and Blade follow-up. If you connect with the initial Axe strike it's also safe to transition into the follow-up. Do watch out though; being a longer total animation, you are left vulnerable for longer, so this can be risky to use during encounters with a group of enemies.

![](images/6fa26fc3cf5972d1467e6bf14b10cdad6ecd2d94165a52cf0b7590b3874225d7.jpg)

Ungo's Sugar synergizes with Fang and Blade by lowering the damage taken when armoring through attacks with the Axe.

# Spring-load Axe Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Axe reinforced with a spring mechanism. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. The strength of the Loaded Axe lies in its heft. The weight allows one to shrug off incoming attacks, and can easily turn a wooden shield into splinters. Storing and unleashing energy in the spring mechanism allows for large, sweeping attacks despite its weight.

![](images/0a0c5aa6cda3a87d558f82c2ecdd6b0fe9c1c07c9044817c8a27880226e5049c.jpg)

With the Spring-load you can charge up the Axe for a very damaging two-hit strike consisting of a WhirlingSlash into a helm-splitter. This can then be followed by Fang and Blade for three hits. The charged attack takes even longer to strike, but deals massive Vitality and Posture damage. The Axe in general is a high-risk, high-reward tool, and the Spring-load emphasizes this even further; the reward is even greater, but so is the risk.

If you press  $\boxed{R1} / \boxed{R2}$  again right after the WhirlingSlash, you will do another one. You can then continue pressing  $\boxed{R1} / \boxed{R2}$  to keep on spinning indefinitely, turning you into a (mostly) unstoppable vortex of death. Each rotation costs two Spirit Emblems. As long as Vitality and Spirit Emblems allow, you can keep on spinning, though do watch out as the WhirlingSlash has less stopping power than a standard Axe strike, so doesn't break armored attacks as reliably.

# Sparking Axe Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Axe with an attached percussion hammer to create flame. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Metes out attacks bathed in flame from the axe's blade. Hitting the sparking percussion hammer causes a violent eruption of flames and increases the effective area of the attack. This is both firearm and heavy axe.

![](images/ba9acd13193621c4009aee02996afaa7ff3aa630cbb129e08fa66bac79d0eea6.jpg)

The Sparking Axe costs one more Spirit Emblem, but adds an explosion to the Loaded Axe's attacks. The Fire explosion increases the range and area of the attack; its large area of effect and ability to inflict Burn make it strong against crowds of weaker enemies. The explosion and Axe are two distinct sources of damage. The explosion deals Fire damage, and the Axe still deals physical damage. Only when they coalesce will full damage be dealt.

![](images/20ad5b29c73eecb9e93247cd2a96ce33f42578c7c86af7cdacf9577405cc2a76.jpg)

# Lazulite Axe Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Axe blessed with the favor of the Fountainhead Lapis Lazuli. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. The hefty lazulite blade inflicts damage even on guarding enemies. The sound of the lapis lazuli blade striking home creates a powerful reverberation capable of dispelling enemy illusions.

![](images/4dc019dd3b116981e463ff69103982058d8caa3951f3401b5194eb240fd1f561.jpg)

The Lazulite Axe changes the Fire attribute of the explosion to Spirit. The attacks all do roughly  $10\%$  more damage, and despite also emitting a large explosion like the Sparking Axe, aside from being blue now, it is not a separate attack from the Axe itself. This means the Lazulite Axe has a slightly smaller area of effect than the Sparking Axe, and so is not as effective at managing crowds. The fire properties are now lost, so it won't be as effective against Red-Eyed enemies, but Spirit damage is highly effective against Illusions.

# Loaded Spear Prosthetic Tool

A Prosthetic Tool loaded with Gyoubu's Broken Horn. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Unleash far-reaching thrust attacks. Lighter enemies struck by the spear may be dragged towards the wielder. Those of large build will at times force themselves into poorly-fitting armor. Such armor could be torn clean off; coined by Gyoubu as Armor Stripping.

![](images/178e697de9b0e7c068f1ea66cecaea9facf54617db1327390e37ea9b1ef8a775.jpg)

# Overview

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Thrust</td><td>C</td><td>C</td><td>1</td></tr><tr><td>Drag</td><td>E</td><td>-</td><td>-</td></tr></table>

Acquisition Use the Gatehouse Key to open the locked building in Ashina Reservoir. Gyoubu's Broken Horn can be found inside (P.215).

The Loaded Spear is a mid-range tool that can be used to launch a Thrust attack on an enemy from a distance. Being a Thrust attack, it cannot be guarded, however it is prone to being deflected, which only deals very minor Posture damage. Aside from being a waste of Spirit Emblems, this can also be very risky, so poking around aimlessly with the Spear is not recommended.

While the damage is average, the Spear boasts incredible range. In comparison to your other long range tool, the Shuriken, is much less damaging. So, the main purpose of the Spear is to chip away at an enemy's Vitality from a reasonably safe distance by punishing the recovery on their moves. Against enemies that have ongoing spinning attacks, such as the Red Guard, the Spear is also a good way to inflict Vitality damage on them from a safe distance.

Another useful application of the Spear is crowd control. By pressing RT/R2 twice, you will thrust and then pull back the Spear. This will Drag lighter enemies towards you, thereby separating and isolating them from a crowd. As you upgrade the Spear it also starts gaining some very useful area-covering attacks, allowing you to manage groups of enemies in a variety of patterns. The charged attack on the Thrust type is ideal for dealing with a row of enemies directly in front of you, while the circular attack of the Cleave type is great for dealing with a group of enemies clustered around you.

![](images/0c834d104b03b8c386384683e7d4a1e4ea87e9440ccd64fa056874e792becb47.jpg)  
The Loaded Spear can strip the armor off of certain enemies, resulting in major Posture damage.

A very specialised feature of the Spear is its Armor Stripping ability. This only works on a handful of enemies, but is indispensable in these encounters. By latching onto their Armor with the Spear, and then pressing  $\frac{R1}{R2}$  again to yank the Spear back, you can rip the armor off of enemies such as the Bell-wielding Taro Troop guarding the entrance to the Abandoned Dungeon, inflicting a large burst of Posture damage. It can even be used to pull the parasite out of one of the bosses, dealing massive Vitality and Posture damage.

![](images/0de29456a9d5a26fca87a8d1b892b3f04188c48f324bc81f75e685509d5bb2b5.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

As with all tools, unlocking the Mid-Air Prosthetic ability allows you to stay mobile with a jump while still attacking the enemy. This is especially useful with the Loaded Spear, since its main use is to punish the recovery of an enemy's moves. By jumping laterally and then using the Spear in mid-air you can both evade an incoming attack and then immediately punish. Jumping forward into the Spear attack greatly extends the Spear's range, allowing you to punish missed moves and interrupt slow attacks from a long distance away, though you must be careful that the attack doesn't have armor properties. Jumping backwards with the Spear is the most situational option, but can be used to occasionally punish enemies who chase after you.

![](images/271af8ec9c02d3a43953c9eb8dc464270a3fc057c9161e06f4d2bfd0463104a5.jpg)

Due to its range the Loaded Spear is an excellent tool to punish the recovery of an enemy's attack. This is made all the stronger if you can follow up with Chasing Slice. Dance around the enemy's maximum range to make them miss an attack, and then retaliate with a Spear thrust followed by a Chasing Slice. Avoid using this combo recklessly and instead wait for a clear opening before striking. As mentioned, the Spear is quite prone to being deflected, so carelessly following up with a Chasing Slice when this happens effectively just places you in harm's way. If the enemy deflects your Chasing Slice, always be ready to instantly guard or deflect an incoming counterattack.

![](images/6843a5814d7d86cf836d0de4431297bf3a5fd2eb001ed4e14d1d461756a49c9d.jpg)

# Fang and Blade Skill P.58

By pressing  $\mathbb{R}1 / \mathbb{R}2$  twice, you can use the Spear to Drag enemies and start attacking them at close range. With Fang and Blade unlocked, this strategy becomes much more effective as you can then immediately start attacking after dragging the enemy towards you. This again should only be used as a punisher on a vulnerable enemy, since if you hook in a guarding enemy they can often interrupt you before the Fang and Blade. However, it can be a very effective way of methodically picking off enemies from a crowd without putting yourself in harm's way. The strategy of dragging an opponent and striking with Fang and Blade is generally only recommended against weaker enemies, as many bosses and tougher enemies will be able to deflect or even interrupt the follow-up after being dragged, even if they weren't guarding.

# Spiral Spear Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Spear with a spiral chiseled into the blade. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Sharp thrust attacks from this Prosthetic Tool damage an enemy's Vitality and Posture, even through their guard. The spear's spiral creates a corkscrew shockwave that gouges and rends as it penetrates.

The charged attack really allows you to plow through enemies directly in front of you for considerable Posture and Vitality damage, regardless of if they are guarding or not. Its increased damage output also makes the Spiral Spear's standard Corkscrew Thrust all the more effective as a means to punish enemies who leave their guard open.

# Loaded Spear Cleave type

# Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Spear further reinforced with an enhanced spring mechanism. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Unleash far-reaching thrust attacks. Lighter enemies struck by the spear may be dragged towards the wielder. Can also tear poorly-fitting armor from heavier foes. Store energy in the spring mechanism for a powerful cleaving attack.

The Cleave type changes the charge attack of the Loaded Spear into a wide, circular attack, making it an excellent tool for managing groups of enemies. The wind-up is quite lengthy so you should try to charge the Cleave attack from a safe distance. You can also cancel a large portion of the recovery by guarding or dodging. The only risk comes from its slow wind-up leaving you vulnerable.

Once it gets going the Cleave boasts a lot of stopping power, meaning it can interrupt many armored attacks. It also causes a guard crush even on even heavier enemies, which pushes them back while dealing significant Posture damage. This leaves the enemy unable to deflect a Chasing Slice follow up. Overall the Cleave type excels at crowd-control, being particularly effective against the Seekers in Senpou Temple, and gets only stronger once upgraded to the Leaping Flame.

![](images/f89103e0fe99a91380a328ffbbda5040f2df14c0f32dadd9d65734f6a5ac98ff.jpg)

# Leaping Flame Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Spear with an attached percussion hammer to create flame. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Bathe the tip of the Loaded Spear in flames making it a dangerously sharp spear and firearm. A charged strike of the spear will knock enemies down and consume them in a fiery blaze.

A Prosthetic Tool made with the blade Sabimaru, allowing for a quick series of attacks together with the sword. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. The blue, poisonous rust on Sabimaru's blade applies "Poison" status abnormality. Wielded in wars of old, the blade's blue rust was used to drive off inhuman Okami warrior women. Even now, it is likely to be effective against their descendants.

![](images/e4bb8c127f30d10988eec92f0bbe475cc0c2e26c61ae251c1dda2a6802e02fd5.jpg)

# Overview

The Sabimaru is a poisoned dagger that launches you into a flurry of attacks that build the enemy's Poison gauge whether they hit or are guarded. This is a Poison unique to the Sabimaru, known as "Blue Rust Poison", and will have a strong effect on Okami type enemies. Once poisoned, their Vitality is continually drained for around twenty seconds, at which point the effects of the Poison wear off. The Posture damage when guarded is not especially impressive, though; the purpose of the strikes is mainly to inflict Poison. A single flurry will be enough to poison weaker enemies, while several will be needed against more resilient foes.

Due to the high rate of attack, Sabimaru can force some enemies to guard until the final strike where they'll almost assuredly deflect. Watch out though, as some enemies can perform an armored attack through the Sabimaru Combo. The full string is a six-hit combo, alternating with each strike between the Sabimaru and Kusabimaru. Starting the combo costs one Spirit Emblem, and every time you use Sabimaru, another Spirit emblem will be used, so the full string will consume three Spirit Emblems. This means if you want to use Sabimaru you'll need to be careful about rationing your Spirit Emblems. Also, when you attack with Sabimaru, your back is completely exposed for a long time, so be very careful when using it during group encounters.

Due to the high Spirit Emblem cost and how it leaves you vulnerable for so long against crowds, the Sabimaru is quite a specialized tool. When used in the right place against the right enemy though, the Sabimaru is devastating. It is a great tool to use when you get an opening on a single, tougher target. Sabimaru isn't really worth using against weaker enemies since Poison is slow-acting and weaker enemies can be killed very quickly through regular means.

![](images/a2f7ec7cc9171fa9fcab600e5c33012cdf13c178962bb4bc23738ae8f8c9e8e7.jpg)  
The Sabimaru boasts a high rate of attack which makes it good at locking enemies down.

The Sabimaru can inflict Blue Rust Poison on enemies, which is particularly effective against Okami...

Sabimaru is most effective against Okami type enemies. Once poisoned, Okami enemies will incur massive amounts of Posture damage and also go into in a unique, vomiting lun animation which leaves them vulnerable. The duration of this lun varies depending on the particular enemy, but will always lead to at least a few hits.

![](images/76fc2517af15f5423901a8efb6e60349d334e95bf5d37f2edf67bcbc06f26e11.jpg)  
...this will inflict heavy burst Vitality and Posture damage, as well as leaving them in a unique vomit stun.

With the Mid-Air Prosthetic skill, you can use Sabimaru during a jump to unleash two hits in quick succession. It can seamlessly transition into a Sabimaru Combo upon landing, so you can inflict a bit of Poison damage with the initial mid-air hits for a low cost before immediately transitioning into the rest of the Combo. The mid-air Sabimaru hits effectively replace the opening strike of the Combo so you seamlessly continue into it when you land. It's a great way to initiate a Sabimaru Combo, since you get the benefits of air mobility and can quickly close the gap.

On top of this, since the mid-air Sabimaru hits twice, initiating the Combo from mid-air deals a bit more Poison build-up for the same cost of three Emblems, making it both more effective and cost-efficient. Be sure to start the attack as you're descending from a jump, otherwise the first attack will go over many enemy's heads. Against taller enemies the timing is naturally much more lenient, though.

![](images/d8795bdbf3e6c0416f2c39de06334a84814761b160a83604ff659013f97f77fc.jpg)  
A mid-air Sabimaru strikes twice for the cost of one Spirit Emblem.

# Improved Sabimaru Tool Upgrade

An improved Sabimaru with a special mechanism for unleashing the blade. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Due to the revised mechanism, one can fluidly swap between two separate sets of attacks as desired. Has a blue rust poison applied to the blade that eats into enemies' defense and inflicts "Poison" status abnormality.

![](images/76dd26aff7f5f7ec6e9384603ca390ad2ca6c8d750b3294edb7e076f83d052cf.jpg)

The Improved Sabimaru allows you to unleash the Combo Change Attack with your katana at any time during the Sabimaru combo by pressing  $\boxed{R8} / \boxed{R1}$ , and then transition seamlessly into a new follow-up Combo with  $\boxed{R1} / \boxed{R2}$ . This follow-up Combo is slightly less airtight than the initial Sabimaru Combo, as it can be deflected on the 4th hit even if the enemy is guarding. You have a lot of time to delay in between the attacks though, so take your time to observe how the enemy is responding to the 2nd Combo and adapt accordingly. Stop attacking immediately if the enemy deflects, and be prepared to guard or counter-deflect.

The Combo Change Attack can also be used in combination with a directional input on the left analog stick to either move sideways or even backwards while attacking. When timed perfectly, you can use

![](images/d44cb7a1e3ef651cbf20fb2b06a8082f7bddc7505b1cbd7d97875befd338a668.jpg)  
The Combo Change Attack has some invincibility at the start, allowing you to evade enemy attacks if timed well.

# Lazulite Sabimaru Tool Upgrade

Sabimaru blessed with the favor of the Fountainhead Lapis Lazuli. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. The combination of Lapis Lazuli and the rusted blue blade produces a poisonous mist with every swing. Dissolving the Lapis Lazuli over the blade caused the ancient blue rust to bubble to the blade's surface.

![](images/695b7e299526f87497f48dc48f2582b5048aa05a2698ae4c17bcbeb5fc4ec73a.jpg)

The Lazulite Sabimaru removes the Piercing damage attribute of the Piercing Sabimaru. Instead each attack now emits a Poison mist, which lingers for a long time and has a wide area of effect. With this, the Sabimaru takes on a whole new utility. Along with increasing the rate of poison build-up during its combo, you can now also use the Sabimaru more defensively by attacking once and then retreating. The enemies are oblivious to the effect of the lingering poison cloud, and will walk right into it and Poison themselves while trying to approach you. This is especially effective when used with a hit-and-run strategy in tandem with mid-air Sabimaru strikes. Considering the main function of the Sabimaru is to inflict Poison, this is easily the best version of the tool, and overall a potent weapon with which to whittle down the Vitality of both groups of enemies as well as bosses. Against Okami enemies, the Lazulite upgrade also takes the Sabimaru from being merely powerful to absolutely devastating.

# Loaded Umbrella

# Prosthetic Tool

A Prosthetic Tool created by fitting an indestructible Iron-ribbed Umbrella to the Arm. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. When spread open, it will protect against attacks from all directions. Hold it out while moving to protect from light attacks. But this is an umbrella after all. It won't protect you from low attacks such as sweep attacks.

![](images/3635dce6ab6858833f516436dad6c40f41f4b08dabb4d6687063a6bcdf1f531e.jpg)

# Overview

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Projected Force Slice</td><td>B</td><td>A</td><td>1</td></tr></table>

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  Buy the Iron Fortress for 1600 Sen from Blackhat Badger (P.206) in Ashina Castle near the "Old Grave" Idol.

The Loaded Umbrella is a purely defensive tool that in and of itself has no attack to speak of. By holding  $\boxed{R1} / \boxed{R2}$  it creates a 360-degree shield around you that guards from all directions. This is useful when surrounded by enemies, and also to protect from projectiles that may blindside you. The Loaded Umbrella protects against all projectiles, even cannon-balls, but you will need an upgrade to protect against Fire or Spirit attacks. The Umbrella also allows you to move more freely while guarding against weak attacks, allowing you to quickly slip away from an overwhelming situation.

The Umbrella also guards Thrusts, which usually need to be deflected or Mikiri Countered, and is also invulnerable to Grabs. However, it is still vulnerable to Sweeps. It has more lenient timing for deflecting attacks than your regular katana, making it easier to deflect tricky Consecutive Attack strings that yield a lot of of Posture damage. It's also very good for deflecting attacks that you might feel are tricky or risky to deflect, but that can leave the enemy vulnerable when deflected. Due to this more generous deflect timing, and a  $50\%$  increase in the amount of Posture damage that a successful deflect yields, the Loaded Umbrella is particularly effective against enemies where playing defensively is required, such as O'Rin of the Water or the Ashina Elite. You can Posture-break one in as little as two Umbrella deflects on their Ashina Cross attack with two timed taps of  $\boxed{R1} / \boxed{R2}$ , though this is dependent on whether you've been boosting your Attack Power as it scales with deflect.

![](images/d3b6d55620ebaf0ee9a84a8c613f795929ba78fd6a178f0759b878d4d0a72f69.jpg)

The Loaded Umbrella provides 360-degree cover against projectiles.

The number of times you can guard or deflect with the Umbrella is limited due to the Spirit Emblem cost, preventing you from overrelying on the lenient deflect timing. One major weakness of the Umbrella is that your Posture will not recover while guarding with it. Be sure to intermittently release the Umbrella's guard in order to allow your Posture to recover. While guarding melee attacks with the Umbrella will result in taking the same amount of Posture damage as with a regular guard, it reduces the Posture damage taken from projectiles by  $80\%$ .

![](images/a23894c37f2eb4383dba7438c786e1e0f627da06d4259942538f748c622ceed8.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage

Skill P.57

Since the Umbrella isn't actually an attack, its mid-air applications are unfortunately quite limited. If you haven't unlocked the Mid-air Deflection skill under the Shinobi Arts skill-tree, which allows you to guard in mid air, it can make a good, if resource consuming, surrogate. Once the Umbrella is unfolded in mid-air it will stay open upon landing. If you attempt to use a jump into a mid-air Umbrella in order to escape a dangerous situation, you are vulnerable at the beginning of the jump before unfolding, so it's better to just use the Umbrella on the ground and walk away.

It's not completely without use, though. Despite the animation showing the Umbrella only protecting you from the front, it also has a full 360-degrees of protection. Since you are invulnerable to Sweeps while in mid-air, you are actually in a perfect guard for a brief time. A practical application of the mid-air Umbrella is to ensure your safety after jumping to avoid an attack, for example against a big area-of-effect attack, or to cover you while advancing towards the enemy, though this isn't something that a regular mid-air guard cannot achieve.

![](images/a8cfac6f72a4262a6d55c0b06a1fbd213a1adddcef295d5096449da5e3178df1.jpg)

The Mid-air Umbrella allows you to ensure your safety after jumping away from a wide area of effect attack.

<table><tr><td>Shockwave Lv1</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>A</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>A</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td><td>-</td></tr><tr><td>Shockwave Lv2</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>A</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>S</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td><td>-</td></tr><tr><td>Shockwave Lv3</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>S</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>S</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td><td>-</td></tr></table>

Projected Force allows you to launch into a wide cross-slash attack with both your katana and the Umbrella by pressing RB/R1 while guarding with the Umbrella. Although quite slow, the perfect time to use it is after you've deflected an enemy's attack. It has some armor properties, which will allow it to blow through light attacks if the enemy recovers in time after being deflected. This will deal considerable Vitality and Posture damage. Be careful not to overuse the Projected Force after every deflect with the Umbrella though; if the enemy is in the middle of a Consecutive Attack then you will be interrupted. If you guard enough enemy projectiles then the Loaded Umbrella will begin to emit steam, and charge with energy. You can then unleash that energy with the Projected Force to deliver an extremely long-ranged attack. This is particularly effective when facing a Cannon-wielding Sunken Valley Clan enemy since it only takes a couple of cannon shots to fully charge it, and then the Projected Force retaliation will almost guarantee a Posture-break. This charge will remain even if you fold the Umbrella, so you can unleash it any time, as long as you don't unequip the Umbrella in the menu.
