# Loaded Umbrella - Magnet

Tool Upgrade

A Loaded Umbrella upgraded with a magnetic mechanism. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. When spread open, it will protect against attacks from all directions. Hold it out while moving to protect from light attacks. Has a tempered magnetic shaft that makes it nearly unbreakable. Enemy attacks can be deflected by spinning the open umbrella.

![](images/71a5cd4043167455e1e8c06820f8cf8563e6692f03053d294b7c275e925074bb.jpg)

The Magnet variation of the Umbrella allows you to spin the Umbrella while it's open by pressing LB/L1, which will deflect incoming attacks. This effectively allows you to deflect while guarding. Each spin of the Umbrella retains the generous deflection timing of activating the Umbrella, and also the  $50\%$  Posture damage bonus, but costs another Spirit Emblem. The Umbrella Spin is a powerful defensive tool against enemies who struggle to Posture-break you, for example slow lumbering mid-bosses with a low rate of attack like Juzou the Drunkard. This allows you to get up close and focus on evading Sweep attacks, since everything else can be guarded or deflected. Be sure to sometimes release the Umbrella's guard and retreat in order to give your Posture time to recover.

![](images/ef81c0698397ec7943f3bf439618a7891192eadc911614d6a1f25f2277133196.jpg)

Against Juzou the Drunkard you can focus all your attention on avoiding his Sweep attack since everything else is guarded.

Emblems to use. When spread open, it will protect against attacks from all

An interesting feature of the Lotus Umbrella is that Red-Eyed enemies who fear fire, such as the Chained Ogre, will go into a cowering animation merely by unfolding it--you don't even need to attack. # Shinobi Firecracker Prosthetic Tool

A Prosthetic Tool fitted with Robert's firecrackers. Costs Spirit Emblems. Unleashes an explosive flash that briefly blinds foes and inflicts Posture damage on beast-type enemies. Has a wide, frontward field of effect that can impact multiple foes at once. Suitable for temporarily immobilizing enemies and particularly good for scaring beasts.

![](images/4aa958c32bbaa8fd4064ba9d9c467cd1c4a380456ed0a1bdd2ec79b810cc3314.jpg)

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Shinobi Firecracker</td><td>-</td><td>-</td><td>2</td></tr></table>

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  Buy Robert's Firecrackers for 500 Sen from either the Crow's Bed Memorial Mob (P.161), or the Battlefield Memorial Mob (P.171), both of which can be found in Ashina Outskirts.

# Overview

The Shinobi Firecracker is a multi-purpose tool that releases explosive squibs in an arc in front of you. It can be used both offensively to initiate the attack, and defensively as an escape tool. As you upgrade the Firecrackers, they also become a set-up tool leading to traps that can inflict tremendous damage if pulled off successively.

The Shinobi Fireracker explosions blind enemies, which puts them in a stun animation. Blind stun is quite long, lasting about three seconds, giving you time to set up slow but powerful Combat Arts such as Ichimonji or Mortal Draw. You also have enough time to run behind enemies and hit them in the back with your basic attack. This allows you to deal more damage against enemies who can guard since they'll have to turn around before they can begin guarding your attacks again. A Fistful of Ash can also be used to blind enemies, however it has a much shorter range than Shinobi Firecrackers and no area of effect.

Defensively the Firecrackers can buy you enough time to retreat from a tactically disadvantageous encounter and go back into stealth mode by hiding in nearby tall grass or otherwise escaping from sight, They also give you enough time to use items such as the Healing Gourd or status buffing Sugars. Since these items are slow to use, it's important to stop enemies from interrupting you, and

the Firecrackers are perfect for this. Shinobi Firecrackers are particularly useful against bosses and tougher enemies for this reason, many of which have fast, ranged attacks that make it difficult to find a time to heal. By throwing some Firecrackers first, this gives you some breathing space to safely take a swig from the Healing Gourd. Remember that keeping your Vitality high is crucial, since it directly influences the rate at which your Posture recovers.

The Firecrackers are also very potent against Beasts, which are startled by the sudden sight and sound. Hounds or Valley Monkeys, for example, will be put into a Posture-break state, allowing you to finish them off immediately. Firecrackers are also very effective against Gyoubu's horse, Onikage, putting it into a lengthy stun allowing you to deliver several attacks. Just be careful when you throw the Firecrackers; certain attacks have spun immunity and so will simply blow through the explosives, which means you'll have expended Spirit Emblems for nothing and possibly lost a chunk of Vitality in the process. Do note that certain stronger enemies such as Gyoubu can't be repeatedly blinded or startled by Firecrackers. In those cases, there's a cooldown period before they can be blinded again. If they're a Beast-type enemy, however, you can still inflict large amounts of Posture damage by repeatedly using Firecrackers even while this cooldown is active.

![](images/ed7da339ca93a297d2f108157ba4b85b04210ac7acecd6bbf91cfb641732df59.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

While on the ground, in the time between throwing the Firecrackers and them actually exploding, you are left stationary and vulnerable. However, by jumping while using them you remain a mobile target, thereby greatly reducing the risk involved.

Jumping backwards before using Firecrackers is advised for when you want to run away in order to safely use an item, as it creates more space between you and the enemy. The range of the Firecrackers is longer than you would think, extending beyond that of the direct explosions. If you want to initiate offense from a distance with the Firecracker, then jumping towards the enemy before using them will greatly extend their range.

![](images/016dc8471abac0771943d219530e2eba97b5767e5175aea0e5877f3e38d6638c.jpg)  
Even if the explosions are right above an enemy's head they will still be blinded.

Firecrackers have deceptively long range, and the Chasing Slice is an excellent attack to quickly close the gap after blinding an enemy from a distance. Against weaker enemies such as Hounds, the Chasing Slice lets you instantly move in and take them out. Against stronger enemies, as mentioned previously though you can follow up with more powerful moves such as Ichimonji, or run behind them to deliver attacks to their back, you often won't be in range to do this. Here Chasing Slice is your most reliable option for delivering damage from a distance.

You'll have enough time to confirm whether or not the enemy has been stunned by the Firecracker, even at maximum range, and then as soon as you see that they have, press RB/1 to launch into a Chasing Slice. Finally, Chasing Slice also has wide lateral range, particularly to your right side, making it quite effective against a group of enemies directly in front of you.

![](images/73a19422fc4e6324011aa3bb214148317714a163ed82d2489b937e3b489eeecc.jpg)  
Use Firecrackers to stun a tightly packed group of enemies, then attack them all with Chasing Slice.

# Spring-load Firecracker

# Tool Upgrade

A Firecracker upgraded with a spring mechanism. Costs Spirit Emblems to use.

Unleashes a loud explosion and bright flash which causes foes to recoil and inflicts

Posture damage on beast-type enemies. Charging up the spring mechanism adds

rotational energy when spreading the Firecrackers, affecting enemies in all directions.

![](images/195c859dcd8cb2d82573fe32216377a53229ae40609ab1f90c72a9f1b05a3337.jpg)

The Spring-load Firecracker allows you to charge the Firecracker and spread them around him in a circle, making it a useful tool for when you're surrounded, especially by packs of Beasts. For example, this absolutely decimates troops of Valley Monkeys, and is equally effective against packs of encircling Hounds. Do beware that that charging the Firecracker for this 360-degree attack does take more time, so if the enemy is very close and is about to attack, it's better to just guard, or even better, deflect or Step Dodge.

# Long Spark

# Tool Upgrade

An upgraded Firecracker using compound gunpowder. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Compounded gunpowder is said to have a long spark, and by increasing the proportion of Black Gunpowder the effect can be prolonged for longer than the average Firecracker. The flames of the firecrackers bloom for a short while.

![](images/ed23257158e87891c30181b7f4ddd6b7bcf4eb4c8bafd7bf776cc92194a0deda.jpg)

With the Long Spark the Firecracker explosions will last for significantly longer; approximately three times more than those of regular Firecrackers. The actual duration of the blind stun is always a constant though, at approximately three seconds. It is not made longer by the lingering explosions of the Long Spark.

The longer lasting explosions allow you to Step Dodge into them and effectively use them as cover. Any enemy who tries to approach and attack you if you remain close to the ongoing explosions will be blinded. You can either use this cover cautiously, by first confirming whether the enemy is blinded and then acting accordingly, or pre-emptively, which is riskier but leads to greater rewards. If you

# Purple Fume Spark Tool Upgrade

An upgraded Firecracker that uses a purple, smoke-emitting compound gunpowder. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. The tweaked compound gunpowder is known as "Purple Fume Spark". The addition of fatty wax lumps delays the explosion slightly. Enemies blinded by the blast take slightly more Vitality and Posture damage for a brief period of time.

![](images/3053957ac818b8ebc05ce19ec5bfdf8b862a1a8910d959e07226f8e9724d2ea4.jpg)

The Purple Fume Spark doesn't retain the longer duration of the explosions from the Long Spark, and there is an approximate second of extra delay between using the tool and the Firecrackers actually going off. While this sounds like a strange downgrade for the final form of the Firecracker, and indeed while it isn't quite as useful as a panic move to get out of sticky situations, the delayed explosion allows you to set up some devious, and very rewarding, trap. The explosions of the Purple Fume Spark themselves also boast a larger area of effect than that of regular Firecrackers.

Upon pressing RT/R2, instead of releasing Firecrackers, you will instead emit Purple Mist from your Prosthetic arm. When the enemy is then caught in the blast radius of the delayed Firecrackers, they are saturated with the mist. This inflicts a defense debuff to both their Vitality and Posture, allowing your subsequent attack to deal  $12\%$  more damage. This debuff lasts as long as the enemy is stunned by the Firecracker—approximately three seconds.

The goal of the Purple Fume Spark trap is to lure the enemy in when the Purple Mist is thrown, and then immediately commit to another action while the enemy unwittingly tries to attack you. This attack will then be interrupted by the delayed Firecracker, giving you more time to both set up powerful Combat Arts and use multiple items. Throw the Purple Fume Spark from a specific distance, just outside the maximum range of the enemy's attacks, and then immediately charge up a Combat Art such as Ichimonji or Empowered Mortal Draw. When they move into range and are about to attack you while you're charging, the Firecrackers will then interrupt

The delayed Firecrackers also give you even more time to use items if spaced correctly. # Flame Vent Prosthetic Tool

A Prosthetic Tool made from a loaded Flame Barrel. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Deals fire damage to enemies via a short-range blast of fire while also inflicting Burn status. It is difficult to control the rage of those with "Red Eyes" through the power of man alone. They do, however, fear the flame above all else. This tool has the power to make them tremble.

# Overview

The Flame Vent emits a Fire Breath from the Prosthetic Arm which deals Fire damage and builds the enemy's Burn gauge. If an enemy is afflicted by Burn they will go into a stun animation, take ongoing Vitality damage for ten seconds, and will also be unable to recover Posture damage during this time. Once an enemy has been Burnt this presents a good opportunity to finish them off then and there. The Flame Vent, much like the Sabimaru which inflicts Poison, is thus a tool primarily centered around crippling the enemy with Status Abnormalities, coupled with dealing heavy Vitality damage in the process.

Weaker enemies can often be afflicted with Burn (or outright killed) after just one Fire Breath, however stronger enemies are more resistant and may take multiple blasts. Against such enemies, you will want to douse them in Oil first, which makes them  $100\%$  more vulnerable to the Burn status, as well as making Fire inflict  $25\%$  more damage.

![](images/1f3f1a2842e54cd2871fde366ae93bf66d6404773a61bddc752287a7d74f8f68.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

The Flame Vent's main issues are its sluggishness and lackluster range, which make it quite difficult and risky to land against faster enemies. The Mid-Air Prosthetic Skill helps considerably in this respect. Jumping towards the enemy before using the Flame Vent greatly increases its range, allowing you to quickly get within range to punish an enemy's missed attack from a distance. Do note though, that the expulsion of the flame will stop your forward mo

![](images/a1af29cfa638c91cea7338302c6f924e0f3eeabbdc989485080f2c7f4769031e.jpg)

# Living Force Skill P.59

Once the Living Force skill has been unlocked in the Prosthetic Arts skill tree, the Flame Vent can be used to imbue your katana with fire. Simply use the Flame Vent and then press  $\overline{\mathbb{R}}\overline{\mathbb{B}} / \overline{\mathbb{R}}$  to unleash an attack that envelops the katana in flames. Because of its short seven second duration, the best way to take advantage of Living Force is to blast an opponent with a Fire Breath and then

The Flame Vent is particularly effective against Red-Eyed enemies, which are weak to Fire-based damage, such as the Chained Ogre in Ashina Outskirts. Red-Eyed enemies will enter a panic stun at the mere sight of fire. Just be careful not to try to attack them while they are performing a stun-immune attack. The Valley Monkeys will also enter a unique stun animation as they try to shrug off the flames, and this even works on the first phase of the Guardian Ape boss battle, making it a great way to apply Burn and deal lots of damage while he is stunned.

Some downsides to the Flame Vent are that it is somewhat slow, and the range is deceptively short, especially since your view of the attack is obstructed by the Fire Breath. Compared to other, slower tools, such as the Loaded Axe, it also lacks any kind of armor. Finally, at three Spirit Emblems per use, the Flame Vent requires careful management of your resources. Overall, it's quite expensive, both in terms of Spirit Emblems and if you decide to use Oil. It can also be quite risky due to its short range and slow speed. However, if used judiciously, it can quickly dispatch even the toughest of enemies with alarming efficiency.

mentum and push you back a little in the air, so it might be slightly harder to capitalize on the Burn stun. Jumping laterally and then using the Flame Vent in mid-air is also useful, as it allows you to evade attacks and punish the enemy with an aerial Fire Breath. Backwards jump into Flame Vent isn't particularly useful, unless you've evaded an attack that moved the enemy forward a lot. Unlike the Loaded Axe which receives a damage reduction after being used in Mid-air, Fire Breath remains the same.

immediately follow up with it. If doused in Oil beforehand, there's a very high change the enemy will be afflicted by Burn and from there you can deal large amounts of damage by continuing to attack until they recover. The combination of Oil, Flame Vent and Living Force is one of the most potent in the game, and can be used to quickly inflict massive amounts of damage even on many bosses.

Living Force can also be used pre-emptively as a simple damage buff for the cost of three Spirit Emblems. When your katana is on fire it will deal  $20\%$  more damage, as well as inflicting some Vitality damage and Burn build-up even if the enemy is guarding.

# Spring-load Flame Vent

Tool Upgrade

A Flame Barrel fitted with a gunpowder-loaded mechanism. Costs Spirit

Emblems to use. Deals damage to enemies with gouts of fire, inflicting Burn status abnormality. The spring mechanism can also be charged to release a massive blast of flames and hot air, sending opponents flying.

![](images/e0895d391958be8f5b143009a25aef3a6730dc33827ddf9e56f497bc176fb264.jpg)

The Spring-load Vent allows you to charge up the Flame Vent for a massive Flame Blast. This attack deals more damage and inflicts more Burn build up than Fire Breath. The drawback is the lengthy charge period in addition to the pushback and recovery from the blast preventing you from fully capitalizing on the stun inflicted by Burn. It still only costs three Emblems though, so you're applying significantly more Burn build up for the same cost as a Fire Breath.

This immediately afflicts most enemies with Burn, even without the need for dousing them in Oil first. If the Flame Blast doesn't apply Burn, the enemy will be pushed far back and knocked down. Burn would prevent this from happening since the enemy would be stunned instead and wouldn't be knocked down. An example of an enemy this commonly happens against are the Taro Troops.

There are actually two separate attack ranges associated with this attack. An inner flame, and an outer flame. The inner flame deals considerably more Fire damage and Burn build-up, while the outer flame cannot knock down Burn-resistant enemies. Due to its large blast radius, the Spring-load Vent is good to use against a group of enemies clumped in front of you. Though do be careful, as it's slow to begin, and while the range is superior to a Fire Breath, it's again not as great as the enormous vision-obstructing blast of flame may suggest. As with all charged tool attacks, Flame Blast cannot be charged while in mid-air.

# Okinaga's Flame Vent

Tool Upgrade

A barrel containing smoldering resin that acts as an explosive catalyst. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Emits a short-range flame blast. Continuous fire damage will inflict the Burn status. It is able to maintain a continues stream of flames due to the smoldering resin inside of the tube mechanism.

![](images/e8b0b554940f97d4778950135b3b83f59dba347041134142fb4a3a994d6ceebc.jpg)

Okinaga's Flame Vent effectively turns your Prosthetic Arm into a flamethrower with the Flowing Flames, as well as making Fire Breath and Flame Blast deal around  $10\%$  more damage. By pressing  $\boxed{LT} / \boxed{L2}$  again while Fire Breath is still on-screen, and then holding it down, you can activate Flowing Flames. You can move around afterwards to direct the flames, but only at walking pace. If Fire Breath afflicted the enemy with Burn, then they will be left reeling in the Burn spun animation while you continue to blast them with fire, dealing tremendous amounts of ongoing Vitality damage to the enemy.

The initial Flame Breath consumes three Spirit Emblems, then an additional three are consumed once you press RT/F2 again to trigger the Flowing Flames. From there, three Spirit Emblems are consumed every four seconds. Although there's a high initial cost of six Emblems, once it gets going you can keep Flowing Flames active for a significant amount of time. With a full stock of Emblems, you can keep this going for roughly 16 seconds. This will deplete all your Emblems though, so it is expensive. It can be very powerful however, as certain bosses will continuously try to evade sideways to avoid the flames. The wide conical area of effect will ensure that you still hit them though. For instance, on a Samurai General, it's possible to apply Burn as the Flowing Flames begins for a cost of six Spirit Emblems.

Though expensive in terms of Spirit Emblems, Flowing Flames can help you conserve Oil, since enemies that are normally afflicted with Burn after two Fire Breaths can quickly be set on fire from one Fire Breath plus one hit of Flowing Flames. Since the third consumption of Spirit Emblems is four seconds away from the second, the total Spirit Emblem consumption is still only left at six, even if you maximize the fire damage from the Burn stun. This is highly effective against even some tougher enemies, such as Fencers, who can be outright killed in just one Flame Breath to Flowing Flames combo for six Spirit Emblems. Be sure to circle the enemy while us

Flowing Flames are powerful, but resource intensive. This can be mitigated if you understand the rate at which they consume Spirit Emblems, though.

ing Flowing Flames. Even though they have very low stun, Flowing Flames still slow down the enemy slightly, and if you circle around them it takes extra time for them to attack, since they need to turn to re-orient with you. Okinaga's Flame Vent is also incredibly useful in Mibu Village, where the Infested Villagers recoil at the sight of fire. You can walk around torching enemies with little resistance there, making it a good place to farm Sen and Skill Points.

# Lazulite Sacred Flame

# Tool Upgrade

A Flame Barrel blessed with the favor of the Fountainhead Lapis Lazuli. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Damages even apparitions with its blazing purple flame. This flame does not, however, inflict Burn status abnormality. The sacred lapis lazuli fires are divine. Cleans the deep-seated hatred with flame.

![](images/c86d15b06f13396c99e2390ed600391527b7f1fc9a38fac6807400bee5483712.jpg)

The Lazulite Sacred Flame changes the attribute of the of the Flame Vent from Flame to Spirit, making it very effective against Illusions. However, since these are no longer regular flames, they cannot inflict Burn any more, which means dousing enemies in Oil in conjunction with the Lazulite Sacred Flame is completely pointless. While the loss of Burn does seem significant, and indeed against certain enemies Okinaga's Flame Vent is still recommended, the attacks from the Lazulite Sacred Flame have significantly more range and deal roughly  $10\%$  more damage. This makes it a much more effective mid-range tool. Many enemies will struggle to even approach you through the barrage of purple flames, particularly a Sacred Flame Blast, which will continually knock enemies away, and now boasts some truly oppressive range.

When using the Sacred Flame Blast, you want to start charging just outside the enemy's maximum range, so that when they charge in to attack, they are hit with the full brunt of the inner flame. You can also play more compactly and safely by peppering them with the regular, uncharged Sacred Flame, which is less risky, but also less rewarding.

The Living Force Skill also changes, since it now imbues your katana with Spirit, not Fire damage. Similar to imbuing your katana with Fire, this enhances your attacks with a  $20\%$  damage increase. Spirit also deals slightly more Vitality damage than Fire on a guarding enemy;  $75\%$  and  $67\%$  respectively. The effect of this is exactly the same as using Divine Confetti, a rare and expensive item, however the duration is much shorter. Whereas Divine Confetti lasts for over a minute, Living Force imbues your blade with Spirit for only seven seconds.

A Prosthetic Tool loaded with the feather of a Mist Raven. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. When attacked in the assumed stance, disappear like the mist and move away. Once you think you've caught one, all that will remain is feathers. That is the mark of a true Mist Raven.

![](images/28f9d0cb25c14b75eda7b39eade40274832a2712826029955a5e693944d0d699.jpg)

# Overview

<table><tr><td>Basic Info</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td></tr><tr><td>Mist Stance</td><td>-</td><td>-</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4">Acquisition ▶Pick up the Mist Raven&#x27;s Feathers near the &quot;Bamboo Thicket Slope&quot; Idol in Hirata Estate (P.180)，and bring it to the Sculptor.</td></tr></table>

Using Mist Raven causes you to briefly assume an elusory Mist Stance—if struck by an attack while in this stance, you will instantly vanish and warp away. This negates all damage that would have otherwise been dealt, and is extremely useful for gaining a positional advantage or to make a quick escape when trapped or cornered. Mist Raven works against nearly all types of melee and projectile attacks and makes you completely invincible from the moment the warp is triggered to the moment you re-emerge—but be careful, as you are still vulnerable to grabs while in Mist Stance. Though you can warp through enemies, you will still collide with walls, doors, or other such obstacles, so pay attention to your surroundings to avoid putting yourself in a disadvantaged position.

Mist Stance is only active for a brief moment, so time its activation just before an attack connects, then use the left analog stick to warp in the direction of your choosing (or leave it neutral to warp directly above). This is far more lenient than a deflect, but proper timing is still crucial, as entering the Mist Stance too early or too late can cause you to get hit and take damage. Spirit Emblems aren't consumed until an attack connects, so it's possible to repeatedly enter Mist Stance at no cost. With the low recovery time, Mist Raven can be used to protect yourself against dangerous attacks that would otherwise prove quite difficult to avoid or deflect.

The Mist Raven tool is particularly effective when used to warp straight through an enemy and appear behind them. It's often possible to score multiple hits from this angle before the enemy even has a chance to turn around, and it can give you enough time to use a slow but powerful Combat Art, such as Ichimonji. This tactic also presents a perfect opportunity to heal or use an item against enemies that give you very little room to breathe, since Mist Raven's warp is quicker and covers more distance than a Step Dodge.

Think of Mist Raven as both an offensive and defensive tool. Use knowledge of your foe's behavior and attack patterns to help determine which direction it's best to warp in. For instance, if an enemy uses a dashing attack to close the gap and you're aware that this puts them directly next to you, warp above them and come down with a falling slash (once you've unlocked Fang and Blade) to both deal damage and avoid the attack. When the camera isn't giving you the best view of the action and there's no room to maneuver, use Mist Raven to move to a better position.

# Poisoned Mist Raven

An interesting feature about the Mist Raven is that if you are poisoned you can vanish at any time, bypassing the need to be hit by an enemy attack first. This is one of the main reasons for using Contact Medicine to intentionally poison yourself, which inflicts you with a much less potent poison that drains only a third of the Vitality poison normally would, and as usual lasts for forty seconds.

When poisoned Mist Raven effectively turns in a vastly more evasive Step Dodge, though at the cost of two Spirit Emblems per use. Since the vanish also warps through enemies, this is a great way of getting to their back to deal Vitality damage without having to wait for them to attack first. This allows you to dance around tougher enemies while striking at them from vulnerable angles with the Fang and Blade follow up. Other uses for poisoned Mist Raven are to safely pass through particularly hazardous areas filled with tough enemies, and also to close the gap on ranged attackers such as Snake Eyes.

![](images/aa2b96c521abd835d462e3784267b4e3e2a87b1bf7bf7f4f29238e0e5e811f75.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

The ability to use Mist Raven while jumping essentially increases the situations in which you can enter Mist Stance, and subsequently evade attacks with a vanish. This can be used as a last-minute safety net if you mistimed a jump to evade an enemy's attack. Since the Mist Raven costs nothing to activate, there's also nothing to lose in covering your jump with Mist Stance to protect yourself. The mid-air vanish will always bring you back down to the ground. If no direction is pressed on the left analogue stick, then you will vanish directly down.

![](images/75f5d9a07f0dba5161bd4f1c4f48d63cc7932616945be804e5d7912ed040d771.jpg)  
Mid-air Mist Raven can be used to make your jumps safer.

<table><tr><td>Ground</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>A</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>A</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td><td>-</td></tr><tr><td>Mid-air</td><td>Vitalty Dmg</td><td>S</td><td>Posture Dmg</td><td>S</td><td>Spirit Embl.</td><td>-</td></tr></table>

Fang and Blade is an integral part of using Mist Raven offensively, so if you intend to use this tool then unlocking this Skill should be an absolutely priority. One of the best uses of the Mist Raven is to quickly reposition yourself behind an enemy with ironclad defenses by vanishing through them. This allows you to deal some Vitality damage on their open back before attempting to break their Posture. While you do sometimes have enough time to follow up with a damaging Combat Art after a vanish, other times you may not be in range or simply may not have time. If contending with a group of enemies, they will also likely interrupt a slower Combat Art.

The grounded Fang and Blade, performed by activating Mist Stance combined with a direction on the left analogue stick and then pressing RB/R1, allows you to follow up a vanish with a fast, long-range, reliable dashing attack that will consistently punish an enemy that you have vanished behind. Very often you will be able to land several attacks on the enemy's back, as the Fang and

![](images/18998776a265a26460c9202009dfe3a8708f6851f2bbc3d43e8eec7d9c666c65.jpg)  
The grounded Fang and Blade follow-up is more consistent and can hit multiple enemies.

Blade will segue naturally into your basic five-hit attack string. You can also do a falling slash after a neutral vanish if no direction is pressed on the left-analogue stick, as this will cause you to vanish upwards into the air.

The aerial Fang and Blade from a neutral vanish deals  $33\%$  more damage than a grounded Fang and Blade, but since you are still in front of the enemy, it offers less opportunities for follow-up attacks, and since it has a much narrower attack width, will hit less consistently. If you aerial vanish through a move with fast recovery, then the enemy may even be able to recover in time to evade the falling slash. However, with the grounded Fang and Blade, the enemy will at least have to guard the incoming attack, which will inflict some Posture damage. Against slower attacks with long recovery it is recommended to use the aerial Fang and Blade for the higher damage, whereas against faster attacks with shorter recovery, you should stick to the grounded Fang and Blade for its more consistent range.

![](images/9f8d3fe132e2eefc4cf862a0c1ea21c5cf0a2a6111002ed69b6682aed65bcee6.jpg)  
The aerial Fang and Blade follow-up can only hit one enemy, but deals more damage.

# Aged Feather Mist Raven Tool Upgrade

Mist Raven feathers with notches in the tips. Costs Spirit Emblems to use.Disappear like the mist and move away. Can be performed not only from the assumed stance, but also after taking damage. The slight notches in the tips of the feathers give the appearance of an old Mist Raven. They are there to allow one to dissolve into the mist even more easily.

![](images/6c8a35725c49106e6b5662bbd4e0e70b9e1fafd5247225db606849b1631fe80d.jpg)

The aged Feather Mist Raven allows you to vanish even after being placed into a hit stun animation. For example, after you are knocked down or put into a stumble stun, you can enter the Mist Stance even while on the floor and vanish to safety. This could easily mark the difference between surviving an attack and getting killed.

# Great Feather Mist Raven

# Tool Upgrade

Mist Raven fused with crimson feathers. Costs Spirit Emblems to use.Disappear and displace, like the mist. Can be performed from both the assumed stance and after taking damage. Dyed red to resemble the Great Mist Raven, the feathers vanish in a scorching wake. The great raven is a god of the land, and the touch of gods is to be feared.

![](images/5ea0399bd7fe9cbf6643c808357d755109f9a2dc95bca015cfb134298b0df9aa.jpg)

The Great Feather Mist Raven unleashes a column of fire in the trail of a Mist Stance vanish. Now vanishing through enemies will deal Fire damage and inflict Burn build-up, while still also letting you use the Fang and Blade follow-up.

If the enemy is doused in Oil then this technique becomes absurdly powerful, as many enemies will become afflicted with Burn after a single Flaming Mist Raven. Once the enemy is afflicted with Burn, you should generally use a neutral vanish into aerial Fang and Blade, since it deals more damage. Vanishing behind the opponent is not as important any more, since when the enemy is afflicted with Burn they will often enter a long stun animation. However, in some cases you will still want to vanish behind the enemy, since if the enemy's attack recovers quickly enough, they can evade in time to avoid the vertical pillar of fire that follows the neutral vanish into aerial Fang and Blade. Maximising your damage from a vanish will require some knowledge and experience of the enemy's move-set. Another way to hasten the rate at which you can afflict Burn, perhaps if you don't want to use Oil or against Burn-resistant enemies, is to follow-up a vanish behind the enemy with a quick change of Prosthetic to the Flame Vent, and then firing them with a single Fire Breath. For this we recommend only having the Great Feather Mist Raven and Flame Vent (any except for the Lazulite Sacred Flame) equipped so that you can quickly switch between the two. This is one of the few circumstances where you don't want a variation of the Shuriken equipped in a Prosthetic slot.

Regardless, once the enemy has been afflicted with Burn, the pun animation gives you enough time to land a guaranteed thrust as well as single basic attack after the Fang and Blade follow-up, which adds up to tremendous Vitality and Posture Damage. You can also use a fully-charged Combat Art such as Ichimonji or Empowered Mortal Draw. Since the enemy will continue to take Vitality damage and cannot recover Posture during the next ten seconds when they are afflicted with Burn, this presents an excellent opportunity to finish them off.

Usually, in order to afflict an enemy with Burn you need to use the Flame Vent or Sparking Axe, which due to their short range and sluggish start-up speed can be quite risky. The Leaping Flame is considerably safer but takes much longer to Burn enemies. However, with the Great Feather Mist Raven you can adopt a low-risk, high-reward strategy by dousing the enemy in Oil, before continually vanishing through the enemy's attacks until they are afflicted with Burn. For this reason, the Great Feather Mist Raven is, in terms of speed, efficiency and risk-to-reward ratio, one of the best tools for afflicting Burn, and overall is amazingly useful for dealing with many of the tougher enemies. The strength of the Great Feather Mist Raven is balanced by the increased Spirit Emblem usage, which means you'll need to pick your moments and carefully judge when to tap into its power.

# Divine Abduction

# Prosthetic Tool

A Prosthetic Tool loaded with a large fan. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Gathers and releases a gust of wind, forcing enemies caught by the vortex to turn around. It is a mild sort of being spirited away that can be returned from quite quickly. However, it's said that one can only return from being spirited away once, and if taken again, there is no coming back.

# Overview

Acquisition  $\triangleright$  Take the Large Fan from the Long-arm Centipede Giraffe's room, just after the "Gun Fort" idol in the Sunken Valley. (P:255)

Divine Abduction are a set of fans that turns enemies around, leaving them open to Backstab Deathblows. They first need to be charged by pressing RT/2. This surrounds you in a Gathering Vortex for about three seconds. If RT/2 is then pressed again while the Vortex is active, you will unleash Divine Abduction around your body. This turns enemies around, briefly confusing and disorientating them long enough to either escape should you so desire, or land a Backstab Deathblow—even if the enemy was in full alert a mere moment ago. Unleashing Divine Abduction costs no Spirit Emblems, however charging Gathering Vortex costs three.

This is a powerful tool to deal with enemy groups when combined with Ninjutsu. Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu will briefly put all surrounding enemies into a vulnerable state, allowing you to go around and neatly pick them all off with Backstab Deathblows. An alerted enemy can be turned into an ally through Puppeteer Ninjutsu. If you'd prefer more attack power and range, perhaps to face off against a tough nearby enemy, then use Bestowal Ninjutsu to wreathe your blade in their blood for 30 seconds.

The downsides to Divine Abduction are that it needs to be charged first, Gathering Vortex doesn't last long, it's rather expensive at three Spirit Emblems per Vortex, and it ranges from not very useful to completely useless against bosses or mid-bosses. While some

# Finger Whistle

# Prosthetic Tool

A Prosthetic Tool created by fitting a slender finger to the Prosthetic. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Its sound will grab an enemy's attention and draw them to the whistle's location. By locking on to a target, only the targeted enemy will hear the whistle. The sound of the finger whistle enrages beasts, making them unable to distinguish friend from foe.

![](images/61872675c774d797c7c82bf509fc41dfa4bc2089ef1ca20dc550dee5123be342.jpg)

(P.263)</td></tr></table>

# Overview

The Finger Whistle is used primarily during stealth. By blowing on a finger-shaped whistle attached to the Prosthetic Arm, you can emit a sound-wave that will grab the attention of nearby enemies, signified by their Alert Indicators going yellow. The range on this sound-wave is quite wide, and you probably don't want to simultaneously attract all enemies to your current position. Fortunately, by locking on you can target a specific enemy, thereby isolating them and luring them in for a stealth kill. This is very useful when your Presence is suppressed by hiding in tall grass, as the enemy will walk right up to you, still unaware of your Presence, so you can easily maneuver around and stealth kill them.

![](images/1f2e20952887ca28d218644e20febfa78bc4581ed508ca9fd35a02d8b8d568e1.jpg)

Another useful effect of the Finger Whistle it that it sends Beasts such as Hounds and Valley Monkeys into an enraged berserker state where they cannot discern between friend or foe. This is signified by a swirling sound-wave above their head and is a permanent effect. The enraged animal will then start attacking everything in its general vicinity, including you and their previous allies—human and animal alike. When used specifically on Hounds it will also make their Ashina Soldier or Lone Shadow masters start attacking them back out of self-defense. If a Lone Shadow blows the whistle to order the Shinobi Hound, then it will immediately turn to attack its master. In general, it sends the battlefield into complete disarray, which you can then capitalize on by attacking the distracted enemies.

![](images/e684ab0bdd93b52abb1e6c7c907a9d2637d8e00a01dd269f711d73685b2bad68.jpg)

![](images/6f10e5096b2fc81de701765a226def4592eba260bdf0d63444d3a5177d1cc909.jpg)

# Mid-air Usage Skill P.57

As primarily a stealth tool, the mid-air application of the Finger Whistle doesn't have many practical uses. However, it does allow you to enrage animals and stun Apparitions with the Malcontent while staying mobile and evasive with jumps.

![](images/fa73e5d4b9d42e89176127146374432a1751e0bc0a0e805d1dbe31ee41fc656f.jpg)

# Projected Force Skill P.58

Pressing attack immediately after using the Finger Whistle causes you to slash the sound-wave and send it flying. Tilting the camera up or down lets you adjust the vertical trajectory, while Locking-on causes it to go towards a target. Projected Force can't be performed while crouched. It has several applications when used in conjunction with the Finger Whistle. First it allows you to fire the sound

wave directly at Beasts to enrage them from a distance. When combined with Mountain Echo it operates as a delayed whistle that can be launched at a specific location for greater tactical control of the battlefield. It also works with Malcontent, where it can be used to stun and safely approach Apparitions such as Headless from afar.

# Mountain Echo Tool Upgrade

A finger whistle that can create an echo effect. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Its sound will grab an enemy's attention and draw them to the whistle's location. By locking on to a target, only the targeted enemy will hear the whistle. Taking a deep breath before performing a whistle allows for the sound to be delayed.

![](images/dcd29e14aabcbb915882c24ec509408cf1582f59be3782c67ff7322c92dc8afe.jpg)

Mountain Echo allows you to charge the Finger Whistle, delaying the emission of the sound-wave. After five seconds it will make a sound, and in that time you can move into a more tactically advantageous position. When combined with Projected Force, which allows you to launch the sound-wave to a specific location, you can manipulate enemies more precisely in order to set up Backstab Deathblows.

![](images/5cc6a3a530b88cbd5525392e5e5a62ac7536e90e21eb4829a75b755ed4241c1c.jpg)  
The Mountain Echo allows you to release a charged sound-wave...

![](images/122f867301b98782a501488291ce06e92e8decb8d03953bfc6ee892e3180fe24.jpg)  
...which then emits a sound five seconds later.

# Malcontent Tool Upgrade

Finger Whistle reinforced with the Malcontent's Ring. Costs Spirit Emblems to use. Can be used to drive beasts mad, and to torment apparition-type enemies. "Kingfisher" is etched onto the ring. The Kingfisher's cry could be heard along the waterfront of Sunken Valley. Now, she cries no more.

The Malcontent no longer puts Beasts into an enraged state. Instead it will briefly stun Apparitions, rendering them temporarily immobile with anguish. Similar to an animal's enraged state, this is again signified by a sound-wave appearing next to their head (or stump in the case of the Headless). This allows you to both safely approach these enemies from a distance, and also land a few easy attacks when at close range.

![](images/9cbb094605a100829c00e83ac2447717c18e320b86e9736c153ff515c377b231.jpg)

![](images/ad689d3fb2dcfcffcef5fef799b27cead21044f9866d9186092932fcd3a3f510.jpg)

(P.272)</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4">Additional Properties ▶ Stuns Apparitions, no longer enrages animals. Can charge the Whistle to delay the sound by five seconds.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4">Req. Materials ▶ 1500 Sen, Scrap Magnetite x4, Adamantite Scrap x2, Lump of Fat Wax x4, Lump of Grave Wax x2</td></tr></table>

Unlike the enraged effect on Beasts, which is permanent, the stun on Apparitions is temporary and only works up to three times on a single target. The first two blows of the Malcontent whistle will stun an Apparition for five seconds. On the third use the duration of this stun is halved, though you can still see the sound-wave next to their head for the full five seconds, so be careful. The Malcontent will cease to have any effect on an Apparition on the fourth attempt. The Malcontent is overall one of the most specialized tools, especially since it now costs four Spirit Emblems, meaning you have to be quite strategic with how often you use it. However it can make battling some of the most challenging foes significantly easier.

# Items & Materials

A Shinobi's greatest strength doesn't lie in their blade, but in their resourcefulness. In the hands of a skilled assassin, even something as simple as a piece of broken pottery can provide a means of eliminating foes with precision and stealth. The amount of options in front of you can be daunting, from the blessed hard candies of the Senpou Temple to charms that will bring you to a completely different time and place. Seeing your journey through to its end will be much easier if you know how to get the most out of every available item; you've arrived at the perfect place to begin studying the ins and outs of your arsenal.

# Consumables

![](images/12a216c2a93263abb8748682c0fc989ff6d8ab0e89745a325d24eb80cc8f962e.jpg)

Consumables come in many forms, from healing pills, to confetti that will allow you to harm the undead, to small purses filled with Sen. They may not always been the most impressive tools, but they are often the

most direct and practical options at your disposal. Consumables are defined by their ability to be equipped as a Quick Item, which allows you to use them on the battlefield without having to enter the main menu. Your space is limited, however, so make sure you choose your items wisely.

You can only carry a limited number of each consumable item at a time, and once you've used them all, you'll need to either find more or replenish them by resting at an Idol. The amount that you can carry is shown for every item in this section, indicated by the number that follows the usage type.

# Restorative Items

The items listed here are your primary means of healing yourself. Some of these will directly restore your Vitality and Posture while others will cure status abnormalities, such as Poison. Several of these items will self-replenish whenever you rest at a Sculptor's Idol. Always keep in mind that it's possible to safely use items from the pause menu, regardless of whether you have them equipped in your Quick Items. If you find yourself afflicted in any way, don't hesitate to check your inventory.

![](images/9ac99a91b21f88bbb80bac857819769046a26fb90af259da50f6937ec5a13f86.jpg)

# Consumable Use Types

There are three different types of consumable item, and it's important to understand the distinction between them. The difference lies in the way they work; some are single-use, some need refilling and some are simply infinite in use.

<table><tr><td colspan="2">Use Types</td></tr><tr><td>Refill</td><td>Items that self-replenish upon resting at a Sculptor&#x27;s Idol such as the Healing Gourd.</td></tr><tr><td>Finite</td><td>Items that are completely consumed upon use and need to be collected elsewhere in the world in order to restock such as Pellets.</td></tr><tr><td>Infinite</td><td>Items that can be used endlessly with no need to replenish them in any form such as the Homeward Idol.</td></tr></table>

Healing items are affected by some healing-boosting Skills that you can learn throughout the game. These Skills are covered on P.59, but for ease of reference we've included a summary of how they affect healing items here.

<table><tr><td>Skill</td><td>Acquired From</td></tr><tr><td>Emma&#x27;s Medicine: Potency</td><td>Purchased in the Prosthetic Arts Skill Tree for 4 Skill Points</td></tr><tr><td>Emma&#x27;s Medicine: Aroma</td><td>Purchased in the Prosthetic Arts Skill Tree for 5 Skill Points</td></tr><tr><td>Shinobi Medicine: 1st Rank</td><td>Rewarded for defeating the Chained Ogre near the Stairway of Death in the Ashina Outskirts</td></tr><tr><td>Shinobi Medicine: 2nd Rank</td><td>Rewarded for defeating the Blazing Bull</td></tr><tr><td>Shinobi Medicine: 3rd Rank</td><td>Rewarded for defeating Chained Ogre at Ashina Castle during the Interior Ministry Raid</td></tr></table>

![](images/82c25cf1b17715346b7bdcb7420a1360a1adb19e4bc5331261c8ce05e4820cf4.jpg)

# Healing Gourd

Refill x1-10

A gourd filled with Vitality-restoring medicine. Resting refills the Gourd. Made by an apprentice of the extraordinary doctor, Dogen. Though it is strange that the gourd's medicinal waters refill automatically, the seeds within may hold the secret to how it works.

Given to you by Lord Kuro, this item is the most reliable form of healing that you'll have access to. It can be refilled at any point by resting at a Sculptor's Idol, allowing you to use it with relative freedom. As such, it's a good idea to have it equipped in your Quick Items at all times. When it is first given to you, the Healing Gourd holds only a single sip, but its capacity can be increased by giving Gourd Seeds to Emma the Physician. See the Gourd Seed entry on P.140 for the locations of these rare items. Additionally, the amount it heals can be increased by way of the various Medicine skills, up to a maximum of  $60\%$ . Be wary in its use, however, as you're entirely vulnerable when drinking from it.

Effects Restores  $40\%$  of maximum Vitality; Can be upgraded to  $60\%$  through various skills.

Acquisition NPC: Divine Heir Kuro

![](images/6ce69a3c9775300d5519f621bd0f414c5a79693939bbf6bb32934dbe252fd43e.jpg)

# Pellet

Finite x3

Medicinal Pellets that slowly restore Vitality. A secret treatment passed down for generations in these lands, records say it has been used in battles since times long gone, and lent to the famed resilience of Ashina warriors. A pill case full of these pellets would also serve as a battle charm.

Consuming a Pellet will refill your health slowly over time. They serve both as a way to keep your Vitality topped off in between fights without wasting a drink from the Healing Gourd, and as an emergency source of healing in a pinch. They are not as reliable as the Healing Gourd, due to their finite nature and delayed effect, but they can mean the difference between life and death if your Gourd has been spent. They are among the most common items you'll find and are relatively cheaply purchased. Over-using them will see your stores quickly run dry, but with proper management there's a good chance you'll never have an issue with supply. Any Shinobi worth their salt would do well to keep them on hand.

Effects Restores  $3\%$  of maximum Vitality per second over the course of 10 seconds. Can be upgraded to  $45\%$  through various skills.

![](images/118a21a6bb9754ac5073734cd60daffd3534c7971d991bc1799f8695f1957303.jpg)

# Divine Grass

Finite x1

A secret medicine that fully restores Vitality and cures all status abnormalities. One small part of Ashina is exceedingly old. The ancient soil, rocks, and water that pervaded the land are said to have attracted the attention of the gods. The doctor Dogen studied the plants in this ancient place, resulting in the recipe for this special medicine.

This is the only item you'll find that's capable of healing you of multiple afflictions at once. This makes the Divine Grass immensely useful when fighting powerful foes who are as reliant on inflicting status abnormalities as they are at dealing direct damage. Additionally, if you find yourself deprived of any other means to heal, a Divine Grass can serve to give you once last chance at victory. However, their immense rarity means that you'll be unable to rely on them in anything other than the most dire of situations, use them only when victory depends on them.

Effects Completely restores both your Vitality and Posture as well as healing you of any active status ailment or related build-up.

Acquisition Peddler: Pot Noble Harunaga (1 Scale) Area: Ashina Outskirts, Ashina Castle, Sunken Valley, Ashina Depths, Fountainhead Palace NPC: Divine Heir Kuro, Master's Chamberlain

![](images/4044a7017ca3f26d91775f9c7eb83dfde5f6f3e4fba6d4294d0f302e3be9dc58.jpg)

# Persimmon

Finite x3

A red, ripe persimmon, ready to eat. For a time, allows one to recover Posture even when attacking or taking damage. Ashina persimmons are particularly nutritious, perhaps because the trees grow in such pure water. Persimmons become blood, blood becomes rice. This may be of help to one short of blood.

When eaten, the Persimmon will consistently heal any Posture damage you've taken for each second it remains active. This can be massively useful against enemies that are reliant on wearing down your Posture as it is one of the few means to regain Posture while you are under attack. Should you find yourself repeatedly getting your Posture broken, this may be able to give you the edge you need. Be careful though as they do have a separate use: if you begin taking Rice from the Divine Child of Rejuvenation, she will eventually fall ill from the effort and will only be able to begin granting Rice again after being given a Persimmon. Given the broad usefulness of Rice as a healing item, it's highly recommended that you keep at least one on hand for this purpose. Check the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's entry on P.535 for more details on her questline.

Effects Restores  $10\%$  of maximum Posture every second over the course of 30 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Shugendo Memorial Mob (x2, 30 Sen) Area: Senpou Temple NPC: Shugendo Memorial Mob

![](images/5518f2007952e08e491929906a9f1fc28dd9df8e7ef4dce5813224a477df81d8.jpg)

# Taro Persimmon

Finite x3

A conspicuously red persimmon at the peak of its ripeness, commonly called a "Taro persimmon". Greatly increases Posture recovery for a time, even when attacking or taking damage. The Ashina Taro Troop are practically raised on these fruits, which is why they all know the best time to pick them.

Taro Persimmons are a stronger variant of the standard Persimmon, granting a higher Posture recovery rate. While active you may still have to somewhat manage your Posture damage, but if your opponent isn't especially adept at dishing it out then there's a good chance this can recover your Posture faster than they can reduce it. Combined with its respectable duration, this makes it one of the best items for protecting your Posture in fights against any foe. Note that you can only acquire one of these per playthrough, and the limited availability means you need to choose carefully which encounter you use it on. It's recommended to save these items for some of the tougher enemies and bosses encountered in the latter half of the game.

Effects Restores  $20\%$  of maximum Posture every second over the course of 30 seconds.

Acquisition NPC: Kotaro

![](images/2d2468d99eae3d5cf44202f58ad292182dbf98adbdc72d40c6276cb338e18f3b.jpg)

# Rice

Finite x3

Rice that spilled from the palms of the Child of Rejuvenation. Gradually recovers Vitality for a time. Even in falsehood, the power of the Dragon's Blood brings a bountiful harvest. Rice is precious. The flavour grows richer with each bite and is sure to raise one's spirits.

This Rice is a powerful healing item granted to you by the Divine Child of Rejuvenation after you have acquired the Mortal Blade. No other readily-available item can give you as much long lasting healing as this mystical Rice, making it perfect for keeping your health up over long, drawn-out battles. You will only be able to receive one of these at a time from the Divine Child, but you can continually request more from her as many times as you'd like. Be careful though, as after receiving the first several handfuls, the Divine Child will fall ill and not be able to create any more Rice until given a Persimmon. Check the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's entry on P.535 for more details on this. So long as you can maintain a steady supply, this can be one of the most powerful tools you have to keep your Vitality up and death at bay.

Effects Restores  $5\%$  of maximum Vitality per second over the course of 30 seconds.

Acquisition NPC: Divine Child of Rejuvenation

![](images/61d945cafa66e9a0c16002301f106e734d4c46135e8ea145ddbff96e134438e0.jpg)

Finite x3

Chilled, silvery rice that spilled from the palms of the Child of Rejuvenation. Gradually recovers Vitality for a time, slightly more so than regular rice. The cold sweetens the rice. Rice is indeed precious. The flavour grows richer and richer, raising one's spirits higher than ever.

This chilled rice is essentially a more robust variant of the already powerful Rice. If you complete the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline, the Rice she would normally give you is replaced by this. For this reason, it's recommended that you take the time to complete the Divine Child's questline, even if you do not plan on achieving its related ending. # Sweet Rice Ball

Finite x1

Sweet, sticky rice ball made by Kuro using rice from the Child of Rejuvenation. Slowly grants medium Vitality recovery and constant Posture recovery over time. Once when the Wolf was starving, his father wordlessly handed him a rice ball. It was astoundingly delicious. This one is sure to taste just as good.

To acquire this rice ball you must deliver the Rice for Kuro item from that you get from the Divine Child of Rejuvenation safely into Lord Kuro's hands. This may very well be the most powerful support item you can use when fighting enemies that aren't reliant on inflicting status abnormalities. Its use will make your Posture next-to-unbreakable while continuously recovering the damage sustained when missing a Deflect. You're only granted two of these over the course of your journey, so it would be wise to save them for only the most powerful foes. Combat, however, isn't its only use. Eating this after Lord Kuro gives it to you will result in unique dialogue which, in turn, will unlock unique dialogue with the Divine Child of Rejuvenation. # Ceremonial Tanto

Refill x 3

Dagger with a stark white blade and hilt. Converts Vitality into Spirit Emblems. Originally this tanto was used in a ritual offering to the dragon, in which an emblem would be cut from one's own life force and set adrift on the Fountainhead waters. The blade is inscribed with its true name: "Devoted Soul."

This is an essential item for any Shinobi who relies on their Prosthetic Tools. With it, you can ensure more frequent access to many of your most powerful tools. The Spirit Emblems this grants are added on top of your standard Spirit Emblems and do not count against your maximum carrying capacity; this effectively adds  $+5$  to your maximum Spirit Emblem capacity, in exchange for a Healing Gourd charge. Any tools or skills that require emblems will take their cost from these additional emblems before your regular ones. This does come with its own limitations, though. These red emblems cannot be stored and will be removed upon dying or resting at an Idol. Additionally, you'll be unable to use this item if you're below  $50\%$  Vitality, and can't give yourself more than five additional Spirit Emblems at a time. It can also only be used three times until you die or rest again. Nonetheless, the Tanto still counts as one of the more useful items you can acquire, and will ensure that you have better access to any of your Tools, so long as you can afford the cost.

Effects Grants 5 Spirit Emblems in exchange for  $50\%$  of your maximum Vitality.

Acquisition Drop: Shichimen Warrior (Abandoned Dungeon)

![](images/1d0cbb3ffcdfae62acd1d65174a979fa54a9b4c9ae6bb57f07496c4888262db5.jpg)

# Dragon's Blood Droplet

An item that is rarely dropped by a Divine Heir of the Dragon's Heritage. Using it will slightly increase Resurrective Power. Restore the power of life to those who have been drained of it by offering this drop to the Sculptor's Idol with the Recovery Charm in hand. In turn, all afflicted with the Dragonrot will be healed. The incessant coughing must cease.

After you have received the Recovery Charm, you can use these at a Sculptor's Idol to cure those afflicted with Dragonrot and remove all Rot Essence from your inventory. Check out the entry on Dragonrot on P.13 for more details. This item can also be used to remove the lock-out that prevents resurrection. Notably, it can be used even on your first death, unlike the Bundled Jizo Statue.

Effects Cures Dragonrot when used at a Sculptor's Idol.

# Jinza's Jizo Statue

Finite x1

Buddha effigy bound in light pink cloth. Raise in prayer between one's palms to restore a node of Resurrective Power. To enswathe Jizo statue is to express feelings of parental love. "Lord Sakuza... Please take this cloth and use it to bundle this little one, so that he may live on in peace."

Bundled Jizo Statues Taking a moment to pray to this small Statue will restore a single node of Resurrection Power. The unfortunate caveat, however, is that you'll only be able to use this item to restore your second and third Resurrections. This severely limits its usability, but that doesn't mean it's not valuable. If you find yourself on your second Resurrection yet still facing down death, this will give you the ability to continue the fight for at least one more life and hopefully see the battle through to the end.

# Green Mossy Gourd

Refill x5

A curved, moss-covered gourd filled with medicinal water. Refills upon rest. While it does not heal "Poison" status, it reduces Poison buildup, and increases Poison resistance. This gourd was made out of necessity by those that made poisonous lands their home. It's said if you live there long enough, eventually poison won't affect you at all.

Much like the healing gourd, the Green Mossy Gourd can be refilled by resting at a sculptor's idol. This makes it especially useful when exploring the poisonous depths of the Sunken Valley Passage, or while fighting off groups of Geckos. Do note though that, while it can reduce Poison build-up, it cannot cure an already active Poison status abnormality. As such, it's best used while still having Antidote Powder on hand.

# Withered Red Gourd

Refill x5

A curved, withered red gourd filled with medicinal water. The gourd's medicine refills upon rest. Reduces Burn buildup, and slightly increases Burn resistance. It cannot heal the Burn status abnormality, however.

Just like the other Gourds, this one can be refilled by resting at a Sculptor's Idol. It's most useful in areas where Fire damage is common, such as the Hirata Estate, or while fighting enemies such as the Blazing Bull. However, like all colored Gourds, it may be able to remove build-up but cannot cure already active abnormalities. For this reason, it's highly recommended that you keep at least a couple Dousing Powders around in the event that a Burn occurs.

Effects Removes Burn gauge build-up and provides a weak temporary resistance, reducing the build-up speed of Burn by  $70\%$  and Fire damage by  $50\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Pot Noble Harunaga (2 Scales)

# Mottled Purple Gourd

Refill x5

A curved, mottled purple gourd filled with medicinal water. Refills upon rest. Reduces "Terror" status buildup, and increases Terror resistance. This gourd's twisted form was formed with use in graveyards, corpse-strewn battlefields, and other forlorn places of death. It follows then that drinking its waters can help prevent the onset of Terror.

The Mottled Purple Gourd can act as an effective supplement to Pacifying Agent when facing down some of the more foreboding foes you'll encounter. Most enemies that are reliant on inflicting Terror are powerful bosses or sub-bosses, such as the Shichimen Warrior that have considerable health and will be able to generate Terror build-up consistently and often. In practice, this can make it difficult to find enough Pacifying Agent to manage the build-up, especially over the course of multiple attempts. Fortunately, the resistance granted by this Gourd can prove useful in keeping you from having to over-use your supply and stacks with the Pacifying Agent buff.

Effects Removes Terror gauge build-up and provides a weak temporary resistance, reducing the build-up speed of Terror by  $50\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Exiled Memorial Mob (1800 Sen)

![](images/b44da67775a8543ba4ed560da43a6315045fe00da9ba8af0e14c494ceaeb1e08.jpg)

# Antidote Powder

Finite x5

A powerful antidote concocted by the Sunken Valley clan. Heals status abnormality "Poison", and temporarily increases Poison resistance. Magnetite deposits are found in the Sunken Valley, but the place is dangerously toxic. Antidote powder is essential for anyone attempting to mine the ore.

While items like Divine Grass can also cure Poison and the Green Mossy Gourd can cure Poison build-up, Antidote Powders are the only easily-acquirable item you have to remove Poison after you have already been infected. Additionally, the resistance they grant makes them one of the best options when you need to reduce the chance of being poisoned altogether. This is one of the most essential items you will need over the course of your travels, so make sure you keep some on hand at all times.

Effects Cures active Poison status abnormalities, removes Poison build-up, and provides a temporary resistance, reducing the speed of Poison build-up by  $70\%$  of its normal speed for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Crow's Bed Memorial Mob (x6, 30 Sen), Battlefield Memorial Mob (x3, 30 Sen), Fujioka the Info Broker  $(\infty)$  100 Sen), Toxic Memorial Mob  $(\infty ,120\mathrm{Sen})$  Farm: Sunken Valley, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths Area: Ashina Outskirts, Senpou Temple, Sunken Valley, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid)

![](images/70f53014f7eddec20180fe757fa07b0c557bbace11218e467b8ee7374e92ad37.jpg)

# Contact Medicine

Finite x3

Powdered medicine with poisonous effects used through the ages by Ashina shinobi. A weak "Poison" status abnormality is inflicted upon consumption. By inflicting a weak poison on oneself, all other forms of poison become ineffective. Some shinobi also use this medicine for a specific technique. Poison is said to expand the mind.

Though this item's effect may seem detrimental at first glance, it actually serves two very useful purposes. The first and foremost of these is preventing more severe forms of Poison, since you can't become Poisoned if you're already suffering from the ailment. As such, this can be a good way to avoid using your valuable Antidote Powders, and is especially useful when exploring the toxic depths of the Sunken Valley Passage. Secondly, its use can allow you to utilize the Mist Raven tool at any time: while it's active, you will be taking constant damage, and damage is exactly what's needed to activate Mist Raven's effect. As such, you'll be able to active its dodge at any point while the Contact Medicine is active, so long as you can pay the two Spirit Emblem cost. This is an especially potent option once you've acquired the Great Feather Mist Raven, which will leave behind a trail of flames after each use that can stop Red-Eyed foes in their tracks, as well as decimate multiple weaker enemies in tight quarters.

Effects Inflicts you with a weak Poison that saps you of  $25\%$  of total health over the course of 40 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Abandoned Dungeon Memorial Mob (x8, 30 Sen) Farm: Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid) Area: Hirata Estate, Sunken Valley, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths

![](images/6137efcecb03ddd3adcbcfb07eb085022d4f9af507a1e45f044fc68e322abcf2.jpg)

# Dousing Powder

Finite x5

Medicine for treating burns. Heals the "Burn" status abnormality, and for a time decreases Burn buildup, increases Burn resistance, and reduces damage from incoming Burn attacks. When fire is used on the battlefield, Dousing Powder is crucial for survival.

As a means of handling a status abnormality, Dousing Powder does for Burn exactly what Antidote Powder does for Poison. It has the same advantages and drawbacks as the Antidote Powder: it's the only readily-acquirable means to cure Burn after it's been inflicted, and to acquire a temporary resistance to Burn after use. Take note that it does come with the added ability to reduce Fire damage for its duration. This can make dealing with foes like the Blazing Bull substantially less daunting. Even if you aren't concerned with suffering from Burn, you would do well to keep this on hand for when you have to face down any opponents that are reliant on Fire-based attacks.

Effects Cures active Burn status abnormalities, removes burn buildup. Also grants a resistance which reduces the speed of Burn build-up by  $60\%$  of its normal speed for 30 seconds and reduces all Fire damage by  $40\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Fujioka the Info Broker  $(\infty ,100\mathrm{Sen})$  Farm: Hirata Estate, Hirata Estate (Revelation) Area: Hirata Estate

# Ministry Dousing Powder

Finite x5

Powdered medicine for treating burns, carried by Interior Ministry guards. Slightly more effective than regular dousing powder, it heals "Burn" status, reduces Burn buildup, and reduces damage from incoming Burn attacks. The Ministry feared Ashina, her eyes bloodshot with the waters of Rejuvenation. This powder acted as a ward for when the time came to turn flame to her walls.

This item essentially serves as a direct upgrade to the standard Dousing Powder, but you won't be able to get your hands on it until particularly late in your journey. The improved Fire defence can be immensely helpful against certain late-game foes. However, given that it has no other perks over its basic counterpart, it would be wise to hold on to this until you find a flame-wielding enemy worthy of its use, such as a Red Guard (Flamethrower) or the Demon of Hatred boss.

Effects Cures active Burn status abnormalities, removes burn buildup. Also grants a resistance which reduces the speed of Burn build-up by  $80\%$  of its normal speed for 30 seconds and reduces all Fire damage by  $60\%$  for 30 seconds.

# Pacifying Agent

Finite x5

Powdered medicine for calming nerves, used by those who deal in unspeakable deeds. Reduces "Terror" buildup and increases Terror resistance for a time. Grave keepers, executioners, the Memorial Mob... all who keep death close keep this powder closer, adhering to a simple rule: If seized with fear, cover your rear.

Consuming Pacifying Agent will instantly cure Terror build-up and reduce additional accumulation for 30 seconds. Since Terror kills you instantly once the gauge fills, it cannot be used after the status has been afflicted. If you find Terror raising, don't hesitate to use this powder to counter it. This item's effect stacks with that of the Motted Purple Gourd, which cures Terror build-up while being infinitely refillable. The buff provided by the Gourd may be less powerful, but is often more than enough to get the job done. Nonetheless, if you still find yourself struggling to overcome the Terror, then nothing else at your disposal is as capable of preventing the fear all together than Pacifying Agent.

Effects Removes Terror build-up and provides a temporary resistance, reducing Terror build-up by  $50\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Peddler: Fujioka the Info Broker  $(\infty ,100\mathrm{Sen})$  Farm: Abandoned Dungeon, Ashina Depths Area: Abandoned Dungeon, Senpou Temple, Sunken Valley, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths

![](images/a21be0fd0b5cab856a26a6e9629c43422b713a9f7e5dc6ed00a5a010f1f6ddae.jpg)

# Eel Liver

Finite x5

A miraculous drug capable of banishing lightning, offered at the Ashina Clan altar. Greatly reduces the amount of damage received from lightning attacks, as well as the "Shock" status abnormality. Lightning is a force of the gods. Eels, while small, are relatives of dragons. Even a god's force can be suppressed, though probably not for long.

This item will reduce the damage you take when affected by Shock. Note that it only reduces the damage received from Shock itself -this is the burst of damage when you touch the ground while affected by Lightning. The Lightning damage taken when you perform a Lightning Reversal is unaffected, even if you take the hit with your body instead of guard/deflect. Despite this, it's still very useful if you aren't confident with your Lightning Reversal timing, since the damage taken for accidentally landing on the ground before performing the reversal is greatly reduced. See the Lightning Reversal entry on P.29 for more details.

Effects Reduces damage taken from Shock by  $50\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Available for 50 Sen from all Peddlers after acquiring the Dragon's Tally Board Farm: Fountainhead Palace Area: Ashina Castle, Sunken Valley, Fountainhead Palace

# Enhancement Items

The items listed in this section are used to increase various attributes and factors, such as strength, defense, the drop rate of Sen, and many more. Whether it be an edge in battle or speeding up the acquisition of other tools you need, these items will be able to assist you in accomplishing your goal. If you're struggling in any way, there's a good chance you can find a helping hand here.

# Gokan's Spiritfall

Infinite

Fallen, headless spirit of Gokan. Reduces Posture damage taken for a time. Consume Spirit Emblems to use repeatedly. Headless are the ruined form of corrupted heroes who once fought for their country. Dedicated burial mounds quietly appease the spirits with severed heads, though none call upon them for long.

Acquisition Drop: Headless (Sunken Valley)

Spiritfall Each Spiritfall is, in effect, an infinitely reusable version of its respective Sugar, at a cost of between two and four Spirit Emblems per use. In exchange for being unlimited in use, the length of their effect is cut by half. There is no such thing as a Spiritfall that isn't worth having, but the drawbacks of some can be more impactful than you may think. For Ungo's effect, it's short duration and non-trivial Spirit Emblem cost means that there is little use for it, as you'll be paying three Spirit Emblems to potentially reduce the damage of a what will often be just a single hit.

Ako's Spiritfall is a little less situational; the increase to damage will be as useful as ever, but under most circumstances you'll be able to deal more reliable damage by simply spending the same amount of Spirit Emblems to utilize a Prosthetic Tool. However, it can still be useful against enemies such as Taro Troops, who are known to leave themselves vulnerable for long periods after attacking. If you only have limited time to bring a foe down, few things will benefit you more.

Much like it's Sugar counterpart, Yashariku's Spiritfall functions best as a means to make a last stand. However, as with Ako's Spiritfall, if you have the Spirit Emblems to spare, they would most likely be better used to fuel your Prosthetic Tools. Nonetheless, if you find yourself in a situation where you can't make effective use of your Tools, then this may be a worthwhile choice when things look dire.

Gokan's Spiritfall is highly useful. The increase to Posture defense can often mean the difference between life and death, especially against foes that are especially adept at dealing out Posture damage.Out of all the Spiritfalls, none provide as much broad utility as Gachiin's-in most situations, this will be able to replace the already powerful Sugar variant. While it may have a relatively high cost to use, its effects can allow you to dispatch or avoid numerous enemies from total safety. Additionally,

while the Sugar variant may last longer, this Spiritfall's lengthy, 30 second duration will seldom fail to carry you from cover to cover. While it may not be able to provide much of an edge in major battles, few things will be able to empower you more when exploring the world at large.

Senpou Temple Candies are the first means you'll acquire to boost your abilities. Each Sugar has its own advantages and uses. Ako's Sugar is perhaps the most practical, as its flat damage increase will provide a distinct edge in any combat encounter you may find yourself in.

If you're confident in your defensive abilities, then using a Yashariku's Sugar can turn you into a force of pure destruction. It cuts your maximum Vitality in half, though. If you're already under  $50\%$  of your maximum health before using one, then your current health will remain at the same level it was before. If you find yourself out of healing items and need to make one last grasp at victory, then this may be a wise gamble.

Few things will give you a stronger advantage than a Gachiin's Sugar when exploring Ashina. This not only makes it easier to execute a stealth approach, but it can enable you to avoid detection, leaving many enemies vulnerable to Stealth Deathblows.

Lastly, Ungo's Sugar and Gokan's Sugar provide options to increase your defense. The former can be particularly useful against powerful enemies who possess the ability to cut you down in an instant, as it will generally prevent you from being killed by a single attack. Likewise, Gokan's Sugar will be able to help protect you from having your Posture broken by all but the most powerful foes. Keeping both of these on hand will allow you to bolster your defenses against any type of foe you may come across.

As such, their value is largely dependent on how useful and scare the resource they provide is. The Mibu Balloon of Soul can be situationally useful, since needing to refill a node of Resurrection Potential is a fairly uncommon event, and needing to quickly refill one is even rarer. That's not to say you won't be thankful for it when those moments arise, however.

# Mibu Pilgrimage Balloon

Finite x5

Mibu balloon made in the year of the Dragon-spring pilgrimage, sealed with a prayer for healthy upbringing. Burst the white Mibu balloon while clasping one's hands in prayer. Those splashed with the water will enjoy increased gains of all sorts for a time. On it is crudely scrawled: "To Tenkichi, from Badger".

Effects Increases Resurrection Potential, Spirit Emblems, Sen, and frequency of items dropped by slain foes for 150 seconds.

Acquisition NPC: Blackhat Badger

The usefulness Mibu Balloons of Spirit is largely dependent on how often you use your Prosthetic Tools and Spiritfalls. If you're not particularly reliant upon them, you may find little to no use for this item. However, if you continually find yourself in what seems to be a drought of Spirit Emblems, then few things will be able to help you as much. While purchasing Spirit Emblems from Sculptor's Idols may be the fastest way to replenish your stocks, this item allows you to acquire them without a detour and without spending a single coin. It would be wise to always try to keep at least one on-hand in case of emergencies.

The Mibu Balloon of Wealth is probably the most useful of the common Balloons. If you find yourself light on Sen and about to enter combat with numerous foes, then there's little reason not to pop one of these before the encounter to earn some extra coin. However, if your sole goal is to gather as much Sen as quickly as you can, then it may actually be the Mibu Possession Balloon that will yield the greatest reward. Popping it before fighting foes who can drop valuable items may net you a sizable payday after you've sold the excess at one of the many merchants across the kingdom. Regardless of which method you prefer, however, keep in mind that there's nothing preventing you from using both Balloons at once.

Lastly, there is the rare Mibu Pilgrimage Balloon, which grants the effects of every other Balloon in a single use, making it easily the most powerful one you'll find. If you find yourself down on your luck after a few setbacks, no other tool will get you back on your feet as quickly as this. Just don't expect to be able to use it often.

![](images/93a711ed1ff60a2da688cb09a9a04554d13c81099299fb0e5186bfb3897bac16.jpg)
