After sprinkling some Divine Confetti your blade will become wreathed in a divine blessing, which will allow you to use it to face down Apparitions in direct combat. Without its use, your sword will be all but useless against foes such as the Headless, and will only deal minimal damage to enemies such as the Shichimen Warrior. If you plan on tackling any of these creatures, ensure you have a solid supply of Divine Confetti, lest you find yourself in a fight that you simply cannot win.

Finite x3

A round, red lump, found inside the body of reedy Dojun. Consume to gain red-eyes and reduce flinching from enemy attacks, but also prohibits the use of Resurrection. Dosaku and Dojun were the quintessential master and disciple. Often when pursuing the ideal self, one need only look within.

Effects Bestows Red Eyes, granting resistance to flinching but preventing Resurrection and reducing resistance to Fire damage and increases Burn build-up by  $50\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Drop: Dojun

Red Lumps Regardless of its source, every Red Lump works the same. Once consumed it will bestow you with Red Eyes for 30 seconds. While in this state, you will not flinch when taking all but the most brutal of damage. This means that you'll be able to power through the enemy's attacks to deliver your own barrage with very little fear of being interrupted. This can be especially useful against enemies that have near-unbreakable defense but low total health.

Remember, however, that just because you aren't flinching doesn't mean you aren't taking damage—keep an eye on your Vitality if you find yourself trading blows with an enemy. There are many encounters in which using this item would be a bad choice; any attack or combo that would knock you down under normal circumstances will be allowed to continue, which proves your opponent with an even more deadly offensive flow. In the hands of a skilled warrior, though, this can be an acceptable risk, and provides a way to dish out colossal damage without fear of being slowed down.

# Utility Items

These items are used for a variety of purposes. From small bags of coin to medicines designed to Poison you, to fistfuls of ash, everything here has its own purpose. Some items in this section are more useful than others, but even the most innocuous item can potentially be used to bring down the most of powerful foes.

# Red Lumps

![](images/9afdf34a5a17d2884793218393021be6a87461c1933b65d5d85bae9d1016dd33.jpg)

# Red Lump

A round, red lump, found inside the body of red-eyed Jinzaemon. Consume to gain red-eyes and reduce flinching from enemy attacks, but also prohibits the use of Resurrection. The red mass will not mold nor wither, and though it does no harm, it will likely remain in the stomach even after its potency has worn off.

Finite x3

Effects Bestows Red Eyes, granting resistance to flinching but preventing Resurrection and reducing resistance to Fire damage and increases Burn build-up by  $50\%$  for 30 seconds.

Acquisition NPC: Dojun, Kotaro, Jinzaemon Kumano Area: Abandoned Dungeon, Ashina Depths, Fountainhead Palace Drop: Kotaro, Jinzaemon Kumano (after sending one of them to Dojun)

![](images/91c46018828245efcce6e8e651954166769b48c17f2de2a2f3a4891ca864ce0b.jpg)

# Ceramic Shard

Finite x10

A piece of pottery that breaks with a satisfying crack when thrown. Throw it at an enemy to draw their attention. Throwing and smashing such pieces made for a popular sport amongst Ashina boys. Even after growing up, they remember the old games well.

As simple as it may seem, few items can open up more opportunities than a Ceramic Shard. When thrown on the ground, the piece will loudly shatter, drawing the attention of all enemies within earshot. Once thrown, their effective range isn't as large as it may seem; they can only be heard by most foes from about two body lengths away. This is often more than enough, however. Once a foe hears the sound, they will immediately enter a Caution state and turn their head in the direction it landed; more curious enemies will head over to investigate. This can leave them vulnerable to a deathblow from behind or make it possible to sneak past them entirely. When thrown directly at melee enemies, it will also cause them to investigate the area you threw it from, allowing you to lure them in for Wall Hug Deathblows. There are few tools as as readily available that will give you as much reliable control of the battlefield as this piece of pottery.

Effects Creates a loud noise when thrown.

Acquisition Peddler: Anayama the Peddler (x8, 20 Sen) Farm: Ashina Outskirts, Ashina Depths, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Castle Area: Ashina Outskirts, Hirata Estate, Ashina Castle, Ashina Reservoir, Abandoned Dungeon, Senpou Temple, Sunken Valley, Ashina Depths, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid), Fountainhead Palace

![](images/d0c281a69d58ff0f2b731aad3fe98b49b6357ba543612d56eb65b3cdf1ecf20f.jpg)

![](images/81dc872066ebdc4c6a327ec98f6e27b1862119c8903cebd16bfd8e8ea6cc6378.jpg)

# Fistful of Ash

Finite x10

Ash gripped into a hardened clump. Throw it at an enemy to temporarily distract them. In Ashina, the snow falls thick and thus the hearth runs thick with ash.

Despite its unassuming nature, few tools are as universally versatile as a Fistful of Ash. After locking-on to an enemy, you may throw this item at them to temporarily blind and stun them, similar to the Shinobi Firecrackers, but its area of effect is much smaller, and it won't startle beasts. They have may practical uses. Blinding an enemy will often give you an opportunity to hit them and deal Vitality damage. It can also temporarily disorient them, allowing you to quickly crouch into a bush, around a corner, or grapple up to a roof, to get out of sight and revert back to caution state. They work on the majority of enemies, including several bosses, but against stronger enemies you will only get a brief moment of respite before they automatically detect you again. The downside to a Fistful of Ash is its extremely short range, requiring you to be in close proximity to land it. Good timing and knowledge of the enemy's attacks are crucial, but the opening it provides is often worth the effort.

Effects Temporarily stuns foes.

Acquisition Peddler: Anayama the Peddler (x6, 30 Sen), Battlefield Memorial Mob (x12, 30 Sen) Farm: Ashina Outskirts, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid) Area: Ashina Reservoir (Prologue), Ashina Outskirts, Hirata Estate, Ashina Castle, Ashina Reservoir, Abandoned Dungeon, Senpou Temple, Sunken Valley, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths, Hirata Estate (Revelation), Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid), Ashina Outskirts (Central Forces raid)

![](images/ed0d3e394ce16ef25f697614621d68b3b359fecedcfa27b84ca84244fef5d8a2.jpg)

# Oil

Finite x10

Plain oil. When the jar breaks, the oil covers everything nearby. Enemies doused in oil are easily set alight, causing them to take additional Vitality damage from fire attacks and making them more vulnerable to the Burn status abnormality.

While one of these jars can be useful for dealing extra fire damage against any enemy, it is especially potent against foes that are weak to fire and Burn, such as the Guardian Ape or enemies with Red Eyes. When combined with tools and abilities such as the Flame Vent or Enchant Slice, the damage it enables can be staggering.

Effects Increases damage dealt by Fire based attacks by  $1.25\mathrm{x}$  and halves the resistance to Burn of any enemy hit with it for 30 seconds.

Acquisition Farm: Hirata Estate, Hirata Estate (Revelation), Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid), Ashina Outskirts (Central Forces raid) Area: Hirata Estate, Abandoned Dungeon, Ashina Depths, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid)

![](images/e13477210d148d97ff16d6cca39177dcce480d9f0a95c49284f83f5c49ce8738.jpg)

# Snap Seed

Finite x10

Fumewort seeds that make a loud noise if you snap them. Useful for breaking the effect of illusion techniques. If an illusion occurs, it is because someone created it. To crush the phantoms and return to reality one must defeat the creator of the illusion. Snap seeds can be of great help in that regard.

Snap Seeds are powerful items, despite having few uses. Using a snap seed will severely damage or destroy any illusion enemies in a large radius centred around the Wolf. Against weaker enemies this will kill them instantly, which is extremely useful when facing the Phantom Bandits in the Ashina Depths, or when surrounded by Lady Butterfly's illusory minions. Stronger illusions, such as the first Corrupted Monk battle, will take some damage and be stunned for a short duration, without being destroyed outright. Snap Seeds are hard to come by early in the game, however, so its best to save them for situations where they're truly needed.

Effects Dispels all Illusionary enemies within a large radius.

# Nightjar Monocular

Infinite

A bamboo tube used to see distant objects. While shinobi already have good vision, looking through this tube with one eye enables one to see even further. The Nightjar Ninja serve Isshin Ashina, guarding the rooftops of Ashina Castle, their sharp eyes on the lookout for any would-be trespassers. Not much escapes the eyes of a Nightjar.

A small telescope that can be used to zoom in on points of interest from a first-person perspective. If you prefer to attack with strategic stealth over brute force, than this will serve as a powerful reconnaissance tool. It is possible to use this to aim certain items, most notably Ceramic Shards; it's not especially useful for this, though, as few items can make use of this in a situation where simply locking-on wouldn't be a more reliable choice. To exit out of its view, simply use the item again, or perform an action such as jumping or attacking. As a bonus, this item may be the best way to take in the often beautiful scenery around you.

Effects Shifts camera to first person perspective and zooms in.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Outskirts

![](images/18c710e4fefe1e0999c46f1d56ef05e9c3e1b9c4fed99ca568721d93f3dad14c.jpg)

# Five-color Rice

Refill

A gourd with five-colored rice used by shinobi as landmarks. Intended to be spread on the ground in recognizable patterns. The white gourd is blessed with fertility, and resting at a Sculptor's Idol will replenish it. This rice is not edible, however.

Using this item will cause you to pour grains of green, yellow, red, blue, or orange rice on the ground. Which color will appear is completely random and does not change their effect. The rice will remain shimmering where you poured it until you travel via an idol, suffer a true death, or reload the game; this allows you to leave a trail to mark where you've been. You'll find this helpful in darker areas, or if you find yourself consistently getting turned around.

Effects Pours shimmering rice on the ground.

Acquisition Peddler: Shugendo Memorial Mob (1600 Sen)

# Teeth

![](images/eea5281d963f8e89e04ceb77cca23168f7fa3a0b98fc81cb2b7391de59e7b771.jpg)

# Hidden Tooth

Infinite

False tooth loaded with a secret shinobi drug, blue in color. Can be used repeatedly. Crush the blue nostrum between the back teeth to die as often as one pleases. Could be useful in certain situations. Surely an unnecessary reminder, but the first death is typically one's last.

Effects kills you instantly.

Acquisition NPC: Hanbei the Undying

![](images/68a76f36a45cadf64752cc2b7231ee5fa95f8734b1769c950b07bdc73a7ec526.jpg)

# Bite Down

Finite x3

Secret shinobi drug, blue in color. When times call for death by one's own hand, samurai turn their swords on themselves as a matter of pride, while shinobi demand a swifter means. Simply crush in the back teeth to die. Nothing more is required. Resurrection is not limited after use.

While there are few situations where this item is practical, it does have its uses. Killing yourself can allow you to lose a foe's attention, giving you an opening to resurrect and catch them off guard with a Backstab Deathblow when they turn away again. Additionally, if used to take your own life while you have access to a Resurrection, you'll be able to access your next Resurrection Node immediately. This is useful when you have little healing and are close to death against a powerful enemy or boss, since you'll revive with more Vitality while still retaining the ability to resurrect if you die again. In combination with a Bundled Jizo Statue, this can allow you to easily Resurrect multiple times, even in one-on-one fight where landing Deathblows can be difficult. The Hidden Tooth is the infinitely reusable counterpart to Bite Down and carries the same effect.

Effects kills you instantly.

Acquisition Peddler: Blackhat Badger (x2, 30 Sen) Farm: Abandoned Dungeon, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid), Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid) Area: Abandoned Dungeon, Ashina Depths, Fountainhead Palace

![](images/40ff36a2a1612cca5eb45613fcf05c5402e6b2ef0376c8c28929898129bde4f3.jpg)

# Illusive Hall Bell

Infinite

A five-pronged bell made of aged bronze. Can be used repeatedly. When rung, Monkeys and Wolves alike are returned to their initial states. However, a monkey caught in the folding screen will not escape, whether the bell is rung or not.

This is a special item that will only exist in your inventory during the encounter with the Folding Screen Monkeys. Ringing this will reset all enemies to their default position and return you to the temple's entrance. Crucially, using this bell will not revive any monkeys you've managed to kill thus far. This is highly useful if you are unable to find a foe or are otherwise unsure how to progress. See the entry for the Folding Screen Monkeys encounter on P.453 for full details of the puzzling battle.

Effects Returns you and any remaining enemies in the Folding Screen Monkeys battle to their starting positions.

Acquisition Automatically acquired upon entering the Halls of Illusion. Area: Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

![](images/ae486df83d49e2113074ab46c10c1fadf323b974293e5420919f0ebde7382423.jpg)

# Bell Demon

Finite x1

A demonic spirit sealed within the Iron Bell of Senpou Temple. Possesses those who ring the bell, strengthening enemies around them. The Bell Demon confers hardship, but perhaps also slightly better spoils. Using this item has no particular effect aside from causing the demon to leave.

The Bell Demon acts as the earliest difficulty modifier you are able to access. After you have rung the bell at the Bell Demon's Temple, you will have this automatically added to your inventory so long as you don't already have one already. So long as it is in your possession, all enemies will have the same stats that they would have at one time of day ahead of the one you're in. The increase in item drop rate means that there is use to be found for it outside of simply boosting the challenge. If you ever find yourself farming for specific materials against foes who you can easily over power, picking this up beforehand will speed up the process. Be careful though, as some tactics that are safe normally can become dangerous gambles thanks to the enemy's boosted durability. If you ever want to get rid of it and return the game to normal, simply use the item from the Consumables menu to remove it from your inventory at no penalty.

Effects Changes enemy stats to those equivalent to one time of day ahead of the one you're currently in. To see the exact values, turn to P.42.

Acquisition Area: Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

Coin Purses Coin Purses come in three different sizes, and are more than just a way to quickly get some extra coin whenever you need it. Under normal circumstances, you'll lose all of the Sen you were carrying you die while being unable to resurrect. Sen stored in Coin Purses is the exception to this rule: like all other consumables, these bags of coin will remain in your inventory until used. It's for this reason that it is highly recommended that you open a Coin Purse only if you are planning to immediately spend the money it contains.

If you find yourself with an excess of loose Sen, then it may be wise to use part of it to purchase a Coin Purse from one of the various Merchants you come across. These typically come with a mark-up of  $10\%$ , but spending an extra 10 Sen to insure you do not lose 100 is not a bad deal. If you're confident in your ability to avoid death then such an investment may very well be a waste, but there's little reason to take such a major risk for such a minor reward. Once you have the Promissory Note, however, there's no reason to avoid them if you can afford them, as the  $10\%$  discount the Note provides cancels out the additional cost.

![](images/0ed55988eb4a3e8e2c4f84e7acf3e1a1f3c9deea9214a4fa2898043b54916248.jpg)

# Homeward Idol

Infinite

A small, palm-sized wooden Buddha. Can be used repeatedly. Held by the Wolf ever since he was saved by his father, its corners are rounded with use. This Buddha is used to return home. It will return the user to the last visited Sculptor's Idol or the Dilapidated Temple.

The Homeward Idol stands alongside the Healing Gourd as one of the most essential items at your disposal. Being able to return to an idol regardless of your current location is incredibly useful when you want to rest and replenish your supplies or upgrade your arsenal of tools by visiting the Sculptor. However, the lengthy activation period means that the Homeward Idol can't reliably be used to escape certain death when trapped in an arena with a powerful foe. If you can first retreat to higher ground or get out of reach of your opponent, then attempting to warp away as a last ditch effort to avoid losing your precious Sen and Skill EXP can be worth the risk.

Effects Used to return to the last Sculptor's Idol you rested at or the Dilapidated Temple.

Acquisition Starting equipment

![](images/991a10b598b3da64fc8602da4c553d38f95fff35afae1ccb1cd899eea5550dff.jpg)

# Key Items

![](images/ef8ccc028cf5619cdb818a6e17154e6f1cc335f4e6911a44d32dd16e1bb612d2.jpg)

The items listed here are unique items that are usually either story-related, a rare form of currency, or something capable of granting a permanent stat increase.

them will automatically be added to your inventory after a story event has occurred.

![](images/80e50107f0ec28adccac928d091b4757063a12d8a77658af3ed01f7d5b7ddaf9.jpg)

# Kusabimaru

A katana given by Kuro, the Divine Heir. An heirloom of the Hirata family, a cadet branch descended from Ashina. Once thought lost, it has found its way back into the hands of the Wolf. The name Kusabimaru beseeches, "A shinobi's role is to kill, but even a shinobi must not forget mercy." A mantra the blade itself may manifest.

Bestowed upon you by Lord Kuro, this sword will be your primary means of attack and defense during your time in the Ashina territories. With it, you can deflect enemy attacks to deal Posture damage and strike them to deal Vitality damage. Its Attack Power can be increased by either converting Mementos into Remnants or with the use of the Dancing Dragon Mask. Mastering the use of this blade will be essential to surviving your journey. To become truly adept in its use, head over to the Combat section, starting on P.19.

Acquisition Given to you by Lord Kuro upon meeting him in the Moon-view tower during the prologue.

![](images/1d7824b57218dafb24bc5a41a6fcd4b13a027f249dd5c6afb9d78469ee13ec09.jpg)

# Shinobi Prosthetic

The artificial arm of a shinobi, passed down by the Sculptor. A replica of a human arm fitted with a variety of mechanisms, apparently designed with modification in mind. While it bears a number of cuts and is stained thick with blood and oil, it has been impeccably maintained.

After the Wolf loses his arm, he awakes to find that this powerful replacement has been attached to him. Once it has been acquired, you'll be able to use the Grappling Hook to swing up to high ledges and across broad gaps. It also grants you use of the Prosthetic Arm Tools, powerful weapons with a wide range of uses. Once you have acquired the Mechanical Barrel and returned it to the Sculptor, you'll be able to upgrade the prosthetic in a number of ways. See the Prosthetic Arms Tools section on P.82 for the full rundown of potential upgrades.

Acquisition Automatically acquired after completing the prologue.

![](images/911992ead24a69ca5545542d4a05227425d8a8fcf8a3956b201da9ac169fd3a6.jpg)

![](images/2539104c5b5989d979ec0f7c24aebe19d2fac7d918cfbd16acc21e3184273339.jpg)

# Mortal Blade

An odachi capable of slaying the undying. Its crimson blade will take the life of any who dares draw it. Without the power of Resurrection, one could not hope to wield this weapon, which allows one to defeat even infested beings. Long concealed within Senpou Temple, the blade is inscribed with its true name: "Gracious Gift of Tears."

This sword is a key part of Lord Kuro's quest to sever his immortality, and one of the four items needed to reach the Divine Realm. It is bestowed upon you by the Divine Child of Rejuvenation in the Senpou Temple. With this in your possession, speak to Lord Kuro while also possessing the Lotus of the Palace, Shelter Stone, and Aromatic Branch to open the path to the legendary Fountainhead Palace. The Mortal Blade is the only weapon that can claim the lives of those who possess immortality, but will kill anyone who attempts to wield it. One you have acquired it, it will remain on Sekiro's back for the remainder of your journey. Claiming this sword also grants you the powerful combat art Secret Technique: Mortal Draw. See P.70 for more details on this.

Acquisition Given to you by the Divine Child of Rejuvenation after defeating the Folding Screen Monkeys and speaking with her.

# Progression Items

The items listed here are essential to progressing events over the course of your adventure, both in the main story as well as the various side quests that you'll encounter. Some of these will provide certain benefits, such as unlocking new mechanics or strengthening you in some way, but most are simply what will be needed to continue your journey. Without these, you won't be able to get far.

![](images/430e0f07b993e3d8a19990478baa356d1a9f44ac6bcea05e9e9184a1f12d9d1a.jpg)

![](images/4ffe54f9a72159d933b4763bca78e0629654b88e4d7335d7d231f598c8fe0fc1.jpg)

# Lotus of the Palace

A white lotus flower found blooming in the depths of the Sunken Valley, where the Fountainhead Waters pool deeply. The flower's aroma attracts female apes. Thus the Guardian Ape carefully tended to it, so as to offer it to his bride. One of the incense ingredients sought by the Divine Heir for Immortal Severance.

One more of the four items that are required to reach the Divine Realm. This can be found in a cave after defeating the Guardian Ape in the Sunken Valley Passage. Give to Lord Kuro while possessing the Aromatic Branch, Shelter Stone, and the Mortal Blade to open the path to the Fountainhead Palace.

Acquisition Area: Sunken Valley Passage

![](images/917df2504a632a8353cdc2602b8e5d58daa765524ffa583148e5d8ed73e700f5.jpg)

# Shelter Stone

A stone found on an altar deep within the village of the water-dwellers. Stones will sometimes appear in the bodies of those who have long drank from the Fountainhead Waters. "Step into the marital shrine and offer the fragrant, auspicious stone." One of the incense ingredients sought by the Divine Heir for Immortal Severance.

Part of Lord Kuro's quest to sever immortality. One of the four items needed to reach the Divine Realm. It's found in a cave behind the Corrupted Monk in the Ashina Depths. Give to Lord Kuro while possessing the Lotus of the Palace, Aromatic Branch, and the Mortal Blade to open the path to the Fountainhead Palace.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Depths

![](images/542d3d711f35b5742eb3c51dd362d068193063796f02e5325471d331a2cbfa21.jpg)

# Aromatic Branch

Dried aromatic wood from the Everblossom. Plucked by the Wolf's father. The Everblossom is a sakura tree, and as such is ripe with nostalgia. Take-ru would likely gaze upon this branch when once it bloomed, reminded of home. One of the incense ingredients sought by the Divine Heir for Immortal Severance.

Another piece of the puzzle in Lord Kuro's quest to sever his immortality. This is dropped by the Owl upon his defeat in Ashina Castle. Give it to Lord Kuro while possessing the Lotus of the Palace, Shelter Stone, and the Mortal Blade to open the path to the Fountainhead Palace.

Acquisition Drop: Great Shinobi - Owl

![](images/76215a931088811946c065035106bc440fa1387f7986b5bbe250d7ba729268d0.jpg)

# Aromatic Flower

Flowers of the Everblossom that bloomed in an old memory. Grafted by Takeru, who took the branch from the Divine Realm as a parting relic. One who seeks Purification may impart the Dragon Tears and these flowers to the Divine Heir of the Dragon's Heritage, thus severing the shackles that bind the immortal bearer of Dragon's Blood.

This item is needed to attain the Purification ending. To receive it, you must receive the Father's Bell Charm from Emma the Physician (P.551) and then use it at the Kind-faced Buddha after having defeated Lady Butterfly. This will transport you to an alternate version of the raid on the Hirata Estate. At the end of the path, you will find the Owl lying in wait. Defeat him and you will receive the Aromatic Flower.

Acquisition Drop: Owl - Father

![](images/cc1fe27954259a2bd18f640a96d461362ccc2415c4a692fdc0f72558bb1d64c0.jpg)

# Divine Dragon's Tears

Tears received from the Divine Dragon. The gracious gift of tears can only be granted by the Mortal Blade. The body of the Divine Dragon is eternal, and its tears, once shed, will maintain their form and moisture in perpetuity. Should one of the Dragon's Heritage partake of the dragon's tears, Immortal Severence will be reified.

The final item needed to complete Lord Kuro's quest to sever immortality. Give this and this alone to Kuro to receive the Immortal Severance ending.

Acquisition Drop: Divine Dragon

![](images/37b214e93202a9fa90cdd9bbd32c1a2cd8e02fb2dc42a8822c08646e631d4e4f.jpg)

# Fresh Serpent Viscera

The persimmon-like heart of a Great Serpent. The Great Serpent is considered to be a god of the land, and the heart is believed to be where one's spirit resides. While its shape bears similarity to a persimmon, in fact this is the red viscera of a god. It is safe to assume that eating it would be poisonous to one's health.

Part of the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline, this Viscera can be acquired by performing a Plunging Deathblow on the Great Serpent from the perch near the Sunken Valley Cavern idol. It can be given to the Divine Child alongside the Dried Serpent Viscera to receive the Frozen Tears. See the section on the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline on P.535 for more details.

Acquisition Drop: Great Serpent

![](images/941ec2403f0611581978ee0033f095104d9d8bd2832e22f5df7d18915adc4280.jpg)

# Dried Serpent Viscera

A dried, persimmon-like heart of a Great Serpent. The Great Serpent is a god of the land, and the heart is believed to be where one's spirit resides. While it looks much like a persimmon, in fact this is the red viscera of a god. Apparently, denizens of the Sunken Valley worship the organs believing they represent the deity itself.

This Viscera is found inside a shrine at the lowest point of the Sunken Valley Passage, near the Bodhisattva Valley Idol. It can be traded in to the Divine Child alongside the Fresh Serpent Viscera to receive the Frozen Tears. Head to P.535 for more details on the events relating to the Divine Child of Rejuvenation.

Acquisition Area: Sunken Valley Passage

![](images/0e9e20b0a3276aa7f05e1be170acf13b05f1acab0efdc6ca6b32bb558f21fcb3.jpg)

# Frozen Tears

Tears that were shed by the Divine Child of Rejuvenation once she became the cradle. They are but frozen drops. By having Kuro drink both the Dragon Tears and Frozen Tears, the Cradling ritual can be performed. Cold Dragon Tears are just that.

The Frozen Tears are the final item of the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline. After giving the two Serpent Viscera to the Divine Child, return later and she will give you this item. When prompted during the games final moments, hand over this item along with the Divine Dragon's Tears to attain the Return ending. See the section on the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline on P.535 for more details on this series of events.

Acquisition NPC: Divine Child of Rejuvenation

![](images/6b23c3567117bd7733c6c02c0f93b4643bf0ffe1ca520ca92c65554b105a5faa.jpg)

# Sakura Droplet

Pale pink crystal residue known to form when an immortal oath fails to establish. Increases Resur-rective Power, allowing one additional resurrection. To repeat the vows of the undying and be awarded Resurrective Power once more surely necessitates the aid of a Divine Child of the Dragon's Heritage.

Dropped by Lady Butterfly upon her defeat, this unique droplet grants an extra Resurrection Node once given to Lord Kuro or the Divine Child of Rejuvenation.

Acquisition Drop: Lady Butterfly

![](images/d9bf97566cb840c09a5f07ed0753e15fbb0f21621268954c93c36055ff66d516.jpg)

# Young Lord's Bell Charm

A bell charm received from an old woman, who asked that it be offered to Buddha. Bell charms protect their holders through Buddha's divine protection. If one finds themselves the owner of another's bell charm, offering it to Buddha on their behalf is common courtesy. The Sculptor at the Dilapidated Temple can advise on how it should be offered.

A charm that can be acquired from Mother Nogami in the Ashina Outskirts. This grants access to the memory of the Hirata Estate when you use it at the Kind-faced Buddha Statue in the Dilapidated Temple.

Acquisition NPC: Mother Nogami

![](images/ac7be047870d6807f9057ab6357a19ba9b6a227e7dbc568292455d90f5506f61.jpg)

![](images/381562ca22778e856d0ea28bcfde35a71b19422ab717d25c222714b3086546d1.jpg)

# Father's Bell Charm

A bell charm previously owned by the Owl. The Owl held this bell for a long time. Offering it at the Dilapidated Temple may result in seeing a different memory than before. There's no way of knowing why this protective bell exists. Perhaps the Owl kept it for himself, or perhaps he meant to give it to someone...

To acquire this charm you'll need to eavesdrop on Emma as she speaks to the Sculptor. See Emma's entry on P.551 for details on exactly when to do this. After acquiring this bell, return to the Dilapidated Temple and use it at the Kind-faced Buddha to revisit the attack on the Hirata Estate from a new perspective. Completing this area leads to item needed for the Purification ending.

Acquisition NPC: Emma the Physician

![](images/83d7fe9987d4a165af28df8ad6b9ea40280b0bda92816dacc6d0365aa40bcd5b.jpg)

# Red and White Pinwheel

A small pinwheel made of red and white paper. Found about halfway up Mount Kongo. The red and white pinwheels simply spin round and round. Everyone is right here.

Acquisition Area: Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

![](images/3afeaf52098b01809ad79d7967fc432d9f7ee712768340baec5645dedab9376f.jpg)

# White Pinwheel

A small pinwheel made of white paper. Found below a cliff at Mount Kongo. Perhaps it was carried there by the wind. It is simply a single, pure white pinwheel. Only the child is right here.

Acquisition Area: Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

Pinwheels These pinwheels are required as part of Kotaro's questline. Giving him the Red and White one will cause him to trust you, giving you the ability to tell him where to go, while handing over the White one will restore his memory, allowing him to safely return to the Divine Children. For more on Kotaro, head over to P.558.

![](images/b96f2f24ff857d308800ce09a5118c3c2ce909fad5b6ad2218e3944af79badd2.jpg)

# Rice for Kuro

Rice that has spilled forth from the hand of the Divine Child of Rejuvenation. Intended to be a gift for Kuro. "Rice is precious. I want nothing more than for the Divine Heir of the Dragon's Heritage to get better." Kuro would likely be pleased to receive it.

This special rice is acquired as part of the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline. Once you receive it, this rice can be handed over to Lord Kuro, who will use it to make a Sweet Rice Ball for Sekiro.

Acquisition NPC: Divine Child of Rejuvenation

![](images/23aeefc11dacb757da6cfcad98fb693b67a20b9a4f63c890d82278b581aea8de.jpg)

# Red Carp Eyes

A carp that lived in the Mibu Village Pond. It has two red eyes. Carp with only eyes that are red cannot become "masters". Though they're considered incomplete creatures that lack the ideal number of scales, their eyes are said to be everlasting. The researcher Dojun in the Abandoned Dungeon wants these eyes to improve his "procedure".

You'll acquire this item after killing the Red-Eyed Carp in the Mibu Village lake, and is required as part of Dojun's questline. Check out the entry for the related quest on P.554 for more details.

Acquisition Recieved after killing the Red Eye Carp in the lake of Mibu Village; Requires Mibu Breathing Technique.

![](images/ec63a725ee320143ce859f0cba5903204f50ab71181cb895887d5b46adb4153d.jpg)

# Precious Bait

This is precious bait. The texture is slimy, and something resembling horns seem to jut out of it. Just the kind of bait the "master" loves. "Ring the bell, drop the bait."

A rare bait that can be fed to the Great Colored Carp. After feeding the first Precious Bait to the Great Colored Carp, you can talk to the Master Chamberlain to receive one Treasure Carp Scale. This will also cause the Carp to become passive towards you, allowing you to swim past it in safety. After feeding it a second Precious Bait, talking to the Chamberlain will yield three Treasure Carp Scales. Feeding the Carp three or more will not yield anything else.

Acquisition Area: Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths, Fountainhead Palace

![](images/df2b4f31ab94a539270d6539aa8a92d5e1a60a6627505ac1b6451acae66125b0.jpg)

# Truly Precious Bait

This is truly precious bait. If bait has hair, you know it's something truly special.

Harunaga: The Hirata noble in the pot is obsessed with thoughts of becoming a "master". "He who receives the scales of the carp becomes closer to a carp himself... I bestow unto you my secret treasure."

Kuromori: The Fountainhead Palace noble in the pot is obsessed with becoming one with the "master." "Present this bait to the master, the Great Carp. Offer it earnestly, but quietly, so no one knows..."

Feed to the Great Colored Carp to poison it. Once it has been eaten, you'll need to rest at any Idol. When you return to the water, the Great Colored Carp will be nowhere to be found. To find out where it ends up, head to P.579 for an explanation of all carp-related events.

Acquisition NPC: Pot Noble Harunaga, Pot Noble Kuromori

![](images/bb2d80ac035692c3858319e2b73c209b2fb408eccb835c89bcd92358ccfa9435.jpg)

# Great White Whisker

A priceless white whisker taken from the Great Colored Carp. While the Great Carp is naturally immortal, if killed, its whiskers can be plucked. The sound of the whisker being removed is surely music to the ears of certain people. Some would feel relief at the sound of their mission being completed, others, the joy of having their heart's desire granted.

Collect this from the corpse of the Great Colored Carp at the Guardian Ape's Watering Hole after feeding it a Truly Precious Bait. Give to the Master's Chamberlain to let him know that his master has passed, and he'll reward you with a Divine Grass.

Acquisition NPC: Great Colored Carp

![](images/feb2f33edaf2f874306e4b39b0b5bf5c06325218a8889edd83c911e0d3ac3404.jpg)

# Water of the Palace

A cup filled with divine waters, a drink popular with nobles of the palace. When a wedding process- sion arrives at the Fountainhead palace, this is the drink they are greeted with. "The nectar of the palae- ance nobles. Go ahead, drink to your heart's content."

Found in a treasure chest in the Mibu Manor in the Fountainhead Palace, this can be turned over to the Mibu Village Priest in exchange for a bottle of Dragonspring Sake. After handing it over to him and resting, the priest will transform into a Palace Noble that drops five Treasure Carp Scales upon death.

Acquisition Area: Fountainhead Palace

![](images/bc7227fdf01a9f52980a22d6a93ef31177821e8facc903b3ae0333aab13831e9.jpg)

# Dragonrot Blood Sample

Blood sample of a Dragonrot victim. Contains stagnated blood. Emma can use this to find a cure for Dragonrot.

Once you reach a certain point in the story, you can gather this from any of those currently afflicted with Dragonrot. Give it to Emma and then rest at an Idol to acquire the Recovery Charm (see P.551 for full details).

Acquisition Can be collected from anyone afflicted with the disease.

![](images/f3951a1f884c3a11a25cd55b4527a8d31add95f0076cf6de5310956303fe0684.jpg)

# Recovery Charm

A Dragonrot Recovery Charm created by Emma. With this charm, one can offer a "Dragon's Blood Droplet" at a Sculptor's Idol to restore all afflicted with Dragonrot back to health. The charm contains a Dragonrot victim's blood, which Emma managed to purify and solidify into a bloodstone.

This charm is given to you by Emma after providing her with the Dragonrot Blood Sample. Once you have this, you will be able to offer a Dragon's Blood Droplet at a Sculptor's Idol to restore the health of those afflicted with Dragonrot, simultaneously clearing out the Rot Essence items from your inventory and resetting your odds of receiving Unseen Aid back to their default of  $30\%$ .

Acquisition NPC: Emma the Physician

![](images/ed2a33aa57408d726a4764f12687b9a85a554b10150a4cb26e98422547160f90.jpg)

# Kuro's Charm

Charm received from Kuro. Placed on the Wolf's person in secret, after he lost his life in Hirata Estate and gained the power of Resurrection. The charm has protected the Wolf well, tempering his ordeals. To part with it would mean facing a path of hardship beyond that endured thus far.

A charm that automatically appears in your inventory on any subsequent playthrough after having completed the game once. Giving this over activates the Hard difficulty mode (see P.44).

Acquisition NPC: Automatically acquired at the start of any  $\mathrm{NG + }$  cycle

![](images/917f37448f4c91cad78d106131a368df77a8fb0217239103f8d983ebc0a4d784.jpg)

# Treasure Carp Scale

A sparkling scale from a Treasure Carp. To the average person it is just a beautiful scale. But there are some who exalt a certain "master", who consider these scales among the most precious things in the world. For this reason, collecting them could be worthwhile.

Treasure Carp Scales are a rare currency, accepted by only two Merchants. The items you can trade these for are all exceptionally valuable, and include Combat Arts, status-curing Gourds, and pieces of the powerful Dancing Dragon Mask. None of these items are necessarily required, but they each provide you with a distinct and powerful advantage that is well worth their price. You will most often find these scales by killing the various Treasure Carps you find in bodies of water throughout the world. Many of these will not be reachable until you've learned the Mibu Breathing Technique, which will allow you to pursue carps underneath the water's surface. Head over to the entry for the Mibu Breathing Technique on P.71 for more details on where and how to use it. As long as you're sure to check each body of water you come across, you'll most likely track down a lot of these scales organically. Just be careful to not mistake a Treasure Carp for its more dangerous cousin, the Man-eating Carp, especially in large groups.

Acquisition See P.539.

![](images/fb00ee5f8de156f429d37b8a5781d7334456c10af92d7f66bb18591406f647b2.jpg)

# Promissory Note

An Ashina trade promissory note. Matabei Anyama's last piece of product. Discounts the cost of items when purchasing from merchants. A sen saved is a sen earned. And so long as one draws breath, business will continue.

Sold to you for 1 Sen by Anayama the Peddler at the conclusion of his questline during the Central Forces Raid. Once in your possession, you will receive a permanent  $10\%$  discount at all Peddlers that deal in Sen.

Acquisition NPC: Anayama the Peddler

![](images/c459d2959696e66acf49ee840be8bfea0d9b07414147f58239b11f461fd7ecca.jpg)

# Dragon's Tally Board

A tally board carved from a large piece of jade. Possessing this increases the stocks that can be purchased in merchants' shops. Such a tally board is highly prized by the merchant class. Old custom dictates that those of dragon rank are recognized as supreme merchants by the imperial palace, and should be given the best possible treatment.

Dropped by the Corrupted Monk in fountainhead Palace, this is an important late-game item. Once you have it in your possession, most merchants will begin to sell Eel Livers, Divine Confetti, Snap Seeds, Scrap Iron, and Black Gunpowder with unlimited supply. See the Peddlers section starting on P.559 for the exact details on how merchants are affected.

Acquisition Drop: Corrupted Monk

# Dancing Dragon Mask

![](images/2a1ab511256fc86edfa043d9d20698b5a5a50893846c8901b670418a143541d7.jpg)

# Mask Fragment: Right

A fragment of an old dancer's mask. The original must have been broken into several pieces, and this fragment appears to be the right side of the mask.

Acquisition Peddler: Pot Noble Harunaga (7 Scales)

![](images/0922f278cf839ded74ab0ff61174ac95aca91e6cccdb545fb6f9a90ffdd12113.jpg)

# Mask Fragment: Left

A fragment of an old dancer's mask. The original must have been broken into several pieces, and this fragment appears to be the left side of the mask.

Acquisition Peddler: Pot Noble Koremori (12 Scales)

![](images/609f6f5b1a2b442aa6a6c503b13d1c71533d9b13f8eb14ab00118a29b603ec30.jpg)

# Mask Fragment: Dragon

A fragment of an old dancer's mask. The original must have been broken into several pieces, and this fragment appears to be a decoration at the top of the mask.

Acquisition Peddler: Abandoned Dungeon Memorial Mob (5000 Sen)

Mask Fragments This elusive mask is split into three pieces. Each piece is exceptionally difficult and expensive to come by on its own, but collecting all of them rewards you with a powerful ability: once you've gathered the entire mask, you will be able to trade five Skill points at a Sculptor's Idol to permanently increase your Attack Power. Besides Mementos, The Dancing Dragon Mask is the only means of increasing your attack power, and the only way that isn't limited per playthrough.

Given the difficulty and high cost of acquiring the pieces, this is best reserved as a late-game or even New Game + goal. Before then, any Skill points you have are almost certain to be better spent on actual Skills and abilities. However, on a long enough timeline, you'll eventually reach a point where you will find yourself with nothing left to spend the Skill points on. Once that happens, this item provides you with their only practical use. This mask may not help you much on your first journey, but it will be invaluable on  $\mathrm{NG+}$  and beyond.

# Sake

These alcoholic drinks make for both a perfect gift and an easy way to get someone talking. Once given to either the Sculptor, Emma, or Isshin Ashina, they will begin to talk to you about themselves and their past and, from time to time, will reveal more than they intended. The discussions this enables are essential to understanding many core elements of the Ashina clan's history and lore.

![](images/6ceac88ad6fe83c9ff748b05d0ee8b88a70166253164f03ad44950e53b3c2522.jpg)

# Ashina Sake

A bottle of Ashina-brewed sake. Sake is a drink meant for sharing. While it does not contain water from the fountainhead, it is made from the purest of waters, and is a drink beloved by the people of Ashina.

This traditional Ashina drink is best given to either the Sculptor or Isshin Ashina first. Handing one to the former will grant you the history of your prosthetic arm, while offering it to Isshin will see him reminiscing on the rebellions that formed the Ashina clan. However, you do also have the option giving the sake to Emma, which will result in her telling you the story of a difficult patient she once had.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Depths, Hirata Estate (Revelation) NPC: Emma the Physician

![](images/a8c2eb957b624ee39cd7c8b13d712d49bc0848fece35da00ba3c8f0eaee07ba6.jpg)

# Unrefined Sake

A bottle of cloudy, unrefined sake. Sake is a drink meant for sharing. This cloudy sake is one of Isshin Ashina's favorites. It has a rich, full-bodied flavor. On the other hand, it has a reputation for getting one too drunk, too quickly.

Giving this powerful sake to Isshin Ashina will cause him to tell you of Genichiro's mentor, while it will cause Emma to reveal who taught her to wield a blade. Most interestingly though, offering it to the Sculptor will get him to tell you how he lost his arm. You can receive three of these over the course of your journey, so you're free to choose who you'd like to hear first, but it's highly recommended that one of the earliest ones make their way to the Sculptor as the tale he tells is revealing.

Acquisition NPC: Isshin Ashina Drop: Juzou the Drunkard, Tokujiro the Glutton

![](images/96f59590752930fcd60c6d8488f0a31c735ede314e957bdb711f2b33a0de3e1c.jpg)

# Monkey Booze

Alcohol created by dew pooled in a hollow tree. Fruits hidden by monkeys in tree hollows can sometimes ferment and turn into sake with a bit of luck. While it's known for its brutally harsh flavor, some find this acquired taste irresistible.

Handling this natural wine to the Sculptor will result in him discussing the training he endured in his youth. Providing it to Isshin will end with a conversation in which he explains what a Shura is. Finally, offering it to Emma will cause her to tell you of a time that a monkey saved her life. If you opt to give a Dragonspring Sake to the Sculptor, then it's highly recommended that you give the first Monkey Booze to Emma, as the two conversations are related.

Acquisition Area: Senpou Temple, Ashina Depths

![](images/a9b4fb9c0570827f6a63a7507cf736bdf541535004f08e553a98ddd615d49ad9.jpg)

# Dragonspring Sake

A bottle of crystal-clear sake. Sake is a drink meant for sharing. A top-shelf sake brewed by the Ashina brew master with water from the Dragonspring. The pure water extracts every last bit of flavor from Ashina's finest rice. There are no words that can do the flavor justice. To understand, one must taste it for themselves.

The finest sake on offer. After taking a sip, Isshin Ashina will tell you of the parties that always seemed to occur the moment he got a bottle and the fools it attracted. Emma will do likewise, discussing how she would use those same parties as a chance to sneak out of the castle. Lastly, providing it to the Sculptor will cause him to tell you the story of how he met Emma and their general history together. It is strongly recommended that you give this to the Sculptor when you first receive it, as his conversation provides critical backstory and context to both himself and Emma.

Acquisition Peddler: Exiled Memorial Mob (1000 Sen) NPC: Mibu Village Priest

# Skill Texts

These texts are the primary way in which you'll unlock Skills over the course of your journey. While you will on occasion discover an ability out in the wild, the majority of Skills are only revealed through the Esoteric Texts. Once you have acquired such a text, they will enable you to access different skill trees, where you can spend your Skill points to expand your abilities. These range from granting you Combat Arts to providing you direct increases to the efficiency of certain items. Obtaining these as quickly as possible is highly recommended, as each provides unique benefits and perks that will assist greatly in staving off death. For more details on each of the skill trees that the Esoteric Texts unlock and the different abilities each of them have to offer, see P.46.

![](images/45f7b6fd03844df1fde4ca86a9ae4760aec8b0e8a39c981d5c12dae81b03cac4.jpg)

# Shinobi Esoteric Text

A book of secrets that details a variety of techniques employed by Shinobi. Grants the ability to learn "Shinobi Style" Skills. Within this text are the innermost secrets of the Shinobi Arts, such as attacks performed in the air and hiding one's body to avoid detection. Such moves could never be practiced by samurai.

Unlocks access to the Shinobi Arts skill tree, which is primarily focused on improving your defensive and stealth capabilities. This will most likely be the first Esoteric Text you acquire and is filled with many of the most essential skills that you would do well to claim early. You can acquire by speaking to the Sculptor after gaining your first Skill Point.

Acquisition NPC: The Sculptor

![](images/34ed634661d71b57db1be4d7a4d2129434b34d93d59c266d326785cf0254d6b6.jpg)

# Prosthetic Esoteric Text

A book of secrets that details a variety of techniques for use with Shinobi Prosthetic. Grants the ability to learn "Prosthetic Style" Skills. Written by a man who abandoned the path of the Shinobi, but could not bring himself to discard his painstaking research. He never expected to pass these on to anyone else.

Once you've acquired this Text, you can begin investing in the Prosthetic Arts skill tree. This gives you access to a wide array of offensive abilities to expand the use of your Prosthetic Tools, as well as options for upgrading the amount of Vitality your healing items will restore Affix three tools to the prosthetic arm and the Sculptor will hand over this valuable text...

Acquisition NPC: The Sculptor

![](images/7730bdfffc0616ca91ef39820c407c42a77ea2c96c49cb615ce773df52989fcf.jpg)

# Ashina Esoteric Text

A compendium of the Ashina Sword Style. Allows one to learn "Ashina Style" Skills. The text reads like a history of Isshin Ashina's battles; when young, Isshin fought desperately time and time again, polishing his technique in the blood of his enemies. He consolidated his learnings under the "Ashina Style" name for the sake of his clan's dominance.

After executing an Assassin for him, this Text will be bestowed upon you by the Tenu of Ashina. With it, you'll have access to the Ashina Arts skill tree and the foundations of the Ashina fighting style. Once mastered, no other Arts will do more to strengthen the power of your deflects.

Acquisition NPC: The Tenu of Ashina

![](images/77278635b9e94f10d8f521d74aa9461a52b33551d6c5b0023c1d6d35a65ebcb4.jpg)

# Senpou Esoteric Text

A book of secrets that grants the ability to learn "Senpou Style" Skills. Those of the Senpou Temple mastered martial arts in the pursuit of virtue. They considered strong fists and strict discipline essential against Buddha's enemies. However, Senpou Temple was seized by an obsession for the Undying, which corrupted their teachings and style.

This Esoteric Text is perhaps the easiest to miss, but as long as you keep an eye out for it you'll be able to pick it up with little difficulty over the course of your travels. Once it's in your possession, it will endow you with the Temple Arts skill tree. The Temple Arts are filled will powerful martial arts attacks and direct increases to Sen and item drop rates.

Acquisition Area: Senpou Temple

![](images/a85160f0c9aa1325b35b85a10041e21a9610b5b0604c9de49e5035d3e54dd12c.jpg)

# Mushin Esoteric Text

A unique text of the legendary Ashina Mushin Compound Style. Young Isshin would stop at nothing in his lust for power, and this single-minded search for strength ended in him taking Ashina for his own. This is the result of combining techniques from the styles he encountered. This drive defined Isshin's achievements and as such, this text will never be finished.

An Esoteric Text that unlocks the Mushin Arts skill tree. This particular tree offers you some of the most powerful Combat Arts in the game, but you'll need to have mastered at least one of the other trees before it will be bestowed upon you, and two other trees before you can acquire any of the skills it contains.

Acquisition NPC: The Tengu of Ashina, Emma the Physician

![](images/8c6af2d6a606be2b197e599cdd9303a3acf9df9b97277b6180c1520e5a8a4937.jpg)

# Anti-air Deathblow Text

Compendium on the Shinobi Martial Art, "Anti-air Deathblow". Skill unlocked upon acquiring this item. "A technique which serves the shinobi who is not bound by the earth in battle. Leap towards an opponent who has exposed himself in mid-air, and strike, killing him before he hits the ground."

Once purchased, you will automatically unlock the 'Anti-air Deathblow' Skill. This Skill creates opportunities to instantly cut down certain foes as they leap up to attack. Head over to P.71 to learn more about this.

Acquisition Peddler: Blackhat Badger (1200 Sen)

![](images/2a78e311fe440bd3dfe9bc01bb18a704a5d78f683c47bf7f87de2eae8d1a43f7.jpg)

# Floating Passage Text

Compendium on the Combat Art, "Floating Passage". Skill unlocked upon acquiring this item. "Unleash attacks in a flowing, dancelike form, overwhelming enemies in a furor of graceful aggression. This technique belongs to the Ashina sword school, though it has been deemed heretical due to its foreign origin."

Purchasing this text will teach you how to perform the 'Floating Passage' Combat Art, a powerful combo of relentless attacks. See the Combat Arts section on P.69 for more details.

Acquisition Peddler: Pot Noble Harunaga (5 Scales)

# Documents

Not all of the items below are strictly required for any particular purpose, but their descriptions often hold valuable knowledge, ranging from vital information that you will need to understand the world around you, to texts explaining important aspect of the Ashina clan's history. If you find yourself unsure where to go, then taking the time to read these will often set you on the right path.

![](images/09e0ba269ebda88be0873af8bcc5550d00fdfa3feea2bf5109d1ff361522bb19.jpg)

# Immortal Severance Text

A book from Kuro on the art of severing ties with the Dragon's Heritage. It looks old. The binding is torn, and several pages are missing. "Herein describes the means to perform the Rite of Immortal Severance. Beyond the Fountainhead Palace, locate the Sanctuary and imbibe the tears of the holy dragon on the divine realm."

Acquisition NPC: Divine Heir Kuro

![](images/b2ab833fc39a7ab7ba03687cd3c8ecda9595d5022f23da30d88574456a45bc32.jpg)

# Immortal Severance Scrap

Part of the Book of Immortal Severance, left behind by Takeru. "With Mortal Blade in hand, my blood may be shed. With my blood, the aroma will be complete, the divine realm will be in reach. Immortal Severance will be at hand. I must ask Tomoe to assist with the beheading..."

Acquisition NPC: Emma the Physician

![](images/3b7c90a8387450dd75725d4e3430dc7c0f1d8e0d287e7aab40bae6dc2a287b2f.jpg)

# Fragrant Flower Note

A note from Kuro, written by Takeru, former Heir of the Dragon's Heritage. "It is said that relatives of Tomoe once gathered the Fountainhead Fragrance and arrived at the palace. You may find a key where the waters of rejuvenation converge in a deep pool. A white and deeply fragrant flower..."

Acquisition NPC: Divine Heir Kuro

![](images/d644c352e136cde8648c20a310edb71e1065feeeb58a5b6c40a7441e51bdcc8e.jpg)

# Tomoe's Note

A note written in Tomoe's soft handwriting. "Lord Takeru's coughs are worsening still; Returning to the divine realm is hopeless, and I wish only to sever the Dragon's Heritage and restore his humanity. Restoration requires the Everblossom and Mortal Blade, and yet I cannot acquire the latter. It was hidden by the High Priest of Senpou Temple, who has no desire to sever the immortal ties..."

Acquisition NPC: Emma the Physician

![](images/c0e74bc81bf36338633a2976f05bd1d63c13441a02d6aab5bfe170333638a87b.jpg)

# Page's Diary

An old diary entry written by Takeru's page. "Lord Takeru held his arm over the incense burner, and attempted to cut it with a sword. But incredibly, his wound healed instantly, and not a drop of blood was shed. Lady Tomoe said, 'Without it, your blood cannot be spilled.' What could she be referring to, I wonder?"

Acquisition NPC: Divine Heir Kuro

![](images/72e30fe9a05eb08a30b0683502693cdc791330226476a743155462e9867854c6.jpg)

# Okami's Ancient Text

An old note left by the Okami clan, who sought to reach the divine realm. "A fragrant stone, enshrined in a village within the depths of Ashina. One must throw oneself for it to be found. With this, the fountainhead fragrance is complete. Let us depart now, to the divine realm."

Acquisition NPC: Divine Heir Kuro

![](images/81afd8a42c2437b32ad003b9a496ae3ab2fcd622500b5b9f92182db2229bc2b0.jpg)

# Rotting Prisoner's Note

A note left by a dead and rotting man in the Abandoned Dungeon. "Supposedly the fragrant stone is enshrined in a village in the Ashina Depths. But how to interpret 'throw oneself'? This is as far as that old Okami tome could take me. But did they truly reach the Fountainhead Palace? I'd like to know, but it seems I never will. Kotaro... forgive me..."

Acquisition Area: Abandoned Dungeon

![](images/0722c274aea7d7b96ef5adc02d3dda7ee56e41aede28f574c416d7684bf960da.jpg)

# Black Scroll

An old text describing a black Mortal Blade. "In addition to the red Mortal Blade, there exists one that is black in color. The blade's name is "Open Gate", and is said to hold the power to open a gate to the underworld. It is through this power that it creates life. I beseech you, make offerings for the Dragon's Blood..."

Acquisition Area: Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid)

![](images/b98bc2405de1586992b040692d680020d7752ce5b5c3544de6484cb3644f708b.jpg)

# Holy Chapter: Infested

A passage describing a journey to enlightenment. "For an age, I have been blessed by the worm. To be undying is to walk the eternal path to enlightenment, thus I must become enlightened to understand why I cannot die. It is said the holy dragon's origins were in the west. So I wonder, how did the worm come to be bestowed upon me?"

Acquisition NPC: Holy Senpou Priest Area: Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

![](images/e36b23609ccae9dd294bafa201d08f3a3f1530fc03b9dd372fb06b7d0a1c8241.jpg)

# Holy Chapter: Dragon's Return

Sacred passage on a path to enlightenment. "Undying, I pray for the Dragon's return. Undying, lo, let us wait an age; for the Divine Heir to assimilate the cold dragon tears; for the cradle to consume the pair of serpentine fruits. Let the cradle endure, giving Him shelter; granting His return to the west."

Acquisition Area: Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

![](images/a7ca657f548c44acec3dff694e0188f9edb7b3867711cf8aa97a14147060893a.jpg)

# Ornamental Letter

A letter thrown into a well. "Kuro's Wolf, Your destiny awaits you at the moon-view tower. Escape from the well and find the tower bathed in moonlight. Even without a blade, you can reach it. Stay silent. Stay vigilant."

Acquisition Area: Ashina Reservoir (Prologue)

![](images/f073e9f30803aba58f3c022f2b7c6e170ba7ec6b7922949d45d2677e80a9d6e3.jpg)

# Rat Description

A description of the "rats" that have snuck into Ashina. Speak to the Tenu again once the rats are dealt with. The rats: - Assassins from Senpou Temple - Short stature, wear bamboo hats - A number of rats are lurking about - Last seen around Ashina Castle Gate

Acquisition NPC: The Tenu of Ashina

![](images/3aaac11018fe59e4e4eecc02c5b96033a1c2e01a48ec998c90d84e64bd43a40e.jpg)

# Isshin's Letter

A note left by Isshin in the watchtower. Perhaps Emma knows his current whereabouts. Dear Emma, The Ashina Castle Gate has grown loud with the sound of scurrying. The Tenu will see to the rats. Worry not. Isshin

Acquisition Found in Isshin Ashina's room before fulfilling the conditions for making him appear there

![](images/7ade8a1a63f873ad29cc46bd69cd860b00188c2541f86be18150c8d011cd8daf.jpg)

# Surgeon's Bloody Letter

A worn and bloodstained letter from Dosaku, the surgeon in the Abandoned Dungeon: Required: 1 tough man Preferably a strong samurai, or a young, large soldier such as a member of the Taro Troop. Must be delivered unharmed. -Dosaku

Acquisition NPC: Dojun

![](images/e3cc9ad1fa2d00d165d92e32b7ae5c218adce36c6c329f4e5e32c7d6f580be50.jpg)

# Surgeon's Stained Letter

A tattered, blood-covered note written by Dosaku, the surgeon in the Abandoned Dungeon. At the bottom of the Mibu Village pond, You will find a Sakura carp. You will know it from its red eyes, which are said to never rot. I require those red eyes. -Dosaku

Acquisition NPC: Dojun

![](images/234ae8580e4d14171aee9fbd286082b6892bfbab92b1fc3bc28680f9aa9e7feb.jpg)

# Dosaku's Note

An old note left by the surgeon Dosaku: My disciples have abandoned me for Dogen. Unwilling to dirty their own hands, they all left me for that hypocritical quack. Dojun! My last disciple! Even if I die, the research must continue. Finish the procedure, for Ashina's sake. -Dosaku

Acquisition Area: Abandoned Dungeon

A page torn from the Ashina Herb Catalogue, a compendium of flowers and herbs. "The 'Snap Seed' naturally grows in ravines and deep valleys. According to denizens of the Sunken Valley, such places are appropriate for offering oneself in marriage to the Great Serpent. If one wishes to become a bride, they must enter the belly of the Serpent in the valley."

Acquisition Received after killing the Assassin near the Ashina Castle Gate Fortress idol.

A tattered note written by Anayama. Seems to be from some years ago. "Lucrative info #36 When we broke into Hirata Estate, we found a barrel that spewed flame. The boys lit a roaring bonfire with it and made merry with the drink. Must have been a shinobi's tool."

# Keys

There are a few doors you'll find that you will be unable to bypass without the use of a specific key. If you've encounter a door that you are unable to open up, then you will most likely find the means to do so here.

![](images/6e276df0b830909ff7923bcad66b1f116dd392d326f0f153d61b4516e3b7d081.jpg)

# Hidden Temple Key

The key to the Hidden Temple in the Hirata Estate, given by the Owl. The secret temple is located in the very back of the Hirata Estate. "Two, The lord is absolute. Defend him with your life. If he is taken, bring him back at any cost."

Acquisition NPC: Ukonzaemon Usui (The Owl)

![](images/ba0572d81f37938938a824b31da980f6c8966df830c9c53d5e164107f21f22bc.jpg)

# Gatehouse Key

The key to a samurai gatehouse located in the Ashina Reservoir, not far from the well the Wolf was kept in. Here, Gyoubu the Demon's Broken Horn is respectfully guarded by Ashina samurai. The Broken Horn is the spear blade once wielded by Gyoubu the Demon. It's said that no prey can escape Gyoubu's horn. It pulls enemies in, and is even capable of stripping an enemy's armor.

Acquisition Received by killing the soldier on the bridge leading up to the Abandoned Dungeon Entrance. Area: Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid)

![](images/bb64b4d5ae2cbb8133a07cffde6b08df4afa0cbe64c0038e56b3a16150654ddf.jpg)

# Gun Fort Shrine Key

The key to a shrine deep within the gun fort. The gate behind the shrine's idol is made to be opened. The Sunken Valley clan will shoot any stranger who approaches, and the Snake Eyes' guns are particularly feared. This elite group of women are descendants of the ancient Okami Clan. Their especially sharp eyes allow them to snipe victims at great range.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Castle

![](images/aea83449fa3614cad69c4b2d24909cc0d8aa63b8743dda897d55ef9b55b91c00.jpg)

# Secret Passage Key

The key to the secret passage that leads out of Ashina Castle. The secret passage can be found at the end of the moat in the Ashina Reservoir, not far from the Moon-view Tower. Kuro has escaped the castle through this passage, and the Wolf looks to join him there.

Acquisition NPC: Emma the Physician

# Prayer Beads

Individual Prayer Beads have no effect on their own. Once you have collected four of them, however, you'll be able to use them at a Sculptor's Idol to craft a Prayer Necklace, the only item that can permanently increase your maximum Vitality. 40 of these beads are scattered all across the Ashina lands—some you will find on the bodies of powerful enemies, others will be stowed away in chests. # Prayer Necklaces

# Gourd Seeds

After you have collected four Prayer Beads, you'll be able to use them at a Sculptor's Idol to make a Prayer Necklace. These necklaces are worth striving for, as they're the only means of increasing your maximum Vitality. This upgrade will also grant more overall healing from your Vitality-recovering items, as they all heal based on a percentage value. Gathering the resources needed to piece these together can often be a challenge, but few things are going to be more essential to your survival. If a Prayer Bead becomes unavailable for whatever reason, such as if the foe that drops it disappears, it will appear in the Offering Box at the Dilapidated Temple for 1500 Sen.

![](images/2515e83a43956c49d8f54200966be4281acff2d312858bffaf261f7d830a91e6.jpg)

# First Prayer Necklace

Loose prayer beads strung together in offering to a Sculptor's Idol. Increases maximum Vitality and Posture. A prayer bead necklace befits the strong. The ferocity of Ashina's army is renowned throughout the nation. Its generals are especially talented, every one of them accomplished in the Ashina sword style.

Second: In Ashina, there is a towering pink ogre of a man, said to have gone red-eyed and run amok before he was long shut away in a forsaken dungeon...

Third: The bull was a fiery, rampaging beast and nothing more. In the last great war, the corpses of Ashina samurai piled high. Something had to be done.

Fourth: Only those who have mastered the Ashina blade may set foot inside the castle dojo. Isshin will often stop by unannounced, just to keep the students on their toes.

Fifth: The gun fort of Sunken Valley is commanded by the Snake Eyes, an elite force of women able to pierce distant targets with mighty flint cannons and phenomenal vision.

Sixth: The Centipedes will seek out a leader, often changing names out of loyalty. Centipede chiefs are known as "Long-arms," for their large talon-like weapons.

Seventh: An unrivaled sumo wrestler once served a great feudal lord. Dismissed after giving to drink, he fell to a life of brigandry. And so he was dubbed Juzou the Drunkard.

Eights: Lone Shadows are the Interior Ministry's most trusted agents. Each of leader Masatsuna Oribe's seventeen born has a specialty, from poison to shinobi hounds.

Ninth: Robert's father came from afar across seas to the south, in search of the Undying. Repelling a thousand blades was a small price for the blessing of rejuvenation...

Final: The Seven Spears of Ashina were pivotal in Isshin's coup. He awarded the lance to none but his most loyal samurai. Yet now, only a few of the Seven remain.

Gourd Seeds may very well be the single most valuable item you can find. Once you have found a seed, it can be returned to Emma the Physician to permanently increase the uses of your Healing Gourd. There is never a situation where having a greater ability to restore your Vitality isn't vastly preferable to the alternative. Having found or missed even a single seed can often mean the difference between life and death. Not all of them are readily apparent, and some are cunningly hidden away. If you find yourself near one then acquiring it should always be your top priority.

# Memories

Memories are the unprocessed memories of your most affecting battles. Once they've been confronted at a Sculptor's Idol and turned into a Remnant, they will permanently increase your Attack Power by one, upping the damage you deal with both Kusabimaru and your Prosthetic Tools. You will acquire the majority of them naturally over the course of your journey—they are incredibly valuable and should always be used as soon as they are acquired. Of all the foes who will grant them to you, only Lady Butterfly's isn't mandatory before you can potentially reach an ending. If you ever feel as though your attacks are coming up short, then taking the time to hunt down a foe who grants one of these may give you the edge you need.

# Memories

The battle memory of an extraordinary foe, lingering in the mind of the Wolf. Commune with a Sculptor's Idol and confront memories of battle to permanently increase Attack Power.

# Remnants

Remnants are all that remains of your memories of important battles once the related Memory has been used at a Sculptor's Idol. Each one will increase the damage you deal with any weapon once. Outside of the power they bestow, each Remnant also holds a piece of history about the foe you claimed it from. Examining them will help you better understand the foes you face and the world you find yourself in.

# Remnants

The battle memory of an extraordinary foe. Although distant, recollection of such a memory provided sustenance for the Wolf.

![](images/0ed78a5487183d74c263389ef3c0504613236fd688aab72467fc36650ff120b1.jpg)

# Remnant: Gyoubu

Gyoubu Oniwa once led a group of infamous bandits, but was defeated by Isshin, who was so captivated by his show of strength that he took him in as an Ashina warrior. Oniwa would later go on to become Genichiro Ashina's most trusted retainer.

![](images/4901eda837fa314c5f0c15ba0b17f23aaa8bfe689688297da25e8ca94ca5cb8e.jpg)

# Remnant: Lady Butterfly

The Phantom Lady Butterfly was appointed by the Wolf's foster father as one of his mentors in shinobi techniques. These mentors employed strict methods. The cultivation of shinobi techniques can only be achieved in the midst of battle.

![](images/9cc004f5ecf88663cba317b5ee0737dcac60d925b2031e802fd00675b3731fbe.jpg)

# Remnant: Genichiro

Born a peasant, Genichiro Ashina was taken in by the Ashina after his mother's death. With his country on the brink of defeat, Genichiro took to heretical arts and mastered the Lightning of Tomoe. Such heresy may be the key to saving her.

![](images/bc97ea97d9f4deadfc1fafa4c866e9eca7ef3223b934b35e67cec4ce21dd8575.jpg)

# Remnant: Screen Monkeys

The Halls of Illusion lie on the threshold betwixt life and death. Departed souls of the Divine Children drift and sway, taking shelter in the monkeys of the temple. Such is why the Divine Child of Rejuvenation speaks of them as friends.

![](images/2346499fd4147a6bc29d7faa257d420c6378193265be52aa79e583e420ff739d.jpg)

# Remnant: Guardian Ape

They say that an infested body is the mark of the undying, but such a long life would surely be quite lonesome for even an ape. Perhaps the echoing roar of the Guardian Ape was in fact a solicitation of sorts...

![](images/e9aaffefe23ae60c1ed4f7c1afbe8934862da8a11fc5ce275ac7aedcdcb3657e.jpg)

# Remnant: Headless Ape

At one time the Guardian Ape shared its den with a mate. But he alone became infested, while the other passed away. Now, even the flowers offered in tribute to her passing have withered to dust.

![](images/2e5d270ce378cdee8649bc3f67fa4d033d955ed68d142ace258e11cab3c4b6f4.jpg)

# Remnant: Corrupted Monk

The Corrupted Monk donned the mask of a fierce guardian deity. Her form was nebulous, appearing as if in a dream. What reason could there have been for guarding the Mibu Village cave entrance?

![](images/d1b33378a59d8e920ea63f846c8d831f03a1c7128eb765e7d4c0ce6d7983e4d1.jpg)

# Remnant: True Monk

The Corrupted Monk was among the infested, standing over the Fountainhead Palace. Indeed, immortality would seem a fitting quality for eternal watcher of the palace. Her true name is Priestess Yao.

![](images/786a67bae35b932a93efd5ec91d67756a0aab6bec194c820fec3752bcd6ce444.jpg)

# Remnant: Great Shinobi

The Great Shinobi Owl's unbridled ambition was to obtain the power of the Dragon's Heritage. Now is the time to let one's true name ring out across all of Japan. It was all for the sake of this ambition.

![](images/41a41885fdc3cad62671c335b238f0c7e6acb5d2013492c916043ad6c8bff60b.jpg)

# Remnant: Foster Father

Owl took in the hungry cub on a whim and raised him as a shinobi. The process was so engrossing that he hoped they might enjoy a true battle to the death some day. He got his wish, if only in an old memory.

![](images/7e5aa26576135791cab6370df4a09fbd9e6ac167afde22b5673268649ad62259.jpg)

# Remnant: Divine Dragon

The Divine Dragon of the Everblossom came from the west long ago, eventually making its way to this land. Some parts of Ashina are exceedingly old. Water coursing through her ancient rocks and soil allowed the Dragon to take root.

![](images/17b98bb45b32de128b541d21b92d5a9935c3deb0916e9755de5591f701cd3d2b.jpg)

# Remnant: Saint Isshin

One who returns from the great beyond does so at the peak of their prosperity. Isshin coveted strength and all manner of techniques throughout his mortal struggle. He wished for war until his final hour, and that is precisely what he got.

![](images/3fab84f3dd32028129ccec9f16620136d112ffffb1df0a71458100f3a73080bc.jpg)

# Remnant: Isshin Ashina

The elderly Isshin was akin to a sharpened blade. His steadily honed techniques culminated in the Ashina Style, soundly eliminating all wasted or idle movement. A master who took the spirit of his craft to its pinnacle; a true sword saint.

![](images/ddfe4908f78dbccafc6d84e6c5f5752145c82721cc7f4b516451367a1d6eff3d.jpg)

# Remnant: Hatred Demon

A man who failed to become Shura instead became a vessel for the flames of hatred. As fate would have it, he was bound stubbornly to this world. It wasn't until he became a demon that he was finally able to depart for the next.

# Rot Essences

Rot Essence is the physical manifestation of the Dragonrot, a disease that will infest the populace of the Ashina territories the more you take advantage of your ability to resurrect. If you possess a Rot Essence, then the character it's connected to will fall ill, potentially restricting their ability to talk or perform other actions. Having these in your inventory will also substantially reduce the likelihood of receiving Unseen Aid. These Essences cannot be used or thrown away. The only way to remove them from your inventory is to use a Dragon's Blood Droplet at a Sculptor's Idol after you've obtained the Recovery Charm. For more information on Dragonrot, check out P.13.

![](images/e3e9676827d8a4ac2b5c03de4e714f0bfb90819c474f29cbf40e347477514b9f.jpg)
