# Restructuring Components

![](images/fc26fbc882cfd5556a130aeb49a49be06661e325639a6e3bb5cded5ef1dcc01d.jpg)

Perhaps the most powerful aspect of the Prosthetic Arm lies in its adaptability. Scattered across the Ashina territories are weapons, tools, and artifacts that once combined with the Sculptor's skills can turn

into powerful Shinobi Tools. From hefty battle axes to blinding fire crackers or a basic whistle, these tools are often more than just simple ways to deal a heavy hit. Finding them, however, is only the beginning—each tool also needs to be improved and upgraded. The items in this section are used for that purpose and are well worth tracking down.

# Tool Upgrade Parts

The items listed here are used to add some kind of new tool or feature to the Prosthetic Arm. Once you have acquired them, they will needed to be handed over to the Sculptor, who will permanently load them into your arm. Finding these will be essential to building a worthwhile arsenal. See the section for Prosthetic Tools on P82 for full details on each tool.

![](images/5d985a089b56c46e05030bbc4b9d09fa9b2e3f1e7bb165d5bc0d60708cf7fd54.jpg)

# Mechanical Barrel

A mechanical metal barrel that can be given to the Sculptor to enable Prosthetic Tool Upgrades. It appears to have been made to fit perfectly inside the wrist bone of the Shinobi Prosthetic. A reinforced core is sure to make a shinobi's fangs even sharper.

Acquisition Drop: Gyoubu Oniwa

![](images/dc6b7dbf94443a6f1a0eabcb12825c462824a706469dd938432c4b7556a567e6.jpg)

# Shuriken Wheel

A mechanical device made by the mechanical genius Dogen. Can be fit into the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a working Prosthetic Tool. While it is palm-sized, a surprising number of shuriken can fit into the Shuriken Wheel, as the edges were designed for stacking. A fine example of what can be achieved when one matches mechanical finesse with a Shinobi's talent.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Outskirts

![](images/739fbd34cfb6f3648b87434b17fd2d210c564b93cf95f71cc5d0ddbbcdbcdc0a.jpg)

# Shinobi Axe of the Monkey

A heavy, black iron axe used by shinobi. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a working Prosthetic Tool. This boorish axe is used less for cutting and more for breaking things with its weight. Once the favored weapon of a shinobi known as the "Bounding Monkey of the Sunken Valley," it was lost along with his left arm.

Acquisition Area: Hirata Estate

![](images/92b0cace9a5f9e26b02ebdb5743e480693946f33ecde1845ba3b113eaaafd43c.jpg)

# Sabimaru

An ancient kodachi short sword, its blade mottled with bluish rust. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to create a Prosthetic Tool. Forged by the Ashina clan to resist the inhuman evil that had invaded Ashina in times long forgotten. It was the poisonous gift of the blue rust that finally drove the spirits out.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Castle

![](images/f02873130031fbffdcef3d70ce4e2db1acd58e5e72ae86e3b6c1303b0e319a39.jpg)

# Iron Fortress

An iron fan made in the far west. Can be fit into the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a working Prosthetic Tool. Experienced iron-ribbed fan users can deflect arrows and even bullets using this tool. Passed down through generations of assassins serving Senpou Temple, it wouldn't be surprising if the next owner decided its weight was impractical.

Acquisition Peddler: Blackhat Badger (1600 Sen)

![](images/129dd779b48d82bfc9d05055e8e7ddbfaf880ce316bd86081448f3dbd6fff52c.jpg)

# Gyoubu's Broken Horn

Famed horn-spear once used by Gyoubu Masataka Oniwa. Affix to the Shinobi Prosthetic to create a Prosthetic Tool. The horn contracts to pull enemies in, also capable of stripping crude armour. When the horn was broken during the rebellion, Isshin praised it for its "splendid shape," awarding Oniwa with the cross-bladed spear of Shuzen Tamura.

Acquisition Area: Ashina Reservoir

![](images/54dfd13a810ff68c229d8c25d2eb4b8b411b8407b7f405dc86d404aa8c1737b5.jpg)

# Robert's Firecrackers

Firecrackers from across southern seas. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a Prosthetic Tool. Makes a deafening sound, frightening to animals. Sold by little Robert and his father to raise funds for their travels. Their voyage brought them to Japan, where they would seek the "Undying" in an attempt to extend Robert's life.

Acquisition Peddler: Crow's Bed Memorial Mob (500 Sen), Battlefield Memorial Mob (500 Sen)

![](images/720cdf7665a86f6495e019229d3a454bf9e75b27e6103fd32515b0023fafa1b6.jpg)

# Flame Barrel

An iron barrel that spews fire. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a Prosthetic Tool. It is difficult to control the rage-filled Red-eyes with the power of man alone. However, a fire-based weapon could be a means of resisting them. They are said to fear fire above all else.

Acquisition Area: Hirata Estate

![](images/3e34f3dbf6b53886f8dfff9c74b229e2be8936f7ee33068bffed3a83891b3bbf.jpg)

# Mist Raven's Feathers

A bundle of Mist Raven feathers. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to create a Prosthetic Tool. In Usui Forest far to the north of Ashina, live many mysterious birds of prey. The Mist Raven is the only one to have eluded capture by all who have tried. Should you somehow manage it, you'll find it gone, only feathers in your grasp.

Acquisition Area: Hirata Estate

![](images/11b8036e34ed3f47eb3690cecb367ee44e58e1e7b93517370463e08934cfbd18.jpg)

# Large Fan

A large fan made of dyed red Japanese aralia leaves. Can be fit to the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a Prosthetic Tool. Fanning it creates a large vortex of wind, spiriting away those it catches. "Divine Abduction through an eight-handed fan. Once is fine, but twice and you'll never return. If abducted, we'll head to Mt. Kongo. At Senpou Temple we'll perform virtuous deeds."

Acquisition Area: Sunken Valley

![](images/1951dcf83d765a74ac52095eb50aabdb90323c6e9a5af7eaa2faad4671d79326.jpg)

# Slender Finger

The slender finger of a young woman. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to create a Prosthetic Tool. Found in the belly of the Guardian Ape, it is partially digested. There is a shinobi technique called the Finger Whistle that can drive beasts wild. The one who used it before clearly used it for this purpose, as evidenced by the finger's open hole.

Acquisition Drop: Guardian Ape (Headless)

![](images/138c94a1e33a171c5b9a22d0a2a0caaa8ef8247e32713717a80ebd5af57ec471.jpg)

# Phantom Kunai

A kunai used by Lady Butterfly that can be used to upgrade the Loaded Shuriken. A ringing sound is heard when the kunai is thrown, and phantom butterflies appear in the kunai's trail. Since childhood, Lady Butterfly had accumulated much experience in Usui's forest, far from civilization along Tozan Trail. His forest is filled with mist and mystifications, making it ideal for training in illusion techniques.

Acquisition Peddler: Anayama the Peddler (3000 Sen)

![](images/6c6cb141d66820e5346a33e5761e58fb42f80dc5940d95ae4f15aef371ff4ee2.jpg)

# Pine Resin Ember

A piece of resin that contains a continuously smoldering flame. Can be used to upgrade the Flame Vent. The resin was found in a black pine within the forests of Mibu Village. The ever-smoldering flames acted as a landmark to find one's way to the village. In time the villagers came to loathe the flames, and the black pines were lost. Those who defended the flame were equally loathed.

![](images/3eee76883b8aa39e13ab7044723b6945a77b43fe10824d5a866f412645d9d139.jpg)

# Maltcontent's Ring

An old ring well-suited for slender fingers. "King-fisher" is engraved on the underside. Can be used to upgrade the Finger Whistle Prosthetic Tool. Wearing this ring as you blow the finger whistle will create a somber tune. The weeping voice is full of solitude and beauty. Possibly somber enough to temporarily quell a voice of rage.

Acquisition Drop: Shichimen Warrior (Guardian Ape's Burrow in Ashina Depths)

# Upgrade Materials

The items listed here are used to upgrade your already-acquired Prosthetic Tools. Being able to reliably acquire a steady supply of each of these materials is essential to unlocking many of the most powerful weapons you can hope to find. Some of these will be easily searchable from merchants, while others will require you to scour the land in order to find them. However, if you manage to gather enough to build your tools up to their peak, then you'll have the potential to cause mass destruction at a moment's notice.

![](images/925763973b19b68a526385d87ad95401cb7ffb20e8f02408343cd484bf594f51.jpg)

# Scrap Iron

Iron dregs mined in Ashina. Widely used for basic reinforcement, it can serve as a base material for Prosthetic Tool upgrades. Ashina is burdened with thick snow and infertile land, but the scrap iron dug from her soil is anything but crude.

Acquisition Available for 150 Sen from all Peddlers after acquiring the Dragon's Tally Board (except Anayama: requires quest advancement) Farm: Ashina Outskirts: Ashina Soldier (Katana, Hassou Stance/ Weak, Spear), (Hassou Stance/Strong); Ashina Castle: Taro Troop Nightjar Ninja, Shinobi Hunter  $\rightarrow$  Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo: Spear Adept  $\rightarrow$  Assassin (Wooden Hat), Centipede; Sunken Valley: Elder Monkey, Rock Diver; Hirata Estate: Bandit (Axe, Katana); Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid, Interior Ministry raid): Lone Shadow Area: Ashina Outskirts, Ashina Castle, Ashina Reservoir, Abandoned Dungeon, Senpou Temple, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths

![](images/1daa3e54cdc91ea49018802b330c0ae0a2b5c07af01b570657c7f4afe714681f.jpg)

# Fulminated Mercury

Highly precious grains forming the base for a devastating form of gunpowder. Used in explosive Prosthetic Tool upgrades of advanced rank. Created in secret by the Interior Ministry using knowledge from across southern seas. The central forces' military might owes much to this tiny tweak of chemistry.

Acquisition Farm: Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid): Red Guard (Flamethrower, Firebomb) Area: Sunken Valley Passage, Hirata Estate (Revelation), Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid), Ashina Outskirts (Central Forces raid), Ashina Reservoir (Central Forces raid)

Acquisition Area: Ashina Depths

![](images/99e298d24a6493f701f91b1e285745e71384636c2f622f8b92c154b8b42251ef.jpg)

# Scrap Magnetite

Magnetic ore mined in Ashina. Base material commonly used in Prosthetic Tool upgrades of intermediate and higher rank. Forging with magnetite produces a hard steel; a precious commodity in Ashina. Bedrock offering up this ore is constantly mined out, making it a rare one at that.

Acquisition Peddler: Shugendo Memorial Mob (x2, 330 Sen), Anayama the Peddler (#2) (x4, 300 Sen) (requires quest advancement) Farm: Ashina Castle: Ashina Soldier (Katana, Hassou Stance, Spear  $\bigcirc$  Taro Troop  $\bigcirc$  Shinobi Hunter  $\bigcirc$  Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo: Spear Adept  $\bigcirc$ assin (Wooden Hat)  $\bigcirc$  Shugendo Memorial Mob (x2); Sunken Valley Passage: Rock Diver  $\bigcirc$  Fountainhead Palace: Okami Warrior; Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid): Red Guard (Kodachi, Dual Katana), Nightjar Ninja, Lone Shadow Area: Ashina Castle, Abandoned Dungeon, Senpou Temple, Sunken Valley, Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid), Fountainhead Palace Drop: Lone Shadow Longswordman

![](images/e95ea921c79ac98deba43fa29c8a64ed285c1547ade80f28a402307807f730aa.jpg)

# Adamantite Scrap

Adamantine ore with a dull, silvery shine. Base material commonly used in advanced Prosthetic Tool upgrades. Adamantite can only be mined in the oldest parts of Ashina. Ancient rock and soil is said to attract the grace of gods, perhaps lending this metal its supple strength.

Acquisition Peddler: Exiled Memorial Mob (x2, 600 Sen) Farm: Ashina Castle: Shinobi Hunter  $\bigcirc$  Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo: Spear Adept  $\bigcirc$  Ashina Depths: Exiled Memorial Mob (x2); Fountainhead Palace: Okami Warrior; Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid, Interior Ministry raid): Red Guard (Kodachi, Dual Katana), Lone Shadow Area: Sunken Valley Passage, Ashina Depths, Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid), Hirata Estate (Revelation), Fountainhead Palace, Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid), Ashina Outskirts (Central Forces raid) Drop: Lone Shadow Masanaga the Spear-Bearer

![](images/7abe89e92d474850d915026260cabd36fb495ff3b1b189b7495281f525a3a5fe.jpg)

# Yellow Gunpowder

Amber-colored grains forming the base for powerful gunpowder. A precious commodity only found in the Sunken Valley. Used for explosive Prosthetic Tool upgrades of intermediate and higher rank. The yield from yellow powder is greater than that of black, lending the valley stronghold defenses their fiery vigor.

Acquisition Peddler: Anayama the Peddler (#2) (x3, 300 Sen) (requires quest advancement), Toxic Memorial Mob (x2, 270 Sen) Farm: Senpou Temple, Mt. ![](images/62d5557eb1aa31cca053c247e88973ea617871f76b2b3a699f90c578bdc68006.jpg)

# Black Gunpowder

Black grains forming the base for gunpowder. Material used in alchemical Prosthetic Tool upgrades, including those of an explosive and occultic nature. Even the most mundane form of gunpowder has a wide variety of applications.

Acquisition Available for 150 Sen from all Peddlers after acquiring the Dragon's Tally Board (except Anayama: requires quest advancement) Farm: Ashina Outskirts: Ashina Soldier (Matchlock Rifle); Hirata Estate: Bandit (Fire Bow); Senpou Temple, Mt. ![](images/0e8775bdb1b2b7d5721d2c9adebbc6a7de10579cfca94c8d912f26bb424e829c.jpg)

# Lump of Fat Wax

These lumps of fatty wax form inside the body in rare circumstances. Can be used for intermediate and higher Occultic upgrades for Prosthetic Tools. Considered omens of disease, they are known to grow larger as the illness worsens.

Acquisition Peddler: Anayama the Peddler (#2) (x3, 300 Sen) (requires quest advancement) Farm: Ashina Castle: Old Maid  $\square$  Sentry  $\square$  Senpou Temple: Seeker (Fists, Bo Staff)  $\odot$  Infested Seeker; Sunken Valley: Old Maid  $\square$  Ashina Depths: Mibu Taro Troop  $\odot$  Fountainhead Palace: Palace Nobility (Red Garb, Blue Garb) Area: Senpou Temple, Ashina Depths NPC: Dojun Drop: Lone Shadow Vilehand

![](images/6e733ecb930f4122a36b555d3ae0548541317d7489e39006c616b2995d1b3906.jpg)

# Lump of Grave Wax

A lump of fatty wax that has formed inside the body and turned pitch black. Used for occultic Prosthetic Tool upgrades of an advanced nature. A long-suffered illness will see the growth turn large and blacker still. It is customary to run water over the site of an extracted growth.

Acquisition Farm: Ashina Depths: Mibu Taro Troop  $\bigcirc$  Fountainhead Palace: Palace Nobility (Blue Garb) Area: Sunken Valley, Fountainhead Palace, Ashina Outskirts (Central Forces raid) NPC: Dojun

![](images/21231f5683daccbf15c65a93d7cc42a5af679d44b1ca24e4c342660ac3e6cc85.jpg)

# Lapis Lazuli

Precious azure lazulite, used for the highest level of Prosthetic Tool upgrades. Fountainhead lazulite is a symbol of eternity, and anything forged with it will never break nor rust thanks to the blessing of the Divine Dragon. Tools forged with lazulite transcend human intellect, and are dubbed as treasures of the Divine Dragon.

Acquisition Peddler: Pot Noble Koremori (x2, 6 Scales) NPC: Pot Nobles Drop: Shichimen Warrior (Fountainhead Palace), SPOILER: Demon of Hatred (x2)

![](images/e1957b96005534617f396d6ccf7ddbcc218fb4dd7466ab4170969444cdc007fd.jpg)

Chapter 3

# Path of the Shinobi

Like the waters of fountainhead, the mysteries of Ashina are deep and ancient, and the Wolf is caught in a battle for the secrets that this land has long concealed. This chapter follows the Wolf as his quest takes him to every corner of Ashina, avoiding or eliminating anything that gets in his way.

![](images/879a239e958cabf539f20a3b97c7e732a3d10156fba53dfc4db241ca34f23956.jpg)

# About this Chapter

Here we'll go over the way we've presented the walkthrough and explain each of the elements used. You'll find an icon legend here, and we've reprinted it on the Chapter Overview page at the very start of the book to make it easy to flip to if you're ever uncertain what an icon represents.

![](images/fd301479f7d3855fd744d74c963b734a0d7af6e94d76156452df43e83f2380f4.jpg)

# Using the Map

The environments in Sekiro are extremely complicated, with a lot of verticality. To convey as much information as possible on the maps, we've used a not entirely top-down perspective to give you a sense of that verticality, and used different colors for the specific environmental features to make them clearer.

# $①$  Sculptor's Idol

Each Sculptor's Idol is highlighted like this, with accompanying text letting you know some of the key features of the nearby area. Each one is also marked on the overview map at the start of the area with a page reference, so you can easily skip to where you are in the game.

![](images/b16f6dc9b7b7d490006c550d367e4764786178d1b8d569e0349a2cee11222e2a.jpg)

$\Theta$  Main Waypoint Black Waypoints show the main suggested path through an area, taking you along most of the key encounters while heading towards the primary objective in that area if there is one.

![](images/3ee563c619aef993d177e378cee1e0ac2aa5da193be6dbf112e98181d04dbeb4.jpg)

Exploration Waypoint Blue Waypoints occur when there are multiple routes or methods for reaching an area. They can be anything from alternative stealth options, to ways that allow you to quickly get through the area. Most commonly, however, they will take you along paths that explore parts of an area not along the main route, often leading to additional loot, enemies, or other areas. Where possible they have been arranged so that you can either follow them directly from the preceding Main Waypoint, or skip ahead in the sequence and just pickup the route again at the next Main Waypoint.

![](images/c8368ec206c89e02a48757e84c5225106481ef1bbf3a10107e7f26e8b6e6529e.jpg)

# NPC Information

Every time either a new NPC appears, or theres an event that that can happen related to one that has already been introduced, you'll see one of these boxes. They will always appear in the sequence of the Waypoints at the time you would encounter them when following the route. Each NPC is also marked on the map so if you're not following the route you can still find them easily, and then read this for context.

Boss Information There are many tough bosses to overcome as you progress through the game, so along with some key strategies in the text, you'll also find these small information boxes. Contained within each one are the amount of Vitality and Posture the boss has, along with how many Deathblows are required to finish it off and the Skill EXP you'll gain upon defeating it.

# $\odot$  Quests and Endings (Spoiler)

There are a total of four possible endings you can attain in the game, most of which require you to complete specific actions to obtain the required items. To ensure that you don't miss out on those things, we've included these boxes that will update you at anytime something related to an ending can be accomplished. We've made them red so that they stand out, allowing you to avoid reading them if you don't want to learn about the endings as you progress.

![](images/3fb206226d11ffaf6300877f27592bfa5d2a84921e53e498fed6858380db57d0.jpg)

You awaken wounded and unarmed at the bottom of a damp waterway. Directly in front of you you'll find the Ornamental Letter that was dropped by the mysterious lady above. Reading it will inform you that your Lord, the Divine Heir Kuro, is locked in the nearby Moon-view Tower, and that he's in need of help.

# 0

Run along the underground channel and jump on top of the ledge ahead, then wall jump up to the top of the next series of ledges to emerge outside. With no weapons or other means of defending yourself, stealth is your only option if you wish to reach Kuro alive. Run forward to here and shimmy along the narrow ledge to reach the long grass on the other side, and then crouch down in it so that you're hidden from sight.

![](images/0280100ea1bdbf3a191a613ee4c67c033d16e7454112b5d2f0ef1b6b5001e440.jpg)

# 2

Sneak through the long grass, past the conversing soldiers and go into the crawlspace beneath the small building. There are holes in the floorboards, and if you position yourself correctly, you'll be able to eavesdrop on a pair of soldiers inside.

![](images/16dbf23058385e39846c3a677a6b26f2d5e3d83f3d1c686bc24a8fff27e3c20f.jpg)

# Item Legend

1 Ornamental Letter x1  
2 Pellet x1

![](images/17b637e133d905c0e71508f4a611182a065c1d2d1dbbc3d1ae15b8c6175dc5b7.jpg)

![](images/e797d34d0a37bbf1e43c0e03ae435916eb0a00de5aa66d5234b018d008c765d7.jpg)

![](images/0517434fac28f252f46cd70be77e3c41ba3ee2456da9dfd5626f7e9a508e065a.jpg)

Continue on through the hole on the opposite side of the crawlspace, and follow the grass to the edge of the cliff here. From there you can eavesdrop on another pair of soldiers, and then you'll need to drop down and shimmy along another narrow ledge.

![](images/0a276e81cad2fb915e0a738e1959963fb130b7178ef52a630ecb39a0c086f8c0.jpg)

After pulling yourself up, run along and jump over the gap in the path, and then climb up a series of ledges to reach a hole in the side of the tower.

![](images/a4c20bc7b897c631364f24210576bfdb8c41a1c3d0fce7441a770733e1f41b36.jpg)

After conversing with Lord Kuro, he'll hand you the katana Kusabimaru, along with a Healing Gourd. Worried for your safety, Kuro will not let you leave the building until you place the gourd in your Quick Items, and since your Vitality is low, you may as well use it now. Now that you have a weapon, it's time to clear a path to the secret passage so that the both of you can escape, so unbar the door and take the battle to your enemies.

![](images/f300a675b7ebc8e55b39ee6b7a40702427b6cb5b9eca60bf96bc01b6c7fc3cac.jpg)

Before leaving the building, make sure to go upstairs and grab the Pellet laying on the floor, so that you have access to some additional healing if you need it.

![](images/2a399022d9adb26ba11cd518427d2524241968d41979c685f3d0df909961d371.jpg)

Most of the soldiers in this area have very low Posture and Vitality, so one or two hits is all it takes to break their Posture and allow you to land a Deathblow on them, whether they guard or not. They also only have a couple of attacks, so take some time to get used to them and try to practice deflecting; deflecting attacks is generally much more beneficial than guarding them, so becoming comfortable with this is a crucial aspect of the game.

![](images/2d6efb9de9438d62220f29076e1bfd850ac7b9d06472a8970ef8fecb757d7246.jpg)

The soldier at the top of the stairs directly ahead of the tower has his back to you; crouch down and sneak up behind him so that you can use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/ca8f15446a27a063b895d1b0f02df9385a6c1fc31317b6e7067c120efdccee55.jpg)

Another soldier at the bottom of the stairs will spot you—let him come to you so that you don't attract the attention of a third soldier further ahead.

![](images/60ebebdd30b1cf9dd56c0711c755412e66a13769ace293c6f347e66aa4c4509f.jpg)

None of the enemies in this area provide any Skill EXP or drop any loot, so if you just want to get through the area you can run past most of them and head directly to the secret passage, picking up at Point 10 on the following page.

![](images/1f941b887dfa7d5707da940351da90654c6cec8caebcb0431bb9237192fd7a66.jpg)

![](images/f5c92ecf038e3b2edcca952d255646df54d561cc1fd9958e764b75295a58d6f5.jpg)

At the top of the stairs you'll find the imposing Leader Shigenori Yamauchi attempting to block your escape. Like the other enemies in the area, you can simply run past him if you wish. This enemy type is fairly common throughout the game, so it's worth taking some time to learn the basics of how to fight them, especially since you don't have anything to lose at the moment.

You'll notice that he has two Deathblow Markers, which means that you'll need to either deplete his Vitality twice, or break his Posture twice so that you can land the required two Deathblows to finish him off for good. Counter-slashes are an excellent means of inflicting a lot of Posture damage, so you want to try to set up some predictable deflect opportunities. If you attack him and he guards, he'll always retaliate with a counter-slash of his own; use single attacks until he guards, and then just wait and Deflect his counter so that you can follow-up with your own counter-slash.

Just around the corner from where you first face him you can also pick up a couple of Fistfuls of Ash. This item will blind him temporarily if you throw one at him, which can create a bit of breathing room if you need it.

![](images/28bbf0559540717f90485f21f1026bd4d3ce8e19485ec6bbe00242091f85a862.jpg)

![](images/0c5d57e119e7022f5014aa5e9587dfca1555407ee656ff9e99798963ffdaca89.jpg)

The door that Yamauchi was guarding is locked, so to continue you'll need to run around to the right of it and along the large protruding branch at the end of the path. Jump across from the end of the branch to the ledge on the other side of the gap.

![](images/1b8f2318c86da75cb01632499e3e0bc11bd884c9497953a68811eab0290560e7.jpg)

Wall jump up the support, grab onto the beam at the top, and then shimmy along until you can eavesdrop on the two guards standing on top of the bridge.

![](images/d33cd086f2736da215abe418a4d7c7032dc6a03537b3718ae5fb88375509a082.jpg)

If you want to avoid fighting the Assassin, drop back down to where you wall jumped up, and then drop down again to a narrow ledge further down the wall. From there you'll be able to follow a path around the outskirts of the area to reach the secret passage. If you happen to fall down, however, you'll need to contend with some Geckos that have made their home in the shallow water. Because they're so low, however, you can just jump above them and instantly use a Plunging Deathblow to kill them, even after they're alerted.

![](images/d5f8eaa140b30017d69517fe88c3fdbadb490496aeb00913a8f0e059f6128820.jpg)

After their conversation, continue shimmying along until you can pull yourself up, and then quickly close in and start attacking the Assassin that's standing on the beams beneath the bridge. Continue along to the end of the beams and you'll be able to drop down and hang onto the edge of them, which will allow you to shimmy towards the wall and eventually drop down onto the ledge below.

![](images/4ea217a0a9b6ee14f1d6d15f596519c201f429fcb5c75bd09baeb63e032568c1.jpg)

![](images/fdbdd8ec374d8fb7144e2afc87455528d716634f731f362e41c230c80cfce468.jpg)

Follow the series of ledges down (grabbing the Pellets along the way), and then inspect the door. You'll automatically use the reed whistle and call for the Divine Heir. Once he arrives, you'll find yourself in a narrow tunnel beyond the door, and you'll be able to speak with him again if you wish. Head straight along the tunnel, and as you exit you'll be greeted to a field of wheat bathed in moonlight. After a few steps, it will be revealed that you are not alone. Lord Genichiro Ashina lays in wait, ready to reclaim Kuro.

![](images/843e3bd9d37af8fa37cba08e1333917d2fe3c8401b7f449962f77d2dc0502ba6.jpg)

After years of neglect and despondency, you're completely outmatched by Genichiro at this time and defeat is all but assured. It is possible to defeat him, but no matter how valiant your effort the end is always the same: Genichiro will cut off the Wolf's arm and take your Lord with him as you lie bleeding and defeated. Your efforts will only affect the cutscene that leads to that unfortunate end.

You'll have a much better chance against Genichiro after you've been through the game once and have a good deal of combat experience. If you want to see the alternate cutscene on your first playthrough, though, check out the tactics on P.442 for a little help.

![](images/08c6653566e05e521a636487aacb1dd00b4349d29c8f3cc8e220f5220376fb85.jpg)

The Ashina Outskirts are a collection of fortifications on the cliffs below Ashina Castle. A bridge once connected this area to the castle grounds, but the current unrest means that many approaches to the castle are either destroyed or heavily guarded.

![](images/1e4346bb64b9d5ff6f949a165a3dc2bd5ea55c0f713fe2bcfbe6d586ae46fd42.jpg)

![](images/358da066c8801382d665fb12e912a412bc842b3e573e014948550de3f53b7f75.jpg)

# Item Legend

![](images/9abbebf54a46751a3c6fc727bf5c05e1af1e62f29041bb151e8f40a207d24507.jpg)

Light Coin Purse x1

![](images/29211978e381d2d99d62b27e3be0be546e3124de5b6122234a5b92fa0353d3f8.jpg)

Pellet x2

![](images/61d593360ea883fd7ee09c69b5096b7cfe669b70ab0a2fe7cb3c79e5c62f3379.jpg)

# Dilapidated Temple

You awake in a temple filled with hand-carved Buddha statues, with the Sculptor himself hard at work on his next creation. The first thing you'll notice is the new Shinobi Prosthetic that has replaced your original arm. If you'd like to learn more about it or how you got here, speak to the Sculptor. Once you've exhausted all the topics of conversation, head outside.

![](images/7592157e45562b4556224669b07e49b96bc0ddb616d2d29ce9e8ef227c7e47fd.jpg)

![](images/c533e84fc538540fa285e0bb666b516e4d7eecf07eb751d803c9584e58218f26.jpg)

In the courtyard, you'll find your first Sculptor's Idol. These mysterious statues provide you with a myriad of useful features that you'll gain access to as you progress through the game. If you die, you'll revive at the last one you communed with, and resting at them will restore all of your Vitality and refill any gourds and consumables. Resting will also revive most of the enemies in the area, so it brings with it some risk. Find rare Prayer Beads or Memories from particularly intense battles and you'll be able to offer them to the Idol in exchange for increasing your core attributes.

![](images/cd53685517f1c6c40018963f3073e2fe3fc81a506f9d69450b177c9defe67dce.jpg)

![](images/f5d1f866c659b043f1e9f1c822f54587ed3ec6c9cf544ab4ae9bdda7e1f19fdb.jpg)

# The Sculptor

The Sculptor plays a vital role in helping Sekiro throughout his journey, as only he has the ability to install new Prosthetic Tools. You don't have anything he can work with at the moment, but you'll be returning to him frequently over the course of the game.

![](images/26d8d73f455aa3329daca8840adc47005b4ea2b261383413bc15ae9d26cfdb87.jpg)

# Emma the Physician

If you rest at the Idol, Emma the Physician will appear just in front of the building that the Sculptor is in. Emma also has a pivotal role to play in that only she is capable of increasing the capacity of your Healing Gourd. If you manage to find any rare Gourd Seeds, be sure to bring them to her.

![](images/89ec42a7f8dfe0f87ce1b629b2d575672e58d7d3a724a5be145fb89c458e8e51.jpg)

# Hanbei the Undying

Up the hill at Position A you can find Hanbei the Undying standing next to the Offering Box. The Offering Box is a magical device that will allow you to purchase items that have otherwise become unavailable due to the Peddler selling them being killed or otherwise incapacitated. Talk to Hanbei and the first thing you'll have to do is face him in a duel so that he can test your swordsmanship.

Once you win the duel and Hanbei's true nature is revealed, he'll offer you the choice of using him as a sparring partner if you like. There's no downside to accepting his offer, and training with him will allow you to practice many of the game's core mechanics whenever you like with no permanent risk. As you unlock new skills, or are killed by certain types of attacks, Hanbei will gain new training options, so check back with him often.

![](images/749c6b50f146b6f5ab39ec127084a2f9e02b711535c6943f180f687ba0d57057.jpg)

Heading down the small tunnel to the side of the temple will lead you to an apparent dead-end, but if you look closely at the wooden panel at the end you'll notice a human-sized outline has been left on it. While you're unable to make use of this one currently because it is locked from the other side, it's important to keep a lookout for any suspicious looking walls. Some may turn out to be hidden doors known as Shinobi Shortcuts. Hugging these can lead to hidden rooms or even bring you to entirely different areas.

![](images/6919e639523508e01c318109d2b36a67fab17e0d38eb01e482614b0fc36c46ac.jpg)

![](images/96f17f242d014735f71e510df0e69ffc0e4f3a4700ed6f4eacef52c1314ec713.jpg)

Return to the main courtyard and head around the back of the temple building so that you can get the Light Coin Purse that's laying on a pile of rocks. Sen is an extremely important and valuable resource, especially at the start of the game when you don't have many means of acquiring it. Purses are especially important, because if you die a true death you'll lose half of the Sen you currently possess (as well as half of any Skill EXP not spent on Skill Points), but you won't lose any of your purses. Try to only take the money from purses when you know it is safe to do so, and when you're going to spend it straight away.

![](images/ffab33f0a690ad729b2515933dc78490f59f3fd2fe34c9aa1dfb15bcd543fcb7.jpg)

Once you're ready, head to the main gate. As you pass through the gateway, you'll quickly find that the primary bridge is down, seemingly cutting off access to the outside world. Thankfully, one of the abilities granted by the Shinobi Prosthesis is the use of a Grappling Hook to reach otherwise inaccessible areas. Use the hook to swing up to the nearby branch and walk along its length to the cliff-side, then use a wall jump to grab the ledge. Pull yourself up, and after walking forward a short distance you'll be able to see your current goal, Ashina Castle, in all its glory. Grapple onto the branch directly ahead of you after admiring the view, and then rest at the Ashina Outskirts Idol.

![](images/a8218e95dd9f2a7c3a027fca3d8ea841c52c89934b683ed9cf60473a626bd7bf.jpg)

![](images/962f00043a79f41c9d1a073b264e865b1051a35c075c54c676842f8d76e67aa2.jpg)

![](images/1fc5758761ef6e0189a77262597d95be9814906cb5eca76831e0b3772499abfb.jpg)

# Ashina Outskirts

Now that you've discovered more than one Idol, you'll be able to freely travel between them at any time. It's worth equipping the Homeward Idol to your Quick Items now, because any time you get into trouble you can use it to travel back to the last Idol you visited, or to the Dilapidated Temple.

![](images/407e81786a1be2f6104de7e7ec5f98f7884e5e2a2c026c8cc50d7a1ee29f6c17.jpg)

There's no penalty for using this item and it has infinite uses. There's an item on the ledge just above this. idol, so grab that and then drop back down.

![](images/0ae8f73ba4aa7231f9e236f29ee94ac1714b0a26a996ed7d592c07d3cb2b3f4c.jpg)

![](images/27d151418bfce721a821cdedab813e66d68885672694c41dc1ad5d8a2f8fd3ff.jpg)

Look down over the cliff here and you'll see a platform below that you can drop onto and access a cave containing an Ako's Sugar, which will come in handy shortly. Go back out onto the ledge and you can use a grapple point to get back across to the building.

![](images/199c643486cd33efc0522dfda7487d979af4c4d71594d100cd61e7eaec86a989.jpg)

Head through the gap in the wall and you can grapple up to a branch. From there, jump across to the roof of a building. Follow that roof around to the right and jump onto the cliff on the other side to skip the remaining enemies and reach the next Idol.

![](images/fb1f982a0bffc1afa05adbb5daa7c7ae14c2716b9c7a28f3038c738a6c722dfe.jpg)

Resist the urge to use a Plunging Deathblow on one of the soldiers below you here because it will alert the other one. Instead, drop down and sneak behind the one near the gate to Backstab Deathblow him, before doing the same to the other soldier

![](images/263a6e0e6b21284189c14459ebbfc374bc008ea42947a1539b9bc4447afd9967.jpg)

![](images/64d3b8aa0020271e4d472a09d285ece7cd603c40ddaf3890a03615baa91dab21.jpg)

Go around the outside of the broken wall and shimmy along to reach this point. Wait there for a patrolling soldier to get close so that you can Wall Hug Deathblow him.

![](images/36666d687d29ce65d3dbbb3326a7a4c3ea9be7f2e2517d2917c465d8ef919f64.jpg)

Crouch in the long grass and move to Position B. From here you can Wall Jump up and grab the ledge for a Ledge Hang Deathblow on the soldier above. Shimmy to the right before climbing up, and then sneak around and Backstab Deathblow the remaining soldier.

![](images/59e68ad7d8f2b28f3efbc9d7549173ba7352e3321e3aa30d6ac9191f399932da.jpg)

![](images/cb54bc9a0c05c009d5796226c8a6bc4bc87990ce40d231649dd4e99c46058785.jpg)

Grapple up to the top of the gate and use a Plunging Deathblow on the Attack Hound below. Carefully make your way into the long grass here and wait for the remaining hounds to move to the middle of the area. Once they're in position, jump onto the nearby wall and Plunging Deathblow one of them before attacking the other to clear the path to the Idol.

![](images/488e39361f605bf22ef4a7287e151f1e5992d87405f6e305204975d0c8fe61f7.jpg)

# Outskirts Wall - Gate Path

![](images/87fb9d6dc2a60d83254827c2cf9fb1b85fed0d1440f7242786acc99e753faf12.jpg)

When you return to this Idol you should have the huriken. This tool can easily deal with the hounds nearby, at the cost of some Spirit Emblems, and makes resting at this Idol before facing the upcoming Samurai General a much less stressful affair.

![](images/342fc9b8c9728a725ed7035361c296a326ed07c0376c5c518afb908dbb0e5cfc.jpg)

Grapple into the second story of the building directly ahead of you and you'll find the Shuriken Wheel next to a dead Nightjar Ninja. Head back to the Dilapidated Temple and give it to the Sculptor for your first Prosthetic Arm Tool: The Loaded Shuriken. Be sure to equip it before you leave. Prosthetic Arm Tools are extremely versatile and powerful additions to your arsenal, but their usage is limited by the number of Spirit Emblems that you have, so try not to use them haphazardly.

![](images/67fe92728db926ca91e056dd543d9feabe5c5c318000cecc8a8324920dff4c9c.jpg)

![](images/7595cae31454141c7b52cd4d4bd00bb7324651b203e1915f3459a695083aae8b.jpg)

When you exit the temple building you'll automatically receive two Spirit Emblems, and you'll be able to find more out in the world or quite often from defeating enemies. You can also buy them from Sculptor's Idols, but given how little Sen you'll have at this time, doing so is not advised. Travel back to the Outskirts Wall - Gate Path Idol when you're ready to continue.

![](images/d9d90185e5e207474f245a899f2bfdc52ade9dec19a72bf1523515a57812611a.jpg)

Grapple up to the top of the building, and walk to the other side of the roof so that you can survey the fortified area below. Standing alone towards the back of the area is the toughest enemy you've come across so far...

![](images/829b0e19ecf31fce6f1a4523c78f59cc68ce90c675d184a257ab66823b0ff626.jpg)  
Ashina Outskirts

# Item Legend

13 Pellet x3  
14 Bundled Jizo Statue x1  
Fistful of Ash x2  
16 Gachiin's Sugar x3

![](images/38a430be59ee45e14d0eb4f8c85a6448f5e4db5989a8aa82147279344c1e2e56.jpg)

![](images/d8a05cff6c24511c36b84b2af474317e8b273504c05a4e55be7d83b4d9fa0845.jpg)

This General has a lot of Vitality and hits much harder than previous enemies. If you're not feeling confident in your ability to fight him, you can avoid him entirely if you wish. From Position A you can sprint jump across to the opposite side of the valley and snag a grapple point there to land safely. Doing so will also allow you to skip the battle after the General. From that same position you can also drop directly down to gain access to a hidden cave with a very rare Bundled Jizo Statue.

![](images/c10bd48f1ae70915a6b7802a82447877a2011e80db4752284309ee44a070722d.jpg)

![](images/0e24cc7473ef6e3f5249497a2bd36f9df7ecb5b1d964ea844cf5d385b562a323.jpg)

If you just want to skip the General and not the enemies afterwards, follow the ledges leading down to this point from the rooftop and continue from here. You can still skip those enemies by continuing to drop down the ledges to the left, and then grappling across to the other side of the valley if you choose.

![](images/81b48d9eae4a52eb00056842433f2a48d64c9c027422554bdcc4e51d44cd387f.jpg)

If you want to fight the General, this is a great place to start. Grapple up to the nearby rooftop and you'll be able get behind and above the General so that you can jump out and use a Plunging Deathblow to remove one of his Deathblow Markers. Because of the amount of Skill EXP you get from the General, and the items he drops, it's highly recommended that you attempt to defeat him before moving on, especially since he won't respawn when you rest at an Idol after killing him. To aid you during the fight, you may want to equip the Ako's and Ungo's Sugars that you've picked up, and any Fistfuls of Ash you have can be used to temporarily blind him, allowing you to use other items safely. For more information on how to fight him, flip to P.396.

![](images/da154c6f00bada3359c55d689c34e5adbd70627a9b466e9f9e9668ec66ffe50a.jpg)

Once you defeat him you'll be rewarded with your first Prayer Bead, starting you on your journey to increasing your Vitality and Posture, and a very useful Gourd Seed. Use the Homeward Idol to return to the Dilapidated Temple and give the Gourd Seed to Emma so that she can increase the capacity of your Healing Gourd to two sips. Travel back to the Outskirts Wall - Gate Path idol again after completing your upgrade and return to this point.

![](images/be0d825d8f571373f816ca971217d6769cfc4b036be5ebea7e4b5565c7b84ba6.jpg)

There are a large amount of enemies in this area, so be very careful while moving around. Standing in a ruined building in the middle of the area is an Ashina Soldier with a rifle, and his wide field of vision covers almost everywhere on the side of the area he's looking towards. Because of that, starting here where you're behind him is a much safer approach. Sneak around the corner so that you can Backstab Deathblow the soldier standing with his back to you, and then return to the corner of the wall and wait for the patrolling soldiers to walk past.

![](images/ce9f09a4da03b565be74be8ead9eb54ef8699f33d0d5aa77915d5fbaa92d3040.jpg)

![](images/38281a336e1101187e9b37f46f0a496c23fd6aa73b1e840ef14ad361dd1a36ac.jpg)

Grapple up to the top of the roof at Position B and wait there for the patrolling enemies to have their backs to you before dropping down inside the building and using a Backstab Deathblow on the soldier there. Move back away from the edge afterwards so that the soldier on the opposite platform doesn't spot you.

![](images/136169d642f4ec2f7e5f795570bd9bfe2f681f986c63a8e60303195e515a83bf.jpg)

![](images/ee1f08868d813e71945cd8b28ebfa0ce4d0434b508114a71fbeda8782446fc3b.jpg)

Drop out of the house and head to here, and then follow the cliff-edge until you can grapple to the branch at Position C. Eavesdrop on the two soldiers below and then Plunging Deathblow one of them and kill the other quickly, before the patrolling enemies come back around.

Standing near the edge of the cliff nearby is a powerful Taro Troop soldier, but if you drop down here you can sneak behind him and finish him off with a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/d5a8f2abe34629bbc9041f7144799cdad0a82c6d926dc377bd99158f40a42889.jpg)

![](images/b8a25477c7f734c8c6398e89ee818fc40d1d2c56c6a104426c8e9fe20420c0a8.jpg)

Of the four patrolling soldiers, one will usually separate from the others, so grapple back up to the building at Position B and wait there until you can pick him off without the others seeing.

![](images/73c2f7656dfa7ec9fc3bbeb4efa56803f0e579048adf9c0224b23be423582ea0.jpg)

Grapple back up to the building afterwards so that you can wait for the remainder of the group, and then use a Plunging Deathblow on the soldier with the straw cape since he has the most Vitality. Use basic attacks to finish off the final two. All that remains to kill now are the two Gamefowl near Position D and the area will be secure.

![](images/41f6c7c2b55859f8b1d45b231596c8aa0f26787664d6a528b03a56629b388bb4.jpg)

# Inosuke and Mother Nogami

On the middle floor of this building you'll find a mysterious old woman constantly ringing a bell. Talk to her and she'll mistake you for her son, Inosuke, and give you a Young Lord's Bell Charm that she wants you to offer up to Buddha. If you take the charm to the Buddha statue in the room the Sculptor sits in at the Dilapidated Temple you'll be able to dive into a memory from the past and visit a key moment in time at the Hirata Estate. Unbeknownst to the old lady, her son, Inosuke is actually nearby, sitting up against a rock and suffering from a grave wound. If you talk to him, his one dying wish is that you check in on his mother. For more information on Inosuke and his mother, please turn to P567., and check P.187

![](images/c998e4659b5ec688bf3156472556e1520b930144dce1f3dedebd96cd4e6b9c8b.jpg)

to find out what's going on at the Hirata Estate. There are many Prosthetic Tools to be acquired at the estate, so the trip is well worth it.

![](images/6a72b36613ac0d38a23adebf7a17bf9dcac695968368ad9021a6dc9e7beacd54.jpg)

Before going through the gate and starting the next encounter you can grapple up to Position E. From there, follow a series of grapple points up to the plateau at the top, where you'll find the first of many Memorial Mob Peddlers.

![](images/e40bd4f8e81a88f492555da230e4be70b47aec5f4363ad6aeebc9c740f544605.jpg)

# Crow's Bed Memorial Mob

You can purchase many useful items from these interesting characters, but from this particular one you should try and obtain Robert's Firecrackers. This item will allow you to have the Sculptor install another Prosthetic Tool into your arm, and this particular one is extremely useful in an upcoming boss fight. If you picked up all the purses along the route so far, you should have enough funds to buy it.

![](images/cf71a0385adac593df1ab15672d1ceec379835f55fc56e6885f7a709c846439b.jpg)

If you proceed through the gate you'll immediately come under fire from a very dangerous, cannon-wielding Sunken Valley Clan member standing on a platform at the top of the stairs ahead. Trying to fight the other enemies while avoiding his bombardment is very risky, so dealing with him quietly should be your priority. Hug the side of the gate and wait for the Ashina Soldier to patrol past you so that you can sneak up behind him for a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/75be69350602f5e26d14e946acbe8b94b5b96d7a565fd9de470695cb0a8e6c13.jpg)

![](images/e4edca8c14349114e6815be260f2f79b70f1c4c086b948490dc0cebe7f30b262.jpg)

Grapple up to Position E beside the gate, and then use the long grass and grapple points to sneak past the Valley Clan member until you reach Position F. From there, you can move around behind him for a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/d2b258741ac4dce623c4ab691b4f966e510711b3fc276ea5e4d2405c8b03dca6.jpg)

Plunging Deathblow the soldier standing in front of the gate below you, and then grapple up to Position G and do the same to one of the two soldiers standing on the path below. Finish off the final soldier with basic attacks.

![](images/32cf00b33ef11f2184602c12cf6045fd807ff75c1481aebdde5eb2d043ccb23e.jpg)

Grapple out onto the branch at Position H and you'll be able to follow along a series of ledges and grapple points that lead you to some useful items. Follow the route to the end and you'll have an alternate means of reaching the Outskirts Wall - Stairway Idol.

![](images/f5624efa514626454f1960765bbd4fb81b8defb81c7111a0006bcd4c96690f1c.jpg)

# Outskirts Wall - Stairway

After resting at this Idol, make sure to drop down and interact with the Remnant near the stables to get some insight into Kuro and Emma's relationship. You've more than likely acquired your first Skill Point at this time, so before continu

![](images/1ce9ce12997d60f0f7030c809bdfc641956f066ae1bf3f1c02a566692dcb2ab4.jpg)

ing, head back and talk to the Sculptor to acquire the Shinobi Style Esoteric Text if you don't have it already.

![](images/16bae068e92bb3914e3d490e101cad5fbee4def5e6f703228799d65a255d7a16.jpg)

![](images/b616c827b4b3567d324b8442f69cb91a0d1a72c24f2f1e0a5327976f2f65e729.jpg)

# Anayama the Peddler

Sitting under a roof opposite the stables is the entrepreneur Anayama the Peddler. This industrious fellow is looking to open up a shop, but before he can do that he's going to need the funds to acquire some stock. Luckily, he has some valuable information that he'll let go of for a price to start him on his way. Pay him 50 Sen and you'll be able to find out how the two of you met during that fateful night at the Hirata Estate, and then pay him another 100 Sen and you'll get a document giving you a hint as to the location of a Shinobi Tool in the estate grounds. If you've already been to the estate and have the tool, he'll give you some Oil as compensation. Similarly, if you attacked him to the point that he became aggressive (but did not kill him) while you were at the estate, he will have some additional dialogue. If you actually killed him during your visit to the estate, he will not be here at all. Rest at the nearby Idol after purchasing the 50 Sen information and Anayama will have set up his shop. It's possible to attack him here, and if you attack him enough, he'll become hostile and fight back. Once that happens he will stay aggressive and you'll lose access to his shop, with your only options being to either

![](images/3b521baba4da746ea6a2788e0eebe41a870665aad8ceacff496b19d9f6585934.jpg)

kill him or stay away from him. To find out what he has for sale, and how to increase his available lineup, flip to P.561.

![](images/23551d9a28dc91dc9476be5d52aff5a6acafdfd0fa0a0ff87f0025cd477adb73.jpg)

Grapple onto the roof here, and then to the next rooftop, and finally to the tree branch nearby. From here you can see a massive monstrosity struggling to escape at the top of the stairs, and if you eavesdrop on the two soldiers below, you'll get a hint as to one of its weaknesses. Plunging Deathblow one of them after the conversation, and then fight the other one normally.

![](images/3eee1ac309acb0786b6d80616388f4210eea8ead7600c342be32c50e6c275675.jpg)

As long as you don't start making your way up the stairs, the Ogre won't break free of its shackles, so you have time to prepare. There's a barrier blocking your progress, so the Ogre must be defeated before you can continue. The Ogre is very weak to Fire, so if you have the Flame Vent, be sure to equip it; the Shinobi Firecracker can also be handy. There's no way to sneak up on it, but if you sprint up the stairs fast enough you can inflict a lot of damage before it breaks free. Do not over-commit to your offense, however, because once the battle has started the Ogre has a very fast grab attack; stick to one or two hits before backing away in case it attempts the grab.

![](images/b8d551cc113075cafefb4fe126dd6e2e99bfd53da59d8e7ec19c574d9ad3af4b.jpg)

Try to keep the fight parallel with the staircase, because the Ogre has a lot of grab attacks that will cause him to throw you over his head if you get caught, which can easily lead to you being thrown off a cliff. Evade his grab attacks (or sometimes even during them), you'll see a grapple prompt appear on his shackles that you can use to cause him to flinch, creating an opening to land a few blows of your own. If you need to create some room to heal or use other items, retreat down the stairs and grapple back up to the branch, where you'll be totally safe. Go to P.399 for even more information on the Chained Ogre.

![](images/1b862d4a75afa78cd2661ab2fcd0b5839a6f1584811b5ab27d32e9a3005a5a53.jpg)

Once the Ogre has been dispatched, sneak up behind the soldier here, so that you can Backstab Deathblow him and grab the item.

![](images/718e4954e1356e9be628a1e2743408977787d32a231d03be21505ab7c20775bc.jpg)

![](images/2bf99d521a750859b5815816fc1c0fbe32396aa8eaf2aad833fa0bd59f910753.jpg)

Grapple up to the hole in the building now that it's clear. Directly in front of you is a Nightjar Monocular to pick up, and if you head left down the hallway you'll find another Gourd Seed. Return to Emma again to increase the capacity of your Healing Gourd before continuing, and then make your way back to the hole in the wall.

![](images/6ff74b421a95721282d7f38bb847e8e0bab75b94ca9b0a983db2d98ce9f6ca6a.jpg)

![](images/59e0e2d1739e555e912bc53e061a9824e421dd8380935e9e58efe833ee0fe4cc.jpg)

![](images/a14ce319fdf543532b4424fc5a3f07e156a51fd82c4fbe9fb6ebf594613ca9cd.jpg)

Look out through the hole in the wall and you'll be able to see a General guarding the far end of a courtyard, with a large number of soldiers surrounding him. While you could jump straight down and engage them all at the same time, through a bit of strategic movement and planning you can whittle down his reinforcements and tackle things in a more shinobi-like manner.

![](images/7b6a36226a153850253b3f5fd416baa1d3706f467d25d09ae429750ab846bf06.jpg)

![](images/15d4bc2b9688cdb974634a519e1abd064aaca58d558710a5dfb0e8c589477f83.jpg)

From here you can either continue around the outside of the courtyard and go directly to the Underbridge Valley Idol, start the fight from this advantageous position, or take the narrow path down towards Position A and explore. Along that path make sure to pick up the Divine Confetti hidden amongst the statues, because they're rare until much later in the game and they're required if you want to even attempt fighting an upcoming enemy. If you want to fight the enemies, skip ahead to Point 7.

![](images/ef321fe92490daf4a302478b7565cea32bde497fc22e3b2a035f923cc4c36881.jpg)

# Ashina Outskirts

![](images/135ec2a7e2b6795398c2b0124bbcf5cf57421eff9334b4d7a72c2406cfa5aada.jpg)

![](images/27cd0fb9bc6a96f1e4c49a7159951cdbfc49a55cd1ce7b0d0d8eebb65dcd8406.jpg)

Get close to the building here and you'll see a note pinned to the side that gives warning about a headless beast that cannot be harmed through conventional means. While that beast is indeed along this path, there are other things that are worth making the trip for even if you don't intend to fight it. Jump out from the walkway behind the building and grapple onto the branch at Position B, and then look down towards the cliffs and you'll see a ledge below you that you can jump across and grab. Shimmy along the ledge and pull yourself once you're able to, and then jump down to the open area in front of the cave entrance below.

![](images/b481efc211dfebbfaa41af2a71acf42de3894235fc0240db3af838124b79e8bd.jpg)

The Headless lies in wait at the bottom of a pit directly ahead of this position, but it's strongly recommended that you do not attempt to fight it at this point in the game. Headless can inflict the Terror status abnormality, which you have no means of curing at this point. You cannot damage it at all under normal conditions and must first imbue your weapon with spirit energy. At the moment the only means of doing that you have is the one Divine Confetti, and it's highly unlikely that you'll be able to inflict enough damage to kill the Headless before it wears off due to your low Attack Power. You can get another confetti in the Hirata Estate area, but a better option for now is to return later once you're stronger and have more means of dealing damage to the fiend. To find out just what those means are, turn to P.401.

![](images/2f00be878cf86318d730db32c69e5b730b1bce91fb5e66ce78bf1b5fcbad7439.jpg)

While you should avoid fighting the Headless, you may still want to risk a trip past it. If you run around the outskirts of the cave you can reach the narrow tunnel at the back without taking any damage from the Headless. At the end of that tunnel you'll find a Shinobi Shortcut that you can activate by hugging the wall. The passage beyond that wall will take you to the Bell Demon's Temple area of Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo. There you'll be able to ring a massive bell and acquire the Bell Demon item which strengthens enemies, but also increases their item drop rates. To find out more about the workings of the Bell Demon, turn to P.45

![](images/0b96f0e61d1853eeaf081f90c2b5104eec1da80a669051537a377769fb68f867.jpg)

![](images/1d65bf04a35fab0aac7469b27274f74b451bcd3a16495ea572b653dea6141dc1.jpg)

Follow this tunnel and you'll emerge on a small platform from which you can use a series of grapple points across to Position C. A Gecko will attack you as soon as you pull yourself up to this area; you can simply jump and use a Plunging Deathblow on it. Kill the other gecko in the ruined building, and after grabbing the item, grapple up to the hole in the wall above you. In this room there's a valuable Divine Grass item. Open the door and follow the hallway back to where you picked up the Monocular.

![](images/5ddedafa073523df8f8f5f3df78c97d06aafe203d02ad3a4c74d42a9029d898c.jpg)

Begin clearing the enemies by sneaking behind the Sentry near Position D for a Backstab Deathblow. An Ashina Soldier will patrol along the path leading away, moving down a set of stairs to the right; wait for him to move back up those stairs, and then drop down to the area near them. When he's almost back at the ledge the Sentry was on, head up the stairs and Backstab Deathblow the soldier at the top.

Go back down and follow the ledge along until you see the gap in the fence; when the patrolling soldier has moved past you, grab the ledge and pull yourself up. When that soldier patrols back near the stairs, you can Backstab Deathblow him without risk of detection, then go back and do the same to the stationary rifleman.

![](images/4954554ffd6378b1095072483e62adee9022a304c94bf1beb652dd627da560f7.jpg)

Go here and peak around the corner to check the status of the other patrolling soldier. If he has his back to you, go around the corner and Backstab Deathblow the rifle soldier, but if he's walking towards you, go back along the path to where the gap in the fence is and drop down again. Wait there for this patrolling soldier to start walking back along his route, and Backstab Deathblow him. Once he's out of the way you can go back and deal with the rifle soldier.

# Ashina Outskirts

# Item Legend

32 Scrap Iron x1  
38 Pellet x2  
39 Snap Seed x5

![](images/13e4523ed47883f2e0096beed0fac8d73498106dd0cac032672e49690ed342f7.jpg)

![](images/4689480805447f34290e19757ad9e1d59459e0007f8dd1e7576e5e27571dbf21.jpg)

Peek through the broken wall here and you'll be able to see the General in the courtyard below, along with another soldier just behind him. You can drop down and Backstab Deathblow the soldier, but doing so will often get you detected by the General. A better option is to jump out and use a Plunging Deathblow on the General to remove a Deathblow Marker and give you a big head start in the fight, and then kill the soldier while the General is recovering.

This General is fairly similar to the previous one that you faced, but instead of using mainly Sweep attacks, this one likes to employ Thrusts. If you have acquired the Mikiri Counter Skill, this can be an excellent opportunity to become familiar with it and take advantage of its strengths. Turn to P.396 for more advice on battling Samurai Generals.

![](images/708027dd80a8c500c95d3a3b497303a6108dd530a3cde7aa1d53fc7625c1a301.jpg)

![](images/edcb30e4d8a52ac5da70b0f59c5fcd25378e51a28742afd9225bba75e0693465.jpg)

Once he's taken care of, head across the courtyard until you see a collapsed bridge. Drop off the edge to the left of it, onto the landing below. Here you'll find two Pellets, but approaching them will cause a Gecko to drop down from above you. Kill it quickly or you risk being poisoned by its venomous spit. Now turn around and drop down to the next landing, where you'll find the Underbridge Valley Idol.

![](images/fc5f81e8bfd78b5ab6839e5ac8e1edec1c192e4dea216542391df265994ad926.jpg)

# Underbridge Valley

This Idol marks the start of a dangerous gauntlet as you traverse the cliffs ahead. Up until this point, you've generally been the predator, but until you escape the canyon, you'll be the prey. The Great Serpent cannot be killed, and being spotted will spell almost certain death, although you can actually deflect its attacks with some very precise timing. Due to its massive size, it will be unable to pursue you into tight quarters such as caves. If, however, you're caught out in the open with nowhere to run, it will likely make short work of you. Once you've made it through this area, the Great Serpent won't appear on subsequent trips to this Idol.

![](images/54755863e6aaa17a05869931fa565d19f00f147e515b00dd4e10f7d3520524ce.jpg)

![](images/c691d8bf34d65128e69ea7af204fa2359555b9da8817977bd4e748d861de9ef2.jpg)

To proceed, you can drop down the ledges, and then jump and grapple onto the branch at Position A. Once across, walk along the branch and hug the nearby wall. As soon as you do, you'll see the creature that makes this area so dangerous rise from the canyon below: The Great Serpent.

![](images/334360ebbd0f129ffff8bef76d8bf49f306e4abc7d22a08ff6b3bf78ba7acf49.jpg)

![](images/7692c48d52bcd45dffedf65eda8cf28480b7e3157c8ed55124fc52b4ef06c750.jpg)

If you're feeling brave, you can head straight to Position B from here. When facing the branch on the other side, jump to the left instead and you can grapple to the branch below you on the same side. This option is faster, but also riskier; crouch as soon as you land and continue from Point 6.

![](images/15fbde619bfb666e94867677ef4cd0340a6efa18aed83040ce05a6a2191e124a.jpg)

![](images/e1eb4ede13dce6b41a43b35bee37ada81d2194ce78e3e1a11638bd5b64b159bf.jpg)

While still hugging the wall, peer around the corner to get a better view of it. Don't worry, it won't be able to spot you from here. Looking down, you'll see a small ledge with some long grass at Position B; wait for the serpent to look away, and then grapple across and drop into the safety of the grass. You can also bypass the ledge at Position B by simply falling off here to the right and landing by the cave entrance below.

![](images/65ff3445747fe8283e3bade6fb1f447aa746fac90a6e792cd04bdfc66f6d8bff.jpg)

Your next goal is to enter the cave here, which you can see across the chasm, so once again wait for the serpent to look away, and then quickly jump out and grapple across. Run forward into the cave as soon as you land so that you're out of the serpent's reach.

![](images/136e31846685d955f74b74b1d22afbb54b2a9ac21b58d5bc35ded26f914badce.jpg)

Hug the wall here and you'll be able to peak around the corner to watch the serpent's movements while moving left, out of its view. It will begin to move into the cave, and then double back to the other side of the canyon; when you see it start that movement, follow behind it and jump across the gap to the safety of the long grass.

![](images/050d1827e3d8e45a3565146f558bcdfc2892899c2e6f225ff18bf9b9ffbe8822.jpg)

![](images/058cac2f7987621f7bc8823f8318f191616be97f96920d592bef5dd2cfd97671.jpg)

Look up to watch the serpent, and when you see it look away from you, move to the cliff in front of you and shimmy along the ledge. Dash straight into the palanquin at Position C once you reach the other side. The serpent will become curious about the palanquin and move towards it to get a closer look. Eventually it will get a bit too close and a Deathblow Marker will appear on its eye, allowing you to initiate a Deathblow on it.

![](images/4da751683fc6a7ecf389f30c7edac753b9932047304e76898e71927f861aa3f0.jpg)

![](images/f1c90effd1db902a492cd4c903f0c32c6d10e99da2717e27aa841214b4fd08ce.jpg)

It will let out a dire screech and begin to violently and indiscriminately thrash around. You can still be damaged by those thrashes, so make sure to keep your distance. Immediately turn around and sprint towards the grapple point at Position D, and then follow the series of grapples to reach a tunnel in the side of the cliff.

![](images/e540cc4c0661ae1586622032fca6414ec4d47592306be121b37faa36ba86ac5c.jpg)

Once you reach the very end of the tunnel the serpent will retreat from the area to recover from its wounds. This leaves you safe to go back and pick up the Snap Seeds on the small tree near the palanquin. After picking them up, continue towards the Ashina Castle Gate Fortress Idol.

![](images/95ccdec461ee7fd3802bbb41913670eb9cb18d013a640c699e912606b9e556e8.jpg)

Wall jump up from here and grab the ledge above. Wait there and a patrolling soldier will come to a stop directly above you, allowing for a Ledge Hang Deathblow.

![](images/3050003e6152f685082b37b9637e8654376a2c9632de31ea2af8cc6fed5f7cfb.jpg)

# Ashina Castle Gate Fortress

Before leaving the area near this Idol, be sure to kill the Assassin standing at the edge of the cliff nearby. Even though he has his back to you, he'll turn around as you get

![](images/f0efd31256bfd1841bf7763a4fc11020c648f1a46eed70a3fac5ba10f97a8bba.jpg)

close, so you'll need to fight him head on; defeat him and he'll drop the Herb Catalogue Scrap note, which contains some interesting lore.

![](images/5b2ca75238468e27d644a55f37f628c2418d795466e74d744786b4cb5dc2214c.jpg)

If you just want to get straight to the boss in the area ahead and skip past all of the enemies in between, start by grappling up to the top of the watchtower at Position A, and from there grapple across to the top of an adjacent wall. Once you're on the wall, simply run along it until you're past the patrolling enemy down to the right. Now drop down and grapple up to the tree at the end of the path. From there, grapple up to the roof of the nearby building and drop down into the battlefield.

![](images/1267166eab9461ebcec9a4316af990933e5c3bffdb5c82c1295f5bfb1e333b18.jpg)

![](images/b16928df42751b5b59d18e4999ebc8b8fbb028135e1597596f4a1c8a0cb443aa.jpg)

A patrolling Taro Troop enemy will soon come by, but you can't kill him with a Ledge Hang Deathblow, and if you attempt a Backstab Deathblow, then the soldier in the broken building ahead will often spot you. To avoid that, as soon as you kill the first soldier, pull yourself up and jump through the hole in the building here, then Backstab Deathblow the soldier there. Move back afterwards, so that you avoid detection by the two soldiers in the middle of the courtyard.

![](images/8b5dd89ad878d43de13c8718fdb7de4cbe1bcca06784200d20eb15d648301d53.jpg)

Stay in the house while the Taro Troop enemy makes his way slowly along the path, and then when he's past the hole, drop out and use a Backstab Deathblow to kill him.

![](images/31b9704bb1499b733cb98ba725540d08e7174b63f170df8c83bdcbcf4316408d.jpg)

![](images/7ca2a429ec71b399976590decce216c79430bd030c7ce59ba6885470c1173c68.jpg)

Stick close to the outside wall and make your way along the path until you can Backstab Deathblow the soldier at Position B, and then grapple up to the top of the watchtower at Position A.

![](images/f0a61621ddcdea955c71eb0e851741e78a20e370c117caaa43982d3fa1859723.jpg)

![](images/1098d9bdb8982f0e34f26487fa530fd9ac19869d27f1faf76a32f9d53ab600cb.jpg)

After eavesdropping on the conversation between the two soldiers below, jump across to the broken bit of wall nearby, and from there use a Plunging Deathblow on one of them, before using normal attacks to finish off the other one.

![](images/d0432d1c9c44dd390f75391776e49d68ce1cfcb5cac514e2ee49c2aebb849311.jpg)

![](images/63c06009d275b16eedad9ff9173dd1eb30bbecbf5392e4ddcba97ef4f1ed5321.jpg)

Grapple up to the top of the wall here, and then if you walk forward along it you'll be able to eavesdrop on the soldier below to get a hint as to a potential weakness of the upcoming boss. Use a Plunging Deathblow to kill him when he's finished talking.

![](images/cd19030be3540e2a965b46530b3dc78c86b308a368ab9d85c29e834c3789d5ad.jpg)

![](images/745e6bca007be2b0efd14cd6b49ba15fefae016d53e220fd56942cf323c112a4.jpg)

With the advantage of the higher ground here you'll be able to use a Plunging Deathblow to dispatch the patrolling soldier below with ease.

![](images/5e1d2d851d2866e7128a44f9d923083a8ba61039127e5945297935f5d00b93de.jpg)

![](images/02d3e8dc5dd77fb55090076f7c3e923ba2fd8c9d9afd08148218d622814a5b75.jpg)

With all of the enemies defeated, interact with the Remnant to learn more about Kuro's history with Genichiro, and then gather up any remaining items you may need for the battle ahead. When you're ready to face him, grapple up to the tree at the end of the path, and then again to the nearby rooftop. Drop down into the battlefield below to initiate the battle with Gyoubu Oniwa.

![](images/d9dcd686487b79e7c3ff7615a7d5bfb3c36ec36e9a17a6c07ac8a18891e6409a.jpg)

![](images/639b197f0514e30faf0f18e8e004cf98e474b4ca169936cb27c2b5cc7c97d187.jpg)

![](images/931aadb346f58a363f386dd487f64027cff7ab3854e29d5c34231742c95106ba.jpg)

![](images/a21ac1b4508f184da1298f9a0a333fc5101c38b7032e5c1f74272500a0096b43.jpg)

Gyoubu has been tasked with guarding the gate leading to Ashina Castle, and it is a responsibility he takes extremely seriously. If you purchased Robert's Firecrackers and had the Sculptor install them for you, make sure to have the tool equipped, because the Firecrackers will startle the horse that Gyoubu is riding, allowing you to land some attacks until it recovers. You should also look for grapple opportunities during the fight when Gyoubu rides away and starts to wind up for some of his bigger attacks. Grapple onto him at those times and you'll stop the attack and give yourself a small window in which to attack. To learn about his attacks in detail, head to P.434.

![](images/9526df20ad635b5f677c2e5700b7bac2007a020953f921344b3071d45004b219.jpg)

![](images/cf801911447154551bf99d10db993ab41c5b1e25a0b372b5b4973882cf728def.jpg)

Once Gyubu has been defeated, the barriers will lift and the Ashina Castle Gate Idol will appear in front of the gate. Before continuing to the castle (or Hirata Estate if you haven't been there yet), there is a bit of exploring to do here.

![](images/9bb64812c66946719d90cdf6cdb397cd44cc0891ee258051f85b55d4ef7741f6.jpg)

![](images/6c7c6091b75f96fa8f9c98feeea458199721ecff0bffe5d25c8812a41ba46784.jpg)

# Sculptor Update

Gyoubu will drop the Mechanical Barrel item when he dies, and if you take that back to the Sculptor you'll open up the ability to upgrade your Prosthetic Tools at the cost of various materials and Sen. To see a full breakdown of what upgrades you can obtain, and what is required for them, check P82.

![](images/e878b315bd06b34f8e6d09d8fc96ae97757fbc599c0516c00e287c3c346b467a.jpg)

The barrier on this opposite side of the battlefield to the Idol will also clear upon Gyoubu's defeat, allowing you to reach this area, where you'll find another helpful Memorial Mob peddler. This particular one has a very valuable Gourd Seed for sale, along with a Dragon's Blood Droplet to cure anyone that may have contracted Dragonrot.

![](images/c91de984e3f3ae7f2344dffc2f669bf9290c8f2975b85558cd83b38fa4366919.jpg)

![](images/296890e04c8d1f94309f64709fd6d6b4b219b43394a310c140b90be0c84f8996.jpg)

# Tengu of Ashina

Go inside the building and you'll find the mysterious Tenuu standing over the corpse of a Lone Shadow. Talk to the Tenuu and after a brief exchange he'll propose that you help him clear Ashina's streets of a group of "rats". Accept and he'll give you a Rat Description note with some hints about who your targets are, and where they're located. If you want to find out, turn to P.568. It's highly recommended that you complete his task, because if you return to him afterwards he'll reward you with the Ashina Style Esoteric Text Skill Tree.

![](images/cbbc216fa6b0e69d7b5f4095288ff669b7775223f94994960bf25238549e3b3b.jpg)

![](images/4c7c1cdbae1d276ff471f8f185dc34bcedc883aa55cf11de0bc8189d209f61b5.jpg)

The door here can be unlocked from this side, giving you an alternate way into the building, and the mysterious Shura Storyteller standing in the nearby hallway can be spoken to, though her words are cryptic.

![](images/e3efc0226a74b440b82ca14dac2f60acddccfad6b19882082d0dae6e87c9dcec.jpg)

![](images/4c1fa51db89db7e324a5383b0b1cd6b19ba68b0a9cbcd914dbedbd548a966a35.jpg)

The stairs next to the Tengu lead to a walkway, and if you follow that you'll find a grapple point at Position C that you can use to land on a beam. From there you can grapple across to Position D. Follow the beams around the room until you reach a broken beam at Position E, and then climb up that to reach the attic. At the back of this room you'll find a chest containing a Prayer Bead. Now that you have everything, continue onward to Ashina Castle.

![](images/fda4b03fca53d7df4ab62bce1645ae5ac092d6e6af4f682ac1c127dbaa411345.jpg)

Lord Kuro's ancestral estate lies on the bank of the Dragonspring. Three years ago, the Wolf infiltrated the estate in the dead of night, and his fate became entwined with the Divine Heir's.

![](images/51f7e86b100278201010f582718741a9c3e4849970c433b004d2666bd3d3d8d1.jpg)

Hirata Estate - Main Hall

![](images/0d713c758b6615e097cd194367290ddbda20cb907c3c57efe96b064e51de1e3c.jpg)

# Dragonspring - Hirata Estate

After offering the Young Master's Bell Charm to the Buddha statue in the Dilapidated Temple, you'll be taken into the memory of a night three years in the past. You'll be experiencing things that the Buddha wants you to see, so there's no way to know the accuracy of these events. There are

![](images/b21cabb79cc3489d45d56d1e713930579ae08141c321dd084fb635fee6216265.jpg)

a large number of Prosthetic Tool components to be acquired here, so it's recommended that you come here as soon as possible.

# Ending Update: Purification

If you want to attain the Purification ending, you will need to complete the Hirata Estate in order to be able to revisit it upon acquiring the Father's Bell Charm. For more information, turn to P.551.

![](images/616e55fc2c731a371559ac66d566e44a146aeea75ff9f34011da4298a7d3e8bb.jpg)

The jump from the top of this cliff may seem treacherous, but you can grapple to some branches as you fall to make it to the bottom safely. There you'll be able to speak with a wounded Nightjar Ninja to gain more information about your current whereabouts.

![](images/001af92b65bab2bb12ea86e7be8a3a20d6d7a741ba9d01c80beb242305c56c03.jpg)

![](images/c4170bbe4e26c3dca759138da1eea0962c0d449d1431f7e05e85f5ded6f62f84.jpg)

Wait for the two patrolling Bandits on the bridge to start walking away, and then grapple down to the bridge from here; Backstab Deathblow the first one you come to before cutting down the other.

![](images/391cfd86016cdb312239bc032454269c8495edcabfa170e7e456f97fc5e1d77c.jpg)

This bridge leads directly up to the main gate of the estate grounds, and there's a large enemy group standing in front of it. You can run and engage them head-on, or use the lake to circle around to the side for a stealthier option.

![](images/725031a73de556b75e99da6ba566c69624eec0baece3bcfec61a25f8370848f4.jpg)

The waters of this lake are teeming with rare Treasure Carp that you can kill to obtain their scales. Only two can be killed here while you're on the surface of the lake; the remaining two are underwater and requires the use of the Mibu Breathing Technique.

![](images/0ad446c7e7a7e475645fc5e687fd3b5d2ddc6723707e51950467638fb3dfcfb9.jpg)

![](images/79a1464021e5f23067c17bf86c5bb8ee057e804acf5cddc5febda71563ad8040.jpg)

# Pot Noble Harunaga

On this small island you'll find one of two Pot Nobles. These strange creatures like to hide themselves in pots while they try to acquire the one type of item they desire above all else: Treasure Carp Scales. Speak with them and you'll see a list of goods that you can exchange for various amounts of scales. In this area you can get a total of four Treasure Carp Scales without the need for the Mibu Breathing Technique, an additional three if you have it. As you acquire more, make sure to return often to buy up the things.

Of note from this one is the Withered Red Gourd, which at only two scales you can easily afford and will come in handy to combat the large amount of fire damage sources in this area.

![](images/0451df479ad787f6a30c6e9daf4e31117cb693d8df07528238caed49e211bffe.jpg)

The Mask Fragment and Floating Passage Text are both also very useful, but you'll need to save up for those.

![](images/89e29e6e646b6230b8e2559c824230650aea627a9819add6981b41b1fb63220d.jpg)

Take a wide approach up the bank of the lake here and you can reach the stairs behind the enemies without them spotting you. Use a Shuriken to deal with the Hound and a Backstab Deathblow on the Bandit, the order of which will depend on their positions when you get there.

![](images/c45551372f0d8cdeb4d6548704198a29aa931931d1a0bc4106fe67c48f1b10ca.jpg)

![](images/4fd3b13b47a25ac2ecb91c2b5966a4d20adebc95652beb9b82b7a146abc361ff.jpg)

Jump onto the wall here and follow it along to the rooftop above the main gate. From there you can Shuriken all the Hounds below you, and then Plunging Deathblow the Bandit. The lone Bandit remaining guarding the bridge will have his back to you from this position, allowing for an easy Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/7207336b9c709a9e03b79529cbf5db288e30df1ee5b6bf91e5d7bd1048096c2a.jpg)

![](images/30ffaaf9721cf7a6ccf276fe862d483c4e4966f99d4667f6827c299845a6bb2c.jpg)

# Estate Path

This Idol provides you with an excellent point from which to explore the grounds surrounding the main estate. Its location is such that you have quick access to most of the housing areas, especially once you've opened the interior gate from the other side.

![](images/97e9e5c24f68ace6bc3046b8311d003b66cae90b72b6d9002022e1dd48d9418d.jpg)

Hug the wall here and use a Ceramic Shard to lure the patrolling Bandit down towards you; when he turns around to go back, quickly Backstab Deathblow him and then get back around the corner so you're not detected.

# Hirata Estate
