# Upper Tower - Kuro's Room

Ashina is now under a renewed siege effort by the Central Forces of the Interior Ministry, and this time their attack has spread beyond the bounds of the castle. Not only are all of the castle Idols unavailable for travel again, but so too are all of the Outskirts ones, other than the Dilapidated Temple. The raging fires that have been spread by the invaders have also caused some traversal routes to become unavailable, so you won't be able to proceed deeper into Ashina Outskirts from the Dilapidated Temple, and similarly, if you enter the castle through the Abandoned Dungeon, the door leading out to the castle is blocked off. Lord Kuro has fled through the

![](images/45b02cea7aea40a5492ddfa8d79a5dfef0230a502adc5ad9f3686931edea5161.jpg)

secret passage in Ashina Reservoir, and while reaching him is your ultimate goal, there are still many opportunities for exploration along the way.

![](images/1b97c1ff06acf9fffbc3de1766d953ddfaac9cbc05bd4294e546cc818e16e5be.jpg)

# Update: Emma the Physician

Emma can be found sitting next to Isshin in Kuro's Room. If you speak with her she'll give you the Secret Entrance Key, which is required to open the door in Ashina Reservoir and reach Lord Kuro. Depending on your previous actions with her and Isshin you may also have the option to ask her about Isshin's last words, or Dragonrot. Isshin's last words are regarding the Mushin Esoteric Text, so if you already have that, the option will not be there. Similarly, if you have previously discussed Dragonrot with Emma you will not have that option, but if you didn't then you can speak with her about it now to obtain the Recovery Charm, which allows you to use Dragon's Blood Droplets at Sculptor Idols to cure Dragonrot in anyone that may have it.

![](images/5b812f4bb63863125b3e92fbc229065b7e42d6156d083e108ca4fc5975f3f756.jpg)

# Update: The Sculptor

If you return to the Dilapidated Temple you'll find that the Sculptor has gone, and speaking to Fujioka outside only reveals that he stumbled off somewhere while muttering about "the flames. Thankfully, you'll still be able to make use of his toolkit inside the building to upgrade your Prosthetic Tools. As for what has become of him, you'll need to reach Ashina Outskirts to find that out.

![](images/fc15a3d695ad2c3562f241c45213b0e84bbd9eed0bc0d95d294659a83a696901.jpg)

The only exit available to you is the window in the library, so jump through it to reach the castle rooftop. From the rooftop you have a number of paths you can take. Look straight ahead down the main stairs and you'll notice the purple smoke that Emma spoke of, emanating from rooftops to the right of the stairs. That smoke leads you towards the entrance to Ashina Reservoir, which is where you'll need to go to reach Lord Kuro

The base of operations for the Central Forces has been set up in part of Ashina Outskirts, and if you want to go there, you can make use of the newly-repaired bridge near the Old Grave part of the castle. To head straight there, go left along the castle roof and jump

over to the tall watchtower; from there you can reach one of the lower rooftops and make use of a new unmountable kite grapple point to propel yourself over towards the Old Grave.

Our recommendation, however, is to make sure you're fully prepared for the upcoming battles by first clearing the castle and the surrounding streets of enemies, and grabbing all of the items. When you have everything here, only then head to Ashina Outskirts to investigate the disturbance there, before going to Ashina Reservoir. To begin that process, follow the rooftop around to the right and enter the window that leads to the Ashina Dojo.

![](images/4cb0cc51e4e1cda0c9c578b4297353a4cdfd0707e2ca725da079acd5d61e4866.jpg)

![](images/5ab2bb8cf493f2979f463a835182bf5dd5e710394629e14c4d139dfdb46ac93c.jpg)

The same Lone Shadow from the previous raid is hiding on the opposite side of the wall here, so don't go running straight ahead unless you want to fight him in open combat. For a more sneaky option, move to this point while crouched, and then use the Finger Whistle. Quickly move around so that you're as close to the nearby wall as possible and the Lone Shadow won't spot you when he comes to investigate the sound; wait for him to turn around and head back, and then close in and use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/ca80a8e7622b1c984b122a1f5c0e0d7001a1d76401441cfa7f85df2f37f047ee.jpg)

![](images/4c2b9c8eb6d9bb8c93f86fd94070785d5d5372602e2293cfcbaa9ce78e6c9fb0.jpg)

# Upper Tower - Ashina Dojo

![](images/576430e794347fedf4cfc0b57090fd4fcb25f5c87e660157298965343eb1fdd8.jpg)

There are a couple of big battles taking place on the lower floors of the castle, along with a particularly tough encounter; make sure to commune with the Idol here before heading down the stairs.

![](images/8043995dcd0ed450558ff47a2da2a21f7a987dd3cf6c3f307a69857cbdbfc10e.jpg)

There are no enemies to contend with in the hallway here, so continue along it towards Isshin's watchtower.

![](images/4f7aad5c409a4fbfaf282f28991047c235ee905f2b36707c83bcb6437096f029.jpg)

Before going into the room to face this enemy, make sure to eavesdrop on him to hear about his unyielding devotion to Isshin, even in the face of the overwhelming invading forces. This elite is similar to previous ones you may have encountered, but thanks to the powers granted to him by his red eyes, he is significantly more powerful. His keen senses also mean that he'll detect you as soon as you cross the threshold into the room, so there's no sneaking up on him.

His red eyes may grant him additional strength, but they also bring with them the fear of fire; take advantage of that by sprinting up to him at the start of the fight and using the Flame Vent on him before he can get up. His Posture recovery is also very bad, so working on his Posture with Combat Arts like Ichimonji is a good follow-up after the vent. It's also important to remember that you cannot fully guard his cross slash normally, but you can with the Loaded Umbrella, so having it equipped is a good idea just in case you get put on the defensive. Try to pace your Flame Vent uses so that you still have enough emblems to use it a few times after removing his first Deathblow Marker, and keep up the pressure until he falls.

![](images/819a59610bdcf790479ef21deace07c683b0eb8d11856d81650bd8ba7c5fe6e4.jpg)

Before continuing past this point you may want to go back up to the dojo area and rest at the Idol to resupply, especially if you used a lot of Spirit Emblems during the previous encounter. When you're ready, crouch down and sneak into the room so that you can use a Backstab Deathblow on the Lone Shadow standing with his back to you. Grapple up to the hole in the ceiling once he's down.

![](images/e0016bf2de3773d98ea9ed0d23bd6d91de2f9082e773dbf04861bb2812b77903.jpg)

Make your way around to this point so that you can see into the room below, where you'll find a number of Lone Shadows and Fencers. The Lone Shadows will make short work of the Fencers due to how run-down the Ashina forces are, so try to even the odds a bit by starting the fight with a Plunging Deathblow on the whitehooded Lone Shadow. You'll then need to prioritize targets based on how the fight is progressing. If you're left alone with one of the Fencers take him out while the other enemies are distracted before you start attacking the other Lone Shadow. Try to keep the fight inside the room, because if it spills outside there's a good chance that the Lone Shadow near the Upper tower - Antechamber Idol will hear it and join in.

![](images/26e723f8c5e4a8c3894413b83d3e96579c4199d50c6b419b26145dc42e0d1f66.jpg)

![](images/3b0a8b2d2a95b92cfb38a1eeef574bbc0afd38b1c87862d3ec95901257187989.jpg)

If he wasn't dragged into the previous fight, you'll need to defeat the Lone shadow in the room ahead before you can resupply at the Idol. The easiest way to do that is to hug the edge of the doorway, peek around it, and then without locking on, use the Finger Whistle to lure him in for a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/4e2503f76e8d5898dfbc5468672dd9686b900de4b37f337f9f144dac81e447a6.jpg)

Make your way back here after resting at the Idol, and then jump over the railing and grapple onto the beam below. Look down from there and you'll see Red Guard standing either side of the door leading out to the front of the castle; use a Plunging Deathblow to kill one of them, and then either cut down the other with basic attacks, or use Divine Abduction to make short work of him. From here you can head out the back door and towards Ashina Outskirts without facing any other enemies if you wish, but there are many more enemies to kill and items to get out the front, which is where we recommend you go.

![](images/d7fe39796beec6938392e72fa703dd02f68975f8655284c4a18abb30c23d5a28.jpg)

An all-out war will break out between Ashina and Interior Ministry forces on the large stairs as soon as you step out onto them, and the Ashina side will not last long against the strength of the Red Guard. Use the chaos of the battle to your advantage by grappling up to this rooftop, and then run along the subsequent rooftops until you're behind the group of Red Guards. Drop behind them and sneak up so that you can use a Backstab Deathblow on one of them, and then follow that up with the Bestowal Ninjutsu. As soon as you recover, start cutting down the other enemies, focusing on the Kodachi-wielding ones first.

![](images/8c03b33093fc2721d32e3ae2ed4c535188086c4c963e92fd82887b68504a32a3.jpg)

![](images/a33581c6f1a9f26a911e8b2e3d0fd78263c506bd33f28f62871d4b150b31248e.jpg)

The rooftops on this side of the street are defended by a Lone Shadow, but if you grapple up here and run along the lower tier of roof, you can get around behind him undetected and use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/1053c45950870ee05490b9f85dea1e9701e3031c809d12b74ab7358408c7626f.jpg)

![](images/12c7290927d7aebedde8c9ea69fb53c19120dbe943685ed9c14f56ad5de15929.jpg)

# Ashina Castle

Make sure to commune with this Idol again if you intend to explore the remainder of the castle grounds before going to the reservoir, so that you can travel back here later and won't have far to go. Red Guard during this time of day also have the chance of dropping Fulminated Mercury, and since there are so many nearby, this Idol is the perfect place

![](images/522d81ef3468a8e65de9d0f30299cb81c57dfc85f0304827e57fa796bb3753fe.jpg)

to try and acquire some. You may also want to consider using the Golden Vortex Tool on them if you have it, to double your item yield.

![](images/4e203d14d1636d8cefc15262038b29b076eff642f73421981a2135eca1711c09.jpg)

A Red Guard can be found battling against a Samurai General in this courtyard; if you're quick you can take advantage of the situation and close in for a Backstab Deathblow on the Red Guard and then engage the Samurai General.

![](images/27c3959af8d7909af5fe21372b32636125c244c8f205bb2ff776aa4f430b10f6.jpg)

![](images/b9cff2e514f4410949f6292308ff280e7c169d63cb9cb351f38ddcd63e05650a.jpg)

Grapple up to the wall here and wait for the Taro Troop patrolling the street ahead to start walking away, then drop down and sneak up on him and use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/b9cef2888462de903500ae1ffb64b839ee3a9f6424ab6e6e1d6f24194268cd96.jpg)

There's no good way to get positional advantage on the other Taro Troop here, so you'll have to fight him directly. Divine Abduction is a good choice of tool to use and will allow for a swift victory.

![](images/498cf4ad327fe46dd426aaae658e5c41b71f668597f8171e1a01cd220f7cb38e.jpg)

![](images/3661cd68fc52c7572ec73a4e9a4a4c379f8f0d0abb158cd359baa33dfce32aed.jpg)

![](images/a25702f1961c50ad53616fd375a3c2ba3ed0079be055e774055c6542965af2d9.jpg)

When both Taro Troop have been killed, grapple to the middle tier of this roof and run along it to this point. From here you'll see a brave Samurai General run out to face a flamethrower-wielding Red Guard; the more powerful Red Guard will always win, so wait until the Samurai General is about to lose, and then drop down and use a Backstab Deathblow on the Red Guard just as the Samurai General dies.

![](images/963fc49401013171a2009cde7d155811c9587a7412b1e31879159ffe9a85e364.jpg)

![](images/89ff43c6fa6a2549143460a0cdabf4e415d415db53235d653049d71b039183c7.jpg)

# 5

While you were dealing with the enemies on the streets, another battle was waging between two groups of Nightjars up on the rooftops; grapple up to this rooftop and crouch down near the peak so that you can observe the situation. If the fight is ongoing, use Shuriken to weaken and pick off the Nightjars while they're distracted. The victors in the fights are usually the red-eyed Nightjar Ninja, so if only they remain, close in and use your Flame Vent on them to take advantage of their fire weakness.

![](images/c131c17f3bc0d66548bb54d305186cada7fe6b3f4415b52f0652511137863100.jpg)

# 6

With the front of the castle now clear, it's time to turn your attention to the rear. Go to this rooftop and use the unmountable kite grapple point to propel yourself over towards the Old Grave.

![](images/9530dbaca221254b21c63132fd271f777cd6ed330389b44ff39ff97af7eda521.jpg)

![](images/de1dcaac78fc58a93de491e7300d903cc1c745d7d623cf55837d71c2fb5b9fd3.jpg)

There are no threats in the immediate area when you land, because all of the enemies on this side of the bridge are far too fatigued from battle to even stand unless provoked first. The new bridge leading back into Ashina Outskirts can be seen below you, but so can the large numbers of enemies fighting for control over it. You'll need to cross the bridge eventually if you're going into the Outskirts, but you should commune with the Old Grave first to resupply.

![](images/7942b55f9e6aed1b47624aa6c19810fbb8d7a5ed224bd5dcc6b371ac18543718.jpg)

![](images/bbc20781421c44a098226a00cb2ae3ff440109fc233628e5b186ebe0389e454a.jpg)

# Old Grave

This Idol will serve as your launching point from which any attempts to cross the bridge into Ashina Outskirts can be made. Communing with it now before exploring down

to the Great Serpent Shrine is also advised, because then you can travel right back here afterwards.

![](images/23d985e93a5ff458947656139d8c74275759dde79fec2d6f983f7aac835c3528.jpg)

![](images/94e9d75bf7bdb9630e2b33a280f91cadaf8fad395223a3613b19fcdc524e3755.jpg)

Eavesdrop on the Shinobi Hunter here to find out that, even in the midst of a second battle, he is still more concerned with money and saving himself than helping out. While he's pondering how to escape, sneak up behind him and use a Backstab Deathblow. If you want to fight the Red Guard near the rear door of the castle, you can easily do so from here by jumping into the water and swimming around behind him, so that you can land a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/215b6aca7976e6169e60e631d4d098bb11e0b82e5dc73701d719d682d97eeaeb.jpg)

![](images/e465dbe087e8116a170c2cbc33dbe8f734a47980735386a0b0d031f3016bb641.jpg)

An even greater number of monkeys have made their way up from the valley during this raid, and the first of them can be found along the path here; have your Shuriken equipped and use them to make short work of the monkeys.

![](images/dca90362b12f51d4832fc1f4af1610cc9fc4282c8f7b839b10982569f04ea7f3.jpg)

![](images/d3b060f8fc754fd23bce109f00dde30a39a9bd98c570475565cd9726b2a2c593.jpg)

A brave pair of Hounds are trying to fend off the monkey uprising outside the building here, but they won't last very long against the odds they're facing. While the fight is ongoing, run into the middle of the group, and without locking on, use the Finger Whistle to enrage them all so that the monkeys start attacking each other.

The two Elder Monkeys will finish off the normal ones fairly quickly, then they'll start fighting each other. You can either wait until their health gets low and then finish them off, or close in and use Firecrackers to stun them and speed up the process. One of those monkeys will drop a Bundled Jizo Statue, which may prove useful against the extremely challenging bosses coming up. Now that the grounds have been fully explored, we recommend that you had over to Ashina Outskirts.

![](images/2d4b4ab235886174e68ce1a9807b7384211bf4d424467bc5f3935dd633649b83.jpg)

![](images/8edbbdceeb1a3acd5586a5c48bb138c36abfad043bc58a1787fcfffc8cdadefa.jpg)

![](images/2335f1cbdc0f7c9e9886aa4134ea9ab5e2d919c64242ac7a1c46c2cb977f60b3.jpg)

The outskirts of Ashina castle are in disarray. Buildings stand ablaze and the ground has been scorched and shredded by a powerful force. The path of destruction isn't caused by the Central Forces alone, and it leads towards the Ashina Castle Gate.

Outskirts Wall - Stairway P.335

![](images/9ecaf98f8db2b00135c7ba979fb9ccad8459022c85bd97ab992c12ee05c77acc.jpg)

![](images/cd308d67424baa91ffe25d0b248e4794ddfdfa159f5e8db655dcb0a940bed5a1.jpg)

# Item Legend

1 Ministry Dousing Powder x2  
3 Gachiin's Sugar x2  
4 Heavy Coin Purse x1  
5 Fulminated Mercury x1

![](images/889755876954b02164a27e5c41fc14b6a326c24fd870d6611784c0abb8dae64c.jpg)

![](images/7d70b9353b1e3962346049640e7af91d7b9dd49765b94ae4cec83fb853b1f3a0.jpg)

The Ashina Soldiers on and near the bridge will not attack you when you get close to them, because they're far more concerned with the group of Red Guard that are approaching from the other side. Four Red Guard in total will start crossing over the bridge, and since they're being attacked by the Ashina Soldiers, you can simply run right past them while they're distracted. Wait for them to start engaging the soldiers, and then start attacking the Red Guard one at a time from behind until they're defeated.

![](images/afe6153f271db89705f36d9851e3efdf0f66d21acd9414dbbcdc0013f91aaf1d.jpg)

![](images/b5e54c01628ba60e55dfadae02ae9336f4efc7a806a5b672549f8cd703e18c34.jpg)

# Underbridge Valley

After resting at this Idol, grapple only as far as the first ledge nearby, rather than going all the way up; wait there for the fight between the Ashina and Interior Ministry forces to begin, so that you can take advantage of the situation. When the fighting starts, grapple up, and then take out the two rifle-wielding Red Guard at the rear, before crossing the bridge to take on the other two. Clearing them out again will make

![](images/bf6066986b727a1550d9c31fe5d3f97cb18e4fe2dcc3f296426c08fddbf2cd06.jpg)

moving this around this area much easier, which is important if you're attempting to take on Shigekichi.

![](images/252392a978c23fb72402b4f954fa6b3ea681c5a5ce04f16939cde8553e1e44c0.jpg)

If you don't want to pick a fight with Red Guard Shigekichi, you can take this side path around the courtyard and only have to deal with one Red Guard. Divine Abduction doesn't work on this particular enemy, however, so you'll need to face him head-on. You can then take the route through the caves, ending up in the hallway behind Shigekichi. There are two Assassins in the room you grapple up to, so be ready to take them on when you land.

![](images/6cd8bfd9f074052ca569621aad715af57c2dac94917062a2b31ea20345cad15f.jpg)

![](images/eb46dd65a6da2303477f1ea0040a5a0574d8ae5bdb5690bd0ba665be97d4b97f.jpg)

Clearing out the other enemies before facing Shigekichi will make the fight with him much easier, but the Sentry sat above him makes it difficult to move around with being detected; a better option is to bring the two remaining Red Guard to you. One of them is hiding around the corner of the wall, and the other is patrolling back and forth along the courtyard in front of Shigekichi, and it's possible to lure them both in at once. Use the gaps in the wall to see when the patrolling Red Guard is close, and then use the Finger Whistle.

The sound will cause both Red Guard to come and investigate, so quickly move and drop down the side of the stairs near Position A and hang on the ledge there. It will take the one in the courtyard much longer to reach the investigation site, so when the nearby Red Guard is just starting to walk back, throw a Ceramic Shard at him to lure him to your ledge for a Ledge Hang Deathblow. Once the other one gets here, do the same to him.

![](images/1dfb50689bd9b1be8f9cda3f6f864a407f6d73a76f24b96f59d72cf384a16d13.jpg)

![](images/cc4018f18a7b4a14f390dc001fc671c4c4e6712f8c641337f12c0905bfff8f54.jpg)

When all the Red Guard are dead, crouch down near the corner of the wall here, and then start heading towards the building at the end of the path; as long as you stick to the outside of the path, the Sentry won't spot you.

![](images/80917979da5c418d59a512e2bb60291f8cc0ecb7cf90a12e9101a7d208a62cd6.jpg)

Crouch and go through the hole in the wall here, and then sneak along the roof tiles to get behind the Sentry and use a Backstab Deathblow. His alert meter will start to build up as you close in, but as long as you don't hesitate you can make it in time. Resist the urge to go to the opposite side of the area and attack the Red Guard there—if you attempt to do so, Shigekichi will spot you.

![](images/bb17a498fa800f3bfa3a8f5fdd8a4831ea3a54a743ca8c5c295198b3b3b5f819.jpg)

![](images/ee4ea900826d232b78d49c06eb6e8218468ba8bcd05f708cbed8eb5a6e31126f.jpg)

From your position above him, you can start the fight with Shigekichi by using a Plunging Deathblow—this makes the encounter significantly easier. He earned his name through his ability to breath and imbue his attacks with fire, along with his rather impressive armor, and these are the two traits you'll need to focus on during the fight. Make sure you use some Dousing Powder to reduce the Burn build-up from his flaming attacks. You should also equip the Loaded Spear and make use of its armor-stripping capabilities against him.

Attacking him while he has his full armor will deal very little damage—remove it fully by performing two armor strips with the Loaded Spear, and you can get back to inflicting normal levels of damage. Similar to the other Shura Samurai, he will often drink from his gourd, and this is the perfect time to close in and strip his armor. Removing his armor will also inflict a lot of Posture damage, so trying to break his Posture rather than deplete his Vitality is usually a quicker way to defeat him.

![](images/5353ff301c78db09106d8a06852fd319dc96437645c097aec83e14ade8716dbd.jpg)

Now that the courtyard is clear, you can grapple up and take on the Red Guard hiding in the grass without any interference. If you want to end him quickly, use Divine Abduction as soon as you're within range, and then Backstab Deathblow him.

![](images/c68cb58d28385dac9415643b2459ae7779fb8be9b7d7ffb82b74e34f21c89b58.jpg)

Two Interior Ministry Assassins have taken up positions in the room at the end of this hallway, and if you want the item there, you'll need to defeat them. You can't lure them to you with tools or items, but if you step around the corner so the first one sees you, it will approach you, allowing you to fight it without having to worry about the second one. With that one out of the way, run into the room and take on the one that was hiding behind the door.

![](images/dab30f16ccb65348b2ea8dd3420a178e1ef055e9e719313a57b2b25d42d44866.jpg)

# Ashina Outskirts

![](images/cae5008312ff71404cdf9026d0ee42f4ad4869af6bc04b9dedac808603ac39d0.jpg)

![](images/ec22674f800a534afca4066ceaf01a1e74c11e2d92c7f9df40bca2031b462e08.jpg)

For the remainder of the area you need to move around very carefully, because the Interior Ministry forces have set up numerous watchtowers, manned by their incendiary rifle-wielding Red Guard. You'll also see red crates throughout the area that are filled with explosives; the riflemen will often fire at them if you're close enough to one to be caught in the blast. Their height gives them a commanding view over the area ahead of them, so it's best to sneak around and try to get behind them.

![](images/9225c0b8e9ba02ffb5816e3e445b07a6c0c1f81e4eea3ee51017f71a1b1ef8f7.jpg)

![](images/619c79baa715b027e649a474ec43389af5576f8f91da613c005f4df4d04b03b4.jpg)

Crouch down when you head through the large door and wait by the side of the cliff here. Two Red Guard will patrol along the path towards the door, so wait for them both to walk past you, and then Backstab Deathblow the one at the rear and use basic attacks on the other.

![](images/fc0174acddd77104a753a02c6defdbf7d15e9f1cd6d1d9f611413d3386b8bd0b.jpg)

It is possible to sneak along the cliffs to get around the first watchtower without any additional aids, but doing so is very difficult. To make things easier for yourself, use a Gachiin's Sugar when you get to this point, so that you're much harder to detect. If you don't have any, you can find some in the hallway of the building nearby.

![](images/f1883d235865f7f08d12af213bd4496b6c01b74622d9b9358e8c73160a14a6c6.jpg)

While remaining crouched, make your way down the ledge to this point, and then cross over the roof of the building so that you're behind the watchtower.

![](images/1e1ad7b20e78b60cf917ad8c7c8fe3714174a53e68e6fffb53ca42597171b449.jpg)

![](images/5e0c4736e5c519cd91f14db72f1f7150e25669fdf7c2dc635cbb340c2b9a0e91.jpg)

From this ledge you can run to the watchtower, grapple up to the back of it and Backstab Deathblow the Red Guard standing there. When he's dead, drop back down from the back of the tower, and then drop down again—this will leave you behind the enemy that stands beneath the tower, so treat him to a Backstab Deathblow. The final enemy in this area is just on the other side of the nearby gate. Since he has his back to you, you can easily Backstab Deathblow him if you want.

![](images/161e6b6ef938ee758823d2bd2be9b09c2577f139063ee78e2d40ecc53da74442.jpg)

# Outskirts Wall - Stairway

![](images/8529b0d6c2e9a7f323428b29c14a8a8ebde482876fc1b0aca114a55f265db053.jpg)

Much like the previous Idol, any time you rest at this one, make sure to kill off the nearby enemies again to ensure that you don't get shot in the back while exploring.

![](images/d56f7068e025e9209d888fc3638834fcc6be139b8077ee1284ab5138c5d0a8de.jpg)

# Anayama the Peddler Update

If you sent Kotaro to Anayama before the Interior Ministry forces ravaged Ashina Outskirts you'll find him sitting near a fire, stripped of all of his goods and wealth. He did, however, manage to hide one special item, and he's willing to sell it to you as a final gift. The Promissory Note can be purchased for 1 Sen, and once it's in your possession, all other merchants will sell their wares at a discounted rate. You only get once chance to purchase this item, because Anayama will pass away when you exit the menu whether you purchased it or not, so don't squander your chance.

![](images/ebee3e033c159daf315e6adb5e2f7e1ffa1fac5f4e53f6ac42cdc836f1748e6b.jpg)

Drop down onto the branch here, and then grapple across to the large branch further along the cliff. From that branch you'll be able to see a Assassin hanging off the cliff; throw a charged Shuriken at him to knock him off, sending him falling to his doom. Once he's down, backtrack to where you first dropped down from.

![](images/13adf8d36265b00e39d02016e38c38770e8320bf043ff19d532bb75b59c79b29.jpg)

![](images/f387711b64ed3a281b9d388c48e566ba91970c6f73ff06516fe91350daf7c39c.jpg)

Use a Gachiin's Sugar here, and then use the unmountable grapple point nearby to reach a patch of tall grass and crouch in it.

![](images/c4f4c60e114d82580991fb57472e20caa8c1e7d9019629d29fc4ab5a47407d53.jpg)

While crouched, move along to the end of the branch and drop down to the ledge below. Make sure you're as far along the branch as possible and jump towards the edge of the of the ledge, so that the Assassins in the area don't spot you. Staying as far to the right as you can, jump up to Position A and sneak behind the Assassin to use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/1c737dcf415ffea0373c123ceb5163472e1ad635fabb5d5714b28c6a21ee68a6.jpg)

![](images/affb3e7831960551e694af9fbfa31b219b85ac0245922638ec2aef7e0a1d1e38.jpg)

On the path below you'll see a patrolling Red Guard, and if you look towards the gate to the right you can see another one hiding behind it, waiting to ambush you. Wait for the patrolling enemy to be walking away from the gate, and when he's past the ledge you're on, drop down behind him and use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/e4d0961cdc0d1d17c26deca51744ece87d45d15c52ce38e759946e95ad7c4069.jpg)

Stay close to the edge of the cliff and advance towards the gate while crouched. When you reach the side of the gate, hug the wall and peer around the corner to spot a patrolling Red Guard that starts making his way down the stairs ahead. Wait for him to walk past you through the gate, and then sneak up behind him and use a Backstab Deathblow when he's further along the path. Return to the outside of the gate once he's dead, but this time go around to the other side of it. From there there you'll see another Red Guard waiting in ambush on the other side of a fence; dodge into the fence to break it, and then quickly Backstab Deathblow him.

![](images/00e5d324b6294a65470c9a4abdd8976c950e38c7ea243db44880a40982c45ed8.jpg)

![](images/332f777dc9f2f245c90dfa0f9f5add0f55eed3dfea00f3c78d0d0d5d3ec31440.jpg)  
Ashina Outskirts

![](images/bc0cb430758ef3838b6c36c08d96077b7ddb60a29bebc85d688d60fe024fc861.jpg)

With the other enemies out of the way, you can grapple up to this ledge, where you'll be behind the final Assassin and can then sneak up behind him for a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/8a719da6ca123166949b9273b57d5d6df0463597456c7dde8e09777dfd6c1811.jpg)

Resist the urge to grapple up to the Memorial Mob at the top of the nearby cliff, because if you attempt to do so, the rifle-wielding Red Guard in the watchtowers further ahead will spot you and open fire. If you want to strike from the shadows in true shinobi fashion, you'll need to work your way around the area to get behind them first.

![](images/ba370fd78f92c823606787e669c89ee0b6400f9ed0bff12156613899978bac74.jpg)

Jump up to this ledge, and then jump over to the winding path leading up the cliff-side and follow it to the top. From there, wall jump up and grab the top of the wall, so that you're beneath the enemy standing above you. A pair of Red Guard along with a Chained Ogre patrol the area in front of the enemy you're hanging near; wait for them all to be facing away, and then use a Ledge Hang Death-blow on him.

![](images/7b4f7509db284e7f3383a221bf2a5ed9368112aff584e348f210faf6f7aa36c5.jpg)

![](images/7b01ab69d8afd9a5c6359da3a271573427419b8ca15eac25a55cc1d78066601c.jpg)

Stay hanging on the ledge and wait for the two patrolling enemies to come back around; when you see them, lock onto one of them and use the Finger Whistle to lure him over to you for another Ledge Hang Deathblow. Do the same for the other one when he comes back into view. Don't try to use the Finger Whistle on either the Chained Ogre, or the enemy with a rifle that's standing up the hill to the right, because you cannot Ledge Hang Deathblow the Ogre, and the whistle will just cause the Red Guard to attack.

![](images/8b36910405afce930f5762986627bd0548e54499c8abd1d86c259e4d04209b6b.jpg)

![](images/1abc41cc5aea260b972994e9a82920e6b0807b2532ca248670e2f34d8f7c2710.jpg)

When only the Ogre and the rifle-wielding enemy remain, shimmy as far to the right as you can. When the Ogre is facing away, pull yourself up and move into the nearby tall grass while crouched. Move through the grass until you're behind the Red Guard, and when the Ogre is walking away, jump up to the path and sneak behind him to use a Backstab Deathblow.

![](images/9862f98b88771bd683e6d076e16a358ecbb6d2f3926017da51f0ba58f59326ba.jpg)

![](images/d38932a778054680de39d2e1dc0a49360843c8426ddbf4e2273fe7f464b8664e.jpg)

Quickly crouch down in the grass near the dead Red Guard, so that the Ogre doesn't see you when it starts walking back. This Ogre is significantly weaker than the previous ones you've faced; only a single Deathblow is required to defeat it, which makes it a prime target for a Backstab Deathblow. The timing for the Backstab Deathblow attempt is quite strict, however, because there's another Red Guard on the stairs nearby, and if you're too far down the path when you Deathblow the Ogre, he'll spot you. As long as you Backstab Deathblow the Ogre just as it begins to turn around, you can make it back to the grass undetected. If you just want to get to the boss of this area, then now is the time to head through the nearby gate; to continue from there, skip to Point 4 on the next page, or alternatively, continue around this area to clear it out and gather the items.

![](images/57ec6f959d6d54a09aecd4ba63fbb41eb4dbd8621e28728b917003f72f015d3d.jpg)

Follow the edge of the cliff behind the watchtowers and you'll be able to drop down behind the Red Guard with the flamethrower and Backstab Deathblow him.

![](images/ddb68c61a901464a4b08dbee369e9a493c9bfaca7aacb3fae6f9ec75cffe0322.jpg)

From the top of the stairs here, you can grapple straight up to the back of the watchtower and Backstab Deathblow the Red Guard standing in it.

![](images/500d8e66faa4c16d09acfcacea4c0297f014df7a63a6b15bc6a9216807227b17.jpg)

Jump out towards the other nearby watchtower, so that you're within range to grapple up to the back of it. The wooden boards around the tower will keep you hidden from the rifleman in the watchtower near the corner of the area, which means you can Backstab Deathblow the Red Guard in this tower without worrying about being detected

![](images/83f5e7eaa3a2870ad5fcac21fb18ae355e62ff28a5141a995e9430f8253c5e05.jpg)

Be careful when exiting this watchtower, because it's very easy to get spotted by the Red Guard in the corner watchtower; the safest option is to grapple back across to the ledge below the previous watchtower. To get behind the corner watchtower undetected, go to Position B, drop down to the path below, and then crouch down and follow the edge of the cliff until you're within range to grapple to the back of the watchtower. Backstab Deathblow the enemy as soon as you land so that he doesn't detect you.

![](images/9b3c887378fc7af94bb1ac0c3fef07bc4c41923dc9fbb9d708a517ffbd7b07a0.jpg)

# Ashina Outskirts

![](images/aa740cdcec0253436bc8a9641b521add8ac29a8c794875a91e547f327b60d72e.jpg)

![](images/c1becead27254566b7e46df6c270e280018746d150031d4d03e092a47d2bec0e.jpg)

The scorched earth and smoldering claw marks are clear indications that something of immense power has been through this area. And the trail of dead bodies reinforces that fact. So in shock are they by what they witnessed that the enemies in this area will not attack you, which means you can go straight to the Idol at the top of the hill. This is no ordinary idol, however, and as soon as you commune with it, you'll be transported to the battlefield in front of Ashina Castle. There will be a new idol right next to you when you appear there, so you can still resupply before the boss encounter, or leave the area if you wish.

![](images/11e964c970d19b49f4d2e3b5c289b1a053682993c32b82cc4a834be3ba86afc6.jpg)

![](images/a6e8d3d2ae7d945ba55fcba89c76d69dc143ddcac2aee07745f4b54ab4d728ed.jpg)

The battle against the Demon of Hatred is one of the

toughest in the game, so make sure you commune with this. Idol before venturing out to face it. If you have any untapped

![](images/188947f5128137f1a09dae7b741a695090db5265d1035f933c783f18559a6c78.jpg)

sources of Prayer Beads, or anything similar that would give you a significant boost strength and survivability, now is the time to acquire them.

![](images/fb49d6354b5373a42c72dd2f08f1c877d1df219c5afee71a0718bb4544d8d125.jpg)

The Demon of Hatred has a lot of Vitality, so this is going to be a long fight. Items such as Ministry Dousing Powder and the Withered Red Gourd will be essential to mitigate some of the Burn damage inflicted by this enemy. Similarly, Suzaku's Lotus Umbrella is an extremely potent defensive tool during the fight.

Running out of Spirit Emblems will make the fight much more difficult, but the Ceremonial Tanto can help to give you access to a few more of them when needed. If you have the Malcontent upgrade for the Finger Whistle it can be used to stun the demon briefly, creating a small window to land a few attacks. This will only work three times, however, so you'll need to pick your moments wisely.

When you first enter the battlefield, you'll see that there's a small group of Red Guard attempting to battle the demon, and while their attempt to put an end to his rampage will ultimately fail, they can still prove useful. At the start of the fight, try to position yourself so that you're on the opposite side of the demon to them, allowing you to hit him in the back while he turns to face them. The swirling flames surrounding many of his attacks may make them seem impossible to counter, but if you turn to P.477, you'll find out everything you need to know to attain victory.

![](images/9022ca2716c561be86ee32c309c7f3f5e2bef19fef31fc4f6cd9b9b72d414280.jpg)

The barrier surrounding the battlefield will drop once the demon has been defeated, so you can once again access the Memorial Mob here to replenish your supplies.

![](images/a87cf66d3b9fb9ba5e51c3288cd03da1933fa8cddd1485b32478299fc51e74fe.jpg)

The Shura Storyteller will have some interesting words for you after the battle with the demon. After talking with her and grabbing the nearby item, you'll have done everything in this area, so it's time to head to Ashina Reservoir for the final showdown. The easiest way to get there, if you haven't activated the Idol yet, is to travel to the Ashina Castle Idol and proceed on foot from there.

![](images/9206c2ebba4dfdc0e10bc02fd9d42caab80b44a5ca96e0cec6da674b638bd725.jpg)

![](images/e7089121760f64540b03cc82a4ae338555565d8189361a955429969253d75705.jpg)

The Wolf returns to the site of his failure, with memories of Genichiro severing his arm still fresh. He must once again make it to the secret passage before Lord Kuro is lost to him for ever.

![](images/09bcaab1ce5ce28cbe2ad3f317d7d1ba0f1c342532f4af8d7745aac573a2449a.jpg)

![](images/df540f3fbf7d1780bace89084ea2f37f54bb6155de13591045bbd4095f337d7d.jpg)

![](images/d05f50351627966a7eabed93fd0e0354035322a710946f30b92a81e0dea62002.jpg)

![](images/b638169488c3f5a1d649c60a97c25540230151357c81bba26e2590cc2c38afb3.jpg)

# Ashina Reservoir

If you battled your way here from the castle grounds, make sure to commune with the Idol to resupply before proceeding, because, while the end is within sight, there is still one more battle to get through along the way.

![](images/44161d98aa78aec7a33f4286ca9bc9f7ec76da3fde9f6ad3573692ba924ec15a.jpg)

![](images/62cc3b3ea112bf5ff1ab469927fb9425365f677f0e66330b43a43a97fb17efc8.jpg)

Crouch down near the top of the stairs here, and you can eavesdrop on the two enemies standing near the burning gate to hear the results of their nefarious plan. You can ignore them if you like, by running straight to the branch protruding from the cliff around the corner, but one of those enemies holds the final Prayer Bead—a prize that you should not leave behind.

![](images/511754b41a3ca0f8664031b72e0368428584f0251f9896bc952d54fa32bb5823.jpg)

![](images/6e45660578a83e97a0278722277f472410c28f16d57a145db7ccb47c5c752022.jpg)

If you crouch and stay close to the castle wall, you can sneak around the area until you reach this point. Both enemies are facing just enough to the side that you can sneak between them to land a Backstab Deathblow on the Samurai General to get him out of the way. To make fighting the remaining enemy easier, you should follow that deathblow with either the Puppeteer or Bestowal Ninjutsu, depending on your playstyle. The Samurai General can make for a fairly decent distraction, but Bestowal will usually work out for the best. With Bestowal active, you can be a lot more aggressive against this enemy and will rarely need to pause your attacks until it runs

out. Once it does, take advantage of the many opportunities to perform a Mikiri Counter, and try to break his Posture once you've depleted some of his Vitality.

![](images/0b11fab583fa941b6472335873b18e55f7bce8c504c9186bcfee053aade39ed6.jpg)

![](images/de8bca54087f798983fb02a920bd025c901a36f1b47db35c30f90b0be5beb8f5.jpg)

All routes to the other parts of the reservoir have been destroyed by the flames, so your only way forward is to run out onto this branch and grapple over to the path below the castle wall. There are no other enemies in the area, so when you land, make your way over to the Idol outside the secret passage.

![](images/3da06cbc560b5901c5dbba49a47644c120c3bf1ecd11e27f570a35a6d8c9772f.jpg)

![](images/0b13e80a38d8f7808b2a04c440ff38779ac426e183d4c7530b7a18ec68d03c1e.jpg)

# Near Secret Passage

If you haven't already spoken with Emma in Kuro's Room to obtain the Secret Passage Key, you won't be able to get through the nearby door and will need to travel back there and get it. Lord Kuro awaits you at the end of the tunnel, so when you're sure that you've made all possible preparations, proceed along it to confront your nemesis one final time.

![](images/03e6cd96d35e09caa2a0e71eb754a03970dc43f403d2b477c5f77065e57b4ca5.jpg)

![](images/e78e4095dd40f14f755c468aa49093092c6085be73e92265aaeb802b5576f2e1.jpg)

For the final showdown with Genichiro, the lightning-based attacks that he used during the previous encounter have been replaced by significantly more dangerous attacks with his black Mortal Blade. These attacks have deceptively long range, so if you're keeping your distance, it's best to stay slightly further away than you might think. Learning the timing and range of this attack is one of the keys to defeating Genichiro. It's a very deadly attack, but it's also quite slow with a lot of recovery; with proper spacing or timing you can often hit him while it recovers. The fight against Isshin will begin immediately after you defeat Genichiro, so defeating him using minimal resources will make taking on Isshin that little bit easier. To find out all of Genichiro's weaknesses, turn to P.489.

![](images/e7f4c8abeb7dc97d94d3c68e6bed956a59fe8072a267ab88bc4e3c7f455dbc82.jpg)

# Boss Battle

# Isshin, the Sword Saint

8400

2475

20000

Isshin at the height of his power will be a true test of your reflexes and endurance, with each phase of the fight bringing with it an array of new challenges. Tools such as the Lazulite Sabimaru or Okinaga's Flame Vent can be very effective for applying status abnormalities to him, regardless of the phase, so it's recommended that you always have them equipped. At the start of the fight he wields a katana and uses Ashina-style swordplay, which means you'll need to be wary of his Quickdraw and Ichimonji attacks.

When you best his sword and remove his first Deathblow Marker, he'll perform a large knock-back attack and switch to using his spear. During this phase you should look out for Mikiri Counter opportunities, or any small recovery windows within which you can land a few attacks; be careful, however, when dodging his attacks, because Isshin also uses a gun during this phase, so it's usually best to stay close and dodge towards his back. While the spear is his main weapon, he does still use his sword in this phase, so you'll still need to watch out for some of his sword-based attacks.

Defeating him during that phase will cause him to become enraged and gain lightning properties on many of his spear attacks, which he'll retain for the final phase of the battle. Make sure you use Eel Livers to mitigate the lightning damage, and take advantage of any Lightning Reversal opportunities—they are the key to victory in this phase. Isshin is an extremely difficult and complex foe, so for even more information on how to fight him, head to P.492.

![](images/133373c956f7ec21c6bde2ea201059da9485de69a969cb22f606ff19d6b432df.jpg)

![](images/026134ed9d6cee32b2a85247e18b9985dae7c9ed6b84d64856e983c6d30f3041.jpg)

When you finally emerge victorious from the battle with Isshin, he will admit defeat, and you'll need to stand behind him and perform one final Finisher Deathblow to give him a warrior's send-off. When the fight has concluded you'll find Lord Kuro laying on the ground nearby with a prompt telling you to kneel next to him. You can still leave the area before and after kneeling next to him, but eventually you'll need to make a choice as to what his ultimate fate will be.

# Ending Update

Depending on which quest lines you've completed along the way, you'll have between one and three options when you speak with Lord Kuro:

> Give Divine Dragon's Tears for the Immortal Severance ending.  
> Give Dragon's Tears and Aromatic Flower for the Purification ending.  
> Give Dragon's Tears and Frozen Tears for the Return ending.

Regardless of which ending you chose, once it's over and the credits have rolled you'll have the option to either proceed directly to another playthrough to start the adventure again at a higher difficulty, or to stay on the current playthrough. Staying on the current playthrough will allow you to go and back acquire any items you may have missed, or simply gain some additional Skill Points before starting on the next difficulty.

# Congratulations! You've seen Sekiro's journey through to its conclusion.

# 及對勢力

Chapter 4

# Opposing

# Forces

The Wolf is a lone shinobi in a world of lethal opposition. The obstacles he must overcome are truly daunting; there are many who gather against the

Ashina clan, there are those within the Ashina who plot against Lord Kuro, and there are creatures of this ancient land, none of whom will move aside and let him pass. Here we'll impart the knowledge needed to brush them all aside.

![](images/f5da8f9999dcd1f645a0628c63485e59396639dbe0315197c1e47f04002fab79.jpg)

# About this Chapter

The enemies the Wolf faces are incredibly tough, so this chapter is designed to make finding help easy. We've split the enemies into four categories: Regular, Strong, Sub-boss and Boss. For regular and strong enemies, a few key tips are usually all you need, but for sub-bosses and bosses, we want to let you decide how deep you want to dive. There are key strategies that will help any player to get through the battle, but we've also provided strategies that allow for true mastery by applying in-depth knowledge of the enemy's attacks and the swordplay and super armor systems. Here we'll go through exactly how each category is covered and how the tables work.

# Regular Enemies  $\triangleright$  Page 348

Regular enemies have the simplest tables since their attack patterns aren't as complex; only their Skill EXP and Sen values are shown. These values are separated according to the area you'll encounter them in, so a Gamefowl in Ashina Outskirts, for example, may give less Skill EXP than one in Hirata Estate. We've grouped enemies together whenever it made sense to do so.

# Strong Enemies▶Page 376

For strong enemies, we've gathered all of their key stats here: Vitality, Posture, Skill EXP and Sen. The dots beside their Vitality value represent their Death-blow Markers. These are again listed by the area they appear in, and the values shown are those for the earliest possible point that you could encounter them. Note that Okami Leader Shizu is actually a Sub-boss, but we've included her here because she's more suited to being covered alongside the other Okami Warriors.

# Sub-bosses  $\nVdash$  Page 396

Sub-bosses are where the complexity begins to ramp up; in addition to the information provided for Strong enemies, you'll find any guaranteed drops they may have, you'll see their key attacks listed and described, and we've included our recommendations for the Vitality, Attack power, Tools, Skills and Items you'd be best able to tackle them with.

# Bosses Page 434

Bosses have the same information as Sub-bosses, but we've expanded their key stats to cover each phase and time of day variation. They also have their Key Strategies highlighted separately and their main strategies are split between their different phases. One phase in this case means one Deathblow Marker

# CounterSlash

# All Phases

PROPERTIES CA | Reaction Only | E(Guard) | E(Deflect) | P(Deflect)

Fast leftward or rightward slash used as counter when pressured; can chain into more counter slashes if you deflect. Be ready to guard / deflect when engaged in swordplay with boss.

These tables describe each Boss and Sub-boss' key attacks and explain how to avoid them. They also list some important properties and Swordplay reactions. Here's what each property means:

# Super Armor

![](images/0cab88d6d58fc6528f60aa344819ec0cb9c55362265924de3452145dbadc1595.jpg)

Some enemies have Super Armor, which means they'll be able to shrug off your attacks without being staggered or flinched. Usually these enemies can't block or engage in Swordplay, but this isn't always the case. Dealing enough damage to these enemies will result in a stun, which leaves them vulnerable for a short period. Each enemy has a certain amount of Super Armor, and their own rate of recovery, which begins anew after you land each attack. These values are shown in the chart here; to see how much Super Armor your attacks remove per hit, head to P.31 in the Shinobi School chapter, and go to P.45 to see how these values change on New Game+ and Hard Mode.

# Ashina Soldier

These soldiers make up the main force of the Ashina army, and are among the first enemies you'll encounter. Ashina Soldiers are stationed all across the Ashina lands, but are most commonly found guarding the Outskirts and Castle. How difficult they are to fight is largely dependent upon their numbers and how well you've mastered the fundamentals of combat. If you've learned how to properly time deflects and Mikiri Counters, then you'll be able to easily cut through even large groups of Soldiers with brutal efficiency. If you haven't, though, then these enemies can be lethal, even one-on-one. Each of them has the ability to rapidly deal serious damage and to guard your attacks to some degree.

The Ashina Soldiers' abilities complement each other exceptionally well when faced in groups. The soldiers who wield their Katanas one-handed will operate as aggressive cannon fodder, while the more skilled spear-wielding and two-handed warriors deal substantial damage while being difficult to quickly bring down. Meanwhile, Soldiers wielding matchlock rifles will do their best to pin you down and snipe you from afar. Fortunately, the lay of the land will often give you the chance to thin the herd using Stealth Deathblows beforehand. You'll most often face them in wide open areas, which allow for multiple angles of approach, granting you the ability to easily retreat when spotted. In a pinch, though, the explosive flash of the Shinobi Firecracker can allow you to blind whole groups at once if properly utilized, allowing you to safely escape or swiftly cut them down.

# Ashina Soldier (Katana)

Fighting these enemies one-on-one is often a matter of keeping your distance and waiting for them to attack. Once you've guarded or avoided the attack, it'll be a simple task to counter-attack and overwhelm their defense with a consistent volley of basic attacks. The biggest threat in their arsenal is a rapid 5-hit consecutive attack that they often like to follow up with two hefty, overhead swings. If the first hit of this lands, you need to start deflecting quickly to prevent further damage, and once you have started guarding, the entire combo will guard lock. After you've acquired the Loaded Shuriken you can use it to quickly interrupt any of their attacks at a distance and, in conjunction with the Chasing Slice skill, dispose of them with little difficulty. It is also worth noting that, if you alert them and retreat to a perch where they can see you but can't reach you, they will respond by pulling out a rock to use as a projectile.

# Ashina Soldier (Hassou Stance)

These soldiers are notably less aggressive than their one-handed counterparts and are all the more dangerous for it. Due their strong defense, you will not be able to easily

![](images/333a922beb1b970f9ef14a2ca54bce6f3d482c2e20e3878309ae0a2979a1ef5c.jpg)

face these soldiers without the patience to guard or deflect their attacks. Attacking blindly will often only result in your second hit being deflected, leading to a powerful counter-attack. Fortunately, you can us this to more or less keep this enemy locked in a combo while you break his Posture, provided you can continually deflect his attempts to respond. You'll also occasionally encounter versions of this enemy who don't counter-attack after deflecting you. They're more focused on defending, which gives you time to hit them with thrust attacks to penetrate their guard. If you're still learning how to properly deflect, then you can use the Flame Vent to set them on fire; this deals considerable damage to them and applies the Burn status. They also have the ability to pull out a rock to use as a projectile in the same manner as their one-handed allies.

# Ashina Soldier (Matchlock Rifle)

The top priority with this enemy is to close the distance as quickly as possible; you must avoid their gunfire and face them in close combat. From far away, the shot can often be avoided by zigzagging while sprinting towards them. If you have a multi-hit Shuriken, such as the Spinning Shuriken, you can use it to interrupt them while you move in. At mid-range, their shots can be guarded or deflected, and a well-timed dodge can also do the job while helping to close the gap. Once you're in striking range, use a thrust to bypass their guard and stun them. From there, their low Posture and Vitality make them a simple foe to take care of. Don't get careless though, as they'll still be able to deal decent damage with either a quick or hefty butt of their rifle. Lastly, if you're attempting a stealth approach, eliminating these soldiers is of the highest priority. If you alert them and they manage to get a shot off then all enemies in earshot will be either partially or fully alerted to your presence.

![](images/dae3e926c67079a2055b4a1759b2162a5a657a1ebfce2d152e43f90d208892b1.jpg)  
Spear-wielding Ashina Soldiers can be easily disposed of with a Mikiri Counter.

# Ashina Soldier (Spear)

If you've mastered the Mikiri Counter ability, then there's a good chance you'll be able to dispose of any Spear-wielding Soldiers you come across with a single blow. The Mikiri Counter works against every attack they can use, and will deal an amount of Posture damage that will almost certainly allow you to follow-up with a Deathblow. If you haven't mastered or acquired the ability, however, then dealing with this enemy can be significantly more difficult. Their many thrust attacks will pierce through your guard from a considerable distance, leaving you no option but to deflect or dodge sideways to avoid them. Thankfully, most of their attacks involve a lengthy wind-up period, which allows you to interrupt them with a hit from the Loaded Shuriken. Once you're in close, you'll be able overwhelm them with slashes and close it out with a Deathblow.

![](images/47f9ef57b528ccc09da864451aa4cc5d606091274d5b12e861e0f32f6b8e335f.jpg)

You'll encounter plenty of Assassins over the course of your journey, many of whom will have their own unique traits. Some use the standard gear provided by the Senpou Temple, others wear large hats that can shield them from attacks, and there are those who operate under the order of the powerful Interior Ministry. Regardless of their gear or intentions, however, they all fundamentally operate the same—these agile killers will make use of constant, rapid movement to disorient you and avoid your blows, closing in to deal chunks of damage and escaping to begin the cycle again. Even once you manage to close in, you'll find that they have an incredibly strong defense that will allow them to reliably guard and deflect your attacks.

Few normal enemies have more options available to them than Assassins. In addition to their relentless melee attacks, they can also throw darts from a distance or fling a lingering Poison on the ground that can make approaching them dangerous—some Assassins will use these ranged attacks almost exclusively in lieu of standard attacks. You'll also encounter a variant of these ranged Assassin's whose projectiles can inflict Poison build-up. Once you're within range, most Assassins have a chance of performing an aerial grab that will easily decimate your Vitality. All of this, combined with the fact that you'll often be fighting several Assassins at once, make them one of the most dangerous foes out there.

While it can be difficult to find an opening, there are ways to create one. The Loaded Axe is especially useful in bringing these enemies down. Landing a blow with it will deal heavy Posture damage, often enough to leave them vulnerable to a Deathblow--a follow-up

![](images/b4922288bf0e3c1551f20af6c45615ff3e40070ff6745deb017e13359d14d718.jpg)  
Keep an eye out for the Assassin's deadly aerial grab.

from Fang and Blade and a couple of basic attacks will always seal the deal. The Loaded Axe will also destroy the helms of the large wooden hat Assassins, breaking their Posture in the processes. Alternatively, Divine Abduction is exceptionally good at interrupting their onslaught and leaving them vulnerable to a Backstab Deathblow. Surprisingly, it's actually possible to deflect the Assassin's aerial grab, and doing so will leave them open to nearly any counter-attack you can think of. Lastly, it's possible to use both their skill and preference for group encounters to your advantage by performing a Backstab Deathblow and using the Puppeteer Ninjutsu to make one of them your ally. This can help immensely in taking the heat off you.

# Hound

![](images/b31314da0bdde075a32c86989423ea6472048b236dda3a7c3d3147579dae5afc.jpg)

You will often encounter aggressive Hounds alongside more skilled warriors. In group fights, they'll primarily serve as a distraction from the main force, interrupting and harassing you with swift attacks from a moderate distance, or as pursuit enemies, chasing you down when you try to escape. They typically rely on having allies nearby to prevent you from simply hunting them down. However, it's still possible to quickly bring them down even in these situations, as a single deflection will yield an instantaneous Deathblow. In addition, due to their beastly nature, you can break the Posture of any Hound with the blinding flash of the Shinobi Firecrackers.

# Hound

The simplest way to deal with these agile attack dogs is with the use of the Loaded Shuriken, as even a single blow will usually be enough to bring the beasts down. However, if the Shuriken is unavailable, you'll find that they will usually move around at mid-range before choosing the right time to pounce at you. If they are too far or too close, they will more often than not attempt to reposition themselves a few meters away from you before trying to attack. Once they move to strike, all you'll need to do is deflect their attack and you'll be able to immediately break their Posture and finish them off. Alternatively, a well-timed side step can allow you to avoid their attack and follow up with a counter. Be careful, though, as you'll rarely face Attack Hounds alone. In a group, their raw aggression can easily overwhelm those who do not deal with them quickly. You'll also encounter specialized Shinobi Hounds accompanying certain Lone Shadows over the course of your journey, recognizable by the shinobi headbands they wear. These trained attack dogs behave identically to Attack Hounds, but deal increased damage and will attack when given a whistling signal by the Lone Shadow that commands them.

# Palace Hound

The otherworldly Okami Hounds of the Fountainhead Palace often act exactly like the standard Attack Hounds. Each will take its time and keep its distance, before suddenly pouncing to deliver their attack, but they can easily be brought down with a hit from the Loaded Shuriken. If they're wearing a stone around their neck, however, they will have the ability to channel lightning, which they will then throw directly at you. It is possible to perform a Lightning Reversal on this attack and return it back to the beast, and all its nearby allies. You'll often be fighting these creatures while ankle deep in the waters of the Palace. If the lightning hits the water, it will travel through the current and explode in a sizable blast.

# Gamefowl

Early in your journey, there will be few enemies more capable of decimating your Vitality more quickly than Gamefowls. On the ground they can use quick pecks to interrupt many of your close-range attacks. Their most dangerous attacks, however, come after jumping in the air—a series of devastating clawing attacks that can sap you of your Vitality in a single moment. If you're hit by the first kick, don't give up—at any point in its aerial combo you can interrupt it with a deflect, even if you've been hit. Once you've landed the first blow you should be able to easily chain basic attacks together to finish it off.

If you've purchased the Anti-air Deathblow Text from Blackhat Badger, you can use the skill it provides to jump towards a Gamefowl and finish it off in a single attack after guard

ing or deflecting its aerial combo. Lastly, due to their beastly nature, they are exceptionally weak to any form of Fire. Showering them in Shinobi Firecrackers will break their Posture and leave them completely dazed and vulnerable, while a single hit from the Flame Vent will set their feathers ablaze, killing them in the process. Be careful if you choose the latter though, as the Flame Vent's lengthy wind-up can leave you vulnerable to its jumping claw attack.

# Sentry

On its own, a Sentry is almost completely harmless. If you get near them, they will be able to flail and poke their gong stick to monumentally interrupt you, but they lack any means of dealing noticeable damage or any worthwhile defense. Their real danger lies in an ability to almost immediately alert all those within a sizable range to your presence. To make matters worse, they have exceptional vision, allowing them to see you from distances greater than any other enemy. Fortunately, they do have their limitations—as long as you're behind them to some degree, they will be completely unable to notice you. Their vision is limited directly to their left and right and, unless it takes notice of you in some way, they will never turn around. If they do notice you, though, you'll only have a brief moment to interrupt them before they alert any nearby allies in the area. This means you should always make the Sentries your top priority when attempting a stealth approach. If you are about to be spotted by one and you are close enough, quickly throw a Shuriken to take them out.

![](images/fe1a7b57a5d119966176e7a5ec93da83e490560043756b6fa61a3301622efa5a.jpg)  
Once they've noticed you, Sentries will alert all foes within earshot to your presence.

![](images/76f17e79bbe8fda62ddc08a8d4f8fe24c0e878e72819b4cb40281f5f4f9fb0dd.jpg)

# Infested Seeker

Infested Seekers have incredibly poor senses and will not notice you as long as you make some kind of effort to hide yourself. This makes it easy to perform a Backstab Deathblow on them or avoid them entirely. Even if they notice you, they won't pursue you as long as you're outside their range. These are purely creatures of self-defense. However, if you alert them and enter their range, they will immediately begin to vomit bile in your direction. This bile will remain on the floor for around 10 seconds and inflict minor damage to you if you step on it.

There also exists a second variant who can spawn up to three Crickets at once. If you encounter this, kill the Seeker as quickly as you can, as it will almost instantly replace any Crickets you may kill, with no upper limit on how many they can replace. Thankfully, due to their low Vitality and Posture, it's relatively trivial to overwhelm them once you've landed the first hit. However, you'll need to use the Mortal Blade to deliver the final Deathblow and kill them off for good. Without it, they will simply revive, completely healed, after around 10 seconds.

![](images/de61be39974c8e07da3131bcdd55b17fb7848913ef06c5cafad0e160cb8d98fd.jpg)  
Coming into contact with the bile an Infested Seeker vomits up will cause any nearby Crickets to go berserk and attack you.

# Crocket

Bandits stalk many of the Ashina territories in some form or another, but you'll primarily deal with them as you relive the raid on the Hirata Estate. In practice, Bandits behave like the Ashina Soldiers, but with a stronger focus on offense. Few of these unskilled outlaws pose much of a threat one-on-one, as they generally have terrible defense and can often be brought down with just a few simple blows. However, their sizable groups, fast attacks, and relentless aggression can make them one of the most overwhelming forces you can encounter if they are not managed properly. Additionally, several of these Bandits will employ fire-based attacks that will cause Burn build-up, even if deflected, and you'll often encounter them alongside packs of Attack Hounds.

Even large groups of foes are still only as good as their best warrior, though. While it may not be safe in every situation, properly timed deflecting will deal massive Posture damage and leave them stunned, allowing for a counterattack that can put most of them down. Likewise, if you can land the first hit, you'll be able to break their Posture with a few more hits. For this reason, it's wise to try to isolate each Bandit and deal with them one at a time, or approach them using hit-and-run tactics to whittle down the force. If you get surround, a fistful of Shinobi Firecrackers can blind a good number of them and allow you to make your escape.

You'll also encounter illusionary versions of these Bandits in the Hidden Forest. These foes behave identically to the normal version, but they lack the fire-based attacks. You can use a Snap Seed to dispel these illusions and kill them instantly.

# Bandit (Axe)

Deflecting is the simplest way to deal with these Bandits. Deflecting their Axe attacks will stun them and leave them vulnerable to a counter-attack. The Flame Vent is particularly useful here, as it will not only deal considerable damage, but will also inflict Burn immediately. Launch a relentless offensive of basic attacks while they're stunned and you'll often finish them off before they can recover. Be cautious though, as this is one of the few super armored enemies in the game. In order to stun them, you'll need to hit them with two regular blows, or one thrust. It's typically safest to hit them with a thrust in between their attacks and then back off, rather than trying to interrupt them during their attacks. Additionally, while it's rare, they may occasionally opt to throw an oil pot at you, which will increase any Burn build-up you receive from any other Bandits, or kick up dirt in an attempt to blind you. It's also worth noting that, if you fight Anayama the Peddler, he will attack in a manner identical to these Axe-wielding Bandits.

![](images/1e5712d64bf6056ed2cb949cf211490839c3de405f01dfa5542d7e922e65a703.jpg)  
Deflecting their Axe attacks will stun them for a while.

# Bandit (Katana)

These Bandits are similar to the one-handed style Ashina Soldiers in the Ashina Outskirts, but even more aggressive. They'll charge at you much more frequently and are typically quicker to perform follow-up attacks once you guard or deflect their first attempt. You can use this to your advantage by baiting their dash attack and dropping a Shinobi Firecracker in their path to stop their charge, leaving them wide open. Once you've landed the first hit, you'll be able to easily overwhelm their defense with a volley of standard slashes. Be careful, however; if you aren't able to finish them off while you have them on the defensive, they'll respond with a quick retreating slash the moment you let up, even if they have only guarded one attack. If you allow them to land the first blow, there's a good chance that you'll not be able to safely respond with anything other than a retreating dodge or a series of deflects.

They will sometime use a thrusting Perilous Attack that can pierce your defense for a sizable amount of damage. This actually allows you to dispose of them in a single blow if you're able to respond to it with a Mikiri Counter. You may also notice that they are not above fighting dirty and will occasionally take a moment to kick dirt in your eyes, temporarily stunning you and breaking your lock-on. It's a rare trick to see, but can easily spell your demise if it catches you off-guard.

![](images/7b8a4e2f1d303e4ace391e94f33d816ef3af7c847d60b06f6f68699b22e655ce.jpg)  
The long range of Whirlwind Slash can interrupt many Bandit's running attacks.

![](images/989706737f760cf975ab6bdf9dbb2c71b6edeefa5a34ca0da9101432dac400de.jpg)  
Katana-wielding Bandits will sometimes attempt a running thrust Perlious Attack that can be easily Mikiri countered.

# Bandit (Katana & Bow)

Which weapon these bandits use is entirely dependent upon your distance from them. If you're up close, they will default to their katana and become functionally identical to any other Katana-wielding Bandit. At a distance however, they'll employ flaming arrows that can deal sizable damage and cause Burn build-up, even if they are deflected. Fortunately, these projectiles are slower-moving than any of the guns, which makes them much easier to avoid by zigzagging and keeping on the move as you as approach. After you've closed in, it will take them a moment to switch from their bow to their blade. This will give you the perfect opening you need to initiate your attack and dispose of them. Due to their versatility and skill at dealing damage from afar, it's recommended that you consider them among the highest priority targets in any group. When you revisit the Hirata Estate with the Father's Bell Charm, you'll encounter a variant of this enemy who uses arrows that inflict Poison, so make sure to equip some Antidote Powder.

# Bandit (Katana & Shield)

The Loaded Axe is almost purpose-made to counter these enemies. A single blow from it will shatter their shields into splinters and decimate their Posture, leaving them open for a Deathblow. If they somehow survive, they will in effect become standard, Katana-wielding Bandits and become all the easier to deal with. If the Loaded Axe isn't an option, however, the safest course of action is to simply run in circles around them until they attempt to attack you, and then take a swing at their back after they miss. It's also possible to bait them into using a charge attack by performing a jump kick off their shield. You can then avoid it with a dodge to the side, and will be able to easily punish them once they've come to a stop. Do your best to avoid hitting their shield with any weapon besides the Axe, as doing so will not only fail do deal any Vitality or Posture damage, but is highly likely to be answered with a shield bash that deals a surprising amount of damage for how quick it is.

# Bandit (Katana & Torch)

The addition of a torch to a Bandit's arsenal increases their deadliness much more than one may expect. Not only does it grant them access to a quick poke that can interrupt your attack, but also allows them to cause Burn build-up even when you deflect their attacks. Even with a flawless defense, you may find yourself taking serious damage if you aren't careful. For this reason, you'll typically want to stand just outside of their attack range and wait for them to come to you. Once they take a swing, dodge backwards and toss a Shuriken, then follow up with a Chasing Slice and a barrage of slashes to quickly overwhelm them. Alternatively, they have two combos that each involve thrusting Perilous Attacks late into their chains—you can easily Mikiri Counter these once you learn to recognize them, allowing for a quick kill.

![](images/3e794916601c53eb329f454b6a327a145c6765cbe32bcdac6b132999278f2f12.jpg)  
The slow moving arrows of Bow-wielding Bandits are easily avoided with sideways movement.

![](images/81b86031f807677928ca3388ba44cf769b06bec03137b6f1412aa312bb038a98.jpg)  
The Loaded Axe will shatter a Bandit's shield in one blow, leaving them vulnerable to a Deathblow.

![](images/fbd441ec717ae83fe15379250109a0136e8108872f22f56d534b3a42e67b65b5.jpg)  
Watch out for a torch-wielding Bandits sneaky, thrusting Perilous Attacks.

![](images/efd05d3cab1e3aa3fece00567e17a8ad7c05eb7ee6d05bc7cceecd13fef6d436.jpg)  
They'll use their torches as improvised fire attacks that cause Burn build-up.

Treasure Carp (Red Eyes) - Basic Info  

<table><tr><td>Location</td><td>Skill EXP</td><td>Sen</td></tr><tr><td>Ashina Depths</td><td>84</td><td>-</td></tr></table>

You will encounter Carp in most of the bodies of water across the Ashina territories. In most instances you'll want to be on the lookout for the brightly-colored Treasure Carps, which will yield valuable Treasure Carp Scales when killed. At a distance it can be very easy to mistake the violent Man-eating Carp for a Treasure Carp, which will quickly attack you the moment it sees you. On occasion, you'll find the two seemingly working together, with Treasure Carps being escorted through the water by small schools of Man-eating Carps. The Treasure Carp should always be your top priority in these situations, as they will try to escape once they've been alerted to your presence and, with them gone, you'll seldom have any reason to fight the rest of the carp. It's also worth noting that there is no way to attack carp that are underwater without being underwater yourself, meaning you'll have to acquire the Mibu Breathing Technique before being able to hunt those under the surface. You may encounter a Red-Eyed Carp in Mibu Village; this Carp will not attack you, and will yield the Red Carp Eyes for Dojun's questline when killed.

# Man-eating Carp

These deceitful carp will circle around you from a considerable distance before attempting to swiftly charge at you with a bite. Fortunately, though, this attack can be deflected even underwater. Due to the fact that Man-eating Carps almost always move in schools, there's a good chance that their sheer numbers will overwhelm you if you aren't careful. When fighting groups it's best to keep mobile, with lateral underwater dashes to avoid their attacks and find an opening to attack one when they temporarily stop. If you

# Treasure Carp

Treasure Carp live up to their name, as the primary source of valuable Treasure Carp Scales. For every one you kill, you'll receive one Treasure Carp Scale. To catch a Treasure Carp, you'll need to be stealthy and move quickly when you strike. The moment it notices you, it will attempt to escape, and will do so at a speed that few other creatures could keep up with. Even if the carp hits a wall, they will still disappear after a moment and escape entirely. Underwater dash attacks can be highly useful in catching them, but in general, if they notice you, you'll only have a moment to reach them before they vanish, requiring you to wait until they respawn at their original location for another attempt.

angle it correctly, there's a good chance you'll be able to kill more than one with a single strike. However, as soon as they take notice of you, they'll immediately disperse and begin to swarm, at which point you'll generally have to tackle them one at a time. If you find yourself in need of escape, try to stay underwater as long as possible, because the underwater dash goes further than the one on the surface, and Man-eating Carps that patrol the water's surface will never dive below to attack you.

![](images/ed37e4129c78fb89a71de2d4fa15c0c73e679aa9d4738236fa2d765fd61a26fd.jpg)

Sneaking up and suddenly catching a Treasure Carp by surprise with a dash attack is your best bet at killing them before they can escape.

# Nightjar Ninja

![](images/eac593c253feebe9b9d0f9cf918220243e660b7cf861a37bd1c5eee642014388.jpg)

A Nightjar Ninja's keen senses will often make a stealth approach challenging and, once they've noticed you, they will chase you from rooftop to rooftop. In direct combat, you'll find that few enemies are more capable of negating your attacks—their agile nature often makes it difficult to land a direct hit, and their defenses are very capable. Some of them use Shuriken to deal considerable damage from long distances, and they still pose a serious threat up close. Some are so dedicated to protecting their lord they will choose to ignite explosives on their body and throw themselves at you. When you see them light on fire and start screaming, jump or dodge away from them to avoid the explosion, since it can't be guarded or deflected. Finally, some employ a close-ranged, spinning blade that can hit you multiple times in a single attack—the most skilled among them will coat this in fire for added damage.

Even one-on-one, challenging them can be daunting, but they do have their weaknesses. The thick feathers they wear can be set ablaze with a hit from the Flame Vent, inflicting a Burn and leaving them stunned for a follow-up attack. It can also be simple to overwhelm them with standard attacks, though the Melee variant can sometimes perform a very fast counter-attack. Handling two of them at a time is challenging even in the best of situations, and handling more than that is all but a death sentence. Retreat is not only a wise choice if you're feeling overwhelmed, it's also a useful tool to split up groups and give you the chance to face them one at a time, if only briefly.

![](images/2934c5ca0c6e6c871a00e7b02a16e3e524402a41746ad3c40821bc1594ba59d0.jpg)  
The Loaded Axe can deal serious Vitality and Posture damage.
