# Vengeful Spirit Nightjars

If you defeat Genichiro before defeating the Corrupted Monk, you'll begin to encounter the Vengeful Spirit Nightjar Ninja in the Ashina Depths, Sunken Valley, and Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo once nightfall approaches. These variants behave identically to the standard versions.

# Nightjar Ninja (Melee)

When using Melee weapons, the Nightjar Ninja will rely on a series of spinning blade attacks, with multiple hits that can easily catch you in their grasp if you approach at the wrong time. The most dangerous of these to watch out for is a retreating roll followed up by a lunge, with the spinning blade extended out in front of them, which can deliver up to seven brutal hits. Between this and their speedy movement, it can often be hard to safely land a hit.

To counter this, it's often easiest to simply wait for a chance to deflect and then counter-attack. Guarding or deflecting the first hit of the spinning blades is key. While the numerous hits can be in

# Nightjar Ninja (Shuriken)

These Nightjar Ninja try their best to overwhelm you with Shuriken and quick lunges. Combined with the jagged territories they often patrol, this can make getting close to them a challenge on its own. Even when you do get near them, you'll find that they have a solid defense and are exceptionally skilled at escaping after delivering a quick blow. Thankfully, it's possible to use their fondness for jumping against them. Hitting them with a Shuriken of your own while they're airborne will cause major Vitality and Posture damage. If you manage to deflect their projectiles, then you can often safely counter with a NightjarSlash, then follow up with a hit from the Flame Vent and a flurry of slashes to bring them down. Be careful before you commit to fighting this Nightjar, though, as their long-range attacks and ability to jump great distances can make retreat difficult.

# Black-Feathered Nightjar

These elite Nightjar Ninja fight almost identically and share all the same weakness as the Melee-oriented Nightjar Ninja. They are still highly vulnerable to being deflected in rapid succession, and can rack up Posture damage quickly if you guard. They do have one extra tool that complicates matters, though; on occasion, they'll retreat to set their blades on fire. Once this effect is applied, all their attacks will cause Burn build-up and fire damage, even when deflected. The effect will remain active on their blades for 60 seconds. This can make the fight significantly more dangerous, as you can still take heavy damage even when deflecting flawlessly. Dousing Powder can help mitigate the Burn build-up, but you'll still take fire damage, so it's a better idea to rely on hit-and-run tactics until their fire buff runs out—dodge their attacks and pressure their guard instead of deflecting. They're open whenever they set their blades aflame, so make sure to punish them for it.

![](images/1448587ed095ece9447a54a8da5d2efd3a6bf654c2aa444d27fa8e4fc0403c7d.jpg)  
As evening falls, Vengeful Spirit Nightjar Ninja may begin to appear across the land.

timidating, as long as you guard the first, you'll automatically guard the rest. From there, you can attempt to deflect each hit in relative safety as it dishes them out. Additionally, you'll be able to follow up with a blast from the Flame Vent after some of their more sluggish abilities, most notably their lunging attack. However, be careful if you aren't able to consistently deflect their relentless barrage while the Vitality damage can be negligible if guarded, the Posture damage will stack up quickly. You'll also encounter a stronger RedEyed variant of this enemy, cloaked in white feathers. They behave the same as the standard version, but will also possess the same fear and weakness to fire that all Red-Eyed enemies possess.

![](images/7c0fa49870fe04ccd3c6b4d7b1529066eb34fdb3616f3fb57e4d752debda1d5f.jpg)  
Nightjar Shuriken will turn mid-flight to home in on your position.

# Test Subject

Always do your best to keep your distance from Test Subjects until you're ready to go in for the kill. While they only have one attack at their disposal, it is a super-armored grab that you cannot guard or deflect, which has the potential to deal considerable damage. This grab's long wind-up period will allow you to stun or even kill them if you start hitting them while they're initially getting up. Otherwise, it's best to circle behind them and attack them while they're in the middle of the grab, as they can't turn around to latch onto you. If you find yourself in their clutches, you can rapidly press the face and shoulder buttons to escape early. Pressing the buttons fast enough will prevent all damage, but you must be very fast to achieve this. While their direct defense may be lacking, they do possess an immunity to Poison, as well as the ability to resurrect once after dying.

Their resurrection ability can be prevented by one of two methods: either use a Fire-based weapon to inflict Burn on them before killing them, or use any Ninjutsu after delivering a Backstab Death-blow. The latter can be executed very easily with the use of the Divine Abduction tool. Test Subjects also fear fire, causing them to recoil in fear at the very sight of it, leaving them vulnerable to attack. Their slow movement speed also means that they're easy to avoid, as long as you don't get caught in tight spaces with them.

# Old Maid

Old Maids are more of an obstacle to be aware of than a true enemy. A single quick attack or Shuriken thrown from afar is usually enough to dispatch them. They have very poor senses and will often struggle to notice you if you're sneaking, unless you're directly in front of them. Once they do notice you though, they'll let out a shriek that causes all within earshot to come and investigate. After this, they become completely harmless. The Maids lack any attacks whatsoever and, if encountered on their own, all the can do is try fruitlessly to run from you before tripping and cowering where they land. However, due to their ability to draw the attention of more dangerous foes, it's still recommended to take them out as quickly as possible. It's worth noting that you'll encounter a variant of this enemy among the Valley Clan members near the Gun Fort which, aside from a change in appearance, is identical to the standard version.

# Gecko

![](images/3ac2b2a9ddfecb721f2c8e27a6721f41df5aaf79b372fbb3f094f00fdfcc4134.jpg)

# Gecko

Defeating a Gecko one-on-one can be done by simply jumping above it. Once you're above it, you'll be able to perform a Plunging Deathblow to eliminate it. This can be a problem when facing the groups of them that will ambush you, however; Gecko primarily attack by spewing venom that turns into a poisonous cloud once it hits the ground, and will continue to cause rapid Poison build-up. You may be invulnerable while performing a Deathblow, but you'll quickly take Poison build-up as soon as it completes. The Poison can be countered by keeping an Antidote Powder on hand to use after clearing out a group, but this can still result in taking serious damage. Instead, it's often ideal to use a Contact Medicine to weakly Poison yourself beforehand, preventing their more hazardous Poison from taking hold. It's also worth keeping in mind that you can dispose of them with a single charged toss from the Spinning Shuriken. This can be particularly useful if you manage to catch them unaware while lying in wait. While it's not often a practical option, it is possible to use them to spew Poison at other foes by using a Backstab Deathblow to perform a Bloodsmoke Ninjutsu.

# Albino Gecko

Wherever you find narrow caves or tall grass, you're also likely to find Geckos. These lizards will often lie in ambush just out of sight. Once you've entered far enough into their lair, they will spring on you as a group, dropping down to surround you or launching their attacks suddenly from their hiding spot. They will then begin to coat the battlefield in their dangerous venom and take quick bites that can quickly sap you of your Vitality. If you find yourself encircled by Geckos, Mist Raven can allow you to quickly retreat to safety, or can send you straight upwards to deliver a counter-attack. Fortunately, their low Vitality and inability to defend themselves often makes it easy to eliminate them with only a single hit.

Albino Geckos function almost identically to Geckos. They often lie in wait in groups to ambush you with their venom, and can be easily defeated with a hit from the Loaded Shuriken or a Plunging Deathblow after jumping near them. The difference lies in their projectile: the venom of Albino Geckos causes no status build-up, but will deal minor damage to your Vitality if you stand where it lands. This makes them noticeably less dangerous than the Geckos, but they can still pose a hazard in large numbers. A unique property of all Gecko variants is that if you use either the Bloodsmoke or Bestowal Ninjutsu, your blade will take on the properties of the Gecko's blood. For normal Geckos you will either create a poisonous cloud with Bloodsmoke, or coat you blade with poison if using Bestowal. With Albina Geckos, Bloodsmoke will create a cloud that heals you over time, and Bestowal will cause every katana strike that hits an enemy to heal you for a short period of time.

![](images/26a3377096aa36f4759f493d11e31931a55705f4c83e0b7c87a1c6f3b6b6f800.jpg)  
Geckos often hide along walls and ceilings, waiting for a victim to ambush.

![](images/eaf28883a67273d9e461985ec16c2615a1b0cca82887cad7ce6d20c2f6f2d655.jpg)

The inhuman Okami Warrior women guard the Fountainhead Palace with their unusual martial arts style. Fond of constant hops and spinning movements, many of their attacks involve them leaping into the air. This tendency to stay airborne during their attacks can be turned against them by knocking them down with a Shuriken, dealing critical Posture damage. This is particularly effective against the highly evasive Bow-wielders. Both the Katana and Kemari variants each have an attack that provides an opportunity to finish them immediately with an anti-air Deathblow.

Their constant movement can make them difficult to pin down, since the bow users will hop away from your close-range pressure, and the melee variants can respond with powerful counter-attacks after deflecting you. The Katana and Bow variant comes in two varieties: one starts out with a katana and will only pull out the bow if you are in a position they can't reach, whereupon they have access to the normal bow attacks until you get close again. The other starts with a bow and pulls out the katana when you get close; you can differentiate them from the regular bow-wielding Okami Warriors by their much higher Vitality and Posture—if a bow user is surprisingly difficult to kill, be careful since they're likely to suddenly pull out their katana.

All Okami Warrior women are extremely weak to blue rust Poison. Only a single hit of Sabimaru is required to apply Poison to them, building up their Posture dramatically and stunning them for a long duration.

# Okami Warrior (Bow)

They initially start out simply shooting their bow at you from range, but as you get close, bow-wielders will begin long, gliding leaps to get away from you, releasing mid-air bow shots as they move. This can make it difficult to hit them with Sabimaru, but if you have the Mid-air Prosthetic Skill you can time a jump sideways and throw a Shuriken at them mid-air to both avoid their shot and knock them down. This will deal massive Posture damage and

![](images/e2918cd925597c272c7eac518217899747676dfa61561111a97852746eaa60aa.jpg)  
Jumping sideways to avoid their arrows and throwing a Shuriken at them mid-air when they leap is a fast way to break their Posture.

knock them down, allowing you to quickly run to them and use basic attacks to break their Posture. If you don't have the Mid-air Skill, you can time a sprinting Shuriken as you close in, but the timing is quite tight. If you're fighting a group of them, their Vitality and Posture is very low, so you can quickly kill one at range with several Shuriken while staying mobile to avoid the others' attacks.

![](images/ebc9ecc8f0d4ff272194cbcb9a821f7ca8fec06ab9b6f21e309a2942e335b12b.jpg)  
If a Bow-wielder is surprisingly tough to take down, they're likely to pull out their Katana once you get too close.

# Okami Warrior (Naginata)

Their naginata gives their normal slashes and slams long range, and naginata-wielders have numerous Perilous Attacks that you need to watch out for. They can perform a thrust with one hand that has extra range—be sure to watch out for this as you close in after deflecting their attacks and Mikiri Counter it. They have two sweeps; the first comes after a horizontal slash and the second is the Quadruple Spinning Sweep often used after pressuring their

![](images/dfa50b9191c063c4938fda049c752f72246fea1414ad4cd3048e5288de68c31e.jpg)  
Their one handed thrust has long range.

guard or when they deflect you. You can find the attack table for this Perilous Attack in the Okami Warrior (Lightning) section (P.390). Jump-kicking their sweeps will deal a tremendous amount of Posture damage to them, often allowing you to finish them off with a few more strikes, even if they're guarded. Deflecting their leaping vertical cleave will always cause them to respond with a special jumping thrust from mid-air, to which you can respond with a Mikiri Counter.

![](images/8580cc171a314078870ec625a7f215ea95c16338897351ec1729a09ede80a735.jpg)  
Deflect their leaping cleave and they'll react with an immediate jumping thrust you can Mikiri Counter.

# Okami Warrior (Katana & Bow)

Their hops can give many of their attacks surprising range and some of them are armored as they start, so resist the urge to approach when they are preparing to attack. Instead, back away and wait for them to miss before moving in. Be careful of their long-range leaping thrust; if they suddenly leap straight into the sky with a scream and you see the Danger Symbol, prepare to Mikiri Counter or dodge. Constantly pressuring their guard until they deflect will force them to respond with either a fast, two-hit consecutive combo or their longer falling passage multi-hit flurry. This attack is similar to Sekiro's own Falling Passage combat art—a six-hit combo that ends with a final, longer-ranged slash. Deflecting the final slash

![](images/9b8274234414fa2ff6d9285ee0b2a723543e442ab774751aa8160225e6306783.jpg)  
Jumping towards them mid-air after deflecting the last attack of their leaping passage combo gives you an anti-air Deathblow opportunity.

will push them away from you in mid-air—leap up after them for an anti-air Deathblow opportunity. This is a useful attack to bait if you're overwhelmed by multiple Katana-wielding Okami Warriors. Keep moving away from them until one of them starts the falling passage attack and move back in just to deflect the final slash.

Most Katana-wielding Okami Warriors also carry a bow, which they'll switch to if you move to a place they can't reach. Occasionally you will fight one without it, allowing you to retreat to the rooftops if you need space to heal or use an item.

![](images/56b4d9bbec2ddcbb10d9d61b9b305b0fdedca6fa4562fd4e294199ecded6ebf3.jpg)  
Their leaping attack combo will never end once you've started deflecting it; they'll keep looping the same two quick then slow leaping slashes until you stop deflecting.

# Okami Warrior (Kemari)

The Kemari-wielders' main method of attack is kicking their Mari ball at you. They have two attacks they use at long range, both of which involve leaping into the sky. When they leap upside-down to kick, the ball travels in a straight line and deals massive damage if it hits its target. This attack has an anti-air Deathblow opportunity, providing you're close enough and jump up to them while they're leaping into the sky. Their second leap attack sees them kick the ball sideways, so it curves in on you, but the ball's curving path can't hit you if you are too close to them. As you close in they can kick their ball on the ground twice—the Mari ball's path is linear for both kicks and can be easily avoided by sideways dodges.

![](images/f1cf66b58e97aec146fd475afae64b91acaec315b49ad3b06fbfef692bec8ee1.jpg)  
When they leap upside down to kick the Mari ball you can jump towards them for an anti-air Deathblow opportunity.

When you're right next to them, they have an armored jumping double kick; deflecting this will push them away from you, so it's better to guard it or dodge backwards to avoid it. They have little Vitality or Posture, so the easiest way to defeat them is to throw a Shuriken during their initial leaping attacks from some distance away to knock them down. You can then close in and attack them to finish them off. If you're fighting them in a group, watch out for their leaping upside-down kick—jump up after them to anti-air Deathblow.

![](images/600b0f4974afd537d39dbd78689e4ae97e6710055dc6d9de362884cf204302d1.jpg)  
As you approach them they'll often try to fend you off with two Mari ball kicks. Make sure to dodge both before you close in again.

# Palace Noble

![](images/70fceea55bd834d73eb44b431aa9f0e40940fb09533ff57a46e52f46a957ed4d.jpg)

Mist Noble  $\text{一}$  Basic Info  

<table><tr><td>Location</td><td>Skill EXP</td><td>Sen</td></tr><tr><td>Asha depts</td><td>257</td><td>39</td></tr><tr><td>Fountainhead Palace</td><td>530</td><td>87</td></tr><tr><td>Fountainhead Palace</td><td>210</td><td>32</td></tr></table>

The residents of the Fountainhead Palace are rarely a direct physical threat. Each lacks defense, possess weak attacks, and rarely move with any urgency. However, what they lack in strength they more than make up for with their magical capabilities. If they have magic at their disposal, few creatures can spell your doom much faster than the Palace Nobles. Thankfully, if you can manage to close the space without being noticed, you'll be able to dispose of them with ease.

# Palace Noble (Blue Garb)

Perhaps more than any other enemy, stealth is required to deal with these Palace Nobles. If you can get near them without being noticed, you'll be able to cut them down with a single slash. If you have trouble getting to them without being seen by others, a few charged hits from the Spinning Shuriken can break their Posture from a distance, allowing you to close in and Deathblow them.

If they notice you, they'll immediately begin casting a spell that causes a unique status abnormality to begin building up. Once it fills, you'll be transformed into a decrepit old man, incapable of fighting back. While in this state, your maximum Vitality will be reduced to a sliver, movement speed will be slowed to a crawl and you'll be unable to jump, dodge or use items other than the Homeward Idol. Additionally, you'll only be able to attack with an incredibly slow sword swipe that will often do more to leave you vulnerable than it will to help. Worst of all, though, is that you'll also be stripped of your power to Resurrect and will suffer a True Death upon being killed.

# Palace Noble (Red Garb)

These are the highest-ranking Nobility of the Fountainhead Palace, and most of them are busy gorging themselves on the bodies of deceased Okami Warriors, allowing you to safely pass unharmed. That doesn't mean they won't ever take notice of you-if you open any door or chest near them they will immediately turn their attention towards you. The same is also true if you attack any one of them or alert one by standing directly in front of it. The Palace Nobles will then begin to slowly make their way towards you. While they can be dangerous if you let yourself become surrounded, their lethargic attacks, lack of defense, and low Vitality make cutting them down with just basic attacks a simple feat.

![](images/dd402fcf01134ed5c9b9498df3192643ca790fef7307a21cd4af8a189c8e5b11.jpg)  
Avoid remaining in a Palace Noble's line of sight at all costs or you risk becoming Enfeebled.

# Centipede

![](images/5135861862b2808eec8224ed0e7408ee53ad6d0916dc423aeeb8592c9628c162.jpg)

Centipede - Basic Info  

<table><tr><td>Location</td><td>Skill EXP</td><td>Sen</td></tr><tr><td>Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo</td><td>46</td><td>12</td></tr><tr><td>Sunken Valley</td><td>80</td><td>14</td></tr></table>

While their bulky leaders will attempt to break you down with unrelenting blows, the wall-crawling Centipedes prefer to put pressure on you by tossing three fire bombs at a time, spreading flames that will linger across the area. Given that you'll most often find them in confined spaces, this can make it very difficult to avoid damage and Burn build-up. It is possible to keep out of range of the fire bomb's radius by sticking close to the Centipede, but they will respond with a variety of agile slashes that deal a surprising amount of damage. Since you'll almost always encounter them in groups, these creatures can prove intimidating at any range.

They do, however, have a few key weaknesses. Hitting them with a jump kick will automatically break their Posture, allowing you to perform a Plunging Deathblow on your way back down. Additionally, while slightly more difficult to pull off, you can also perform a Plunging Deathblow if you jump towards them while they are not attacking. Likewise, a single toss from the Loaded Shuriken will be enough to knock them off the wall, once again leaving them vulnerable to a Plunging Deathblow.

![](images/6f9178f33c67e372efe6113b442faa0d61643d946f37cad90befe0e15be9c779.jpg)  
Centipedes possess the ability to crawl on walls.

![](images/4bb329845b1786e1266afb9da20f4f9c70c064b29aa0a57f5269d199d497037e.jpg)  
Centipedes are primarily reliant on setting the battlefield ablaze with their firebombs, so make sure you are packing some Dousing Powder in case you need it.

![](images/eebca949e33709c3eeea51f4126adecddd8e8944bb1a148619858773967961bc.jpg)  
Jumping towards a Centipede will open them up for a Plunging Deathblow.

# Seeker

Kongo</td><td>87</td><td>35</td></tr><tr><td colspan="3">Seeker (Psychic) ▪ Basic Info</td></tr><tr><td>Location</td><td>Skill EXP</td><td>Sen</td></tr><tr><td>Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo</td><td>87</td><td>35</td></tr><tr><td colspan="3">Dojun ▪ Basic Info</td></tr><tr><td>Location</td><td>Skill EXP</td><td>Sen</td></tr></table>

While the Seekers of Senpou Temple spend the majority of their time perusing enlightenment and immortality, each is still well trained in the Senpou style of martial arts. This fighting style is centered around quick evasive movements that lead to sudden, powerful blows. Even one-on-one, the melee fighters can quickly bring you down if you aren't consistent with your deflects and Mikiri Counters, especially if they consume a Sugar beforehand to boost their stats. However, you'll most often find Seekers in close proximity to each other and will often be forced to fight several at a time. Enduring the combination of lethal strikes, wide staff swings, and raining firebombs can be a struggle for even the most seasoned shinobi.

They do have a glaring weakness, however-a single hit from the Divine Abduction Arm Tool will instantly spirit away any Seeker you encounter, leaving only their Sen and items behind. If you can properly time your attack, this can be used to eliminate massive groups of them in one fell swoop. Likewise, using the Living Force ability to apply the powers of Divine Abduction to your blade will cause any Seeker that takes a direct hit from it to vanish from the battlefield. While it can be a bit of a detour, taking the time to get this Prosthetic Tool before facing these foes can reduce them from a threat to a nuisance. However, there may come times when using Divine Abduction won't be an option, especially as the process of using the Tool can be interrupted. If you are unprepared to defend yourself from them directly, they can still bring you down with brutal efficiency.

![](images/a9a7d4ce3c94884cb26fc30679507577129344b09c14a07fbea915ebb7ea7623.jpg)

# Seeker (Bo Staff)

Seekers armed with Bo Staffs will fend you off with a combination of broad swings and powerful thrusting attacks with considerable reach. Their defense does have its weaknesses, though—these Seekers will always deflect a third consecutive hit and respond with a quick hit followed by a thrusting Perilous Attack. If you manage to guard or deflect the first hit, you can then respond to the predictable Perilous Attack with a Mikiri Counter, all but ensuring a Posture break. If you're struggling to find an opening, a handful of the Shinobi Firecrackers followed up with a Chasing Slice will often allow you to close in. They'll also sometimes use an Ungo's Sugar to strengthen their defense against your attacks.

![](images/80302eb4706a1d48823ec3b5d8c02bf9b3e1626f41ff6659f802757710da25d1.jpg)

Seekers equipped with Bo Staffs can use them to vault up before delivering a brutal overhead slam.

# Seeker (Fists)

Unarmed Seekers are perhaps the most capable bare-handed fighters you'll commonly encounter. They can deliver powerful combos which can be devastating if each hit connects. Their most dangerous move sees them cross their arms to take a defensive stance and wait for you to approach. Once you enter their range, they'll abruptly lunge at you and perform a grab that requires precise timing to dodge sideways up close. If they start this stance at range it's often easier to jump or dodge away from them until they cancel the stance on their own. In addition, despite being unarmed, their dexterity will still allow them to guard and even deflect many of your blows with their hands alone. This defense does have its limits, though; once you land the first hit, you'll be able to keep up your offense until you break their Posture.

They are all but defenseless against the hefty attacks of the Loaded Axe, which can often break their Posture in a single swing, especially when accompanied by a follow-up Fang and Blade attack. Likewise, while their full combos can deal serious damage, there's often pauses between each hit that will give you a good chance to properly time your deflects. This, combined with their low Posture, often means that you can easily bring them down with consecutive deflects over the course of a single combo if you stay attentive. If you retreat to somewhere that still gives them a clear line of sight of you, such as a tree branch, they'll begin to throw sturdy projectiles at you to force you to either escape entirely, or return to the battlefield. Lastly, they may take a moment in combat to consume an Ako's Sugar to bolster their damage output. If you fight the surgeon Dojun over the course of your journey, you'll find that his fighting style is identical to these warriors with the added weakness of his Red-Eyes making him weak to fire. Note that Divine Abduction will not spirit him away.

# Seeker (Psychic)

These shrouded Seekers pose little threat one-on-one. They have no quick attacks to interrupt you with and little Vitality or Posture. They also have poor defense, making them very easy to cut down, even with low Attack Power. As is often the case, encountering them within groups makes them much more of a threat. With other enemies to distract you, they'll be able to safely lob paper fire bombs in your direction. Once they've been thrown, they will slowly proceed to home in on you. These bombs won't explode if they touch

![](images/0cbe4279c296679e8434bc6c08c4cf6e93595c6bf6566a1b96983fa2770850ef.jpg)  
The firebombs thrown by Psychic Seekers will reach and home in on you, even if you try to hide on rooftops.

![](images/710bef6bf41b5f163c2f503f97633c4fd0977f844c0249df15d405f531724c5e.jpg)

you, though; they will land on the ground near your feet and explode into a massive and powerful fireball after a brief pause. Given the small, floaty nature of the bombs, they can be easy to miss in the heat of combat. Fortunately, since they won't detonate if you touch them, you can often charge these Seekers early with little opposition and prevent them from littering the battlefield with their explosives while you handle the more capable warriors nearby.

![](images/8362b32996940db9c7b7ce25abc401794859bd5546969ee38cc183b6b6b689b6.jpg)  
Psychic Seekers are not completely defenseless in close range. While very rare, they can sometimes use a straightforward two hit fist combo that ends with a jumping kick

# Sunken Valley Clan (Rifle)

![](images/2f5d175c716fe368b144d0eb867a8d323463403b7b5f9a573aaad8f39bc730b8.jpg)

These marksmen are immensely skilled, and can deal significant damage from extremely long range once they've noticed you. Of all the enemies you'll face, very few are as difficult to approach using stealth. When dealing with Valley Clan members, you should always assume they will spot you before you can reach them, unless you're approaching from a particularly obscured route. Even If you do manage to close the range, you'll find that they still pose a serious threat. They'll fire their rifle shots in rapid succession and also have access to melee attacks, including a thrusting Perilous Attack.

Among their weaknesses are the fact that you can take advantage of Mikiri Counters against their Perilous Attacks, and that they lack the ability to guard against thrusting attacks. It's possible to hit their guard once to provoke them into attempting a thrust, and then use a Mikiri Counter to quickly deplete their Posture. Additionally, a single hit from the Loaded Axe or a full combo from Sabimaru will be able to break their Posture with ease. Of course, you still have the ability to deflect any of their attacks, including the shots, and while their odd attack timings may make it difficult to defend all of them, dodging sideways to avoid their bullets always remains an option..

![](images/4b75ba4bde803669488a80e2e056363b624023c5ad81fe0287b27a32fdedf047.jpg)

When they crouch down before firing, the shot will track sideways movement perfectly, even if you are sprinting. Either guard/deflect or time a precise sideways dodge to avoid it.

![](images/03e783525736c9b522245f4bdeba1ea14a81b84e88014ef394b662c7aa98b41e.jpg)

Sunken Valley Clan snipers often stand watch from vantage points that allow them to attack you from well outside of your range.

# Valley Monkey

The Monkeys of the Sunken Valley rely on overwhelming you, both with their numbers and their agility. Only on rare occasions will you encounter these animals one-on-one. Instead, you'll usually enter combat with hordes of Monkeys that will immediately begin to swarm around you, each looking for a chance to score a quick hit with a projectile or a lunging attack. Few of their attacks will deal significant damage on their own, but they will often come in such rapid succession that it can easily whittle you down while disorienting you with their speedy movement. The Katana-wielding Monkey especially can cause significant damage if it catches you unaware.

Luckily, they all share some core weaknesses. Each has low Vitality and Posture with very few direct defenses from your blade, and a single deflect from any melee attack they throw at you will immediately break their Posture. Additionally, a single normal toss from the Spinning Shuriken is enough to completely drain their Vitality, or drain their Posture if they guard it. Likewise, their beastly nature means that they can be easily intimidated by the Shinobi Firecracker, which will instantly daze them and break their Posture. The Flame Vent can apply Burn to them immediately, while the constant blaze from the Okinaga's Flame Vent is an excellent way to take care of groups. It's also worth keeping in mind that, once you acquire it, the use of the Finger Whistle can pit Valley Monkeys against each other, taking attention away from you in the process. The combination of these tools can allow you to clear out even massive groups of Valley Monkeys with almost no resistance.

# Valley Monkey (Bare Hands)

These are the most common variety of Valley Monkeys you'll encounter, both because they're the most numerous in the wild and because each of their armed counterparts essentially turns into this once they've thrown away their weapons. While their flailing attacks and pounces may not be very powerful, lacking even the ability to knock you down on their own, their swipes can quickly rack up damage if you're not careful. Additionally, they possess the ability to throw dirt in your direction that will briefly incapacitate you if it hits. Their most powerful attack, an aerial belly flop, can be countered by jumping towards it while it's airborne and performing an Anti-air Deathblow. Be careful however, as they will be able to damage and interrupt you as soon as they begin their decent. Otherwise, their complete inability to defend against your blade and their low Vitality should allow you to cut them down with ease.

![](images/cd2c9cf9bc2e0de5615a73ae2763393e4c8cf2de1767fe8d88ab70d0c5a067a3.jpg)  
A Valley Monkey's belly flop attack can be countered with an anti-air Deathblow.

# Valley Monkey (Matchlock Rifle)

Valley Monkeys armed with Guns will always try to keep their distance from you, even jumping across massive distances to escape, making for one of the most unpredictable encounters you'll have. Once they feel like they're safe, they'll take aim and fire away, only having to take a moment to reload after 3 shots. At mid-range, they will continue to try to avoid you with a series of jumping shots that will carry them a considerable distance away from you, making it difficult to close in. Once you have, though, they'll attempt to fight you off with quick swipes and an overhead slam from their rifle. This latter attack will cause the rifle to explode, dealing sizable damage to anything nearby and destroying the rifle, leaving the monkey to fight bare-handed. A few Shuriken from afar will break their Posture, or you can easily overwhelm them with basic attacks at close range.

# Valley Monkey (Katana)

No other Valley Monkey can deal as much damage on their own as this one. In particular, its 5-hit slashing combo can deal brutal damage if each of its swings connect. Thankfully, this also gives you plenty of opportunities to deflect an attack and break their Posture for a Deathblow. They can overwhelm you by approaching very quickly, using a series of agile jumps and slashes, especially in groups. To add to this, if you continually stay out of its range, it will eventually get frustrated and attempt to throw its Katana at

you, becoming bare-handed in the process. If you can manage to avoid it long enough, this can be a good way to significantly reduce the danger it poses. It's worth noting that these are the only Valley Monkeys that can guard against your blade to any degree. Their low Posture still makes them easy to overpower, though, and they cannot guard against thrusting attacks.

# Valley Monkey (Poison/Bare Hands)

These Monkeys behave almost identically to bare-handed Valley Monkeys. They perform roughly the same attacks, share all the same weaknesses, and are equally as aggressive. The difference lies in the properties of the attacks themselves. Every attack involving their fists will cause Poison build-up, even when guarded or deflected, and they no longer have the ability to throw dirt. Instead, once they step into the poisonous muck of Bodhisattva Valley, they will frequently attempt to fling a wave of swamp water at you, which will almost instantly Poison you if you're standing close enough. To avoid this, always do your best to face them only on dry land.

![](images/c67cbfb984e8863e81b70fcc14c00bc046a4b1235156b42234e41ad045cc80f1.jpg)  
Be wary of the Valley Monkey's ability to weaponize the poison water of the Valley.

# Valley Monkey (Poison/Gun)

Much like the Valley Monkeys that reside above them, the Monkeys of Bodhisattva Valley have also managed to acquire firearms and will employ them in identical fashion. They will fire on you from afar while leaping away whenever you begin to close in, and will slam their rifle into the ground once cornered, exploding the weapon in the process. However, once they become unarmed, they will behave exactly like any other unarmed Valley Monkey and continue to try to fend you off with poisonous attacks.

![](images/7283eb3c391a35023d3f9aa5eccb6341d8712b0da6a036206b4201a2a421520c.jpg)  
Valley Monkeys armed with Guns can sacrifice their weapons for an explosive close range attack.

# Rock Diver

![](images/39839fda4cde03f6f258cb63efe825efaee84c9e940a8f5746ffd9078bb2de65.jpg)

These foes are permanently encased within a single spot of a wall, only able to dig out of it up to their waist to attack you. Watch for the Danger Symbol to indicate when they're about to appear. After attacking them, they'll retreat into the wall again, gaining resistance to damage as they disappear. They can then appear again from the same spot or from other areas of the wall nearby; their appearance is always based on your proximity and there are limited locations from which they can appear. Their Perilous Attacks are a fast thrust used when they first exit the wall, a slower thrust they can use at any time, and a seldom-used armored grab, which you can avoid by quickly dodging backwards when they suddenly fling their left hand out and attempt to snatch you.

They can guard and deflect regular attacks, but they don't attack fast enough to interrupt a continuous onslaught unless they use the grab, which is quite rare. Whirlwind Slash can let you deal continuous damage to them even when they guard, since many of their attacks are too slow to interrupt it. They also can't guard or deflect against thrust attacks. When they exit the wall they'll often perform a thrust perilous attack, which you can Mikiri Counter and punish with a thrust of your own. Lastly, they use various horizontal swings and slams from their elevated position—deflecting any of these will also give you time to land a thrust. If you deplete their Vitality, they'll disappear, but breaking their Posture causes them to retreat into the wall. Walk up to the surface they retreated into and use the Deathblow prompt to finish them for good.

# Mibu Villager

Few of the residents of Mibu Village pose a serious threat one-on-one. Each has low Vitality and Posture, near non-existent defense, and most deal little damage on their own. The real threat of these enemies, however, lies in their overwhelming numbers. You'll often be forced into fighting groups of up to six of them at a time in a variety of combinations. In addition, for each one you kill, another will rise out of the nearby ground to take its place (with the notable exception of the Knife-wielding variant). Each group has a shared life pool that will often allow you to put an end to their revivals after slaying enough Villagers, though the amount needed is dependent on the group in question.

Fortunately, the groups these Villagers like to congregate in are more often than not tightly clustered and vulnerable to a stealth-based approach. In conjunction with their poor defense, this makes them highly vulnerable to large area-of-effect attacks, such as those of the Leaping Flame, or those with massive sweeping arcs such as the Bestowal Ninjutsu. However, once the fight begins, you'll have to be wary, as their ability to re-appear can cause you to become quickly surrounded if they begin to revive close to you. The constant opportunities for Deathblows while fighting these groups of these foes makes the Breath of Life: Light skill especially useful in keeping your Vitality up.

# Vengeful Spirit Villagers

If you defeat the Corrupted Monk (Illusion) before defeating Genichiro, you'll begin to encounter Vengeful Spirit Mibu Villagers in the Sunken Valley, Abandoned Dungeon, and Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo once evening approaches. These Villagers will fight with the exact same attacks and behavior as their physical counterparts with the exception of being unable to revive once killed.

# Mibu Villager (Bamboo Spear)

Every move this Villager uses can be countered with a Mikiri or deflected to break its Posture for an easy kill. Additionally, their attacks are all slow enough that charging them with a sprinting attack will often be enough to completely overpower them. Unlike most enemies with thrusting attacks, you can guard against this foe's spear with relative safety. This doesn't mean you shouldn't take them seriously, however, as their long-range attack makes it much easier for them to land a surprise attack than most. This is especially true once you inevitably become preoccupied with other Villagers, and it will deal meaningful damage once it lands.

# Mibu Villager (Bare Hands)

When fighting bare-handed, there is very little that Villagers can do to harm you at close range. All they will be able to do is push you away and try to retreat, only dealing weak Posture damage in the process. However, you'll find that they have a few tricks up to their sleeve if you ignore them. At any time, they can fling a ladle filled with damaging liquid at you in a broad arc. Additionally, if left alone long enough they'll eventually pick up a rock that they will then either use as a bludgeoning weapon or as a projectile that can deal respectable damage. Due to their ability to deal damage at range, it's recommended that you consider taking them out with a sprinting attack as a priority when fighting groups.

![](images/b6c72f7dfc2482ffea6e03dfb9becb021d5e22531cb3b175cc936d83a6325519.jpg)  
Villagers will panic when they see fire. Fire-based Prosthetic Tools are good crowd control when facing groups.

![](images/8b153be77f14aa86fe1b490b82a77560fa566ac544bbfa38336fbcf23d1dbf7a.jpg)  
Villagers revive from specific locations in the nearby area.

# Mibu Villager (Bare Hands/Bombs)

These Villagers lie in wait in easy-to-miss corners and blind spots. Once they've noticed you, they'll begin to sluggishly throw bombs at you. These bombs will explode into an ominous cloud that will cause Terror build-up if you stand in it. If the bombs hit you directly, they'll instantly inflict a sizeable amount of Terror build-up. Fortunately, the bombs are easily avoided as long as you stay on the move; they are slow-moving enough that it's possible to avoid them even just by walking to the side. After you've closed the distance, these Villagers may attempt to weakly push you away or fling a ladle of damaging liquid at you, much like the Bare-Handed Villagers. They will, however, be unable to put up any serious defense against your blade, allowing you to cut them down in no more than two slashes.

![](images/53f0557ae1b82d0d5e9d08d1c6a4827368da9997a2c73ac0d52a7f10a1b6c6a0.jpg)  
The cloud produced by a terror bomb will linger for a moment after exploding.

# Mibu Villager (Knife)

No other Villager can deal as much direct damage as the knife-wielding variant. Their general attacks are sluggish and don't reach very far, while leaving them vulnerable to a counter-attack. If, however, you get caught in either their combo or their grab, they may very well manage to kill you before you have a chance to respond. Each hit of their primary combo deals a hefty amount of damage, while the grab will most likely kill you on the spot if you haven't strongly improved your Vitality or were injured beforehand. Luckily, a single Spinning Shuriken hit from the Gouging Top is enough to put them down from a safe distance. Also worth noting is that, unlike the other Villagers, they will not revive when killed until you've rested at a Sculptor's Idol or die.

![](images/9da61505f16b69bbd3cd9de01cf91e307a93f8e4d19e4e96e7c0098528d106dd.jpg)  
Keep alert for the Knife-wielding Villagers deadly grab attack.

![](images/d01591dfe840d80e5dae1a7c99b703f86de783cabb27069ab2fbad635002b0be.jpg)

# Mibu Villager (Hoe)

The most dangerous tool in their arsenal is a hefty two-hit combo that can deal respectable damage if it hits. It has a sluggish start-up period, however, and can easily be avoided by simply walking to the side. Additionally, if you manage to deflect even one of its attacks, its Posture will instantly break. As is often the case, their true danger lies in their ability to keep you preoccupied while their more dangerous allies close in on you.

![](images/074df95c000a65d9f3f2f5634840430dab0f734d9bed14bf464beec825562d30.jpg)  
Villagers can erupt from the ground and try to hold you in place. Mash the face and shoulder buttons to break free faster.

# Mibu Villager (Loom)

What makes the Loom-wielding villagers stand out is the huge, sweeping arc of its weapon, allowing it deal damage across a wide area. While its weapon may not reach as far as one might think, it's sweeping horizontal attacks can still ensure that it deals respectable damage to any foe in the immediate area. It's best to interrupt their slow swings with a fast attack.

# Mibu Villager (Rake)

This Villager relies on a moderately-ranged, multi-hit combo to harass you. Its primary distinction lies in the combos themselves, as this Villager's attacks are unusually fast and are comprised of three hits. Fortunately, any one of these attacks can be deflected to allow for an instantaneous Deathblow.

# Infested Seeker (Parasite)

Infested Seeker (parasite) - Basic Info

# Overview

Infested Seekers are host to a parasite that bursts out of them when you approach. It's the parasite that performs the bulk of the attacks you must deal with; it uses long-reaching, lunging attacks from afar, and a fast Counter Slam combo up close, making it dangerous to approach when they're not recovering from an attack. The Infested Seeker's high Vitality and Posture, combined with the parasite's dangerous close-range attacks, makes fighting this enemy a ranged battle of attrition. Deflecting many of the parasite's attacks will stun it briefly and let you attack it directly to deal higher damage; a thrust, Flame Vent, or the first hit of the Mortal Blade combo are

# Strategy

If you guard at a step dodge's distance away, they'll often use the Parasite Rushdown, making it easy to predict and deflect the final hit to damage the parasite. Make sure to keep alert for the Parasite Lasso. You can also use hit-and-run tactics, moving in to trigger an attack and then retreating to two step dodge's distance away from them; most of their attacks will miss, allowing you to sprint into a thrust attack. Both of their grabs have long recovery periods, so

# Attacks

# Parasitic Rushdown

# PROPERTIES CA

Parasite raises up on Seekers right side, then quickly lunges forward three times; two quick lunges, then a short delay before final lunge. Deflecting final attack stuns parasite. Often follows-up final hit with further attacks on guard or miss.

# Counter Slam combo

# PROPERTIES CA

Parasite quickly moves to the left side of the ascetic and slams the ground in front of it, follows up with either a long lunging attack or Parasitic Rushdown. Very fast attack often used to knock you back when you approach. Deflecting the lunging attack will stun Parasite.

![](images/11db04dbc83417b614d262221bd9f72c836735948dbb132fb8caf239671caada.jpg)

good options here. They're weak to Fire, and a single Flame Vent can apply Burn to them, letting you hit them a couple of times before needing to back off again. Their two Perilous Attacks complement each other: the short-ranged Parasitic Constrictor can suck your Vitality to replenish their own, while the longer-ranged Parasite Lasso is intended to drag you within range of the Parasite Constrictor. Their immobility makes it very easy to back away to regenerate Posture, Heal, or begin long-ranged attacks of your own. Infested Seekers can't be killed permanently until you have the Mortal Blade; after killing them, stand near their corpse and you'll see a second Deathblow prompt to finish them for good.

make sure to punish with a thrust when they miss; if you've jumped the Parasitic Lasso, you still have time to hit them once after landing. If you have the appropriate mid-air Skills, you can also jump towards them and hit them with a Combat Art or Prosthetic Tool before they can react—Ichimonji: Double is ideal here. Lastly, the Divine Abduction Tool can be charged out of their reach and unleashed after sprinting into range to immediately Deathblow them.

# Parasitic Constrictor

# PROPERTIES Grab|AA

Seeker reaches out as the parasite attempts to catch you in a constrictor hold at close range. Sucks your Vitality away and regenerates the Seekers Vitality bar. Quickly step dodge backwards when you see the Danger Symbol up close and punish with thrust.

# Parasitic Lasso

# PROPERTIES Grab, Sweep

Parasite attempts to circle around a large area in front of the Seeker and drag you in. If this attack connects, the next attack is an immediate Parasite Constrictor. Jump to avoid. If caught, quickly jump backwards to avoid the second grab.

# Overview

These traditional samurai mostly use straightforward vertical slashes and rising sword attack combos, mixed with a long-reaching thrust attack. They guard and deflect frequently, but most of their vertical attacks can be step dodged sideways, leaving them open. Beware that if you let them continuously hit your guard, they'll often continue battering it down with fast attacks. After some of their attacks, they can even attempt to retaliate after you deflect them, although a counter-slash will interrupt any such attempt. Since they deal a lot of Posture damage, guarding them isn't advised—it's better to rely on step dodges or deflects.

When their Posture gets low, they'll begin using a Posture-recovery stance that will regenerate some of their Posture upon completion; you'll need to quickly interrupt them with an attack when they raise their sword above their head and start channeling a white aura. If you need an easy Deathblow, the Divine Abduction Tool will allow you to Backstab Deathblow them, and they can be fooled by resurrecting yourself after dying, unless you're right beside them—you just need to wait until they finish sheathing their sword before they turn away. The Fencer (Student) has less attacks than the regular

![](images/c5ee6a0c23790c500cd808207c3048d07eb8835992538d9b42d8dfe739909c04.jpg)

Fencer; they're unable to use the rest of the attacks after the first slash of the Delayed Vertical Slash combo, most of the stand-alone variations of that combo, or the 5-Hit Advancing Chops. They can occasionally retreating slash into thrust, so keep alert.

![](images/d663400d7671192030d868ac63c0c4263cee6798cd9230ba17d1bad370007e3a.jpg)  
You'll encounter Vengeful Spirit versions of these enemies later in the game if you defeat Genichiro before the illusory Corrupted Monk.

# Fencer (Defensive Seigan Stance) — Strategy

If you hold your guard a step dodge's distance away, he will often use the slow-to-start Delayed Vertical Slash; since he only uses the first hit, you can quickly dodge away then hit him with a thrust or even an Ichimonji of your own. Keep alert, though; he can also start the Lunging Thrust and occasionally other attacks. If you see the Danger Symbol, prepare to Mikiri Counter, otherwise dodge away from his other attacks. Resist attacking his guard too aggressively, since he uses the Fast Lunging Thrust after deflecting you and can mix this with the Posture-damaging Hilt Strike Slash—unless you are very confident using Mikiri Counters at short notice, it's dangerous to attack him until he deflects.

![](images/0553dc9f9cf627b87c7879abfb2206d0dcfb1969e5f279aaafc187f19f98978c.jpg)

You can tell they're about to use the Lunging Thrust when you see the danger symbol and sword shine on their weapon.

A safer way to pressure him at close range is to hit his guard once to provoke a counter-attack, then deflect or step dodge it. He'll react with the Counter Overshoulder Chop, the Counter Rising Slash, or will back away and perform the Lunging Thrust. The chops and slashes are the most frequently-used responses, and can be performed from either side of his body, but they have the same deflect and dodge timings. You can either deflect them and counter-slash yourself once, or dodge sideways and then punish until he starts guarding again. Repeating this guard reaction loop is an effective way to take him down quickly. The Lunging Thrust is rarer than the other two attacks, but if he suddenly backs away, prepare to Mikiri Counter.

![](images/5b9b8f5b8d5c642ee70ffe5eb96d609af77564ff4bfb39d28c074e4f3d51980d.jpg)

# Fencer (Offensive Seigan Stance) — Strategy

This Fencer is capable of performing the full Delayed Vertical Slash combo, unlike the defence stance Fencer. This makes it dangerous to provoke him, since the combo deals a lot of Posture damage and the Perilous Attack thrust at the end is very fast. He can use individual parts of this combo on their own as well, so keep an eye out for him starting a combo with any of those hits, since they all lead into the same thrust. He can also use his 5-Hit Advancing

# Fencer (Seigan Stance) - Attacks

# Hilt Strike Slash

PROPERTIES CA | E(Deflect)

Hits forward with the hilt of their sword, then swings into a delayed rising slash with the sword.Slash deals high Posture damage and has tricky deflect timing. Step dodge sideways to avoid slash and punish.

# Fast Lunging Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust | AA | Reaction Only

Very quick lunging thrust used after they deflect you. Watch for the Danger Symbol and the shine on their sword when you see them deflect. Mikiri Counter as soon as the sword shine flash is brightest.

# Counter Overshoulder Chop

PROPERTIES Reaction Only | E(Guard) | P(Deflect)

A single over the shoulder two handed chop. Can be used from over the left or right shoulder with same deflect timing. Deflect (or dodge sideways) just as sword passes over his shoulder.

# Counter RisingSlash

PROPERTIES Reaction Only | E(Guard) | P(Deflect)

# Overview

Taro Troops have strong super armor on their slow and damaging attacks, many of which have long delays that can make them tricky to deflect. They often have a long recovery period afterwards, so hit-and-run strategies are reliable against them. They have high Vitality and Posture, but one of their attacks gives you an opportunity to deplete their Posture quite quickly.

When they thump their weapons on the ground and yell, that means they've started their Perilous Attack Berserker Rage. They repeatedly attack the area in front of them blindly with no regard for your current position, building up their Posture during the attack and leaving them exhausted for a while after it's over. Backing off when you see this attack and sprinting around to attack their back is a great opportunity to deal a lot of Vitality and Posture damage. Landing enough hits in a short duration will break their super armor and stun them. They often begin their berserker rage attacks after this

![](images/ef1b641029f9918371537e9fba0d0eb9f6663d8659cc9a4636611401122cb235.jpg)  
When they thump the ground like this directly after a stun, they're starting their dangerous berserker rage attacks.

stun, so make sure to back off if you interrupt them. Hit them while they're blinded by Firecrackers or Fistfuls of Ash to easily stun them and provoke their berserker rage attacks.

The Divine Abduction tool will allow you to Backstab Deathblow them, and if you die, they won't notice your resurrection once they've turned away, unless you're right beside them. The Temple Service Taro Troop can be killed instantly with the Divine Abduction tool without needing to Deathblow them.

The Mibu Village Taro Troop will panic when you use Fire-based Prosthetic Tools, giving you a long window to deal damage to them. Some Taro Troops wear an armored chest plate that greatly reduces damage taken from the front—you can strip it off with a single pull attack from the Loaded Spear.

![](images/a2676a8c424b7d6b09526ef743ac87899c30b6a284941d0602ad4e834871d52d.jpg)  
Some Taro Troop members have damage reducing crude armor chest plates that can be stripped with a pull of the Loaded Spear.

# Taro Troop (Wooden Mallet) — Strategy

Keep a step dodge's distance away to bait these brutes into attacking, and then dodge away and retaliate with a thrust or fast Combat Art when they miss. Their horizontal swing at close range can lead to an opportunity to attack; deflecting this swing will push them off balance for a while. Their two vertical slam combos both guard crush with their first hit, so it's a bad idea to hold your guard up close. The punches in the Vertical Slam and Punches combo travel forward quite far, so guard if you see the first slam miss within a step dodge's distance away. If they begin the leaping attack at close range, you'll need to dodge to the left when they're halfway down to ensure it doesn't catch you.

# Taro Troop (Kanabo) — Strategy

While this variety of Taro Troop shares a lot of their vertical slam attacks with the Taro Troop (Wooden Mallet), they have more horizontal swings to watch out for, including a fast left-to-right swing, often used to punish over-aggression at close range. When using hit-and-run tactics against him, limit yourself to a single thrust before backing away again. His Swing and Sweep can be jump-kick

![](images/559b7687cb7225f75df6627cbff5782d9035f9bdc133deb7832fa89d7fb110fc.jpg)  
Be careful of the Vertical Slam and Punch combo when attempting to retreat, since they lunge forward a long distance during the punch attacks.

countered, but doing so won't stop his follow-up vertical swing; it's better to dodge the first hit backwards, since he won't use the rest of the combo if you're far away. He has a different variant of the berserker rage that isn't a Perilous Attack: the Berserk Swing. Sprint away from him until he misses, then run back in and attack him while he's hunched over and recovering.

# Taro Troop (Greatshield) — Strategy

You can't easily apply hit-and-run tactics here, since their great-shields protect them from most frontal damage, and they turn very quickly during their various close-range shield pushes and slam attacks. From far away, they'll perform the long-reaching Shield Charge, which can easily track your movement. They lack any variant of the berserker rage, and you can break their shield with the Loaded Axe for an immediate Deathblow. This can take a few

# Taro Troop (Bell) — Strategy

This Taro Troop's bell is attached to a rope they use to swing it around, but only the bell itself can hit you. If you stay a step dodge's distance away from them and guard, they'll often try a long-range overhead bell throw. You can dodge towards them to make the bell miss, giving you time to land a few blows, but be careful since they can hit you with the bell as they reel it back in—step dodge to the right to avoid it before backing away again. The Circular Bell Swing covers a huge area around them, but you can dodge forwards after the second swing and attack them until they recover. Be careful of guarding this attack at close range, since the second swing can guard crush and push you into the third swing, causing you to get hit. If they raise the bell directly above their head in both hands, you can expect the Bell Slam grab Perilous Attack. They'll sometimes use this instead of going berserk after you make them flinch. They have a non-Perilous Attack version of the Berserker Rage that involves slamming the ground with the bell and then using a few over-the-shoulder bell tosses that give the combo extended range—keep sprinting in a circle around them at a distance until they stop, before moving around to their back to retaliate.

# Taro Troop - Attacks

Axe blows, depending your Attack Power—blinding them with Fistfuls of Ash is a good way to keep them locked down until it's broken, while Fang and Blade helps conserve Emblems. You can also stay just over three step dodges away from them to bait them into using their Shield Charge, then quickly hit them with the Axe as it recovers.

![](images/41e771e1d1238dbe6abe7618a54147b3d5aadcf2334b67b364e893de586b0d45.jpg)  
Forward dodging through the third swing of the Circular Bell Swing will give you a chance to hit them before they recover.

# Overview

Fighting this enemy requires you to negotiate his different scatter-shot attacks to close in and deal damage. Once you are close enough, you need to dodge and counter-attack his melee attacks and chase after him when he attempts to roll away from you. These enemies run and roll around, firing off shots from their homemade scatter-shot cannons. The spread of the bullets will differ depending on the attack; the horizontal spread is low and can be jumped over, while the vertical spread is higher and should be dodged sideways. His scatter-shot attacks deal a lot of Posture damage, so it's better to focus on avoiding them rather than guarding. He has trouble hitting you with them when you're up close, and he'll respond with armored melee attacks after guarding your attacks, or will attempt to Roll Shot. You can use the forward momentum of a thrust to stick close to him as he tries to roll away from you, but be careful not to thrust when he's about to shoot.

The Flame Vent and Loaded Umbrella are useful against him; you can apply Burn with a single Flame Vent blast to stun him briefly, and the Loaded Umbrella can absorb his bullets and let you retaliate.

# Strategy

Knowing which type of scatter-shot spread he's going to use when approaching is the key to getting close to him without taking damage. The spread will be horizontal when he fires from the hip while standing, rolls backwards or forwards, or after running to the side, so you can jump towards him and use mid-air Skills such as Flame

with Projected Force at range, but it takes several shots to charge up. The Divine Abduction tool will allow you to Stealth Deathblow him, and he won't notice you resurrecting once he's turned away.

![](images/c05f26fa3b11ede0708681fc106131360fc339f1c475c62b32f3b33aa061549c.jpg)  
You can jump over his horizontal buckshot to close in on him.

Vent or Ichimonji as you reach him. If he rolls sideways or brings the gun up to his shoulder, then the spread will be vertical, so dodge diagonally to continue your approach. Attack with a thrust as you close in, then watch how he reacts. If he immediately starts a Horizontal Swipe, you can dodge backwards or deflect it and pun

ish. If he tries to evade with a Roll Shot, you can chase him down with another thrust and still have time to dodge the follow-up shot. If he deflects your thrust, or guards a normal attack, he'll use his Horizontal Swing, Front Kick, or Roll Shot, so stop attacking and prepare to react. The two armored melee attacks are more common than the Roll Shot when you hit his guard; take advantage of this by hitting his guard once and quickly dodging backwards to make his melee strikes miss, then punishing with a dodge counter-attack. Sometimes he will Roll Shot immediately after the Horizontal Swing, or otherwise use the Roll Shot when you are too far to chase him down safely. In this case it's often better to note which direction he rolled and use the appropriate evasion to avoid it and close in on him again, rather than try to chase him down with a thrust, or you may risk taking scatter-shot to the face.

![](images/ff8c2a28d5cb1968772870029e241360335e50cfc40bd56bd1b8b24817ee5c05.jpg)

His vertical buckshot attacks can hit you if you jump towards him. Dodge sideways to avoid them.

# Overview

Armed with massive hand cannons, this enemy will constantly barrage you with long-distance Cannon Fire. The cannonballs produce an explosion upon impact—this blast cannot be guarded or deflected unless you use the Loaded Umbrella. The shot follows a parabolic arc and takes a while to travel to you, so as long as you keep sprinting it will land behind you. The explosion deals less damage at the edge of its radius; if he fires a shot at close range and it's too late to sprint away, you can quickly jump away from the impact point to reduce the damage.

When you get close, he'll grab his cannon with both hands and use armored melee attacks to push you away. The Horizontal Swing pushes you away when guarded, while the dangerous vertical slam is part of his Vertical Slam Blast attack. Deflecting his melee attacks will knock him off balance and stun him for a while. A single burst from the Flame Vent will apply Burn and stun him, allowing you to land several more hits. The Loaded Umbrella can let you absorb his Cannon Fire and charge up a Projected Force to deal heavy Vitality and Posture damage. Attacks with strong stun, such as Ichimonji or the Loaded Axe, can interrupt his armored melee swings. If you're in need of an easy Deathblow, he's also susceptible to Divine Abduction and doesn't notice resurrecting.

# Strategy

If you start the fight far away, you'll need to be constantly moving at high speed as you approach in order to avoid his deadly Cannon Fire. Use the environment and jump, grapple, or sprint to him as quickly as you can, being careful not to run straight into the path of a cannon ball. Once you're close, he'll start using his armored melee attacks. You can dodge both of them backwards, but the Horizontal Swing is difficult to punish with Vitality damage unless you dodge towards his back, since he guards quickly again from the front. Be very cautious of the Vertical Slam Blast; the point-blank Cannon Fire at the end of this combo can easily deal heavy damage if you're caught by surprise. It isn't an armored attack, so make sure to quickly interrupt it after guarding or dodging the slam. If you're stuck in an enclosed area with this enemy, your best bet is to focus on deflecting his melee attacks—this can give you a chance to land a strong attack, such as a Flame Vent or a fully charged Ichimonji: Double.

# Overview

The Elder Monkey constantly moves around while fighting—he's able to sprint or hop towards you to start his attacks, which means they can reach you quickly from a good distance away. He can also perform retreating slashes that leave him out of reach, and many of his sword swings involve multiple quick hits, so if he breaks your Posture with the first strike he'll hit you with the second. Many of his leaping attacks have super armor, and he guards and deflects frequently, so it's tricky to whittle down his Vitality using hit-and-run tactics—try to use attacks that can penetrate guard, such as Whirlwind Slash, or Shadowrush.

Deflecting his horizontal and rising slashes won't always stop his attacks, but his leaping attacks will usually signal the end of his attack strings (with the exception of the Leap and Sweep). There's several ways to reduce his Vitality; you can punish after he misses a huge blow, use attacks that deal Piercing damage, or blind him with Ash/ Firecrackers. The Flame Vent will apply Burn immediately and let you land several blows, while Firecrackers will damage his Posture and stun him for several seconds—combine this with Combat Arts

# Strategy

At the start of the fight you need to start reducing his Vitality quickly, so that he doesn't keep regenerating his Posture. Blind him with a Fistful of Ash or Firecrackers, then switch to the Flame Vent to set him on fire, and then land a few blows while he's stunned. Ash or Firecrackers will also allow you to run around to his back

![](images/967965e31a33f30dc66c7773dbe81bff1774e13df69ff6a661123cf21f5f229c.jpg)

that deal high Posture damage, such as a charged Ichimonji: Double to finish him very quickly. Divine Abduction doesn't allow you to Backstab Deathblow him, and he'll notice when you resurrect, even at a distance. When he reaches low health, he'll add an extra jumping attack to the end of his Monkey Flurry; jump towards him when he winds up this attack for an Anti-air Deathblow opportunity.

![](images/bca5710bf6d1d5578d8815305506e6c5358897afc3e8e9df1595fc3699929fc1.jpg)  
His deadly Double Horizontal Slashes deal massive damage and their long range makes it easy for him to catch you with them if you aren't watching out for them.

and hit him twice before he can turn around again. Dodging his vertical and jumping attacks leaves him vulnerable longer than dodging his horizontal attacks, and it's worth remembering that you can interrupt the sweep in his Leap and Sweep combo. Staying far away from him will often provoke his Double Horizontal

Slashes or Rising Slash combos; keep backing away until he misses the last attack and punish. If you're having trouble hitting him in time, consider piercing Combat Arts or Shadowrush; if you back away immediately after these attacks he'll be unable to hit you afterwards. After you've reduced his Vitality, begin striking his guard to deal Posture damage, then quickly step dodge backwards to avoid retaliation. It's not safe to dodge backwards if he deflects you, since some of his attacks will reach, so keep alert when you see deflection sparks.

![](images/67c5b18c44bff9f56c3e1dedd9cbef84cfe2d48afc4230b1dd9ccbd25797e7ba.jpg)

The Leap and Sweep has spectacular forward range even though he hops so far away from you before the leap. He can still hit you even at this distance.

A Spear Adept spends a lot of time moving and leaping around the area, throwing Shuriken and using long-ranged attacks. You can throw a Shuriken at him whenever he's airborne during his attacks to deal critical Posture damage and knock him to the ground. His attacks can cover a lot of ground, so quickly guard if he begins one on the ground at long range. They also frequently cause him to rush straight past you when he recovers, leaving him out of reach. In closed environments these attacks that rush past you will often break your lock-on, so try to draw him to more open areas. He has two long-ranged sweeps that can easily catch you, so always jump

![](images/d26298b5b65c66a23842a6c1dcae9141b8e1b1b127d4442a9acd6003aaf82ecb.jpg)  
He frequently tries to Glaive Vault over you after deflecting you....

# Strategy

It's difficult to make him guard and to deal Posture damage effectively until you've whittled down his Vitality. He cannot punish Whirlwind Slash even if he deflects it, so it's a very useful way to reduce his Vitality; its Piercing property lets you use it whenever he finishes a combo or attack. He often performs his Glaive Vault after deflecting you—this gives you a chance to knock him out of the sky with a Shuriken. If he runs toward you and uses his forward flip slash, you can interrupt it with a quick attack to immediately knock him down, and then hit him several times before he recovers. Once you've reduced his Vitality to below  $75\%$ , keep an eye out for his Vertical Buzzcutter Dive; an Anti-air Deathblow after he leaps into the air will let you finish the fight immediately. Once you've reduced his Posture regeneration, you can start using basic attacks to build up Posture damage. Jump kicking his sweeps can deal good Posture damage, but the distance they cover will often send him dashing out of range, underneath you. The dashing sweep he often uses after his Glaive Vault will always travel a fixed distance of two

# Overview

This strong variant of the Lone Shadows has some key differences that change the way you'll need to fight him. Firstly, he's a lot less aggressive, lacking many of the gap-closing moves Lone Shadows use, such as the Flying Spin Kick or the Backwards Spin Kick combo (although he still has the Lunging Diagonal Slash). He also

![](images/f0f15c9b3e8b2d7cc6534ee6ee5f71e394b9912c4a8461e747ba51f7641b8933.jpg)  
Backing off and timing a Spinning Shuriken into Chasing Slice during his attack recovery is an effective way to whittle down his Vitality safely.

![](images/f7dc9e07aace8264543d7f2155f3f3903a00285890107193d74355a39e241d37.jpg)

doesn't use the Double Spin Kicks or the Leaping Hammer Kick. Many of the combos that would have a Flying Spin Kick or Leaping Hammer Kick at the end are replaced with all or part of his Vilehand Strike combo, and some of the kicks in his combo attacks are also replaced with Vilehand strikes.

![](images/8a28804bc27fb979844c4795c4beb17a7d42c5bbe69bb047a10e6312e32ccb34.jpg)  
The Spinning Right Kick has a Vilehand Strike follow-up. You can't easily damage his Vitality until you've dodged the follow-up strike.

He can react with Vilehand Strikes after guarding or deflecting you, with the latter being particularly hard to react to. The attacks he uses after guarding are more expansive; he can use a lot more combos in addition to the regular counter-attacks that other Lone Shadows use, which makes it difficult to use the guard loop strategy against him. He'll still use the Kick Rush after deflecting you, but otherwise this is the only time he uses the Thrust Kick. Keep Antidote Powder in your Quick Items in case you need it.

# Strategy

Back off to a step dodge's distance away from him, where he'll often attempt to hit you with his various two-hit slash combos or his Spinning Right Kick combo. The two-hit combos that start with a right side rising slash have a long recovery period after the second hit, which you can punish. The Spinning Right Kick combo and the DownwardsSlash combo, meanwhile, both have a Vilehand Strike follow-up that you'll need to dodge before punishing. You'll need to move backwards during his attacks to make sure you stay out of range of his second sword swipe, and if he backs off suddenly and pulls his left hand out of his robes, he'll rush towards you with the Vilehand Strike combo.

![](images/7a8d9222c4273bb75a9c7070180520a35eea0886916bc6d04c9a28495cebe997.jpg)  
There's two main two-hit combo attacks you can punish since they have no follow-ups and long recovery after the second hit. This is the Rising Slash combo....

![](images/e26d218eebcddc91038c560058ef390b1d00b5f955620f77f95af745da2ad781.jpg)  
The Downwards Slash combo also has a Vilehand Strike follow-up after the second hit you need to dodge before you can damage his Vitality.

His general passivity and lack of fast gap-closers means that he'll often slowly walk towards you if you're too far away from him, allowing him to regenerate his Posture; you need to stay close enough to provoke an attack to prevent this. He also has access to a Posture-recovering stance, so be sure to quickly interrupt it if you see it. His slow-recovering combos often allow you to punish with powerful options, such as the Flame Vent or Ichimonji: Double to damage his Posture. You can also opt to attack him from a distance with Combat Arts like Ashina Cross or Shadowrush—just watch out for the Lunging Diagonal Slash.

![](images/f95806cf16fc1ef44aaab8a9defe531b2d8c303da632fc1bf3d6d93922e643a7.jpg)  
...and this is the Lunging Rising Slash combo. You need to stay a little further away from the Lunging RisingSlash combo since it has longer range.
