# Overview

These powerful Okami Warriors have a strong command of Lightning, and are able to infuse it into their attacks. Some of these attacks are variants of moves used by the regular Okami Warriors. All their Lightning attacks are highly telegraphed by a delayed vertical leap, allowing you to use a Lightning Reversal to turn the tables, or throw a Shuriken to knock them out of the sky. They often use these Lightning attacks while at a distance, and signal them with a slow windup prior to the leap, so keep a close eye out for whenever

![](images/2b0f418f2964c28c982a4bcf903d9a07ea90d99f802f00fb07e645f0030cf894.jpg)

For most of their Lightning attacks the ideal timing to leap into the sky to perform a Lightning Reversal is just as the lightning strike from the sky hits their weapon.

they jump high into the sky. It can sometimes be useful to keep a Lightning Okami Warrior alive in order to use their Lightning attack to perform a Lightning Reversal on other nearby enemies, but you should only attempt this if you are confidently in control of the situation. Sabimaru can apply blue rust Poison to them very quickly. Keep some Eel Liver on your quick slots and take it before engaging them to reduce the damage from a missed Lightning Reversal.

![](images/78781112d4f2d8dd8f3b1dce102b1b4bcbbee999db4c24631966cb42bc9a83f2.jpg)

Their weakness to Sabimaru's blue rust Poison lets you deal high Vitality and Posture damage and stun them for a long duration after only a few blows.

# Okami Warrior (Lightning Katana) — Strategy

Unlike the regular Okami Warrior (Katana), this variant doesn't use many attacks. She favors attempting to hop out of range to use her Lightning Sword Stab. You can throw a Shuriken at her to knock her out of it, or jump and use a Lightning Reversal to stun her with her own attack. She must be at a specific range for a while before she'll use this attack; this causes her to continually hop away if you keep moving towards her. You can chase her down as she tries to escape by continuously dodging towards her. As long as you keep on top of her, she'll rarely use the Lightning Sword Stab, or most of her other attacks. She's capable of using the jumping attack combo that will continue infinitely if you keep deflecting just like the regular katana-wielding Okami Warriors, but she can mix this up with a sudden lightning cleave attack that you need to Lightning Reversal or quickly dodge sideways to avoid. Her Lightning Passage starts the same as the normal Floating Passage combo, but she leaps into the air to perform a Lightning-infused final slash.

# Okami Warrior (Lightning Halberd) — Strategy

This variant comes equipped with three new Lightning-based attacks that she'll use from a distance. The Lightning Spear Stab is executed quicker than the other two and she moves backwards during it. This can make your Lightning Reversal miss, so you'll need to jump towards her—if you're not sure which attack she's using, throw a Shuriken every time she leaps. She still has many of the naginata-wielding Okami Warrior's attacks, and you'll have to keep an eye out for many of the same Perilous Attacks. She can use her Quadruple Spinning Sweeps, her quick one-handed thrust, the jumping sky thrust reaction after deflecting her leaping vertical

![](images/2d452756f80229209c5db76e662194c9239c1812aff9b513918e58252501ec61.jpg)  
Their Lightning Spear Stab attacks much faster after the lightning strike than their other lightning attacks, so learn to recognize its distinctive leap.

![](images/ad0bcc3b5f6bd050547e479221e9a4ad626d41e43398bb91df6c7313fbfacd28.jpg)  
The long ranged Whirlwind Slash is great at catching her as she tries to hop away.

slam, and her various horizontal slashes and combos. Attempting to pressure her too much at close range can be dangerous, since she can deflect you then immediately hop backwards into her superarmored Quadruple Spinning Sweeps. If she suddenly hops away then starts spinning, immediately press jump and prepare to jump-kick. Staying away to provoke her into using her Lightning attacks, then jumping towards her to use a Lightning Reversal is easier than dealing with her various close-range attacks. Quickly follow it up with a Sabimaru combo to Poison her, and then a few more hits against her guard should break her Posture.

![](images/7aeb191638de51e1ce7929491887b13e54666ecbc6bcb84f47cd562576b42a1c.jpg)  
If you are pressuring them and they suddenly leap away at an angle like this they're starting the Quadruple Spinning Sweep.

# Okami Leader (Lightning Kemari) — Strategy

![](images/017d69a775547b68dddcbcaffc0acb195cdbd7e76849de234c38bbe3d1b86e99.jpg)  
There's a long pause between kicking the Mari ball and it shooting towards you during the Lightning Mari Kick. Wait before jumping up to Lightning Reversal.

The only difference between an Okami Warrior (Lightning Kemari) and a regular Okami Warrior (Kemari) is that her leaping Mari ball kick is now infused with Lightning, becoming a Lightning Mari Kick. Otherwise, she has all the same attacks and weaknesses as a normal Okami Warrior. The Lightning Mari Kick is a little different from regular Lightning-based attacks, as it shoots out a slow-moving, Lightning-infused Mari ball in a straight line with a short delay after the kick, making it trickier to time a Lightning Reversal. It's easier to knock her out of the sky with a Shuriken before she finishes the attack when you're far away, and then sprint over to attack her on the ground. You can still perform an Anti-air Death-blow, just like the regular version—if you're close enough to hit her

with a Lightning Reversal, you're close enough to jump towards her and Anti-air Deathblow. You still need to keep an eye out for her regular Mari ball attacks, including her Leaping Mari Curveball, which can catch you off-guard, and her very linear double Mari kick on the ground, which she often uses when you try to close in. Once you're close, she can't defend herself well, so you can easily finish her with basic attacks. All her attacks except the Lightning Mari Kick can be guarded normally.

![](images/7987bf8d303713c73d0790b5bee5f3c1b302ff5530735851b9f8369fcedfe01f.jpg)  
You can leap up and Anti-air Deathblow them when they attempt the Lightning Mari Kick.

# Okami Leader Shizu - Strategy

Okami Leader Shizu is technically a sub-boss, but unlike most sub-bosses the strategy for defeating her is very straightforward. When you grapple onto the branch she's perched upon, immediately start sprinting straight for Shizu. She'll most often leap vertically and attempt either her Lightning Mari Shot or her Leaping Mari Curveball, so quickly lock-on to her and throw a Shuriken to knock her down. Sprint over to her and immediately attack her repeatedly. As long as you don't stop attacking, she usually can't get away and the fight will be over quickly. If she manages to get away, back away from her to provoke her into trying another leaping attack, and knock her down with another Shuriken.

![](images/8493c6c71aa65df9c9e5c1aee0fd737474546ff40a84fc9da0c3191fc48d6b76.jpg)  
You can lock-on to Shizu to throw a Shuriken from a great distance.

# Overview

Each member of the Red Guard presents you with a different challenge. The Firebomb-wielders shoot slow-moving projectiles that deal Fire damage and cause Burn build-up, even through your guard. When you get close to them, they pull out their dual katanas and use armored, Posture-damaging slashes that are often followed up by the Dual Sword Thrust perilous attack. The Red Guard (Dual Katana/Firebomb) uses numerous slow, armored attacks that deal high Posture damage, and will frequently close the gap with the Shoulder Dash Combo into the Dual Sword Thrust if you back away during their attacks. They also come equipped with a fire-bomb launcher, and will pull it out if you get too far away or move to a place they can't reach. The Red Guard (Flamethrower) will continuously shoot a stream of medium ranged fire at you, until his flamethrower needs refilling, giving you an opportunity to close

![](images/51f37eda5cdf9c0f2a2ca0365694aeaa6348cc52aceab645361f4d82e3e8e093.jpg)

The Red Guard (Dual Katana/Firebomb) will use the Shoulder Dash Combo as a gap closer when you move away from him.

in and attack. The Red Guard (Kodachi/Dual Katana) have few armored attacks, but use faster attacks with numerous long, slashing combos that have tricky delays and timings to throw off your deflecting and overwhelm your Posture. Many of them are short ranged, so you can dodge backwards away from them and punish. They can also cancel into the Sidestep Backspin Slash combo both as they recover and during some combos.

All Red Guard can be easily defeated with the Divine Abduction tool, except for the Red Guard (Dual Katana/Firebomb), who doesn't give you the chance to Backstab Deathblow him afterwards. It's a good idea to make sure you have plenty of Dousing Powder at hand when fighting the Firebombs or Flamethrower-wielding variants. They won't notice you resurrect unless you are right beside them, so let them move away a little first.

![](images/96364c60ad4ae838fbfcf4717a3e1f504018eb41470854e18cbd37bef84f0bd3.jpg)

All the Red Guard that dual-wield share the same Dual Sword Thrust Perilous Attack. They each use it at the end of different combo attacks and in different situations.

# Red Guard (Flamethrower) — Strategy

It's best to stay far away from them while they're spreading flame onto the ground with their flamethrower and wait for them to run out of fuel. Quickly sprint and attack before they manage to reload. Sometimes they try to swing their flamethrower at you as you close in; quickly deflect it to stun them. Their low Vitality and Posture means you can quickly finish them with basic attacks.

The Red Guard (Flamethrower) in Ashina Castle never runs out of flame and will restart the flamethrower nigh instantly at close range while you attack him. There are a few ways to use Prosthetic Tools to defeat him without taking much damage. You can throw Shuriken at long range, sprint around his flame into sprinting Firecrackers and then start hitting him in his back, or start the Divine Abduction tool and sprint around the flame then use it to Death-blow him when close enough.

![](images/21d66cd88232412fccd6cc7b5cbb8bee9c1154480060f0823e4f386cb4fc4d02.jpg)

They can swing the flamethrower around to catch you, so don't wait too long before attacking.

# Red Guard (Dual Katana/Firebomb) — Strategy

Back away from them to just over a step dodge's distance away and provoke them into using their Shoulder Dash Combo to close the gap. They most often use this when you move away from them after they've begun a combo. As soon as you see the white dash effect, guard until they use the Dual Sword Thrust at the end of the combo, then Mikiri Counter it and retaliate with a thrust of your own. Pressure their guard until they deflect, then quickly back away again to provoke another Shoulder Dash Combo.. If they use other

# Red Guard (Firebomb) — Strategy

Sprint or dodge sideways to avoid their firebomb launcher shots, then close the gap with a sprint attack. They'll usually respond to this by pulling out their dual katanas and performing a left to right horizontal slash followed up by a Dual Sword Thrust. Guarding the slashes and using a Mikiri Counter against the thrust will usually break their Posture immediately. Otherwise, pressure his guard with basic attacks to quickly finish him off. You'll sometimes meet a version of this enemy that lacks the firebomb launcher and only uses his dual Katanas. He uses a simplified Red Guard (Dual

attacks, you can back away and thrust punish them as they recover, but they can cancel many attacks into the Shoulder Dash, so it's usually better just to wait for that. Make sure to hold your guard while waiting to regenerate Posture, and be very careful if they approach while winding up a slash with both swords—these attacks deal a lot of Posture damage, so you need to step dodge away from them. You can deflect to knock them back and give yourself time to punish with a thrust.

![](images/3b6513c5e2cb381a7d9c58abfcdf25c6d34fd46d84f7464d88e60a653249ee46.jpg)

He still has many armored attacks, but you can easily dodge backwards to make his combos miss, then punish with a thrust after the final hit. If he guards, he won't attack until after he deflects, so keep up the pressure to break his Posture quickly. He can use the Dual Sword Thrust after he deflects, so keep an eye out for it. Ichimonji: Double and the Loaded Axe into Fang and Blade are very effective at breaking his Posture quickly.

# Red Guard (Kodachi/Dual Katana) — Strategy

Because of their tricky swing timings, numerous fast, multi-hit combos and tendency to cancel into sideways dash attacks, it's best to focus on hit-and-run tactics against Kodachi-wielders. Back off to a step dodge's distance away and wait for them to start a combo, then time a thrust during the pauses between their swings. Be careful of their Leaping Double Slash, since they can use it as a gap-closer and it's often followed up with the deadly Double Crossed Slashes. Deflecting the last hit of their Double Crossed Slashes will leave them open for a counter-slash. Watch out for their Sparking Sword Flurry too, since it can quickly overwhelm your Posture; you can dodge backwards repeatedly to escape the rest of the combo once you've started guarding, but be wary of the Leaping Double Slash he'll sometimes use to catch you. While rare, he can use the Dual Sword Thrust Perilous Attack shared with the other dualwielding Red Guard.

He guards and deflects frequently, but it's dangerous to pressure his guard until he deflects, since he can use a fast, counter-attack overhead slash that will catch you if you step dodge. This attack leads into a long combo, and they can mix this with other attacks such as the Leaping Double Slash. If you see the deflection hit sparks,

# Samurai General - Overview

![](images/254b24ba08cb324e24a76120b2e207295d36618c9b746153d9ba4d2e6c8c5c99.jpg)

You'll encounter many of these enemies throughout the game, and while their specific move-set is usually slightly different, there are a large number of fundamentals that can be applied.

When up close, Samurai Generals' delayed attack timings and armored attack retaliations can make them difficult to deal with, so keeping your distance and punishing their missed attacks is often the best approach. Guarding their attacks at close range isn't recommended, since they can extend nearly all of them into overhead slashes if you guard them—those slashes can then transition back into other regular attacks, making for relentless chains that decimate your Posture. Fortunately, deflecting, or making the preceding attacks miss, prevents these follow-ups from occurring. If you do have to guard an attack, know that a follow-up is likely coming and be ready to deflect or dodge it. If a Samurai General performs a Leaping Helmbreaker, this will always end the chain of attacks.

When their Posture gets low, they'll start to back away and enter a recovery stance, indicated by a white aura. They regain a significant

# Samurai General - Attacks

# Lean Back Overhead Slash

PROPERTIES AA

Leans back with sword held vertically then leans forward into a long range, two-handed slash. Can use this at close range even when pressured. Tracks early sideways step dodge. Wait until sword moves past his head before deflecting / step dodging laterally.

# Leaping Helmbreaker

PROPERTIES AA | P(Guard)

Leaps into the sky and comes down with a two-handed vertical slash. Often uses at range, but will rarely surprise you by performing it at close range even when pressuring him. Wait until halfway down before deflecting/ step dodging laterally.

# Double HorizontalSlash

PROPERTIES CA

Steps forward into a horizontal slash, then reverse slashes. Second slash has follow-up on guard. Step dodge backwards or deflect first slash and interrupt second with counter-slash.

# General Yamauchi Tenzen, General Kuranosuke Matsumoto

# Lunging Uppercut

PROPERTIES AA

Takes a stance with sword held backwards down by hip, rushes into a lunging uppercut when close enough. Very fast and long range. Step dodge towards back on right side.

# Double Rising Slash to Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust | CA | Reaction Only | P(Deflect)

Two rising slashes on either side then a one handed thrust. Thrust has long range, be alert even if the first two miss. Mikiri Counter as soon as thrust starts moving forwards.

# Step in Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust

Takes a step forwards before thrusting the sword forwards with both hands, wait out the step before you step dodge or Mikiri Counter.

# General Naomori Kawarada, General Yamauchi Tenzen, General Kuranosuke Matsumoto

# Hilt Strike toSlash

PROPERTIES CA|E(Deflect)

Strikes forward with hilt, then slashes left to right. Deflect when sword halfway through arc or time step dodge backwards to avoid slash. Can sometimes use knockback kick instead of slash that deals high Posture damage. Dodge backwards to avoid.

# Circular Sword Sweep

PROPERTIES Sweep|AA|P(Deflect)

Leans down and aims a circular sword slash towards your feet. Deceptive range, can catch backwards step dodge. Animation can be mirrored, but same properties and timing. Jump and jump-Kick counter.

# Leader Shigenori Yamauchi

The first Samurai General you meet in the Prologue, Leader Shigenori Yamauchi, has a very simple moveset. He lacks all the Perilous attacks, the guard-battering follow-ups, the Lunging Uppercut, and the Posture-recovery stance. He also guards attacks less often and is much less aggressive overall. After being attacked he'll often immediately retaliate with an armored attack instead of attempting to guard the second strike, so limit yourself to single attacks before retreating. His simple move-set makes him ideal for practicing deflection into counter-slashes to finish his Posture once his Vitality is low.

The first real General you encounter in Ashina Outskirts, General Naomori Kawarada, lacks the thrust-based Perilous Attacks, only using the Circular Sword Sweep. He does not have the Lunging Uppercut, so you'll have one less thing to watch for at range.

![](images/aa3a2e95dd66be75b0ec657aaaaf06985acf58215f5802613eaaa909dcf4d905.jpg)  
The Lean Back Overhead Slash causes a slight guard stunned that will not allow you to step dodge the follow-up, but you can still guard or deflect, so if you guard that attack, make sure to deflect the follow-up after it.

![](images/c98ae4a2ffc716d7339e3e0c75a3b3d1fc46eef75bde19d86c4656b7e2cf0700.jpg)  
Prepare to jump the Circular Sword Sweep when you see the danger symbol and the sword shine start behind their back.

![](images/63f8c94129b847346c6dfcb3def8c218b5dc0e7f3ad0f4c407e17726d043a427.jpg)  
Generals will sometimes use a consecutive series of three very quick slashes that have good tracking and will catch step dodges; you'll need to deflect each hit if you spot this attack.

# Samurai Generals - Strategy

Try to maintain a range of a little bit more than one step dodge away, as that will limit the number of attacks they'll use against you and give you the most time to react to them. The key to victory here is not to be too aggressive; limit your punishment to one or two hits (or a well-timed thrust), and then immediately step dodge out of range to avoid their retaliation.

The Double Horizontal Slash combo has deceptive range, because they step forward during the animation—if you find yourself a bit too close, either step dodge to avoid the second hit and then punish it, or interrupt it with a quick attack of your own. The Leaping Helmbreaker is an attack they'll use to catch you while you're backing away, so it's recommended to use a second step dodge until you become very familiar with the range at which it will hit. Sometimes they'll run up to you before using it, but if you're maintaining your distance then you can always step dodge away.

At closer ranges, one of their more dangerous attacks is the Double Rising Slash to Thrust combo. Due to the consecutive nature of this attack, they will continue the combo even if the first two hits miss, so while you're creating distance, you should always be ready to evade or deflect the final thrust, because it has a lot of range. Note that you'll only ever see this attack if you deflect him. One more attack you need to be especially careful of is the Lunging Uppercut. The speed of this attack makes it difficult to react to at first. You can dodge to his back just as he lunges forwards, but it's safer to guard this attack a few times until you've gotten used to it before attempt-

ing this. If your Posture is broken, immediately safety roll away as quickly as possible to avoid his deadly grab follow-up. If you're fairly close and see them change their stance from up high to down by their hip, you'll know the Lunging Uppercut is imminent, but if you're too far away, they'll eventually revert back to their default stance.

Most of their other combos can be avoided by backing away if the first hit misses, but if the Hilt Strike toSlash combo is used when you're close, you'll need to time a backwards dodge precisely to avoid the slash. If you get hit by the first strike, it's best to immediately guard. The Step in Thrust recovers quickly, even when it misses, so it's better to wait for them to follow up with another attack, rather than retaliate instantly.

While it's possible to defeat this enemy solely with this strategy, the fight can be sped up significantly if you're a little more aggressive at close range once you've depleted some Vitality. Instead of backing away, stand your ground, deflect their retaliation, and then use your own counter-slashes to pressure their guard while being mindful of their occasional attempts to use armored attacks to escape your pressure. Always stop attacking when they deflect you and prepare to deflect their counter-attacks. Staying at close quarters does mean that you'll need to be mindful of their Perilous Attacks. Fistfuls of Ash or Firecrackers can create openings for a thrust or even time to sprint around and setup a Combat Art into their back; if you manage that, a fully charged Ichimonji is ideal.

# Chained Ogre - Overview

All of the Chained Ogre's attacks have super armor, so don't expect to stop him in his tracks. He never guards or deflects any of your attacks, however, so a hit-and-run strategy is very effective; stay away from him until he misses, then punish him a few times before retreating. You can stun him temporarily by dealing enough damage in a short period, and using Fire-based tools near him will make him panic—both situations allow you to land several blows before he recovers. Applying Burn results in another stun reaction, allow

![](images/72a0f1019e5a6b61817b6cd5cbe1b4d79fea0ceed37287abf8215376a71c96fa.jpg)

ing you to land even more blows, but be careful as he'll no longer panic in reaction to your Fire-based tools when he's already burning--you'll need to wait for Burn to end.

The wooden board around his neck allows you to grapple up to him after he performs certain attacks or after you've been thrown.

![](images/abefaa4493c469cd423aba6af6ec98346465b0021de915cd5ef08b5aab00632f.jpg)

![](images/1b2674da75c836f0766b38221eeb25692b65ec4d7669e26e772872a385b20774.jpg)  
If he throws you off a cliff, grappling back onto his collar will avoid almost certain death.

Grappling will temporarily knock him off balance, giving you some time to deal damage—this is particularly effective with the Grapple Attack Skill. The cooldown on Fistful of Ash/Firecrackers applies to Chained Ogres, so it's best to save them for when you really need to heal safely and rely on Fire-based tools like the Flame Vent to panic and stun them instead. If you have it, the Loaded Umbrella can guard his grabs; equip it during later fights with the Chained Ogre and use it whenever you see the Danger Symbol.

The Chained Ogre you meet in Ashina Outskirts takes a while to break free from his restraints, so rush up the stairs and deal as much damage as possible before he frees himself. The second Chained Ogre in Ashina Castle doesn't give you this opportunity; he will break his restraints as soon as you get close. You can, however, Plunging Deathblow him from the beam above his position to remove his first Deathblow Marker. Late in the game there's a version of this enemy that lacks the red-eyes and begins the fight using only kicks until he breaks the restraints that tie his hands behind his back. He will not panic when you use Fire-based tools, but you can still stun him when you apply Burn—consider throwing an Oil before your first Flame Vent to set him on fire immediately.

# Chained Ogre - Strategy

Start the fight by staying a step dodge and a half's distance away, then wait for him to miss an attack, and move in to punish. While most of his attacks are slow, the Quick Grab isn't, so you won't have time to react to it if you're overextending your offense—avoid committing to more than one or two hits from the front before retreating with a backwards step dodge.

Be alert for the Diving Grab at all ranges, since it has almost perfect tracking and surprising speed; you need to be ready to jump as soon as he leans down to start diving towards you. Watch out for the Sideways Kicks combo when moving in to punish. The kicks have deceptive range and the third attack doesn't always follow,

# Chained Ogre - Attacks

# Double Fist Groundpund

PROPERTIES

Raises both arms and pounds the ground with fists. Knockdown on hit. Step dodge backwards.

# Sideways Kicks combo

PROPERTIES CA

Two kicks, left to right, right to left, then can finish with either an elbow drop or a left front Kick. Sideways Kicks have deceptive range and track laterally, step dodge backwards. Stumble on hit, dodge roll to avoid followups.

# Right Front Kick

PROPERTIES

Brings back right leg and swings it forwards. Short-range, step dodge backwards.

# Dropkick

PROPERTIES

Launches forwards into a dropkick with both feet. Step dodge laterally. Two versions: one has short-range, second has greatly increased range and tracking.

![](images/fd90ca544c235dbc6d6ffb20e15216980a4fda68c70e0c6254a8b780f64044b6.jpg)  
The Master's Chamberlain in Fountainhead Palace lacks the collar, so you can't grapple onto him.

so make sure you confirm before you move in to attack. He has two versions of his Dropkick: a very short-ranged one that is easy to back away from, and a second one with tremendous range and tracking. Keep watch for the second one when you're further away and be ready to dodge sideways to avoid it.

After punishing several missed attacks, you'll eventually stun him, but only for a brief period. You'll have enough time to land 3-4 blows if you are quick, but don't get greedy. It's better to hit him less and back away to safety than be caught by the Quick Grab. Once he's Posture-broken, you'll get another grapple opportunity, allowing you to immediately grapple over and Deathblow him.

# Quick Grab

PROPERTIES Grab

Very fast grab towards his feet with both arms. Uses when right next to him. Step dodge backwards. Grapple opportunity if thrown.

# Step in Grab

PROPERTIES Grab

Takes a few steps forwards and grabs in front. Only uses when small distance away. Step Dodge laterally at close range. Backwards at distance. Grapple opportunity.

# Running Grab

PROPERTIES Grab

Runs at you with arms outstretched for several steps then grabs. Uses at distance. Immediately Sprint away. Step dodge laterally at close range. Grapple opportunity.

# Diving Grab

PROPERTIES Grab

Dives forwards with outstretched arms, sliding along ground. Uses at all ranges. Cannot be step dodged, jump to avoid, or sprint away immediately after he starts crouching down to dive forwards. Grapple opportunity.

# Headless - Overview

Headless ranks among the toughest enemies you'll encounter, so you need to make sure you are thoroughly prepared before attempting to fight one. The only reliable way to damage the Headless is with Spirit-based attacks and Tools; this makes Divine Confetti an essential item. If you run out, your attempt is best aborted until you get some more. Their attacks build up the Terror gauge significantly whether they hit or are guarded, but deflecting them prevents this. You'll also take Spirit damage if you guard or deflect if you don't

![](images/99253cedc08beee8b7d6c2bee7c6afcd97321a9c79a150d67a3bf1ee9f69834e.jpg)

have Confetti active, and if you guard even with Confetti. The high Terror build-up and Spirit damage on their attacks means you need to deflect or avoid most of their

![](images/f2d76e46d01b6fa31e814087fc55f680014b9a60a0b0281a10a0d4b2e140074a.jpg)

![](images/8ad1cd407505afa769e719df58c96978f4b2f86123eb42ad3ea467fe79ff7136.jpg)

Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella is incredibly valuable when fighting a Headless. It will protect you from both Spirit damage and Terror build-up, and will let you simply walk away to safety in the middle of their combos.

attacks to stand any chance of success. Using the Pacifying Agent and Mottled Purple Gourd items can help greatly at managing the build-up, but don't waste them all trying to keep your resistance high--you'll still need to use them constantly throughout the fight to remove built-up Terror.

Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella can guard their attacks without Terror build-up. This allows you to simply walk away from their combos to safety. Be careful not to use the follow-up Projected Force attack if you have it unlocked, since it will cancel your Divine Confetti. You can ensure you won't accidentally use Projected Force by walking or guarding briefly before attacking after letting go of the Umbrella.

The fog that surrounds a Headless will reduce your movement speed and disable step dodging completely. You can still slowly jump to move around, or hold sprint to increase your movement speed back

# Headless - Strategy

If you have the Malcontent Tool, you can start the fight by buffing yourself with Divine Confetti then immediately using Malcontent to stun the Headless. Attack it relentlessly until you break its super armor and stun it again, which will let you land even more blows. This will deal massive damage and likely leave the Headless almost dead, but don't immediately use Malcontent again to finish it off. It's better to finish the first Deathblow marker without it, so you can use the second full length stun at the start of the second phase.

When fighting them without Malcontent, staying a couple of step dodge's distance away from a Headless opens up two key damage opportunities. Both require a lot of room, so you'll need to proactively move and jump around to prevent being cornered. They'll often cancel their combos into a stumbling walk towards you after you move away, and transition into a slow horizontal slash when they get close enough. This attack recovers slowly, so keep moving backwards to make it miss and then move back in to punish with a few blows. The second major opportunity is by foiling the Soul-Stealing Grab it uses after the Vanishing Circular Slash. You have enough time to land three or four attacks while they're vulnerable before you need to start defending again. Ensure you don't back too far away, or they may respond with the Vengeful Projectiles.

Be careful whenever it recovers from its attacks, since the first hit of both Fast Slam combos are extremely quick and can easily punish over-aggression; if you get hit you need to time your safety roll to avoid the second attack. The two combos work together to foil

![](images/f2af9713b93cd642b9b20459ac454f645946e9bad51bb1dc5c989c376df683e0.jpg)  
After it uses the Vanishing Circular Slash, holding the sprint button and moving forwards will prevent the Headless from catching you with its Soul-stealing Grab...

to normal walking speed. The Headless relies on the fog to slow you down enough for many of its attacks to hit. Getting into the habit of always holding sprint to remain mobile will let you quickly move out of range to heal, reapply Divine Confetti, or use items to manage Terror build-up. Jumping can let you retreat quickly, but you need to time it well since some of their longer ranged attacks can catch a mis-timed jump.

The Headless is a super armored enemy with a seven second timer, but it only takes super armor damage when you hit it with a Spirit-based attack; it's impossible to stun it with your attacks without Divine Confetti. The slowing fog around the Headless will temporarily vanish if you manage to break its super armor, allowing you to move and step dodge normally until it eventually produces the fog again. The only other way to temporarily disable a Headless is with the Malcontent Prosthetic Tool.

deflect attempts; the second hit of one is a very slow vertical slam, while the second hit of the other is a faster horizontal slash. Both second hits deal very high Terror build-up when guarded, so trying to deflect them is extremely risky. This is a good time to use the Lilac Umbrella to escape, but you can also jump backwards after the first slam to avoid the rest of either attack, which will often provoke them into using the Vanishing CircularSlash.

![](images/6ae1f306146edfa8f6e75612fab8e84fe50ee33ef1f5dfa60999b94964f5f7d6.jpg)  
...you can then turn around and face it to cause the Headless to stand still for a little while. You can attack it without retaliation until it recovers.

# A Serious Challenge

The high difficulty of this enemy means you shouldn't expect to defeat them the first time you encounter them. Returning later with much higher Vitality and Attack Power will greatly improve your chances of defeating them. You'll also have better access to Divine Confetti, Pacifying Agent, and the Mottled Purple Gourd later in the game. Having as many of these items as you can carry should be considered essential prior to any attempt. The Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella and the Malcontent Prosthetic Tool both help greatly with fighting a Headless. Waiting until you have both Tools is a good rule of thumb for judging when you can expect to start defeating them.

While you can move away from many of its attacks, eventually you'll need to deflect an attack that you can't otherwise escape. If your deflect causes a deflect stun, it will start using its deflect swordplay reactions. This can lead to a deflect war, as it uses the Counter DiagonalSlash to try to hit you repeatedly. Whenever it enters a deflect spun, resist the urge to counter-slash; the Counter DiagonalSlash will punish this before you can recover. Instead, stand your ground and prepare to deflect its swordplay reactions while waiting for a chance to back away. Eventually it'll use the Counter Vertical Slam or the Vanishing CircularSlash. The Vanishing CircularSlash has a tricky deflect timing and starts up very quickly; as soon as you see the Headless duck down, immediately deflect. You can avoid all of their deflect swordplay reactions if you jump backwards immediately after deflecting an attack that causes deflect spun, or simply use the Lilac Umbrella to escape.

When you're fighting a Headless and really need to disengage to heal or use items, you can either use the Lilac Umbrella to make space, or utilize the environment you are fighting in to your advantage. There's a ledge you can use to get away from the Headless in the Outskirts fight, you can hide behind the trees in the Hidden Forest, and the Sunken Valley Passage Headless is surrounded by

# Headless - Attacks

large statues you can get behind. Be very careful of its Vengeful Projectiles when you try this, since it uses them whenever it can't figure out how to get to you. You might also find it will teleport behind you with the Vanishing Circular Slash, so don't lose track of it or you may find yourself suddenly in the clutches of its Soul-Stealing Grab.

![](images/64f8582be92b536455752062e522c2f100f9f5ae0f6e927fb795942c11412b3f.jpg)  
The Malcontent Prosthetic Tool can stun a Headless for five seconds and has significant range. The third time you use it the Headless will cancel the stun into a Vertical Slam, and from then on Malcontent will no longer work.

# Counter Vertical Slam

PROPERTIES Terror | Reaction Only | P(Deflect)

A slow overhead Vertical Slam. Used as a mixup for the Counter Diagonal Slash. Often follow-ups immediately with a variant of the Vanishing CircularSlash, that can't hit in front of it at the start. Deflect the slam and move away.

# Fast Slam to Slow Slam combo

PROPERTIES Terror CA

A fast vertical slam, followed by a second vertical slam, then a diagonal right to left slash; sometimes uses Vanishing Circular Slash during or after combo. Guard/deflect first slam then jump away. If no room, must deflect combo.

# Fast Slam to Slow Slash combo

PROPERTIES Terror|CA

A fast vertical slam, followed by a left to right horizontal slash, then a diagonal right to left slash; sometimes uses Vanishing CircularSlash during or after combo. Guard/ deflect the first slam then jump away. If no room, must deflect combo.

# Counter DiagonalSlash

PROPERTIES Terror | Reaction Only | P(Deflect)

Diagonal downwards slash from over the shoulder used after you deflect its attacks. Can be used on either side. Can chain into itself when deflected. Deflect just as the slash passes by its chest.

# Vertical Slam combo

PROPERTIES Terror|CA

Slams the sword two-handed onto ground twice, then swipes with left fist before final slam. Can be circled right to its back while locked-on by holding sprint.

# HorizontalSlash combo

PROPERTIES Terror|CA

Leans back into two slow horizontal circular slashes; first one way, then the other. Can start combo from either left or right side. Can attack a couple of times during its windup then stop to deflect. Arms can damage you up close, back away a little to make it easier to deflect.

# Vanishing CircularSlash

PROPERTIES Terror|PDeflect)

Ducks down with sword pointed towards you, then slashes  $360^{\circ}$  circle until it's holding sword skyward before vanishing. Teleports behind you to attempt Soul-stealing Grab. Deflect startup as it bends down. If startup misses can avoid rest by sprinting right as it circles around.

# Vengeful projectiles

PROPERTIES Terror|CA

Spins sword around body and launches homing projectiles that circle in towards you. Deals damage through guard. Sprint sideways away from them to avoid them. If uses in fog, hold sprint to speed up and allow you to evade.

# Bellyflop Bomb

PROPERTIES Terror

Crouches down, leaps into air, arcs across the space towards you, and bellyflops onto the ground. Only used at long range, has aoe splash upon landing. Damages through guard. Very long recovery, back away to avoid and punish with multiple attacks.

# Soul-stealing Grab

PROPERTIES Grab

Teleports behind you and attempts to grab you from behind. Sprint forwards short distance after Headless vanishes and turn around to face it to prevent grab. Vulnerable to attacks for short period after grab fails.

# Bull-Overview

Bulls will charge at you and attempt to Head Ram you every chance they get. This attack usually doesn't stop after it hits you or you guard it—the bull continues charging around the area you are fighting it in, trying to get space to Head Ram you again, and performing skidding turns to line itself up. If you're in the way, these skidding turns can bump into you and deal damage, but they don't deal any elemental damage so you can safely guard them. The Bull doesn't use any attacks other than the Head Ram, its skidding turns, or the Sliding Horn attack while it's actively charging, and only uses its other attacks when it slows down. The Swiping Rush can transition

![](images/fccf23751ba11a8e2335e9955085694b78ca482a863d72fdef27b3108f18c8d3.jpg)

from a standing start back into a charge, so you'll often see it use a Head Ram straight after that if you happen to be in front of it.

The Blazing Bull's head attacks inflict Burn build-up and Fire damage through your guard, with deflect reducing the damage. The small Fire damage upon deflecting can be easily managed with Pellets, as long as you don't try to deflect every attack. Keep Dousing Powder and the Withered Red Gourd in your Quick items to help

manage Burn build-up. The Sakura Bull of the Palace deals Spirit damage instead of Fire damage, so you don't have to worry about any status abnormality build-up. You can deflect it's attacks without damage if you use Divine Confetti or Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella. A Bull takes extra damage to its head, but its constant aggression makes this a dangerous area to target. Fortunately, there's a large opportunity to deal damage to its head if you deflect its Head Ram attack. This will cause it to skid to a stop facing you and stun it for long enough to land several high damage blows. Make sure to keep an eye on your Vitality as you deflect the Bull's attacks, and heal if necessary. The Head Ram deals high damage, so always make sure you're topped up on health in case you take a hit.

The Bull is a super armored enemy, so you can stun it briefly once you've hit it enough times. Attacks to its head deal bonus super armor damage compared to hitting its body. It also reacts with a much longer stun after it reaches  $40\%$  health, a reaction that is independent of super armor. Ensure you don't waste either of these opportunities to deal extra damage to its head. While it's affected by the

blind cooldown, Shinobi Firecrackers will deal Posture damage and cause the bull to rear up for a long duration, allowing you to land several blows to its rear legs. It's best used while sprinting around to its side or rear so you can make the most of the time available.

# Bull - Strategy

By far the fastest way to defeat the Bull is to deflect its Head Ram attack. Start the fight by sprinting in a circle around the Bull to avoid its initial charge, then move away from it so it has plenty of room to line up on you—now prepare to deflect its Head Ram. Quickly get close after deflecting it and use a thrust on its head, then several more blows will often stun it further, allowing you to deal another couple of blows before needing to back off again. It's better to cut your attacks short if you aren't sure you'll stun it and back off again to set up a deflect on another Head Ram.

![](images/ccd43d342407382ad42a0cf9327ca308b58cb0676ac93c92cf88922669b43baf.jpg)  
The Head Ram is usually only used when it's charging at you.

A safer but much slower way to fight a Bull is to sprint sideways in a circle, following it as it charges, and hit its side with sprinting attacks as it slows down during its skidding turns, then back away again to continue sprinting. You need to watch out for its Sliding Horn Slam when sprinting sideways, since it can catch you if you

# Bull - Attacks

When it reaches low Vitality, a Bull will scream, rear up, and start its Berserk Charge. Get out of its way and let it run itself into a wall to Posture-break itself, then immediately sprint up to the head while it's knocked down and perform a Deathblow to finish the fight.

don't have enough space--make sure to stick to the middle of the area as much as possible and if you're in doubt, quickly guard. Avoid approaching the Bull's head as you close in on it after a skidding turn or it will immediately Head Ram you at point blank range.

At close range, when it's not charging around, be careful of its Swiping Rush and Vertical Horn Swipe when you're directly in front of it, since they both have good forward range. The Turning Head Swipe is often used to catch you when you're at its sides or rear. If it swipes it head in a large motion to one side then appears to pause with its head turned, then it's using the Head Swipe combo instead, so don't try to punish until it's finished the second attack. These attacks can be punished with a Shuriken into Chasing Slice from long range, but don't attempt this on its charging attacks, since the Head Ram can hit you while you recover.

![](images/9e9e7e661da4ddeda5f3a242203f3d267f5e0cc4d326e845e2d22c88e6e98037.jpg)  
Deflecting its Head Ram will cause it to skid to a stop and stun it long enough to land several blows on its head.

# Head Ram

# PROPERTIES

Ducks head extremely low then rears straight upwards while lunging forwards. Used while charging. Deflecting this attack will cause bull to skid to a stop facing you. Sprint laterally to avoid.

# Head Swipes

# PROPERTIES CA

Swipes the flaming torches on its horns side to side twice, both swipes have huge range to the sides. Step dodge towards its rear or away. Short moment of opportunity to hit its head with an attack after second swipe.

# Swiping Rush

# PROPERTIES CA

Swipes its head from side to side three times then immediately starts charging. If you are too close it can immediately attempt a Head Ram afterwards. Huge forward range, step dodge sideways towards its back through swipes. Sprint laterally at range.

# Vertical Horn Swipe

# PROPERTIES

Ducks its head and turns its horns vertically, then attempts to hit you with a rising slash of its horns. Step dodge to the right towards its rear legs.

# Turning Head Swipe

# PROPERTIES

Swings its head sideways trying to hit you with its flaming horn. Often uses when you are standing by its side. Step dodge further towards its rear, or away.

# Sliding Horn Slam

# PROPERTIES CA

Slides out of its charge and slams its head sideways to hit you with its horn. Very fast attack. Often uses this when you are sprinting sideways as it charges towards you. Can transition immediately into further attacks if it hits. Deals no elemental damage, so safe to guard / deflect.

# Berserk Charge

# PROPERTIES CA

Screams and rears, then starts continually bucking while charging forwards. Each buck can deal damage. Avoid by sprinting away from path of charge. If it hits a wall, will immediately result in a Posture-break.

# Shinobi Hunter - Overview

Armed with a long spear and highly mobile, the Shinobi Hunter will relentlessly attack you with his long-range spear combos and many Perilous Attacks, most of them thrusts. His defenses are good, making it difficult to deal damage to him when he misses, and his Vitality can take decent punishment. His low Posture is a critical weakness, however, and his tendency to use thrust attacks gives you many chances to Mikiri Counter them to deal great Posture damage. Since it's difficult to deal Vitality damage to him and impact his Posture regeneration, simply attacking his Posture in a passive manner with hit-and-run tactics will allow him to regain it quite quickly. The fastest way to defeat him is to keep the pressure on him

![](images/4bef6763dc93fa1ff99e8356459a6d6de8d0a2d619f0b815293d7fcae0b9f0a7.jpg)

with attacks on his guard in between Mikiri countering his thrusts, so he doesn't have much chance to regain the lost Posture.

![](images/0e825f77783737d9db9f79ac7008293a24a45c3363be07c9c1f6fe50bebc1e79.jpg)  
At the end of the Dashing Thrust he uses a one handed grip to give the attack extra reach. This makes it very difficult to avoid with a backwards step dodge.

The most important thrust attack he uses is the Dashing Thrust; its long range can easily catch a backwards step dodge if started too close. He will frequently attempt to dash backwards away from you while you're pressuring his guard and use the Dashing Thrust while you're caught in the recovery of an attack. It's important to recognize this tendency and prepare to Mikiri Counter this move whenever he backs away.

Later in the game you'll find a Strong enemy variation of the Shinobi Hunter; he wears monk robes and has a new trick up his sleeve. He's able to cancel his Spear Sweep into an upwards, anti-air spear stab in response to you jumping towards him. If you have Mid-Air Deflect you can deflect this attack after jumping, and he doesn't do it if you neutral jump, or jump backwards.

![](images/71099f7398d8d5ae2f771fae0d94632efcbf3f40b05ef82c6f03ffdf143bba44.jpg)  
Mid-air deflecting the anti-air stab will always Stagger a Shinobi Hunter Monk, allowing you to immediately deathblow them as soon as you land. You need to jump towards them for this to work, and you can force them to do it even when they aren't using their sweep if you jump at them when they aren't currently attacking.

# Shinobi Hunter - Attacks

# Spear Impale

Thrust, Grab | AA

Dashes backwards twice then assumes a stance with shine on spear; lunges forwards with two large leaping steps then rising stabs upwards. Can use without backwards dashes. Can deflect and Mikiri Counter, wait until second leaping step or Danger Symbol fades away.

# Four Thrust combo

PROPERTIES Thrust CA

Thrusts spear forwards four times. Deflect does not cancel combo, Mikiri Counter does. Can Mikiri Counter next attack even if hit. Very linear, Step Dodge right towards back to avoid. Optimal posture damage is three deflects then Mikiri.

# Spear Sweep

PROPERTIES Sweep | AA | Reaction Only | E(Deflect)

Leans down and sweeps the spear in a half circle at foot height. Jump-kick and come down with mid-air attacks to continue pressure.

# Dashing Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust|AA

Takes several steps forward then thrusts spear out one handed to extend its range. Always steps. Wait for first couple of steps before Mikiri Counter or deflect. Can dodge towards back on right side when close. Often backdashes first, only backdash has armor.

# Haft Strike to Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust | CA | Reaction Only | E(Deflect) | P(Deflect)

Spins the spear point backwards and strikes forward with haft end, then spins around again to thrust with spear point. Guard then wait out spin into thrust before Mikiri Counter, or interrupt spin with quick attack.

# Rising Haft Strike to Sweep

PROPERTIES Sweep|CA|AA

Ducks forwards and delivers a rising strike with the bottom of the spear, then immediately performs the Spear Sweep perilous attack. Only the sweep is armored. Doesn't use sweep if you are too far away.

# Backwards Stab

PROPERTIES Thrust

Strikes backwards with spear at targets behind. Uses when you get behind him. Cannot be Mikiri Countered, but can be deflected. Step dodge laterally or interrupt.

# Double Haft Strike combo

PROPERTIES Thrust CA PDeflect

Strikes upwards with butt of spear, then segues straight into the Haft Strike to Thrust combo. Often doesn't use last thrust attack when you are too far away.

# Shinobi Hunters - Strategy

If you have difficulty recognizing the beginning of his various thrust attacks and combos, you can back away to two of his own spear lengths away. Maintaining this distance makes it easier to see his Dashing Thrust and Spear Impale. From here, the first hit of his Four Thrust combo will usually miss, giving you plenty of warning to Mikiri Counter the second thrust. Timing a Mikiri Counter on the Spear Impale is a gamble, considering its high damage, but it recovers slowly, so it's safer to back away and punish it instead. Make sure to punish any of his missed attacks with a few blows before retreating again.

A strong way to control the Shinobi Hunter's options is to attack him until he deflects you. This reduces his options to four moves: the Haft Strike to Thrust combo and the Spear Sweep are only used directly after he deflects, while the Dashing Thrust and Spear Impale are used while you're pressuring his guard. Of these options, the Haft Strike to Thrust is the fastest, and the one you must always watch out for, since it will catch a backwards step dodge—always guard once he has deflected you. If he uses it, wait for the thrust and then Mikiri Counter it. If he ducks to use the Spear Sweep, use a jump-kick counter followed by mid-air attacks to force him to guard again. If he immediately uses a single dash away from you while you're pressuring his guard, then he's going to use the Dashing Thrust. You can either Mikiri Counter it, or immediately back away as soon as you see him retreat, wait for him to miss, then resume attacking him.

![](images/8a6eb7b5de076339328ede972f9b5d2ceda9e0f4a773dc8461b3c32da7a63e17.jpg)  
The Spear Impale is one of his most dangerous attacks. Watch for the shine on his spear to warn you it's coming.

![](images/590186209a43f250a1d75a880055f6f804eba8963684cb345e6b32f82e911e48.jpg)  
The timing for Mikiri countering his Spear Impale can be tricky. This is the exact moment you need to Mikiri, as soon as his foot lands on the ground after his second long step.

If he backs away twice, he's going to use the Spear Impale, and the same options apply, but beware the range of this move if you choose to wait for him to miss. Once you're comfortable with dealing with his deflects, it's a powerful strategy to simply keep him in a deflection loop. A thrust of your own can be useful here to reduce the guesswork, as he'll always deflect it if he's able to. Since it deals almost no Posture damage when deflected, you need to rely more on dealing with his attacks to deal Posture damage to him.

![](images/cd0b664c31723c9c035bd947d5efc37cd67b4ea238b1863fba51f2e9192d0b02.jpg)  
The thrust at the end of his Haft Strike combo requires him to spin his spear back around  $180^{\circ}$  to point towards you again, giving you plenty of warning to Mikiri Counter.

If you don't have the Mikiri Counter skill, most of his attacks are linear and can be step dodged to his side or back on the right side, allowing you to land a few attacks before he can guard. It's also possible to sprint in a circle anti-clockwise at two of his spear lengths away, so his linear attacks miss, then circle around to hit him in his back. Note that you need a lot of space to use this tactic, so depending on where you're fighting a Shinobi Hunter, it may not be an option. Be careful as you approach his back as he's very likely to attempt his Backwards Stab, but sprinting to the right often makes this attack come out at a somewhat awkward angle that you can then punish. If you position yourself right behind him and use basic attacks, he'll frequently try to respond with a Backwards Stab, which you can repeatedly interrupt by continuously attacking. When he eventually turns around, back away and resume circling. You can also use Fistfuls of Ash or Firecrackers to easily get around behind him to set yourself up in this position, but he recovers quickly, so it's best to use them at close range after he misses an attack.

![](images/ff01275ac7fa192eb0425e7716c28acbf4fd23bf388e2dc3570960b0166de32f.jpg)  
Sprinting to the right and circling around him will make many of his attacks miss, giving you a chance to attack his back.

# Shura Samurai - Overview

Slow-moving, but extremely hard-hitting, a Shura Samurai is a rare super armored enemy that uses extensive swordplay. His attacks deal a lot of Posture damage, so relying on guarding is not a good strategy. If you end up being Posture-broken, always perform a safety roll, since there's often enough time to recover before getting hit.

![](images/56fcd6e980489f01fa65bb0105305c123aa52578b10d49e239c808e2ec5388c7.jpg)

Moving in and out of range while countering with thrusts and sprint attacks leads to a more protracted encounter, but it's by far the safest method of dealing with him. It's

![](images/da7f2cdbde7cbf2bf795f906e101f5ab71e6db075a70e396bbc6ec953abf2563.jpg)

Juzou the Drunkard (Hirata Estate Rev.) ■ Recom. Setup

![](images/33a4b93e6b8768b1ea0c5525bb38ffcefb7336026e1d2b8a20968760d5368758.jpg)

You'll meet Red Guard Shigekichi in Ashina Outskirts during the Central Forces Raid, and he comes equipped with armor that greatly reduces damage unless stripped off with two pulls from the Loaded Spear.

essential to time your attacks carefully while he's recovering; there's a short period where he will deflect attacks in between recovering and starting a new attack.

After deflecting you he often retaliates with the Counter DiagonalSlash. The instant you hear the distinct deflection noise and see the hit sparks, get ready to press the guard button to deflect these diagonal slashes. He's also capable of using this after you deflect his attacks, sometimes resulting in a deflection chain where he continuously attacks you after you deflect him. You can avoid this chain on flat ground by sprinting backwards immediately after you see him hit your guard or deflect, but if you wait too long or are fighting on a slope then your only option is to deflect.

When you're at a distance, he often takes the opportunity to drink from his Sake Gourd. Drinking allows him to either perform the Sake Spit attack, or to imbue his sword with Poison by spitting the sake onto it. He doesn't have to perform either immediately, and after using one of them he must drink before using it again. Guarding or deflecting his sword once it's been imbued with Poison causes Poison build-up, so focus on hit-and-run tactics until the Poison runs out. The Poison left behind by the Sake Spit takes a second to spread out, but ends up covering a large area; avoid retreating backwards or you'll end up in the thick of the cloud as it disperses; move laterally instead. Use Antidote Powder if you end up getting Poisoned, since it deals a lot of damage.

Stay about two step dodge's distance away, wait for him to miss an attack, and then move in to punish with thrusts and sprint attacks. Be alert for his Stomping Palm Strike combo when keeping your distance from him; the first palm thrust will often be followed up by a second one if you try to step dodge away. The Charged Palm Thrust and Sumo Grab have great range but are easy to pre-emptively avoid by moving even further away. He doesn't always finish the second attack of his HorizontalSlash and DiagonalSlash combos, so make sure to confirm before moving in to punish. If you get deflected when attempting to punish, watch out for his Counter DiagonalSlash. Both his Counter DiagonalSlash and normal DiagonalSlash combos have good reach, so if you're backing away as he's about to hit you, you'll need to time a deflect. Be wary of the Headbutt to Vertical Slam he sometimes uses after running towards you, since the one-handed version of the slam in this combo has long range and can follow sideways movement very well.

Make sure to move in and punish his Drink attempts and whenever he spits poison onto his sword, since both animations are quite lengthy and leave him open. Fistful of Ash items can be used to blind him once every 15 seconds. He will deflect any frontal attacks; to counter this, move to his back and slash away until he recovers.

He often follows up with a Sword Sweep if you get stunned by the spit, so if you've lost him and you hear the Danger Symbol sound, immediately jump. While you can finish him with a hit-and-run strategy, a much faster way to finish the fight once you've dealt enough Vitality damage is to stay close. Keep up the pressure at close range by deflecting his attacks and counter-attacks and step dodging his linear vertical attacks, then punishing. Watch out for his Sword Sweep and Sumo Grab at close range; the grab needs to be step dodged laterally at close range, but the Sword Sweep is fast enough to catch you and should be jump-kicked. Look for their distinctive cues to indicate which ones he's going to use.

Ichimonji is a useful punisher that guard crushes him so he can't counter-attack. You can easily finish his Posture after depleting his Vitality by using Ichimonji as your primary punishing attack, and Ichimonji: Double just makes this strategy even better. Be careful of when you use it though, since many of his dangerous attacks such as the Sword Sweep or Vertical Slam will always armor their way through it.

# Ashina Elite - Overview

Ashina Elites are dangerous practitioners of the Iado sword style, armed with a blindingly fast, long-range quick-draw attack. Fighting an Ashina Elite is a battle of reflexes and intense concentration. Their goal is to land one of their devastating quick-draw Ashina Cross attacks on you, with their other attacks only used to complement this strategy. When fighting the Ashina Elite, you must always be prepared for this attack, and always be watching carefully for the small bright flash on their sword sheathe that signals it.

The dash they use while moving around the arena is armored, and they often dash sideways or at oblique angles to alter the timing of the Ashina Cross. The Ashina Cross has strong armor, so you cannot challenge it with basic attacks. Slower armored attacks (such as the Loaded Axe) will cause you to take full damage from it, which is never worth the trade. While this attack takes time to activate, you can't pressure him to prevent it, since he'll deflect you then often follow up with either the Ashina Cross itself or the armored Perilous Attack Horizontal Draw. The Horizontal Draw's armor can cut through overextended aggression very easily.

![](images/84a73c97008ff64fee8405327016efb371b98bb35a0f525cecd2ad685a6e7f40.jpg)

The second Ashina Elite you meet during the Central Forces Raid, Ujinari Mizuo, will panic when you use Fire-based Prosthetic Tools and he won't attempt to guard or deflect during this time. The best time to use one is just after step dodging his Ashina Cross to his back; you can then attack him until he recovers from the panic.

![](images/d601f069b25147a83406a4403f3e30eff1ccdd480ed2840e7e47788f2acada17.jpg)  
You can use fire based Prosthetic Tools from quite far away to make Ujinari Mizuno panic without running into his Ashina Cross.

The two primary ways to deal with an Ashina Elite are step dodging to deal damage to his side or back, and deflecting to break his Posture. There's no safe range to hold against him, since he can suddenly dash into your range and activate the long-range Ashina Cross at any moment. If you want some breathing room you need to sprint a long distance away, since he only advances with forward dashes, which will give you some time to Heal before he can catch up. It's best to stay about one step dodge's distance away when fighting him to make it easier to see the bright flash that signals the Ashina Cross.

You can step dodge through the Ashina Cross, ending up behind him, where you can land a thrust. Don't follow-up with anything more, because he can dash sideways or backwards and immediately Ashina Cross in retaliation. Instead, back away a little so you can see his sword sheathe clearly and prepare for his next attack. Quite often, doing this will result in a kind of loop where you step dodge an Ashina Cross, punish it, then he retaliates with another that you step dodge, and so on. Occasionally he'll use a Hilt Strike that will flinch you; resist the urge to Brace Guard, as he's very likely to immediately attempt an Ashina Cross afterwards—instead, prepare to dodge immediately.

He'll sometimes use the Retreating Slash to get away from you. Be careful if you are hit or guard this, as again, an Ashina Cross is likely incoming afterwards. If you're too close, or he deflects one of your attacks, be alert for his Perilous Attack Horizontal Draw; while you can jump-kick this attack, you need to be careful as you land, since he'll likely attempt an Ashina Cross. Unless you're comfortable deflecting his Ashina Cross, it's safer to jump away from the Horizontal Draw instead.

While step dodging his Ashina Cross and punishing can defeat him, a much faster way to deal with the Ashina Elite is to stand your ground and deflect both hits of this attack. Doing so will deal massive Posture damage to him and can finish the fight with lightning speed. It can be useful to first step dodge it a few times into a thrust, and listen to the distinct "swoosh" sound of both slashes to learn the timing before attempting to deflect it. Don't attempt to follow-up with a counter slash after deflecting it, just wait for the next one. Sometimes he'll use a retreating slash after you deflect him. You can either deflect this too, or quickly dodge it, but don't try to punish or you might expose yourself to an Ashina Cross. You also need to watch out for the Horizontal Draw in this situation.

# Ashina Elite - Key Attacks

The Loaded Umbrella can help immensely with this strategy, since the deflection window at the start is long enough to deflect both slashes of the Ashina Cross with one press, and it deals extra Posture damage as well, requiring less deflects to break his Posture. The Mist Raven Tool allows you to dash behind him after using it on his Ashina Cross. He will spend a lot of time flourishing his sword and slowly sheathing it, which allows you to set up any attack you like straight into his back. A fully charged Ichimonji: Double is excellent for dealing Vitality and Posture Damage, but many other attacks can hit him, so if you have attacks such as Enhanced Mortal Draw (or NG+ attacks, such as Dragon's Flash) you can use those too.

![](images/e13f10a5eefde681eaf9da42fec4c4fdaf73baf3b538b779b8bcb918ca74caab.jpg)  
The shine on his sword hilt is the only warning you have before he starts the deadly Ashina Cross.

![](images/8fe2cd5dfdc510122d01d0759c832a74039013193e06fa4f1c91d310cd379dcd.jpg)  
The Loaded Umbrella can deflect both hits of the Ashina Cross as it opens, and the extra Posture damage it deals when deflecting will help Posture-break him very quickly.

# Underwater Headless - Overview

Unlike the regular Headless, you don't need Divine Confetti to deal significant damage to an Underwater Headless. On the other hand, you can't use a Pacifying Agent underwater, so the Mottled Purple Gourd is your only way to reduce Terror build-up. It's best to clear

![](images/cf27e2a99853172c54e86e6e90b95e83b10ffcd4ee300a8616b3e559c5008fc9.jpg)

your Quick Items of all items except those you can use underwater, such as the Healing Gourd and the Mottled Purple Gourd.

Fighting an Underwater Headless is a unique experience, since you need to get to grips with a different control scheme. Your main defensive move is your long underwater dash, as well as a quick dash backwards (done by tapping the step dodge button without holding the analogue stick in any direction). You can guard and even deflect

underwater, but because you can't use Divine Confetti, you must deal with Terror build-up when doing this, so it's not as reliable as outright avoiding an attack. Only guard if you can't otherwise avoid getting hit by a damaging attack such as the Water BladeSlash.

Resist the urge to dash straight at the headless and begin attacking wildly, as it has two super armor attacks it can use at close range that deal great damage: the CircularSlash and the Vortex Grab. The Vortex Grab is almost guaranteed to kill you at the time you can first face this enemy. Instead, you want to use your high mobility for a hit-and-run strategy, staying away from the headless, waiting for it to miss an attack, then dashing in and landing a couple of hits before dashing away again.

It's best to stay around a full underwater dash's length away and continuously dash in a circle around the Headless. At this distance, the Vengeful Projectiles can't hit you if you keep moving. Wait for it to use its long-range Water BladeSlash. Then you can quickly dash around to its back and deal a few hits. You must first confirm that it hasn't used the second slash, or you could take a lot of damage. Limit yourself to one or two attacks, then quickly tap 3/0 to dart backwards away from its CircularSlash counter-attack. If you see the Danger Symbol, immediately use two long dashes to get away from it, as this signals its Vortex Grab, which needs to be avoided at all costs. After you've dashed way from it far enough, it will often cancel the grab immediately into a ranged attack, such as the Vengeful Projectiles or the Water BladeSlash, so be careful and start immediately dashing laterally again. If you've waited a little too long for the Vortex Grab, start doing a full lateral underwater dash in a circle around it.

As you get used to the timing of when the Underwater Headless will use the Vortex Grab and Circular Slash, it's possible to avoid and easily punish both moves by doing a neutral step dodge away from it and then continuously dashing in a circle. When you are dashing laterally at this distance at full speed, the Vortex Grab can't track you, allowing you to dash in and deal damage to its back during its long recovery period. If you find it difficult to dash attack towards its back, you can just stop moving when you are behind it and use a thrust to shoot yourself forwards. Land a few hits, then

![](images/4921638753983f446104ce7b1d43f9bc3ed00a4e77c92c6dfb69a1ff515ec9d4.jpg)  
You'll have to face two Underwater Headless in the Fountainhead Palace fight. The Illusory twin has less Vitality and Posture so its best to kill it first.

# Underwater Headless - Attacks

# CircularSlash

# PROPERTIES Terror

Spins sword around in a circle until pointing skywards. Uses when you are close range. Underwater dash away then back in again to punish. Same animation as Headless Vanishing Circular Slash, but cannot teleport.

# Water BladeSlash

# PROPERTIES Terror CA

Winds up a sword slash surrounded by bubbles that fires off a slash shaped projectile. Underwater dash sideways repeatedly to avoid. If caught at close range, attempt to time a deflect on the projectile to avoid Terror buildup. Can follow-up with second slash.

neutral dash away again and resume dashing in a circle around it. Most of the time it will repeat either the CircularSlash or the Vortex Grab. Resist the urge to punish the CircularSlash too early, since the sword may come back around and hit you again; it's only safe to punish when the sword is pointing skywards. If you ever get hit by the CircularSlash, immediately dash laterally, since it often tries to follow up with a Water BladeSlash that is difficult to react to it at that distance unless you're already moving.

Sometimes the Underwater Headless will repeatedly use the Vengeful Projectiles and you'll find the area filled with them. You can't get close to it to stop it from doing this, because the homing projectiles will turn around and follow you, trapping you. It's a good idea to get even more distance from it and start cutting back across the projectiles' path, aiming to dash through the empty spaces of water in between packs of projectiles. This will make it very difficult for the homing projectiles to turn and follow you back in before their duration runs out and they disappear. Eventually the Underwater Headless will start using its Water Blade Slash, which you can then dash around and punish.

# Underwater Headless (Fountainhead Palace)

The main difference with this encounter is the phantom twin standing on a nearby ledge, close enough to hit you with its Vengeful Projectiles and Water BladeSlash. It has less health than the main Underwater Headless you are fighting, so it's best to take out this twin first. Use the larger space to dash far away from both, then carefully pick your moment to dash past the projectiles and deal a single dash attack to the phantom twin. You can't stay too close to it or the Vengeful Projectiles and Water Blades from the other will quickly catch up to you, so stick with a single hit before dashing out to open water again. You are in much deeper water here, so you can change your height to help escape the projectiles. If you're overwhelmed you can disable lock-on to quickly aim yourself with the right analogue stick, then lock-on again after escaping. Be careful that the phantom twin doesn't catch you with a Water BladeSlash as you approach its narrow ledge. Kill the twin first, then the remaining Underwater Headless can be tackled using familiar tactics.

# Vengeful projectiles

# PROPERTIES Terror

Spins sword around body and launches homing projectiles that circle in towards you. Deals damage through guard. Underwater dash sideways away to avoid them, or dash through gaps in between groups of projectiles.

# Vortex Grab

# PROPERTIES Grab

Winds up left hand by side, then pushes out and creates a cone shaped water vortex. Will suck you into grab on contact with vortex. Quickly underwater dash diagonally away when you see the Danger Symbol, then circle around to back and punish during recovery.
