# Shichimen Warrior - Overview

Shichimen Warriors fight from a distance by summoning dozens of spirit orbs during the fight, which they use to control the area around them. They can spread these spirit orbs around themselves to interfere with your movement, and they'll slowly home in on you. Meanwhile, they fire off streams of small spirit orbs or begin summoning very large ones that also attempt to home in on you. You can avoid both types of Spirit Orb by continuously sprinting sideways. All their Spirit attacks cause Terror build-up, so make sure to bring enough Pacifying Agent or the Mottled Purple Gourd.

Divine Confetti is the key to fighting a Shichimen Warrior. When you have Divine Confetti on your weapon, the damage you deal to them is heavily increased, your sword swings will automatically destroy any nearby spirit orbs on the same level as you (this effect

![](images/e72ea71a0df0e416dd9f1cc5bd783a2b54d90c2ebe4d8c185eaacc591849bbb2.jpg)  
When a Shichimen Warrior leaps high into the air during the Leaping Spirit Orb Mine, they're vulnerable to an anti-air Deathblow.

occurs within a small radius around you), you can deflect their Spirit attacks without taking damage or Terror buildup, and it unlocks the ability to anti-air Deathblow them when they use certain jumping attacks. Although they are a super armored enemy and can be stunned briefly after enough hits, they will only take super armor damage from Spirit-based attacks.

They will teleport away from you after guarding your attacks, so it's quite difficult to finish a Shichimen Warrior within the duration of a single Confetti due to the time it takes to close in on them; make sure you have at least four on you. If it's taking you more than two Divine Confetti to remove a Deathblow Marker, and you end up dying, consider coming back later when you have more Attack Power.

Both Fistfuls of Ash and the Shinobi Firecrackers will blind them

and let you land a few blows, but both are affected by a 30 second cooldown, so it's often better to save it to stop a difficult to deal with attack, or to give you time to reapply Divine Confetti. If you have it unlocked, Malcontent can also stun them for five seconds, but after the third time the stun will be cancelled mid-way, and after that it stops working. Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella can safely guard a Shichimen Warrior's attacks, including their Charged Spirit Beam, without Terror build-up, so keep it equipped if you have it unlocked.

Your aim when fighting a Shichimen Warrior is to get close and deal damage, then deal with their Charged Spirit Beam after they guard and teleport away. They often use leaping attacks after this beam; get over to them fast enough and you can anti-air Deathblow them before they land.

# Shichimen Warrior — Strategy

# Predicting Teleport Locations

Shichimen Warriors have fixed teleportation locations, and usually pick the farthest one in the fighting area to teleport to. Once you've gotten used to these spots you can quickly turn and run towards their likely location, but stay alert to their sounds in case they decide to pick a different spot than you expect. This can allow you to get the drop on them before they finish charging their beam attack, so you can interrupt it with Ash/Firecrackers or just sprint behind them. This is particularly useful in Fountainhead Palace, since this one only has two locations, either end of the stream. It's almost always possible to arrive before it has finished charging the beam if you sprint immediately after you hear the clang of its guard.

It's better not to buff yourself with Divine Confetti before you engage them, because they'll usually start off with the Spirit Summoning Mist at the beginning of a battle. You'll take constant Terror build-up if you step into the mist, so you'll need to wait until that's finished before approaching. Start the fight by running straight to them and cancelling their Spirit Summoning Mist with Ash/Firecrackers, then buff yourself with Divine Confetti while you wait. If it's too late to get close to it because spirit orbs are already heading your way, you'll need to sprint in a circle around it until it finishes the entire Spirit Summoning Mist attack, while being careful not to run into any of the spirit orbs in the area. Then you can quickly get close and blind it to give you time to use your Divine Confetti.

Once you're close, it will often retaliate with short-ranged melee attacks such as Double Staff Swipe or Overhead Staff Swipe, cast the Large Spirit Orb Summon, or attempt to use leaping attacks to back away from you. You can guard or deflect the melee swipes, but dodging through them towards its back will give you time to hit it before it recovers and faces you again. If they start charging the Large Spirit Orb Attack, you'll need to quickly disengage and avoid the large homing Spirit Orb by sprinting sideways. Keep a close eye out for when they leap high into the sky and hover for a while,

# Shichimen Warrior - Attacks

since these are usually an anti-air Deathblow opportunity you don't want to pass up; quickly jump towards them in mid air and to activate the Deathblow prompt. Sometimes they'll attempt to avoid you by jumping at a low height away from you; you'll need to approach them again at an angle to avoid their attacks.

When they guard your attacks and vanish, expect them to teleport and cast their Charged Spirit Beam. Turn around and locate them, then sprint towards them as they charge the beam. If you have Divine Confetti on your sword you can deflect this beam and take no damage, while Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella offers a much more forgiving way to block the beam. Once you've deflected or guarded it, the rest of the beam can't hurt you any more, so immediately continue sprinting. It will often attempt jumping attacks after the Charged Spirit Beam, and your aim is to get over there fast enough to anti-air Deathblow it. If it doesn't use jumping attacks, continue attacking it until it guards again and repeat the cycle. If you aren't comfortable deflecting the beam you'll need to sprint sideways until it's finished, then sprint straight at the Warrior, but you are less likely to manage to reach it before they it finishes its jumping attacks. Note that they can use the beam at any time, so if you see its distinctive charging animation, you'll need to prepare to react even if they haven't recently teleported away.

# Double Staff Swing

# PROPERTIES CA

Swings the staff one handed right to left in a wide ranging horizontal swipe, then follows with left to right swipe. Guard first hit then step dodge backwards. Can step dodge through swings to back.

# Overhead Staff Swing

# PROPERTIES

Swings the staff two handed from over right shoulder. Knockback on hit. Guard recovery appears heavy, but can still punish with an attack after guarding. Step dodge left towards back.

# Spirit Orb Summoning Mist

# PROPERTIES CA

Plants staff in ground, creating mist around itself and summons Spirit Orbs that fire at you in a stream, followed by large homing Spirit Orbs. Standing in Mist causes Terror Build-up. Sprint sideways to avoid Spirit Orbs.

# Large Spirit Orb Summon

# PROPERTIES

Holds staff above head and summons giant Spirit Orb that homes in on your position. Sprint sideways until they lose track of you. Penetrates guard. Can deflect with no Terror buildup or damage.

# Spirit Orb Stream

# PROPERTIES CA

Holds staff towards you and summons multiple small Spirit Orbs that stream towards you one by one. Very linear, sprint sideways to avoid. Can angle towards them while sprinting sideways and still dodge attack.

# Leaping Spirit Orb Mine

# PROPERTIES

Leaps into air and summons Spirit Orb mines around the area. Floats one way, then swings again and floats the other. Long Anti-air Deathblow opportunity.

# Leaping Spirit Orb Stream

# PROPERTIES CA

Leaps backwards while firing Spirit Orb stream at you. Small anti-air Death-blow opportunity if you leap straight at it when close. If far, sprint sideways.

# Charged Spirit Beam

# PROPERTIES

Sucks nearby spirits into the staff, then fires a long beam of spirit energy at you. Sprint perpendicular to path of beam to avoid. Can deflect beam with Divine Confetti and take no damage, wait to deflect until beam is halfway to you. Beam cannot hit you when right next to them.

# Snake Eyes - Overview

Snake Eyes are versatile opponents; they can pepper you with ranged shots from afar, and will use their rifle as a powerful melee weapon up close. Being overly aggressive will get you punished by their armored Kick Shot, the Backdash Shot, and the armored Hook Grab, the latter of which deals massive damage and cannot be guarded. The window of opportunity for dealing damage to a Snake Eyes is small, since they guard and deflect frequently.

Their most dangerous attack, the Hook Grab perilous attack, is very slow to start and features almost perfect tracking; recognizing its distinctive spin is important. They can use this attack on its own, but they most frequently use it as a reaction to you pressuring them.

![](images/15a83d6a85ffa1bd0efe5b53162516012c111bc230b8f7f234d31b19b0a352eb.jpg)

Despite it being a grab, it's possible to deflect this attack with good timing; they point the rifle directly forwards before they hook in to catch you, so you'll want to tap the guard button just before the rifle would touch you. A safer way to deal with it, if distance allows, is to jump backwards as soon as you recognize it, but you must jump early or they'll still catch you. It recovers slowly enough that you can use a thrust to punish her after it misses.

Most of a Snake Eyes's cannon shots can be guarded and deflected safely, except for the piercing attack Sniper Shot, which can only be deflected (though it can be guarded with the Loaded Umbrella). You can spot this if you see that the projectile has a spiral around it. Fortunately it's a very linear attack and you can avoid it by continuously dodging sideways.

![](images/f080f2d96fc77ec0f2eda2e2bb32f29102534eb2869c6922281f52236a22b535.jpg)  
If you've accidentally step dodged backwards just as she starts her Backdash Shot, a timed deflect during your dodge recovery can prevent taking damage.

Against a Snake Eyes, your first goal is to reduce her Vitality, and there are two ways to do this. The first way is to stay a step dodge and a half's distance away and bait her into attempting to shoot you or start a swiping attack, then punish her with an attack while she recovers. The Three Swing Combo can be interrupted with a quick attack after the second hit, the Left Rising Swipe combo can be interrupted before the shot, while the various shot attacks recover slowly enough to step dodge the bullet laterally, straight into a step attack or thrust. Be careful of her Right Swing Kick combo, since it has longer range than her left side swings and she usually sequences into the Kick Shot afterwards. Make sure you don't get cornered when fighting—you need space behind you to use this strategy.

She holds the rifle up the same way during the Sniper Shot and the quicker Standing Shot, making it hard to tell them apart. The Standing Shot can track a step dodge, but she always fires it immediately after she raises the gun to her eye, while the Sniper Shot has a much longer delay, but is extremely linear. Always time your step dodge as if she is doing the Standing Shot, and if she's still sighting at you, continue moving sideways to avoid the Sniper Shot.

You can provoke most of the same melee attacks by hitting her guard and immediately dodging backwards. This puts her on the back foot, making it difficult for her to catch you with her attacks and putting you in a position where you can easily retaliate. Always be alert for the Hook Grab and make sure you don't punish too early and get dragged in; wait until the hooking in part of the animation has finished. Since you're closer to her for this strategy, you can often step dodge towards her when she fires the shots at the end of her combos. She can't hit you easily at close range with any of the shots that involve her raising the cannon high before firing.

![](images/eab5a6890a60ce70197f4c495af72617367b37152be393f4b0492cf84236b889.jpg)  
It's possible to deflect or dodge the Hook Grab with precise timing; wait until her cannon is almost pointing directly forwards and deflect/dodge just before she quickly hooks inwards.

While you can defeat her with Vitality damage alone, you can kill her much faster if you focus on Posture damage after reducing her Vitality. Start off by pressuring her guard then stop and prepare to deflect her attacks. All her rifle swings can be bounced back on deflect, preventing the rest of the combo and allowing you to counter-slash to pressure her guard again. Keep an eye out for the Hook grab, which she can start at any time; you can deflect this if you're supremely confident, but it's much safer to jump backwards to avoid it and punish.

Resist the urge to attack her until she deflects, since she has three dangerous reactions to watch out for; the Kick Shot, the Hook Grab and the Backdash Shot. The first two can be avoided by dodging backwards immediately after she deflects, but the Backdash Shot can catch you unless you time a deflect while recovering from your dodge. It's often safer to immediately guard once you see the deflect sparks and watch to see what she does next, then respond appropriately; guard/deflect the kick and dodge forwards to avoid the follow-up shot, jump away from the Hook Grab, and dodge through the Backdash Shot to hit her with a dodge counter-attack as she recovers. If you choose to attack her aggressively, make sure to back away from her occasionally to recover your Posture by holding your guard, since her Kick Shot deals heavy Posture damage and if it breaks your Posture, the follow-up shot can't be avoided.

If you have the Loaded Umbrella and Projected Force Skills unlocked, the two combined are extremely powerful. The Umbrella lets you safely guard (or deflect) the Hook Grab then punish with Projected Force. Deflecting any of her melee attacks with the Umbrella will also usually allow you to land a Projected Force, dealing good damage and breaking her Posture much quicker than swordplay alone. If you don't have Projected Force, the Umbrella can still be an effective defleeter, but it's better to save your emblems to guard the Hook Grab.

![](images/5bd202b419ee4bdbcc1a95707cb921abbeb28f7b5d70a6649b264e22db852e83.jpg)  
A slow but safe way to damage Snake Eyes is to get to a spot they can't reach and guard their Sniper Shots with the Loaded Umbrella....

![](images/2d1026cd077b6167cfd0af5feecccb450ba643737191986ad6299061a1c6072d.jpg)  
...once you have reached maximum charge, use Projected Force to damage them.

![](images/7d9e3eed06ec7e7fbc7f6c0bafc222b32a5c3d4049f8d0d747612a1c0dea872f.jpg)  
Shiraftugi's weakness to blue rust Poison makes Sabimaru one of the best ways to use your spirit emblems.

![](images/dd176ceccd58c8e65d2aa65d553709856bf9bf6f63fd4dca3dcb1eece216695b.jpg)  
Shirahagi has great resistance to Poison, making the Loaded Umbrella a better choice, especially if you aren't comfortable with deflecting or dodging her Hook Grab.

# Snipers - Attacks

# Three Swing Combo

PROPERTIES E(Guard)

Swings the cannon three times, left side swing, then right side, then final rising left side swing. First two can be deflected to cancel combo. Step dodge towards back on left side to prevent followups.

# Right Swing Kick combo

PROPERTIES E(Guard)

Steps forwards while winding up a one handed right side slash from behind back then performs Kick Shot. Step dodge swing towards back on left side to cancel kick. Only kick is armored. Deflecting swing cancels combo, deflecting kick won't cancel cannon shot.

# Kick Shot

PROPERTIES CA|AA|E(Deflect) |P(Guard) |P(Deflect)

Spins into a backwards kick with left leg, follows up with immediate cannon shot. Kick tracks well, causes stumble on hit, time safety roll to avoid shot. Can dodge towards her after guarding/deflecting kick to cause shot to miss.

# Sniper Shot

PROPERTIES

Sights along rifle while standing for two seconds then fires a piercing round that deals reduced damage through guard. Deflecting prevents damage. Very linear, step dodge or circle sideways. Can interrupt with Shuriken.

# Snipers and Sabimaru

The two Snipers have a difference in Poison resistance caused by their choice of habitat. The Sniper in the Poison Pool, Shirahagi, has great Poison resistance, making Sabimaru an ineffective choice against her. It's better to save your emblems for Firecrackers or the Umbrella, especially if you have Projected Force. It's possible to lead her into the poison pool or attack her with her back to it so she dashes backwards into it, but it takes an extraordinarily long time for Poison to take hold.

On the other hand, Shirafuji is weak to blue rust Poison, so a good way to open the fight is to sprint directly at her and unload a full Sabimaru combo on her. She will usually deflect the last attack; immediately back away and wait for her to miss, then retaliate with another Sabimaru combo. Most of the time this should Poison her, inflicting great Posture damage build-up, although sometimes it requires part of a third combo to finish applying it. You can switch to the Umbrella after this to help finish her off, but make sure you save enough emblems for at least three more combos of Sabimaru in the second phase just in case you need them.

# Backdash Shot

PROPERTIES AA | E(Deflect) | P(Guard) | P(Deflect)

Dashes backwards then fires cannon from the hip. Only the backdash is armored. Tracks early step dodge, guard if unsure of timing. Time a step dodge laterally and punish with thrust. Step dodging forwards through projectile guarantees thrust punishment.

# Standing Shot

PROPERTIES

Sights along rifle while standing then immediately fires a shot. Tracks early sideways movement. Time a lateral step dodge, or guard/deflect.

# Left Rising Slash to Shot

PROPERTIES E(Guard)

Brings the cannon low into a left side rising slash, then immediately transitions into a shot holding cannon over head. Shot misses if standing toe-to-toe. Step dodge backwards then interrupt shot, or step dodge to back. Deflecting slash prevents cannon shot, guard does not.

# Hook Grab

PROPERTIES Thrust, Grab | AA | E(Guard) | E(Deflect) | P(Guard) | P(Deflect)

Performs a delayed backwards spin then hooks in with the blade on the cannon. Can be Deflected. Loaded Umbrella can guard and deflect. Deflect or step dodge just as cannon is pointing forwards. Safest to jump backwards and punish with thrust after you land.

# Long-arm Centipede

# Long-arm Centipede - Overview

A Long-arm Centipede will try to slash you to ribbons with the razor-sharp claws attached to his hands. He attacks with two long consecutive combos, with the second only coming into play after removing the first Deathblow Marker. His combos have very long reach and he advances forwards with each attack, making backwards evasion not very practical. It's possible to sprint towards his back on the right side during the pauses in these combos, but the angle is tricky and he isn't vulnerable for very long after the final slash, which makes dealing Vitality damage difficult. On the other hand, deflecting the last hit of his combos will cause him to dash backwards and use the Lunging Claw Sweep, which you can jump-kick to deal great Posture damage. His constant aggression means

![](images/c4c9d86ab624a97621ac52a5926c768c0771dbf4f65f207e82a12ee398d089ef.jpg)

he doesn't spend much time regenerating Posture, so it's possible to defeat him very quickly purely by deflecting his combos and jump-kicking his sweeps.

# Long-arm Centipedes - Strategy

For the first phase he'll exclusively use the 10-Hit combo as his initial attack. Position yourself in the middle of the room so he must approach you, then guard the first few slashes of his combo. During the first pause in the slashes, sprint towards his back on the right side (if you are locked-on and facing him, point the analogue stick towards the 2 o'clock position). He'll try to turn towards you with the rest of the combo, but your sprint will cause you to automatically move away from him. Once you're far enough away you can keep backing away until you avoid the rest of the attack. You need to be at least a step dodge's distance away to avoid the final slash like this; if your path is blocked off by the environment you'll need to start guarding or deflecting instead. Since he isn't vulnerable for very long after the final slash, it's best to hit him with a quick attack or set up a powerful un-guardable attack, such as a charged Flame Vent. Make sure to reposition yourself immediately afterwards so you have enough room to sprint around him again. This is also a good way to heal or regain your Posture if you need to.

Even with this strategy, killing this enemy with Vitality damage alone can be a grueling affair, so unless you're taking him on with very low Vitality it's much faster to focus on breaking his Posture. In this case, you want to deflect the last hit of his combo so you can then jump-kick his follow-up Lunging Claw Sweep. You can either sprint through his pauses and simply deflect the last hit instead of avoiding it, or stand your ground and deflect as many slashes of the 10-Hit Combo as you can to deal even more Posture damage while you wait for the opportunity to deflect the final slash. If your Posture is high after you deflect the last slash, hold guard for a moment to recover a portion of it while he dashes back to prepare the Lunging

![](images/e7e2d75ac7a1abb8e33db9f082428ce6c9872d904005faadf644e05fbf671024.jpg)  
If you are in a spot he can't reach, he'll pull out and throw up to six firebombs. The firebombs leave fire on the ground afterwards that can damage you and build up Burn if you stand in it.

# Long-arm Centipedes - Attacks

# 10-Hit Combo

PROPERTIES CA|AA

Winds up right claw hand, then launches into a continuous 10-hit slash using both hands. Four slashes, then slight pause, five more slashes, slight pause, final double slash with both hands. Deflecting final slash causes him to use Lunging Claw Sweep.

# Firebomb Throw

PROPERTIES Burn|CA|AA

Winds up and throws up to two sets of three firebombs. Only uses when he can't currently reach you on the ground. Leaves a patch of fire residue on impact that will inflict fire damage and cause Burn buildup if you stand in it. Dodge to avoid.

Claw Sweep, then jump straight out of your guard into a jump-kick counter as he comes back in. A mid-air attack after the jump kick will often stun him briefly and let you hit him with one more basic attack afterwards, before you need to deal with his attacks again.

# No Deflecting Downside

You cannot drop your guard at all once you have started guarding the 10-Hit Combo, so there's no downside to attempting a deflect on each individual slash; you can't take Vitality damage even if you get your deflect timing wrong. The Posture damage you inflict if you deflect the entire string and then jump-kick the follow-up sweep is well worth the effort. This also applies to the 8-Hit combo, but you need to jump the sweep in the middle.

After you've removed the first Deathblow Marker, he'll start mixing in the 10-Hit combo with the 8-Hit combo. The sweep in the middle of the 8-Hit combo attack has long range and can catch a sprint towards his back, so you must jump and jump-kick counter whenever you see the Danger Symbol. The trick is that the 8-Hit has the sweep after the third hit in the combo, while the 10-Hit has the pause you can sprint through after the fourth hit. It's better to aim for Posture damage in the second phase over Vitality damage, since standing your ground and jump-kicking the sweep in the 8-Hit will cancel the rest of the combo and inflict excellent Posture damage. If he tries to use the 8-Hit combo several times in a row you can defeat him very quickly.

If you get hit by the sweep, make sure to quickly brace guard and continue deflecting the rest of the combo; aim to deflect the final slash to trigger him into using his Lunging Claw Sweep. You can quickly take a single sip from your Healing Gourd while he dashes backwards and still have enough time to jump the sweep.

If you have enough Vitality, the Loaded Axe with Fang and Blade is quite effective at trading Vitality for Posture damage with the first hits of his combos, especially if paired with an Ungo's Sugar to reduce your incoming damage. Mist Raven is good for escaping when cornered; vanish to his back then immediately run away to gain space. If you have the mid-air combat arts skill, using Ichimonji: Double on the way down after jump-kicking his sweep is an excellent way to devastated his Posture. Senpou Leaping Kicks will deal massive damage to his Posture if you time the downwards kick onto one of his sweeps.

# Lunging Claw Sweep

PROPERTIES Sweep | AA | Reaction Only | P(Deflect)

# Armored Warrior - Overview

The Armored Warrior won't be defeated the same way as other enemies, and there's three things you'll need to know about him right off the bat: his Vitality can't be damaged at all, he doesn't recover Posture over time, and the only way to defeat him is to break

![](images/01af92f202a9a514606d216f2ad3e7d07f8b2e7f3843d8c14bb248c6a5b27116.jpg)

his Posture near one of the walls of the bridge, then use a Deathblow to push him off the edge so he falls to his death.

He doesn't guard or deflect, instead relying on his super armor to allow him to power through your attacks. Hitting him with five normal attacks in a row will break his super armor and briefly stun him, but you don't get much time to hit him, since the stun is quite short, so limit yourself to only one or two quick attacks. Note that his super armor timer is only seven seconds, so you can't be too passive in between attacks if you're aiming to stun him.

His heavy attacks all deal a lot of guard stun and he's capable of breaking your Posture quickly if you simply stand and guard. Many of his combos continue unless deflected or step dodged to his back; either of these options can give you a chance to land a few hits. Most of the time, deflecting his combos simply stuns him temporarily, but he'll occasionally react to a deflect with a short combo, so make sure to confirm that he isn't starting an attack before you hit him.

The Deathblow animation for this enemy is a special one in which the Wolf kicks him backwards a few feet, so you need to make sure the wall is on the opposite side and that he's close enough to it to fall, or else you'll waste your chance and he'll immediately regain half his Posture. The only other time he can regain Posture is if you fail to Deathblow him after breaking his Posture, which will set him back to  $25\%$ . If you aren't in a position where you can push

![](images/3e7d42f63a792f08bad2f88168565c27f8a55a8f54c58a2ded3580bca9dd542a.jpg)

![](images/5a58777debf9cd783f4c03d9dc6907b8e9538759719cc6a11adf6c9d81819be0.jpg)  
The only way to defeat the Armored Warrior is to deathblow him off the edge of the bridge.

him off the edge when you break his Posture, it can sometimes be worthwhile to deliberately avoid attempting the Deathblow so he doesn't regain half of his Posture. But it's better to keep an eye on his Posture and draw him over to a wall when it's about to break.

The walls of the bridge are breakable, with unbreakable pillars spaced out along their entire length. His attacks can break the walls, but they don't need to be broken to push him off the edge; if you set up the Deathblow correctly, he'll smash straight through them. He won't fall through the pillars, however, so you must make sure you have the right angle. If you have the Vault Over skill and you happen to break his Posture with your back to a wall, you can quickly Vault Over him to Deathblow him off the edge.

Aim to stay several step dodge's distance away until he misses, then sprint back in to hit him a couple of times as he recovers, before retreating again. From a distance he'll often try to use his Horizontal Slash. When you see him take several steps forwards, be prepared to avoid this attack—dodging through it to his back can let you land several blows before he recovers, but it's safer to dodge backwards if you aren't confident in your timing. Watch out for his various vertical slams; they all have extended range and can easily catch you unaware. The Running Vertical Slam is a great opportunity to slip around behind his back, since its extremely linear. The last slam of the Shove to Vertical Slam tracks sideways movement extremely well and has deceptively long range and speed. It's safer to guard the slam if you're unsure, rather than try to dodge or deflect it, since it has no follow-up when guarded or if he breaks your Posture; you can simply safety roll to reset the situation.

While you can guard the first hit of many of his combos then immediately sprint backwards to avoid the rest, be wary of the Sword Thrust used at the end of some of them, since it has longer range. Whenever he uses this attack, it's usually preceded by either a diagonal overhead slash or a rising slash, but sometimes he'll cancel a regular combo into a Sword Thrust. Watch for the distinctive way he holds his sword before he thrusts—he holds it pointing forwards near his head—and be sure to Mikiri Counter it. If he manages to knock you down, make sure to time a safety roll to avoid his ground thrust. If you need space to heal or regain Posture, you can sprint along the bridge far away from him, and he'll take a while to catch up to you.

Unlike most super armor enemies, he only has one attack that will ignore incoming super armor damage—the ferocious Berserk Rush. When he hunches over and roars, he's starting this attack. You can sprint far away to avoid it, but there's a huge window of opportunity to hit him if you deflect the final attack, since it will stun him for a long time afterwards. After being blinded, he's affected by a 15 second cooldown, but occasional Firecrackers and Fistfuls

# Armored Warrior — Attacks

of Ash will allow you to land several good hits before he recovers, sometimes even enough to stun him for longer.

Make sure to draw him closer to the walls once his Posture is almost broken, but don't stand with your back to the wall since he can knock you off with some of his attacks. Instead, back away so you're fighting parallel with the edge. Then, when you break his Posture, you can quickly circle around to Deathblow him and knock him off. If you are very close, use Ash or Firecrackers to finish him off safely.

Ichimonji's high Posture damage makes it a powerful punisher after dodging through his attacks to his back. Its high super armor damage means you'll stun him briefly every second hit. Note that if you attempt Ichimonji: Double and he isn't stunned on the second hit he'll often recover and hit you before you can move again. To be safe, it's best to only equip the normal Ichimonji. You'll have time to land a fully charged Ichimonji after dodging many of his attacks but be sure you have confirmed that he isn't continuing a combo before you start. This works after dodging his Vertical Slams.

![](images/bd38d1d73177bcd3ea0223ac8587fc38da06d9e71f13dacc5ee0d3d2d6da0b09.jpg)  
Deflecting the final hit of his Berserk Rush will stun him for several seconds. If you attack him relentlessly you can often break his super armor before he recovers, extending the time he's vulnerable.

# O'Rin of the Water - Overview

O'Rin of the Water relies on tricky spins and gliding movements to catch you off guard. She can go briefly incorporeal when she hops backwards and from side to side—she can't be affected by any of your attacks when she is in this state, nor does Divine Confetti allow you to hit her while she's incorporeal. Divine Confetti will greatly increase the damage you deal to her, though. Many of her standalone attacks and swordplay reactions have an incorporeal backwards hop at the start designed to trick you into over extending yourself

![](images/ba251e5c0fd6924f5173e85b467c06b1904c3b6f92ac24bb5fe971dfcec522b5.jpg)

so her follow-up attack can hit you. To counter this, always dodge backwards yourself whenever she hops backwards to give you plenty of room and time to respond to her attacks.

She guards and deflects frequently, making it difficult to damage her Vitality from the front, and her long consecutive combos advance her forwards with each attack, preventing you from dodging backwards mid-way to escape. The Gliding Slash combo and the Spin CounterSlash combo both have a follow-up sweep Perilous Attack at the end of them. Her high Posture damage makes guarding her long combos very risky, if you get caught guarding one you need to deflect as many hits as you can to prevent a Posture break. Battling O'Rin is a two-stage fight that involves first finding openings to deal Vitality damage to her to reduce her Posture recovery, then focusing on pressuring her guard, deflecting her counter-attacks and jump-kicking her sweeps to break her Posture. In both cases the best way to fight her is to stay at range and make her come to you.

![](images/cd7ca0001b0137d0d4e77f9cb52913f743e73f2405fd1fd1b84372f3610a191e.jpg)

O'Rin will frequently attempt to grab you whenever she breaks your Posture, sometimes even canceling her combos midway. Quickly retreat with a safety roll to avoid her grab and then attack her before she recovers.

![](images/44122a548ad75c39dcfd5fa9955bdcdec02aa659e98303ee17868b3d8ca4aa2f.jpg)

![](images/3e5946a091654930903e5fa83b7b775dd528ab3e7cf4f42cb65cecb4da93011c.jpg)

Her Spin Counter Combo is signaled by a hop backwards then a sideways dash to the right. In phase 2 she omits the sideways dash and starts her first spin in the opposite direction. Back away from her to prevent her from slipping behind your guard.

At the start of the fight put several dodges distance between yourself and O'Rin. At this distance she can only threaten you with the Mist Dash Double Slash and the GlidingSlash combo. Both can be dodged to her back and punished with a thrust. She uses the Mist Dash Double Slash the most often, and its speed can catch you by surprise even when you are expecting it. Hold your guard up as she dashes in, that way if you wait too long to dodge you'll guard the slashes automatically. Stick to one thrust before backing away again to provoke another Mist Dash Double Slash. Note that you cannot hit her during her dash forwards since she's incorporeal, so don't try to challenge it, wait until the dash has finished. Once you have whittled down her Vitality to half, you can switch to damaging her Posture by pressuring her guard to provoke her into using attacks you can punish with deflects or jump-kick counters.

Back off to the same distance and attack her guard after she finishes the Mist Dash Double Slash. If she deflects you, be prepared to deflect her fast Counter SpinSlash, then immediately back away again to avoid her reactions. You don't need to worry about timing a deflect on the Counter Spin slash; it's so fast that simply holding guard the moment she deflects will deflect this attack automatically.

Whenever she goes incorporeal and hops away, stop attacking and dodge backwards while watching out for her attacks, but don't move so far backwards that she starts using the Mist Dash Double Slash. A couple of dodges is the key distance. She uses the Hop Back CounterSlash, the GlidingSlash combo and the Spin Counter Combo after she hops backwards; the latter two both have sweeps at the end you can jump-kick. Land with mid-air attacks after to continue the pressure on her guard. Be extra cautious not to chase her whenever she hops backwards while you're pressuring her guard; if she starts the Spin Counter Combo at close range, the first incorporeal slash can end up spinning around behind your guard and hitting you in the back. If you find yourself too close to her immediately jump backwards to make enough space to prevent this.

If you have trouble deflecting all the hits of the Spin Counter combo, she will stop after the first two hits if you are too far away, so you

# O'Rin of the Water - Attacks

can just back away further to avoid it, then move in to pressure her guard. Be careful in phase 2, since she gains an extra spin attack during the Spin Counter Combo prior to the last two hits. Watch out for the Horizontal Slash combo when you're backing away from her, as the first two hits advance forwards to catch you; keep an eye out for the horizontal slash from right to left without any spin prior that signals the first hit. If you're ever in any doubt about what to do next, back away until she starts using the Mist Dash DoubleSlash again.

While she's weak to blue rust Poison, you need to make sure not to wait too long in between Sabimaru combos or it'll take too long to apply it. Be proactive about attacking her with Sabimaru as soon as she finishes an attack or combo; Piercing Sabimaru is particularly effective if you have it. Fistfuls of Ash, Firecrackers and Malcontent can stun her for long enough to run around behind her back and deal a few blows, setup a Combat Art, or get off a Heal, but make sure she isn't incorporeal when you use them or they won't work. Note that Malcontent only works three times and after that she resists it. When pressuring her guard to deal Posture damage Ichimonji: Double is more effective than your regular attacks since she'll be forced to block the second if the first is guarded, but only use it as a punish since its too slow to interrupt her attacks. It's particularly effective in mid-air after jump-kick countering a sweep.

![](images/fa6b54afb2857de3ff9ffd116748dda1a0f033d516f2b61c52b7b1414d0e4196.jpg)  
Her Gliding Slash combo has two follow-ups; a sweep when close, or a dash into a rising slash if you are far away.

Backwards spins into a low rising slash, then does a reverse slash after short delay. Can glide forwards for both slashes if you are far away. Step dodge to back and thrust punish. Deflecting first hit cancels combo.

Begins a quick right to left horizontal slash, then pauses slightly and slashes three times, slight pause, final slash. Can catch a backwards step dodge. Guard first slash then step dodge right during pause and punish with thrust.

# Seven Ashina Spears - Overview

A Seven Ashina Spears puts all his weight behind his long range spear attacks. The first attack of his  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash and Ground Slash combos guard crush; if you guard them, your only option is to dodge or Mikiri their follow-up attacks. The weight he puts into his thrusts means a successful Mikiri Counter doesn't necessarily end his attacks; he will often push you off then retaliate with a single rising slash or overhead slam. Deflecting either of these two

![](images/deb41b3963a280b69eb9244aecf4b1fa54c67f0e629d9a2165439943116f0675.jpg)

attacks will knock him off balance and stun him, leaving him open long enough to land a thrust or setup a strong Combat Art such as a fully charged Ichimonji.

This enemy has many swordplay reactions to watch out for when fighting him. He can relentlessly batter your guard with the Quick CounterSlash and the first hit of the Vertical Slam Thrust, and can also use several of his Perilous Attacks as swordplay reactions, including the dangerous Ground Drive Thrust and the Circular Spear Sweep. He guards and deflects frequently, making it difficult to deal Vitality damage at the start of the fight by backing off and punishing his missed attacks. Fortunately he's quite aggressive and doesn't spend a lot of time regaining his Posture. Staying away from

![](images/e5ad9aa205440987a0c5cb676cfa000dafb855e75e1d660ae4fea10b05f1d373.jpg)

him and Mikiri Countering his various thrust attacks can act as a way to deal Vitality damage, while chipping away at his Posture at the same time.

![](images/4b264edccfc1906a465166247957207c661f91de35e7a8daff175b2999978a7f.jpg)

His armored  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash combo will guard crush, making it impossible to deflect the follow-up thrust. You can Mikiri or dodge it sideways instead.

# GroundSlashcomb

PROPERTIES CA|AA

Assumes stance with spear held down by waist pointing forwards; when close drives spear into ground on right side and rising slashes, then follows up with armored leaping slam. First slash guard crushes, wait until leaping slam is halfway down then step dodge left.

Quick overhead diagonal slash. Step dodge right and punish with step attack. Will often transition into further swordplay reactions if you deflect or guard this attack.

Steps into a long range horizontal slash right to left, then comes back with a left to right slash. Step dodge through second slash and punish, or pressure guard after second slash. Guarding or deflecting second slash can lead to follow-up attacks.

Steps forward and thrusts, then slashes horizontally with spear, followed by a vertical slam. Wait out brief steps on initial thrust then Mikiri Counter.

Raises spear sideways before thrust, Mikiri when point moves towards you. Only first slash is armored. Step dodge right at close range to prevent follow-up. Guard crushes, can only Mikiri or dodge follow-up thrust.

Runs towards you for several steps then thrusts forward with spear. Spear is raised horizontally before thrust forwards, wait until spear point starts moving towards you then Mikiri Counter.

![](images/dba9666bda072a8810107a7d32b79a26df8572bac5311582d6bb9307ebfb4fae.jpg)  
Many of his thrusts, such as the Running Thrust shown here, have a shine on the spear point that slowly travels up to the tip. Wait until it reaches the tip before attempting a Mikiri Counter.

PROPERTIES Sweep|CA|AA

Ducks down low and sweeps spear around in a circle, then immediately follows up with  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash combo. Jump-kick counter sweep to stun and prevent follow-up. Only  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash is armored.

# Sidestep Thrust combo

PROPERTIES Thrust | P(Deflect)

Steps sideways while winding up spear then thrusts three times; two fast then a long delay before final thrust. Wait out sideways steps before Mikiri. If hit by first or second thrust can Mikiri Counter next one. All three thrusts track sideways step dodge.

# Circular Sweep

PROPERTIES Sweep | Reaction Only | P(Deflect)

Ducks down low and sweeps spear around in a circle. Uses this stand alone version of sweep only as swordplay reaction. Jump and jump-kick counter.

# Ground Drive Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust | E(Guard) | E(Deflect) | P(Deflect)

Steps back with shine on spear, then pushes spear point into ground and drives forwards into rising thrust. Wait until forward steps almost over then Mikiri Counter. Tricky timing; backing away and punishing long recovery is often safer. If started close, interrupt with attack.

# Vertical Slam Thrust

PROPERTIES Thrust | Reaction Only | E(Guard) | E(Deflect) | P(Guard) | P(Deflect)

Quickly slams the spear down onto the ground then follows up with a thrust. Guarding or deflecting first slam prevents thrust. Deflecting or guarding slam causes follow-up swordplay reactions.

![](images/96c3662c630ca7b37dfeb09ffa5da71eec517c691d7e9ec180162efdcdb7bcbc.jpg)  
An exception is the Ground Drive Thrust, which takes a lot longer to land after the shine has reached the tip—wait until the danger symbol starts to fade before you Mikiri.

When dealing Vitality damage at the start of the fight, back away from him and Mikiri Counter the various long range thrust attacks he'll often use as a gap-closer, then deflect his follow-ups to stun him. He turns to the side during this lun, which limits your retaliation options since he'll quickly guard. If you dodge sideways first, you'll end up directly behind his back and can land more attacks before he starts guarding again. He won't always use these followups after every Mikiri counter, but if he doesn't, he'll back off and resets the situation. If you immediately dodge forwards you can usually blind him with Firecrackers before he can react, allowing you to land a thrust or move around to his back to land a couple of blows.

If he backs off to use the Ground Drive Thrust, it's best to sprint away from it, since it's hard to deal with but has a long recovery period that will let you close in and land a sprinting attack. If he starts it right next to you, interrupt it with a quick attack. He'll be open for a while after he uses the guard-crushing  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash combo; if you move in and dodge towards his right side it will miss, letting you land several blows.

Dodging forwards through the second hit of the Double HorizontalSlash also leaves him open for a while, and if he misses the thrust attacks at the end of his combos you'll have enough time to sprint over and attack him before he recovers (watch out for the Step in Thrust, though, since it starts a combo instead). If he holds the spear down by his hip with the point directly facing you, this is the cue for the guard-crushing GroundSlash combo. The first slash is lightning fast, so immediately put your guard up if he starts this stance at close range and prepare to dodge the follow-up.

![](images/7cbbc8cc178b499e7310ab7568d1779762a2fab65ad599c456b64e4228d6e4ac.jpg)  
After a Mikiri Counter he will often follow-up with either a rising slash...

![](images/b9d2c7da6bcc2fe5e46f780bf83baa8fd55346b76307cc5ceead9e63a8eae2cd.jpg)  
...or an overhead slam. Both attacks have a similar deflect timing.

![](images/acfbe5a239825c8fcd754b3d5880e21b649dfbe25d312812a7f7bfa83ed98180.jpg)  
Deflecting either of the follow-ups he frequently uses after a Mikiri Counter will stun him.

Once you've reduced his Vitality below  $75\%$ , you can start to pressure his guard when he misses attacks, aiming to deal Posture damage. Keep Mikiri Countering his thrusts and jump-kick countering his sweeps. Keep alert for the distinctive spin start-up of his  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash combo while you pressure him. Once you've gotten used to the timing for this attack you can land a couple of hits during his wind-up before dodging. After a hit or two on his guard, back away while staying alert for the Vertical Slam Thrust combo—he still uses the follow-up thrust even if the slam misses.

If he deflects you, resist the urge to immediately dodge backwards, because his Vertical Slam Thrust and Quick CounterSlash will catch you. Instead, it's better to stand your ground and deflect them and only then dodge backwards, while you have the advantage. He can also use Perilous Attacks in that situation, so keep an eye out for them. The Ground Drive thrust, the Circular Sweep, and the Step in Thrust are all attacks he frequently uses after you deflect him.

Staying far away from him and timing a Spinning Shuriken into Chasing Slice when he misses his thrusts and leaping attack is a safe way to chip away at his health. Using the Mist Raven can let you vanish behind him, but be careful if he's in the middle of a combo that involves the  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash, since that attack can hit you behind his back. Ichimonji can interrupt all his armored attacks, so you can reliably use it to punish his missed attacks to finish off his Posture, or even react and interrupt the  $1080^{\circ}$ Slash.

![](images/fb76ceb1195b74413f8cd5726e99da8141c1cb58fbecb4da3afef61d33660d1b.jpg)  
The first hit of his GroundSlash combo is another guard crushing attack that will prevent you from guarding his follow-up leaping slam. Dodge to the left instead to avoid it.

# Lone Shadow—Overview

<table><tr><td>Vitality</td><td>18+</td><td>Attack Power</td><td>10+</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Tools</td><td>Skills</td><td>Items</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Gouging Top</td><td>Mikiri Counter</td><td>Fistful of Ash</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Long Spark</td><td>Shinobi Eyes</td><td>Ungo&#x27;s Sugar</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Great Feather Mist Raven</td><td>Chasing Slice</td><td>Ako&#x27;s Sugar</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2"></td><td>Flowing Water</td><td></td></tr></table>

Highly mobile and capable of applying fierce pressure at any range, the Lone Shadow is a difficult opponent to defend against. Using passive hit-and-run strategies will rarely work well. Guarding is generally ill-advised, since they'll follow a guard stun with counter slashes and kicks that make it near impossible to safely chip away

![](images/618abaf09d9cc4df4836e5cf670a5903a265fd8f26b0b7f8ef3846ebbb490a8a.jpg)

at them. They'll even follow up when these attacks are deflected, but the extra recovery time means you get a chance to counter-slash and damage their Posture.

They guard frequently, so it can be difficult to damage their Vitality with punishment or counter-slashes. Once they go on the offensive they are very aggressive, so you'll have little time to patiently regain Posture. It's often best to completely break away and run a long distance before turning around and guarding. They don't allow you much time to heal, often following up their missed attacks with long-ranged gap-closers, and can even react to a close range healing attempt with a perfectly-timed Flying Spin Kick. All of which means you need to make sure you have more than enough space before healing. If you're feeling extremely pressured, Fistfuls of Ash or Firecrackers are a good way to gain time to drink safely.

Lone Shadows can whistle to draw any nearby Hounds into the fight and attack you. Later in the game you'll fight strong enemy variants of the Lone Shadows that are often accompanied by Hounds; use Shuriken to kill them as soon as possible. You can also use the Finger Whistle to drive them berserk; when their owner whistles for them again, they'll often attack the Lone Shadow instead of you.

The most effective way to fight a Lone Shadow is to focus initially on dealing Vitality damage; stay at a distance to bait attacks that you can proactively step dodge and punish, then switch to focusing on Posture damage by pressuring their guard. When focusing on Vitality damage, the attacks with long enough recovery that you

![](images/fcfdae0e811fbb5ac22c0f4270dea6044efff00ca081f3541d2567cd40cd9531.jpg)  
Lone Shadows have the same Posture recovery stance as Samurai Generals, so make sure to interrupt them with a quick attack whenever they back off and start posing with a white aura.

can thrust punish are the same ones they use to chase you down or punch through your guard. When dealing Posture damage, pressuring their guard forces them to retaliate with a more limited set of attacks that are easy to deflect or step dodge.

# Masanaga the Spear-Bearer

You'll encounter Masanaga twice during the course of the game, each at different times in his life. The first time you meet him at the White Serpent Shrine Idol during the Interior Ministry Raid he comes equipped with two Vilehand poison attacks and the ability to buff himself with Yashariku at the cost of some of his health after his first deathblow marker is removed. This buff never runs out, so there's no point in trying to wait it out. Some of his combos are a little different, in that some enders and follow-ups are replaced with the first strike of the Vilehand Strike combo. For example, the slow standing spinning right kick that normally signals the Flying Spin Kick is now followed up by the first hit of the Vilehand Strike combo instead.

Trying to restrict his actions with the deflect loop is not advised, as he can now use the second hit of the Vilehand Strike straight after deflecting you and follow up with the Vilehand Double Slash; this version of the Vilehand Strike is very fast and difficult to react to at close range. It's best to stick with the guard loop. When aiming to damage his Vitality at the start of the fight, the slower Vilehand Strikes are an excellent opportunity, since they can be easily dodged to his back. When he buffs himself with Yashariku it's no longer safe to guard any of his attacks, as his Posture damage increases tremendously. You'll need to rely on deflecting and dodging to avoid having your Posture broken. The Lone Shadow Vilehand you encounter prior to this version of Masanaga acts identically, only lacking the Yashariku buff.

Later in the game you'll encounter a past version of Masanaga in Hirata Estate (Revelation). As a younger man, Masanaga lacks the Vilehand attacks and Yashariku self-buff. His move-set is identical to the Longswordman, but he isn't completely free of tricks. During the fight he'll whistle and summon three Shinobi Hounds to attack you and can summon them three times. The Finger Whistle can make them go berserk, so you can quickly back off and force him to fight his own reinforcements to get rid of them.

# Lunging DiagonalSlash

PROPERTIES CA

Leans over and brings sword behind back then dashes diagonally towards you while slashing. Often follows up with Lunging Leg Sweep. Step dodge towards back then thrust to punish. For Posture damage, guard/deflect then jump-kick counter Lunging Leg Sweep.

# Leaping Hammer Kick

PROPERTIES CA|AA|E(Guard)PDeflect)

Leaps high into the air and spins left leg over head then slams leg down onto ground. Often follows up with Lunging Leg Sweep. Step dodge sideways and punish with thrust. Often does this after attacking his guard, and sometimes after you deflect his attacks.

# Double Spin Kicks

PROPERTIES CA|AA

Runs up, ducks down, and does a jumping double spin kick, left leg first, then right leg from behind mid air. Follows up with Thrust Kick. Kicks are very fast, guard quickly when he suddenly ducks after running at you, then Mikiri Counter the Thrust Kick.

# Flying Spin Kick

PROPERTIES AA | E(Guard) | P(Deflect)

Leaps at you with a yell and delivers a mid-air spinning kick with right leg. Deflecting this attack pushes him back, frequently follows up with Kick Rush. Slight mid-air delay before kick, wait it out before deflect. Dodge left and thrust punish. Often cued by sideways dash.

# Backwards Spin Kick Combo

PROPERTIES CA|AA

Spins into a high backwards heel kick with right leg, then leans back and lunges forwards into two rising sword slashes. Only kick has armor. Often follows-up with Lunging Diagonal Slash or Flying Spin Kick. Kick stumbles, time safety roll to avoid slashes.

# Masanaga the Spear-Bearer, Lone Shadow Vilehand

# Vilehand Strike Combo

PROPERTIES Poison CA E(Deflect)

Unveils his left hand from within robe and dashes into two poison hand stabs usually followed by fast Vilehand Double Slash. Applies poison buildup on hit, guard and deflect. Step dodge left and punish. Doesn't use full combo during swordplay or combo enders.

# Vilehand Double Slash

PROPERTIES Poison | CA | E(Deflect)

Poses with sword pointing at ground and left hand held above head. When close dashes into a quick double slash with the poison hand. Deals damage as well as poison buildup. Step dodge to the left.

![](images/5464b6a56f1fb131cf59bcdc0177a08d39cd3829b2de8ab38c613438a6dbf9ad.jpg)  
Wait out the slight delay on the Thrust Kick as he raises his leg up...

# Counter Right Kick

PROPERTIES Reaction Only | E(Guard) | P(Guard)

Kicks towards your head with his right leg in a compact motion while still standing facing you. Can chain into itself if guarded. Slight delay before kick. Deflect or step dodge backwards.

# BackhandSlashCombo

PROPERTIES CA | Reaction Only | E(Guard)

Winds up one handed backwards slash from right to left then spins into a Thrust Kick. Guarding, deflecting and step dodging prevents the Thrust Kick follow-up, prepare to Mikiri Counter if hit. Step dodge first hit towards back on right side.

# Fast Overhead Slash combo

PROPERTIES Reaction Only E(Deflect)

- Does fast one handed diagonal swing over right shoulder, then spins into a kick with right leg. Deflect or step dodge to back on right.

# Fast Backhand Slash

PROPERTIES Reaction Only | E(Guard) | P(Guard)

Winds up a faster Backhand Slash with no follow-up. Leans in during the slash, dodge or deflect just after he starts moving his sword arm forwards.

# Thrust Kick

PROPERTIES Thrust

Raises right leg up and charges it before thrusting it forwards. Glides forward and tracks early dodge. Only used at end of combos. Wait out charge up before Mikiri Counter; thrust punish after Mikiri. On miss can follow-up with Lunging Diagonal Slash or Flying Spin Kick.

# Lunging Leg Sweep

PROPERTIES Sweep

Ducks down and sweeps in a circle with left leg. Often uses as follow-up after Lunging Diagonal Slash or Leaping Hammer Kick. Long forward range but slow startup. Interrupt with attack to deal damage or jump-kick counter to deal Posture damage.

# Kick Rush

PROPERTIES CA|AA|Reaction Only|E(Deflect)P(Deflect)

Leaps into a four hit kick combo, followed by Thrust Kick. Can step dodge to back on left side. Deflect all four kicks and Mikiri Counter the Thrust Kick to deal massive posture damage.

![](images/1e3497bd48ab24c2c229ddc3f927c45a2141404c19b2ddf422640e78d3bc62c5.jpg)  
...then Mikiri Counter and punish with a thrust.

# Posture damage opportunity.

Deflecting the Flying Spin Kick offers a notable opportunity in this fight, as long as you are confident at deflecting their Kick Rush. Deflecting this attack will push them spinning away from you, and they are extremely likely to retaliate with the Kick Rush after this. Deflecting the entire combo and Mikiri countering the Thrust Kick at the end will deal a lot of Posture damage.

# Lone Shadow - Strategy

Against a Lone Shadow, you should always begin by focusing on depleting his Vitality. This is best accomplished by moving several step dodge's distance away and provoking him into using attacks you can punish. Of the ones he'll most often use when you are constantly backing away from him, the Lunging DiagonalSlash and the Leaping Hammer Kick have a Lunging Leg Sweep follow-up that can be interrupted with a thrust, while the Backwards Spin Kick combo can be interrupted after the sword slashes miss with a quick attack. Be careful of the delayed Flying Spin Kick follow-up; it's better to back away if you're too far and punish that instead.

You can land a thrust of your own any time you Mikiri Counter his Thrust Kick, and backing away often makes him run towards you and use the Double Spin Kicks combo. You can use Firecrackers or Mist Raven to get to his back, and charged Shuriken into Chasing Slice is excellent for punishing in his small recovery windows. Always keep alert for the Flying Spin Kick while backing away, as he often uses it at the end of many of his combos to catch you.

If you don't have the room to back away from him to make this strategy work, it's possible to control a Lone Shadow within a tight space by taking advantage of his swordplay reactions. When you attack his guard then back away, he'll react with a small set of attacks; a single dodge backwards will avoid most of them, allowing you to dodge and counter attack to damage his Vitality, then follow-up with another attack to provoke his guard reactions again. The attacks he uses when you hit his guard are the Counter Right Kick, the Backhand Slash combo, the Fast Backhand Slash, the Leaping Hammer Kick, and a sideways dash into the Flying Spin Kick.

The first three attacks can be avoided by dodging backwards and immediately using a dodge counter-attack, but watch out for the

![](images/a7b8dc3b65880abb75a374216b080b4a599a8760f14d9ff8044f90101bdc66d4.jpg)

The Leaping Leg Slam is a dual opportunity. It's easy to dodge it sideways to deal Vitality damage, then when you want to start dealing Posture damage you can guard/deflect it and jump-kick the follow-up sweep instead.

![](images/051ec1bddada8bf251a91b9c5d278294daca90fc4f86349d18b4a7f5027b76b7.jpg)

Lone Shadows often use the armored Flying Spin Kick as a gap closer when you back away from their combos.

thrust kick after the Backhand Slash combo. Your dodge counterattack can interrupt it, or you can use a Mikiri Counter. If he does the Leaping Hammer Kick you can either dodge it sideways or dodge backwards twice to make it miss, then punish with a thrust. Keep alert for the sideways dash that signals his Flying Spin Kick and prepare to dodge and punish. Most of the time he only uses the first three attacks, so its easy to loop him repeatedly.

Once you've reduced his Vitality, you can take advantage of the same guard reactions to deal Posture damage instead. Instead of dodging backwards, stand your ground and deflect his kicks and slashes, then counter-slash once into his guard to reset the loop. The only two attacks that are trickier to deflect are his Leaping Hammer Kick and the Flying Spin Kick, both of which are easier to dodge left to avoid then punish. If you do guard/deflect the Leaping Hammer Kick, make sure to jump-kick counter the follow-up sweep. An Ako's Sugar greatly increases the effectiveness of this strategy, and can let you kill him with Posture damage alone if taken before you start the fight.

There's another set of reactions you can take advantage of to deal even faster Posture damage if you are comfortable with deflecting a multi-hit consecutive attack. Instead of only hitting his guard once, keep pressuring his guard until he deflects you. He'll only use two attacks directly after deflecting you; the Fast Overhead Slash or the Kick Rush. Deflecting the Fast Overhead slash lets you counter-slash and restart the loop; repeat until he uses the Kick Rush. Deflecting all four kicks of the Kick Rush and then Mikiri Countering the Thrust Kick at the end will do high Posture damage, greatly speeding up the fight. He can still use the Leaping Hammer Kick while you are pressuring his guard though, so hold back your attacks when you see it and prepare to defend.

![](images/d42e56d08d180a705edd6143834cb572b311f038361882a3109b1eb4134cfbff.jpg)

The four initial kicks of the Kick Rush have a steady rhythm despite their chaotic appearance. Listen for the impact sounds when guarding this attack to learn the timing for deflecting them.

# Gyoubu Oniwa

Gyoubu the Demon was once an infamous bandit chief feared throughout the land, but after defeat at Isshin's hands, his strength left such an impression that he was taken in as warrior of Ashina. Although Gyoubu's famed horn-spear was broken during the rebellion, Isshin entrusted him with the cross-shaped spear of general Shuzen Tamura—a weapon he now wields with unmatched ferocity. Serving as Lord Genichiro's

![](images/d5f0d3b1ce09e8a851e839d31232ad3a247b5cb53ea4a56e8ca8ef87a835667e.jpg)

most trusted retainer, Gyoubu currently guards the gates of Ashina atop his imposing armored steed.

# Preparation

Two Gourd Seeds can be obtained before facing Gyoubu; one for defeating General Naomori Kawarada near the Outskirts Wall - Gate Path Idol, and the other picked up immediately past the Chained Ogre's location. Purchase Robert's Firecrackers from the Crow's Bed Memorial Mob to unlock the Shinobi Firecracker tool, since it's quite effective during this battle. If you're struggling, progressing part way through the Hirata Estate allows you to collect enough Prayer Beads to increase your Vitality, and enough tools to unlock the Prosthetic Arts skill tree. Invest a Skill Point into learning the Grappling Hook Attack, since it lets you deal more damage each time you grapple onto Gyoubu. Lastly, equip some Pellets and Ako's Sugar, and don't forget to purchase as many Coin Purses as possible to safeguard your Sen.

![](images/cd0df76f1898e0392fe3aa7c8b2aca6c6a05546150680667b4326565bea50ca6.jpg)

![](images/dd8c95bdafdaa40d234b4bb5cab6645d9426e9ef70e28ad1e4aba0d80e20b54c.jpg)  
Gyoubu won't make his entrance until you move past this point.

The boss area is a large, open battlefield that features uneven terrain and a few obstacles that can obstruct your line of sight and prevent you from grappling onto Gyoubu. Of note are the three watchtowers—two on the eastern half and one in the northwest corner—as well as the sections of wooden fence near the center of the field. These obstacles can all be destroyed if the boss rams into them, but it's best to avoid fighting near them if you can.

Stepping into the fires strewn across the field will slowly drain your Vitality and cause Burn to build up, so be careful. Above all, avoid fighting in the northwest quadrant, as in addition to the cluster of fires found there, it's also possible to inadvertently fall off the edge of the cliff. Instead, do your best to stick to the southern half of the field since it's largely uncluttered.

# Key Strategies

Gyoubu is vulnerable for the entire duration of his introductory animation, so meet him head-on and slash away without hesitation until he rides off. Always stay within grapple distance of the boss as he rides across the battlefield, and latch on whenever he performs a Drift Turn or uses either his Spinning Rope Spear or Piercing Harpoon attacks. In mid-air, delay your Grappling Hook Attack until you're right next to him to ensure that both hits will connect.

Once you've landed, use Firecrackers to startle Gyoubu's steed and briefly stun him, then deal as much damage as possible before he recovers.

Firecrackers can only be used to stun him once every 20 seconds, though, so be sure to wait until at least that much time has elapsed before hitting him with another round. Landing enough hits in quick succession can also result in a stun that's signaled by Gyoubu's steed rear

ing up—use this opportunity to further lower his Vitality whenever it presents itself. During Phase 2, be careful when using Firecrackers, since he'll now respond with a quick recovery slash after being stunned by them. You'll also need to anticipate and jump over the Scraping Grab he's guaranteed to follow up with after his Impaling Charge or if you retreat from his Leaping Stabs.

# Gyoubu Oniwa - Phase 1

Gyoubu lies in ambush next to the northern gate on the opposite side of the battlefield, but the fight only begins once he's detected you. Taking a few steps towards the center of the area will cause him to ride in your direction before stopping to make his entrance; he's completely vulnerable for the duration of this animation, so don't hold back and deal as much damage as possible before he storms off.

Although Gyoubu can use a rope to extend the reach of his spear during a few key attacks, you're generally safe until he rides in close. When this happens, he'll come to a halt and begin relentlessly attacking with his spear until he rides away again. Deflecting can quickly deplete his Posture, but unless you're confident in your timing, it's best to keep your guard up and sprint out of range as he winds up a powerful strike. Always keep a close eye on your Posture and retreat to heal when necessary. Gyoubu is unable to guard against any of your attacks, so slashing at his steed lets you quickly deal both Vitality and Posture damage. You'll need to pick your moments carefully, however, since his inherent Super Armor prevents him from easily being interrupted by your attacks. Land

![](images/e5d12866509db4f2c8f908aea582fd3bda220fc1fd104be49f6c7b9388769d63.jpg)  
Waiting until you're roughly at this height before initiating your Grappling Hook Attack ensures that both hits connect.

ing enough hits will result in a lengthy stun that causes his steed to rear up—always take advantage of this by switching to an all-out offense until he rides away.

The large horn adorning Gyoubu's helmet briefly turns into a grapple point whenever he Drift Turns to change direction; this opens a safe opportunity to close the gap and deal some damage, since grappling at that point will destabilize him. There's enough time to use a Grappling Hook Attack followed by a single slash as you land. Both his Piercing Harpoon and Spinning Rope Spear attacks also present grapple opportunities—hitting him with a Grappling Hook Attack during either of these moves will knock him off the saddle and cause him to hang from its side, which lets you deal additional Posture damage. It's important to always stay within grapple distance whenever he rides away, since you'll otherwise miss out on opportunities to deal damage.

Firecrackers can be used to startle Gyoubu's horse and inflicts a lengthy stun in addition to dealing Posture damage. He's guaranteed to passively ride away after being stunned during Phase 1,

![](images/739218ce6daf254f3787f6dfbab8ed390e582167cf9969c65d9d8b6e0ad1055f.jpg)  
Both his Triple Overhead Slam and Twirling Overhead Crash leave Gyoubu vulnerable if you back away to avoid their delayed final hit.

Simply spamming Firecrackers won't be effective, however, since there's a 20 second cooldown before he can be stunned again using this method. The best moment to use this tool comes directly after landing from a grapple, as this prevents him from starting his offense and lets you deal extra damage. He'll likely Drift Turn after riding away, so be ready to grapple again. Firecrackers can also be used to interrupt his offense if timed as he winds up a slower attack; just remember to space out their use or you'll be left defenseless if they fail to trigger a pun.

As Gyoubu rides in your direction, he'll either make a pass at you by flailing with Alternating Slashes, or he'll come to a halt after performing a quick horizontal slash or delayed Charged Swipe. There's also a possibility that he'll transition into a Spinning Rope Spear following his Alternating Slashes; be prepared to quickly jump and grapple onto him if this happens. The rope itself can't hurt you, so you can safely deal damage from up close. Gyoubu is faster than you, but it's possible to avoid engaging at close-range by continuously sprinting backwards as he approaches or by guarding his attacks before sprinting away as he winds up a slower strike. This tactic has the added benefit of creating plenty of grapple opportunities by causing him to use Drift Turns as he chases you down.

When engaging at close-range, repeatedly dodging towards his vulnerable left flank as he attacks can allow you to land some hits. Be ready to guard his Turnaround Slash, however, since he's almost

# Gyoubu Oniwa - Phase 2

Gyoubu gains a few new attacks after recovering from the initial deathblow, most notably the ability to enter a jousting stance and perform an Impaling Charge following a Drift Turn. This attack hits multiple times in rapid succession, and its strong tracking ensures that you'll get caught if you try to avoid it by sprinting sideways. Because it isn't considered a thrust, it's best to stand your ground and guard instead. After finishing his Impaling Charge, Gyoubu drags the tip of his spear across the ground and attempts to grab you as he rides next to you; jump over his spear when you see the Danger Symbol appear and slash at him in mid-air. This Scraping Grab deals severe damage and will likely kill you if it connects, so learning to anticipate it is crucial. If you fall in battle at any point, Gyoubu will repeatedly circle your corpse—coming back to life causes him to ride away though, so it's safe to immediately heal (using Pellets if your Healing Gourd is empty).

The other attack Gyoubu gains is a series of two Leaping Stabs used when engaging you at close-range. Both stabs can easily be avoided by continuously sprinting sideways towards his vulnerable left flank the moment his steed leaps upwards, but watch out if you retreat instead, since he'll chase you with a Scraping Grab after landing from the second jump. Lastly, Firecrackers are less effective during Phase 2, since Gyoubu now uses a recovery slash after being stunned with this tool. This vertical slash features exceptional tracking properties, so it's important to begin guarding after a maximum of two slashes. If you have any Spirit Emblems remaining, switch to the Flame Vent and set him ablaze during openings instead of using Firecrackers. Outside of these changes, the battle unfolds identically, so continue using the previously mentioned tactics until the opportunity to perform a Finisher Deathblow presents itself.

guaranteed to use it to reposition himself. Some of his slower attacks also feature strong tracking, so be careful if you see him rotate sharply in your direction as he winds up. Learn to recognize both his Triple Overhead Slam and Twirling Overhead Crash combos, since deflecting their delayed final hit will create an opening to deal damage with a thrust before he recovers. When aiming to deflect, keep a bit of distance or it'll be difficult to clearly see which attack he's about to use next. If the Danger Symbol appears, watch out for his Piercing Harpoon since it can't be countered with a Mikiri. Instead, immediately jump or sprint sideways before grappling onto him.

# Lady Butterfly

Lady Butterfly was one of the Wolf's teachers, appointed by the Owl to mentor him. Having spent her childhood training in Usui's forest where mist and mystifications were commonplace, she became a master of illusion techniques. With theses abilities, she was able to

![](images/b6fe0bae6e1e5c7c1a4d7c14aa635f97fe3790a88d046a2a13ace2122b99747e.jpg)

strictly train the young warrior in the shinobi way using direct combat. Why she seeks to take Lord Kuro, however, is known only to her.

# Preparation

Lady Butterfly can be fought at any point during your journey, so remember that it's always possible to return to her later if you're struggling. Her stats will increase as the game progresses, however, so she'll always remain a challenge. If you choose to tackle her early, defeating Gyoubu beforehand lets you raise your Attack Power and gives you access to many areas and NPCs from which Gourd Seeds can be acquired. Of note is the one sold by the Battlefield Memorial Mob and the one obtained from a chest just before reaching the Upper Tower - Antechamber idol in Ashina Castle.

Equipping the Loaded Shuriken is essential as it allows you to force her to the ground. Both Firecrackers and Fistful of Ash can be used to briefly blind her and create openings. Assign Whirlwind Slash to your combat arts if you've unlocked it and travel to the Underbridge Valley idol to collect the five Snap Seeds growing in a tree near the palanquin. They'll prove effective against her minions. If you're adept at deflecting, both the Ascending and Descending Carp skills from the Ashina Arts tree are well worth investing into.

![](images/459b8919c52db8af4ab6f470ccce2a803dea9015e8a5167e9b0bea70096e7f06.jpg)

# Environment

The burning temple in which you face Lady Butterfly is much longer than it is wide, and its tall ceiling is supported by a column of four, evenly-spaced pillars on each side. There's plenty of room to maneuver around each of the eight pillars, so they act as perfect cover from the boss' projectiles when you need to heal or recover your Posture. With that said, it's best to fight along the length of the middle section as you'll often need space to retreat. If she moves to the space between the pillars and sidewalls, avoid fighting there and draw her towards the center instead. The fire eventually spreads to the base of the pillars as the battle reaches its climax, but this is purely cosmetic and doesn't inflict Burn build-up.

# Key Strategies

Focus on guarding or deflecting Lady Butterfly's strikes and take advantage of the brief pauses between her combos to deal some Posture damage with basic attacks. Keep your offense compact, since her Double Kunai Sweep can easily catch you off guard otherwise. Use Shuriken to force her to the ground whenever she jumps to a steel wire; this inflicts Posture damage and gives you an opening to lower her Vitality with a thrust as she lands. Time your

Shuriken throws so they catch her in mid-air to prevent her from deflecting them.

At the start of Phase 2, surprise her with a thrust or powerful combat art the moment she lands at the foot of the statue, then immediately throw a Shuriken followed by a Chasing Slice to prevent her from summoning her minions. Hit her with another Shuriken whenever she retreats with a backstep since this signals that

she'll attempt to summon them again. If she succeeds, stay away from her or she'll join the fray; focus on eliminating as many minions as possible before she activates her Butterfly Barrage. Using a Snap Seed instantly dispels all nearby minions, but these items are quite limited so use them sparingly. Watch out for her Slashing Frenzy combo and sprint away to avoid both her slashes and the homing butterflies before punishing her.
