# Lady Butterfly - Phase 1

Lady Butterfly is an exceptionally agile opponent that has the unique ability to jump atop razor-thin steel wires placed at different heights. This allows her to stay out of harm's way and to set up a variety of dangerous attacks; keeping track of her as she darts across the room is essential so be sure to lock on again if her fast movements (or the pillars) cause the targeting to disengage. Her melee combos all feature multiple quick hits and can transition into retreating or advancing volleys of kunai projectiles—this makes her a threat at any range, so it's important to always stay on your guard when facing this boss.

Breaking her Posture and landing a Deathblow is the main objective, but accomplishing this can prove challenging without first dealing Vitality damage to slow down her Posture recovery rate. She'll guard most strikes from the front, so you'll need to create openings by dodging certain key attacks or by knocking her out of the sky with Shuriken. Whirlwind Slash can also prove useful, since its slashes can pierce through her guard, but avoid using this combat art carelessly since it can leave you vulnerable.

![](images/a32b54a719b56eb0a244ec777abc462a68fc99d36de2f625904f6fec0a448516.jpg)  
Prepare for Lady Butterfly's Axe Kick Combo when she assumes this pose. Deflect twice in quick succession and dodge the kick sideways to create an opening.

![](images/1779cbd16b0a058f593d59d80f55177abfdf54e14db2d803e962a2e7f4b2e025.jpg)  
Watch out for Lady Butterfly's Roundhouse Counter when her back is turned in this manner.

# Shuriken Tactics

Shuriken can be used to deal Posture damage and knock Lady Butterfly to the ground whenever she's airborne; this creates an opening to sprint towards her and lower her Vitality with a thrust while she's vulnerable. Properly timing your Shuriken throws is crucial, since she can deflect them when idling atop a wire. Always aim to catch her in the middle of a jump as she can't guard while in that state. Learn to recognize her Dismounting Kunai Toss and throw a Shuriken just as she's preparing to drop from the wire—this move is always used after her Ascension Kick, so it can easily be anticipated. Using this tactic to interrupt her Aerial Kick Slam or Aerial Leg Grab might seem like a good idea, but it isn't recommended since your Shuriken will miss unless timed at the last second.

Lady Butterfly's highly aggressive nature makes her quite intimidating, but keeping your guard up (if your Vitality gauge is full) allows you to withstand her offense for lengthy periods of time. Take advantage of this to get a feel for which attacks leave her vulnerable, as well as to internalize the timing required to deflect her various combos. It's worth noting that many of her fast attack strings (such as her Flowing Combo) lock you in a guard state after guarding the

first hit, so there's no risk in attempting to deflect subsequent hits unless there's a significant delay between them. When up close, her Axe Kick Combo should always be regarded as an opportunity to deal damage—guard or deflect the first two slashes, then dodge the delayed axe kick to the right before hitting her exposed flank with a dodge counterattack. The same can be said of the Aerial Kick Slam, since dodging this move leaves her wide open.

Pressing your offense after dealing direct damage or during the short pause at the end of her melee combos lets you weaken her Posture by forcing her to guard. However, it's best to stick with no more than two guard-pressuring hits. Since she can retaliate with a quick Roundhouse Counter if she deflects (or when you deflect her attacks). Anticipate this counter kick and prepare to deflect it whenever her back is slightly turned following either of these swordplay interactions. If the Danger Symbol appears when Lady Butterfly is grounded during Phase 1, this signals her deadly Dou

# Lady Butterfly - Phase 2

Lady Butterfly's corpse will vanish at the beginning of Phase 2, and she'll soon reappear on the left shoulder of the gigantic statue at the back of the temple. Lock on and prepare for her to land between the two nearest pillars where she'll be briefly vulnerable. Hit her with a thrust from behind, then get ready to throw a Shuriken followed by a Chasing Slice to prevent her from summoning her minions. This will cause her to fight normally for a short period before retreating and attempting to summon again. Repeatedly preventing her from summoning is tricky, so it's likely that she'll succeed at some point. Note that she can summon multiple times during a fight, but she'll only attempt to do so again once you've lowered her Posture. Keep your distance from the boss once her minions have joined the fray, since she'll stick to throwing a few kunai volleys from a distance unless you get close. If she dismounts and joins in, sprinting around the room until she triggers her Butterfly Barrage is the safest option.

Beyond her ability to summon minions, many of Lady Butterfly's moves are now modified by the addition of phantom butterflies that feature light homing capabilities. These projectiles travel relatively slowly but deal Spirit damage—as such, guarding will only reduce a small percentage of their damage output. While they can generally be avoided by sprinting or dodging sideways, specific methods are required to completely avoid the homing butterflies tied to each of her attacks, so refer to the notes in the Key Attack table for more details. With that said, the most important addition to her arsenal is the Slashing Frenzy combo she frequently uses from this point on; it's signaled by a lunging kick and two homing butterflies. Avoid this lengthy combo by sprinting away from the boss until she closes it out with a lunging sweep. Either deal direct damage with a thrust, or counter the sweep with a jump-kick to weaken her Posture.

![](images/bf6090eec1123d130ee4a7a4f9b40814ec99fea2526e615db65d62000d9b2471.jpg)  
Sprinting around the outer perimeter of the room is a good way to avoid the homing butterflies spawned by the boss' Butterfly Barrage.

ble Kunai Sweep. This move is armored and has a short wind-up, so keeping your offense compact prevents you from being unable to react if she surprises you with it. She can respond with this sweep after you deflect, and it also features plenty of forward momentum if used unprompted at a distance. Treat it as a constant threat and be ready to counter it with a jump-kick to weaken her Posture.

Her Aerial Leg Grab should be considered a serious threat whenever she's perched on a high wire. This move features good tracking but somewhat limited range, so drop your guard and preemptively start moving backwards whenever she backflips onto a high wire (although it's similar to a backflip, her Ascension Kick never leads into this grab). Continue retreating and prepare to dodge when the Danger Symbol appears. This puts you in the perfect spot to punish her with a thrust as she lands, but jumping or sprinting backwards are both viable alternatives. If cornered when the Danger Symbol appears, sprinting underneath her is your best option.

![](images/221844473020b0de5fb5e6415138683204e76f254ad245ae7a56f715f321676d.jpg)  
Begin sprinting away from the boss when she's readying her Slashing Frenzy.

# Phantom Minions

A group of illusory enemies appears near the temple's center point when Lady Butterfly snaps her fingers during Phase 2. Each of them wields one of three weapons: a plow, a spear, or a knife. They only have access to basic melee attacks but it's important to avoid letting them surround you; the spear variant features a thrusting attack that can't be guarded, so be especially careful around them. Minions have low Vitality, but more appear to replace the ones that are killed. Eventually, Lady Butterfly will snap her fingers again to transform any remaining minions into homing butterflies used to power her Butterfly Barrage attack. The more minions on the field, the more projectiles will soon be heading your way—hide behind a pillar and begin sprinting away if the boss draws near. Unlike other homing butterflies, the ones used during the Butterfly Barrage won't deal damage when guarded. Be careful, though, since this can easily result in a Posture-break.

Minions have a high chance of dropping a Spirit Emblem when defeated, so they can be taken out with basic attacks to replenish your supplies if low. Throwing Shuriken from a distance is a much safer way to dispatch them, but you'll spend more emblems than you get in return when using this method. Snap Seeds can instantly dispel any nearby minions and prevent more from spawning, but only go for this option during promising attempts, since these items are quite rare. It's important to always keep track of the boss during all this, since accidentally getting too close will cause her to join the fray.

# Genichiro Ashina

The illegitimate grandson of Isshin Ashina. His insecurities about his birth and his desire to reach the same heights as his grandfather caused Genichiro to constantly hone himself on the battlefield from a young age. He is expert in both katana and bow, and leads the Ashina Ninja, the Nightjars. With his country on

![](images/25580e6f77ae3a1f8577506261a11240ce5c7873cfe65a8ab70b20c13ff19a5e.jpg)

the brink of defeat, Genichiro took to heretical arts and mastered the Lightning of Tomoe. He now seeks Kuro's immortal powers in order to save Ashina from distress.

# Preparation

Upgrade your Healing Gourd to hold at least five charges and equip some Pellets, since this is a lengthy battle. If you're struggling, seeking out an extra Gourd Seed or Vitality upgrade can make a significant difference. Shuriken are the best tool during this encounter as they can interrupt some of Genichiro's attacks. Upgrading to the Spinning Shuriken increases their effectiveness by forcing him to guard multiple hits, and learning the Chasing Slice skill lets you instantly close the gap after a throw. The Loaded Umbrella or Shinobi Firecracker are fine secondary choices; the former can be used to protect yourself against most attacks when cornered while the latter stuns him and synergizes with Chasing Slice. Be sure to pick up the Eel Livers found in Ashina Castle and equip both Akos Sugar and Ungo's Sugar. Lastly, Fistful of Ash can be used to briefly blind Genichiro and buy yourself some time to heal or land a hit.

![](images/00d61cab3454da6cf2eb3974296d4820807a4812b0f8d94921d657414d39450b.jpg)

This flat area at the summit of Ashina Castle is almost entirely devoid of obstacles and affords plenty of room to maneuver, but you won't have the luxury of cover to hide behind when attempting to heal or use items. Invisible walls prevent you from leaving the battle by jumping over the balcony railings. There are decorative samurai statues and an opened set of doors alongside the back wall, as well as two supporting structures on the opposite end; none of these obstacles can be destroyed and they can hinder your movements when fighting next to them. Try to stick closer to the center of the room, except when pressuring Genichiro, and do your best not to get cornered.

Obey the Code. Enact your vengeance and rescue Lord Kuro.

# Key Strategies

Put Genichiro on the back foot by using a compact offense consisting of a basic slash followed by a guard-pressuring slash the moment he guards. He will either get hit and allow you to repeat the process, or respond with one of the following moves: quick diagonal slash, Leaping Helmbreaker, Counter Thrust, Slashing Frenzy, or evasive backstep. Make sure to never attack after he deflects, and instead focus on defend

ing against his counter of choice before going back on the offensive. Close the gap with a Shuriken and Chasing Slice whenever he tries to escape. Use this to corner Genichiro and quickly break his Posture during Phases 1 & 2.

In Phase 3, jump and perform a Lightning Reversal whenever he uses one of his newly-introduced Shock attacks. This inflicts a lengthy

stun and deals severe Vitality and Posture damage. He's more dangerous at this stage, so remain outside of his sword range and punish his Lunging Impale with a Mikiri Counter followed by a thrust to deal some damage. Eel Livers can be used to make Lightning Reversal safer, but they're quite limited so make them count.

# Genichiro Ashina - Phase 1

Unlike your first encounter in the prologue, Genichiro makes full use of his bow here, so watch him closely and be ready to guard at any range. Most of the various sword slashes he opens his combos with can be avoided with a well-timed forward dodge—this places you directly behind him, where you can deal damage with a few basic attacks or a combat art such as Ichimonji. While Genichiro can be aggressive, he will often pause and slowly pace sideways before making his next move; this gives you breathing space and presents a safe opportunity to attack. Finding openings to deplete his Vitality is important, but your focus should be on breaking his Posture to land a deathblow. Pressuring Genichiro through swordplay is the best way to accomplish this, as it limits his ability to use certain attacks.

When the battle begins, he always opens with a bow shot followed by a TumblingSlash to close the gap. Guard or deflect this slash, then immediately retaliate with a basic attack followed by a guard-pressuring slash the instant your sword clashes with his guard. This brief two-hit combo should form the cornerstone of your offense, as slashing at him randomly will only lead to taking damage after he deflects and counters. Always watch for the distinct orange hit effect signaling that your slash has been deflected and familiarize yourself with the timing required to deflect either of the quick diagonal slashes he often responds with. Not only will this damage his Posture, but it also allows you to instantly transition into a Counter-Slash to continue pressuring him. Whenever you land a hit, introduce a slight pause before starting another combo and aim to drive him into a corner to prevent him from escaping.

When Genichiro goes on the offensive, guarding can allow you to withstand most of his blows. Properly reacting to his many Perilous Attacks is crucial, however, since he has access to a mix of Thrusts, Sweeps, and Grabs. His Gut Punch Grab is particularly deadly if it connects—the trick is to recognize the spinning hop slash that always precedes it and then use a basic attack to cause Genichiro to stumble as he's running towards you. When this happens, always follow with a thrust to deal some Vitality damage. Watch out for his Sweeping Slash too—it isn't used as often, but the bow shot that follows can easily catch you off guard. Hold your ground and jump over the slash, then guard the arrow as you land.

Keep an eye on your own Posture and Vitality, and retreat by dashing away when necessary. Always expect him to ready a Charged Shot the moment you begin healing; there's just enough time to dodge sideways the moment he fires. If you're far enough away, it's even possible to simplyStrafe while healing to narrowly avoid the arrow.

# Swordplay Reactions

Genichiro responds in a few different ways under pressure, so learning how to deal with each of his potential reactions is essential. When he retreats with a backstep, it's often to surprise you with an Aerial Barrage using his bow—throw a Shuriken followed by a Chasing Slice to interrupt him and deal some damage. If he attacks with a Leaping Helmbreaker, expect a Quick Thrust which you can counter with a Mikiri to deal significant Posture damage. Another possibility is an armored Counter Thrust that won't be interrupted by your basic slashes—quickly perform a Mikiri if you see the Danger Symbol appear after striking his guard. Lastly, there's a Slashing Frenzy combo that only continues if you deflect its two initial slashes—if you're confident, deflecting the entire combo will greatly weaken his Posture but be careful as it can result in your own Posture being broken if you fail. Always use a safety roll when knocked down or Posture-broken, since Genichiro can try to finish you off with a downwards stab.

![](images/eb9be520395ae2ee70c6ed27269f6b1a8dc8c5e02a8bc584812a4b129004b1ba.jpg)  
Dodging sideways when Genichiro performs this kick creates an opening to land a direct hit.

# Genichiro Ashina - Phase 2

The key difference during Phase 2 is that Genichiro's Leaping Helmbreaker can now also lead into a Circular Sword Sweep. Watch the glint on his sword closely when the Danger Symbol appears following this attack, then either jump or counter with a Mikiri. If you

![](images/5c888fe21d31a47cd7b25c5da8c879b99a70aebb65d6fe0d40f59a7488002624.jpg)  
Guard or deflect the floating slash that precedes Genichiro's Gut Punch Grab...

retreat out of range during his Slashing Frenzy combo, he's now able to cancel into a bow shot to catch you by surprise. Put your guard up or quickly throw a Fistful of Ash to interrupt him before rushing back in to resume your offense.

![](images/db5c4a82f9c8a3963a73bf1c92b7645c3a398341d4ce5b9b98c12cb5684ecaae.jpg)  
...then strike him before he grabs to interrupt and create an opening.

# Genichiro, Way of Tomoe - Phase 3

Phase 3 is where things really heat up, as Genichiro sheds his armor and calls upon the Lightning of Tomoe to power a trio of Shock-infecting Perilous Attacks. He's far more aggressive, runs faster, and has a new Lunging Impale thrust used to quickly close the gap. He uses this attack often, but it can easily be countered with a Mikiri to weaken his Posture before hitting him with a thrust. He'll also use this attack whenever you try to heal, so make sure to first retreat outside of its significant reach to avoid taking damage. Deflecting or getting hit by a Lunging Impale will cause Genichiro to use his Rushdown Grab; immediately sprint away from him since he'll run straight at you. If there's no room to retreat, quickly jumping sideways or deploying the Umbrella can save you. Prepare to counter his Lunging Impale with a Mikiri the moment you gain control at the beginning Phase 3.

Be careful when pressuring Genichiro since he can now respond with a Sweeping Slash in addition to his lightning attacks. The latter are all signaled with the Danger Symbol and can be recognized by the angle at which he jumps. Each of them can be avoided with a well-timed lateral dodge, but the timing required varies slightly depending on the attack. Never attempt to guard or deflect them from a grounded position, or you'll take severe damage. The best way to deal with these attacks is to purposefully get hit in mid-air by jumping just as Genichiro reaches the apex of his own jump. This will re

sult in taking a small amount of damage as you catch the lightning, but immediately pressing the attack button lets you discharge it back at him. Focusing on this tactic is the key to making Phase 3 easier, as you can break his Posture quicker once his Vitality has been lowered. Lastly, watch out for the delayed Counter Thrust he now uses after you deflect the final hit of his Slashing Frenzy combo; wait for the Danger Symbol to appear before countering it with a Mikiri.

![](images/06f15c79d64aa911cd7b154ea23a9e43a7af722a48066be57b59756a88fb2eee.jpg)  
Jumping forward as Genichiro readies a Shock-inflicting attack can help mitigate the Lightning Reversal's limited range.

![](images/62f1ffda484d43877a962710cc545adf0b15212be6e28f0e49623f2b3653566e.jpg)  
This stance signals an incoming Lightning Cleave or Lightning Swipe.

![](images/29d4b2b6f8c7e756eb3c1cd0265dc6bb26f593dd781fef9bb406fbb00c803a0f.jpg)  
Be sure to immediately discharge the lightning before touching the ground!

# Guardian Ape

A giant ape that has been infested and gained immortality. The large blade lodged in his neck is thought to have once belonged to a master swordsman whom it fought long ago. Once, the Guardian Ape shared his den with his mate. But he alone became infested, and his still-mortal mate eventually died. Now, all that remains of his mate are the flowers he grows in offering to her spirit.

# Multiple Encounters

You'll initially encounter the Guardian Ape in Sunken Valley Passage. There you'll remove the beast's head during battle, but it will fight on regardless. When the battle ends the Ape is seemingly dead, but he'll turn up again in Ashina Depths in an area known as the Guardian Ape's Burrow. There you'll battle him again, this time alongside his mate. After this battle you can use the Mortal Blade to sever the Ape's immortality. This will put a final end to him and will reward you with the Bestowal Ninjutsu.

# Preparation

Upgrade your Healing Gourd to hold at least six (but preferably seven) charges and seek out enough Prayer Beads to raise your Vitality to 14 or higher if you're struggling. During Phase 1, equip both the Spring-load Flame Vent and Shinobi Firecracker, then swap out to the Loaded Spear and Loaded Umbrella during Phase 2. Oil can increase the effectiveness of your Flame Vent attacks. Stock up on Pacifying Agent by purchasing it from Fujioka the Info

# Environment

This encounter takes place on a large, shallow lake that provides plenty of space to sprint around the Guardian Ape's attacks. The trees scattered across the lake's surface and the suspended roots that line its border serve as unmountable grapple points when in need of a quick escape. Note that the trees can be destroyed as the boss stomps about. Two patches of tall grass can be used to momentarily hide after blinding the Ape with Firecrackers during Phase 1—one is near the overlook from which you drop, and the other is near the waterfall in the back. He'll soon find you, but this can be used to safely heal or recover some Spirit Emblems with the Ceremonial Tanto. An invisible wall prevents you from getting cornered next to the waterfall but try to stick to the center of the lake and avoid the two nooks found along the lake's western border.

Broker or by farming it from Infested Prisoners in the Abandoned Dungeon. If you visit the Dungeon, be sure to also obtain the Ceremonial Tanto by defeating the Shichimen Warrior found there. Investing in the various Karma skills lets you carry more Spirit Emblems to fuel the use of your tools. Mid-air Combat Arts or Mid-air Prosthetic Tool can both help you increase the damage dealt after jumping over the boss' attacks.

# Key Strategies

The Guardian Ape is highly weak against fire and hitting him with a charged Flame Blast from the Spring-Load Flame Vent is a guaranteed way to inflict the Burn status; this incapacitates him and gives you a few seconds to freely attack before he recovers. Dousing the boss in Oil lets you inflict Burn with a single uncharged Flame Breath if you don't have access to the upgraded version of this tool. Create openings by continuously sprinting

out of reach of the Ape's attacks, then move in to strike while he's recovering. Grapple onto him when he slowly walks sideways or uses his Intimidating Roar and deal damage with a Grappling Hook Attack.

During Phase 2, steer clear of his Terrifying Scream and use Pacifying Agent to remove Terror build up if necessary. Deflecting the

headless Ape's various slashes and stabs causes him to use a Giant Overhead Slam that can in turn be deflected to topple him. From there, use the Loaded Spear on his gaping neck wound to drag out the parasite nested inside of him and deal a large burst of Vitality and Posture damage. Use the Ceremonial Tanto if you run out of Emblems and still have plenty of healing charges left.

# Guardian Ape - Phase 1

The Guardian Ape attacks in a savage and uncontrolled manner so going toe-to-toe with him isn't recommended. His various swipes and slashes have considerable reach and feature plenty of forward momentum, but it's possible to make use of the large area to continuously sprint just outside of his range until there's an opening to strike—pull in when the Ape retreats and back away if he starts attacking and gets too close. This boss has plenty of Posture but lacks the ability to guard any of your attacks, so the goal is solely to deplete his Vitality during Phase 1. He's quite agile and can quickly attack as he recovers, so guarding or deflecting will often be needed to withstand his offense until there's an opportunity to retaliate or retreat. Keep an eye on your Posture and be sure to immediately transition into a brace-guard or safety roll if you get hit since almost all his blows result in a stumble or knockdown. Heal and recover your Posture as soon as the Ape retreats or there's a lull in the action.

# Burning the Ape

The Ape is distracted as you drop into the lake and he won't turn around until you get closer; this presents a perfect opportunity to rush in and set him ablaze with a charged Flame Blast before he has a chance to act. Applying the Burn status stuns the boss long enough for you to slash at him multiple times but get ready to sprint out of reach when he starts getting up. Wait until he stops burning, then look for an opening to use another Flame Blast once he leaves himself vulnerable. Both his Brutal Combo and Leaping Dung Throw feature lengthy recovery and there's enough time to hit him with a Flame Blast after jumping over his Snatching Grab. Dousing the boss in Oil increases the damage dealt by the flames and lets you apply Burn with a single uncharged Fire Breath. Using the Flame Vent is a great way to severely weaken the Ape during Phase 1 but try to conserve a few of your Emblems in preparation for Phase 2.

![](images/38c1f378f18d97dc7ed6f14b77c5289c448c7cb38660d952a3e127c89a06a659.jpg)  
Striking the Guardian Ape's head deals double the Posture damage. Take advantage of this after his Brutal Combo.

![](images/efd17dd0d59a939beecaf5bedd89501ad766bc5b919e7b72765cd43e3e85306f.jpg)  
Steer clear of the Ape's flailing limbs after his Scraping Uppercut causes him to fall, then hit him as he gets back up.

The Guardian Ape can't be easily interrupted due to his inherent Super Armor, but hitting him enough times in quick succession (or with heavier hits such as Ichimonji) will result in a stun. Reacting quickly and continuing to hack away at him will extend this stun until he's forced to retreat; always press your offense the instant a stun happens since this is the best time to pile on damage. Be careful when attacking up close, however, since the Ape's Snatching Grab is relatively fast and can easily kill you. Watch for him to briefly hop and extend his right arm, then jump to avoid getting grabbed. Once the Guardian Ape's Vitality reaches the  $60\%$  mark, his devastating Pouncing Grab also comes into play; this grab is signaled by the boss closing in on you while walking in an upright stance. Wait for the Danger Symbol to appear and immediately sprint towards him and to the side. This will cause the Guardian Ape to leap past you and gives you an opening to deal damage by turning around and attacking while he's vulnerable.

The sword stuck in the Ape's neck becomes a grapple point whenever he slowly walks sideways or when he stops and lets out an Intimidating Roar. Quickly move within grapple range and hit him with a Grappling Hook Attack followed by two slashes or a charged Flame Blast upon landing. Stop attacking at that point (unless you've stunned him) since the Evasive Stomps he often uses to retreat can easily catch you off guard. Be on the lookout for the boss' Double Swipe Combo, as it causes him to spin around and sit down with his back exposed to you. Wait instead of attacking, since there's a chance that the Ape will quickly turn around and surprise you with his Fist Pound Combo. If he sits there for a second, expect him to retreat while Breaking Wind. Sprint around the cloud of noxious fumes to avoid getting poisoned and chase the boss down in anticipation of his incoming Leaping Dung Throw.

# Guardian Ape (Headless) - Attacks

At a distance or after Breaking Wind, the Guardian Ape will squat and defecate in his hand to signal his Leaping Dung Throw. This move features an obvious and lengthy windup period, so learn to recognize it and move in directly beneath the Ape while he's jumping; this gives you a clear opening to safely deal damage once he lands. If you're too far away when he uses this attack, sprint sideways to avoid the dung pile and move in to strike with a thrust attack if there's time. Once the Guardian Ape's Vitality has been depleted, perform a finisher deathblow to decapitate him—the battle hasn't been won yet, so move away from his corpse then use the Ceremonial Tanto to recover Emblems and heal if necessary.

![](images/21e4939e8ad3c32ec14ef460a5c0e86bc14a17ca688a983df12c334617743451.jpg)  
Watch out when the Guardian Ape walks upright since this can signal a Surprise Swipe or Pouncing Grab.

# Guardian Ape (Headless) — Phase 2

After seemingly being down for the count, the now headless Ape springs back to life and picks up both his severed head along with the large sword previously lodged in his neck. His movements become sinuous and unpredictable, and he gains an entirely new repertoire of attacks. Firecrackers or the Flame Vent can no longer be used to stun him, so swap to the Loaded Spear and Umbrella

![](images/adb417bbac763441f845b00d3f1dd7eb78602f17711b85ce0c933b2ffbab7ae9.jpg)  
Deflect the Ape's stabs be pressing the guard button at this very moment.

![](images/77d71c7f09903c85062c9e5902d31c2073aca824dd8b2a2e9c36499ddc61d138.jpg)  
Prepare to deflect the boss' Giant Overhead Slam when he fully raises his sword...

instead. Continuously sprinting out of reach and moving in to deal damage when there's an opening is still a viable tactic, but deflecting his sword-based attacks lets you set up large damage dealing opportunities by causing him to respond with his Giant Overhead Slam. Deflecting this slow, but powerful slam topples the boss and exposes the wound on his neck; it's then possible to deal a burst of Vitality and Posture damage by using the Spear to drag the parasite out of his neck before rushing in to pile on even more damage while he's stunned. If you're having trouble deflecting, use the Umbrella to make the timing easier—just be sure to have enough Spirit Emblems left to use the Spear once the boss falls over.

The Ape will often try to reattach his head before letting out a Terrifying Scream that gradually inflicts both damage and Terror build up; this scream can quickly prove fatal, so immediately sprint out of its large radius the instant he stops and brings his left hand towards his neck. Using Pacifying Agent can help reduce the Terror build up but you'll still take damage, so avoid this attack at all cost.

The headless Ape also has access to a Leaping Sword Sweep that features an obvious and lengthy windup. This attack should always be viewed as an opportunity to deal damage; jump just as the boss starts coming down from his vertical leap and deal damage the moment he lands. His other perilous attack, the Wide Sweep, is trickier to avoid since it's much faster: look for the Ape to crouch forward when the Danger Symbol appears and immediately jump over his sword.

Watch out for his Sliding Slash whenever he dives on his stomach and slides towards you; jumping forward and to the left allows you to clear the horizontal sword slash and puts you directly next to the boss's exposed flank. From there, you can hit him with a thrust or combat art. The four-hit Stabbing Combo he often uses features a lot of forward momentum, but the stabs can easily be deflected by timing your button presses a split second after he finishes pulling the sword back. Successfully deflecting his slashes or stabs can lead into a variety of reactions, including a faster, but shorter version of his Terrifying Scream and a Frenzy Combo that ends with a variation of the Giant Overhead Slam. Watch out for the Fakeout Sweep he can surprise you with after you deflect a rightward slash, though, since it's quite fast. Getting comfortable with deflecting his various slashes can greatly speed up this fight, but don't forget to retreat whenever you need to heal or recover your Posture.

![](images/fbc7481a82d990a8739449c673298f4e6335f3367067e7c6ffd8fbe5779e1467.jpg)  
...then drag out the parasite by using the Loaded Spear on his exposed wound!

![](images/f4ef355523168ee23595105074d7b00c32ab034fab8c5742cd209baa087e7682.jpg)  
Deploying the Loaded Umbrella shields you from the Terrifying Scream's effects and allows you to get close and deal damage as it ends.

![](images/1fbd9713fadbe45e65565755f49a48b517dee79be1719ebc26403486b134efea.jpg)

After having been defeated at Bodhisattva Valley, the headless Guardian Ape can be fought again in his burrow near the Poison Pool idol in the Ashina Depths. The same tactics utilized during Phase 2 of your previous

encounter with this undying beast still apply, but he'll be easier to topple since he now always uses his Giant Overhead Slam following a Leaping Sword Sweep, Frenzy Combo, or Sinuous Slashing Combo. As before, deflecting this powerful overhead slam sets up an opportunity to deal a burst of Vitality and Posture damage by dragging out the parasite with the Loaded Spear. This time, however, do your best to conserve as many Spirit Emblems as possible for what comes after you land the first deathblow.

Stocking up on Pacifying Agent before choosing to engage is highly recommended since his Terrifying Scream is still just as dangerous.

The Guardian Ape has less Vitality and Posture than he had during the previous fight, so it's possible to overpower him much more quickly. Ichimonji (especially Double) is quite powerful and can be used to quickly weaken the boss' Posture whenever there's an opening. At the start of the fight, the Guardian Ape is found leaning against the burrow's back wall and won't notice your presence until you move closer—sprint in to deal as much damage as possible but immediately retreat or use the Loaded Umbrella if he signals his Terrifying Scream.

# Guardian Ape Couple - Phase 2

Once you've landed a deathblow, the Guardian Ape retreats to the edge of the cave and cries out to summon his mate; following this, a smaller Female Ape joins the fray by dropping down from the hole in the ceiling. Only the Guardian Ape needs to be defeated, but it's best to focus on eliminating the far weaker Female Ape first so you can fight the boss unhindered. She'll slash and roar after landing, so back off and keep your distance instead of trying to rush in and immediately attack her. You'll now have to deal with both enemies simultaneously, but the Female Ape will stay behind her companion and remain passive unless he attacks with either a Sliding Slash, Leaping SwordSlash, or Terrifying Scream. She'll move in to defend him while he's recovering from either of these moves, and the attacks she'll use at that point are determined by which attack the Headless Ape just performed; this makes her behavior extremely predictable. The Female Ape will go back to being passive after completing an attack, but be careful when getting close, since she can often perform a quick Surprise Swipe before retreating.

Stunning the Female Ape and depleting her Posture with multiple back-to-back Firecrackers can allow you to quickly land a deathblow, but attempting to do this while constantly dodging the Guardian Ape's attacks is a bit risky. Instead, remain locked on to him and sprint around the edge of the cave to avoid his pressure (you may need to occasionally guard when he uses his Stabbing

Combo) until he uses one of the three key attacks mentioned previously. When this happens, avoid the attack, then immediately lock on to the Female Ape and prepare to guard since it's now her turn to go on the offensive. If the Guardian Ape used a Sliding Slash or Leaping SwordSlash, always expect her to defend him using a Flying Slam or Scraping Uppercut. There isn't much time to retaliate after either of these attacks, so be patient and wait for the Headless Ape to perform a Terrifying Scream instead. This causes her to respond with a Brutal Combo, and guarding or deflecting until she finishes attacking creates a large enough opening to break her Posture by spamming Firecrackers.

Because the Female Ape is quite frail, it's also possible to use Spinning Shuriken Throws from afar (ideally using the Gouging Top) to significantly lower her Vitality before finishing her off with sprinting thrusts or a few slashes when the Guardian Ape is locked into an attack or recovery animation. If you need to heal at any point when fighting this couple, get some distance and wait for the Guardian Ape to perform an attack that won't trigger the Female Ape to rush in before using your Healing Gourd. Once she's been taken care of, resume fighting the Guardian Ape using the same strategy as before. If you're out of Spirit Emblems to use the Loaded Spear, yet still have plenty of charges left in your Healing Gourd, wait for an opening and use the Ceremonial Tanto to replenish your supplies.

# Folding Screen Monkeys

Monkeys of the temple that guard the Halls of Illusion—a place that lies betwixt life and death. The departed souls of the Divine Children drift and sway, taking shelter in these monkeys. Such is why they've be

![](images/73aa9c81cd26e65d0c8917316033732ec2ee9835cde246486ab24155b71db21f.jpg)

friended the Divine Child of Rejuvenation and seek to keep her hidden from prying eyes.

As this is more a battle of wits than one of brawn, upgrading your Vitality and Attack Power won't make a massive difference, but it can help when fighting the Monkey Shades. Both the Suppress Presence and Suppress Sound latent Skills will have a much more tangible impact and using Gachiin's Sugar can help make you even harder to detect. Upgrading your Shinobi Firecracker to the Long Spark version and learning Mid-air Prosthetic Tool improves your chances of blinding and catching the boss Monkeys. Shuriken are ineffective against your main targets unless you're very close, but can be used to quickly stagger the Monkey Shades. Be sure to stock up on Pacifying Agent since a pack of Monkey Shades could easily kill you without first using one of these items. Lastly, if you have access to the Finger Whistle, it can be used to enrage the Monkey Shades and make them fight amongst themselves.

# Environment

The puzzle-like encounter against the Folding Screen Monkeys takes place within a self-contained temple complex known as the Halls of Illusion—a place said to rise in the gap between life and death. Five unique halls form the perimeter of the complex and a series of walkways connects them all together. The entire area is surrounded by a bottomless pit, so falling off will cause you to take damage and reappear at the starting location. A great tree rises from the chasm in the center of the complex and can be used to quickly traverse to the other sides. There are two main layers to the area: the floors and rooftops. The rooftops can easily be accessed via the numerous grapple points found throughout the complex and it's possible to enter the four smaller halls via the opening on their roofs. The Monkeys generally prefer sticking to the rooftops, but the sloped angle of the roofs can be used to break line of sight and conceal your movements when traversing across them.

# Illusive Hall Bell

This item is immediately received after being transported to the Halls of Illusion and allows you to essentially reset the situation if you've lost track of a Monkey or feel like things have gotten too chaotic. Ringing this bell transports you back to the Folding Screen Platform and resets any Monkeys you haven't caught yet to their default positions on the map—those previously caught won't be set free, so there's no need to worry about losing progress. Using this bell makes things far more predictable and lets you freely experiment with your approach or retry a specific tactic if you've made a mistake. There's no limit or penalty tied to using this item so don't hesitate to give it a ring if things have gotten too frustrating.

![](images/4c145aafd58718ad014732c04567177aea3030ea03b1cc654aa18074cf5e12b9.jpg)  
This massive area can be quickly traversed by grappling onto the tree that serves as its center point.

1 Folding Screen Platform This is the starting location. Looking at the folding screens lets you identify which of the four Monkeys you've caught-any Monkey with its back turned has been caught.You're always transported back here after ringing the Illusive Hall Bell.  
2 Praying Monk Talk to this NPC to hear some lore and receive information concerning the nature of three of the Folding Screen Monkeys.  
3 Deafening Bell Ringing this large bell will temporarily stun the Hearing Monkey and allow you to easily take him out if you first lure him nearby.  
4 Muddy Hall The thick coating of mud layered across the floor of this room will highlight the Nameless Monkey's footsteps and reveal his location.

![](images/8d042c6fc2993e3bd19115a676e45af42911db916b585a1370e197c8cfcd26d4.jpg)

# 5 Roaring Hall

The sound caused by the waterfall prevents the Hearing Monkey from picking up on your movements if you lure him here. The ankle-deep water can also highlight the Nameless Monkey's footsteps.

# 6 Knowledge Hall

The books and scrolls littered around this room can be knocked over by the Nameless Monkey to help reveal his position.

# 7 Light Hall

Opening the large door in the back will invite a chilling wind that blows out the candles and makes the room pitch black. Luring the Seeing Monkey here can prevent him from spotting you in time to escape.

# 8 Abyss Hall

Avoid the bottomless pit below by grappling onto the elevated platform above; no light can penetrate here, so luring the Seeing Monkey to this spot can allow you to take him out before he can run away.

Your objective is to defeat the four Folding Screen Monkeys that inhabit the Halls of Illusion; killing one will deplete a quarter of their shared Vitality gauge and cause his portrait to turn around on the folding screens. These foes are skittish and aren't very aggressive, but they may slash at you a few times if cornered. They're quite agile and will quickly escape if you get close, so a brute force approach will simply lead to a lot of running in circles. Each of them has unique traits and requires a different tactic to tackle effectively, so consult their respective entries to learn how to best defeat them. With that said, it's sometimes possible to intercept the Monkeys with sword slashes or Firecrackers when they quickly double back towards you after attempting to escape; this can sometimes lead to a fast kill but it's very situational. It's best to remain crouched and to adopt a stealthy approach, unless your aim is to force them to move in a specific direction by approaching from the other side.

# > Seeing Monkey (Purple Kimono)

This purple-robed Monkey is gifted with superior eyesight and a wide field of view—he can spot you from long distances so sneaking up to him will prove challenging. However, luring him to a dark place can obscure his vision and prevent him from seeing you in time to run away. Extinguishing the candles in the Light Hall creates the perfect setup to accomplish this, as the Seeing Monkey is positioned on a nearby rooftop by default and can easily be forced to jump down into the now pitch-black room. Approach him from the east and he will retreat through the opening in the Light Hall's roof; from there, you can perform a Plunging Deathblow to catch him by surprise. If you attempt this without first blowing out the candles, he will spot you and escape before you can get within deathblow range. It's also possible to sneak up on him by entering the Light Hall from the ground floor before grappling onto the rooftop from the opening in the ceiling. Luring him into the Abyss Hall by approaching from the south is also an option.

# > Speaking Monkey (Orange Kimono)

This mischievous monkey has the unique ability to alert the others to your presence by crying out and banging on a gong whenever he spots you. He doesn't have particularly great hearing or eyesight so sneaking up to him as he patrols along the southern section of the rooftops (out of sight of the Seeing Monkey) lets you easily take him out with a stealth deathblow. Watch for the orange aura surrounding both him and his footsteps to ascertain his position, but don't linger directly behind him for long since he'll hear you and become suspicious when you get within striking distance. When being chased, this monkey prefers to retreat to the Folding Screen Platform, the tree in the center, or on the Abyss Hall's roof in the back where he can easily survey the scene.

# > Hearing Monkey (Green Kimono)

This monkey has exceptional hearing and can detect your presence by picking up on any sound you make; this means you won't be able to sneak up behind him unless you first find a way to negate his hearing or stun him. The Hearing Monkey prefers to sit on the giant tree in the middle of the complex and can be lured towards the Deafening Bell by grappling onto this tree from the Praying Monk's location. This forces him to move up to a small ledge connected to the Abyss Hall, at which point ringing the bell will stun the monkey long enough for you to grapple up there and take him out. Alternatively, he can be driven to the Roaring Hall by grappling onto the middle tree from the Deafening Bell's location; he'll see you if you approach from the floor, but the sound of the water will prevent him from detecting your Plunging Deathblow.

![](images/8810eedffaff48b390ad9b099f5d6e8a484541677868e06d5cc14ad335ab46ef.jpg)  
Jumping and throwing Firecrackers in mid-air can sometimes allows you to catch one of the Monkeys as he tries to escape.

# > Nameless Monkey (Invisible)

The Monkey that inhabits the seemingly empty panel is completely invisible, but finding and catching him is quite easy once you've been made aware of his existence. He constantly stalks you and is the source of the nearby grunts and footsteps that can be heard whenever you're on the move. Unlike the others, this Monkey is docile and will never attack even if you accidentally bump into him. His bright yellow footprints can sometimes be seen trailing behind you and will make a visible splash when jumping down from above into the mud room, which can be used to pinpoint his current location; simply walk up to where the footprints stop and swing your sword around to catch him. Leading the Nameless Monkey to either the Muddy or Roaring Halls is a surefire way to spot him since his footprints are guaranteed to sho directly behind you when the boss encounter begins, so turning around and slashing can take care of him instantly. Firecrackers can also be used to blind him and highlight his position.

# Monkey Shades

Defeating the Folding Screen Monkeys causes hostile Monkey Shades to spawn as you approach either of the three specific rooftop locations highlighted on the map of this area. The number of Monkey Shades that appear at each location is equal to the number of boss Monkeys you've currently caught, so their presence becomes a bigger threat as the encounter progresses. Each location can only spawn a single group of Monkey Shades until another of the Folding Screen Monkeys has been caught. As such, it's worth taking the time to clear out these additional threats as they spawn or they'll otherwise chase you around the area and make hunting down the remaining boss Monkeys much harder.

Monkey Shades behave identically to Bare-handed Valley Monkeys except that their attacks inflict substantial Terror build up. Focus on evading (or deflecting) since guarding results in enough build up that a few hits will kill you; keep Pacifying Agent on standby when fighting groups of these enemies and retreat if necessary. Both Firecrackers and Shuriken can make short work of them, and if you have access to it at this point, the Finger Whistle can also be used to enrage them and cause them to fight each other.

# Quick Kill Strategies

# Nameless Monkey Strategy

Immediately turn around and eliminate the Nameless Monkey by slashing near this railing...

...or use a Firecracker to stun him before taking him out with a deathblow.

# Speaking Monkey Strategy

# Corrupted Monk (Illusion)

A Corrupted Monk, donning the mask of a fierce guardian deity.

![](images/48d413db5353559d815b29664900794aee263ebb4cb431d4b356383820d77507.jpg)

Her form was nebulous, almost to the point of appearing to be an illusion. How did she come to guard the cave entrance deep in Mibu Village?

# Multiple Encounters

You'll initially encounter the Corrupted Monk as an Illusion in Mibu Village. When you arrive at Fountainhead Palace you'll face the true Corrupted Monk. We'll cover both versions on the following pages; each has its own entry, but most of the boss' attacks are covered in the first part, so you may want to refer to them when reading about the true Corrupted Monk.

# Preparation

Upgrade your Healing Gourd to hold at least seven charges. The Shinobi Firecracker is the best overall tool here, but both Aged Feather Mist Raven and Gouging Top Shuriken (with Chasing Slice) are also effective. Equip either Whirlwind Slash or Ichimonji as your Combat Art. If you haven't already, learning the Ascending Carp, Descending Carp, and Shinobi Eyes Skills can allow you to take down the boss much faster. Stock up on Fistful of Ash items and bring Ako's, Ungo's, or Gokan's Sugar, since the buffs they provide can make a significant difference. Because this boss is an Illusion, Snap Seeds are effective against it, but only consider using them as a last resort since they're quite rare. Lastly, if you're on New Game+ and have access to the Lazulite Axe, it can be used to deal large amounts of damage and stun the boss. This boss is weak against Spirit damage, so Divine Confetti, Phantom Kunai and Lazulite Sacred Flame are all effective.

![](images/712830040fc738f2835161a53519de90144cf3abe9623f94cb5744356c663df1.jpg)

# Environment

This encounter takes place in a medium-sized enclosure that starts out narrow near the entrance, but quickly expands as you arrive at a wide, but short set of stairs. The sloped terrain near the stairs doesn't have any influence on the fight, but the area's border is littered with stone lamps that could cause you to get trapped if forced to retreat near it. The boss' Whirling Combo can easily drive you

![](images/cd794d17d84f29a78b6f99c980f112d94104c05c7f6208ebd1e70f8489a7bdc8.jpg)  
Avoid the area's border and do your best to stick to this center portion.

The entrance can be a deathtrap if you aren't careful and get pushed there, so always be aware of your positioning and return closer to the center whenever possible. If cornered, focus on deflecting or use Aged Feather Mist Raven to make a quick escape.

# Key Strategies

Focus on slowing down the Corrupted Monk's Posture regeneration rate by lowering her Vitality below  $60\%$ . Stay outside of her naginata's reach and look for openings to strike with a thrust after she recovers from an attack. Whirlwind Slash pierces through her guard and allows you to chip away at her Vitality. Both Firecrackers and Fistful of Ash can blind the boss long enough to let you get behind her and deal damage before retreating out of range as

she recovers. Snap Seeds can also stun her, but with the added bonus of dispelling  $10\%$  of her maximum Vitality; this only works three times, though, and should only be used if you're struggling since these items are quite rare.

Once you've lowered her Vitality below  $60\%$ , switch your focus to breaking her Posture. Getting into the rhythm of deflecting the Monk's diagonal or horizontal slashes will cause her to

use thrusts and sweeps far more often; this creates opportunities to significantly weaken her Posture by countering with a Mikiri or jump-kick. Look for a gap in her offense and weaken her Posture by slashing until she deflects. From there, she'll respond with a quick CounterSlash, or a Shove Combo or Overhead Counter that can both be easily avoided to create more openings to deal direct damage.

# Corrupted Monk (Illusion) — Phase 1

You'll only need to land a single deathblow to defeat this illusory version of the Corrupted Monk, but she's still quite dangerous since her attacks feature significant reach and deal lots of damage. She can quickly overpower you with a constant barrage of slashes if you rely solely on guarding, so focus on deflecting or retreating during the lengthy windup of her attacks instead. This boss recovers Posture at an incredibly fast rate, so it's essential that you lower her Vitality below  $60\%$  before focusing on breaking her Posture. She'll guard most frontal attacks, so you'll need to circumvent her defense in order to land a direct hit. This can be done by blinding her with Firecrackers or Fistful of Ash before sprinting behind her, or by staying just out of range before quickly hitting her with a sprinting thrust as she recovers.

At a distance, the Corrupted Monk attempts to close the gap by performing either a Leaping Overhead Slam, Leaping Horizontal Slash, or Advancing Combo. Learn to recognize these key attacks since dodging them can also create openings to lower her Vitality. Her Whirling Combo is particularly dangerous, as its forward momentum can easily drive you into a corner unless you make a conscious effort to move away from the area's border as you retreat. If you get cornered or there isn't enough time to retreat, focus on deflecting each slash or escape using Mist Raven. If you get hit or Posture-broken, immediately go into a brace-guard or safety roll to avoid taking further damage. The final slash of this combo has slightly more range and causes knockback, but avoiding it gives you an opening to rush in with a thrust. Be careful when retaliating, though, as she'll sometimes surprise you with her Retreating Spin Slash or Retreating Sweeps before moving back in with a gap-closing attack.

![](images/7297964ddaac750f0dba478c2f9d322a6919a41ff584a07fe1633b7943900138.jpg)  
Retreat out of reach of the Monk's Leaping Overhead Slam before attempting to heal!

![](images/f2dfe77635b6e6f556919703c348301d90cdf76d80a18d535476e50ba44603eb.jpg)  
Get ready to perform a Mikiri Counter when the boss readies her Naginata Thrust.

The flowing, dance-like nature of the Corrupted Monk's slashes makes deflecting them very intuitive if you focus on tracking her blade and on timing your button presses just as it's about to connect. She'll often use the same leftward or rightward CounterSlash multiple times in a row, so getting into a steady deflection rhythm can quickly weaken her Posture. Be careful once the Danger Symbol appears, however, since she can seamlessly transition into a thrust or various types of sweeps. You'll need to pay close attention to her animations and either dodge forward to counter her thrust with a Mikiri (if she leans back) or use a jump-kick to counter her sweeps (if she places her weapon flat on the ground). This deflection-centered approach forces the boss to use perilous attacks far more frequently. Countering them can quickly break her Posture, so switch to this strategy once you've dealt enough direct damage to lower her Posture recovery rate.

If deflecting proves too challenging, continue lowering her Vitality using the initially described tactics. When there's a significant gap in her offense, use a single sword slash to see if she'll guard by raising her arm. If she does, keep slashing until she deflects. From there, she'll either respond with a fast CounterSlash, or with a Shove Combo or Overhead Counter, both of which can be exploited to create openings. Most of her attacks are armored and can't be interrupted, so be sure to stop attacking if she doesn't guard your opening slash or you'll trade blows and suffer serious damage. If you're having difficulty finishing her off, consider buffing yourself with Ako's Sugar or use Snap Seeds to deplete the rest of her Vitality.

# Preparation

Hunt down all currently available Gourd Seeds so your Healing Gourd holds 9 charges. Since this battle consists of three Phases, consider defeating Lady Butterfly to obtain the Sakura Droplet and unlock an extra Resurrection Node. The Shinobi Firecracker is the most important tool, but both the Aged Feather Mist Raven and the Loaded Umbrella can also prove useful. Stock up on Fistful of Ash to continue blinding the boss once you've run out of Spirit Emblems. Ungo's Sugar paired with the Devotion Skill can help mitigate the damage dealt by the boss' attacks. Assigning Pacifying Agent or the Mottled Purple Gourd to your Quick Item slots can help mitigate Terror build up during Phase 3. Learning Ichimonji: Double can allow you to severely weaken her Posture during Phases 1 & 2.

# Environment

Use the length of the bridge to your advantage when fighting but do your best to avoid getting cornered near the gates on either end. The doors, pillars, and other obstacles there can prevent you from dodging freely, so this can lead to a quick death. If you end up in this position, there's a bit of room to maneuver around the base of the bridge. The Corrupted Monk can chase you there, however, so take care not to fall off into the chasm below as you try to retreat. You can out

![](images/d4361ba95016147d4071ff81c5271cd3a93500c5c23728713c3917e348649d1f.jpg)

maneuver her and escape by grappling onto one of the four large branches surrounding the bridge. The tallest of these branches is located near the larger northern gate and can be used to quickly land

a plunging deathblow when the boss summons her clones during Phase 2. Use the gates as a visual aid when looking to orient yourself and head towards the large gate to quickly locate this branch

# Corrupted Monk - Phase 1

The true Corrupted Monk leaps onto the scene as you approach the center of the bridge. She's vulnerable for a few seconds after landing but you'll get blown back and miss your chance to deal damage if you move in too early. Stop at the bridge's center and immediately sprint behind her after she comes crashing down; from there, continue attacking until she's forced to deflect.

During Phase 1, she behaves almost identically to the Illusive version you've previously faced in Mibu Village, so consult the general strategy described in that entry (P.460) as it's still applicable during

this portion of the fight. There are a few notable exceptions, however. Her Posture recovery rate is inherently slower, so it's possible to quickly land a deathblow by focusing purely on deflecting and countering her perilous attacks. She's no longer vulnerable to Snap Seeds, but won't have access to her dangerous Whirling Combo until later in the fight. Don't expect to be safe when grappling onto the large branches found on either side of the bridge, as she can use a variety of Anti-Air Slashes to reach you there. Because this is a lengthier battle, do your best to conserve your Spirit Emblems for the much more difficult final Phase.

After recovering from the first deathblow, the Corrupted Monk will backstep and surround herself in a black aura before disappearing. A thick mist then shrouds the area and Illusory Clones begin attacking from different angles. They come in waves of three (total of 9 Clones), with each of them slashing once before vanishing. You can't fight back against them or lock on to easily track their movements: either withstand their attacks until the boss reemerges or focus on grappling atop the tallest branch at the far end of the bridge. The latter is by far the best option, as it allows you to land a plunging deathblow and immediately reach Phase 3. It's even possible to avoid dealing with the Clones entirely by immediately grappling onto this branch as the boss disappears during the phase transition. This vantage point places you above the mist and reveals the Corrupted Monk's location near the center of the bridge—quickly lock on and jump forward to perform a plunging deathblow.

If you're too slow and the clones have a chance to appear, swivel the camera to track their location and do your best to guard or deflect their attacks. Take advantage of the small pause between each wave to safely heal, recover your Posture, or attempt to reach the tallest branch. Be wary of trying to evade the clones by grappling from branch to branch, however, since their attacks have good range and can easily cause you to fall in the chasm surrounding the bridge. If you don't have enough Vitality to survive the fall, the option to resurrect won't be available and you'll be forced to restart the entire battle.

When feeling overwhelmed, deploying the Loaded Umbrella lets you automatically guard attacks from all angles and can allow you

# Corrupted Monk - Phase 3

![](images/e207b9f37abb3183241c31565d796cf848d7563f49aca217366f4d56c6c5da17.jpg)  
Expect the Monk's Fast Overhead Slam when she raises her naginata in this manner during Phase 3.

The Corrupted Monk can't be damaged while the parasite erupts from her neck, so keep your distance to avoid the Whirling Combo she always uses after getting back on her feet. At this point, she sheds all defense in favor of pure offense and will no longer attempt to guard or deflect your attacks. Her Posture also recovers at a much faster rate, so focus purely on depleting her Vitality. If you've been saving up your Spirit Emblems, now's the time to use Firecrackers and Fistful of Ash to repeatedly blind her and deal damage until you run out. Otherwise, it's generally best to stay at mid-range (outside of her naginata's reach) and wait for her to finish attacking before moving in. Hit her with a sprinting thrust as she recovers, then retreat out of reach. She's far more dangerous and unpredictable up close, so avoid purposefully going toe-to-toe unless you're extremely confident in your abilities.

![](images/b17ca736261e07c77b4013db607838f013aef09c4efaad1cb87d239b3e5c4e51.jpg)  
Grapple onto this branch when the boss summons her clones.

to safely move towards the deathblow branch. Another option is to purposefully corner yourself against one of the two gates, as this can make it easier to guard or deflect by limiting the angles from which the clones can approach. Snap Seeds can also dispel any currently active clones and give you an opening to safely reach the branch. Even after dodging a few waves of clones, it's still possible to grapple onto the branch and land a deathblow; avoid lingering on the branch for too long, however, as this will cause the Corrupted Monk to resume fighting. She doesn't have access to any new moves at this point, so rely on the same tried-and-true tactics while remaining close to the branch so you're ready to grapple onto it when she summons her Clones again.

Her Fast Overhead Slam is a constant threat once you move in closer, so you'll need to be ready to dodge or deflect it at a moment's notice. It's quick enough that it can punish you if you use more than a single attack or if you retreat too slowly. If you deflect it, immediately transition into a thrust before dodging backwards. Watch out for her new Parasitic Bile attack when she lifts her arm and the Danger Symbol appears, since it hits multiple times in addition to inflicting Terror build up. Both these new attacks are highly dangerous up close but also present safe opportunities to move in and punish her with a thrust if you stay at mid-range and wait for her to miss. The Frenzy Combo she gains access to allows her to quickly transition into a sweep before finishing with either a Fast Overhead Slam or Parasitic Bile. After jumping over this sweep, always dodge sideways the moment you land to avoid taking damage.

In addition to her Whirling Combo, the Monk now has access to a Leaping Spin Slash and Advancing Sweep to quickly close the gap. Although the Leaping Spin Slash can simply be guarded or deflected, it can also be avoided by dodging towards her right side just as she comes down. Doing so creates an opening to land a few slashes as she recovers. Staying at mid-range limits how often she'll use these gap-closing moves, but be particularly careful when attempting to heal, since her Advancing Sweep is extremely fast and can often catch you even when you think it's safe. Wait for her to first commit to an attack and heal while she recovers. Fight along the full length of the bridge, and avoid getting cornered by looking for an opening to sprint past her and switch sides whenever you approach the end of the bridge. Grappling onto the branches or using Aged Feather Mist Raven can also allow you to make a quick escape and reset the situation.

# Great Shinobi - Owl

Once thought dead, the Great Shinobi known as the Owl has returned in a bid to claim the power of the Dragon's Heritage for his own. His aging body has left him with only a fraction of the strength he once had, but he compensates for this with under

![](images/793c1f5f08ebfbaa4eb3b52950c3d31410471ca853099a840727d15f2a6eb22b.jpg)

handedness and subterfuge. He is willing to employ whatever dirty tactics are needed to finally ascend to the seat of power he was subservient to for so long.

# Preparation

Upgrade your Healing Gourd to hold eight or nine charges and collect as many Prayer Beads as possible since this is a challenging battle. Equipping the Spring-load Flame Vent lets you deal more damage during openings, and stocking up on Oil by farming it from the bandits in Hirata Estate increases this tool's effectiveness even further. Shuriken can be used to interrupt the Owl's Posture Recovery Stance during Phase 2, and the Aged Feather Mist Raven can help you create openings or get out of tight situations when cornered. Avoid using the Loaded Spear at all costs since this boss can counter thrusting attacks with a Mikiri. Visit the Divine Child to receive Rice whenever you run out, as it can be used to heal even when affected by the Owl's Healing Seal. Bring the Green Mossy Gourd, Antidote Powder, or Contact Medicine to counteract the Poison that comes into play during Phase 2. Lastly, Ako's, Ungo's and Gokan's Sugar can all come in handy, especially if you've learned the Devotion Skill to increase their duration.

![](images/44d540e5f41e51b865152f58248cce26ebe0c8860bfbc0f3b3124cf95d31a12b.jpg)

![](images/70231e12fd8659c392854164efb4b15a7ceaa91b6847c9ce09253d6f79b475fe.jpg)  
Rice are the only type of restorative items that can be used once afflicted by the boss' Healing Seal.

# Environment

This familiar location hasn't seen any changes since your battle with Genichiro, but this time you'll want to use the full length of the area to bait the Owl into closing the gap. Always make sure there's enough room to retreat after attacking, since getting trapped into a corner can lead to a swift defeat. As before, watch out for the decorative samurai statues and the set of opened doors along the back wall since they can cause you to get stuck. Once the ground gets coated in Poison, do your best to avoid fighting in the affected zones until it clears. When cornered by the Owl's Poison Splash, sprint jumping over the puddles can allow you to safely escape.

# Key Strategies

Keeping your distance forces the Owl to close the gap with either a Chasing Slice, Spinning Overhead Slam, Dashing Horizontal Slash, or Rush Uppercut. Each of these moves can be avoided in ways that leave him exposed long enough to deal Vitality damage before sprinting away to reset the situation. Don't worry about breaking his Posture and instead focus squarely on depleting his Vitality. Dousing the

Owl in Oil before hitting him with a charged Flame Blast when there's an opening can deal substantial amounts of damage and briefly stun him as he's set ablaze. Aged Feather Mist Raven can also be used to easily avoid his attacks and create openings. Be sure to avoid his Healing Seal when he extends his left hand, since the debuff it applies can prevent you from using

any restorative items (except Rice) for a full 30 seconds. During Phase 2, jump backwards to avoid his Smoke Bombs and always steer clear of the poisonous fluid he coats the floor with after vaulting from a Springboard Kick. Switching to Shuriken to interrupt his Posture Recovery Stance can help prevent the fight from dragging on.

# Great Shinobi - Owl - Phase 1

The Owl is an aggressive opponent that relies on underhanded tactics to compensate for the fact that he's past his prime. As Sekiro's shinobi teacher, he has access to variations of some of the techniques you use, including a devastating Mikiri Counter that punishes you for using thrust attacks, and the ability to perform a Chasing Slice following a shuriken throw. He makes frequent use of a Healing Seal bomb that can temporarily prevent the use of healing items and even uses a powered-up version of the Firecracker to create a damaging explosion when pressured. The large sword he wields gives his slashes plenty of reach, and his powerful offense will quickly break your Posture if you rely on guarding. This battle is all about finding openings to deal Vitality damage and slow down the boss' Posture recovery rate. To best accomplish this, keep your distance and let him make the first move; he will then be forced to close the gap with a limited set of key attacks that can each lead to an opening when avoided in a specific manner.

The boss' Chasing Slice is always preceded by a slightly delayed shuriken throw that causes him to shift his weight forward. Guard or deflect the shuriken before immediately dodging forward through the horizontal slice. This positions you behind him, so strike with a dodge counterattack followed by another slash before sprinting away from him. The Owl will often retreat with an evasive hop after taking damage or when being pressured; this is advanta

![](images/9f090a774d59dbf4154a3ee3a275bfb230b9188a27cc2ddf6c0797d29ce7f109.jpg)  
This pose signals the Owl's Rush Uppercut. It features exceptional tracking so get ready to guard or deflect.

![](images/e80519513e7faeb94af3003611b71d1f9675062fb46cbacc8826a3e54b3dd17f.jpg)  
If the shuriken that precedes the Owl's Chasing Slice hits you, recover by instantly dodging forward through his slice.

geous, since it helps quickly reset the situation by creating more distance. Next, his Spinning Overhead Slam is signaled by two rapid-fire shuriken throws. Guard or deflect the projectiles and immediately start sprinting sideways towards his back as he prepares to slam down. This leaves him exposed, so strike with a sprint attack followed by another slash before retreating. If you need to heal at any point, wait until there's enough distance or sacrifice a damage dealing opportunity to safely heal instead.

Another possible gap-closing attack is the extremely dangerous Rush Uppercut. Because it's quite fast and heavily tracks your movements, this attack will almost assuredly catch you if you try to sprint away. Instead, stand firm and watch for the Owl to dash towards you in a straight line while holding his sword back with both hands. Time your deflect (or guard) as he draws near, then pause for a split second before dodging diagonally towards his left side to avoid either the slash or Springboard Kick he always follows this attack with. From there, dodge counterattack and slash once before sprinting away. If his Springboard Kick connects, immediately guard the incoming Shuriken Spread and prepare for him to quickly close the gap again after landing. Lastly, the Dashing Horizontal Slash can be differentiated from the Rush Uppercut by the quick sidestep that precedes it and the diagonal angle the

Owl approaches from. Dodge directly through the slash to create an opening and deal damage. However, be careful if you guard or deflect slash since he's guaranteed to throw a Healing Seal (or use a two-hit cross cut if you're currently afflicted by the seal).

At close range, the Owl most often attacks with a Slashing Combo that you'll want to focus on deflecting to avoid getting Posture-broken. Dodging backwards may seem like a good idea but he's likely to hit you due to his blade's significant reach. Pay attention to the rhythm of his attacks when aiming to deflect. They each have a clear windup period but the slashes themselves are very fast; as such, you need to time your input just as his blade begins its follow through. If he turns his back after two slashes, deflect twice in quick succession since this signals a fast two-hit cross cut. It's also worth noting that all his combos are consecutive, so they can't be interrupted by making his sword recoil when deflected.

His Healing Seal will be a constant threat at close range, but it presents another opportunity to deal damage if you simply watch for his left hand to extend before sprinting around to his back. Always be mindful of the ensuing mist cloud, however, since it lingers for a few seconds and the forward momentum of your attacks could ac

# Great Shinobi - Owl - Phase 2

After recovering from your deathblow, the Owl pushes you away as he begins groveling on the floor. This is nothing but a cheap trick (one that he won't use again on subsequent attempts), but it prevents you from locking on to him at this point. Getting close enough to him or attempting to attack will cause him to backflip away while throwing a Smoke Bomb. In addition to obscuring his movements, this new attack causes you to flinch while breaking lock on. Wait a second, then lock on again since he'll soon be

![](images/ba76131e8d6a18a354515fbf2191c27f6c28718a178d56593c5930e2cec0ea3f.jpg)  
Jumping backwards early enough allows you to completely avoid the boss' Smoke Bomb.

![](images/32c858d83cebb4b4f891047c9e752f721a7c669eee5df425275d1ec0e4403be1.jpg)  
After deflecting one of the Owl's slashes, avoid his Evasive Gunpowder Flash by immediately dodging backwards if you see him hop away.

cidentally push you into it. If you get caught, don't panic and do your best to continue avoiding his attacks for the next 30 seconds until the debuff wears off. You won't be able to use Antidote Powder when the Healing Seal is in effect, but Rice can keep you alive if you have some. Consider using Gokan's Sugar or Ungo's Sugar to improve your chances of survival while you wait for the Healing Seal to go away.

![](images/f6e96ffaa63c8d44ff84372e5680bc0560b6fa118d6f87d56880b843e5e06a12.jpg)  
Prepare to guard or deflect the Owl's two-hit cross cut when he spins mid-combo.

ambushing you through the smoke. Pressing the lock on button too early can cause the camera to re-center instead, so be careful. Expect him to ambush you with a Healing Seal or one of the four gap-closing attacks described in Phase 1. If you see a glint through the smoke, immediately guard since this signals that shuriken are coming your way. Expect him to most often respond with a Smoke Bomb after guarding or after you deflect his Slashing Combo. Avoid being stunned by jumping backwards the moment he lifts his left leg and readyes to throw the bomb.

The same overall strategy used in Phase 1 still proves very effective at this stage, but the Owl's Shuriken Spread is now replaced with a Poison Splash if he connects with a Springboard Kick. This new attack coats a portion of the floor in a poisonous fluid that causes gradual Poison build up if stepped on. Consistently dodging his Springboard Kicks can be difficult, so you'll often have to contend with this new attack; immediately move away from the Poison's location and stick to fighting in a safe spot until it clears. Don't hesitate to use Antidote Powder to remove the Poison if you're stricken by it and consider using Contact Medicine to inflict a low-grade Poison if you find yourself unable to avoid his puddles. When his Posture gets low, the Owl will attempt to enter his Posture Recovery Stance after landing from a Poison Splash. Anticipate this and ready your Shuriken to interrupt him from a distance.

![](images/0ba0cc73f858692d12aea1d17238027ad0d3c9a42cc37b18b5c882b6aafb8823.jpg)  
Shuriken are the best way to interrupt the Owl's Posture Recovery Stance during Phase 2.

# Owl - Father

The Owl took in an hungry cub on a whim and raised him as a shinobi. The process was so engrossing that he hoped they might enjoy a true battle to the death someday. He got his wish, if only in an old memory.

# Preparation

Collect any missing Gourd Seeds to upgrade your Healing Gourd to its maximum capacity. This optional boss is very challenging, so seeking out more Prayer Beads to enhance your Vitality can make all the difference. Visit the Divine Child to get some Rice and be sure to stock up on Fistful of Ash. Both Ungo's and Gokan's Sugar can prove useful if you're frequently getting hit or Posture-broken by the Owl's attacks. Upgrading your Shinobi Firecracker to the Long Spark increases your chances of blinding him, and Aged Feather Mist Raven allows you to create openings or escape if you're feeling pressured. The Loaded Umbrella lets you easily guard or deflect his Warp Slash during Phase 2. Ichimonji: Double is the best choice in terms of Combat Arts and can be used to severely weaken his Posture during openings. Since the Owl is one of the most challenging opponents you'll face, it's worth considering using a Bundled Jizo Statue to replenish your resurrective power if you're close to winning.

![](images/b9f784c63d6750408bb15f7121f0443e44ef46e69f53c57dfb333fcdf93a3165.jpg)

# Environment

This area remains unchanged since your encounter with Lady Butterfly, except that the raging flames have now fully engulfed the pillars. Approaching the pillars still won't cause any Burn build up, but you'll want to avoid fighting near these obstacles since they can restrict your range of movements and make dodging difficult. Stick to the center of the temple and avoid chasing the Owl near the corners or between the pillars and side walls if he moves there. His Explosive Slice is particularly dangerous if cornered or near obstacles, so do your best to keep the battle away from these problem areas. With that said, the pillars can help block his attacks if you need to heal or use items, but don't expect to be safe from his Blazing Rush during Phase 2 as it'll pass right through them.
