# Key Strategies

The Owl's Evasive Gunpowder Flash can conceal his next move, so keep your guard up after avoiding it. Always be ready to counter his incoming Shadowfall with a Mikiri if the Danger Symbol appears in that situation. Pay close attention to the boss' movements since his fast zig-zag dash always signals either a Shadowfall, Tumbling Sweep, or a shuriken throw that

leads into a Spinning Overhead Slam or Chasing Slice. Guard or deflect his sword combos and avoid his Explosive Slice by sprinting towards his left side. Immediately jump over his Tumbling Sweep when the Danger Symbol appears at close-range. Anticipate the Slow Overhead Slam that almost always follows this sweep and create an opening by dodging the

slam just as he shouts. During Phase 2, jump over the boss' Blazing Rush, then counter his incoming Shadowfall with a Mikiri. When he vanishes, track his Spectral Owl and deploy the Loaded Umbrella to deflect his incoming attack. This forces the boss to respond with a predictable Counter Sweep or Slow Overhead Slam that can both easily be punished.

# Owl-Father-Phase1

You'll be facing the Owl at the height of his power, so expect him to be faster, more aggressive, and to pose a far bigger challenge this time around. He can dart around the room at high-speed to begin his offense from different angles, and his combos can now end with an Explosive Slice or Tumbling Sweep to mix you up. He'll also make frequent use of his Evasive Gunpowder Flash to retreat before using the smoke generated by the explosion to mask a gap-closing attack or his new Shadowfall thrust. As before, you'll generally want to avoid using thrusts against him since he can punish them with a Mikiri Counter; however, thrusting at his exposed back or after countering with a Mikiri of your own is safe. He no longer makes use of his Healing Seal bomb, so you'll never have to worry about being locked out of healing. If you're hurt, get some distance and seek shelter behind the pillars before drinking from your Gourd or using items.

As in your previous encounter, let the Owl make the first move so you can dodge or defend in a manner that creates openings to deal direct damage from the side or back. Once he's vulnerable, deplete his Vitality and Posture by continuing to attack until he's forced to deflect. After deflecting your attack, he'll either retreat with a backstep or Springboard Kick, or retaliate with a fast CounterSlash, Explosive Slice, or a Slow Overhead Slam. Most of these reactions are quite fast, so be ready to guard or deflect the instant you notice the telltale orange deflection glow. When he's performing a combo, deflecting his slashes is ideal but guarding can also work if your Vitality is high enough—just make sure to recover your Posture before he attacks again. If you're having trouble dealing with his pressure, use Aged Feather Mist Raven to escape mid-combo. Blinding him with Firecrackers or by throwing a Fistful of Ash when he's slowly moving sideways at close-range can allow you to create a small opening.

![](images/827db31765b82c6a477e8d5efe5ce79bc07d49ad7386ae1fec7757c83d15f44a.jpg)  
When the Owl begins winding up a Slow Overhead Slam, wait for him to shout before dodging sideways. This prevents him from surprising you with a counterattack.

# Shadowfall

At a distance, the Owl will frequently use his signature Shadowfall thrust to lunge forward and impale you. If it connects, he'll surge upwards before unleashing two spinning slashes (that you'll need to guard or deflect) on the way down. During Phase 1, he'll only perform this perilous attack following a fast zig-zag dash or after retreating with his Evasive Gunpowder Flash. Be on the lookout for the Danger Symbol after either of those actions since this is your cue to dodge forward and counter with a Mikiri just as he begins lunging. Once you've learned to recognize and anticipate it, Shadowfall becomes a reliable opportunity to lower the boss' Vitality and Posture.

Both the Owl's Rush Uppercut and Dashing Horizontal Slash lead into longer combos that typically end with a Tumbling Sweep or Explosive Slice. Because this is the only perilous attack he'll use at close-range, the sweep can easily be avoided by jumping the instant the Danger Symbol appears during his combos. His Explosive Slice is always preceded by a shoulder bash that leads into a horizontal slash, so learning to recognize it is essential. Guard or deflect both hits, then immediately sprint towards the boss' left side to get behind him as he spreads gunpowder and prepares to slash. At range, his Chasing Slice remains a big threat, but guarding or deflecting the shuriken before dodging directly through the slice also creates an opening. His Spinning Overhead Slam can still be preceded by two shuriken, but it can now also be performed following a zig-zag dash that leads into a single shuriken. The key to differentiating between these two gap-closing attacks is to pay attention to the Owl's stance when he throws shuriken: if he leans forward and slightly delays the throw, always expect a Chasing Slice.

# Slow Overhead Slam

The Owl often transitions into a Slow Overhead Slam after his Tumbling Sweep or after he deflects. This vertical slash has a lengthy windup period and appears to leave him wide open, but be careful, as dodging or moving to his side (or away from him) will cause him to instantly transition into a counterattack to catch you by surprise. To prevent this from happening, listen for his shout (or watch for his hands to move past his head) before dodging. He won't be able to cancel into a counterattack at that point, so this creates an opening to deal damage. Alternatively, you can interrupt the slam by hitting him with a quick Ichimonji.

Phase 2

PROPERTIES AA

Leaping slash performed after reappearing from Owl Warp; uses longer range version if you're too far from warp point. Track Spectral Owl's location and prepare to guard / deflect incoming slash. Deflect always results in Slow Overhead Slam or Counter Sweep.

Phase 2

PROPERTIES AA

Descending slash performed after Spectral Owl flies towards ceiling; track bird's location and sprint away or prepare to guard / deflect. Deflect always results in Slow Overhead Slam or Counter Sweep.

# Owl-Father-Phase2

After recovering from your deathblow, the boss is most likely to attack by igniting his Spectral Owl companion before sending it flying straight in your direction. This low-flying Blazing Rush counts as a sweep and is extremely predictable, so simply avoid it by jumping over the Spectral Owl before readying to counter the boss' incoming Shadowfall with a Mikiri. If you're at long-range when this attack begins, jumping forward over the Spectral Owl can help put you in range of the boss' Shadowfall and ensure that your Mikiri Counter will connect.

As the fight continues, the Owl will frequently recall his companion by reaching out with his left hand. This signals a Blazing Rush and should be viewed as an opportunity to weaken his Posture and deal Vitality damage. Outside of this new perilous attack, his entire Phase 1 move set remains largely unchanged and the same tactics used to create openings still apply here. Be careful when he uses his Springboard Kick, though, as you'll have to guard or deflect the spread of shuriken he now throws in mid-air. Beyond these changes, you'll also need to contend with his dangerous new Owl Warp technique.

# Owl Warp

The Spectral Owl continuously flies around the room during Phase 2, but it isn't an active threat and can't be killed. From here on out, the boss gains access to his Owl Warp technique: this allows him to vanish and warp into the Spectral Owl before soon ambushing you with a Warp Slash or Overhead Warp Slash as he reappears at his companion's location. Locking on isn't an option, so stay sharp and manually adjust the camera to keep track of the Spectral Owl as it circles around at high speed. The time it takes for the boss to reappear and attack is variable, but always expect him to warp in whenever the Spectral Owl performs a corkscrew directly through you or after it flies towards the ceiling.

The safest way to avoid an incoming Warp Slash is to dodge and sprint away once the Spectral Owl comes to a halt, flies upwards, or dashes through you. If you're feeling confident, positioning Sekiro so he faces the direction from which the Owl will reappear can allow you to deflect the incoming WarpSlash. This forces the boss

# Blazing Rush

Phase 2

PROPERTIES Sweep/Burn | AA

Sweep performed by igniting Spectral Owl and sending it flying low in your direction; always followed by Shadowfall. Prepare to jump over Spectral Owl when boss extends left hand and Danger Symbol appears, then counter Shadowfall with Mikiri.

# Counter Sweep

Phase 2

PROPERTIES Sweep | Reaction Only

Fast sword sweep used exclusively after either Warp Slash or Overhead WarpSlash have been deflected; anticipate sweep and counter with jump-kick if Danger Symbol appears after deflecting one of the boss' warp attacks.

![](images/1ad64bb2616d5b4a074a678c7917fd2cffcc74d0babd61ba24e86654f5cfe736.jpg)  
Jump forward to avoid the Blazing Rush and prepare to counter the incoming Shadowfall with a Mikiri.

![](images/61de0a125f57bcac772595e45787e65ae79ba70ed3f12aa40f34be80d365c232.jpg)  
Tilt the camera upwards if the Spectral Owl flies towards the ceiling since this signals an Overhead Warp Slash.

to respond with a Counter Sweep or Slow Overhead Slam, both of which can then be avoided to create a guaranteed opening and deal damage. Deploying the Loaded Umbrella makes deflecting these attacks much safer and easier. It's worth noting that this version of the Slow Overhead Slam can't be cancelled into a counterattack, so it's safe to immediately dodge. After a bit of time has passed, the boss will vanish again following either an Evasive Gunpowder Flash, Gunpowder Slice, Slow Overhead Slam, or Spinning Overhead Slam. Use this knowledge to anticipate his next Owl Warp.

# Preparation

If you haven't already, it's now possible to fully upgrade your Healing Gourd so it can hold a maximum of 10 charges. Okinaga's Flame Vent or the Leaping Flame upgraded spear are the best tools here due to their fire-based attacks and wide area of effect. In terms of combat arts, both Whirlwind Slash and Mortal Draw are great for slicing through the Old Dragons. Assign Antidote Powder or the Green Mossy Gourd to your Quick Items slots to help counteract the Poison build up caused by the Old Dragons' poisonous fumes. Lastly, Eel Livers can reduce the Shock damage taken if you get hit or pushed away while attempting to perform a Lightning Reversal against the Divine Dragon.

![](images/033c6d5a97f20b30f85c394c3da40d4a268fa045f99a9f6cf38de2bb622d255c.jpg)

Grappling onto the gnarled branch summoned by the Old Dragons allows you to take out a large number of them with a unique plunging deathblow.

![](images/5afa5e21c991ec1c673c7bfc027e63c5b25085fdc95c56a5552d3576e3a95d61.jpg)

# Environment

The divine realm this battle takes place in is a completely flat open field with no obstacles to speak of, except for the withered remains of the Everblossom resting at its center point. This area has no clear visible boundaries, but it's essentially a giant circle that affords all the space you need to maneuver. Gnarled branches that can be

When fighting the Divine Dragon, avoid going around him and instead focus on staying in front where you can easily see his shockwave attacks coming and can make use of the branches to hit him with Lightning Reversals.

# Old Dragons of the Tree - Phase 1

A single Old Dragon stands in front of you as the battle begins, but beware, as a large group of them will soon emerge around him. The white-colored Old Dragons are feeble and slow, but their Noxious Cough is dangerous as it can quickly inflict Poison if you get close. They can also defend themselves by slowly swiping at you with their ritual canes, but this doesn't pose any real threat unless you're surrounded. A small portion of their shared Vitality gauge is depleted each time one of them is killed, and another Old Dragon emerges not long after to take its place. Once their shared Vitality gauge reaches the halfway mark, black-colored versions will begin emerging to replenish the group's numbers. They lack the ability to spew Poison, but can perform a Lunging Swipe as well as submerge below the clouds to reappear next to you if you move away. At that point, focus exclusively on isolating and dispatching the remaining white Old Dragons since these are the only ones that count towards depleting the group's shared Vitality gauge.

Once at least one of them has fallen, the Old Dragons will collectively begin chanting to summon three gnarled branches that erupt from below your current position. These attacks track your movements but can be easily avoided by continuously sprinting as soon as you see the Old Dragons lower their heads and clutch their canes. The

final two branches immediately wither and fade, but the first to erupt lingers for approximately 25 seconds and acts as a grapple point from which you can perform a unique plunging deathblow. This is extremely powerful as it results in a large 360-degree swing that lets you instantly take out any surrounding Old Dragons. You're completely safe when perched atop the branches, so lock on to the white Old Dragon closest to the center of the pack and take them all out in one fell swoop. There's usually enough time to grapple back onto the branch and repeat this process again before it withers. When it does, the group will immediately begin chanting to summon more, so continue using this tactic until all the white Old Dragons have been defeated.

If no branches are currently available, position yourself on the outskirts of the pack and use Okinaga's Flame Vent to incinerate large clusters of Old Dragons with a stream of Flowing Flames. You won't be needing Spirit Emblems during the next portion of this boss fight, so don't be afraid to spend them here. Whirlwind Slash or Mortal Draw are both good alternatives but be sure to retreat after every attack to avoid getting poisoned. Prepare to sprint away whenever they begin chanting, since your attacks can't interrupt the summoning process.

The Divine Dragon of the Everblossom is the source of Divine Heir Kuro's powers and the Rejuvenating Water.

A living God in dragon form originally from the West, its tears have the power to sever even the most powerful forms of immortality.

# Divine Dragon - Phase 1

The Divine Dragon manifests himself in the Everblossom at the center of the area and remains rooted there for the duration of the fight. He'll immediately push you back with a Wind Blast as the battle begins, and your objective now shifts to avoiding the shockwaves launched by his seven-branched sword while pressing forward to get within grapple reach of the branches spread out in front of him. During Phase 1, always expect either three Vertical Shockwaves or a pair of Sweeping Slashes whenever he attacks from a distance. Watch his sword carefully, and if he lifts it straight up, sprint at a 45-degree angle to avoid his Vertical Shockwaves while closing the gap. If he swings the blade from side to side and the Danger Symbol appears, get ready to jump since this signals his Sweeping Shockwaves. Sprint jumping over them allows you to quickly reach the branches.

![](images/eb9832063df62773fe45ce5873c3e14c1262750101706ec354011461b3dbafe7.jpg)

Jump over the Sweeping Shockwaves when the Divine Dragon swings his sword from side to side.

Throughout the battle, lightning bolts periodically rain down from above to strike one of the five branches that serve as grapple points in front of the boss. Look for a yellow glow and a streak of flickering energy to identify the branches that are currently infused with lightning, then grapple onto one of them to rise and catch the lightning with your sword. Be sure to lock on to the Divine Dragon as you hang in the air, then press the attack button to perform a Lightning Reversal and deal damage.

Unlike a typical Lightning Reversal, catching the lightning in this manner won't cause you to take any damage. With that said, it's important to wait until the Divine Dragon finishes attacking or performs a sweeping slash before grappling onto a branch, as you can still get hit by his slashes in mid-air. If you mistime your approach, his Wind Blast could also blow you away just as you catch the lightning. Be careful, as this will cause you to take severe Shock damage on landing. If you're having trouble, use an Eel Liver to significantly reduce the Shock damage taken during a failed Lightning Reversal.

You'll need to hit the Divine Dragon with multiple Lightning Reversals to lower his Vitality below the  $30\%$  mark and move on to Phase 2. It's possible to avoid being pushed away by his Wind Blast by continuously sprinting a medium distance away from the branches as you wait for one of the them to be infused with lightning. Always reset to this position after performing a Lightning Reversal and retreat by sprinting backwards as he looks skyward and roars to signal his Wind Blast. Once you move closer, it becomes preferable to guard or deflect his vertical slams since purely sprinting sideways proves unreliable at that range. Avoid moving past the branches since this will cause him to burrow his head in the clouds and perform a Serpentine Bite. If you move directly next to him, he'll attempt to drive you away with a powerful Sword Crash. There's no advantage to crossing past the branches or fighting on top of them, so focus exclusively on striking him with Lightning Reversals instead.

# Divine Dragon - Phase 2

Phase 2 begins with the Divine Dragon powering up his sword by gathering energy from the clouds covering the surface. He'll then push you away with a Wind Blast and begin slashing to send out shockwaves at a faster rate. Your only objective at this point is to survive by dodging his shockwaves until he stops attacking. Watch out for his new Diagonal Shockwave and avoid it by sprinting sideways, then anticipate him to do four Vertical Slams before starting up his Beam Barrage. This six-hit combo is signaled by the Danger Symbol as he roars and thrusts with his sword: Sprint sideways to avoid the vertical shockwave sent out by his thrust, then jump to avoid two sweeping shockwaves before immediately resuming sprinting sideways to avoid the final three vertical waves.

![](images/6566c3373c3cbff57caebcee17095a8e9bafaf6a262fa69e20f2dcdf616cba64.jpg)  
During Phase 2, a quick thrusting motion signals the beginning of the Divine Dragon's Beam Barrage.

![](images/fce5d6c8214456ff3d0439d74534ec2083a3a7d34d9a2b181c48a860b3f8f7b3.jpg)  
Staying at this range prevents you from being blown away by the boss' Wind Blast.

![](images/a5754c44122d1bc801ed9903e7e9deb1d168e70e6b26bf56b84e2d9c7a9e2602.jpg)  
Be sure to lock on to the Divine Dragon before unleashing a Lightning Reversal.

![](images/eefb774d3ac80f3cf3073fcc095cef670cd58a9a65fdfc7f66e538c1febbe749.jpg)  
The Divine Wind Blast covers the entirety of the area and cannot be avoided.

At this point, the Divine Dragon will begin gathering energy again and three branches will emerge in front of him. Sprint forward and grapple onto the middle branch to trigger a special Lightning Reversal and break his Posture. Be sure to rush in and perform the Lightning Reversal as quickly as possible, or he'll send out a Divine Wind Blast that can't be avoided and deals severe damage if you take too long. Once his Posture has been broken, run up the seven-branched sword and perform a finisher deathblow to gather the Divine Dragon's Tears.

![](images/e7ed89522cf40f781940d2713f5d23d393c2dbedeec67f36a0b8b8c543938163.jpg)

# Demon of Hatred

The Sculptor, who failed to become Shura, became a vessel for the

![](images/759ea527209756e5da5e740a073288deaf659f6c643cdb01140a906eebbeaf83.jpg)

flames of hatred. It seems that for a long time, death was not his fate. It wasn't until he had become a demon that he was finally able to depart this world.

# Preparation

Upgrade your Healing Gourd to hold 10 charges and be sure to have all three Resurrection Nodes unlocked. If you're struggling with this boss, hunting for Prayer Beads and raising your Vitality to 20 will make a big difference, as will raising your Attack Power to 12 by first defeating the Owl in Hirata Estate (if you've obtained the

Suzaku's Lotus Umbrella affords protection from all the boss' attacks (except for his sweeps) and should be considered essential (though Aged Feather Mist Raven serves as a lesser substitute). The Tokugawa enemies in the Outskirts and Castle areas have a chance to drop both the Fulminated Mercury needed to upgrade the Umbrella as well as Ministry Dousing Powder to help mitigate fire damage. Malcontent can be used to stun the boss up to three times and is incredibly useful. Divine Confetti can also give you a damage buff of  $25\%$ , but only use these items if you've already defeated all five Headless and have a surplus. Don't be afraid to use Divine Grass or a Bundled Jizo Statue if you're close to winning during the final phase.

# Environment

This battlefield hasn't changed since you've faced Gyoubu, but you'll be forced to use the full scope of the area due to the Demon of Hatred's large size and constant pressure. The northwest quadrant remains dangerous, so be sure to avoid retreating there as you can easily fall off the cliff. Many of the boss' attacks require you to sprint sideways to avoid them, so it's important to keep track of your position in relation to obstacles such as the wooden fence running down the middle of the field and the three watchtowers that can also impede your movement. Avoid getting cornered as well, since you'll need room to retreat in order to stay outside the reach of his Whip Slash Combo and Slow Overhead Slam. Elevation changes in the terrain can make certain attacks difficult to avoid, so try to stay on even ground whenever possible. Lastly, it's sometimes better to avoid chasing him down even when there's an opportunity to deal damage if this results in putting yourself in a bad spot (such as the northern quadrant or the main gate). In those instances, let him come to you instead.

# Demon of Hatred - Phase 1

The Demon of Hatred's phantom left arm deals a mix of fire and physical damage in addition to causing Burn build up, while attacks using the rest of his body deal purely physical damage. His combos all incorporate the use of this arm, so it's best to focus on evasion since you'll often take significant damage when guarding or deflecting. He's quite aggressive and will pressure you constantly, but this can be used to your advantage by continuously sprinting outside of his reach and waiting for him to commit to an attack. This lets you safely sprint in with a thrust before further lowering his massive Vitality pool by slashing at his exposed underbelly or legs while he recovers. Landing enough hits will result in a stun that lets you pile on even more damage. Getting in close is the only way to significantly damage him, but it's crucial that you stop slashing the moment he recovers since you'll otherwise be locked into an animation and won't have a chance to avoid his stomps. If you get hurt, resist the urge to immediately heal and instead retreat and wait until he commits to an attack before doing so.

At the onset of the fight, the boss is focused on angrily clawing at the ground near the center of the battlefield and won't turn his attention to you until you move down the stairs. Once ready, sprint towards him but keep a bit of distance since he'll slash twice before extending his right arm and striking a pose. This is your cue to move next to him and deal damage until he recovers. When under him, both his Heavy Stomp and Fast Double Stomp will be the big-

![](images/2ddd312e8a546bf68e97f713227687d96ee07755389f6e90a65304eba373f791.jpg)  
Get ready to sprint jump around the Demon's incoming Burning Wave when he assumes this pose.

gest threat, so you'll need to anticipate them and stop attacking in order to dodge out of their way. If you overcommit and stop a bit too late, focus on guarding or deflecting the stomps instead. At this range, the Demon of Hatred will also use his impressive Explosive Crash, but this move can easily be avoided by sprinting backwards whenever you notice an orange glow surrounding him. A grapple point appears as he lands, so latch on to avoid the

incoming knockback shockwave before dealing damage with a Grappling Hook Attack. When the Danger Symbol appears during Phase 1, immediately jump since this always signals an incoming Rushdown Sweep. This attack causes the boss to dash behind you before turning around and striking a pose. He may seem vulnerable at this point, but he'll almost assuredly use his Fireball Volley attack to keep you at bay if you try to approach him. Jumping backwards (in the direction he's heading) when avoiding the sweep lets you chase him down and often gives you enough of a head start to close the gap by sprinting next to him as he's still winding up his fireballs. This creates a big opening to deal damage, but you'll need to be quick or it won't work. The Demon can also escape with a backdash whenever you're close, and you should also expect a Fireball Volley if you try to approach him at this point. Quickly jumping backwards or deploying Suzaku's Lotus Umbrella are the best ways to avoid his fireballs when caught by surprise.

# Demon of Hatred - Phase 2

After landing a deathblow, the Demon of Hatred will kneel and wince in pain. This gives you plenty of time to heal or buff yourself with Ministry Dousing Powder in order to mitigate the damage dealt by his new fire-based attacks introduced during Phase 2. The boss is completely invulnerable until he unleashes a knockback blast and gets back up, so stay at mid-range then immediately move in to hit him with a thrust after the blast. He'll then transition into a Rushdown Sweep followed by his Burning Wave. Because of this new follow up, sprinting towards him after a Rushdown Sweep can easily get you killed from this point onwards; instead, it's best to keep your distance and preemptively start sprinting laterally the moment you land from your jump. Performing a sprint jump helps to clear the wide blast radius but don't hesitate to deploy Suzaku's Lotus Umbrella if you feel there's no time to avoid the blast.

This Burning Wave attack can occasionally be performed on its own, so get ready to start sprinting whenever he stands up and tilts sideways on one leg. It's possible to latch onto him as he recovers, but avoid using a Grappling Hook Attack since he'll likely attempt to clobber you with a Headbutt or Swipe & Stomp Combo after you land. Instead, back away and wait for him to finish attacking before making your move. He also gains the ability to launch a series of Homing Idols at long-range during Phase 2. Avoiding the projectiles

# Demon of Hatred - Phase 3

Phase 3 begins with the Demon of Hatred extending his phantom arm to sweep the ground in a large circle before performing a second pass at a higher angle. Jump over the first, then immediately rush towards the boss to deal damage as the second swipe passes over you and he reels the arm back in (which acts as final short-range sweep). It's also possible to guard or deflect the above-ground second slash since it isn't considered a sweep. This proves useful at times since elevation differences between yourself and the boss can make it difficult to avoid otherwise. The circular sweep generates a large Flame Prison that keeps you trapped for the next 15 seconds, effectively limiting your range of movements and forcing you to go toe-to-toe with the boss until the flames dissipate.

# Closing the Gap

When the boss is attempting to close in on you, keep your distance by sprinting away and he'll eventually respond with a Whip Slash Combo or Slow Overhead Slam. Waiting for his phantom arm to slam down before sprinting directly towards him gives you a clean opening but be careful since its range can be deceptive. The WhipSlash Combo is incredibly dangerous, so familiarize yourself with its reach and try to remain just outside of its effective range. If you're a bit too close as he begins winding it up, it's possible to jump over the tip of the slashes before immediately sprinting to the right to avoid the slam. You can also move in after he uses his Leaping Fist Slam, but be careful as this move feature significant forward momentum and a large area of effect. It's best to jump backwards and deflect in mid-air to ensure it doesn't connect before moving in. Lastly, there's a great opportunity to deal damage whenever the boss uses his Palm Strike since the follow-up swipe is slow and always misses if you move in close.

is easy if you begin sprinting sideways the moment you see him swing his head in circles, but try to move in closer in the process, since he's always vulnerable after launching the final Idol. Watch out when in front of him at mid-range, however, since he can now instantly close the gap with a Lunging Punch that you'll need to quickly react to by guarding or dodging. If you get killed, confirm that he's done attacking before resurrecting since both his Burning Wave and Homing Idols could instantly kill you again if you're careless.

![](images/881ef4ac263b5cec84c02e75d2f564db5886a031477726565d97aa08449cf51d.jpg)  
Stunning the Demon by whistling with Malcontent creates a large opening to deal damage, but this tool becomes ineffective after three uses.

If you've saved up your Spirit Emblems, immediately use Malcontent to stun the Demon after landing the second deathblow. This interrupts his Flame Prison and can be done up to three times in a row, allowing you to safely deplete a large portion of his Vitality. The third stun is shorter and causes him to slam his head on the ground but don't stop attacking since this can't hurt you. He'll use his Flame Prison once he finally recovers, but you can choose to preemptively get out of its range, or decide to stay in close to deal damage. When he uses his Rushdown Sweep, get ready to jump again if another Danger Symbol appear since this means he'll quickly rush back in your direction to perform a second sweep using his phantom arm. His Explosive Crash also has a larger blast radius during Phase 3, but this doesn't change the way you avoid it—just be sure to gain some distance before grappling onto him.

# Emma, the Gentle Blade

# & Isshin Ashina

The late Lord Dogen's adoptive daughter and Isshin's pupil, Emma is a skilled fighter trained in the art of Ashina-ryu

![](images/6411b41ad4b53f02117a9d5aa0a9821aa4b80d415f6f60bd027a9860e657b818.jpg)

swordmanship. She's witnessed a Shura once before and recognizes that the same burning hatred now stirs within you as well.

# Multiple Encounters

You'll encounter the Owl atop Ashina Castle during the Interior Ministry raid. He'll give you a choice, and if you choose to obey the Iron Code then you'll battle Emma, the Gentle Blade and Isshin Ashina in succession. This is one long battle, so their entries here share Preparation and Environment details.

# Preparation

This is a lengthy back-to-back battle against two challenging opponents, so collect any missing Gourd Seeds to make sure your Healing Gourd can hold nine charges. If you haven't already, unlock the third Resurrection Node by defeating Lady Butterfly. Against Emma, Okinaga's Flame Vent can be very effective if you're willing to spend all your Emblems to quickly move on to Isshin. The Loaded Umbrella can protect you against both boss' quickdraw attacks and grabs. If you have the materials, upgrading to Suzaku's Lotus Umbrella can shield you from a few of Isshin's fire-based attacks during his final Phase.

Isshin is somewhat weak to Poison, so upgrading to Piercing Sabi-maru will make this tool quite potent against him. For combat arts, unlocking Ichimonji: Double can make both battles easier. Stock up on Dousing Powder to mitigate Isshin's fire-based attacks and consider acquiring the Withered Red Gourd by trading a few scales at the Pot Noble in Hirata Estate. Make sure to have a full supply of Fistful of Ash since it can be used to blind both bosses. Because this is a difficult battle, consider using Rice, Divine Grass, or Bundled Jizo Statues during promising attempts to help you secure a victory.

# Environment

As before, avoid fighting near the back wall since the set of samurai statues and open doors can hinder your movements and cause you to get stuck. Small patches of flames cover the floor once Isshin makes his entrance, but they're entirely harmless during the first Phase. Once Phase 2 begins, his Inferno attack will cause every flame patch to briefly erupt into a burning geyser, so you'll need to steer clear of them: watch for the ground around the flames to glow and quickly move out of the way. Look for small pockets of safety between the geyers, and always head towards the nearest corner when caught off guard.

# Key Strategies

Always be ready to deflect Emma's Gap-Closing Slash when she's at mid-range since it's extremely fast. Create openings to deal Vitality damage by interrupting her Quickdraw Ashina Cross with a slash or thrust as she winds up. Alternatively, sprint out of its reach before circling back to hit her from the side or back

while she recovers. Beware of the Aikido Throw she can use after you deflect her attacks and avoid it by sprinting backwards before punishing her with a thrust. Counter both her Lunging Thrust and Needle Thrust with a Mikiri whenever possible. When Emma retaliates with a Sword Dance combo, be sure to deflect its

final slash to create an opening and avoid being thrown off balance. Once her Vitality has been lowered below  $80\%$  strike her guard to weaken her Posture whenever there's an opportunity. Ichimonji: Double can make short work of her at that point.

![](images/9f23ce011d64b3fcb540d57580f79d8654583485f8528faa2aa8de6533008671.jpg)

![](images/4b88301907e0c76d13d49ebbdf70733ec10ab132266ec4cbdf622bfeef864cdb.jpg)

![](images/d7b03ec5657568df0a4730d6dc7a3dc82236ea37d69490b6df6ba53a547a944e.jpg)

# Emma, the Gentle Blade - Phase 1

Emma is highly skilled with the katana and adopts a straightforward fighting style that eschews the use of projectiles or ranged attacks. As Isshin's pupil, she can perform her own version of many of the same attacks you'll see him use. As she's capable of guarding most frontal attacks, this battle is all about finding or creating openings to lower her Vitality before focusing on breaking her Posture. The reach of her blade is relatively short, but many of her attacks feature heavy forward momentum and she can instantly strike at mid-range using her Gap-Closing Slash. This attack is extremely fast, so always be ready to guard or deflect it. You'll also need to watch out for her Lunging Thrust at that range, but it can reliably be countered with a Mikiri followed by a thrust of your own to deal Vitality damage. If you need to heal, retreat well out of reach or wait for her to miss an attack, since she'll either use this Lunging Thrust or her Gap-Closing Slash to punish you.

Because this battle serves as the opener to a lengthy duel against Isshin, it's best to conserve your Spirit Emblems for what's to come. With that said, dousing Emma in Oil before incinerating her with

![](images/1a3f63c30f785e47c1baf194f8aa11f628753df6cbf32720e29c131e569fc768.jpg)  
Be ready to deflect Emma's Gap-Closing Slash when she lunges forward with her blade held in this manner.

Flowing Flames from Okinaga's Flame Vent or using Living Force to coat your blade in flames can rapidly deplete her Vitality and make this fight much easier. Using Ako's Sugar can also allow you to make short work of her and quickly get back to fighting Isshin once you've become adept at creating openings and deflecting her attacks. When her Vitality falls below  $80\%$ , start relying on Ichimonji to break her Posture as quickly as possible.

Emma will often leave herself open by slowly walking sideways at mid- to close-range, so strike at her guard to deal Posture damage until she deflects. Forcing her to deflect (or deflecting her attacks) will often cause her to respond with a unique four-hit Sword Dance combo: she'll backstep and strike a graceful pose, before rushing in and slashing three times in quick succession. Be sure to at least guard the initial slash before attempting to deflect the following two, since there's no risk of being hit by those once you've guarded the first. From there, expect a slight pause before she uses both her katana and scabbard to perform a final slash. It's crucial to focus on deflecting this final slash, since simply guarding it will cause her to destabilize you and turn you around. If this happens, she'll then begin charging up a Quickdraw Ashina Cross; immediately spin around and strike her to interrupt it. If you manage to deflect her final slash on the other hand, you'll gain the advantage and create an opening to hit her with a thrust or Ichimonji: Double.

![](images/8fc47cf366d391153ff9c8a70f788f34bb3fcfa1dcb9bc27f061419c418a46e9.jpg)  
This pose signals Emma's Crossover Slash. Expect her to follow up with a Needle Thrust or DoubleSlash afterwards.

# Emma's Quickdraw Ashina Cross

Emma's signature Quickdraw Ashina Cross is the most dangerous attack in her arsenal, as guarding it causes you to take significant damage and the timing required to deflect both of its hits is very strict. This attack also has excellent range since she can dash forward from its quickdraw stance before lunging and slashing. However, Emma is left briefly vulnerable while she's charging up this attack and hitting her at that point will interrupt it by forcing her to guard. This stuns her, so immediately follow up with a thrust to deal damage or a fully charged Ichimonji to weaken her Posture. Prepare to move in and interrupt her every time she backsteps by performing her Double Slash, since she'll always transition into an Ashina Cross immediately afterwards.

If you aren't too close when she enters the quickdraw stance and there's plenty of room to retreat, it's also possible to sprint away and circle back to hit her from the side or behind while she's recovering. Holding your ground and dodging forward diagonally just as she lunges can avoid the attack and leave you behind her, but this requires good timing. If you're having difficulty dealing with this attack, the Loaded Umbrella lets you easily guard both hits without taking any damage.

![](images/e3cf02a17a0cb79a98e4671fccfb425d55f15ed00f1ead1d40a3a8b39876197b.jpg)  
Guarding the final hit of Emma's Sword Dance combo will destabilize you...

![](images/3280094531273169c84e3fbae0588d5acdb1fa70dac30d04bfb90a21cc68e300.jpg)  
...but immediately turning around lets you interrupt her Quickdraw Ashina. Cross before she has a chance to strike.

Although it's a great way to weaken her Posture, be careful when deflecting Emma's attacks, since this can cause her to retaliate with a highly damaging Aikido Throw that features significant reach. Learning to recognize the flowing bare-handed gesture that signals this grab is key, since you'll need to react quickly and sprint backwards to avoid it. If you're cornered when she uses this grab, avoid it with a well-timed lateral dodge just as she's about to lunge, or interrupt it with a quick Ichimonji. She's briefly vulnerable after missing, so move in and hit her with a thrust before she recovers. If you get caught, she'll smack you down to the floor and attempt to finish you off with a quick follow-up slice; safety roll away from her the moment you hit the ground before retreating to heal. She can also use a fast Sword Sweep after slashing at you, or as a reaction to being deflected or being forced to deflect. Whenever this happens, use the opportunity to hit her with a jump-kick counter to further weaken her Posture.

![](images/d975fcbcc81ecd9aada6cd911f13b822fe6daabd6735581859f806e132801efa.jpg)  
This flowing bare-handed gesture signals Emma's deadly Aikido Throw. Immediately sprint backwards the moment you see it.

# Isshin Ashina

Though his health may be failing, Isshin Ashina is still a master of swordsmanship with a style that has been honed over decades of brutal warfare. While he would normally be content to spend

![](images/776891f310636970845f0e0ba89cfb1122ecb755e2ff6961859ee95e444c6b68.jpg)

the rest of his days assisting Lord Kuro, Isshin will not hesitate to put down any who seek to harm the Divine Heir, including the Wolf.

# Isshin Ashina - Phase 1

Even in his old age and stricken by illness, Isshin is a formidable opponent that will quickly punish a careless offense. To defeat him during Phase 1, you'll need to create openings to lower his Vitality by dodging or deflecting his attacks before focusing on breaking his Posture. Unloading a full Sabimaru combo once there's an opening lets you easily accomplish this by inflicting Poison, but you may need to hit him a few more times before this status ailment takes hold. Alternatively, both Fistful of Ash and Firecrackers can be used to blind him long enough to deal damage with a thrust, but use the latter sparingly, since you'll want to conserve some Spirit Emblems for Phase 2. Once his Vitality has been lowered, Ichimonji: Double can be used to severely weaken his Posture.

Like Emma, Isshin will often walk at a slow pace with his sword held low, but he can also surge forward with a quick Gap-ClosingSlash (his version features follow-up slashes) or ready a Quickdraw Ashina

![](images/eaa20aaa9db1a0f242ca564592c2a52b2072dc09f1aab11f60103cb4b853279c.jpg)

Isshin's Strafing Thrust should always be countered with a Mikiri followed by a thrust of your own.

Cross to begin his offense at mid-range. Stay on your guard and wait for him to make the first move instead of being overly aggressive. When on the defensive, focus on guarding or deflecting his slashes, but be on the lookout for his Cross Cut Combo since it leads into a sweep unless deflected. He can also use his Aikido Throw after stepping to his right and quickly slashing. If this slash connects, the only way to avoid the incoming grab is to refrain from going into a braceguard and instead dodge backwards or sideways to quickly recover.

# Mind's Eye

Attempting to strike Isshin with a melee attack when he's slowly walking backwards or sideways will cause him to use his unique Mind's Eye technique. This lets him anticipate the blow and swiftly dodge by shifting his body to the side before countering with either a spinning horizontal slash or Aikido Throw. His version of this grab has a shorter reach than Emma's, but it also has a much faster startup. Immediately dodging backwards whenever he uses Mind's Eye lets you avoid both of his potential counterattacks, but you'll need to perform a second dodge (or walk backwards after the first) to create enough distance if he uses his Aikido Throw. Because his reactions after using Mind's Eye are so predictable, purposefully striking him while he's slowly walking allows you to create openings by baiting out his Aikido Throw to deal damage as he recovers. Refrain from mindlessly attacking him, however, or he'll punish you while you're locked in an attack animation.

Isshin's version of the Quickdraw Ashina Cross can't be interrupted with regular attacks, but it has less range and is easier to dodge or deflect than Emma's. Either sprint away if there's room to do so (and circle back around to hit him while he recovers) or stay at mid-range and wait for a glint to appear after he tilts his scabbard. From there, immediately dodge forward diagonally to get behind him and create an opening. Opting to instead deflect both slashes is slightly riskier, but it briefly stuns him and gives you enough time to use a thrust. If you're having trouble avoiding this attack, deploying the Loaded Umbrella can protect you, but remember to keep a close eye on your Spirit Emblem reserves. If you move too close when Isshin is in quickdraw stance, he'll surprise you with a Rising Cut & Sweep. Once his Vitality has been lowered, this can be used to your advantage by purposefully baiting him to use the sweep before countering with a jump-kick to weaken his Posture.

![](images/c3a04bb6679c82a19e29475baf8247d7b213c2cc8f74690f96b4279bd2ba34c8.jpg)  
Striking Isshin when he's walking in this stance will trigger his Mind's Eye.

Deflecting Isshin's attacks or striking his guard will often cause him to respond by holding his sword overhead with both hands to windup a powerful Ichimonji. Wait for him to fully pull his katana back and immediately dodge towards his left side the moment he leans forward to strike. Circling around him is an easier way to avoid this attack, but this only works if you're right next to him so don't rely exclusively on this tactic. Both methods position you behind him and create an opening by also avoiding his potential follow-up slash. Deflecting Isshin's Ichimonji during Phase 1 is another viable option, but as this will get you killed during Phase 2, it's best to focus on dodging instead. Guarding this attack should only be used as a last resort, since the first hit will crush your guard and leave you defenseless against the potential second hit.

Continuing to attack once you've created an opening will force Isshin to begin guarding your slashes, and is a good way to weaken his Posture. Be careful, however, since he'll soon deflect. Always be ready to immediately guard or deflect back the instant this happens since both of his potential responses are extremely fast. He'll most often answer with a modified Triple Slash Combo that begins with an extremely fast rising slash before finishing with the same two slashes as the standalone version. His other option is a Palm Strike into Thrust that can easily catch you off guard. Guard or deflect the palm strike and dodge forward to counter the thrust with a Mikiri. Lastly, prepare to counter his Strafing Thrust with a Mikiri if he starts walking towards his left after you deflect one of his attacks. This move is very easy to punish once you've learned to recognize it, but he'll never perform it unless you deflect his slashes.

# Isshin Ashina — Phase 2

Things really heat up during Phase 2, since Isshin will make use of the raging flames overtaking Ashina Castle to power up a host of new fire-based attacks. Using Dousing Powder to bolster your fire resistance is a good idea at this point since it'll help mitigate some of the damage dealt by these attacks. Suzaku's Lotus Umbrella can protect you from his Burning Wave and Fiery Ichimonji if you have it, but be careful when deploying this tool, since it won't work against his Scorching Sweep or Inferno. Applying Poison with Sabimaru is still effective, but remember to wait for an opening before launching into a combo.

After recovering from the deathblow, Isshin immediately uses his incredibly dangerous Inferno attack to cause the burning portions of the floor to erupt into flaming geyers. He'll slash twice to stoke the flames, and you'll then have a second to quickly find a safe spot before the geyers erupt and he rushes in to perform his One Mind quickdraw technique. The corners of the room are always safe, but the zoomed-in camera when pressed against the wall can make it difficult to get a clear view of the action as he rushes in. The open balcony features a few safe spots and retreating there works well. If you react quickly, striking with Ichimonji can also let you interrupt his Inferno as he winds up.

![](images/0e4eff44065b8813f747332aeecf20d92cdec6f7db8782d9328f508583920b98.jpg)  
Successfully dodging the opening slash of his One Mind quickdraw combo lets you get behind him.

# One Mind

Isshin always performs this unique quickdraw technique after setting the room ablaze with his Inferno attack. He'll rush towards you through the flames and unleash a single quickdraw slash before kneeling and sheathing his blade. This is then followed by a four-hit flurry of inhumanly-fast cuts before he lunges forward to perform a powerful finishing slash. Isshin tracks your position as he rushes in to perform his One Mind, but it's possible to cleanly avoid his opening slash by dodging towards his left side just as he's about to slash. From there, dodge backwards to escape the bubble-like radius of his flurry before punishing him.

Due to their piercing properties, guarding these slashes will only negate  $50\%$  of the damage dealt. Deflecting them is a better option (deflect once as he draws near, then watch for the glint before deflecting four times in quick succession, and once more as he clutches the sword's hilt with his right hand) but requires good timing. Guarding the first hit of his flurry ensures that you'll automatically guard the rest, so there's no risk in attempting to deflect at that point. If these options prove too difficult, deploy the Loaded Umbrella to negate all damage or escape using Aged Feather Mist Raven instead.

![](images/3ac744e8ff0f954df4acc44bc9d6c922d25d91d94d40a909e1b411dc999a7ee7.jpg)  
Find a safe spot when the room erupts in flames and prepare to dodge his incoming One Mind quickdraw combo.

Isshin tracks your position as he rushes in, but it's possible to cleanly avoid his opening slash by dodging towards him and to his right side just as he's about to slash; from there, dodge backwards to escape the bubble-like radius of his flurry before punishing him. If either of these options prove too difficult, deploy the Loaded Umbrella to negate all damage or escape using Aged Feather Mist Raven.

His regular Phase 1 move set remains largely unchanged, but you'll now have to contend with his upgraded Fiery Ichimonji. Refrain from guarding or deflecting the opening overhead strike, since this will cause you to take severe damage from the incoming wave of flames generated by this version's horizontal follow-up slash. Instead, dodge towards his left side to avoid the entire attack and create a large opening. He'll often respond with this Fiery Ichimonji after guarding or being deflected and will always perform it as a follow-up to his Crossover Slash, so learn to anticipate it and use it as an opportunity to deal damage.

His Burning Wave is another major threat since it can hit you at any range, heavily tracks your movements, and deals severe damage. The trick to avoiding it is to jump over the incoming flame wave instead of sprinting sideways to outrun it. Landing in the flames won't damage you once the wave has passed, so hold your ground as he bends sideways to wind up and jump towards him to close the gap and punish him while he recovers. Be careful not to overcommit to your offense when attacking him up close, however, since he'll often retaliate with a fast Scorching Sweep. This attack begins with a low spinning slash that can be guarded or deflected before ending with a flaming sweep that can be avoided by jumping towards his left side to land behind him.

![](images/2fb3256617cf03d7319924ee4a10ad886397f736012a09880df1b7377ea487be.jpg)  
Jump forward over Isshin's Burning Wave then rush in to deal damage as he recovers.

# Genichiro, Way of Tomoe

# & Isshin the Sword Saint

After his defeat at the hands of the Wolf, Genichiro sought a way to be able to counter his adversary. What he found was the black

![](images/3c199c27fd88af3921ed7a6185f1f97d158bdb20e0ae08343b4ee81b392ce977.jpg)

Mortal Blade. If he cannot defeat the Wolf, Genichiro is willing to sacrifice his very being and use this weapon to bring forth someone who can.

# Multiple Encounters

You'll encounter Genichiro after reaching Ashina Reservoir's secret passage at the end of the game, and must then battle him and Isshin, the Sword Saint in succession. This is one long battle, so their entries here share Preparation and Environment details.

# Preparation

This climactic battle consists of a final duel with Genichiro, followed by a lengthy clash with Isshin Ashina at the height of his power. It's highly recommended that you upgrade both your Healing Gourd and Vitality by hunting down as many missing Gourd Seeds and Prayer Beads as possible. If you haven't done so already, be sure to also defeat Lady Butterfly before visiting the Page to unlock a third Resurrection Node. Stocking up Oil and unlocking the Living Force skill can allow you to deal large amounts of damage with your Flame Vent. Otherwise, upgrading to the Lazulite version of the Shuriken and Piercing version of Sabimaru also proves useful. Bring plenty of Ako's Sugar since it can make a significant difference during both battles when used in tandem with the Devotion skill. In terms of combat arts, learning Ichimonji: Double can allow you to severely weaken both boss' Posture during openings and Senpou Leaping Kicks can be used to deal even more Posture damage after jumping over sweeps. Lastly, consider making use of Divine Grass and Bundled Jizo Statues during promising attempts.

# Environment

This area is an expansive silver grass field located at the edge of a cliff. It provides more than enough room to outmaneuver both bosses, but be careful when sprinting near its perimeter as you could accidentally fall off the edge and take severe damage. Always be mindful of your positioning and avoid fighting near the cliff's edge: this is particularly important once things get heated during the later stages of the battle against Isshin. The silver grass can slightly obscure opponents' movements and makes it a bit more difficult to recognize their attacks as a result. If this proves to be a hindrance, fighting near the large patch of uncluttered terrain next to the broken bridge on the opposite end of the field allows for the best visibility. During Phases 2 and 3, the few large rocks dotted throughout field can serve as makeshift cover whenever you need to heal. Lightning bolts will periodically rain down across the field at that point, but there's no risk of them damaging you.

# Key Strategies

Sprinting behind Genichiro creates an opening to deal damage if you're already at close-to mid-range when he begins winding up his Horizontal Mortal Draw. If you manage to get behind him, slash a few times but prepare to dodge his follow-up Vertical Mortal Draw before landing a few more hits as he recovers. Ichimonji can also be used to interrupt both types of Mortal Draws if you're quick enough. With proper timing, it's even possible to dodge

![](images/ad3706609703fd887a65684da2d3675a614991e3fa6481cbc459734a8aa315e5.jpg)

directly through the Horizontal Mortal Draw regardless of range. Practicing this can speed up the time it takes to defeat Genichiro.

Always punish Genichiro's Lunging Impale with a Mikiri Counter and reduce his Posture by pressuring him with a few slashes whenever there's a gap in his offense. If he responds with a Leaping Helmbreaker or Slashing Frenzy, deflecting the rising slash that closes out these

![](images/91a39f8acf4d956c3e624f738d325615ff40fc331df4df5cab31281659d6140f.jpg)

attacks forces Genichiro into using a Counter Thrust. This creates more Mikiri Counter opportunities and lets you break his Posture faster. Don't be afraid to use Ako's Sugar to speed up this process, but conserve as many Spirit Emblems and Healing Gourd charges as possible for the battle ahead.

![](images/9bd0bba6cac77924df543c1f09a7b1c2faf3d9c45fca7724f8145756f216217c.jpg)

# Genichiro, Way of Tomoe - Phase 1

Genichiro fights the same way he did after shedding his armor during your previous encounter, but his lightning-based attacks have now been replaced with a deadly Horizontal Mortal Draw. This new attack features impressive reach and can pierce through your guard due to its Spirit-type damage, so focus on dodging it instead of guarding or deflecting. There's enough time to sprint directly behind Genichiro and create an opening if you're at close- to mid-range when he winds up a Mortal Draw. If you're too far, immediately sprint backwards out of reach or deploy Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella to negate all damage. He'll often follow up with a Vertical

![](images/35b3d1bc388aa5ea228b1cdf85ec742c8951c5d726a1945951aee976537e3739.jpg)

Watch as Genichiro's left hand slides along the surface of the blade and dodge through his Horizontal Mortal Draw just as his hand reaches the tip.

Mortal Draw if you're nearby as he recovers, but this can easily be avoided by circling towards his back before dealing damage.

Outside of serving as Genichiro's opening move, the Horizontal Mortal Draw can only be performed as a follow-up attack. Expect him to use it following his Slash & Kick combo and after he fires either one or two arrows from a standing position. Lastly, he can also cancel into it if you retreat during the Slashing Frenzy he performs after running sideways. Learning to anticipate when he can transition into a Horizontal Mortal Draw allows you to reliably create openings by either getting behind him or by interrupting the attack with a quick Ichimonji as he winds up. Taking advantage of these damage dealing opportunities can help you conserve supplies.

Striking at Genichiro's guard with a compact two-hit combo whenever there's a gap in his offense not only deals Posture damage, but also causes him to respond with attacks that lead into Mikiri Counter opportunities. Both his Leaping Helmbreaker and Slashing Frenzy can end with a rising slash that results in a delayed Counter Thrust when deflected. When the Danger Symbol appears, wait for him to ready his blade in a thrusting stance and counter with a Mikiri. His Lunging Impale is often used to close the gap and presents another opportunity to counter with a Mikiri. Always transition into a thrust of your own after a Mikiri Counter to deal Vitality damage. When Genichiro performs one of his sweeping attacks, counter with a jump-kick and follow up with a mid-air Ichimonji: Double to further weaken his Posture.

# Isshin, the Sword Saint

Resurrected by Genichiro with the power of the black Mortal Blade, the greatest warrior the Ashina have ever known returns in his prime. The same strength that allowed him to claim territories and fend off the Interior Ministry once again courses through

![](images/3fd62ec02ea0757b28c53b27450235818641122af0dee49ef7f7adc0c7fdb84e.jpg)

him. If allowed to persist, this single-minded killing machine will surely spread war across every corner of the land once again.

# Key Strategies

During Phase 1, deflecting Isshin's sword slashes or pressuring his guard whenever there's an opening can cause him to use his Strafing Thrust, Ichimonji, Quickdraw Ashina Cross, or Palm Strike & Thrust. Each of these moves can be exploited to create openings and damage his Vitality and Posture. Dousing him in Oil before using a Flame Vent blast followed by Living Force during openings can quickly

lower his Vitality. When he uses a sweep, countering with a mid-air Senpou Leaping Kick can greatly weaken his Posture.

During Phase 2, focus on dodging towards Isshin's back whenever he uses an Overhead Spear Slam and make use of every opportunity to counter his Lunging Impale with a Mikiri to weaken his Posture and deal a

bit of damage. Spend your Spirit Emblems during Phases 1 and 2 and use Ako's Sugar to increase your damage. Once you've reached the battle's climax, the key is to perform Lightning Reversals to severely weaken him whenever he uses either his Lightning Overhead Slam or his Lightning Retreating Slash.

# Isshin, the Sword Saint - Phase 1

The opening portion of this battle is a pure katana on katana duel that will put all that you've learned so far to the test. Isshin's Posture recovers rapidly, so you'll first need to lower his Vitality below  $80\%$  before focusing on breaking his Posture. He has an iron-clad defense from the front, but engaging in swordplay can often cause him to respond with attacks that lead to damage dealing opportunities. Isshin walks at an intimidatingly slow pace when at a distance and won't be a threat until you enter mid-range. From there, he can use a Gap-Closing Slash or Lateral Dash Combo to move in and begin his offense. Up close, he attacks with a variety of sword-based combos that often mix deliberate pauses and fast strikes to throw you off balance. When aiming to deflect his slashes, it's best to focus on timing your input the moment you see him make a move until you become comfortable with his rhythm. If you're too early, this will simply result in a guard instead of taking damage.

![](images/d10ae5e959026d7bbcd5f3cf04c6b67bb3d0a87de4a51e629b5aa97778db20aa.jpg)  
Always be prepared to defend against a faster version of Isshin's Triple Slash Combo if you deflect his slashes or force him to guard or deflect yours.

![](images/5d7826f58d683b07d4c2c17b20bf00a64f307166eead8238690f59effe8eccac.jpg)  
Though riskier, the Circular Mortal Slash can also be avoided by dodging forward once Isshin's right hand clutches the blade's hilt.

Isshin can rapidly break your Posture if you focus too heavily on guarding his attacks, so keep a close eye on your Posture gauge and retreat to regain your composure when necessary. If you ever need to heal during Phase 1, sprinting away from him lets you safely do so since he won't aggressively pursue you. Dousing him in Oil allows you to easily set him ablaze with a regular blast from the Flame Vent followed by Living Force when there's an opening. He'll briefly be stunned when the Burn status takes hold, so continue slashing to deal significant damage. Remember to always reapply Oil before repeating this tactic. Alternatively, Isshin can also be Poisoned with a full Sabimaru combo followed by a few additional slashes. Once this happens, you can simply retreat and wait for his Vitality to deplete before focusing on breaking his Posture. Don't be afraid to use your Emblems during Phases 1 and 2, since the final portion of the battle gives you many opportunities to lower his Vitality without relying on tools or combat arts.

There's often a lull in the action at close-range, so attack with a single slash to force him to guard, or with a thrust to force him to deflect. This tactic can be used to bait out his Strafing Thrust or Ichimonji (when he guards), and his Quickdraw Ashina Cross or Palm Strike & Thrust (when he deflects). Each of these attacks can be avoided or countered in ways that leave him wide open, so they become an opportunity to deal damage once you've learned how to best deal with them. His Strafing Thrust can easily be anticipated, as he always takes a few steps towards his left before thrusting. Countering it with a Mikiri followed by a thrust of your own is a surefire way to deal Vitality damage. Never follow up with more than a single attack after successfully landing a Mikiri Counter,

![](images/a526dec7c92fc67878ac6fd0b20ce03f26de06ddea3b525dcb4d3828a1cbf08c.jpg)  
Bait out Isshin's Palm Strike & Thrust by forcing him to deflect, then counter it with a Mikiri to weaken his Posture.

however, since he'll immediately retaliate afterwards. In that situation, he's most likely to respond with a Crossover Slash that can lead into his Circular MortalSlash once his Posture has been lowered. When he winds up this MortalSlash, it's safest to retreat before rushing back in to deal damage with a sprinting thrust.

Isshin's Ichimonji can be avoided by waiting a second as he holds his sword overhead with both hands, then dodging forward diagonally just as he's about to slash. This allows you to get behind him and deal damage. Expect a fast second slash to immediately follow, but it won't be able to hit you from that position. Opting to deflect his Ichimonji instead will briefly stun you and cause him to retaliate with a Dragon Flash. This is a dangerous situation to be in, but dodging the Dragon Flash's shockwave always creates an opening to deal Vitality damage. When stunned after deflecting his Ichimonji, hold the sprint button down while tilting the left stick backwards to ensure that you start sprinting the instant you recover, then avoid the shockwave by veering to the side once Sekiro steps backwards. If you're confident in your reflexes, it's also possible to deflect the shockwave or to avoid it using a well-timed lateral dodge before circling behind Isshin to deal even more damage.

# Quickdraw Ashina Cross

Isshin enters a quickdraw stance as he begins powering up his Ashina Cross: this attack is quite dangerous since it hits twice, causes him to dash forward, and deals piercing damage. It can either be performed unprompted, or as a reaction if you force him to deflect. It's possible to create an opening by sprinting out of reach as he winds up before circling around behind him to deal damage with a sprint attack. Alternatively, you can also stay at mid-range and dodge diagonally towards his back once he tilts his scabbard downwards and a glint emanates from it.

Getting close to Isshin when he's winding up his Ashina Cross will always cause him to cancel into a Rising Cut & Sweep instead. This can be used to your advantage once his Vitality has been sufficiently lowered, since it creates a reliable opportunity to deal severe amounts of Posture damage. Bait the Rising Cut by moving in close whenever he's readying an Ashina Cross, then immediately guard or deflect before punishing the incoming sweep with a jump-kick counter or mid-air Senpou Leaping Kicks (without the follow ups) for even more Posture damage.

![](images/a5c77ae08a75a7446154b290a89b7307ff9b8a3be793bbc0c212599454192ad1.jpg)  
When guarding, watch out for Isshin's Cross Cut Combo since it leads into a fast sword sweep.

# Isshin, the Sword Saint - Phase 2

Phase 2 begins with Isshin slamming his foot down to push you away before unearthing a large cross-shaped spear he now wields in his left hand. It's possible to slightly delay this from happening by pressuring him, but try to position yourself near his back once he reaches for the spear, since this allows you to land some free hits. Be careful, though, as he'll swipe horizontally after pulling the spear out. At this point, Isshin casts aside the controlled and restrained fighting style he adopted during Phase 1, and gains access to an entirely new set of attacks that utilize both his sword and spear in addition to a concealed firearm. He's now much more aggressive and will actively chase you if you retreat to heal. When retreating, watch out for his sprinting Firearm Barrage or leaping Overhead Spear Slam since they can both hit you from afar. You'll need to veer sideways to avoid his gunshots, while the overhead slam is easily avoided by continuing to sprint away from him. He'll quickly dash forward and slash with his sword after you avoid the overhead slam, so keep sprinting and only use your Healing Gourd once you're out of range of his follow-up slashes.

![](images/efb069e0946087c431f00676ed02e05e311836d665e227276696fa0bd11e52c9.jpg)  
Expect a sprinting Firearm Barrage or leaping Overhead Spear Slam following Isshin's Crossover Advance.

![](images/78e92bdefc839cce4c039d21d355eba2738d11f764f362d7c9c19df53fcae2b0.jpg)  
Be ready to counter Isshin's Lunging Impale with a Mikiri when he lifts his spear in this manner.

Isshin's spear-based attacks are slower but severely weaken your Posture when guarded, so try to dodge or deflect them instead to prevent getting Posture-broken. Both versions of his Overhead Spear Slam present a reliable opportunity to deal damage if you dodge diagonally towards his back as he slams down. If you've doused him in Oil beforehand, this is your chance to hit him with a Flame Vent blast followed by Living Force to take off a large chunk of Vitality. Otherwise, stick to a single thrust or Ichimonji since he'll often recover with a Retreating SpearSlash if you commit to multiple hits. Learn to recognize Isshin's Lunging Impale and punish it with a Mikiri Counter whenever he uses it. This can let you deal large amounts of Posture damage as well as lower his Vitality with a single slash (thrusting won't work) after you recover. This is also a good opportunity to hit him with a Flame Vent blast. He'll often perform his Turnaround Combo when chasing you down, so use this to your advantage by countering the Lunging Impale it closes out with.

His Heavy Combo is extremely dangerous, but there's enough time to retreat out of its range after guarding or deflecting the pair of sword slashes it opens with. Always expect him to close it out with a Lunging Impale or Circular MortalSlash. Be careful when pressuring Isshin's guard, since he also uses his Circular MortalSlash after deflecting. At close range, there's just enough time to retreat, so don't hesitate or you you'll get hit. It's still possible to use a well-timed dodge to go directly through this MortalSlash and create an opening, but as before, this is highly risky. Isshin's Retreating SpearSlash is a constant threat and will often transition into a Firearm Barrage before finishing with a Lunging Impale or Spear Sweep. Stay alert, as you'll need to quickly confirm which of these two attacks is coming when the Danger Symbol appears after he uses his firearm. Watch out for his Concealed Firearm Shot after deflecting his Overhead Spear Slam or the rising spear slash he can perform after being deflected. This surprise shot deals significant damage and knocks you back if it connects, so be ready to dodge sideways or deflect it the instant you hear a gun cocking sound.

![](images/a281d84b3a10206576c4c898b7e3d5c8ccf1154294cde4ce2596632870048147.jpg)  
Watch out for a surprise Firearm Barrage after dodging Isshin's Overhead Spear Slam.

# Deflecting Isshin's Spear Attacks

Focusing on deflecting Isshin's spear-based attacks isn't necessary, but it can allow you to quickly rack up a ton of Posture damage in addition to forcing him to use his Lunging Impale far more often. As such, this tactic can be used to quickly reach Phase 3 once you've lowered his Posture recovery rate. Be aware that this is inherently riskier, however, as it requires practice and good reflexes. Don't be afraid to rely on the previously mentioned strategy if you're finding this too difficult.

Deflecting Isshin's Overhead Spear Slam will always push his spear to your left side, and from there, he can either cross his arms to signal a horizontal swipe, or use his spear to drag himself sideways before performing a delayed rising slash. Deflecting the former will push his spear to the right, where he can then recover his momentum with a slightly delayed rising slash. It's possible to get into a rhythm and chain together lengthy deflect sequences, but it usually won't take long before he uses a Lunging Impale or attacks with his firearm. His sword is also a threat, so be ready to react if he uses it.

![](images/fa6843737c4f97e00b1c4857117a2d69eedbdb8b423e4b91bd7469fde1eeb932.jpg)  
Learn to recognize Isshin's Heavy Combo by the spin he performs before its opening sword slash.

![](images/f6a9a619af485044d1b54a836bbe1b03ac3decea5c5ae503dac3df8f5c18045d.jpg)  
This variation of the Ichimonji is now preceded by a quick rightward sword slash but can still lead to an opening if you dodge forward and diagonally.

![](images/abc10d38130dc7160c9eadcfe1bff80f1bb465a87a19cbe433da1fa10c3e8006.jpg)

# 通程分析

Chapter 5

# Progression & Analysis

There's an abundance of possible routes to reach the Wolf's goal, and each one has its benefits and disadvantages. This chapter is for the shinobi who knows the value of planning and preparation; it lays all the possibilities out before you, so you can leave almost nothing to chance.

![](images/d8a903c82900e764e8e15d544b374f56a78095bf6bf5db6fb03679bfce949c30.jpg)

# Progression & Analysis

This chapter aims to give you an overview of how progression through the game works, and help you to plan your own optimal path through it. We'll recommend when to tackle each area and when to acquire the most important items and upgrades. The progression maps section will help to make finding the locations of NPCs and key enemies and items much easier.

This map of the Ashina lands shows where each of the areas are in relation to the others. Not all of these areas are reachable by traversing between them within the game; you're transported to Hirata Estate and Fountainhead Palace during event scenes. Though Sekiro is not technically an open world game, seeing the whole world illustrated like this gives each area a greater sense of place, and can help with orientation.

# Game Progression Chart

Looking at progression through the game from a high level, we created this chart that shows how all of the areas link together. The order in which you choose to tackle areas and defeat bosses affects the time of day of later areas, so we've arranged the chart to show which time zones each area will inhabit if you complete the required progression goals in our recommended order. For details on progression goals within an area and our recommendations on when to tackle each one, follow the page references shown in this chart. For the exact values related to time of day changes, see P42 in the Shinobi School chapter.

# Morning

After the prologue, the game begins in the Morning time zone. Depending on your skill level, you can potentially use this to your advantage. You can access a lot of areas during this time period, and while you cannot fully complete them until after defeating Genichiro, you can explore them and defeat sub-bosses; they'll have their lowest possible stats, but similarly, your character will not be as powerful as later in the game, so you'll need to rely on your combat proficiency.

# Noon

Time changes to Noon as soon as you defeat either Genichiro Ashina in Ashina Castle, or Corrupted Monk (Illusion) in Ashina Depths. Defeating either of those bosses will also decide which Vengeful Spirits will appear after you progress the time of day again to Evening. Defeat the Corrupted Monk (Illusion) and you'll be facing Vengeful Spirit Mibu Villagers, whereas defeating Genichiro Ashina will lead to Vengeful Spirit Ninghtjar Ninjas and Fencers.

# Evening

Evening will arrive after defeating three of the four main bosses that you can reach after defeating Gyoubu Oniwa in Ashina Outskirts. Those bosses are: Genichiro Ashina in Ashina Castle, Corrupted Monk (Illusion) in Ashina Depths, Guardian Ape in Sunken Valley Passage, and the Folding Screen Monkeys in Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo. The order in which you tackle those bosses is somewhat open; you cannot access the Folding Screen Monkeys until you learn about the Mortal Blade from Isshin Asina, which cannot happen until after Genichiro Ashina is defeated. Similarly, to reach Sunken Valley Passage you need the Gun Fort Shrine Key, which you can't get until after you learn about the Mortal Blade. Evening is when Vengeful Spirits will start appearing. They can only appear in a few areas; look out for the telltale glow of them appearing, because they're often in places that make the normal encounters there much more difficult.

# Night

The change to Night will occur as soon as you first step into Fountainhead Palace, and it will remain that way until you complete the game. Any enemies effected by time of day changes will now be at their most powerful, so if you're going back to explore earlier areas, some extra caution is advised. Vengeful Spirits also still roam during this time.

![](images/d66117de51c7f373bfbd4a97e71fe17f82fa1ca7346cc719fee88a5319ae5793.jpg)

The following pages are home to maps of the entire game, presented in a recommended order. These maps reveal all of the important progression-related items, upgrade materials and NPC locations. Key items are shown in purple and upgrade materials are shown in red.

The opening moments of the game take place in Ashina Reservoir before the main game begins, and are not subject to any time of day changes. Nothing you do here affects the areas that follow it.

While most of the enemies within Hirata Estate are not subject to any time of day changes, Lady Butterfly is. She will be a challenge regardless of what time of day you face her in, but the earlier you can beat her to obtain the Sakura Droplet, the better. Having it ready so that you can give it to Lord Kuro after defeating Genichiro Ashina will mean you can take advantage of the extra Resurrection Node straight away.

# Ashina Castle

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>8799</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>1676</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>3000</td></tr></table>

Your first real progression choices need to be made once you reach this area. The first choice is which of the two available main bosses to head towards: Genichiro Ashina at the top of Ashina Castle, or Corrupted Monk (Illusion) at the end of Ashina Depths. Going straight for Genichiro is the most direct option and presents the most natural event progression, whereas going to Ashina Depths is a longer, and slightly more difficult approach. Which of those two you defeat first will decide the type of Vengeful Spirits you'll face later.

Heading to Ashina Depths rewards you with a large amount of Skill EXP on the way to the Corrupted Monk, and defeating her early will give you access to the Mibu Breathing Technique, meaning less back-tracking to areas of deep water later on. Heading for Genichiro will allow you to progress events more quickly and open other areas. If you go to Ashina Depths first, you'll still need to defeat Genichiro before you can complete those other areas. Whichever option you choose, it's worth taking the time to explore the Abandoned Dungeon and Ashina Reservoir before killing one of those bosses.

# Abandoned Dungeon

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>1669</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>160</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>1400</td></tr></table>

The Abandoned Dungeon is an area with many paths that connect the Ashina territories. You can enter it either via the path from Ashina Castle, or along the water channel from the well in Ashina Reservoir. Senpou Temple, Mt, Kongo can easily be accessed by entering the dungeon via the path from the Ashina Castle, but to reach Ashina Depths from that path you'll have to face a very dangerous Shichimen Warrior. Enter the dungeon from Ashina Reservoir, however, and you'll be on the other side of the Shichimen Warrior and can progress directly towards the depths. You can also encounter Vegenful Spirits in this area, so be mindful if you're here during the Evening.
