# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>13475</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>2943</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>2800</td></tr></table>

You can reach Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo from Ashina Outskirts via the cave where the Headless dwells. From this entrance, you'll only be able to access the Bell Demon's Temple, which means you can get the Bell Demon extremely early in the game if you desire. Getting it early will allow you to reap the benefits of the increased item drop rates for more of the game, as long as you can handle the increased difficulty.

This area can be reached very early in the game while it's still Morning. The Gourd Seed that you can pick up early in the area is especially enticing, and can be acquired with very little trouble. Your main roadblock here will be the Armored Warrior, but he can be defeated without the need to acquire specific Skills or tools. Defeat him and you'll be able to reach the part of the area where you can pick up the Senpou Esoteric Text, containing Skills that allow you to increase item drop rates. You can also acquire the Bell Demon here and combine its effects with the Skills from the Senpou Arts to maximize your item-gathering potential.

Reaching the Main Hall at the top of the mountain before finding out about the Mortal Blade (you can still kill Genichiro Ashina to advance the time of day first) will

allow you to speak with the Holy Senpou Priest. If you've also spoken to the Faithful One in Ashina Castle, you can receive the Holy Chapters: Infested, which means you won't need the Mibu Breathing Technique to retrieve it from the bottom of the pond later. Once time of day has progressed to Evening, this is one of the few areas where you'll encounter Vengeful Spirits regardless of which main boss you killed first.

# Sunken Valley

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>9204</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>1065</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>500</td></tr></table>

Sunken Valley can be accessed by jumping across the ravine at the back of Ashina Castle, near the Great Serpent Shrine. You can reach the area without having killed any boss other than Gyoubu, but you will not be able to continue to Sunken Valley Passage until you have the Gun Fort Shrine Key. Going all the way through this area can be difficult early in the game, due to the amount of enemies with powerful ranged attacks, but there are a lot of upgrade materials, along with a Gourd Seed and some Prayer Beads that you can pick up without venturing too far in; if you're struggling with some of the boss encounters, coming here early to get those items can be a good idea.

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>9284</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>148</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>1600</td></tr></table>

The only way to access this area is by using the Gun Fort Shrine Key to open the door at the end of the Sunken Valley. The key can only be obtained after defeating Genichiro Ashina and progressing the main story to the point where Lord Kuro opens the library. You'll need to defeat the Guardian Ape here to gain access to the Lotus of the Palace: a key progression item. There aren't any Gourd Seeds or Prayer Beads to acquire, so the only reason to explore the area fully is if you want to acquire both Serpent Viscera. To get both of them you'll first need to kill the Folding Screen Monkeys in Senpou Temple, Mt, Kongo for the Puppeteer Ninjutsu, but you only need the Viscera to attain the Return ending; if you're not aiming for that ending, and don't mind not gaining access to the Divine Child's curative items, then you can skip going for the Viscera.

# Ashina Depths

![](images/be2cbecd47b93d1b0d3dc4a74067d8d5846750de960d443505daadec00fdd49e.jpg)

The Corrupted Monk (Illusion) at the end of this area is one of the two main bosses that you can kill after defeating Gyoubu Oniwa in Ashina Outskirts. If you defeated Genichiro Ashina before defeating the boss of this area, and arrive here during the evening, you'll have to contend with Vengeful Spirit Nightjar Ninja and Fencers, which will make some encounters much more difficult.

Waiting to access Ashina Depths until after you've completed the other main areas will give you a much smoother event progression through the game than coming here earlier. It will always be evening when following that route, so there will be Vengeful Spirits around, but you'll be significantly stronger after having cleared the other areas. Because you'll have the Puppeteer Ninjutsu as well, you can arrive here via the cave with the Great Serpent at the bottom of Sunken Valley Passage, rather than going through the Abandoned Dungeon. If you've already acquired everything necessary to recreate the fountainhead aroma, then picking up the Shelter Stone from within the Wedding Cave will trigger the start of the Interior Ministry raid straight away.

After acquiring the fountainhead aroma, return to the Wedding Cave here and enter the palanquin in the middle of the cave. Pray once you're inside it and the straw effigy will transport you to Fountainhead Palace. As soon as you enter that area, time will advance to Night, so if you have any sub-bosses that you haven't killed, this would be a good time to do so before they get more powerful.

Regardless of the order in which you tackled the previous areas, when you acquire the final item to recreate the fountainhead aroma (Mortal Blade from Senpou Temple, Mt, Kongo, Lotus of the Palace from Sunken Valley Passage, or the Shelter Stone from Ashina Depths), the Interior Ministry will launch a raid on Ashina Castle. You'll lose access to all Sculptor's Idols in the area other than the Abandoned Dungeon Entrance Idol, which will now be your only means of accessing Ashina Castle. All of the other Idols can be reactivated, but you need to Commune with them again.

Enemies within the castle grounds are significantly stronger than they were before, but since the raid is contained to the castle, and there is no time of day advancement, enemies in other areas remain unchanged.

The Great Shinobi - Owl awaits you at the Castle Tower Lookout, and once you make it there and speak with him you'll need to make a choice that will effect the rest of the game. Obeying the Iron Code and siding with the Owl will lead to the Shura Ending. Break the Iron Code by staying loyal to Lord Kuro and you'll be able to continue through the remaining areas of the game by handing him the materials required to recreate the fountainhead aroma.

Defeating the Great Shinobi – Owl, and completing the fountainhead aroma will allow you to progress both Emma's and the Divine Child's quests, which you'll need to complete before the next raid if you're aiming for the Purification or Return Endings.

To access this area you'll need to have defeated Lady Butterfly in the initial version of the area, and then break the Iron Code during Ashina Castle (Interior Ministry raid) so that you can defeat Great Shinobi - Owl. You can then progress Emma's quest to the point at which she gives you the Father's Bell Charm. This is a high level area with some very difficult encounters, but if you're not going for the Purification ending, then visiting it is completely optional. The Aromatic Flower that is required for that ending can only be obtained by killing Owl (Father) at the end of this area, one of the most difficult boss fights in the entire game. Because of his difficulty, it's recommended that you venture into the other remaining areas first, so that you can gather more Attack Power and Vitality before facing him. Upon arriving here you'll start just outside the estate grounds, and everything before that point in the area is exactly the same as during your first trip into this memory.

As soon as your feet hit the ground in this area, the time of day will advance to Night throughout the game, increasing the strength of enemies in many areas. If you use the Homeward Bone to leave this area before you Commune with the first Idol, you'll need to go to the Wedding Cave in Ashina Depths and interact with the prompt just in front of the destroyed palanquin to be transported back here. Quest progression for many NPCs will be locked as soon as you defeat the Divine Dragon at the end of this area and the second phase of the raid begins, so if you're going for anything other than the Immortal Severance ending, make sure you get the items required before killing the boss here.

# Ashina Castle (Central Forces Raid)

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>34333</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>2866</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>600</td></tr></table>

After defeating the Divine Dragon in the Divine Realm you'll be transported to Kuro's Room in Ashina Castle, where the Central Forces of the Interior Ministry are launching a renewed offensive. Emma will be kneeling nearby; if you speak to her, she'll give you the Secret Passage Key, which opens the door to the secret passage in Ashina Reservoir that Kuro fled through. You can access Ashina Reservoir through the usual building in Ashina Castle, so you can go straight to the ending section of the game if you want to.

All normal routes into and out of Ashina Outskirts have been destroyed during this portion of the raid, even the route out of the Dilapidated Temple. Your only means of accessing that area now is across the newly-repaired bridge at the bottom of the area near the Old Grave Idol.

# Ashina Outskirts (Central Forces raid)

<table><tr><td>Total Skill EXP</td><td>47473</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Kills</td><td>3935</td></tr><tr><td>Total Sen From Pickups</td><td>500</td></tr></table>

As with other areas that have been occupied by the Interior Ministry, you'll no longer have access to any of the Idols in this area other than the Dilapidated Temple until you Commune with them again. That means your only way into the main part of the area is across the reconstructed bridge between Ashina Castle and Ashina Outskirts. The Idol at the Dilapidated Temple is still active and can be used, and although the Sculptor is no longer there, you can still make use of his toolkit to fit and upgrade your tools.

Many parts of this area are blocked off either by barricades or raging fires, and any area that can be reached is now full of Red Guard and other Ministry loyalists. Exploring this area is not required for any of the endings, nor do you need to go through it to access any other area. Outside of one final visit with Anayama the Peddler if you've been following his quest, the only reason to venture into this area is to confront the Demon of Hatred, one of the most fearsome opponents you'll face. It's possible and highly recommended to fully upgrade your Vitality before coming here, and if you choose not to continue to  $\mathrm{NG + }$  after seeing the ending, you can even take advantage of the extra attack power you receive from that fight to aide you against the demon.

Your final stop before completing the game is the very same place that your journey began. Like the other areas that the Ministry has occupied, most of this area is inaccessible due to fire damage, so the only connecting path leads to Ashina Castle. The sole non-boss encounter in this area is where you'll find the final Prayer Bead, which will give you a very handy upgrade just before facing the bosses. After using the Secret Passage Key to open the door, run to the meadow at the end and face off against Genichiro one last time. After defeating him, you'll straight away be plunged into a battle against Isshin, the Sword Saint, so careful item management during the fight with Genichiro is of utmost importance.

# Upgrade Analysis

This section looks at the various Skills and items that you'll be aiming to acquire as the game progresses. We've complied lists to make some key teams easier to track down, and put together recommended unlocking orders for Skills. For similar help with unlocking Prosthetic Tool upgrades, head to the start of the Shinobi Toolkit chapter on P.82.

# Skill Purchasing Order

With an overwhelming amount of skills to choose from, it can be tough to decide what to spend your Skill Points on. To help ease that burden, we've complied a set of recommendations for how to spend your first 60 Skill Points, focused on different playstyles. These lists only cover unlockable Skills in skill trees; Skills collected through progression or purchases should be obtained as soon as you're able to acquire them.

<table><tr><td>Skill Tree Name</td><td>Pts. Req</td></tr><tr><td>Shinobi Arts</td><td>34</td></tr><tr><td>Prosthetic Arts</td><td>31</td></tr><tr><td>Ashina Arts</td><td>18</td></tr><tr><td>Temple Arts</td><td>22</td></tr><tr><td>Mushin Arts</td><td>20</td></tr><tr><td>Total</td><td>125</td></tr></table>

We've also totaled how many Skill Points you need to complete each skill tree, and how many you'd need in total if you want to unlock everything. On an average playthrough you'll acquire roughly 60 Skill Points, and as you can see, you're going to need a lot more than that for everything, making planning ahead crucial. If your goal is to unlock everything, then it's recommended that you do not spend too much time on your first playthrough killing enemies to gain additional EXP—you'd be much better off continuing to New Game +, where you'll be able to accrue Skill Points at a much faster rate. These numbers also show that if you want to unlock the Mushin Arts skill tree as soon as possible, then mastering the Ashina Arts would be the easiest way to accomplish that.

# Treasure Carp Scales

The speedy carp that these scales belong to can be difficult to track down because of how quickly they can swim away. This is compounded by the fact that you likely won't get the Mibu Breathing Technique until later in the game, meaning you'd have to remember all of the locations you spotted them, but were unable to dive down and harvest their shiny scales. Some scales have also been shed by their hosts and can simply be picked up without needing to harvest them from a living carp, but those too are often found beneath the surface. Here we'll provide a handy chart that will tell you every location where you can find these creatures. The nearest Idol location will enable you to quickly travel there so that you can help the Pot Nobles achieve their dreams.

# Enemy Weaknesses

In case you want to do some analysis of your own, you'll find the strengths and weaknesses of every enemy in the game here. They're all lined up in a useful chart, with brief explanations of the various effects and implications.

# LEGEND

- means an enemy is weak to that attack type or tool. In most cases this means more damage, but in others it indicates a special effect, such as making enemies panic when fire is used against them. For these special effects, check the numbers in the legend below.

$\times$  means an enemy is strong against that damage type or attack. You may deal less damage with that damage type or be less likely to apply any special effects or status ailments.

$\div$  means indicates the attack type has no effect on the enemy at all. This means there's no point in attempting to use it on them. For example, in the case of Poison, an means the enemy can never be Poisoned. An empty cell means the enemy has no particular resistance, strong or weak, to the damage type.

# HEADERS

Spirit Emblems drop rates. If you see two drop rates listed, it means the enemy has two separate chances to drop emblems when you kill them, one usually rarer than the other.

Resurrection Power You usually only get a  $30\%$  chance to regain between  $2\%$  to  $7\%$  resurrection power, depending on the enemy you kill. For Strong and Sub-Boss enemies, the chance to regain resurrection power is  $100\%$ .  $30\%$  chances are shown in pink.

# DAMAGE TYPES

Pierce isn't related to dealing damage through an enemy's guard. Instead, it means enemies weak to Pierce take extra damage from attacks that have this property. Examples of these attacks are Whirlwind Slash or Ashina Cross.

Blunt means You deal Blunt damage whenever you attack an enemy without a weapon, such as via the Praying Strikes Combat Art. Because these attacks generally deal low damage anyway, its better to think of Blunt as a primarily Posture damage attack type.

Thrust means the damage dealt by your charged thrust attack, the Loaded Spear, and certain Combat Arts such as Shadowrush. When an enemy is weak to thrust damage, you'll deal much more damage than normal.

Fire means more than just extra damage from fire-based attacks. Many enemies that are

weak to fire are also afraid of it. This means using a fire-based attack near them will cause them to panic, which is noted as a P here.

Burn shows how hard it is to set an enemy on fire When an enemy is listed as no effect, this means you can never apply Burn to them.

Spirit damage has a special effect against Apparitions; it bypasses their natural damage reduction. Not all spirit-based attacks can penetrate the damage resistance of Apparitions; only Divine Confetti, the Projected Force attack of the Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella, and the Lazulite Sacred Flame. You'll find this noted as "Barrier Break".

Poison shows how easy it is to apply Poison to enemies. If an enemy is weak against Poison, you can apply it very quickly. An enemy listed as no effect cannot be Poisoned.

Sabimaru This column indicates whether an enemy is weak to Sabimaru's special blue rust Poison. This bonus effect is only applicable to Okami Warriors and their descendants.

Shuriken Throwing a Shuriken at an enemy weak to it will always cause a Critical hit and deal extra Vitality and Posture damage. This is often enough to break their Posture in one or two attacks.

Firecrackers Enemies weak against Firecrackers will take Posture build-up in addition to the usual stun. This effect is almost always applied to beasts.

Finger Whistle indicates whether an enemy that hears the Finger Whistle goes berserk or not. The berserk effect causes beasts to attack both friend and foe alike.

Malcontent only indicates whether using this tool will stun an enemy.

Spear Drag indicates whether it's possible to drag an enemy towards you with the Loaded Spear's Drag technique. See P.93 for more details on this.

Divine Abduction If an enemy is weak to this tool, there are three different reactions that can happen: most enemies will be turned around and lose sight of you and are temporarily vulnerable to an immediate Backstab Deathblow. This is listed as "Backstab Deathblow". Some Strong enemies and Bosses, will only be turned around. These are listed as "Turn around only". Many enemies in Senpou Temple will simply disappear, killing them instantly. These are marked as "Disappear".

Snap Seeds only work on Illusion-based enemies. Against those enemies, the most frequent effect is to make any enemy weak to a Snap Seed disappear, killing them instantly.

# Sensitive Information

The denizens of Ashina each have their own concerns and desires, and these often conflict with the Wolf's goals. How things play out, and what you'll learn along the way, depends on how you treat those you encounter. This chapter gives you the knowledge you'll need to easily tell friend from foe.

![](images/571824e0e3c8f36a80163d337ed59dc69704997bd70c69b06a5813322d24168d.jpg)

# NPCs and Peddlers

An NPC is any character not controlled by the player, but with whom you can interact. This means all of the other characters in Sekiro's story, and the peddlers and advice-givers you'll encounter along the way. This section covers all of them in detail, revealing every interaction you can have with them and all rewards they may bestow upon you, providing you deal with them in the right way.

# Event Flow Overview

This chart will take you through every critical NPC interaction needed to complete a playthrough using our recommended route and gather all the items needed to achieve any of the game's endings. Entries here are truncated to act more like a summary than those on the individual characters' pages. Note that not all interactions are included here, only the most important ones in each area.

# Central Characters

This section covers the primary characters in Sekiro's story. Every person mentioned here is, in various ways, deeply connected to the land of the Ashina. Many of these characters have complicated and lengthy questlines that will unfold over the course of your journey. Their ultimate fates will vary wildly, depending on your decisions and the order that you make them in. Choose who you call your ally wisely, as the fate of kingdoms and gods will rest in your hands.

# Divine Heir Kuro

Lord Kuro is the last surviving member of the Hirata clan, and the Divine Heir of the Dragon's Heritage, a distinction that gives him the ability to bestow the blessing, or curse, of immortality on whomever he sees fit. This is not an ability that the young lord takes lightly. Despite being sought after by several powerful Lords and organizations, Kuro has only ever seen fit to grant his power once, to his personal shinobi, the Wolf. This is in no small part due to him seeing, first-hand, the corruption it can inspire in the hearts of men, causing even the most iron-willed to resort to violence and betrayal to acquire it. It is for this reason that Kuro ultimately hopes to sever the immortality provided by Dragon's Heritage once and for all, to spare all those around him from its vile allure.

The Wolf's story and Kuro's are inseparably connected. No matter which path you choose to walk, it will be defined by your treatment of and duty to the Divine Heir. Your early journey will be centered around rescuing him from Lord Genichiro. As soon as you've been reunited with him, he'll enlist your help in severing his gift of immortality and begin to guide you in your quest. If a shinobi is ever unsure as to how to proceed, then speaking to their Lord will often set them on the right path.

If you find a Sakura Droplet (P.131) on your travels, Lord Kuro's powers as the Divine Heir will allow him to use it to increase your number of potential Resurrections by one. Once you've defeated your final opponent, you'll need to give Kuro the Divine Dragon's Tears and, if you have them and choose to do so, the Aromatic Flower (P.130) or the Frozen Tears (P.131). Which ending you receive is determined by the items you hand him at this crucial moment.

# Ashina Outskirts  $\text{串}$  Outskirts Wall - Stairway

# Asha In Outskirts Ashina Castle Gate Fortress

# Asha Castle Upper Tower - Kuro's Room

After defeating Genichiro Ashina, head down the staircase to find Kuro. He'll ask you to help him attempt to sever the immortality that the Dragon's Heritage provides. After continuing to obey the Iron Code, he'll give you the Immortal Severance Text before asking you to check the nearby incense burner. Once you've examined it, speak to Kuro again, who will then send you to go meet with Isshin Ashina.

# Asha Castle Upper Tower - Kuro's Room

Once you've spoken to Isshin Ashina about the Mortal Blade and its whereabouts, return to Kuro's Room and you'll find that he has managed to open up a previously closed off archive. When you speak to him, he'll mention discovering a flower needed to sever immortality. Upon asking him about it, you will receive the Fragrant Flower Note and he'll send you to hunt for the Lotus of the Palace.

# Asha Castle Upper Tower - Kuro's Room

If you acquired the Young Master's Bell Charm, you can ask Kuro about it directly. Additionally, he will encourage you to use it at the kind-faced Buddha until you have visited the Hirata Estate.

# Asha Castle Upper Tower-Kuro's Room

Give him the Sakura Droplet to increase your maximum Resurrection Power.

After speaking to Emma about the Everblossom Tree, speak to Kuro again.

# Asha Castle  Ashina Reservoir

Kuro Remnant found upon revisiting the Moon-view Tower where you first met the young lord. Touch it and Kuro will seemingly begin speaking to The Wolf directly about his uncertainty as to why he has these powers, and what to do with them.

# The Sculptor

The Sculptor is a retired shinobi who resides inside the Dilapidated Temple, where he spends his days carving Buddha statues. You'll first meet him after the Wolf loses his arm to Genichiro—the Sculptor drags you from the battlefield back to his temple. The Shinobi Prosthetic you awake with was originally his, made for him personally by the great doctor Dogen. Of all those you'll meet in the Ashina lands, there are few who will speak more plainly with you, especially if you have a drink to offer him. However, his gruff yet helpful exterior belies a hatred that can only ever truly be found in those who have spent their lives killing. His Buddhas carry the face they do for good reason, and he may very well become a boding portent of the Wolf's future.

In addition to being vital to the events unfolding in the story, The Sculptor is also the primary craftsman for your Shinobi Prosthetic. From the beginning, he will be able to fit you with a variety of Shinobi weapons if you are able to bring him the right items. Additionally, once you've acquired the Mechanical Barrel from Gyoubu Oniwa (P.171), you'll be able to further improve the tools you've acquired, so long as you can gather the correct upgrade materials.

# Emma the Physician

Emma is a caring woman that you will meet early in your journey. A genius doctor and the original creator of the Healing Gourd, she is sent by a mysterious benefactor to assist and watch over you on your mission to rescue and assist Lord Kuro. The Wolf's first interaction with Emma is seen before the story has even begun; she's the one who drops the Ornamental Letter into the cavern where he lies broken. However, you'll first meet Emma properly after you've reached your first Sculptor's Idol and returned to the Dilapidated Temple. From beginning to end, you'll not find a more capable or loyal ally to both you and the Divine Heir. Her extensive knowledge of the human body as well as the history of the Ashina lands will be essential to seeing your journey through to its end. Should you cross her, however, it will quickly become apparent that she is highly capable in battle. While medicine may be her chosen profession, the reasons she knows the craft so well can be traced to more than simple circumstance.

As the Ashina Castle's resident physician, Emma's exceptional skills are often at your disposal. The most common task she'll perform for you is using Gourd Seeds (P.140) to expand the capacity of your Healing Gourd, but this is far from her only ability. If the people of Ashina begin to suffer from Dragonrot, she will be able to find a way to fight back the illness, so long as you are willing to assist her. See the entry for Dragonrot on P.14 for more details on this. You will also require her assistance in order to attain the Purification ending. Lastly, if you find yourself with a moment to spare, offering her a drink can be one of the best ways to get her to open up about herself and her relationships with some of the most important figures in the land.

![](images/7325e3ce74c555bf06aa466cd62a7b8abc8b016e6ce3a750fa778cd79a8ad790.jpg)

# Isshin Ashina

![](images/7db626efd2b3b3c0af8c431fde776987996f20201d79b5d4beb55d0e34d75825.jpg)

Lord Isshina Ashina is the aging ruler of the Ashina clan and adoptive grandfather of Lord Genichiro Ashina. In his prime, he was one of the greatest warriors to ever grace the battlefield, while he led his forces to liberate the land of the Ashina from the Interior Ministry. His skill was such that his mere existence seems to be enough to keep the Ministry at bay. However, as the Lord's health wanes, the enemies of the clan have begun to close in again, probing it for weakness. Despite being well past his prime, Isshin still remains one of the most powerful swordsmen in the land.

You'll first meet Lord Isshin in his watchtower after you've rescued Kuro and spoken to The Tenu of Ashina, where he'll provide information on the location of the Mortal Blade. His health leaves him largely unable to assist you, but you will meet few better drinking partners on your travels. His age and experience as the ruler of the land makes him a treasure trove of information on the history of the Ashina, so long as you can provide him with a good reason to keep talking. Nonetheless, it's apparent to all that the Ashina clan is safe so long as Lord Isshin draws breath.

# Dojun

Dojun is the ruthless surgeon of the Ashina and student of the master surgeon Dosaku. You'll find him in the Abandoned Dungeon, on the hunt for specimens to experiment on, as he pursues his research on how to craft medicine with the rejuvenating water. If you agree to assist him, he'll give you the Surgeon's Bloodstained Letter, which will instruct you to lure a tough man to the dungeon. This can be either Kotaro (P.558) or Jinzaemon Kumano (P.571). Of the two, Jinzaemon is typically the wiser choice, as Kotaro can be valuable to other quests. Rest, then return to eavesdrop on him as he talks to Master Dosaku inside his cell, then rest again. Speak to him once more and he'll give you the Surgeon's Stained Letter, which will instruct you to acquire the Red Carp Eyes (P.132).

Once you've acquired the Red Carp Eyes, return them to Dojun to receive two Lumps of Grave Wax. With those handed over, rest and return to eavesdrop on the doctor inside his cell, then rest again. Now you'll need to speak to Dojun inside the cell, with his victim seemingly nowhere to be found. The victim can be found on a small shore in the middle of the Underground Waterway, consumed completely by the effects of the Red-Eyes. Putting them out of their misery will yield a Red Lump. You'll be able to reach Dojun himself by swimming through an underwater cave leading to the other side of the bars. Rest one last time. When you arise this time, Dojun will have moved to the same shore as his victim and become similarly afflicted with Red-Eyes. Defeat him to receive the Academics' Red Lump, bringing the quest to an end.

# Divine Child of Rejuvenation

Some time ago, the priests of the Senpou Temple attempted to use kidnapped children to create a false Divine Heir in their pursuit of achieving immortality. Of the children they experimented on, the Divine Child of Rejuvenation was the only one to succeed and survive. You will first meet her in your hunt for the Mortal Blade, and she'll warn you of its lethal effects on those who would attempt to wield it. Once The Wolf rises from the dead after unsheathing the blade, she seems to understand who he is, and his relationship with the true Divine Heir. Once you speak to her, she will decide to assist you in your quest by providing you with Rice as often as the harvest allows.

From that point forward, you'll be able to receive one Rice from the Divine Child when you return to the area, provided you've consumed the previous Rice. This will continue until you have received and consumed three Rice from her, at which point she will fall ill due to lack of blood. To counter this, you'll need to provide her with a Persimmon (P.117). Doing this at least once is required for completion of her quest, as it will yield the Rice for Kuro, but she will continue to fall ill for every three Rice you consume for the rest of your journey, requiring another Persimmon to bring her back to health each time. The Rice for Kuro must be given to the young lord before defeating the Divine Dragon, or you will be unable to complete the quest. Additionally, the Divine Child's nature as a false Divine Heir also grants her the ability to use a Sakura Droplet (P.131) to increase your maximum Resurrection Potential, if you happen to find one.

If you've obtained the Sweet Rice Ball made by Kuro and given the Holy Chapters: Infested to the Divine Child, the next time you return for Rice you'll find that she has moved to the Illusive Hall to speak with the divine children of the rejuvenating water in an attempt to choose what to do. When you speak to her, she will request that you speak to the head priest in the nearby cave. Unfortunately, it seems the priest has long since passed away, but he still holds the Holy Chapters: Dragon's Return (P.137) in his skeletal fingers. After you travel back, she will have returned to the main temple. Hand over the text and she will direct you to locate two persimmons of the serpent, so that she may become the cradle to carry the Dragon's Heritage back to where it came.

The items she requires are the Dried Serpent Viscera and the Fresh Serpent Viscera (P.131). Having collected both, return to the Child and give them to her. She'll ask you to leave to spare you from seeing her do what needs to be done. When you return, however, you will be able to eavesdrop on her and hear her struggling to devour the flesh. Return one more time after lighting the incense that allows you to enter Fountainhead Palace to find the doors opened. The Divine Child, now blinded but able to act as the cradle, will reward you with the Frozen Tears which will allow you to achieve the Return ending. In addition, her Rice will be replaced by the more potent Fine Snow.

![](images/2af4f048b5b7a47bec0fc05591e78d1a8d73a125591923fa071842ece7bbd3d4.jpg)

# $\bullet$  Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo  $\bullet$  Inner Sanctum

After receiving the Sweet Rice Ball made with the Rice for Kuro, speak to the Divine Child again.

# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

Once you've spoken to her about the Sweet Rice Ball and consumed your most recent Rice, you'll find her praying to the shrine. Greet her and give her the Holy Chapter: Infested (P.137).

![](images/2e751d5ab8eb5b1a5e49728c3bb4192a547a024e3dff19504bc0c728521a1307.jpg)  
Even immortals require sleep.

# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

Once you have told her about the Sweet Rice Ball and handed over the Holy Chapters: Infested, she'll move to the Hall of Illusions. Use the beam of light in the Sanctum to travel there and speak with her. She'll direct you to a cave near the Main Hall where you can find the Holy Chapters: Dragon Returns.

# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

When you return with the Holy Chapters: Dragon Returns, she will have moved back to her typical position. Speak to her and she will ask you to find the Fresh Serpent Viscera and the Dried Serpent Viscera.

# $\bullet$  Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo  $\bullet$  Inner Sanctum

After acquiring both Serpent Viscera, return to her and hand them over. She will then ask you to leave.

# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

After you've handed over the two Serpent Viscera, rest and return to find the doors to the main building closed, and they'll remain shut until you burn the incense that allows you to travel to Fountainhead Palace.

# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

Once the doors have closed, eavesdrop on the Divine Child inside to progress the quest.

# Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo 9 Inner Sanctum

After eavesdropping on her when the doors are shut, and burning the incense that grants access to Fountainhead Palace, the building will open once again. Speak to her and she'll bestow the Frozen Tear unto you, concluding her quest-line.

Additionally, her harvests of Rice will be permanently replaced with the more potent Fine Snow.

![](images/a4a1de7935bad56aaeacd7886a407719d1673c4bec4d53674c143f616eb9fcb8.jpg)  
The Divine Child's mysterious aura belies a youthful personality.

# Ukonzaemon Usui (The Owl)

The Great Shinobi, Owl, is one of the Lord Isshin's greatest warriors, as well as the adoptive father of the Wolf, though whether the Owl sees him truly as his own child is known only to him. A strict adherent of the Iron Code that puts father first and master second above all else in the world, he demands absolute loyalty and obedience from his son. His massive frame and imposing aura give the impression of a powerful and stoic man, but the Owl is just as capable of committing devastating acts of cowardice as anyone else. His Iron Code has its worth, but there may come a time where it has to be set aside in order to do what is right. Should you choose to align with him, you will receive the Shura ending.

![](images/ea069bbad3b41d3b1c68a3138d8142e958b09a08d136b7591a8a9bda7ac953e9.jpg)  
The Owl was last seen at the Hirata Estate. How he survived is known only to memory.

# Kotaro

Kotaro is a gentle, but naive Taro Troop You'll find him crying under a tree at the base of Mt. Kongo, seemingly abandoned by his family. When you first ask him why he cries, he will not answer directly but instead tell you that he needs a 'pure white flower'. No matter where you look, there is no flower matching that description on Mt. Kongo. There is, however, a White Pinwheel (P.232) and a Red & White Pinwheel. Giving him the former will cause him to regain his memories, revealing that he's actually one of the caretakers of the divine children of the rejuvenating water. Where they are or how he got here, he still does not remember. In his panic, he begs you to use your shinobi powers to spirit him away to where they are. This can be done by using the Divine Abduction tool on him, sending him away in a frantic whirlwind. You'll finally find him in the Hall of Illusions after defeating the Folding Screen Monkeys, tending to the divine children. For helping him, he'll reward you with a Taro Persimmon and, though you may not be able to see the children yourself, Kotaro seems genuinely happy.

Alternatively, you can give Kotaro the Red & White Pinwheel. He will be disappointed that it's not what he was looking for, but will thank you for trying and begin to trust you. This will allow you to tell him where to go and, depending on where you're at in their respective questlines, you can choose to send him to either Dojun (P.552) or Ayanama the Peddler (P.561). Doing this will lead to other regards, but will eliminate the chance to see the ending to his personal quest. On your first playthrough, it's recommended that you send him to Ayanama, as doing so will give you access to many rare upgrade materials and eventually reward you with the Promissory Note, giving you a permanent  $10\%$  discount from all peddlers. Note that you can give the Red & White Pinwheel to Kotaro and then give him the White Pinwheel if you so choose, but giving him the White Pinwheel first will lead only to the Hall of Illusions ending for his story.

![](images/c1498ebf4f11ab592686de95ddbb4cb73464cd4a436200f5b1d7e1d869a242a4.jpg)

# Peddlers

While scouring the land and snatching goods from the bodies of dead soldiers will provide you with the bulk of what you need to survive in the Ashina territories, there will inevitably come a time when you'll find yourself in need of a unique item or a reliable supply of a precious item. In those times, turning to a peddler will be your best option. The overwhelming majority of merchants accept Sen as their primary form of currency, but the two shops with perhaps the rarest goods of all trade purely in Treasure Carp Scales. Additionally, once you acquire the Dragon's Tally Board, every merchants that deals in Sen will permanently expand their inventory with an unlimited supply of several essential items, such as Divine Confetti and Scrap Iron. If any of the merchants that deal in Sen die or otherwise become unreachable, you'll be able to purchase their unique items at the Offering Box at the Dilapidated Temple, though their common items will be lost forever.

# Memorial Mobs

The Memorial Mobs appear wherever death is widespread, supposedly to sell offerings to the recently deceased. Whether or not they're earnest in their stated goal or merely using it as a cover to loot the bodies of the dead is known only to them. Each each has their own personality, but they are all united under the same banner. The goods they have on offer range from standard fare, such as Pellets and Antidote Powder, up to rarities like Prayer Beads and Gourd Seeds. Every Memorial Mob has something unique and valuable to offer, so always pay them a visit when you discover a new one. If you continue on to New Game+, be sure to purchase as many of their unique items any you can manage before starting your second journey.

# Matabei Anayama the Peddler

Anayama is a former thief turned industrious merchant, having barely managed to survive the attack on the Hirata Estate. You will most likely first find him down on his luck in Ashina Outskirts near the Outskirts Wall – Stairway idol. As you talk to him, he'll recognize you from that fateful night, though The Wolf remembers neither him nor the raid on Kuro's home. Ayanama will happily help you remember, for a fee. After paying him 50 Sen, he'll tell you that he saw you while he was part of the raiding party that broke in and started the fire while most the estate's defenders were away at battle. If you find the Young Master's Bell Charm (P.131), you can experience this encounter first-hand by finding him in front of a shrine on the Estate Path (P.177). Once you've made the initial purchase and rested, he will begin to sell basic items as well as information on where to find the Flame Barrel.

After speaking to him again, he'll ask you to help him find out what the Samurai at Ashina Castle are looking for. To fulfill his request, you must eavesdrop on a Samurai General near the Old Grave (P.208). The army is running low on salt and, as it turns out, Ayanama knows how to acquire some. When you return again, you'll find that the windfall granted to him by his dealing with the castle have allowed him to expand his inventory with an unlimited supply of Black Gunpowder and Scrap Iron.

Next, he'll ask you to find him someone big and strong to help him scour battlefields for more goods. Kotaro matches this description perfectly, and he'll listen to your suggestion if you give him the Red & White Pinwheel. Once they've met, the Taro Troop will help further expand Ayanama's stores. However, the pair will disappear during the Central Forces raid on Ashina Castle. If you go to the opposite side of the building under which they usually reside, you'll find Ayanama next to a deceased Kotaro, though the peddler will claim he's just sleeping. To make matters worse, Ayanama has been stripped of his goods and wealth by the Ministry. The only thing he has left to his name is the Promissory Note, which he will sell to you for 1 Sen. With that single Sen, he says will earn back all his wealth and more, before passing away himself.

# Pot Nobles

The Pot Nobles are two separate, yet equally mysterious creatures that live within clay pots near bodies of water associated with the Divine Dragon. The first Noble you'll encounter is floating near the mouth of the Hirata Estate's Dragonspring river. You'll encounter the second Noble in the Fountainhead Palace, past the Flower Viewing Stage Idol. To find him, grapple up to the top section of the bridge closest to the gates of the palace, and swing into the nearby cave then drop down to the ground at its end. Each of the Nobles seems to have a masked disdain for the other, though they ultimately have the same goal. The only part of their body you can ever hope to see is a single, discolored emaciated arm emerging from the pot. However, the most curious thing about them is their eagerness to exchange Treasure Carp Scales for incredibly rare goods such as Lapis Lazuli and pieces of the Dancing Dragon Mask.

As you approach the end of your journey, you'll likely be forced to choose between the two in order to acquire a Truly Precious Bait to take care of the Giant Colored Carp. Regardless of which Noble's bait you opt to use, they will leave behind a single Lapis Lazuli near their pot as they dive into the nearest body of water. The one you didn't choose, however, will permanently disappear, leaving their inventory with their rival, as well as the container they had previously called home.

As merchants, they carry some of the rarest and unique items you'll find. There are only 40 Treasure Carp Scales, many of which are hard to come by. As such, choosing how to spend them wisely is essential. Between the two of them, the most valuable goods they carry are the Withered Red Gourd, Floating Passage Text, and perhaps most of all the two Lapis Lazulis. The Mask Fragments, while valuable, have minimal use until New Game+. However, if you take the time to hunt down every scale, you'll be able to clear out the majority of their offerings.

# Fujioka the Info Broker

Fujioka is a merchant who finds his way to the Dilapidated Temple after you've defeated Genichiro. Of all the people you'll meet at the temple, the Info Broker is easily the most self-interested. There is little he will do for you if you lack coin. However, that does not mean he's without his uses. Having a merchant at the Temple is a great convenience, especially since he carries a Gourd Seed. Additionally, once you've acquired the Dragon's Tally Board, his close proximity to the Sculptor can make upgrading lower level Prosthetic Tools a much simpler task.

# Blackhat Badger

The Blackhat Badger was once one of the many assassins serving the Senpou Temple, but left the organization behind once his gruesome errands became too much to bare. You will first find him in the house directly below the Old Grave Idol, trying to scrape together some cash to survive by selling rare goods from the temple. Once you have purchased the Iron Fortress and spoken with Isshin Ashina, he'll have acquired enough money to fund his journey and vanish once you have acquired the Mortal Blade. In an unexpected turn, however, the Badger was gathering the money for the sake of visiting the grave of his son Tenkichi in the Sunken Valley Cavern. He will remain there until the Central Forces raid Ashina Castle, where you'll find him underneath a tree near the Old Grave, fatally wounded after having saved a child from the clutches of the Ministry's forces. Speak to him and he'll give you the Mibu Pilgrimage Balloon as a parting gift to conclude his quest, before finally being reunited with Tenkichi.

# Miscellaneous

The characters in this section all have a smaller roles and shorter quests in comparison to the primary cast, but are often just as important to your progression. Some of these characters have full stories of their own, while others will pass away as soon as you speak to them, but all of them have something to offer. Due to their smaller roles, they are often quite easily missed. You'll have to scour the lands and be attentive and diligent if you hope to meet all of them and learn the complete story of the Ashina clan.

# Hanbei the Undying

Hanbei is an infested warrior, and will be your primary sparring partner while you learn the essentials of swordplay. When you first meet him, he will challenge you to a duel. Defeating him is a simple matter, and fortunately, Hanbei is kind enough to train you after you have dispatched him once. You will not be able to kill him, no matter what you do. For The Wolf, this has some real benefits: there is no better partner in the land for safely testing your abilities, especially deflecting, Mikiri Counters, Combat Arts. For Hanbei however, this is a curse he desperately wishes to escape. If you return to him with the Mortal Blade equipped, he'll immediately take notice of the weapon and will ask you to cut him down once you confirm its ability to sever immortality. Should you agree, you'll find him waiting for your blade after you rest. After tearing out the worm inside him, you will finally be able to grant him the death he longs for.

# Inosuke & Mother Nogami

Inosuke is a blinded vassal of the Hirata Estate whom you'll meet early on as you travel through the Ashina Outskirts. When you first speak to him, he'll ask you to check on his mother, the Mother Nogami She resides on the second story of the nearby burnt-out house, making it impossible for him to reach her, but it's a simple matter for The Wolf. The Lady's mind has gone when you find her, and she'll mistake you for her son no matter what you say to her. Under that delusion, she gives you the Young Master's Bell Charm and asks that you offer it to the Buddha. This can be used at the Kind-faced Buddha in the Dilapidated Temple to return to the night the Hirata Estate was destroyed. As you enter the Hirata Audience Chamber, you'll also find Inosuke again, freshly wounded by Lady Butterfly. Speaking to him here, he will warn you of Lady Butterfly's illusions and give you a Snap Seed to help fend them off. After making use of the Bell Charm, return to Inosuke in the Ashina Outskirts once the Interior Ministry raids Ashina Castle to find that Inosuke's mother has passed away. You can then speak with Inosuke nearby to hear his own final words before leaving to join his mother.

![](images/c9335042e5a0fd01734fb6fad883a81ab7fc9094ce7af0dd7eb3130bbe86d763.jpg)

![](images/af8c92e0dcea608391842ded89796455fae28cfe6c4c96a1fbea5847ab5e87be.jpg)  
You'll encounter this pair early in the game in Ashina Outskirts.

# Retired Swordsman - Nogami Gensai

Nogami Gensai is a retired swordsman formerly employed by Lord Isshin. Though he may have planned to sheath his blade, the warrior is unable to stand by while the young Lord Kuro is under attack. Once you speak to him, he will charge forward to attack, joining you in battle with Juzou the Drunkard. While the aged samurai is a capable fighter, he will find himself overwhelmed by the foes' sheer numbers if not given assistance. Should he survive, he will lament that his tired, old body is spent and that you will have to go ahead alone.

# The Tengu of Ashina

The Tenu of Ashina is an incredibly fearsome, yet oddly familiar swordsman with an aptitude for dispatching Lone Shadow warriors on his own. This warrior is something to be feared, leaving only bodies of powerful foes in his wake. When you first encounter him, he will presume that you are an enemy and threaten to kill you. When you fail to give him a name to call you, the Tenu is left to deduce that you are a shinobi. In lieu of a proper title for The Wolf, he dubs him Sekiro, the one-armed wolf. Once you've hunted at least one of the nearby assassins that he calls "Rats", he will reward you with the Ashina Esoteric Text. Once you have the text, you'll find him next at the Great Serpent Shrine, again surrounded by bodies. If you've purchased the final Skill any of the skill trees, the Tenu will recognize your skill and reward you with the Mushin Esoteric Text, before giving out a sickly cough. After you rest again, he will seemingly disappear completely.

![](images/155c32e5603221dc7c23246db6a435e41c25424f42ab61c7030a7f54c8490fee.jpg)  
The Tengu's combat prowess is something to be feared.

# Shura Storyteller

You will find this Shura Storyteller hiding in a small hallway behind The Tengu of Ashina. While she will not stand in direct opposition to you, she does little to mask her disdain for not just you, but all those who spill blood in the name of hatred and war. She warns that, should things continue as they have, it will only be a matter of time before a demon rises to lay waste to all who tarnish this land. In time, a demon does in fact appear, and it seems that only she is fully aware of its true identity.

# Faithful Ones

When you first encounter her, the Faithful One appears to be nearly deranged, spewing ramblings with seemingly little rhyme or reason to them. However, this belies her true nature. Once you have learned more of the Ashina territories, you may find that many of her statements are not only surprisingly coherent, but strangely deliberate. You will first meet her on the bridge leading into Ashina Castle and, if you speak to her, she will attempt to direct you towards Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo. Additionally, if you use an item that causes you to assume a praying pose near her, she'll reward your piety with

![](images/3aa62fce22222d132a88fb9f49f376afabd35a76dd70dd7b110cf4e63fbe7e29.jpg)  
Praying for the safety of the Divine Child.

![](images/3be74dc53df0e0b6219a09b0bcf7b70d030a1e5160a646c49b03783882d043ab.jpg)

items as well as information of the Divine Child of Rejuvenation. After this, you'll find her on the ledge near the giant tree at the Senpou Temple, and encountering her, she can be found overlooking the Bodhisattva Valley.

Each time she will attempt to guide you to the nearest Serpent Viscera and will give you additional advice on how to acquire the organs if you're able to provide her with Rice. After you have provided the Divine Child with the Dried Serpent Viscera and Fresh Serpent Viscera, she will appear to the right of the door leading to the Inner Sanctum. The frail woman will thank you for helping the Divine Child and pray for her safety in her coming journey to the west before quietly passing away. There is a second Faithful One, separate from the one that assists the Divine Child. She can be found overlooking the Bottomless Hole, where she'll encourage you to take a leap of faith into the abyss below.

# Jinzaemon Kumano - The Bewitched Samurai

Jinzaemon Kumano is a patrolling Ashina samurai whom you'll meet at the Ashina Reservoir, peering down into the cave you began the game in, listening to an enchanting sound that only he can hear. After you have greeted him, he'll formally introduce himself and ask you if you have heard the sound of a shamisen. If you have talked to Dojun and agreed to help him in his research, you can lure him to the Abandoned Dungeon, where he will end up as Dojun's victim. However, if you choose not do this by the time you defeat the Guardian Ape Couple, you'll find him as you enter the Hidden Forest in the Ashina Depths, in pursuit of the ghostly shamisen he hears. Finally, you'll meet him at the Water Mill, thoroughly enamored by the phantom shamisen's melody. If you continue ahead and round the corner, you will finally see the musician responsible: O'Rin of the Water. Regardless of whether or not you speak to her, she will attack you for your apparent apathy to her suffering. Once she's been defeated, return to Jinzaemon and he will tell you that the shamisen player spoke to him in her moment of release, before gifting you Jinza's Jizo Statue and passing away himself.

# Green Robed Infested

If you find yourself in the main hall of the Senpou Temple before learning of the Mortal Blade, you'll find this priest resting in front of a massive Buddha, wracked with guilt over the fate of the Children of the Rejuvenating Water. If you've spoken to the Faithful One on the bridge at Ashina Castle, then you can ask him about the 'special holy person'. If you do so, he will tell you the fate of the only surviving child of the temple's terrible experiments. As one final attempt to atone for his actions, he will give you the Holy Chapter: Infested to deliver to the Divine Child, if you ever meet her. With only one survivor left, who has been locked away alone, there is little left for him to do but lament the fate of himself, the child, and the temple.

He is still clearly not ignorant, however, as he is able to deduce your relationship with the Divine Heir by smell alone. The priest warns you that, though the Divine Heir may be exalted, a man is still just a man and that you'd do well to find Kuro soon, lest you risk losing him. The statement seems to come from experience. Once you have discovered the existence of the Mortal Blade from Lord Isshin, the priest will vanish, but not before seemingly placing the Illusive Hall Bell on the table in front of the Buddha. If you did not speak to him before speaking to Lord Isshin, you can still find the Holy Chapter: Infested at the bottom of the pond near the Temple Grounds Idol.

![](images/26c3b2b681a2e012ed0545849692a5165f652367c7e6a406c7183d12d0abebb8.jpg)

# Basket Wearer Shosuke

Shosuke is a cowardly, yet kind villager attempting to hide from the other residents of the village while resisting the allure of the village's water. As you talk to him, he will tell you of the history of the village, the villager Inuhiko across the pond who used the Pine Resin Ember to ward off the other villagers, and the Mibu Village Head Priest who was plying the town with sake in order to get them to drink the Fountainhead water. However, if you return after you've acquired the Pine Resin Ember, you will find him having been seduced by the water and left mad as a result, leaving you no choice but to put an end to his suffering.

# Mibu Village Head Priest

The head priest of Mibu Village, he gorges himself on the water of the Fountainhead Palace inside the shrine beyond the Water Mill. To enter the house, you will need to sneak under the floorboards to find a shinobi shortcut door on the floor. Once inside, you will find this deranged madman in the corner, feverishly trying to devour the few drops of the Fountainhead water he has. If you give him the Water of the Palace, he will reward you with a bottle of Dragonspring Sake. After you rest and return, the priest will have turned into a Mist Noble that drops five Treasure Scales upon its death.

# Master's Chamberlain

The Master's Chamberlain is the gentle giant with the eternal responsibility of feeding and protecting the Great Colored Carp, as well as having two daughters, the Old Palace Maids, whom you may encounter. When you first speak to him at the Feeding Grounds, he will direct you to use the feeding bell at the end of the dock. Ringing it will summon the Great Colored Carp, which you can then feed either a Precious Bait (P.132) to receive Treasure Carp Scales, or a Truly Precious Bait (P.132), which you can get from either of the Pot Nobles, to poison the creature. If you do the latter, you'll find the Chamberlain looking over the water in an effort to spot his master. You can put an end to his search by giving him the Great White Whiskers (P.132). Upon receiving them he will act surprisingly grateful, seemingly relieved that his eternal duty has finally come to an end. Once you have rested one more time, you can return to find him having passed away with one of his daughters crying by his remains.

# Old Palace Maids

You'll meet the first of the two Chamberlain's daughters in the Mibu Manor, adorned with a red sash. When you speak to her, she'll ask you to kill the Great Colored Carp to free her father. Once you defeat the Okami Leader Shizu, you'll be able to enter the Fountainhead Palace's lake, where you can find his second daughter, clad in a white sash, standing on the roof of one of the submerged buildings near the Great Colored Carp's den. As you approach her, she'll call out to ask you a small favor: that if you find yourself inside the palace itself, open the doors so that she may complete an errand. You can fulfill this request by opening the front doors of the building next to the Palace Grounds idol. Once you've done this, however, the next time you return to the building you'll encounter a grizzly sight, as the white-sashed daughter repeatedly drives a knife into the final Palace Noble inside, decrying them all for having taken her father away, before collapsing over it's body. You will meet the remaining daughter again after giving the Great White Whisker to the Noble Caretaker. After you do this, she'll appear at the Feeding Grounds, next to her father's body, where she will mournfully lament the terrible fate that befell her family before falling silent once and for all.

# Hirata Estate Residents

The Hirata Estate isn't home to Kuro alone. While bandits raid the estate, many of those who aren't fit to fight take refuge in a collection of small cottages along the right side of the Estate Path. As you approach the gate they hide behind, you'll see a pair of Soldiers that you can eavesdrop on as they attempt to break in. Dispose of them and climb over the gate to find three small buildings, each with an open window on their exterior. Approaching the window closest to the gate will allow you to speak with a woman who recognizes you as the Divine Heir's shinobi and gives you two Antidote Powders to aid you in rescuing the young lord. The next building will allow you to eavesdrop on a doctor tending to a fighter who's been bested by a nearby Shinobi Hunter. Lastly, the building furthest from the gate has a man who recognizes you, but greets you with suspicion. The timing of the bandit's assault was too convenient, and he suspects that they knew when the estate would be vulnerable. In lieu of a better suspect, he opts to blame the shinobi who only appeared after the attack began.

# Dying Sunken Valley Clan

After you have defeated the Guardian Ape, you will encounter a fatally wounded member of the Sunken Valley Clan as you make your way through the Ashina Depths. This warrior tells you with their dying breathe that they were mangled by a large ape. The path of leading further down is slick with their blood, leading to their killer.

# Illusory Hall Monk

A solitary monk who lives within the Hall of Illusion to avoid being disturbed on his journey to enlightenment. When you first meet him, he will offer you advice on how to deal with three of the Fold-

![](images/14ce1127f4b696b356df280e87947681a4cae7fe8ea682d79e8990c2c567b293.jpg)

ing Screen Monkeys. Once they have been dispatched, however, he will politely but firmly tell you to leave, so that he may continue to focus on his pursuit of inner peace.

# Interactions

Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Main Hall

Speak to him in the Halls of Illusion to receive advice on how to handle three of the four Folding Screen Monkeys.

Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

If you return to the Halls of Illusion after defeating the Folding Screen Monkeys, and speak to him, he will politely, yet firmly tell you to leave.

Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Inner Sanctum

If you used Divine Abduction on Kotaro to transport him to the Halls of Illusion, he'll ask that you leave him and Kotaro alone when you speak to him.

# Forest of Mist Temple Master

An emaciated Buddhist Monk whom you'll meet in the Hidden Forest. Upon speaking to him, he will implore you to dispose of the creature creating the fog in the area. You can find this person by

![](images/90eeeaec11a7dcf82108a5c944c87c691b179b588f74e5c4b2bcbad7f9fea909.jpg)

entering a gap in the second floor of the area's only structure. Once the Mist Noble has been disposed of, the monk will thank you for your deed, but offer no reward.

# Interactions

Ashina Depths Hidden Forrest

Speak to him and he'll tell you where to find the Mist Noble causing the fog in the forest.

![](images/1a1c64ee0fbc0e168a5c7bed8abbffec96027941e360cec5a1fbca6d3273b6f5.jpg)

Ashina Depths Hidden Forrest

After you've killed the Mist Noble, speak to him and he'll thank you for disposing of it.

# Wounded Ashina Soldiers

It does not take long for the Ashina Soldiers to become overwhelmed once the Central Forces raid Ashina Castle. If you traverse the battlefield, you'll occasionally come across those who have fallen in combat but have yet to pass on. Speaking to them will

![](images/fc4c7da311a307802d98ccf73f8938216edac67e20fa7289b4c1d8a3a27313eb.jpg)

reveal that the Interior Ministry forces emerged from the Serpent Valley and quickly overwhelmed both the Ashina Castle and Outskirts, leaving the army decimated.

# Interactions

Asha Castle (Central Forces raid) Ashina Castle

A wounded Ashina Soldier lying next to the castle gate will ask you to aid those in the Ashina Outskirts.

Ashina Castle (Central Forces raid) Old Grave

There is a wounded Soldier on the bridge leading to the Ashina Outskirts that will warn you about the Central Forces stronghold on the other side.

# World Gods

The Ashina Kingdom is home to more than just mortals. In your travels, you will encounter a handful of massive, immortal creatures who will block your path. There will be little you can

# Great Serpent

The Great Serpent is the god of the land, worshiped directly by the denizens of the Sunken Valley. You will first encounter this creature as you make your way through the Underbridge Valley, where you will have to avoid being hunted by it. After that, you will encounter it near the Gun Fort (P.257) and at the base of the Bodhisattva Valley (P.267). In order to complete the Divine Child of Rejuvenation's questline, you will need complete all the interactions with the Great Serpent to acquire the Fresh Serpent Viscera and the Dried Serpent Viscera.

Quest Items  

<table><tr><td>Item</td><td>Requirements</td></tr><tr><td>Fresh Serpent Viscera ▲P.131</td><td>Perform a plunging deathblow on the Great Serpent from the Sunken Valley Cavern idol.</td></tr></table>

do about these beings when you first encounter them, but just because you can't face them in direct combat does not mean that you can't harm them in other ways.

# Interactions

Asha In Outskirts Underbridge Valley

Hunts you as you traverse the valley. See P.167 for more details.

Sunken Valley Passage Gun Fort

Will attack you as you cross the rope bridge, and will then hunt you as swim through the water below. Seem P.257 for more details

Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Sunken Valley Cavern

Once you have encountered the Great Serpent after exiting the Gun Fort, travel to this Idol. Go through the cave and you'll emerge above the Great Serpent; walk out onto the narrow beam at the end and jump off the beam towards the creature. During the fall you'll be able to perform a Plunging Deathblow on it, after which you'll receive the Fresh Serpent Viscera for your troubles. See P.259 for more details.

Sunken Valley Passage Bodhisattva Valley

Another Serpent guards the shrine housing the Dried Serpent Viscera; use the Puppeteer on the nearby Valley Monkey to distract the serpent and gain access to the area containing the viscera. See P.267 for more details.

# Great Colored Carp

The Great Colored Carp is an immortal god living in the Fountainhead Palace lake. The carp typically dwells in the underwater cave leading to the Palace Grounds Idol, but you can summon it for feeding at any time by ringing the bell at the Feeding Grounds. If you enter the cave while the carp is present, it will attack you as soon as it registers your presence, unless you've previously fed it some Precious Bait. The only way to kill it is to feed it a Truly Precious Bait, which can be acquired by spending a certain amount of Treasure Carp Scales at the Pot Noble's shop and talking to them. Once you've done this, the Carp's corpse will appear in the Guardian Ape's Watering Hole, allowing you to pluck the Great White Whiskers from his mouth.

Fountainhead Palace Feeding Grounds

# Eavesdropping Opportunities

As you stealthily make your way across the Ashina territories, there will be times where you will be able to catch people unaware and hear things they didn't intend for you to know. These eavesdrop opportunities will give you chance to learn many pieces of valuable information, from useful ways to counter enemies, pieces of valuable history and lore, and warnings of the dangers to come. Eavesdropping on allies is often a simple matter of hid

ing in a specific spot just out of their sight, but listening in on enemies can be more difficult as you will be unable to do so once they have been alerted to your presence. Fortunately, you have many options available to approach them. Swinging up to a tree or employing the use of a Gachiin's Sugar can often allow you to safely close the gap and hear what your foes have to say.

# Achievements/Trophies

This section will make it as easy as possible to unlock every last Achievement or Trophy. Some of them you'll come by naturally while playing, while others will require a truly dedicated effort to acquire. You'll be able to unlock the vast majority of them by completing a single New Game+ playthrough, especially if you follow the suggested Quest Flow on P.531. However, due to the nature of the story's multiple endings, you'll need to complete the game at least four times to earn them all. Beware that this entire section is, by necessity, laden with spoilers.

![](images/40bd2bfdeb9e2dedaf750eab6a30b9125eaa5c3286bd4db9828cbebc9b2e46ad.jpg)

# Progression

Each of these Trophies/Achievements will be acquired naturally over the course of the game; by the time you reach the game's end, the majority of them will be yours. There are, however, some choices you can make that lead to their own separate endings. This means that in order to acquire all of them, you'll have to complete the story in every way possible.

![](images/ed698b83f05b0993e24bc30c7c79ad69e2a5437cda6bee3bca03e09cf615d6f4.jpg)

These are unlocked by finding the Ashina territories' most elusive denizens and, if need be, defeating them. Some of the most powerful foes you'll encounter are listed below, and it's possible to miss them if you don't stay attentive.

The mysterious Lady Butterfly can be found in the depths of the Hirata Estate. Defeat Lady Butterfly to earn this Trophy/Achievement (P.438).

# Great Serpent

![](images/201e5ea2252b6cc1be19e702002d02ca2d56c91f794392ce046607d1bc9ab526.jpg)

Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo

Sunken Valley Cavern

P.577

Defeated the "Great Serpent".

Seeing off the Great Serpent once and for all is a complicated process. First you'll need to acquire the Puppeteer Ninjutsu from the Folding Screen Monkeys, and then return to the Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo Idol. Once there, follow the steps here to get the job done.

![](images/962e10f5172e5c41ae9eff54778aa68fbe1c82f1920cda0e6f2b73eeb971789d.jpg)

Use the Puppeteer ability on the Assassin at the base of the cliff, near the Idol. Once you do, he will walk over to the nearby hand crank to extend a kite over the valley.

Head up the path until you reach the massive tree that reaches over the ravine. Climb up it and grapple across the valley, then follow the cliff face down to reach the Sunken Valley Cavern idol.

From here, provided that you've already encountered the Great Serpent in the Sunken Valley Passage, you can continue down into the cavern to find a cliff over-looking the massive creature. Perform a Plunging Deathblow on the Great Serpent below to acquire the Fresh Serpent Viscera and earn this Trophy/ Achievement.

# Completionist

Of all the challenges that Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice has to offer, these are among the greatest. Many of them will require you to enter at least one cycle of New Game+ for the purposes of fighting specific enemies or finding limited goods. By their very nature, these will take you the longest to unlock, but if you remain patient and determined, none of them are beyond your reach.

# Man Without Equal

![](images/f1e41f2e149b00cd991a5e7fb004307e1d92e43ce68c9234bb8b62e94a7a4029.jpg)

G60

![](images/af8d259545250e79e16f1c760e9882f528b82276405bd53da3117e57ef93d0f7.jpg)

Defeated all bosses

As far as the level of challenge goes, this is likely be the most difficult Trophy/Achievement you'll need to unlock. You'll need to use a single save file to do this, and you're unable to face every boss over the course of a single playthrough, because some of them only appear during one of two possible story paths. This means that you'll have to complete a New Game+ run in order to fulfill all of its requirements. For this reason, it's recommended to pursue any of the endings where you stay loyal to Lord Kuro on your first run, then pursue the Shura ending on New Game+ to face down Emma, the Gentle Blade and Isshin Ashina. This order will circumvent the New Game+ difficulty increase as much as possible, while still allowing you to fight every boss.

Be sure that you've acquired the Father's Bell Charm before defeating the Divine Dragon, as without it you will be unable to face Owl - Father during your first playthrough. Additionally, you'll want to be sure to face the Demon of Hatred on your first playthrough, because you'll be unable to face him on New Game+ while pursuing the Shura ending, and he'll be substantially more difficult if you wait until New Game+2.

# Master of the Prosthetic

![](images/fa8b38b76b69a529315e1b65fa27e0847fba68d97c4b56a092fdb32c15c84ed3.jpg)

Upgraded all Prosthetic Tools to their limit

This will unlock once you've purchased every Prosthetic Tool upgrade at the Dilapidated Temple. You'll only be able to achieve this on New Game+, due to the fact that a total of 10 Lapis Lazulis are needed to craft all the Lazulite tools, but you will only be able to find a maximum of six in a single playthrough. As such, you'll need to be sure that you've collected at least four of this material in your original run, otherwise you'll have to enter into another New Game+ cycle. Head to P.82 for the full rundown on restructuring your Prosthetic Tools.

There are also three unique materials required for this Trophy/ Achievement. The first is the Pine Ember Resin, which you can find in Mibu Village (P.279). The second is the Malcontent's Ring, acquired by defeating the Shichimen Warrior that appears in the Guardian Ape's Burrow after defeating and severing the immortality of the Guardian Ape (P.271). The third is the Phantom Kunai, which can be purchased for 3000 Sen from Anayama the Peddler.

# Master of the Arts

Grasped the inner mysteries of any combat style

This Trophy/Achievement is unlocked by purchasing the final ability (furthest to the right) in any skill tree. Specifically, the abilities that will yield this Trophy/Achievement are: Shadowrush, Living Force, Ashina Cross, or High Monk. How early you will get this is dependent upon how often you die and how much extra combat you partake in. You're likely to achieve it during a single playthrough, unless you spend your Skill EXP too evenly across all skill trees.

# Lazuline Upgrade

![](images/b0d8036d7f07b2a2934724e7cbbd635771fc0c842fe500671a109857050b7d78.jpg)  
G30

![](images/da51aa1ff8f949041783f97e1c86f55880b7e8bd7a5ab5b0fb8c660f58d660b4.jpg)

Used Lapis Lazuli to upgrade any tool to its limit

No other material found in the Ashina lands can empower Shinobi Tools quite like Lapis Lazuli. However, it's also the rarest material there is, and you'll not be able to acquire any at all until you've reached the Fountainhead Palace and defeated the Corrupted Monk. Every tool that utilizes Lapis Lazuli requires at least two of them for the upgrade, which makes Pot Noble Koremori the simplest source for the material. Trade 12 Treasure Carp Scales to Koremori and, once you've met all the necessary prerequisites to build a Lazulite tool and gathered any other needed materials, you will be able to unlock this Trophy/Achievement. The Restructuring section on P.82 and the Treasure Carp Scales chart on P.539 will be helpful in your quest to unlock this Trophy/Achievement.

# Resurrection

![](images/354599f1c9e351cb50efa1b64f85f83ad3d31241226d5f0f22515c44a5cc92fe.jpg)  
G20

![](images/7f1b55b86d185bdc0124fdef4c6c3f69f2010a69a7b7f8bf229f2711fd1f1b9f.jpg)

Returned from the dead using "Resurrection" for the first time

Resurrection defines Sekiro's journey, so this is a fitting Trophy/Achievement. It will automatically be awarded the first time you die and choose to Resurrect. Unless you are exceptionally skilled, you'll most likely come by this Trophy/Achievement naturally over the course of your playthrough.

# Index

In a book of this size, it's hard to beat a good old-fashioned index when you need to find something quickly. Every useful topic is ordered alphabetically, and we've included a simple color-coding so you know where you'll be taken: RED will refer you to the Items & Materials section, while PURPLE will take you to the relevant map position in the Path of the Shinobi chapter.
